generated_text: … honestly, I just think Darren’s mum is getting worse. Not deliberately, you understand, but she  always  manages to steer the conversation back to how wonderful  her  grandchildren are. It’s exhausting. And little Leo was trying so hard to show her his building blocks! Oh, bless him. And bless you for enduring it. Mothers, eh? They're a force of nature. At least you had a nice night out with Sarah on Friday, though? You needed it. Distraction therapy. It was lovely, actually. Proper belly laughs. We went to that new Italian place on the Parade. Remember I mentioned it? The one with the fairy lights? The pasta was…well, let’s just say I’m regretting the extra garlic bread this morning. Worth it, though. It’s just… a bit lonely sometimes, isn’t it? Everyone else seems to be doing these amazing trips, spontaneous weekends… and I’m just… here. Here, holding down the fort, being a brilliant aunt and keeping  my  life vaguely organised while I flap about! You’re not ‘just here’, love. You’re amazing. And honestly, those Instagram versions of everyone's lives are mostly lies. Sarah probably didn’t mention the argument she had with her husband about leaving the washing up until Monday? Probably not. You’re right. Still…seeing her photos from Cornwall…makes you wonder. Anyway, enough about my pathetic wanderlust. How's work going? Still buried under proofreading reports? Buried, absolutely buried. I've got that massive academic paper to turn around by Thursday. Honestly, the footnotes alone are a novel. It pays the bills, though, doesn’t it? And it lets me spend time with this little one. She’s growing so fast. Honestly, she was tiny last week, and now she’s grabbing at everything. She is! She's a proper little character. I can’t believe she's almost six months already. It feels like only yesterday we were all gathered at your place, waiting for the announcement. Do you think… do you think we should start thinking about a little party for her half-birthday? Ooh, that's a good idea! A little milestone celebration. Nothing huge, just family. We could do it here? Your garden's bigger, which is useful for crawling chaos. Yes, absolutely. We could get a little cake… not too much sugar, obviously. And maybe some balloons. Oh, and I’ll need to book some time off work, which is a nightmare at the moment.

… honestly, the sheer  volume  of paperwork they wanted for Bailey, even with the pet passport, was unbelievable. You’d think they’d suspect I was smuggling something more than a slightly anxious Border Terrier. Right? It’s like they actively  want  to discourage tourism. Remember when we did the Interrail thing after uni? It was relatively painless, even hopping between France, Germany and Italy. Now? It sounds like applying for a visa to North Korea. Exactly! I was telling Mam about it, and she was saying even back in the seventies, travelling to Spain with the kids was less hassle. And that was  before  passports were even standard for everyone in the EU! The assumption now is guilt until proven innocence, isn’t it? "Right, where are your stamps? Your proof of onward travel? Your financial statements?" It's exhausting. It's the mindset, I think. Pre-Brexit, there was a level of trust, a shared understanding. Now it feels…hostile. I’m thinking about taking the research to Barcelona next year for that conference, and I’m already dreading the airport. I used to just  go . Oh, Barcelona's lovely! We went a couple of years ago, before everything got… complicated. I’m heading to Amsterdam next month for a different project, and I’m genuinely considering flying into Schiphol and then getting the Eurostar to Brussels, just to avoid UK passport control altogether on the return. Sounds mental, doesn't it? Not at all. That's clever, actually. A bit of a detour, but worth it if it saves you a three-hour queue and a grilling. I heard stories of people being turned away for slightly wonky passport photos.  Slightly  wonky! Don’t even. My auntie nearly missed her flight to Portugal because her photo had a tiny bit of shadow. A tiny bit! She’s a solicitor, for goodness sake, she knows how to follow instructions. It’s just… deliberately obtuse. Do you think it’ll ever go back to how it was? I’m not optimistic, to be honest. Politically, it's all… mess. Even if things  do  soften, the bureaucracy is there now. They've built the infrastructure for this level of scrutiny. It becomes self-perpetuating, you know? Aye, I do. It feels like we’ve lost something precious. Little things, like just deciding on a whim to drive down to France for a weekend.

…and honestly, the whole point of shortbread is  butter . Proper butter. Not that spreadable stuff. It needs to almost crumble when you bite into it, you know? Like little sandy castles. Remember Grandma’s? Grandma’s was the best. She put sprinkles on sometimes. Pink ones. She did! She was a bit of a rebel with the sprinkles, your Grandma. Your Dad used to get so cross she wasn’t sticking to the “classic” recipe. Though he ate plenty of them, I can assure you. Can we  please  go back to Monopoly now? I need more money! Barnaby stole all my hotels! Barnaby, Barnaby, Barnaby. Always trying to bankrupt his sister. We’ll go back to Monopoly in a minute, love. We were just talking about desserts. Imagine a shortbread, lovely and buttery,  with  pink sprinkles… Ooh! And chocolate! Can we have chocolate with the shortbread? We could. Though I was thinking more of a nice raspberry jam. Or maybe even a lemon curd. Something a little bit tangy to cut through the richness. Tangy? What’s tangy? Is that like…sour? I don't want sour. I want money! I landed on Mayfair and Barnaby  still  won't give me any. He said it’s ‘tactical’. Tactical. He's learning all the right words, isn’t he? It means he’s clever, trying to win. Look, Barnaby, you can be tactical  and  fair. You can’t just refuse to pay rent. That’s not how Monopoly works. It's a basic principle of economics, really! Supply and demand, property ownership... Economics? Is that like Maths? I hate Maths. It’s… a bit like Maths, darling. It's about how things work with money, and what people want. Monopoly is actually a really good way to learn about it. See, you're learning even when you think you're just having fun! It teaches you about saving, investing… and the hardship of landing on Park Lane with a hotel! But it’s NOT fair! He keeps buying all the orange ones! He said they're the best because everyone lands on them. He’s right to think that, actually. Statistically, the orange properties are landed on more often. It's not cheating, it’s strategy. Though… you could maybe be a  little  more generous. Remember, the point isn’t just to make everyone else go bankrupt. It's to have a bit of fun.

… honestly, it’s just the principle of it, innit? Like, they  knew  I was starting this new job, and they decide  now  is the time to spring this on me about needing to sort out Grandad’s house? Right before my probation period even finishes? Yeah, that’s… not ideal timing, is it? Your Auntie Brenda’s always been a bit… strategically unhelpful, hasn’t she? It’s like she enjoys creating chaos. Strategic is a polite way of putting it. It’s flat-out passive aggressive! She could’ve mentioned this weeks ago. “Oh, just a little thing, your Grandad left everything to both of you, but the house needs a proper clear-out and you’re both responsible.” Like it's a jumble sale, not someone’s  life  we’re going through! Well, probate can be a bit of a nightmare anyway. It's just the legal stuff takes ages. But yeah, springing it on you now... she definitely could’ve given you a heads-up. Did she at least offer to help? Help? Ha! She said, and I quote, "Well, you’re the organised one, love. You’ll know what to do." Organised doesn’t mean I have magical time-bending powers, Brenda! I'm literally building a searchable database of historical linguistic data for a university project. It’s not exactly a skill transferable to decluttering forty years’ worth of Grandad’s hoarding. Right. Because comparing Old English verb conjugations to collectible biscuit tins is a perfectly logical leap. Look, how much stuff are we talking? Is it genuinely a full house, or just a few boxes in the attic? A  full  house. He didn’t throw  anything  away. Old newspapers, broken radios, three different sets of encyclopaedias… I swear he had a collection of every promotional pen he ever received. And it all smells faintly of Woodbine and mothballs. Oh, lovely. Sounds… charming. Okay, look, maybe we can break it down. We don’t have to do it all in one go. What about a weekend? We can block out a Saturday and a Sunday, get some skip bags, and just… attack it. We can order pizza, put some music on. It’ll be grim, but we’ll get through it. That… actually doesn’t sound awful. Having someone else there to, you know, witness the sheer scale of the madness will be helpful. And someone to argue with Brenda on my behalf if she starts offering unhelpful "suggestions" over the phone. Consider me your Brenda shield.

…No, I’m tellin’ ya, the council’s gone soft. Absolutely soft. Back in my day, if a hedge was overhandin’ onto the pavement, you got a letter, plain as day. Nowt like this dithering about. Old Man Hemmings’ blackthorn’s practically blockin’ the whole bloomin’ path! Ditherin’ is right, Arthur. Ditherin’ sums ‘em up nicely. Remember when they tried to put a roundabout on Dereham Road? An absolute shambles, that was. Spent a fortune, didn’t they? And it made things worse! Oh, don't even  start  me on Dereham Road. I used to take little Timmy down there to the park, and it was a nightmare. Always queued for ages. Though, to be fair, it  is  busier now than it used to be. All that new buildin' up towards Weston Longville. That’s just it, isn’t it, Margaret? More people, more problems. But they don’t seem to be spendin’ the money  wisely . They’re puttin’ cycle lanes everywhere nobody uses. Cycle lanes! In Norfolk! Who’s gonna cycle in this weather? Showin’ off, that’s what it is. Tryin’ to be all…progressive. Doesn’t work, though. Folk round here like their cars. Always ‘ave. My dad, he’d polish his Morris Minor every Sunday. Never seen anything like it. Ernest, you and your cars! Remember when you tried to fix the exhaust on that Austin Cambridge yourself? Nearly set the garage alight! Now, now, Margaret, a man’s gotta ‘ave a hobby. And it weren't  nearly  alight! Just a little…smoky. Besides, it saved a few bob. Everything costs a fortune these days, don’t it? Even a loaf of bread. Tell me about it. The price of everything's gone through the roof. It’s a disgrace. And the television…all this talk of strikes. Nurses strikin’, train drivers strikin’. It’s enough to give you the heebie-jeebies. It's awful, Arthur. They deserve a proper wage. Workin’ like that, lookin’ after people... it's not easy. I always had respect for nurses. Remember Mrs. Davies, when your mother was poorly? She was a saint. Aye, a saint she were. Came round every day, bless her. Though, she did ‘ave a fondness for a little sherry, didn’t she? Didn’t mind a drop, that one. You’re tellin’ me! She’d be round ‘ere lookin’ for a cuppa and a sneaky tipple.

…and honestly, the packaging is  still  giving me grief. I thought sourcing recycled cardboard would be straightforward, but finding boxes that are the right dimensions for the serum bottles  and  don’t look completely… well, cheap, is proving a nightmare. Everything’s either too big, so you’ve got loads of void fill, or too small and you risk damage. Ugh, packaging. The bane of my existence with the jewellery, honestly. It's always something. Did you actually measure the bottle dimensions precisely? Millimetre perfect? Because that’s what I had to do. I was sending out earrings in boxes that were, like, 2mm too short and they kept getting bent. Nightmare reviews. I have! I’ve got a spreadsheet, naturally. Teacher brain, you see. Length, width, height, diameter of the dropper…the whole shebang. It's just… the off-the-shelf options are awful. I'm considering bespoke, but the quotes I've got are frankly terrifying. It would eat into the profit margin before we’ve even sold anything. Bespoke is definitely pricey. Have you looked at eBay for bulk boxes? Sounds awful, I know, but sometimes you can find people clearing out stock and you get a decent deal. I got loads of little velvet pouches for the earrings there, proper cheap. That’s a thought, actually. I’ve been so focused on ‘eco-friendly’ I’ve maybe overlooked practical cost-effectiveness. It’s just… the whole ‘Honest Skincare’ brand hinges on appearing really premium, but ethically sound. It's a fine line, isn't it? It is! And I think people appreciate that you  are  trying with the eco-stuff. They’ll forgive a slightly less fancy box if they know you’re not just chucking everything in plastic. Speaking of which, how's the social media marketing going? Have you started running those Instagram ads we talked about? Slowly. It’s all a learning curve. I did a little campaign targeting women aged 25-45 interested in organic skincare, but the click-through rate was pathetic. I think I need to refine the imagery. It’s all very… botanical and calm, but maybe a bit bland? Bland is the enemy! People scroll so fast. You need something that  grabs  them. Maybe photos of real people using the serum? Before and after, you know? A bit of actual visible result. I find that works really well with the jewellery.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it! Claiming it was a ‘technical glitch’. A technical glitch that managed to misallocate funds to a company registered in the Cayman Islands? Don’t make me laugh, David. It’s blatant, isn't it? Just blatant. You’ve been reading too much of that online stuff, Margaret. Always gets you worked up. It’s probably just incompetence, you know? Bureaucracy gone wrong. They’re not all master criminals. Though, I’ll grant you, it  does  look a bit dodgy. Incompetence on a scale that funnels money offshore? David, I taught history for thirty years! I've seen patterns, I recognize a cover-up when I see one. And did you hear what they’re doing with the NHS now? Allowing private companies to… well, effectively cherry-pick the easy cases. It's dismantling it, bit by bit. Now, now. Don't get yourself going again. I read something about that too, but they said it’s to reduce waiting lists. Apparently, they’ll still treat everyone, just… differently. Streamlined, they called it. Streamlined! It’s privatisation by stealth, that’s what it is. They’ll leave the NHS with all the complicated, expensive cases and the private sector will cream off the profitable ones. It's utterly immoral. And it’s all connected, you know. This corruption, this… erosion of public services. It’s all part of the same rotten system. You always see the worst in things, Margaret. It’s a gift, I suppose, being a historian. Always looking at the decline and fall. But sometimes things aren’t  that  bad. How are you feeling, actually? You’ve been quieter than usual these past few weeks. More… preoccupied. Oh, just…thinking. About Mother, mostly. It's nearly the anniversary, you know. Twenty years next month. It still feels like yesterday sometimes, especially when I'm in the garden. She loved her roses. I know. It does. I miss her terribly. She always had a kind word for everyone, didn’t she? And she made the best scones. Remember those? Light as a feather. Oh, don't even mention the scones. I've tried for years to replicate them, and I’ve never quite managed it. It's a family secret, lost with her, I suppose. It's just… lonely, David. Being here. In the house. It's too quiet. I know it is.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Brussels sprouts my mother insists on making is criminal. It's not  Christmas  without them, apparently. Like a tradition carved in stone. Though, I suspect it’s less about tradition and more about her proving she can still ‘provide’ for everyone, you know? Aye, I get that. Me mam's the same with the trifle. It’s always gotta be  her  trifle, even though no one really eats it. It’s just…there. Symbolism, I think. Though sprouts, aye, that’s a bit much. Still, beats having to pretend to enjoy Uncle Barry’s questionable Christmas pudding. Oh god, the pudding. Last year it was… suspiciously bouncy. I think he added too much brandy  and  something else. Anyway, speaking of providing, have you sorted your heating, Liam? It’s freezing out there. This house is lovely, Esme, but the old stone walls… they just  suck  the heat. Tell me about it. Mine’s a converted barn. Romantic, yes. Efficient at retaining heat? Absolutely not. I’m burning through logs like it’s going out of fashion. Thinking about investing in one of those fancy log splitters. My axe arm is starting to protest. Oh, good idea. Are you still making those incredible benches and tables, Rhys? I need a new small side table for the living room. Something… rustic, but not  too  rustic. And definitely sturdy enough to withstand clumsy postgraduate research habits. Aye, still at it. Got a big commission for a pub table at the moment. Keeps me busy. Rustic’s my bread and butter, but I can do ‘refined rustic’ if that makes sense. I’ve got access to some lovely oak, or I could even work with walnut. What about you, Esme? How’s the research going? Still wrangling with those ancient texts? Unfortunately. It's a bit of a slog, to be honest. Funding bids are the real killer, though. Feels like I spend more time writing proposals than actually…doing the research. It’s all a bit disheartening. Sometimes I fantasize about retiring to a cottage and growing mulberries. Utterly impractical, I know. Retirement? You’re barely thirty! I’m already starting to have those thoughts though. This job’s alright, pays the bills, but staring at industrial machinery all day… it’s not exactly fulfilling is it? I’d rather be fixing things for people directly, maybe open a little repair shop.

… honestly, I just don’t understand why we have so many different forks. Like, seriously, four types of fork? What’s the point of a fish fork when you can just use a normal one? It’s ridiculous. You're sounding like Dad, actually. He's always moaning about the cutlery drawer. Says Mum’s got a fork for  every  occasion. Aye, well, yer Mam always liked to be prepared. It wasn’t about needing ‘em, it was about  having  ‘em. Represented a certain standard, didn’t it? You know, when we had guests… proper guests. Not just the usual lot. She always worried about appearances, your mother. Never wanted to look… wanting. It stemmed from her childhood, I think. Things were tight then. She remembered not having a matching set, ever. Aye… tight. Used to use wooden spoons for everything, we did. Lucky to  have  cutlery, never mind a special fork for a kipper. Right, okay, that's… a completely different perspective. I just thought it was excessive. I'm trying to declutter my flat, and this place is a goldmine of things I don’t need. Although, most of it is lovely, just... a lot. You could ‘borrow’ some, you know, for when you have people round. Impress your mates with the fancy fork selection. They’d just think I’m weird. They eat pizza off paper plates, mostly. Speaking of guests, are we still on for Sarah and Ben next weekend? I haven’t heard anything confirmed. I spoke to Sarah yesterday. She said Ben’s got a work thing, a training course or summat. They’re postponing it till the month after. Gutted, I was looking forward to seein’ ‘em. Haven't seen 'em since Christmas. That’s a shame. Ben’s a good lad. Always polite. Reminds me a bit of… well, never mind. Used to be good to have a house full of young ‘uns. Plenty of noise. Gets quiet, don’t it? Too quiet. It does get quiet, Grandad. That’s why we try and come round as often as we can. Keeps things lively. Although, Mum's still trying to get me to marry Sophie's sister. She thinks they'd be a 'good match'. Oh,  really ? Is she still pushing that? She tried to set me up with the butcher’s son last time I was here! Yer Mam’s a matchmaker at heart, loves it she does.

… honestly, the meeting could have been an email. A  long  email. Three people flew in from different parts of Europe just to… nod at a PowerPoint presentation I’d already circulated. It’s infuriating, isn’t it? Just a complete waste of everyone’s time and, frankly, money. Is ‘infuriating’ a really big word, Mummy? Like, bigger than ‘enormous’? It is a big word, yes. It means really,  really  annoyed. And yes, bigger than enormous, although they’re different kinds of big. Enormous is about size, infuriating is about… feelings. Now, finish your peas, love. But I don’t  like  peas. They’re… green and bouncy. They’re good for you, sweetheart. Think of them as fuel for skiing! Speaking of which, have you been practicing your snow angel technique? Yes! I did one in the garden on the patio. Daddy said it looked like a very wobbly ghost. Your Dad and his wobbly ghosts. Right, so wobbly ghosts are good. That means you’re ready to make proper snow angels in Austria. I’ve been going through the booking confirmation again, and everything  should  be alright. Transfers booked, ski school sorted for you… Will I be in a class with other kids? Yes, you will. A class with kids your age. They’re really good at teaching beginners, and it's a lovely little school. You'll be whizzing down those slopes in no time. Although, perhaps not  whizzing  on the first day. More like… carefully sliding. Can I wear my sparkly helmet? The pink one? Absolutely! The sparkly pink helmet is non-negotiable. It’s the best helmet ever invented. It’s also the safest. Now, about work… honestly, I’m starting to think about looking for something else. This endless cycle of pointless meetings is draining the life out of me. I spend more time  talking  about work than actually  doing  work. Is it like when you talk about cleaning my room and I don't actually clean it? That's… remarkably perceptive, actually. It's a bit like that. Except the consequences are slightly more serious than a messy bedroom. I'm thinking maybe something more freelance, something I can do from home. More control, you know? So you could be home more? And read me more stories? That’s the idea, darling. More stories, more time together. But first, we’ve got a skiing holiday to look forward to.

… honestly, Mr. Davies is taking the  mickey . Like, a whole essay on the symbolism of the green light in  Great Gatsby ? Who even  cares  that much about a green light?! It’s a light, innit? Oh, you’re winding me up. It’s Mr. Davies. He  always  goes deep. Remember last year with  Romeo and Juliet  and the whole, like, fate versus free will thing? He went on for ages. Ugh, don’t remind me. I just want to get through English Lit and move onto something… less… symbolic. What about you? How’s Spanish going? Any closer to ordering tapas without sounding like a complete idiot? Getting there, slowly. Señora Rodriguez is brilliant, but she speaks so fast! I was trying to say I liked paella, and I think I accidentally told her I was dating a chicken. No way! A chicken?! Oh my God, you are hopeless. Honestly, though, I wish I’d picked Spanish. It seems… useful. More useful than dissecting a green light, anyway. It is! Mum keeps saying it'll be good for travelling. And you know, actual jobs. She was going on about translation work and things. What are you thinking of doing when you leave school, anyway? Have you given it any thought, beyond escaping Mr. Davies’ symbolism? Honestly? No clue. Everyone’s talking about apprenticeships and stuff, but nothing really jumps out. My dad keeps hinting I should do something with maths – he thinks I'm good at it. You  are  good at maths! You always help me with the calculus bits I don't understand. But you hate it, don't you? Hate is a strong word. I just… don’t find it  inspiring . It's all numbers and rules. I'd rather do something creative, I think. But what? Everything feels so… pressured. Like you have to have a five-year plan at fifteen. Tell me about it! Mum's already booked me a careers session. Apparently, they’ll tell me my ‘strengths and weaknesses’. As if I don't already know I'm good at art and terrible at public speaking. Oh god, don't even mention public speaking. The thought makes me sweat. Did you finish that Food Tech practical? The one with the soufflés? Thankfully! It was a disaster. Mine collapsed before I even took it out of the oven. Mrs. Peterson said it was “a learning experience”.

… honestly, darling, all these superhero films, they just all blur into one, don't they? Bang, pow, someone flies, another one's got a metal suit - it’s just  noise . Remember when films actually  meant  something? Gran, you say that about everything new! It’s not  all  noise. Some of them are genuinely clever. Like,  Everything Everywhere All at Once ? That wasn’t just bang, pow. It was…complex. And surprisingly emotional.  Everything Everywhere … sounds exhausting just saying it. Too much going on. I prefer a good, solid story. Something like… oh,  Brief Encounter . Now  that  was a film. Real life, real feelings. No capes. Okay, okay, classic British cinema, I get it. But it's a different world now. People want escapism. And a lot of these films  are  offering something. Plus, the special effects are incredible. You have to admit that. Special effects are alright, I suppose. When they’re done properly. Some of ‘em look like they were made by a child with a computer. Remember  Flash Gordon ? Now  that  was gloriously bad. Camp as Christmas, but you knew it was fun. These modern ones take themselves far too seriously. You're right about  Flash Gordon  being camp! Dad showed me that one last year, thinking it would be awful, and we both ended up loving it. But seriously, Gran, have you seen anything recently that  has  grabbed you? Anything at all? Hmm… well, I did enjoy that one with Judi Dench. The one with the Indian hotel.  The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel . That was lovely. Bit predictable, maybe, but nicely done. And the scenery was beautiful. Made me want to go to India, though I suspect it’s not quite as glamorous as they made out. That’s a good one! Mum loves that film. It's feel-good, isn't it? I was thinking, maybe we could go to the cinema next week? There's a new Wes Anderson one out.  Asteroid City . Wes Anderson… oh, the one with all the symmetrical shots and the deadpan delivery? I saw a trailer. Looked a bit… fussy. That’s Wes Anderson. It’s  supposed  to be fussy! It's really visually interesting. And the cast is amazing. Scarlett Johansson, Jason Schwartzman… Scarlett Johansson. She’s a pretty one, isn’t she? Though I preferred her in… what was it…  Lost in Translation . That was a quiet film. A lovely film.

… honestly, Mum, the traffic was  awful  getting up here. Absolutely gridlocked on the M40. I swear, every time I come to Birmingham it’s the same. It adds at least an hour onto the journey. Oh, you poor love. That M40 is a nightmare. Always has been, hasn't it? I remember your Dad complaining about it when he used to drive to London for work. Still, you made it! Coffee’s good, isn’t it? I got that new Fairtrade blend from the market. It's lovely, thanks. Exactly what I needed. Though I’m starting to wonder if it’s worth the petrol money, honestly. And the stress! Maybe I should just get the train next time. The train’s alright, but it's not the same, is it? No freedom. And it’s not cheap, is it? Especially now. Everything’s going up, isn't it? Even a simple cup of coffee. Speaking of which, how  is  teaching going? Still battling with teenagers and their… well, you know. You have no idea. Year 10 are currently convinced Shakespeare is ‘cancelled’. Trying to explain the historical context to them is like talking to a brick wall. It’s exhausting. But good, you know? Challenging. They need someone to steer them, even if they don't think they do. I’m hoping for a pay rise this year, though. It's getting… tight. Especially with saving for a deposit on a place. A pay rise is what you deserve! You work your socks off. And saving… well, good luck with that these days. Property prices are ridiculous. Remember when we bought this house? A fraction of what they are now. Though, I suppose wages were different then too. Are you still walking Buster when it’s pouring? Yes, poor thing demands his walk, rain or shine. He's getting on a bit now, though. His joints aren’t what they used to be. He's a proper old man dog. I've been thinking about getting him one of those little ramps for the sofa. Oh, a ramp! That’s a lovely idea. He’d appreciate that. He’s a good dog, that Buster. I always enjoy seeing him. Did you see the football on Saturday? Aston Villa actually won! I did! I managed to catch the highlights. I’m not a massive football fan, but even  I  was pleased for you.

…and honestly, the student feedback was  brutal . Apparently, my lecture on post-structuralism was “too much, too soon” for a Tuesday afternoon. Can you believe it? Too much Derrida before coffee, apparently. Oh, bless them. They do say timing is everything. Though, if they can’t handle a bit of deconstruction before 2pm, are they  really  ready for university? Still, brutal feedback isn’t fun. Did you at least get some constructive criticism mixed in with the negativity? A couple. Someone said my pacing was good, which is a win. But mostly it was just… bewildered emojis. It’s hard adapting to how they learn here, isn’t it? Different expectations. Back in Norwich, I could throw around Foucault and they’d at least  pretend  to understand. It's a completely different cultural approach to learning. Much more emphasis on rote memorisation, less on critical thinking, generally. Though, I've found that once you break through that, they’re incredibly engaged. My history class is slowly, finally, starting to question sources. Small victories. That’s good to hear. It feels like pushing uphill sometimes. Oh! Speaking of uphill battles… did you manage to find those weirdly specific tea towels I asked about? The ones with the vintage botanical illustrations? That was an  adventure . You know, this city is amazing for everything… except obscure British household goods. I went to three different markets. The first one just had knock-off football shirts. The second had…well, I’m still not entirely sure  what  the second one had. A lot of plastic, that’s all I’ll say. Oh, you poor thing! I should have just ordered them online. But I thought it might be nice to support the local economy. Always a noble but ultimately disastrous plan, isn’t it? Exactly. Eventually, I found a tiny shop hidden down a side street – run by an expat Scot, of all people. He had one set.  One . And he’d priced them like they were made of gold. Honestly! Only in China. How much were they? Don’t ask. Let’s just say I paid more than they’d cost at John Lewis. But I have them. They’re safe. I’m bringing them home with me. We can have a proper English tea tomorrow, with botanical glory. You are a lifesaver! Honestly, you’re the best. I’ve been craving a proper cuppa.

…and honestly, the whole thing with Mrs. Peterson cancelling her book club because of her hair appointment is just  bonkers . Like, a hair appointment trumps Jane Austen? Really? Is Jane Austen about princesses? Not exactly princesses, love. It’s about people, and love, and… complicated families. A bit like ours, actually! Though hopefully with fewer arguments about who gets the last biscuit. I want a biscuit! Is it chocolate chip? Not yet, darling. These are for the photoshoot. Remember? We’re trying to make them look  really  nice. Auntie Sarah wants pictures for her website. Photoshoot? Will I have to wear the sparkly dress? Possibly! It’s a very sparkly dress. But we can talk about that later. Right now, I need to figure out Saturday. I promised Chloe I’d try and meet her in Cambridge, but if I’m baking  and  trying to get you two presentable for photos… I  am  presentable! Roar! You’re a very presentable dinosaur, yes. But Auntie Sarah wants… less dinosaur, perhaps. Look, I was thinking I could drop you two with Gran and Grandad on Saturday morning. Would you like that? Can we read with Grandad? He does funny voices. You absolutely can. He promised to do the Gruffalo. And then I can nip into town and see Chloe. We haven't properly chatted since… well, since forever. She’s just started a new pottery class and apparently, it’s all going brilliantly. Pottery sounds messy. Can we make pottery later? Maybe, after the photoshoot. And  after  a very thorough clean-up. Okay, so Gran and Grandad on Saturday morning. That leaves the afternoon for baking and… hair. Oh goodness, the hair. Freddie, yours is looking a bit wild. It's aerodynamic for dinosaur flying! That’s… a very good point. But Auntie Sarah might not appreciate the aerodynamic look. Lily, have you been brushing yours? Mummy brushed it this morning. But it got messy when I was pretending to be Rapunzel. Naturally. Right. Maybe a quick trim for both of you after baking? There’s that little salon in the village, they're usually good with wiggly children. Although… I really need a haircut too. It's getting down to my eyes. You look like a lion! Roar! Very funny. Look, let's focus on the cookies for now. Can you two help me sprinkle the chocolate chips? And  no  eating them before they're baked, understood?

… honestly, the library's just  packed  now. Like, every single desk is taken. It’s a proper scrum, innit? I tried to find a quiet corner to do my essay on Victorian literature and ended up practically nose-to-nose with someone eating a pot noodle. The  smell , Liv, the smell! Oh, bless you. Sounds charming. Kingston library is always a bit… intense. Especially around deadline time. Mine’s not much better, to be fair. Though, at least I can usually snag a table if I go super early. Like, before nine. Are you actually making any progress on that essay, though? Victorian lit sounds…dense. Progress is a strong word. I've got a rough plan, and I’ve read  some  of ‘Jane Eyre’, but it's just… a lot. It's not like watching a Netflix series, is it? You can't just binge-read critical analysis. Plus, Mum keeps texting me about what I'm having for dinner when I go home next weekend. It's distracting! She wants to know if I’m eating enough vegetables. Honestly, like I’m five. Mums, eh? Mine’s the same! Constantly asking if I’m wearing enough layers. She's convinced I'm always cold, even in summer. But yeah, that essay sounds rough. Honestly, I'm just trying to get through this statistics module. It's killing me softly. I just don’t  get  standard deviation. It feels like they’re just making numbers up. Oh god, statistics. I steered well clear of that. Smart move, I reckon. Listen, are you free later? I was thinking we could grab some drinks – not loads, just a couple – at The Fighting Cocks. They’ve got that student discount on Tuesdays. Might take the edge off this uni stress. Ooh, that actually sounds amazing. I'm definitely in need of a de-stress. I think I officially lost a brain cell trying to understand confidence intervals. What are you thinking of getting? They do a pretty good mojito, although it's a bit pricey even  with  the discount. Mojito sounds good. Or maybe just a simple gin and tonic. Need something that won't lead to a maths-induced meltdown. Oh! Speaking of drinks, remember Uncle Barry’s attempt at making cocktails at Christmas? Honestly, it was like someone mixed paint stripper and lemonade. Oh my  god , yes! And he was so proud of them!

… honestly, I just think people get too obsessed with all-inclusive. Like, you  have  to explore! You’re in Greece, for goodness sake, not Blackpool. I mean, Dad loved all-inclusive, didn’t he? Just sat by the pool all day with a can of Stella. Good for him, but not exactly broadening the horizons, was it? Aye, your Dad was a man of simple pleasures. Though, to be fair, after a long week, just  relaxing  sounds pretty good. I was thinking about maybe doing something a bit more active next year, though. Maybe hiking in the Dolomites? I’ve been looking at some routes. Dolomites? Ambitious! You'll need to up your fitness, Ben. I’m still recovering from that 'gentle stroll' we did in the Peak District last month. My legs were screaming for a week. Harsh, Leo, harsh! It wasn't  that  bad. And I did carry most of the water. Besides, I’ve been going to the gym, alright? Trying to, anyway. Work's been relentless. Tell me about it. This corpus project is just… unending. Seriously, the amount of data we're dealing with. It’s like wading through treacle. Speaking of unending, have you guys seen that new series, ‘The Reeling’? It's on iPlayer. It's about competitive sea angling. Seriously. Competitive  sea angling ? Is that… a thing? Apparently! It's surprisingly gripping. All the tension of a high-stakes drama, but with more wellies and bad sweaters. Honestly, I’m hooked. And the commentary. The bloke sounds like he’s reporting on the Champions League final. “And here we see young Barry, reeling in a magnificent… whiting!” You’re pulling my leg! That sounds brilliantly awful. I’ve been trying to get through ‘Severance’ – everyone keeps saying it’s amazing, but it’s so… slow. ‘Severance’ is good, you just need to persevere. It picks up. Though I’m currently rewatching ‘Taskmaster’. Utter genius. Alex Horne is a national treasure. Oh aye, ‘Taskmaster’ is pure gold. Greg Davies is hysterical. It's just so  silly . Speaking of silly, you wouldn’t believe what Mam made for tea last night. She tried to make paella. Oh dear. That sounds… risky. Risky is an understatement. It looked like something you’d find growing in a petri dish. The rice was completely raw, the chicken was still pink, and she’d somehow managed to add raisins.

…No, no, I’m tellin’ ya, the traffic was  shockin’ . Shockin’. Reminds me of when we took the Morris Minor to London back in ‘68. Took us near on six hours just to get to the North Circular. Six hours! And that was without all this… congestion charge business. Oh, don't even  start  on the congestion charge, Arthur. Highway robbery, that is. We went up last year to see Emily in her new flat near Victoria, and it was dreadful. Still, at least she’s happy. Though I tell you, the price of a cup of tea…! Fifteen quid for two biscuits and a brew. Fifteen quid? Blimey. You're getting robbed! Though, London’s always been expensive. Remember when we took the kids? Little Timmy insisted on a ride on one of those… what are they called, those giant revolving things? The London Eye. Cost a fortune. He was sick five minutes later. Aye, kids. They’re a handful, aren't they? Though, speakin' of handfuls, did you see that stallion at the races on the telly yesterday? Beautiful beast. Reminded me of Dobbin, Old Man Hemmings’ horse. Now  that  was a proper animal. He used to let me brush him, he did. Oh, horses. You and your horses, Arthur. Always were a bit obsessed. Still, it's healthier than watchin’ all that football, isn’t it? Though I do enjoy a bit of Match of the Day. Got to keep up with the lads, you know. It’s a good job I’ve retired, to be honest. The stress of dealing with teenagers these days… it'll take years off you. They haven't got a clue about the value of a penny. Everything’s digital, instant. They used to come to me needing help with their homework, now they just Google it. Google. Blast it all. I tried to sell that old gramophone on eBay last week. Took me hours to work out how to photograph it right. And then some fella offered me a fiver! A  fiver ! For a perfectly good gramophone. Five pounds? That’s outrageous! You should've ignored him. I sold my china cabinet on there, got a decent price. Though, getting it delivered was a nightmare. Had to help the poor delivery man, bless him. He nearly threw his back out. Speaking of selling things, have you two given any more thought to downsizing?

…and honestly, the amount of unsolicited advice is  exhausting . Like, everyone’s suddenly a child psychologist when you’re six weeks postpartum. Old Mrs. Higgins at the post office told me I should be introducing purees  now . Now! He's barely figured out how to latch properly, let alone manage solid food. Oh, tell me about it. My mum was on about weaning Elsie at twelve weeks. Twelve! She said her ‘instincts’ told her Elsie was ready. Instincts. More like reading outdated magazine articles. You'd think having had three herself would make her… less prone to fads. Exactly! It's like they forget how utterly chaotic those first few months are. You’re just surviving, right? I feel like I'm constantly apologizing for not being a perfect, serene mother. It's all Instagram versus reality. Completely. Elsie screamed for a solid three hours yesterday.  Three . And I just sat on the sofa, weeping with her, feeling like a complete failure. Then my aunt phoned, asking if I was “enjoying motherhood.” Enjoying?! Oh, the  enjoying  question! Ugh. Is that even a valid question in the first six months? It’s mostly just… managing. And trying to remember if  you’ve  eaten anything. How is little Elsie doing, anyway? You haven't mentioned her feeding much. Is it still tricky? Tricky is… an understatement. She’s got a tongue tie, apparently. They finally diagnosed it last week. Explains the endless feeding sessions, the weight gain being slow. I’m having to express and top her up with a syringe after every feed. Honestly, I feel like a dairy cow some days. Oh, bless you. That sounds  so  draining. And a tongue tie diagnosis… I’ve heard they can be a nightmare. Has anyone talked about snipping it? They have. The health visitor suggested it. I'm… hesitant. It feels so invasive and I'm worried about the pain. My mum, predictably, thinks it’s the only way, says it’ll ‘fix everything’. Honestly, sometimes I wish she'd just  listen  instead of telling me what to do. It’s the same with Dad – constantly asking when I’m going back to work. Like this is some sort of holiday! It's infuriating, isn’t it? Everyone has an opinion, and none of them are experiencing it themselves. Have you told him it’s not a holiday? Repeatedly. He doesn’t get it.

…and honestly, the price of lettuce! Honestly, eighty pence for a cos lettuce? It's daylight robbery, it is. I remember when you could get one for twenty pence. You and your lettuce, Brenda. It’s always the lettuce. It’s a good job we’ve got a bit growing in the greenhouse, then, isn’t it? Though that’s taking an age to come on. It’s the weather, Dad. Everything's delayed this year. Apparently, it’s been the coldest April on record for… well, quite a long time. Something about the jet stream? I read an article. Jet stream? Sounds complicated. I'm just hoping the weather stays a bit kinder for the garden. I really want to get the hanging baskets sorted this weekend. Mrs. Higgins next door has already got hers up, and they look lovely. Oh, don't start comparing ourselves to Mrs. Higgins, Carol! Her garden is practically a professional display. We’re aiming for ‘charming’ not ‘Chelsea Flower Show.’ Speaking of this weekend, are you two still coming over for Sunday roast? Absolutely, love. Wouldn't miss it. Though I might have to sneak out early to finish that report. Old man Henderson is breathing down my neck about it. Says it needs ‘finalising’ despite me sending him drafts for a week. Sounds about right. Henderson’s a nightmare. I think he enjoys creating stress. I’m free all weekend, though. Maybe I can help with the garden, Mum? Pull some weeds? I feel bad just eating all your roast dinners without contributing. Oh, that would be lovely, darling. Just lovely. There's a patch of bindweed trying to take over the rose bushes – it's a proper battle. Carol, you wouldn't happen to have any of that weed killer stuff, would you? The one with the spray bottle? I think I do, Brenda. I bought some last week, actually, specifically for the dandelions on the lawn. Little terrors, they are. Everything needs doing, doesn't it? I was thinking of taking Pepper for a longer walk this afternoon. He's been a bit restless. Good idea, Carol. He probably senses you’ve been glued to those nursing books all week. You’re working so hard, trying to get your NP qualification. Proud of you, you know. Thanks, Geoff. It’s just… a lot. So much to remember! And the practical stuff is different to the textbooks.

… honestly, Miss Davies is  determined  to make us all fail the trigonometry test. It's like she actively enjoys watching us struggle. Did you manage to, like, even understand half of it? Ugh, don't even  start  on Miss Davies. It’s brutal. I think I got, like, three questions right purely by guessing. Honestly, I’d rather be sorting my nan’s stamp collection than doing trig any day. Which, by the way, speaking of Nan, she’s got this amazing new Guatemalan stamp. It’s got a quetzal bird on it. Ooh, fancy! Nan’s collection is incredible. Remember that time she showed us the Penny Black? She's been collecting forever, hasn't she? It’s way more interesting than sine and cosine, definitely. Though, Dad says stamps are a bit…niche. He’s all about science, always going on about the latest findings about, like, plant photosynthesis. Boring. Your dad  is  obsessed with plants. He’s turned the whole garden into a mini-botanical garden, hasn't he? He even named that weird fern ‘Brenda’. Brenda! Who names a fern? I know! It’s so ridiculous. He said Brenda had “character”. He's got a whole system for everything, little labels and everything. It’s…organised. A bit  too  organised. Anyway, back to more important things. Christmas! Have you started thinking about what you want? A little bit. I really want that watercolour paint set from Cass Art. The one with all the professional colours. But Mum says I need to prove I’ll actually  use  it, not just add to the mountain of art supplies already under my bed. That’s fair. I'm thinking maybe a new Ed Sheeran album? Or…actually, something for the garden. I was helping Dad prune the roses yesterday - they're looking a bit sad - and I realised I really want a proper pair of gardening gloves. Not those flimsy pink ones Mum bought me. They get ripped instantly. Good plan! Although, gardening in December…that’s a bit dedicated, even for you. We’ll probably be battling snow and ice by then. Speaking of battling, do you know what uniform we have to wear for the Christmas carol concert? It's so confusing. They’ve sent out like three emails and I  still  don’t know. I think it's our normal school uniform with a red scarf? But Mrs. Peterson said something about black shoes being essential, and I only have the ones with the little buckle… Buckles are  fine !

…and honestly, Doreen, it’s a right nuisance getting old, it is. Not the aches and pains, mind – though they're there, oh boy are they there – it’s the  seeing . Everything’s getting blurry. I reckon I need to bite the bullet and go for another eye test. Last one, they said, “Oh, it’s just age, Arthur.” Age! Like that explains everything. Oh, Arthur, you’re a grumble-bum, you are. But you  do  need to get it checked. Remember last time you tried to thread a needle? You nearly poked your eye out! It’s very common, Father. The lenses in our eyes lose flexibility as we age. Perfectly natural. Though perhaps you should try a different optician, if you weren’t satisfied with the last assessment. There are some excellent ones in Richmond now. Richmond, eh? That’s a fair trek. Getting to Norwich is bad enough on the bus. You wouldn’t believe the characters you get on those things now. And they’ve altered the route, haven’t they? Always altering the route. Makes a man feel right lost. They did change it, dear. Now you have to walk a bit further from the High Street. I could drive you, Arthur, if you like. No bother at all. Oh, now, Doreen, you’re a saint, you are. But I don’t like putting you to all that trouble. Besides, a bit of walking does me good. Keeps the joints moving, as they say. Though I nearly tripped over young Timmy’s…well, you wouldn’t believe it. Timmy? What has he been up to now? He’s got one of them…rat puppets. A proper one, with moving eyes and everything! He was waving it about on the bus, pretending it was trying to steal my biscuit. Scared the life out of old Mrs. Higgins, it did. Oh, that Timmy! He’s a little terror, but a sweet boy. A rat puppet… Honestly. Children will be children. Though a discerning choice of puppet, I must say. Rats have always been rather fascinating creatures. Resourceful. Resourceful? They’re pests, plain and simple! Reminds me of old man Hemmings down the road. Always fiddling with something, always causing trouble. Speaking of fiddling, have you two been practicing with the handbells? We had a go last week, Arthur. It's harder than it looks! My wrists aren't what they used to be.

...Honestly, tha's why I’m glad we came mid-week. Last time, tryin’ to get a table here on a Saturday was a nightmare. Remember Auntie Maureen nearly had a conniption fit?      Oh, don’t remind me. Maureen and a queue… never a good mix. She thinks she’s royalty, bless her. But you’re right, it’s much nicer like this. More…relaxed. So, right, plans for today then? You said you wanted to actually  see  Venice, not just caffeinate in it?      Aye, that's it. I was thinkin' we could wander towards Rialto, maybe try and get lost in some of the little backstreets. I’ve seen pictures of some proper quirky shops there. And I really want to see the Bridge of Sighs. Is it as gloomy as they say?      Gloomy? It’s got a history, love. It’s where they used to lead prisoners to execution. So, yeah, a bit of a downer, historically speakin’. But it’s beautiful in a…melancholy way. We can definitely go there. We could take a vaporetto – that’s a water bus, for tourists who don’t know - up the Grand Canal first, get a proper view of all the palaces.      Ooh, that sounds brilliant. A vaporetto sounds dead glamorous. It’s just…it’s so different to Bolton, innit? Even the air smells different. Less…factory.      Less factory indeed! I remember comin’ here with your Grandad, years ago. This café wasn’t even here then. It was just a little, dingy fishmonger’s. Venice used to be  rough  around the edges, a proper workin’ port. Now it’s all tourists and overpriced gondolas. Still beautiful, mind, but changed. Grandad used to talk about the smell of the fish… and the shouting of the sailors. Not quite the scent of cappuccino and biscotti, eh?      No way! A fishmonger's? I can’t picture it at all. It’s all designer shops and Murano glass now. Do you think they still make actual Venetian masks, or are they all cheap imports?      There are still artisans, thankfully. You need to go away from San Marco Square, though. Find the little workshops tucked away. They’re pricey, but worth it. Speaking of pricey…have you decided what you fancy for lunch? They do a fabulous seafood risotto at that little trattoria near the Arsenale.      Risotto sounds  lush , but I’m a bit worried about spendin’ too much.

… honestly, the leg day nearly finished me. I think I saw stars for a good five minutes afterwards. Did  you  manage to get a good session in? You were looking particularly motivated when we started warming up. Oh, yeah, it was good! I switched it up, did a bit more upper body, trying to actually build some definition. It's going okay, though I’m still rubbish at pull-ups. Honestly, it’s humiliating. I just dangle there like a particularly pathetic sloth. How’s your training going overall? Are you still aiming for that half marathon? Sloth is a good description! I’m trying to mix it up too, less weights, more cardio because of the half marathon, yeah. I’m officially…terrified. It feels so far away still, even though it's in October. I’m doing a 10k next month as a practice run. Fancy joining? It's out near Grantchester. Oh, Grantchester! Lovely. Tempting, really tempting. But I’m supposed to be going away for a long weekend with some of the girls from work. It’s a health and wellness retreat…ironic, considering we’ll probably spend half the time in the spa bar! It’s in the Cotswolds. A spa bar? That sounds…perfectly balanced, actually. Health  and  wellness. Honestly, you Bupa lot always seem to have the best work perks. We just get a slightly discounted coffee machine in the office. It's not  always  glamorous, believe me. Lots of data analysis and endless meetings about preventative healthcare. It’s draining. Though, the retreat is a nice perk. What about you? Any holiday plans on the horizon? You mentioned wanting to go backpacking last time we spoke. Yeah, still planning it, just trying to figure out the logistics. Thailand is top of the list, but flights are insane at the moment. I’ve been looking at Vietnam as an alternative. It’s a bit cheaper, and apparently the food is amazing. Speaking of which, this peri-peri chicken is saving my life right now. Vietnam! Good shout. I’ve heard the same thing about the food. You absolutely have to try the pho. And you're right about flights – it’s a nightmare. I was looking at going to Greece with my sister in September, and even just a week’s stay is costing a fortune. It's ridiculous, isn't it? Makes you wonder if staying at home and watching Netflix is the sensible option.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of paperwork is astonishing. They’re sending me three copies of everything, all demanding different things. It’s like they actively  want  to make it difficult. This new housing management company is just… appalling. Old Mrs. Higgins had a leak, reported it three times, and they finally sent someone who said it wasn’t their responsibility! My dear Penelope, landlords. Always the same story, regardless of the century. Though I daresay, back in my day, a firm letter from a solicitor got things moving. Nowadays, it’s all ‘procedure’ and ‘compliance’. Utter nonsense. Speaking of nonsense, did you see that the Chichester spire is still… well, not entirely upright? Oh, dreadful! I read something about that. Apparently, it was that Porden chap, wasn't it? A very ambitious design, but… fundamentally flawed? I can’t imagine the cost of repairs. Though, you know, looking at the photos, it almost looks… graceful, leaning like that. Graceful disaster is more like it! Porden was a genius, undoubtedly, but a rather eccentric one. I was reading about him, actually, while researching for the book. It’s coming along, slowly but surely. The British Library has been invaluable, even though finding a quiet corner is a battle in itself. The book! How  is  it progressing? Still on Philip and Mary? I remember you mentioning the Spanish archives. Were they helpful? Remarkably so. The Escorial, in particular. They have everything. Though you need patience. And a good command of archaic Spanish, naturally. I rather suspect Philip genuinely adored Mary, you know. It wasn’t purely a political match. The archives contain such fascinating correspondence... reveals a vulnerable side to him most historians miss. Though, getting access to  everything  was a trial. Bureaucrats, Penelope, bureaucrats! Even the Spanish aren't immune. Sounds exhausting. Still, fascinating stuff. It reminds me, though, we were talking about little Thomas. Eliza keeps sending photos – he’s already got a grip like a vice, apparently! She’s thinking of having him christened in Nice. Nice? Goodness. Born abroad, is he? That changes things. Well, she met Jean-Pierre when she was teaching in Marseille, didn't she? And they've built such a lovely life there. But I was saying to her, a christening in Nice… it feels rather… detached from everything. Detached? Perhaps. But France is surprisingly… robust. People underestimate them. I’ve spent some time in Provence, you know.

… honestly, Mr. Davies is taking the  mickey . Three essays on the Industrial Revolution? Over the weekend?! It’s a joke, isn’t it? Tell me about it. He thinks we have nothing better to do. At least we’re here, stuffing our faces with these… what  are  these, actually? They’re good. Spring rolls, mate. Your mum orders them every time. You’ve had, like, five already. You’ll be square. I'm building up strength for the essay marathon. It’s tactical eating. Besides, my mum loves this place. Says it reminds her of when she used to come here with  her  mum. All that generational stuff. My grandma hates Chinese food. Says it all tastes the same. She’s very… opinionated. Last week she tried to tell me off for wearing black shoes. Black shoes! Like it's a crime against fashion. Seriously? Your grandma’s a character, yeah? Mine just knits. Constantly. I swear she’s trying to knit a full-sized replica of the house. That's dedication. Speaking of dedication, anyone seen Leo lately? He’s gone completely off-grid since Tuesday. Didn't even turn up for Warhammer club. That’s  serious . He said something about his parents putting him on a ‘diet’. Apparently, he was ‘consuming too much sugar’. Can you believe it? Leo? Dieting? The man lives on Monster Energy and biscuits. A diet? That's harsh. His mum’s always going on about healthy eating though. Remember that time she brought kale chips to our gaming night? Kale  chips ! Oh god, the kale chip incident. That was… traumatic. They tasted like sadness. He tried to hide them under the sofa, but his little sister ratted him out. Serves him right for trying to sneak biscuits past her. He's a terrible liar. Though, I feel for the bloke. No biscuits is a sad life. I saw him looking at a comics shop window yesterday, looking  proper  mournful. Said he couldn't even enjoy browsing because his blood sugar was low. He needs to rebel. A proper biscuit-based rebellion. We should stage an intervention. Bring him a care package – biscuits, fizzy drinks, maybe a new graphic novel. Actually, that’s a pretty good idea. I’ve got that new  Daredevil  comic, the one we were talking about. I could lend it to him. It's got some seriously cool artwork. I'm in.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of ‘Happy Birthday’ banners they have now! It's ridiculous. Everything has to be themed, doesn't it? Jonathan just wants a quiet afternoon with cake, not a full-blown superhero invasion. Oh, you’re right, dear. Everything’s branded these days. Used to be, a bit of ribbon and a few balloons would do. Now it's all licensed characters and flashing lights. Makes your head spin. I remember when your father… well, never mind. It's different times. Dad, you’re veering off into reminiscence again. Though you’re right about the branding. It's relentless. I tried to find a simple 'Happy Birthday' card yesterday, and everything was covered in glitter or cartoon animals. It's exhausting just  shopping  for a birthday. Glitter gets  everywhere . It's the worst. Aye, glitter is the devil’s dust. I’m still finding it from little Emily’s fifth birthday, years ago! We're lucky Jonathan isn't fussed about all that nonsense. A good Victoria sponge is all he needs, isn't it? Absolutely. I’ve already ordered one from Mrs. Higgins down the street. She makes the best. It’s practically a tradition. Though, she  did  try to upsell me on a personalised iced message. I said no, thank you. Good for you, love. It's the principle of the thing! Everything is trying to cost you more. Still, the house feels… empty. Now that we’re thinking about Jonathan’s party, it highlights how much we’ve cleared out. It does, doesn’t it? It’s freeing, though. After all those years of accumulated…stuff. Though I miss the study, a bit. Finding space for my writing is proving tricky in here. You could use the spare room, John. It’s not ideal, but it’s quiet enough. And honestly, you had  mountains  of books in that study. We were practically building a fortress! Can I have the spare room computer when you’re finished with it? Mine’s really slow, and I need it for my history project. It takes ages to load websites. That young man needs a decent computer. It's no good him wanting to learn if he's frustrated by slow technology. What's your school saying about that, lad? They said they might get some new ones next year… maybe. It's not very helpful when I have a deadline next month.

… honestly, I just don’t  get  why everyone’s so stressed about picking their GCSEs already. It’s ages away! Like, we’ve barely even started Year 9. Ages away?! Lila, it's practically now! Mrs. Davison was going on about deadlines and options forms in assembly this morning. My mum's already making a spreadsheet. A  spreadsheet ! It’s terrifying. What are  you  thinking of taking? Ugh, don’t remind me about spreadsheets. My dad tried to do one for my clarinet practice schedule. It lasted about a day. And I… I’m leaning towards the usuals, I guess. English Lit is non-negotiable, obviously. And probably History, I’m alright at that. But then it gets tricky. Same! English is a given. I'm thinking History too, actually. But then I was toying with the idea of doing Triple Science. Everyone says it looks good for… well, everything, really. Even just if you don’t want to be a scientist. Triple Science is  hard  though, isn’t it? And loads more work. I’d rather not spend all my free time in the lab. I was thinking maybe Geography? It’s a bit more… visual? And less memorising. Geography’s good. Though Mr. Henderson is a bit… intense. Remember when he went on for like, twenty minutes about bog ecosystems? Oh god, yes! He’s obsessed with bogs. Honestly, he makes them sound fascinating, but still. Bogs! I'd rather watch Emma Chamberlain on YouTube. Have you seen her latest vlog? She went to that pottery thing. Ooh, no! I’ve been catching up on Saffron Barker’s stuff. She’s doing really well, isn’t she? Started as a vlogger and now she’s got her own makeup brand. That’s a proper job, though. Not like… I don’t know, what does my uncle even  do ? Something with spreadsheets, probably. Exactly! Being a YouTuber actually sounds… achievable. I mean, I’m not planning on quitting school or anything, but it’s more realistic than being, like, a world-famous violinist. Or an astronaut. Although, have you seen that new documentary about Tim Peake? It’s amazing. Tim Peake’s cool. But space is terrifying. I think I'd prefer something a bit more down to earth. Like… maybe something in fashion? Or, and this is a really silly idea, but a food blogger? A food blogger! That’s actually a brilliant idea!

…and honestly, I still reckon they’ve built that roundabout all wrong. Utterly wrong. Never seen so much congestion, even for Norwich. They should’ve gone for a proper flyover, y'know? Back in my day, we  knew  how to design a road. Proper calculations, not this computer modelling nonsense.      Now, Arthur, you always say that about new roundabouts. Remember the one on the A47 at Attleborough? You predicted the end of civilisation as we knew it!      Well, didn't it cause chaos for months? Months, I tell you! And now this one, near the hospital… a complete mess. It's all these young 'uns, fiddling with their computers, no practical experience.      Actually, Dad, the modelling isn’t  instead  of practical experience, it’s used  with  it. It lets them simulate traffic flow and test different designs before a single brick is laid. It’s quite sophisticated. I teach some of it, funnily enough.      Sophisticated is one word for it, dear. Complicated is another. I can barely work my email, let alone “simulate traffic flow”. Though, speaking of complicated, have you seen the birds in your garden lately, Eleanor? There’s a little fella, bright yellow, keeps coming to my bird feeder. I haven't a clue what it is.      Oh, that’ll probably be a Yellowhammer. They're becoming more common again, thankfully. We’re seeing a slight recovery in farmland bird populations.      Yellowhammer, is it? Funny names they give 'em. Used to be you'd see flocks of 'em in Costessey fields, used to. Not so much now, though. All built over, see? That’s the trouble with progress, innit? Always something lost. Reminds me of old man Hemmings’ orchard… gone, all gone. Built houses on it.      Hemmings… now there was a character. Sold the best plums in Norfolk, he did. Juicy as anything. Knew a thing or two about grafting as well, apparently. I remember helping him clear some drainage ditches once, back when I was a student. Proper land drainage, using gravity – none of this pumped nonsense. That’s what they should be doing to prevent the flooding, instead of slapping up concrete barriers everywhere.      Oh, don't get started on the flooding, Arthur. My poor neighbour, Mrs. Peterson, had water right through her kitchen last winter. Dreadful. She’s still trying to get the insurance sorted.      It’s a systemic problem, isn’t it? Poor planning, inadequate infrastructure… and increasingly unpredictable weather patterns.

…and honestly, the state of it now, mind you. They’ve changed the whole uniform again. Little Timmy’s got to have a navy blue jumper, not royal blue like last year, apparently. Royal blue is  out . Honestly, what's the point? It's just a waste of good money, that is. My Dorothy, she went to Costessey High, back in the… oh, must be sixty years ago now. We had a uniform, alright, but it lasted! Simple grey skirts and a white blouse. None of this fuss. Oh, don’t get me started on school uniforms! I had three go through Northolt High. The expense! And the complaints! “It’s itchy, Mum!” “Everyone else has the trainers!” Honestly, you’d think they were going to the opera, not primary school. Though, I did have one little rascal who managed to dye his white shirt pink with beetroot juice. That caused a stir! Beetroot juice, eh? That’s a good one! We had a boy in my class once who tried to convince the teachers his arse was permanently stuck to the chair. Said it was a medical condition. Absolute chaos. Kids are brilliant, aren’t they? Though, dealing with parents nowadays... that's a different story. It’s all “my little angel can do no wrong.” They’re all too soft, that’s what they are. Back in my day, a clip round the ear was enough to sort things out. Not that I ever  had  to give one, mind! My Mum was good at that. Though, I do worry about young Timmy. He's a bit… delicate. Keeps complaining about a tummy ache. Probably just wants to avoid homework. Oh, tummy aches are the classic! Perfect excuse. Though, you’re right, things are different now. Everything’s a ‘condition’ or a ‘sensitivity’. Remember when we just got on with it? I was weeding the garden yesterday and nearly had a hernia, but you don't go running to the doctor for  that ! Speaking of doctors, I had a check-up last week. The waiting times are just ridiculous. Sat there for two hours just to be told my blood pressure was slightly elevated and I should cut down on caffeine. As if I didn’t know that already! I tell you what, the NHS is creaking at the seams. Creaking is an understatement! Old Mrs. Higgins down the road waited six months for a hip replacement.

… honestly, I just don’t get the point of a stag do in Blackpool. It's naff, isn’t it? Proper naff. Mark deserves better than hen parties and dodgy arcades. Harsh, love, harsh! He  did  choose it, you know. Apparently, Kev from work organised it and it's all based around a specific… attraction. I won’t go into details. Oh,  please  do. I need to know the depths of this depravity. Blackpool… Honestly, it's a world away from the Lakes, isn’t it? We could have suggested the Lakes. Proper scenery. A bit of hiking. You know, something slightly more… refined. He said Kev’s gone all out. It’s themed. Apparently, there's a "mission" involving inflatable weaponry. Look, it’s not my cup of tea either, but he's excited. He’s already stressing about the costumes. And Carol’s hen do is apparently going to be a 'glamping' weekend with a cocktail-making class. Very different vibes. Glamping? Sounds exhausting. So much  effort . Honestly, sometimes I just wanna stay in and watch  Come Dine With Me . Remember that bloke who tried to make a soufflé? Absolute chaos. Pure gold. Oh God, yes! And the passive-aggressive scoring! It’s addictive. Anyway, focusing on more important things... this snow is ridiculous, isn't it? It was beautiful this morning, proper postcard stuff, but now it’s just turning to slush. The garden’s going to be a swamp. It is a right mess. I was hoping to get the raised beds finished this weekend. I ordered all the wood last week, but it's just lying there getting soaked. I was planning to start the seedlings indoors, but I haven’t even got round to ordering the seeds yet. I’ve been meaning to get those alpine strawberries, the ones Old Man Hemmings swears by. You and your gardening. You're going to have the best little garden in Cambridge. I'm hopeless. I kill cacti. I’m seriously considering just paving the whole thing over. Don’t you dare! You need some greenery in your life. Besides, think of the bees! We need to do our bit for the pollinators. Speaking of doing our bit, have you booked anything for our holiday yet? We talked about Portugal, didn't we? I’ve been having a look. The Algarve’s looking pricey, especially with it being half term.

…No, no, I’m tellin’ ya, margarine just ain’t the same. Never ‘as been. My mum, she’d ‘ave a right go at anyone tryin’ to put that stuff on ‘er bread. Real butter, that's what built us all strong, didn't it? Proper Norfolk butter, from Old Man Hemmings’ farm, mind. You don’t get that now, do ya? Everything’s imported. Oh, Harold, you and your butter! Honestly, you’ve been saying that since I met you, fifty years ago! I used margarine for years when the children were little. Couldn’t afford butter every day. It did the job, and they turned out alright, didn't they? We did, Mum. And you made fantastic fairy cakes with it, I remember. Though I do appreciate a good knob of butter on a hot cross bun now. It's a generational thing, I think. Different priorities. It's interesting, actually, thinking about food and how much it’s changed. We were talking about it with students today. The rise of ‘foodie’ culture, the demand for provenance… it's a sign of the times, isn't it? People wanting to know where their food comes from. Provenance? Is that what they call it now? Back in my day, you just  knew . You knew Farmer Giles, you knew his cows, you knew ‘ow he treated ‘em. Nowadays, you get a plastic tub and a label sayin’ "Produced in Europe" and that’s yer lot. No trust. He’s got a point, actually. It’s all so impersonal. And expensive! Remember when a pint of milk cost next to nothing? Now… well, you wouldn’t believe it. Still, this roast is lovely, Anon. You’ve done yourself proud. Thank you, Mum. I tried to do it as Dad would have, a proper Sunday roast. Yorkshire puddings are… a work in progress, admittedly. They're good! A bit denser than some, but they've got amazing flavour. And the gravy is spot on. You’ve clearly been taking notes during Dad’s masterclasses. Masterclasses, eh? More like standin’ in the kitchen watchin’ me while I got on with it! Always ’ad a nose for gravy, I did. Secret ingredient? A little bit of Worcestershire sauce. Don’t tell anyone. Oh, Harold. Everyone knows that already! You’ve been adding Worcestershire sauce to gravy for seventy years. It's practically a family heirloom.

… honestly, the butternut squash risotto was a disaster. Utterly mushy. I think I overcooked the rice  and  the squash. It was meant to be a nice autumnal thing, you know? Instagrammable. It wasn’t. Sounds about right. You’re a whiz with spreadsheets, Liv, not soufflés. I’m perfectly happy with a good spag bol, myself. Less chance of ending up with beige mush. Aye, beige is good. Reliable. You don’t want fancy when you’ve had a long day. Though, your Mam’s roast is always a winner, isn’t it? That gravy… now  that’s  Instagrammable. The gravy  is  exceptional. She’s always been a good cook, your mother. Remember the trifle she made for my birthday, back in…oh, must be thirty years ago now? Layers and layers of it. Took her all day. Trifle! Now  that’s  a proper pudding. None of this fancy mousse stuff. A good sponge, plenty of fruit, lashings of custard… and sherry, of course. Important the sherry. Grandad, you always make sure the sherry is mentioned. It’s a vital ingredient, apparently. Mum, you really shouldn’t have bothered with three desserts. We’ve already had the apple crumble! Don’t you worry about your Mam. She likes lookin’ after folks. Always has. Remember when I broke my arm, all those years ago? She was round every day with a pot of soup. Couldn't do enough. It's true. She’s a legend. Though, I also remember her trying to teach me to knit… that was less legendary. I ended up with a very wonky scarf. She tried to teach me too. Didn’t go well. My fingers just weren’t… nimble enough. I always preferred building things. Houses, mostly. Funny thing, houses. Used to be you could rely on a good solid build. Now… they’re all flimsy. That’s a bit harsh, Dad. They have to meet different regulations now, energy efficiency and all that. It's not just about brick and mortar. Regulations, bah! It’s about cutting corners. I was talking to old Mr. Henderson down the street, he’s a builder, you know. He says they’re using particle board where they used to use oak. Particle board! It'll crumble in a decade. Used to be, you built a house to last a lifetime. My father built our house, you know. With his own two hands.

…and honestly, the whole thing just blew up. Overnight. Three million views. It was a bloke attempting to parallel park a caravan. Utterly hopeless. The commentary was the gold though, just this deadpan Aussie narration. It reminded me a bit of those early Dollar Shave Club videos, you know? Simple, funny, relatable. Oh, I saw that one! It  was  brilliantly bad. You’re always finding these things. But we were talking about applying that… that viral-ability, I suppose, to something more substantial. Back to the uni stuff. How do we make ‘Critical Thinking’ actually  critical  and not just another lecture series students sleep through? Right. And that's where I was thinking the ‘problem-solving sprints’ idea could really work. Forget essays for a week. Give them a real-world, messy problem – like a struggling small business needing a turnaround plan. Something tangible. I like the 'real-world' aspect. My lot at the school are always saying the disconnect between theory and practice is huge. But a whole week? Won’t that disrupt the curriculum too much? The module leaders will have kittens. Disruption is the point! Look, I built a company on disrupting things. A little controlled chaos is healthy. We could scale it down to three days, but the key is immersion. They form small teams, maybe mentor them with actual entrepreneurs – you know, get someone like old Man Henderson from down the road who started that surf shop empire. Henderson? He wouldn't know a pedagogical approach if it bit him on the ankle. Though, I suppose the practical insight would be valuable. What about assessment? It feels… tricky. It's not something neatly quantifiable like an exam. Exactly! That’s the point. We ditch the traditional assessment. They present their solution - a pitch, a business plan, whatever feels appropriate – to a panel. The panel isn't grading technical correctness, it’s assessing their  process . How did they identify the real problem? How did they collaborate? How adaptable were they when things inevitably went wrong? That's where the critical thinking shines through. It's about the journey, not just the destination. Hmm. Okay, I'm warming to this. It’s certainly a departure from the norm. Though I'm envisioning a lot of students panicking when faced with something genuinely ambiguous. They're so used to being told exactly what to do. Then that’s part of the learning!

… honestly, the deadline for the Henderson report is just looming. It’s all spreadsheets and risk assessments. Thrilling, isn’t it? I swear, if I see another Gantt chart I’m going to scream. Sounds…fun. You say that like you've aged ten years in the last week. You need a proper weekend. Not just collapsing on the sofa with Netflix. Easier said than done. I feel like I’m constantly playing catch-up. Though, I  was  thinking about that Halloween party Amelia’s throwing? Fancy it? Apparently, she’s going all out. Ooh, Amelia’s parties are legendary. Is it a costume thing? I’m rubbish at costumes. Last year I just went as ‘a tired nurse’ which isn’t exactly inventive, is it? That’s…accurate, actually. Amelia said themed – ‘haunted English counties’. Which is ridiculous, but apparently she’s determined. Haunted English counties?! What even  is  that? Is she expecting people to dress as, like, spooky versions of Norfolk? Exactly! I’ve been trying to think of something. I was considering Dorset – dramatic cliffs, maybe some ghostly smugglers? But it feels a bit…weak. Hmm. Maybe something from Yorkshire? The Moors are creepy enough as it is. You could do a Bronte sister, all windswept and mysterious. Ooh, that's actually brilliant! Okay, Yorkshire it is. You’re much better at this than me. What about you? Any costume ideas? I haven’t even  thought  about it. Work’s been…intense. We had a really difficult case this week, a young lad struggling with some serious stuff. It just stays with you, you know? Makes spreadsheets seem pretty trivial. I can imagine. That must be exhausting. It’s good you’re able to talk about it. You always handle things with such grace. That Masters you did clearly paid off, you’re so good at understanding people. Thanks. It helps, but it doesn’t make it easy. It makes you think, though, doesn't it? About what you actually  want  to be doing. I've been doing some thinking lately... actually. Oh? Do tell! Spill. Are you plotting a grand escape from the NHS? Not quite. But I was thinking about specialising. Maybe forensic mental health. It’s a long road - more qualifications, obviously - but it feels…right. What about you? Five-year plan? Still aiming for Project Manager extraordinaire? That was the plan. Honestly? I’m starting to question it.

…and honestly, the price of a loaf of bread these days! It’s highway robbery, I tell ya. Highway robbery. Back in my day, a good white sliced would be, what, ten pence? Maybe twelve? Now it’s… well, I don’t even  look  anymore. Leo tells me, and I nearly choked on my tea. Yeah, it’s mental, isn’t it? Everything’s gone up. Even oat milk, which feels unnecessarily expensive for…well, water and oats. It’s the global situation, Mum. All that stuff happening over in Ukraine, the cost of fuel…it all filters down eventually. Global situation, bah! They always blame a ‘global situation’. It’s just greed, plain and simple. They see what they can get away with. Remember Mr. Henderson at the corner shop? He wouldn’t  dream  of charging that much, even when petrol was going up in the seventies. He was a good man, Mr. Henderson. Gave us credit when your dad lost his job at the factory. I've heard stories about Mr. Henderson. Sounds lovely. But things are different now, aren’t they? It’s all corporate, everything’s about profit margins. That’s what they teach you in uni, anyway. All those presentations about ‘optimising streams of revenue’… makes my eyes glaze over. Uni, eh? Still can’t get my head around you doing a Master’s. All that studying. What’s it even  for ? You’re a Production Controller, aren’t you? Sounds important. It is important, actually. It’s a lot of project management, making sure everything runs smoothly in the factory, hitting deadlines, managing the budget… all that fun stuff.
