Gets your heart racing. You're more of a slow burn kinda gal, aren’t ya? I suppose I am. I like films that stay with you, that make you  think  afterwards. ‘The Witch’ was brilliant for that. The feeling of isolation, the religious fanaticism… it was really disturbing. And the goat. Don’t even get me started on the goat. That goat  was  unsettling. Right creepy looking thing. See, I went through a phase of loving those Japanese horror films – ‘The Ring’, ‘The Grudge’. But they all started to feel a bit…samey after a while. Long-haired ghost, creepy well, repeat. They do lean heavily on certain tropes, don’t they? Although I thought ‘Ringu’ was genuinely terrifying the first time I saw it. The idea of a cursed videotape…very 90s, but still effective! Have you seen 'Relic'? 'Relic'? No, not ringing any bells. What’s it about? It's about dementia, actually. But it's done as a horror film. It’s about a daughter returning home to look after her mum, who’s starting to disappear… and the house is reflecting that. It's really cleverly done. It’s not about jump scares, it’s about the slow erosion of a person, and the fear of losing someone.

…and honestly, the reviews were  brilliant . Everyone said the host was so responsive, and the photos didn’t even do the place justice. It’s just… I’m still a little hesitant about Airbnb, you know? Feels a bit… invasive, somehow. Letting strangers into a home. Invasive, you say? Oh, pooh. In  my  day, we’d have invited them in for a cup of tea and a biscuit and asked after their family. Things were simpler then. Though, I suppose opening your home to folks you’ve only ‘met’ through a… a glowing rectangle… is different. Exactly! A glowing rectangle. And all the security stuff. I was reading about a woman who found a hidden camera. It put me right off. Though, Devon’s generally pretty safe. We’re thinking of using it for Auntie Carol’s visit in June. She doesn't do stairs anymore, and your spare room… well, you know. Carol, bless her. Always a good laugh, that one. Stairs  are  a bother, aren't they? Though I climbed plenty in Wolverhampton as a lad. Used to run up and down those hills like a mountain goat. No, no, an Airbnb sounds sensible for Carol. Better than her struggling with the stairs. Though I do miss having a full house. I know. It’s quiet now, isn't it? Though, quiet is good sometimes. I just ordered a new iPad, actually. The old one was on its last legs. It was so slow, even checking emails was a pain. An iPad? What on earth for? You’ve got a perfectly good computer, haven’t you? All these gadgets. I still struggle with the television remote. Keeps changing channels on its own. It’s possessed, I tell you. Possessed! It's probably just the batteries, Grandad. And the iPad’s for work, mostly. Marking essays, lesson planning… and a bit of Netflix. Speaking of which, I was thinking we could order a pizza tomorrow night? We haven’t had one in ages. Pizza! Now  that’s  a good idea. Pepperoni, if you don’t mind. And a nice garlic bread. Though, I do worry about those delivery drivers whizzing about. They drive like they’re escaping a fire. Pepperoni it is! I’ll order it early to avoid the rush. You’ve been pretty quiet today, haven’t you? What have you been up to? Just…thinking. About your Grandmother, mostly.

…Aye, so that's why I’m sayin’, the descriptions o’ Patagonia, right? It’s nae just the mountains, though they’re spectacular, it's how Chatwin writes  around  them. He focuses on the silence, the emptiness, the way the light hits the rock…It’s almost poetic, y’know? Did ye ever get roon’ tae readin’ ‘In Patagonia’? Ach, I started it, years ago. Got distracted, as ye do. University marking, then the bairns came along…it ended up on the 'to be revisited’ pile, which is essentially a polite way of sayin' I’ll probably nae get roon’ tae it. But yer description makes me think I really  should . Is it as… atmospheric as people say? I’ve seen some photos, and it looks breathtaking, but photos can be deceivin’. Deceivin’ is an understatement. Photos don’t capture the  scale  of the place. And Chatwin… he just gets under the skin of it. It’s no’ about conquerin’ a mountain, it's about bein’  in  the landscape, absorbed by it. It reminded me, strangely enough, of some of the more remote bits we saw in Iceland. Remember that drive across the lava fields? Oh, aye, the one where we practically met naeone for five hours? That was otherworldly. Felt like we were on another planet. Though Iceland had a…brightness to it, even in its starkness. Patagonia sounds…more melancholic? That’s a good word for it. Melancholic. It’s a loneliness, but a beautiful loneliness. Like a sort o’ acceptance o’ yer own smallness, ye ken? It made me think about Robert Macfarlane’s work, too. Have ye read ‘Landmarks’? Absolutely. Brilliant stuff. Macfarlane does that thing o’ weaving mythology and personal experience wi’ the natural world. He's almost a modern-day nanoline writer, isn't he? Bringing back that connection to place. Though, I've always found his writing a little… studied, maybe? Chatwin feels more…raw. That’s a fair point. Macfarlane's definitely more academic, a wee bit more self-aware o' his own role as observer. Chatwin just sort of  disappears  into the landscape. Speaking o’ disappearing, I was thinkin' about that book on the lost cities of the Amazon ye were readin' recently. Did ye finish it? I did! David Grann’s ‘The Lost City of Z’? Fascinating, but deeply frustrating. The obsessive nature o' Percival Fawcett…it’s a classic tale o’ romanticism and hubris.

…and honestly, the sheer scale of it is a bit terrifying. It’s a competition, you see, to redesign a section of the South Bank. Like,  the  South Bank. With real potential to actually  be  built. Oh, love. That  is  big. Right, so, you’ve sent off your initial portfolio then? The sketches and the bit of your dissertation? Yeah, that went last week. This is the next stage. They’ve shortlisted fifty applicants, and they want a detailed proposal. Not just pretty pictures, Mum, but actual calculations, feasibility studies… the works. It's expecting a four week turnaround. Four weeks! That’s… intense. You’re still holding down the part-time at the cafe, aren't you? I’ve cut my hours back. Thankfully, Leo’s been amazing, covering some of my shifts. But even so, it’s… a lot. I’m practically living on coffee and adrenaline. I just keep thinking, if I  could  win this, it would completely change things. Proper springboard for my career. Of course it would, darling. And you’re more than capable. You always were the artistic one. Remember when you used to build those incredibly elaborate castles out of Lego? They weren’t just castles, they were  fortresses . Mum, that was when I was seven. This is a bit different. This is real-world pressure. And I’m worrying I’m biting off more than I can chew. I was explaining the structural load calculations to Gran earlier and her eyes just glazed over. I think she thought I was speaking Martian. Gran hasn’t understood a technical explanation in her life, love! Don’t measure your success by her comprehension. What specifically is causing you the most stress? Is it the competition itself, or the sheer volume of work? It’s a bit of both, I think. The competition is obviously scary – the other applicants will be phenomenal. But it’s the feeling of being constantly behind. Every time I think I’ve made progress, I realise there’s three more things I need to research. And I feel awful, because I promised I'd help Dad with fixing the guttering this weekend. Oh, darling. That's where you need to learn to say no. Your father will understand. He's proud of you, he really is. He'll grumble, naturally, he  is  your father, but he’ll understand. Tell him you’re up against a deadline, you can help next weekend.

…No, no, I’m tellin’ ya, the price of petrol nowadays is scandalous. Scandalous! Reminds me of the ‘73 crisis, queues ‘round the block, though then it was all about the Arabs, wasn’t it? Now it’s… well, who  is  it now, exactly? Seems like everyone’s got a hand in it, squeezin’ folks. Arabs, eh, Arthur? You always did have a good memory for that sort of thing. Though I reckon it’s more to do with taxes, than anything else. The government, always lookin’ for another way to fill their pockets. Don't get me started on Council Tax, either. Robbery, pure and simple. Oh, don’t you two  start  on finances. It’ll bring the whole room down. Lovely to see you both, by the way. It’s been ages. How are things with the roof, Arthur? Still leakin’ when it rains cats and dogs? Still leakin’, Brenda. Still leakin’. Tried patchin’ it up meself, used that stuff you get in a tube, doesn’t stick for toffee. I really should get someone in, but… well, you know. Retirement don’t stretch to roofers, does it? Used to design bridges, I did, massive concrete structures. Couldn’t fix a bleedin' tile now, though. The irony. He’s a clever man, that Arthur. Used to be. Remember when he was workin’ on that road scheme out near Attleborough? Talked about load-bearing and whatnot. Sounded like another language to me. That was years ago, George. Ancient history. And it weren’t  that  clever, just applyin’ principles, really. What about you, George? Still keepin’ busy with the garden? I saw old Mrs. Higgins the other day, she says your tomatoes are legendary. Aye, the tomatoes are doin’ alright. Though the slugs are havin’ a field day. It’s a constant battle, I tell ya. And young David, me grandson, he’s talkin’ about tradin' in his car. Wants one of them electric things. Oh, electric cars! They're lovely, but so expensive, aren't they? And where’s he going to charge it, living in a flat? It’s all very well for people with driveways. This housing situation is a nightmare. No one can afford to buy anything decent, and the rentals are extortionate. My granddaughter, Sarah, she's saving and saving, but it feels hopeless. Hopeless is right. Back in my day, a decent house was within reach.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of bags people are leaving in the art room is becoming ridiculous. It's not a cloakroom, David! We’re supposed to be offering space for  creation , not storage. It's blocking access to the easels, and frankly, it looks terribly untidy. Right, yeah, I saw a bit of a build-up last week. It’s always worse on Tuesdays and Thursdays with the life drawing classes, isn’t it? Ms. Davies brings a whole kit and caboodle, apparently. Ms. Davies is lovely, truly, but a hoarder! We need to gently but firmly address it. Perhaps a notice? “Personal belongings at owner’s risk, limited storage available.” Something polite, yet pointed. It ties into the bigger picture, though, doesn’t it? We  really  need that storage sorted. Remember we talked about converting the old stationery room? Yeah, that’s still on my list. I got a quote from a local builder, Kevin, just down the road. He reckons he can knock through to the corridor and put in some proper shelving for around £800. Seems reasonable. We need to justify it to the board, though. “Improving user experience” is always a good angle. Excellent. And link it to generating income. If we can offer secure storage alongside the room rentals, we can increase the daily rate. We're practically giving the space away sometimes, David. The yoga studio is booming, but barely covering costs. True. And speaking of bookings, the community choir have requested the hall every Wednesday evening in November. They’re a good bunch, always tidy up, but it means the pottery class has to shift. I’ve emailed Mrs. Peterson, but haven’t heard back yet. Pottery has priority, surely? They’ve been with us for years. Gently remind Mrs. Peterson – she’s a little vague sometimes. And we need to get better at showcasing what we offer. I've been thinking about a proper marketing push. Social media…perhaps a leaflet drop locally? I've been dabbling with Instagram, posting pictures of the artwork from the classes. Gets a few likes, nothing major. A leaflet drop’s a good shout, though. I know a graphic design student at Lambeth College, might be able to do a good deal. She owes me a favour – helped her dad fix the fire alarm here last year. Speaking of which, have you checked the fire escape routes recently?

…and honestly, this is almost as good as my Nana used to make. Almost. Though, hers had a secret ingredient – a tiny splash of brandy. Don't tell anyone, it's a family secret!      Brandy, eh? No wonder it tasted good! My Nain never put brandy in hers, just a ridiculous amount of cinnamon. You could smell it three streets away. This is lovely though, genuinely. You’ve outdone yourself, Bethan.      Yeah, seriously good. Proper comfort food. And after that hike this morning, comfort is  exactly  what’s needed. Though, I’m still convinced you’ve snuck some magic into it. You always were a dab hand in the kitchen.      It  is  very good. The pastry’s just the right level of crumbly. You’ve improved since the last time, Bethan. No offence.      Oh, now, Rhys, don’t be like that! She makes a cracking pie! Always has. Remember that one she made for the village fete, and old Mr. Davies nearly bought the whole thing himself?      Oh, God, Mr. Davies. He said it reminded him of his mother’s. That was…flattering, and slightly terrifying. I’m just glad everyone’s enjoying it. I was worried about sourcing good apples down here. Everything's different to Cape Town, even the fruit.      Apples were always good in Herefordshire, you know. Prime growing country. My father - he was a botanist, spent time here studying the orchards. He always said the soil was special. Though, to be honest, I’ve spent so long eating rice and noodles in Singapore, a good apple feels like a luxury!      Rice and noodles in Singapore! You’ve been showing off your global lifestyle again, Dai? We all know you still secretly crave a bara brith and a proper cup of tea.      Never deny a Welshman his tea! Though, a good Laksa does have its merits. Still, this pie’s beating it hands down. So, Bethan, any plans for tomorrow's feast? Are we thinking roast?      Roast would be good. I could tackle the potatoes. I do a mean roastie, you know? All crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside. I’ve been experimenting with duck fat…      Duck fat! Now you’re talking. Yes, roast sounds lovely. I’m happy to do the meat, maybe a chicken? Keeps things relatively simple. And we  must  have Yorkshire puddings. Rhys, you’re on Yorkshire pudding duty.      Yorkshire puddings. The bane of my existence.

… honestly, I just think Birmingham’s massively underrated. Everyone always goes on about London, Manchester, even Leeds gets a look-in, but Birmingham’s got  character . And the Balti Triangle? Forget about it. Proper good curry. Right, the Balti Triangle. You and your food pilgrimages. It  is  good, I’ll give you that. But underrated? I don’t know. It just feels… grey. Like a concrete jungle. Doesn’t have the vibrancy of somewhere like, I dunno, Bristol. Grey?! That's harsh, man! It’s got canals, street art… it's properly bouncing now. Remember when we went down for Sarah’s graduation? The Mailbox was buzzing. And honestly, Bristol’s just  expensive . Everything’s overpriced for what it is. Okay, fair point about the price. London is criminal. Speaking of Sarah, how’s she doing? Haven’t spoken to her properly in ages. Last I heard, she was proper stressed about this new project at work. She’s good, she’s good. Still stressed, naturally, she’s  always  stressed. But she landed the project, which is a win. She’s heading to Cornwall next week with Ben for a bit of a break. They were moaning about trying to find a decent AirBnB that wasn’t charging the earth. Cornwall’s lovely, though. Went there with my family when I was a kid. Building sandcastles, freezing cold water… good times. Speaking of holidays, are we still on for the Lake District in October? I need to book the cottage. Oh aye, definitely. October’s perfect. Boots on, bracing wind, proper autumnal vibes. Find one with a fireplace, yeah? I’m picturing massive mugs of hot chocolate and board games. Got it. Fireplace is non-negotiable. I saw a really good one near Keswick, looked ideal. Did you see that advert on TV last night? The one with the… what were they selling, dog food? Oh God, the one with the talking bulldog? Awful. Absolutely awful. So cringey. Honestly, adverts these days… they’re trying too hard. Remember that Irn-Bru one with the guys building a snowman out of empty cans? Now  that  was a good advert. Oh yeah! ‘Made in Scotland from girders!’ Classic. Actually, talking of weird adverts, have you seen the new one for that car, the… I think it’s a Korean one? It's all about challenging conventions and… honestly, it makes no sense. Which one?

…and honestly, the whole thing with the biopsy results just felt so…clinical. Like they were discussing a widget, not my mother. "Suspicious cells," they said. Suspicious! As if she’s committed a crime. Sounds awful, love. They always do that, don't they? Make it all…detached. Easier for  them , I suppose. My Nan was the same when she had her hip replaced. They talked about the ‘technicalities’ like she wasn’t lying there terrified. Exactly! And then the consultant barely made eye contact when explaining the treatment options. Chemotherapy, radiotherapy… it all just felt so heavy. She barely batted an eyelid, just kept saying "we'll monitor." Monitor  what , exactly? The decline? Oh, the helplessness is the worst, isn’t it? When your mum’s ill… I lost my Dad three years ago now. Liver cancer. He refused chemo, you know. Said he’d rather have quality time than quantity. Stubborn as an old mule, he was. Oh, I'm so sorry. That must have been… difficult. Mum's being incredibly stoic, which isn’t really her. Usually she’s a right chatterbox, always fussing over everyone’s weight, telling me I need to eat more greens, and my brother, David, that he’s getting a bit… substantial, shall we say. Mothers, eh? Always worrying about the food. Mine was the same. Always pushing plates at me. "You're too thin, darling, you need putting on weight!" Even when I was feeling awful. David sounds like my Barry. He’s put on a bit since he stopped playing football. Keeps saying he’s ‘comfortable’, but I think he’s secretly worried. He is. He’s trying to be the strong one, for Mum and for me, I think. He’s not one for showing emotion, David. Always been… reserved. It's me that ends up blubbering at everything. He just nods and says, “Right, well, we’ll sort it.” Which is helpful, in a way, but… isolating. Men are funny about that, aren’t they? My Barry bottles everything up. You wouldn’t know he was hurting unless you really looked. It took months after my Dad died for him to even mention his name without his voice cracking. Have you started thinking about… the arrangements? Funeral planning. It feels… obscene, talking about it while she's still here. But Mum had very specific ideas. She wants a woodland burial, which is lovely, really.

…and honestly, the revisions on that website copy were  extensive . Honestly, you wouldn't believe the number of misused apostrophes. It's proofreading 101, really! People just… don’t read what they’ve written, do they? Still, pays the bills. Keeps me sharp, I suppose. More interesting than, say, your dad’s day, I imagine, David? Sharp is a good word, Sarah. And you’re right. It wasn’t  thrilling . Mostly spreadsheets and firefighting. Had a supplier issue with the packaging for the new widgets – a whole pallet of the wrong size boxes. Honestly, the chaos. Thankfully, managed to reroute another consignment, but it meant a late night. Though, thinking about it, a late night is preferable to explaining  that  to Mr. Henderson. Widgets? What  are  widgets? Is that like, a proper job thing? It is a proper job thing, Leo. They’re… components. Little parts that go into bigger machines. We make them for the automotive industry mainly. Not glamorous, but necessary. And hopefully, keeping people employed. My grandad used to work in a factory. Making bits for cars too, I think. He always smelled of oil and metal. Oh, lovely memory. My dad was an engineer. Same sort of thing, always tinkering. You know, this conversation makes me realise how much has changed. He wouldn't have dreamed of spreadsheets, let alone widgets! Anyway, enough about work. Speaking of things that require precision... skiing! Have you finalise the ski trip, David? Are we still on for Austria in February? Nearly. Just finalising the chalet booking. Found a really good one in Lech – slopes right outside the door. Should be fantastic. Leo, are you still up for trying to conquer the beginner slopes? Conquer is a strong word. Survive, maybe. I’m still a bit wobbly. But yeah, I want to go. It’s just… cold. Layers, darling. Layers are your friend. And hot chocolate at the end of the day. That’s what I live for. Remember that trip to Italy, David, a few years back? The wine  and  the skiing? Paradise. Though, your driving on those mountain roads was terrifying. Honestly, Sarah, they weren’t  that  bad! Just… assertive. These European drivers are much more confident. Plus, the car handled beautifully. I was thinking of upgrading, actually. Seen a rather nice BMW X5… Is it a fast one? My mate’s dad has an Audi, it’s seriously quick.

…and honestly, the light in that one is dreadful. Really flat. You can barely make out the Torii gate at all. It doesn't  feel  like Japan, does it? It feels like…Essex on a cloudy day. Harsh, darling, harsh! I was 22, okay? I hadn’t mastered the art of golden hour photography yet. And besides, it’s the  memory  that matters, not the technical perfection. Remember how ridiculously lost we got trying to find that little ramen shop in Kyoto? Lost is an understatement. We walked in circles for a solid hour, convinced Google Maps was actively sabotaging us. And then that old woman, barely five foot nothing, just pointed us in the right direction with a single, withering glance. It was brilliant. She knew! She just  knew  we were tourists. She probably saw us coming a mile off. Although, the ramen  was  worth it. Best I’ve ever had. This photo… …this is a better one. Look at the colours. Taken just before sunset in Nara Park, right? Ah, the deer park. Those little blighters are absolute menaces. They bow for biscuits, then try to steal your map. It’s adorable and terrifying in equal measure. You look incredibly happy in that picture, though. Genuinely radiant. I was! It was a really good day. Felt…free, you know? No marking, no lesson plans, just wandering around ancient temples and being harassed by deer. Speaking of animals, did you manage to get any decent badger photos last night? You were out there for ages. Don't even ask. Spent three hours huddled in a hide, battling midges and frostbite, and all I got was blurry footage of a bush swaying in the wind. A bush! I suspect a particularly mischievous badger was deliberately taunting me. A taunting badger? Seriously? They’re surprisingly clever, you know. They probably figured out you were there. I’m convinced. I even tried whispering sweet nothings to it… offering it digestive biscuits. Nothing. It held out for something more substantial, no doubt. Probably craved sushi after seeing our Japan photos. You were whispering sweet nothings to a badger? That's… endearing, actually. Although, you’re setting a bad example for the kids. “Daddy tries to bribe wildlife with biscuits.” They’ll be telling everyone. They already  are  telling everyone, probably. Little spies. But honestly, it’s a noble pursuit. Capturing a badger on camera is the modern-day white whale.

… honestly, the Guinness  did  taste better in Ireland. It’s a psychological thing, innit? Like, sitting in a proper pub in Galway, you just  feel  like it’s going to be better. Though, I did nearly get arrested trying to… well, let’s just say skinny dipping in the Atlantic. Bit ambitious, even for me. Oh,  you  did, did you? Classic Leo. Don't tell me the waves were a bit much? You always overestimate your resilience to cold water. I’m more partial to a nice warm sourdough and a flat white, myself. Speaking of which, this chicken is incredible, Anya! Seriously, what did you do to it? It’s my Nana’s recipe. Bit of paprika, lots of garlic, a secret ingredient I’m not telling anyone. You know, the one she learned from her bubbe back in Poland. It's a proper Jewish kitchen classic. Though, I'm trying to branch out. Been looking at Claudia Roden's books, she’s brilliant. Claudia Roden? Never heard of her. Sounds… fancy. Back home, my Nan just chucked everything in a pot and hoped for the best. But this  is  good. Real good. So, Ireland though... sounds chaotic. Did you at least see some good poetry while you were gallivanting about? Always figured the Irish had a way with words. I did actually! Went to a spoken word night in Dublin. Some bloke was reciting Yeats, proper passionate. Almost made the skinny dipping incident worthwhile. Almost. And yeah, the Guinness thing, the whole atmosphere… It's just different. Speaking of different, how's Australia, Ben? Still dodging drop bears and wrestling kangaroos? Drop bears are a myth, mate. Though the spiders are… enthusiastic. Work’s been alright, just slinging coffees all day. Got a bloke coming in tomorrow who reckons he can predict the zombie apocalypse. Said it’ll start with pigeons. Pigeons?! Oh, that’s brilliant. That’s utterly brilliant. Though, honestly, living in London, you’re practically already  in  a zombie apocalypse, just with more complaining and less biting. Speaking of which, I swear Leo snores louder than a herd of elephants. Remember that camping trip? I didn’t sleep for three days. Hey! It’s not  that  loud. It's… robust. A testament to my vitality! And besides, you were telling that awful Jewish joke all night, the one about the two rabbis in the desert... Oh god, don't remind me.

… honestly, I still think Alton Towers’ Nemesis Reborn is a bit underwhelming. All that hype, and it’s just…rough. Like,  really  rough. My fillings nearly rattled loose. You’d think for the money they spent, they could've smoothed out some of those transitions. Rough, aye? I thought it was alright. A bit jarring, granted. But massively improved on the original, wouldn't you say? The theming was spot on, the queue line was decent… it’s a solid day out, isn’t it? Anyway, far better than sitting in front of your computer all day, blasting away at pixelated bad guys. How’s the  new  one going, by the way? The space marine one? Don't start on the games, Liam. It’s a de-stressor! And it  is  good. It's got a ridiculously complex crafting system, actually. I’m trying to optimise build orders for early-game resource gathering. It’s… research, sort of. Applied game theory. Don’t look at me like that. It’s not a waste of time. Applied game theory? Right. And this justifies the weekly raid nights that end at 3am? Look, I’m just saying, we haven’t done anything properly  fun  in ages. Not ‘fun’ involving glowing screens and aggressive button-mashing. We need a proper day trip. Something…different. Not even another theme park, although that's better than nothing. Okay, okay. You're right, we are getting stuck in a rut. What did you have in mind? Not more of that historical re-enactment stuff, please. Last time with the Anglo-Saxons… needless to say, my chainmail chafed. Okay, point taken. No chainmail. I was thinking more along the lines of a proper cinema trip. There's that new sci-fi flick, 'Starlight Vector', getting good reviews. Apparently, the special effects are… insane. Hmm. Sci-fi. As long as it's not another gritty, dystopian future. I'm a bit out of those at the moment. I need something… escapist. Actually, speaking of escaping…did you see that documentary about border security in Australia? Properly mental. Australia? No, what’s that about? It's about the customs officers. The things they find hidden in luggage… you wouldn't  believe  it. Apparently, they busted a bloke trying to smuggle in live goldfish in his hair.  In his hair , Liam! And another one tried to hide snakes in speaker boxes.

…and honestly, the sheer  core  work involved is astonishing. I hadn’t realised. It's not just about being able to pull, is it? It's everything – the slide, the timing, coordinating with the crew… Mrs. Higgins, the coach, is lovely but she doesn’t pull any punches. Absolutely relentless. Sounds… invigorating. A far cry from marking essays, I imagine. Though, honestly, sometimes  they  require similar endurance. You’re doing this for the college, aren’t you? Is it a complete beginner's course? Completely. I’m the oldest by at least twenty years, probably more. All these bright young things, so physically fit. I feel like a creaking galleon amongst speedboats. Though, I did manage not to capsize yesterday. Small victories, eh? It reminded me a bit of that kayaking trip I did in the Dordogne, years ago. Though slightly less… peaceful. Oh, the Dordogne! I remember you telling me about that. Beautiful scenery. Kayaking is lovely, definitely gentler. Though I did have a near miss with a submerged tree root once. Gave me quite a fright! You'll need serious waterproofs for this rowing though. Cambridge weather is utterly unpredictable. That’s what I’m worried about! Trying to find gear that isn’t ridiculously expensive. I saw some stuff online, but it all looks… technical. All those layers and breathable fabrics. My old Barbour won’t cut it, I suspect. No, it really won't. You're better off heading to a proper outdoor shop. They can advise you. It's an investment, certainly, but worth it if you’re going to be out on the river regularly. Speaking of investments… I had a rather strange reunion last month. Oh? Do tell. Well, it was my cousin, David. My mother’s brother’s son. I’d never actually  met  him until now. Apparently, my Gran, his grandmother, kept us separate. Something about family disagreements… ancient history, really. He tracked me down through Ancestry.com. We met in York. Wow. That's… odd. And how was it? Surprisingly good, actually. He's a lovely man. Runs a small bookshop. It felt…oddly natural, you know? Like catching up with someone you've always known. Though there was definitely a sense of lost time. It made me think about Auntie Margaret, of course. Oh, yes. It still feels… raw, doesn't it? It's been over a year now, but… It does.

...Honestly, Dad, it's just quicker to text. All that dot-dash stuff? Who even  uses  Morse code anymore? Mr. Henderson was going on about it in ICT, said his grandad was a radio operator in the war. Felt like a history lesson, not a computer class!      Aye, well, there was a time. Grandad Jack, he knew it. Used to tap it out on the table with his cutlery, driving your Nan mad. Said it kept his mind sharp. Keeps you thinking, see? Like a puzzle. Though I’ll admit, texting's a lot less…clattery. Speaking of which, have you checked for your results yet? They should be up now, shouldn’t they?      Yeah, I looked earlier. Got the email. I cleared everything! A, A, B in my mocks. I’m  so  relieved. Proper brick off my chest kind of feeling.      Brilliant, lass! Really proud of you. All that hard work paid off. University's getting closer, isn’t it? Still leaning towards Manchester then? We need to have a proper look at campus when we get a chance.      Definitely Manchester. I keep looking at different accommodation options online. They're all so…beige. And expensive! And student finance is a nightmare. It's just form after form after form. They want to know everything!      Aye, it’s a mess, that is. We’ll sort it though. Don’t you worry. Just focus on enjoying the summer. By the way, did that Amazon delivery arrive alright? The new trainers?      Oh yeah! They're amazing. Proper comfy. The ones I showed you on eBay, remember? They were a bargain! Though, honestly, sometimes I think I spend too much time online. I’m addicted to scrolling.      We all are, aren't we? It's designed that way. Remember your mum complaining about me spending hours comparing prices for…well, everything? She said my head would square off!      Sounds about right! She’s probably stressing about what we’re having for tea at Grandma’s. She always gets stressed about the food.      She does. Expect a lecture on the importance of vegetables. “You need your greens, love!” That'll be her. Though, to be fair, Grandma’s roast dinners  are  legendary. Are you sorted for pens and stationery? You'll need a good stash for uni.      I think so. I got a big pack last week. But knowing me, I'll lose half of them by the first lecture.

… honestly, the deadline for the dissertation proposal is stressing me  out . I’ve got, like, a week left and I’m still staring at a blank document most of the time. It’s brutal, man. Brutal. Tell me about it. Remember undergrad, thinkin’ essays were bad? Dissertation’s a whole different beast. What you even  doing  it on, anyway? You were rambling about something Japanese last time we spoke – Tokyo, right? Yeah, Tokyo’s the focus. Specifically, the influence of retro gaming arcades on contemporary urban space. Sounds fancy, doesn’t it? It’s basically me justifying a trip to Japan under the guise of academic research. Clever boy. Very clever. I’d take that. I'm stuck with the socio-economic impact of internet censorship in developing nations. Thrilling stuff. Honestly, half the time I just Google "internet censorship stats" and try to make it sound intelligent. Woah, that  is  heavy. Sounds like you’re going to be up all night fuelled by instant noodles and existential dread. Listen, speaking of Japan… I was looking at flights last night. They're not cheap. Especially if I want to be there for, like, a proper amount of time - not just a weekend tourist blitz. Nah, Japan's expensive, innit? I had a mate go last year - barely scraped by on ramen and convenience store bentos. You’ll need to start a GoFundMe or something. Seriously though, have you looked at budget airlines, connecting flights? Yeah, all of it. I’m trying to find something that doesn’t involve spending 27 hours in airports. The ideal is direct, but, well… dream on, right? I’m thinking maybe push the dissertation back a term and actually  save  for it properly. That's sensible, actually. Don’t bankrupt yourself for a research trip. What about exams though? How’s the prep going for those? They’re looming, aren't they? Don't even  mention  exams. I’ve got that history one next week, and I swear, the amount of dates and names I need to memorise… It’s just a rote learning exercise. Makes me wonder what the point is. I feel you. They’re testing your ability to recall, not actually think critically. It’s ridiculous. I've been trying to convince myself it's good practice for… for something. Adulting, maybe? Adulting is a myth, man. A complete fabrication. You know what  would  be a good use of my time right now?

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of photos Mum posts on Facebook is astonishing. It's Buckfast Abbey, Buckfast Abbey, a close-up of a gargoyle at Buckfast Abbey. It's lovely she enjoyed it with you both, but it's clogging up my feed! Oh, now, be fair, love. She was  thrilled  to go. It's not every day she gets to a proper Abbey, is it? And she knows I help her sort through the pictures, otherwise they'd just stay on her phone forever. Speaking of phones, have you got that new cover I suggested? The one with the little grip on the back? Not yet. Still procrastinating. I’m forever dropping the thing. It's a hazard of being a teacher, you know – constantly juggling books, pens, a phone…little hands grabbing at everything! Phones. Humph. In my day, a phone was attached to the wall! And you certainly didn't  take pictures  with it. Used to have a Brownie camera. Took a good photo if the light was right. None of this instant gratification nonsense. Oh, Grandad, you’re such a card. Though you are right, it  is  different. Remember when we were talking about a trip? I was thinking, maybe a cruise? Somewhere warm, you know, escape the Devon drizzle. A cruise? That sounds…nice. A bit  too  relaxing for me, perhaps? I like having a bit of structure. Though, somewhere warm does sound appealing. Have you seen the price of everything these days though? It's frightening. And the insurance! Don't even get me started on travel insurance. Insurance? Bah! More money down the drain for the government. Speaking of which, did you see what that David Cameron was up to? Apparently, fiddling his taxes again. Always one rule for them and another for the rest of us. Used to be a man could trust a Prime Minister. Oh, Grandad, politics again? Let’s not. Honestly. It'll give us all indigestion. Though you’re not wrong about the insurance being pricey. We have to be careful. My friend, Margaret, she went to Spain last year and ended up needing hospital treatment. The bill was… astronomical. Crikey. See? That's what worries me. It’s not just the trip itself, it’s the ‘what ifs’. I remember old Mr. Henderson from the village, he went on a cruise a few years ago, slipped in the bathroom, broke his hip… Broke his hip, you say?

…and honestly, Dad, the roundabout situation near Bruges was  mental . Like, a vortex of cyclists and lorries, all vying for position. You said your sat nav was being a bit…optimistic?      Optimistic is putting it mildly, love. More like actively trying to lead us into the canals! I swear, it kept telling me to turn right onto cycle lanes. Diane was beside herself. "Bernard," she said, "you’re going to cause an international incident!" Honestly, I’ve never known a sat nav so determined to get us lost. It felt like it had a personal vendetta.      Sounds about right. They're never brilliant those things, are they? I rely on good old-fashioned road signs, mostly. Though even  that  can be a challenge sometimes. Did you at least get to see Ghent? I heard the markets there are lovely.      Mum, you know I bombarded you with photos! Ghent was gorgeous. The Gravensteen castle was incredible, and the market  was  brilliant. So much cheese! And chocolate, naturally. You wouldn’t believe the variety. I brought you both some, by the way. It's in my bag.      Oh, lovely! Good girl. Diane and I were saying just yesterday how we missed a proper Belgian waffle. The ones they sell here are just not the same. Too…fluffy. They need that proper crispy edge. And the mussels! Did you have any mussels?      Loads! In Brussels, we went to this tiny little place, completely packed with locals. They were amazing, cooked in white wine and herbs. I’m trying to find the recipe. Honestly, the food was the highlight. Although, navigating the service… sometimes they seemed a bit… disinterested.      That’s Belgium for you. Efficient, mostly, but not exactly known for being overly friendly. Still, a good meal makes up for a lot. How was the driving overall, Bernard? Apart from the sat nav trying to drown you.      A bit stressful, to be honest. Those roads are narrow! And everyone cycles everywhere. It’s brilliant, it is, but as a driver, it's…intimidating. You’re constantly checking for people appearing out of nowhere. I wish I’d taken my old Ford instead of trying to be sensible with the little Fiat. It feels so small over there.      You said you were thinking about getting a new phone, Dad? Have you looked at anything yet? I was helping a friend the other day, setting up her new one, and there are some with really good map apps now, much better than the standard ones.

… honestly, I just think a bit of rosemary with the lamb makes  all  the difference. It's just…fresher, don't you think? Not quite as overpowering as mint, either. Rosemary is good. Though, you know, my mum always used to put a little sprig of thyme in with the lamb. Said it reminded her of Yorkshire. Everything always went back to Yorkshire with her. Of course it did. She  was  from Yorkshire, wasn’t she? Still, I'm sticking with the rosemary. Speaking of scents though, have you tried that new Jo Malone? The one with the honeysuckle and pear? Ooh, no. Jo Malone is a bit… pricey for everyday, isn’t it? I'm still working my way through that sandalwood one you got me for my birthday. It's lovely, actually. A bit more subtle. It is lovely, isn't it? Though sometimes I feel a bit… vanilla . I fancy something a bit more, well,  zingy . It’s like wanting a different accent, you know? Something that just…pops. A different accent? Now you’re talking nonsense. Though I suppose that’s what we do with perfume, isn’t it? Try and project a different persona. You and your metaphors. It’s true! Your accent’s doing a pretty good job of projecting ‘Edinburgh sophisticate’ right now, even in London. It gets stronger when you're teasing me, I notice. It does not! That's just…natural articulation. And I'm not teasing. I’m merely pointing out your penchant for dramatic comparisons. So, lamb and rosemary...are we having potatoes with it? And what about veg? Roasties, naturally. And I was thinking some green beans, but I saw those beautiful tulips at the market today, and I was thinking a small vase on the table wouldn’t go amiss. Bit of colour. Tulips are good. Though they don't last long, do they? It’s like buying a fleeting moment of beauty. Reminds me of… Facebook. All those carefully curated lives. Oh, don’t start on Facebook. Did Sarah post pictures of her new kitchen yet? I saw she was having one done. She did. It’s…very beige. And perfectly symmetrical. It looks like a showroom. I did comment, though. Had to. It's polite. It’s just…so  performative , isn't it? It is. Although I quite enjoy seeing what old school friends are up to, even if it’s slightly…filtered.

...Honestly, the heat just got to me. I’d imagined a pleasant warmth, you know? Like a nice summer’s day in Bristol. But Queensland in December? It’s oppressive. Truly oppressive. And the flies! I’d forgotten about the flies.      Aye, Queensland’s a different beast altogether. I did a bit of business out there, Cairns mostly. Lovely scenery, but you’re right about the heat. Makes a man feel like he’s wearing a three-piece suit even when he isn’t. Speaking of which, the suits those Australian businessmen wore… far too much emphasis on the shiny, if you ask me. All polyester and no substance.      You sound like my father, Arthur. He’d sniff at a polyester blend like it was a personal affront. He was a proper Yorkshireman, through and through. Everything had to be wool, or at least cotton. Though, coming from Sheffield, he wasn’t overly concerned with fashion, per se. More concerned with practicality.      Practicality is good. My teaching days were all about practicality. Couldn’t be swanning around in silk when you’re trying to explain the subjunctive to a class of fourteen-year-olds! Though, I did try to instill a little… elegance, perhaps. I spent a good deal of time in France, you see. Taught in Lyon for three years. Picked up a taste for good tailoring, I suppose.      Lyon, eh? Fancy. I mostly dealt with the practicalities of moving goods. Import, export, that sort of thing. Nothing so refined. Got stung once trying to secure a bank loan for a shipment of…well, never mind what. Australian banks are… cautious, shall we say? Very different from the Northern banks back home.      Cautious is putting it mildly. My sister moved to Perth a few years back. Needed a small loan to renovate the kitchen, and it was like pulling teeth. She said they scrutinised everything – her income, her husband’s job, even their grocery bills!      Goodness me. It sounds exhausting. Perhaps that's why I stuck to teaching. Less financial wrangling, more… intellectual stimulation. Though, the pay wasn’t exactly glamorous, let's be honest. It certainly didn’t allow for frequent trips to Australia. I was born in Almondsbury, you know, just outside Bristol. Never really ventured further than Europe until retirement.      Bristol’s a grand city. I did a bit of work down there once, years ago. Lovely harbour.

… honestly, it’s just relentless, isn’t it? All the curated perfection. I saw Beatrice – you remember Beatrice from Newnham? – she posted a picture of her sourdough, and it looked…architectural. Honestly, like something out of a magazine. And you  know  she burned the first three loaves. Oh, Beatrice. Always one for appearances. Yeah, Instagram’s a nightmare for that. I try to limit myself, really. It's useful for picking up teaching resources, finding interesting articles about TEFL, but the personal stuff… it’s exhausting. Especially seeing everyone’s ‘highlight reel’. Exactly! It's not  real  life. It's the glossy brochure version. I tried to explain that to Mother, but she's fallen completely down the rabbit hole. She’s convinced everyone in Littlebury is living a more exciting life than she is. She keeps showing me pictures of Mrs. Higgins’ granddaughter’s engagement party. Apparently, it involved doves. Doves, Liv! Doves?! Oh, bless her. Sounds… extra. My grandma mostly just shares chain letters about dodgy medical cures. Which is a different kind of exhausting. What about TikTok? Have you dipped your toe in? I’ve found some fantastic pronunciation tips for my students on there, surprisingly. TikTok? No. Absolutely not. Too… frantic. I did attempt Facebook, briefly. Found myself embroiled in a rather heated debate about garden gnomes. Honestly, I felt like I was aging in real time. I much prefer having a proper sit-down with a good television programme. Though, even that feels rather…hollow these days. Hollow? How so? There’s some amazing stuff on at the moment. Have you seen  The Bear ? It's incredible. Really gritty, about a chef taking over his family’s sandwich shop. I’ve  heard  of it. People keep recommending it. But I’m finding it harder to commit to long-form TV. My attention span is… diminishing. It’s probably all the years of not really…doing anything. I’m finding myself gravitating towards podcasts. Much more manageable. Oh, podcasts are brilliant! I listen to them on my commute, mostly. I’ve found a really good one about linguistics, actually. It's called  Lexicon Valley . Quite nerdy, but fascinating. They’re doing a series on dialectal variations at the moment. You’d love it, being from Cambridge. You’d probably recognise bits and pieces. Ooh, that  does  sound intriguing. My Cambridge accent is probably extinct now, though. Years of…well, years.

…and honestly, the way she just  launched  herself off the side, no hesitation! Completely fearless. It’s a good job I was right there, mind you. You two were too busy building that…what  was  that, anyway? A spaceship out of cushions? It’s the Star Destroyer! It needs more blankets for the lasers. And I’m the Darth Vader! Pew pew! Right, excellent. Well, the Star Destroyer will have to wait a moment. We need to talk about Saturday. Remember ANON said they might be able to take us to see their travelling circus? Ooooh, the one with the ponies? And the jugglers? And the man who balances on a chair! That’s the one. But…it means we need to find your passports. Honestly, where did I put them? I swear I had them out last summer, checking expiry dates. Mine’s in my special box! The pink one with the sparkles. I don't  have  a special box. Mine's probably...under my bed with the dinosaurs. Right, well let's have a look later. And it also reminds me, ANON was asking about a photo for their Blue Peter badge application. They’re trying to get one for bravery, apparently. Something about rescuing a hamster…doesn't matter. They said a nice photo of us all playing would be perfect. Bravery? I’m brave! I tackled a spider yesterday. You did indeed, you were very brave. We’ll take the photo Saturday, if we go to the circus. Speaking of ANON…they’re so good with you two, aren’t they? You were absolutely captivated while they were building that Lego castle. They let me put all the sparkly bits on! And they didn’t laugh when I pretended the little man was a king who only ate broccoli. That sounds like ANON. Right, focus. Passports, photo, circus…and then there’s the small matter of pocket money. I think you both deserve a little extra this week, for being so good with Pippy when I was at that training. Can I get a unicorn? A really glittery one? I want a dinosaur! A T-Rex with big teeth! We’ll see. Let’s not get ahead of ourselves. Just remember, it’s earned, not given. Speaking of earned... ANON was telling me a strange story earlier. Apparently, their grandma told them that in China, they eat eggs that are, like,  really  old.

… honestly, I just feel a right fool, ya know? Like, I was trying to be all…sensitive, asking if he was alright ‘cause he seemed a bit down, and he just  clammed up . Completely. Then just…said he was tired. Right. And you think it’s…more than just tiredness? You think it’s  that ? Well, it’s not like he’s suddenly taken up marathon running, is it? And he’s been… well, less interested, let's just say. Not in a ‘he doesn’t fancy me’ way, more like…less interested full stop. It’s been happening a few times now, and he’s usually… pretty keen, y’know? Always has been. It's understandable you’re worried, Liv. It’s just… it’s a sensitive subject. Men get really weird about, well,  everything  down there. My brother… he went through something similar a couple of years ago. Wouldn’t talk to anyone about it. Your brother?! Really? Did he…did he sort it out? I’m worried sick. I don't want him thinking I think there’s something wrong  with  him. I was trying to be caring and now I've probably just made it worse. I said, “Are you sure you’re okay, love? You seem a bit off,” and that was it. Stone wall. He did, eventually. He ended up going to the doctor, which took ages to get him to do. Turns out it was stress, loads of it from Uni. It wasn't… permanent, thankfully. But it was really impacting him, and Sarah – his girlfriend – was totally clueless for months because he wouldn’t open up. It's really common, actually. Stress, anxiety, even just feeling a bit run down can cause it. See, that’s what I was thinking, but I didn’t want to… suggest it. Like, I didn’t want to imply he wasn't 'performing' or whatever. It feels awful even saying it like that. It's like… it’s the one thing men are supposed to  always  be able to do. Exactly! That’s the problem. That whole societal pressure. It's ridiculous. He’s probably feeling awful enough already without you adding to it, even unintentionally. What did he  say  when you asked if he was alright? Anything at all? Just muttered something about a long day at work. But he works from home! He literally rolls out of bed and sits at his computer.

…Honestly, the sheer volume of things you can have on your Healthy Extra B choice is  mental . I was looking at the Slimming World app again and there's like, a whole section dedicated to different varieties of reduced-fat cheddar. It's… a bit much, isn’t it?      Right? It defeats the object slightly, doesn't it? Like, they’re encouraging you to eat cheese, but still controlling it. I’m more interested in maximising free foods. This massive bag of spinach was a steal at Sainsbury’s. I’m trying to get through it all before it goes slimy.      Oh, Sainsbury’s is good for Quorn, isn't it? They always seem to have the best range. Asda’s is… lacking. And the Quorn chicken pieces are basically free, which is a win. Though, I swear, the texture is changing. It's getting… spongier?      Oh god, yes! I noticed that too! It's like they’ve changed the recipe. Anyway, speaking of free, I got a veg box delivered this week and it was  overflowing . Seriously, I'm going to be eating root vegetables until Christmas. It’s a good saving though, and better than the supermarket.      Clever. I keep meaning to look into those. Though honestly, the tax return is looming and I'm terrified. Being self-employed and a pharmacy dispenser at the same time feels like… an accounting nightmare.      Ugh, tax. Don’t even. I'm procrastinating  hard . I need to invoice a couple of clients. It’s just so draining. On a lighter note, have you tried the new 0 calorie syrup from Aldi? The toffee flavour is surprisingly decent.      I’ve seen it! Is it genuinely good? Because some of those artificial flavours are just… offensive. I had a sugar-free cola the other day that tasted like someone had dissolved plastic in water.      It's not amazing, but it does the trick. It satisfies a sweet craving without the syns. Which brings me to – I’m thinking Saturday is definitely treat day. We  need  to plan something. Maybe that new Italian place everyone’s talking about?      Ooh, yes! But we have to be tactical. Look at the menu online beforehand and work out the syn values. Otherwise, we'll blow our target instantly. I was 2.5lbs down this week, finally. Though, my scales are being utterly ridiculous. One minute I’m down, the next I’m up.

...Honestly, the thought of another all-inclusive in Spain just fills me with dread, David. It’s not a holiday, it's… beige. Beige food, beige people, beige entertainment. We did it last year, remember?      I remember. You spent the entire week complaining about the lack of decent coffee and the aggressively cheerful animation team. Look, I get it, it wasn’t  thrilling . But it was easy. And cheap. And after the year I’ve had with that nonsense at Hargreaves, easy and cheap feels pretty good.      Easy and cheap isn't living, David. It’s existing. I was reading an article about the Azores – volcanic islands, whale watching, proper hiking… Now  that  sounds like a holiday. A bit more adventurous, don't you think?      The Azores? Right. And how much would a “proper” holiday like that set us back? Probably the price of a small car. I still haven't fully recovered from paying for that new boiler, you know. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I spend my life fixing things. Boilers, computers, leaky taps…      Okay, point taken about the boiler. And Hargreaves sounds dreadful, honestly. But we  need  to start planning something different. I booked that spa weekend for you, didn't I? That was a little treat. What about something… writing related? Maybe a course in Italy? You’ve been on about finishing that novel for years.      Italy… tempting. But the thought of sitting in a room with a bunch of earnest aspiring novelists critiquing my prose... gives me hives. Honestly, I’m starting to think the novel is a fool’s errand. It’s just… words aren't flowing. It's all a bit…stuck.      Don’t say that! You have brilliant ideas. Remember that scene with the lighthouse keeper? It was amazing. You just need a spark. Maybe the Azores would  be  the spark. A completely different environment.      You’re determined, aren't you? You know, it’s funny. You, all organised and efficient in your work, booking directors’ schedules and smoothing everything over… and then I come home to this whirlwind of adventurous ideas. It’s a good balance, I suppose.      Someone’s got to have the dreams, haven’t they? Though, speaking of smoothing things over, have you seen what Boris Johnson’s up to now? Honestly, the man is a walking disaster.      Don't even  start  me on politics. I'm trying to enjoy my tea.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of tartan on display in Edinburgh was quite something. It was lovely, of course, but relentless. Reminded me of a particularly enthusiastic school fete. Though, thankfully, the whiskey was significantly better quality. Did you see the postcard I left on the kitchen counter? I tried to capture a bit of the castle, but it really doesn’t do it justice, does it? Aye, saw it this morning with my coffee. Nice picture, though. You’re right, photos never  quite  capture the atmosphere. Edinburgh's a good city. We should think about a weekend there, perhaps in the autumn. Less… bagpipe-heavy. An excellent suggestion, David. Autumn would be ideal. Although, before we start planning Scottish excursions, we need to sort out Margaret’s birthday. It’s creeping up on us alarmingly quickly. Have you given any thought to what we’re doing? She dropped a not-so-subtle hint about wanting something ‘cultural’. Cultural, eh? That could be anything. Opera? A pottery class? She’s always threatening to take up pottery. I was thinking maybe a nice weekend away, something quieter than Edinburgh, perhaps. The Cotswolds? We haven't been for ages. The Cotswolds are lovely, but she’s been grumbling about needing a bit more… stimulation, shall we say. Something new. I was tentatively looking at a small exhibition at the National Portrait Gallery in London. A new collection of pre-Raphaelite drawings. She’s always loved them. We could make a day of it, lunch in Bloomsbury… London sounds good. Less driving for you as well, which is always a bonus, isn’t it? You still feel it in your knees after Cornwall, I reckon? You’re remarkably observant, dear. A touch, yes. Though I’m blaming the Cornish hills, not my advancing years. Speaking of which, your birthday’s not far behind Margaret’s. Any wishes? No more technical gadgets, I strongly advise. You and those drones… Alright, alright, point taken. The drone was a momentary lapse of judgment. It’s currently gathering dust in the shed. Honestly, I haven't thought much about it. Just a quiet weekend, maybe? You cooking? That's always a winner. I can manage a quiet weekend and a decent roast, you know. Although, with everything going on, I find myself increasingly distracted. This fuss about Scottish independence again. Honestly, it's exhausting. They really aren’t going to let it lie, are they?

…and honestly, the headteacher just said, “Can anyone bring in a drawing? Something welcoming.” Like  that’s  going to solve anything! But, well, it's a start, I suppose. What are you two thinking? We said we’d all do one for the new family, didn’t we? The ones coming from Syria. I’m drawing a chair. Mine’s going to be a REALLY fast race car! But it needs a driver… maybe the dad could  be  the driver? That’s a lovely thought, Leo. Very kind. And a chair, Lily? That’s… thoughtful. Why a chair? Because they'll need somewhere to sit. When they come. And their house… it won't have everything right away, will it? So they need a chair. Oh, Lily. That’s a very sweet idea. You’re a very kind girl. You’re absolutely right, they will. It’s going to be a big change for them, coming all this way. It's not like moving houses  here , is it? Is Syria… really far away? Further than Grandma’s? Oh,  much  further than Grandma’s. Grandma’s a car ride away, isn’t she? Syria is… you'd need to fly in an aeroplane for a very, very long time. And it’s… well, things have been very difficult there. That’s why they’re having to come and live somewhere safe. What kind of chair should I draw? A comfy one? Or a… a fancy one? Hmm. What  kind  of chair do you like best? We’ve got all sorts, haven’t we? We've got the squishy armchair in the corner, the wooden chairs at the table, the little stool you use for painting… I like the beanbag! But you can’t really  sit  properly on a beanbag. It just… swallows you. It does rather, doesn't it? Lily, you could draw any chair you like. Maybe one that looks really inviting. A chair by a fireplace, perhaps? Or with a nice cushion? A chair with flowers on it! And maybe a little table next to it with a cup of tea. That sounds lovely. Very welcoming. Now, Leo, are you sure about the racing car? Maybe something a little… calmer? Just for this drawing, you can always draw more race cars later. But they might be sad! Maybe a fast car would make  them  happy! To show them we’re fun?

… honestly, I just feel a bit bad for Sarah. She’s been  so  wrapped up in trying for a baby for, what, nearly two years now? It’s all she talks about, and it’s clearly getting her down. Yeah, it is. And it's hard, isn't it, watching a friend go through that? Especially when, you know, everyone else seems to be popping them out left, right and centre. It feels almost… insensitive to even  mention  little Leo being sticky or having a sleep regression. Exactly! I nearly bit my tongue off yesterday when Chloe was showing us photos of Freddie’s first attempt at solid food. It was pure chaos, food  everywhere , and all I could think was Sarah would kill for that chaos right now. Chloe’s lovely, but she does lack a bit of… self-awareness sometimes. Bless her. She means well. It just feels like a different world for Sarah at the moment. Remember how upset she was at Amelia’s baby shower? Tried to put on a brave face, but I saw her in the loo, wiping her eyes. Oh, I do. Awful. And it’s not like she can just ‘switch it off’, is it? It’s constantly there, looming. It’s reminding me a bit of how I felt when I was marking dissertations last term – that constant low-level anxiety. Except, obviously, infinitely more emotionally charged. That’s a good analogy, actually. The perpetual weight of it. Speaking of work, how did your lecture go today? The one on post-structuralism? Did they actually  get  it? A few did. There was a lively debate about Derrida, which is always a win, even if it descended into a bit of a philosophical shouting match at one point. Young Thomas – you know, the one who always sits at the front – he’s a bright spark. He genuinely challenged my reading of  Of Grammatology . Good. You need one of those students who keeps you on your toes. I had a rather… enthusiastic discussion about the Romantic poets today. Apparently, Byron was a total heartthrob. Who knew? It quickly turned into a debate about modern celebrity crushes. Oh, that sounds… chaotic. Though, understandable. They're students. It’s good you can roll with it. Have you heard from David recently? I haven’t seen him since… well, ages. Not really. He messaged me a couple of weeks ago, said he was swamped with research for his book.

… honestly, it was  mortifying . Old Mrs. Higgins genuinely believed I’d jinxed her prize-winning marrow by complimenting it. A marrow, David! Only in Norfolk, eh? You'd think academics would be immune to that sort of thing. Though, thinking about it, some of the history department  are  a bit… peculiar. Professor Armitage and his insistence on wearing a specific tweed jacket for marking essays. Oh, don't even get me started on Armitage. It’s not just the jacket, it’s the  ritual . Apparently, it hasn’t been washed since 1987 because “it absorbs the academic energy.” Honestly! It explains a lot, actually. Speaking of rituals, remember that time we accidentally walked through that farmer's field and he swore we’d ruined his barley harvest? How could I forget? He looked like he was about to call the police! Which, ironically, reminds me of that awful incident with the students and the inflatable flamingo last summer. Oh god, the flamingo! They thought it would be hilarious to put it on top of the police station. "A statement on societal frivolity," they claimed. Right. And Sergeant Miller was  not  amused. He barely contained his rage. He kept repeating, ‘This is a police station, not a Butlins holiday camp!’ The local paper had a field day. University publicity gold, though, wasn’t it? It brought in applications, admittedly. Although I suspect it attracted a particular  type  of applicant. The "challenging" ones. Still, better than no applications at all. Honestly, sometimes I miss just being a pure researcher, you know? No student dramas, no inflatable flamingos, just… books. I get it. But then who'd explain the socio-political implications of inflatable flamingos to impressionable young minds? Someone has to. Seriously though, lecturing  is  tiring. I’m already dreaming of the holidays. Anywhere but here, preferably. Somewhere without prize-winning marrows and suspicious farmers. I’ve been browsing Greek islands. Santorini, maybe. Somewhere with no history of ancient curses or superstition. Just sunshine and hideous tourist shops. Santorini sounds amazing. We both deserve some serious relaxation. It feels like we haven’t had a proper break since… well, since before the flamingo incident, probably. Remember that disastrous camping trip to Cornwall a few years back? Don't! The rain, the midges, the fact you insisted on bringing that ridiculously oversized tent… and then nearly set it on fire trying to make breakfast.

… honestly, Dad, it’s just  easier  to do everything on your phone now. Like, even booking the van for when we move stuff to Mum’s. Remember when we had to actually  call  places? And queue? Queue! Good lord, yes. And then they’d say they were fully booked. A right palaver. Still, I don’t trust these… these digital things entirely. Too easy to get scammed, wouldn’t you say? All these pop-ups and wanting your bank details. That’s fair, you gotta be careful. But the comparison websites are pretty good, they vet the companies. And I’m there with you, every step of the way. I’ll sort the van, you just… try not to get overwhelmed. How’s the fishing been, by the way? Haven't heard you talk about it in ages. Rubbish. Absolutely rubbish. Went down to Dungeness last week. Not a bite. Young Jimmy down the pub, he says the tides are all off. Global warming, he reckons. Everything’s changing. Still, beats being cooped up here. Though, speaking of cooped up, this house… it's too big for one old man, innit? That’s why we’re getting you closer to Mum, Dad. She’s worried, and frankly, so am I. It’s a bit isolating out here, even with the garden. And you’re not exactly leaping around doing DIY anymore. Don’t remind me. My back's playing up something awful. Trying to sort those old biscuit tins in the attic nearly finished me off. Found some right treasures though. A proper Victorian one, all embossed. Might be worth a few quid. Oh, really? You should get those appraised, Dad. There’s a place in Canterbury, I can look up the details. Maybe we can take a box when we move some stuff. And how’s your sister, Auntie Sheila? Have you heard from her? Not for a week or two. She's still going on about the Great Dorset Steam Fair. Says they had a massive turnout this year. Wants me to go with her next time. Honestly, all those engines… deafening! I’d rather sit and watch a bit of  Call of Duty  with young Ben. He's getting rather good, you know.  Call of Duty?  You? I didn’t know you even knew what that  was ! Don't you be so surprised! He showed me. It's a bit like… strategy, really.

… honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it all. Demolishing the library! It’s been there since… well, since forever, hasn’t it? My grandmother used to take me there when I was little. All those Saturday mornings smelling of dust and old paper. It is a bit shocking, isn’t it? I saw the notice on the council website – buried, of course, amongst all the bin collection updates. They’re saying it’s ‘underused’ and a ‘financial burden’. As if a bit of community spirit has a price tag. Exactly! And ‘underused’? It's full after school. Old Mrs. Higgins does her computer classes there, the reading group… it's a hub! They want to put up another block of flats, naturally. Everything’s always about flats. It’s infuriating. Edinburgh seems to be doing a better job preserving things. They actually  value  their architecture. Remember that fight over the old Surgeons’ Hall? They managed to save that, thankfully. Oh, aye, I remember reading about that. We seem to be stuck in this cycle of tearing down anything remotely historical and slapping up something… beige. It’s depressing. Speaking of things needing preserving, have you had a chance to look at those fabric swatches I showed you? For the sofa? I did, briefly. Lots of choices! You were leaning towards the…was it the herringbone? The grey one? The herringbone, yes. But I'm wavering. It feels a bit… safe, doesn’t it? I keep looking at that bolder floral, the one with the muted blues and greens. It’s a bit more me, I think. Though, slightly terrifying. What if I hate it? It’s lovely, actually. It’s got a bit of a William Morris vibe to it, doesn’t it? More character than the herringbone for sure. Though, you're right, a big floral is a commitment. Have you put them all up against the wall, seen what they look like in the evening light? Not  all  of them, no. I did the herringbone and the plain navy. I should probably make the effort, shouldn't I? It’s just… exhausting. I ended up down a rabbit hole looking at news articles about the library again. And then I was reading about how the council is awarding contracts to… well, it’s all very murky. Councils. Don't even get me started. It's always the same story. Backroom deals, favouritism… Honestly, you need to avoid reading the comments sections on those local news websites.

…and honestly, the vinyl revival is baffling to me. All that faffing about, cleaning records, the fragility of it all. Give me Spotify any day. Though, I did rather enjoy rediscovering some of the old Bowie albums on it, admittedly. Still, a bit of a palaver, isn’t it? Oh, come  on , David! It’s not faffing! It’s… an experience! The sound is just  better , you know? Warmer. And it forces you to actually  listen  to an album, start to finish, instead of skipping around. I’ve been getting into Fleetwood Mac lately, proper old-school. I agree with Chloe, actually. There's something nice about the ritual of it. And honestly, after staring at a screen all day for work, physically interacting with something is… grounding. Though I mostly stick to jazz, personally. Nina Simone mostly. Grounding? Bit strong, isn't it? It’s a record, love. Though I can see what you both mean about the sound. I used to have a cracking system back in the day. Still got a few old cassettes knocking around, though haven’t touched the player in years. Speaking of knocking around, have we finalised what we’re getting Mum for her birthday? That’s what I wanted to discuss, actually. I was thinking perhaps a weekend away? She’s been saying she's feeling a bit cooped up. Somewhere coastal, maybe? Ooh, a weekend away sounds lovely! But Mum hates driving, remember? She’d be stressing the whole time. What about something she can do at home? She's been getting really into her gardening, hasn’t she? She has! I saw her Instagram, the roses are looking incredible. Maybe some really nice gardening tools? Or a subscription to one of those seed box things? They send you new seeds every month. Seed box? Sounds… fiddly. She’d probably just end up giving them to old Mrs. Higgins next door. I was thinking a new telly. Her's is ancient. She's always complaining she can’t see a thing during ‘Bargain Hunt’. A telly  again , Arthur? You got her one last Christmas! She barely uses half the features on it. I think she mostly watches repeats of ‘Call the Midwife’. Well, it’s practical! Keeps her entertained. And the last one was smaller. This could be a proper smart telly. Connect to the internet, all that jazz. I think she’d appreciate something a bit more thoughtful, like a gardening thing.

…and honestly, lad, the price just jumped again. Another eighty quid! Eighty! For what, I ask you? For sitting in a garage most of the week? It’s daylight robbery, it is. Eighty quid? Cor, that  is  bad. What did they say when you phoned, Grandma? “Market fluctuations,” they said. “Increased risk profile.” Increased risk profile?! I’ve driven the same way for thirty years, haven’t had a bump, and now suddenly I’m a Formula One driver? Honestly. They’re preying on folks, they are. Is it ‘cos of Dad changing his car then? He said the new one's got a bigger engine. Partly, aye. They link it all, see. Even though  he’s  the named driver on his own policy. They just see ‘household, potential access’. It’s ridiculous. And it's not even a fancy car, your Dad's. Just a sensible estate. He needs the space for all your rugby kit! It  is  a big car. I nearly got squashed by it when I was cycling home from training last week. Oh, don't you start. He’s a careful driver, your Dad. It's these insurance companies, always looking for a way to squeeze more money out. Remember when I was looking at getting a little sporty number, years ago? A Mazda MX-5? Yeah, you showed me a picture once. It was red, wasn't it? Looked proper quick. It was lovely. But the insurance quote… well, let's just say it put paid to that dream pretty quick. They wanted more for the insurance than the car was worth! And I was a good driver then, too! Years of no claims. It’s all about algorithms and statistics these days, not common sense. Algorithms? What are them? Oh, it’s computer stuff, lad. They feed everything into a computer – your age, where you live, the car, your job… even what music you listen to, probably – and it spits out a price. Doesn’t take into account that I’ve lived in North Ferriby and Malton my whole life and know every single bend in these roads! So, is it cheaper for people who live in towns with loads of traffic? ‘Cos you’d think they’d be more likely to crash. You'd  think  so, wouldn’t you? But they look at things like population density, crime rates… everything. And younger drivers, they get it the worst.

...and honestly, the pressure’s been relentless. New security protocols, the Henderson account breathing down my neck, and young O’Malley still learning the ropes. It feels like I'm constantly putting out fires. It's not just  work , you know? It's… wearing me down.      Sounds rough, Dad. Like in those superhero movies, when the bad guy’s just constantly attacking? Is it like that? Like,  Suicide Squad  rough?      Not quite  Suicide Squad  rough, thankfully. Though some days… But really, it’s that constant feeling of responsibility. I was reading about this thing, mindfulness, and how they use apps to measure your heart rate variability, HRV they call it. Apparently, lower HRV indicates higher stress.      HRV? Sounds complicated. I just know I'm stressed when I can’t even string a sentence together properly. Or when Leo decides 3am is playtime. Speaking of which, I need another cup of tea.      It is a bit techy, but the idea is, it gives you a baseline. So you  know  when you’re pushing yourself too hard. It's not a perfect system, mind you. It’s just… trying to be proactive.      Could you, like, get an app for that? And then show me the numbers? I’m good with numbers.      I might, actually. Might be a useful thing to show your mother too, she’s amazing at handling everything but needs to look after herself too. Speaking of things, remember when Ireland was voting on the marriage equality thing? The feeling in the country was electric.      Oh, absolutely. A proper moment, that was. It felt like finally, things were moving in the right direction. And proper grown-up conversations happening, not just whispers.      Exactly. And it’s funny, thinking back, people were so passionate… comparing it to other countries. You could see the frequency of the word “marriage” and “equality” spiking on Google Trends. It was fascinating to watch.           Um… are you recording this?      Recording what? No, no! Why would I be recording this?      Don't be silly, love. Your Dad's not recording us. Just thinking out loud, that's all.      Absolutely not. Just… musing. I was listening to a podcast on the way home yesterday, a fellow was talking about communication. How we use – or  don't  use – words to express our emotions. And the importance of facial expressions.      Oh, those podcasts. I try, honestly I do. But Leo demands all my attention.

...Honestly, Dad, I just don’t get why you’re so obsessed with identifying every single bird. We’re trying to get to Grandma’s, not audition for  Springwatch ! Was that a…a sparrow? Honestly, they all look the same to me. And then you started rambling about how their flight patterns are similar to the approach of a 747. Seriously?      Now, now, Amelia. Your dad’s always been a spotter. It’s a good skill to have, pays attention to detail, like a midwife needs to. And he’s not wrong, you know. The angle of descent, the way they adjust for wind… it  is  like watching a miniature plane.      Yeah, but a plane’s way faster, Mum. And louder. And carries loads more people. You don’t see a sparrow landing at Heathrow, do ya?      Quite. Though thinking about Heathrow, the traffic control aspect  is  similar, in a very abstract sense. Managing pathways, avoiding collisions... It's all systems thinking, really.      Systems thinking?! Dad, you're a management consultant, not David Attenborough! And seriously, remember when we were driving through Italy last year? All those little hilltop villages... They’re what I want to talk about, not aerodynamics. They looked so peaceful. Proper postcard stuff.      Oh, Italy was lovely. Remember that little place near Assisi? The one with the olive oil shop? Beautiful. Though the driving was terrifying. Narrow roads, everyone beeping…and the weather! One minute glorious sunshine, the next a downpour. It's similar around here, to be fair. One minute it’s baking, next it’s drizzling. Typical Bolton weather.      Rain’s good for football, though. Means it’s a bit slippier. I’ve been practicing my slide tackles.      You need to be careful with those, lad. Don’t want a broken leg before you even get to try out for the school team. Speaking of which, how’s the law conversion course going, Amelia? Still thinking it’s what you want?      It's…intense. Honestly, it’s a massive jump from English Lit. I keep getting confused between metric and imperial. Like, if something weighs 2 kilograms, how many pounds is that again? Honestly, it's ridiculous, we're supposed to be sophisticated legal minds, not doing maths.      Around four and a half, love. It’s the same with mileage. Kilometers are easier, but everyone still uses miles over here, don’t they? It’s a mess, all thanks to that EU referendum malarkey.

… honestly, I just think the whole ‘cultured meat’ thing is a bit… unsettling. Like, grown in a lab? It feels… unnatural. Even more so than being vegetarian, which, you know, at least acknowledges the  life  that's been lived, even if it's ending for your dinner. But that’s the point, isn't it, Chloe? It  doesn’t  involve ending a life. No animal suffers. It’s just cells replicating. It’s potentially huge for the environment too, massively reducing land use and emissions. Think of the rainforests! I read an article… Mmm, rainforests are good. Though I’m with Chloe a little, it does sound a bit Black Mirror-esque. It's like, solving one ethical problem by creating a whole new existential one. Are we even  meant  to be doing that kind of thing? Exactly, Finn! And it still needs…stuff to grow, right? Aren’t the growth mediums often derived from animal products initially? So it’s not  completely  cruelty-free. Plus, I’m a pharmacy dispenser, I deal with vitamins all day. People think being vegetarian automatically means you’re getting everything you need. It’s so often not true. B12, iron… it’s a constant battle getting people to take supplements. That’s true about the supplements, and the initial growth mediums are a challenge, but those are solvable problems! They're working on plant-based alternatives. And honestly, the environmental impact of  conventional  meat is just so devastating, we have to explore solutions. I mean, remembering Aunt Maureen going on about her pheasant shoot last Christmas... the sheer glee. Honestly, it felt barbaric. Oh,  please  don’t remind me of Aunt Maureen’s pheasant shoot. She cornered me for twenty minutes explaining the ‘sport’ of it all. Said it was ‘controlling the population’. I just kept nodding and sketching a particularly miserable-looking pheasant.
