It's a weird one, isn't it? People are horrified by the idea of an abattoir, rightly so, but think hunting is… acceptable? It's still killing, just with more tweed involved. It's no better. And honestly, imagining perfectly good food squandered on that… it just feels… wasteful. I remember Grandma used to say ‘waste not, want not’. She’d have a fit if she saw how much food gets chucked away these days. Though she'd also tell me to eat more meat 'to put some colour in your cheeks’!

…Nah, I’m tellin’ ya, the delivery driver just left it on t’ doorstep. Right in plain sight! Anyone could’ve nicked it. Thankfully, it were just me mam’s new kettle. She’d ‘ave had a right go if that went missin’. A kettle? You're stressin' about a kettle? I ordered a graphics card last week and it’s still not ‘ere. Still ‘showin’ as ‘out for delivery’ since Tuesday. That’s proper money down the drain if it's gone walkies. Ooh, are you still waitin’ on that, Liam? That's rubbish! I ordered some new fairy lights from Amazon, and they were fine, came the next day. Though, to be fair, it's not exactly a high-value item. Aye, a graphics card is different. That's a proper investment, especially wi’ how expensive they are now. Did you pay extra for tracked delivery, Liam? Of course I did! What’s the point otherwise? I keep checkin’ the app, but it just keeps sayin’ the same thing. It’s doin’ me ‘ead in. I was hopin’ to get a few games sorted before Christmas. Thinkin’ I’ll just be stuck playin’ FIFA again. Christmas... Honestly, I'm dreading the whole shop. It’s always chaos in town. Especially now that everyone seems to do all their giftin’ online and then returns everything after Boxing Day. Aye, town's a nightmare. I'm thinkin' I'll just stick to gettin’ stuff on the internet this year. Less hassle. What are you gettin’ folks, Sarah? I’ve got a few bits. Got a new board game for me little cousin, she loves them. And I’m thinkin’ about gettin’ me dad one of those phone things… what are they called? The ones that find your keys. A Tile? You mean a Tile? Yeah, them’s good. Dad’ll love that if he's always losin’ stuff. He’s worse than a kid. Remember that time he lost his wallet…in his own house? Oh God, aye! He was convinced someone’d broken in. Turned out it was under a cushion on the sofa! Typical. Speaking of phones, did you see that new Samsung thing, Liam? Looks reet fancy. I saw somethin’ online. Spendin’ a fortune on a phone when I can barely afford to heat the ‘ouse feels a bit…wrong, dunnit? I don’t even really  need  a new phone.

… honestly, the paella was just… disappointing. You build it up in your head, right? All those prawns and saffron and… it was just a bit dry, a bit bland. Like someone had forgotten the paprika. Oh, you and your food critiques! Spain deserves better than that assessment, Liv. I thought you were supposed to be all about linguistic nuance, not… paella nuance. It’s all about observing detail, isn’t it? Whether it’s a subtle shift in vowel sounds or a slightly overcooked rice dish. Besides, it's not  just  the paella. It felt… touristy. Like they weren't even trying. Did you have a good time in Italy then? You were raving about Florence when you got back. Florence  was  incredible. It wasn’t the food specifically, although the gelato was a definite highlight – pistachio, obviously – but the whole atmosphere. Wandering around, stumbling across tiny family-run trattorias… that just felt authentic. Much more 'real' than some of the bigger Spanish resorts. Although, don't get me wrong, I'd go back to Spain. Just maybe not Valencia. See, that’s what I miss sometimes. That feeling of  finding  something. My last proper holiday felt like that, actually - when we went to Iceland with your Auntie Maureen. Remember? Oh,  god , Iceland. Maureen and her thermal underwear obsession. That was… an experience. She nearly froze a toe off trying to get the perfect Northern Lights shot. I know! She was adamant she needed to be  right  at the edge of the glacier, despite everyone telling her it was a terrible idea. Honestly, she’s a force of nature. But it was beautiful, wasn't it? So stark and otherworldly. Completely different to anything I've ever seen. More inspiring than anything I’ve found on a Mediterranean beach, anyway. Definitely. And it put everything into perspective. Like, all our little work dramas just feel… insignificant after you’ve stared into a volcanic crater. Speaking of work, they're starting to hint at restructuring in my department. It’s all very 'we're a family here' whilst simultaneously talking about 'optimising resources'. Oh, brilliant. That sounds… reassuring. They did that at the institute last year. Ended up with poor old Mr. Davies – he was the archivist – made redundant. Absolutely gutted, his family have been in Cambridge for generations. Honestly, these universities talk a good game about valuing heritage but… Exactly! It's all about the rankings and research impact these days.

… honestly, I just don’t get it, do you? Like, Dr. Ainsworth  specifically  said the reading was 'essential background' for today’s lecture, and then he didn’t mention a single thing from it! Not a peep! It's a right waste of time, innit? Three hours on Foucault when I’ve barely slept ‘cause I was trying to wrestle with Deleuze. Aye, well, that sounds about right for Ainsworth. He loves a good tangent, doesn’t he? Remember last semester with the whole thing about the history of buttons? Literally buttons. Completely derailed the seminar on post-structuralism. Don't even  start  me on the buttons! This is my degree, Liam! I’m paying nine grand a year to listen to him ramble about… whatever it was he rambled about today. I felt like I was back in school, just zoning out, drawing little doodles of sheep. Look, you’re brilliant, you always pick things up. One dodgy lecture isn't gonna ruin everything. You’ll be fine. You always are. Besides, you looked knackered yesterday. You should’ve just skipped it. Skipped it? And then what? Fall behind even more? It’s a vicious cycle. And knackered is an understatement. Honestly, I'm thinking of getting one of those massage chairs, you know, the ones that do everything? Knead your back, heat… the whole shebang. A massage chair? Right. That’s a bit… drastic, isn't it? For a bit of uni stress? Shouldn’t you be joining the library more, not investing in reclining luxury? It's not  just  uni stress, is it? It's work, it’s trying to see me mum, it's…everything. I need something that actively  undoes  the stress, not just pretends to help. A massage chair… feels proactive. Plus, think of you! You could use one after all them hours you spend hunched over your research. Oh, now you’re trying to butter me up. You are sneaky. I suppose a bit of back relief wouldn’t go amiss. This PhD is turning me into a proper hunchback. But seriously, they're expensive. They are, yeah. I’ve been looking at ones on finance. It's daft, I know, but I'm thinking long-term. Think of it as an investment in my sanity! And yours, obvs. Always thinking of me. You're a sweetheart. Alright, alright, I’ll entertain the idea of a household massage chair.

… honestly, I still think your Auntie Maureen’s trifle is a national treasure. Nobody,  nobody , makes a proper jelly like her. Though, bless her, she does go on a bit about the ‘young people these days’ not knowing the difference between custard and…well, anything yellow. She does, doesn’t she? It’s her signature tune. Though, Dad, you're not exactly a spring chicken yourself to be making pronouncements on generations. Speaking of which, did you see that report on the news about Calais? Absolutely dreadful. Awful. Just heartbreaking, really. All those people, desperate. I was explaining it to my Year 6 class today, trying to keep it age appropriate, but it’s hard, isn’t it? They see things. They ask difficult questions. Difficult is an understatement. It's a mess. A proper mess. I remember reading about things like this even when  I  was a lad, back in Southend. Never on this scale, mind you. Makes you wonder what the world’s coming to. Though, I suspect people have been saying that for centuries. Still, it feels…different now. Different and increasingly frustrating. The politicians just seem to be bickering. No real solutions. And the rhetoric! It’s so divisive. I just want people to be treated with decency, you know? Exactly. Decency. That’s all it boils down to. And help. They need help. Did anyone manage to get hold of young Liam? I haven’t heard back from him since he said he was volunteering with that charity down there. I texted him yesterday, no reply. He's probably swamped. He’s got such a good heart, that boy. Though I worry about him, getting involved in something so…intense. He always was a bit of a bleeding heart, your brother. Takes after his mother, that one. Now, speaking of intensity… this roast is looking rather splendid, if I do say so myself. Are the potatoes crispy enough, Sarah? They look perfect, Dad. Honestly, they always are. You’ve still got the touch, even after… well, after everything. They are lovely, Arthur. Really. You always did make the best roasties. Though I maintain my Yorkshire puddings are superior. Oh, here we go. The eternal Yorkshire pudding debate. Don't start that again, Margaret. Yours are… perfectly adequate. Adequate? That’s high praise coming from you! So, have we finalised plans for Mum’s birthday next month?

… honestly, the tile guy, absolute disaster. He claimed he’d done dozens of walk-in showers, but you’d never have known it. The falls were all wrong - pooling water everywhere! I had to get another bloke in to fix the mess, and  he  nearly had a heart attack looking at it. Honestly, these days, finding reliable tradespeople… it’s like finding hen’s teeth. Oh, you’re telling  me  about tradespeople, Alistair? You think Cairo prepared you for the Welsh plumbing? Because let me tell you, it's a different beast entirely. I'm renovating the downstairs loo at the moment – tiny little thing, mind you – but getting someone to just  quote  for the job has been a week-long saga. Cairo prepared me for a lot of things, David, but dodgy plumbing wasn’t high on the list. More… bureaucratic hurdles, shall we say. But yes, I see your point. It’s a universal problem, isn’t it? Everyone’s ‘too busy’ or ‘fully booked’ for the next six months. What are you planning for the loo, then? Keeping it simple? Simple-ish. My wife, Bronwen, has a vision. Apparently, “coastal chic” is the order of the day. Think pale blues, driftwood effect, the whole nine yards. I’m mostly concerned about fitting a little storage in – she’s a collector of…well, let’s just say ‘interesting’ hand soaps. Ah, yes. The hand soap enthusiast. A common breed. My wife, Penelope, is currently obsessed with kitchen islands. We’ve already got a perfectly serviceable kitchen, but  no . She’s been looking at magazines non-stop for months, pointing out all the things ours lacks. Granite worktops, a breakfast bar, a wine fridge… honestly, it’s a small kitchen! It’ll be crammed. Wine fridge, eh? Sounds like Penelope knows the important things in life. Bronwen's after a new kitchen too, eventually. Though she's more focused on colour schemes. She’s thinking sage green cabinets. Sage green! I told her it’ll look like a hospital ward, but she says it's 'soothing'. Women. Indeed. It’s a mystery. You know, Old Man Hemmings – retired classics professor, lives down the lane – he completely gutted his kitchen last year. Went for a minimalist, all-white affair. Looked rather sterile, if you ask me. He said his wife, Margaret, insisted on it. Apparently, she’s a devotee of Scandinavian design.

…and I’m tellin’ ya, the spice level was  criminal . Honestly, Sanjay nearly wept. He’s a man who thinks black pepper is hot, y’know? But it was grand, once you got past the initial… incineration. Incineration? Sounds intense. Was it, like, Vindaloo intense? Oh, don’t encourage him, Leo. Your Uncle Sean exaggerates everything. It was a bit spicy, yes, but Sanjay just isn’t used to real flavour. Now, now, Sarah! It  was  hot! It felt like tiny dragons were dancin' a jig on my tongue. Though, speaking of feelin' things… little Finn here tried eatin’ a bit of the Christmas tree stand the other day. Shiny!  What ?! He ate… metal? Seriously? Aye. Tiny bit. Nearly gave your Auntie Sarah a heart attack. Thankfully, he spat most of it out. Said it didn’t taste like biscuits. Don’t remind me. I practically wrestled it out of his mouth. Honestly, the things they put in their mouths… it’s a wonder any of them survive. It’s like he thinks he has superpowers. “Mommy, I can eat rocks!” No, darling, you  can’t  eat rocks. Superpowers would be cool. I wish I had one. Like, super speed. Then I could finish my history homework in, like, five seconds. It's all about horrible history at the moment. I got a book, right? It's got pictures of people being… well, horrible. Horrible History, eh? Good stuff, that. Though, I’d rather be lookin' at biology, to be honest. Fascinatin' stuff, the way things work. Reminds me, we still haven’t sorted out Leo’s birthday. It’s comin’ up quick, isn’t it? It is. He mentioned something about wanting to go to that park thing, with the bouncy castle? Yeah! The Summer Fun Fair! It’s on Saturday. Can we go? Please? They’ve got a massive slide and face painting. We'll see. Depends if I can get away from work. I need to pop down to the bank on Friday too. Remember that night deposit box we were talking about for the extra cash? I should probably get that sorted. It's a pain havin' to bring it all in during the day. That’s a good idea, Sean. Less to worry about. Maybe we could make a day of it? Go for lunch afterward? Sound’s grand. We could try that new Indian place down by the river.

…and honestly, the price of pumpkins these days! Back in my day, you could get a good one for, oh, a shilling or two. Now they’re charging… well, I daren’t even look. Makes a man feel right old, it does. Oh, Arthur, you  always  say that. Everything was cheaper “back in your day”. Though you’re not wrong about the pumpkins, are you? I saw one at the supermarket, nearly a fiver! For something you carve up and then throw away. Seems a bit daft, doesn’t it? It’s the whole commercialisation of it, isn’t it? Halloween used to be bobbing apples and dressin’ up in sheets. Now it’s full-sized inflatable ghouls and themed everything. Lily, are you excited for Halloween at school? Yeah, kinda. We’re doing a spooky story writing competition, which is good. But everyone’s costumes are getting  so  elaborate. Chloe’s mum is making her a full-on Medusa costume. With snakes and everything! Mine’s just… a witch. A witch is a good ‘un! Simple and effective. Always a classic. We didn’t bother with fancy dress much when I were a lad. Just a bit of face paint if you were lucky. Mostly it was about guising, going door to door for sweets. Though Mrs. Higgins down the road used to give out apples. Dreadful things. Oh, don’t I remember Mrs. Higgins’ apples! Hard as rock. You’d think you’d broken a tooth trying to bite into one. Still, it was the thought that counted. Lily, have you been down to the stables recently? How’s Bess going? She’s good! I had a lesson on Saturday. We did some jumping, which was fun, but she’s a bit cheeky sometimes. She keeps trying to stop and eat the grass. Mr. Davies says I need to be firmer with her. Horses are brilliant at testing boundaries. They sense weakness, you see. It's all about establishing yourself as the leader. Similar to Year 8, actually… Leadership. Hmph. When I were a lad, leadership meant following the foreman down the fields. There weren’t much choice involved. Different world, y’know. Though I did once try and lead old Dobbin around the village… didn’t end well. Nearly ended up in Old Man Hemmings’ prize-winning roses. Oh, Arthur! You and your adventures. Remember that time you tried to build a raft on the River Yare?

… honestly, it’s ridiculous. This traffic is just… stationary. I thought leaving at 8am would be early enough, but clearly not. Are we even  moving  at all, Dad? Not a jot, love. Been like this since we hit the A31. Should’ve known. Everyone and their dog seems to be going to this steam fair. Lovely day for it, though, isn’t it? Shame about the congestion. Reminds me of trying to get out of London on a bank holiday…chaos. It’s alright for you two, you can just sit and chat. My back is killing me. Eight hours on my feet yesterday, lifting Mrs. Higgins… she insists on trying to move furniture herself. Honestly, the things I see. She was complaining about the council again, too. Said they’ve still not fixed her leaky roof. Oh, poor thing. Councils are awful, aren't they? Always promising things and never delivering. It's the same with housing. Grandma would have absolutely hated this wait, she’d be going on about needing to get to a proper cuppa. Your grandma had a point, she did. Always knew how to make a fuss when it was needed. And this housing situation… a complete mess. Used to be you could rely on the council to look after people. Now? It’s all private companies, and they only care about profit. Remember old Mr. Davies down the road? Promised a bungalow when his wife passed, waited five years and ended up in that pokey flat above the chip shop. That’s awful. It's just… where are older people supposed to go? Independent living is expensive, and care homes… well, they aren’t exactly known for being luxurious. Mum, do they offer much in the way of adapted housing at Mrs. Higgins’ place? She’s getting more unsteady on her feet. Not enough, not by a long shot. They’ve got a waiting list a mile long for the bungalows with the walk-in showers and grab rails. And even then, they’re tiny. She’d be losing half her belongings. They keep saying there’s a funding issue, cuts and all that. I’m telling you, it’s heartbreaking. It’s a disgrace. When  I  was younger, the council built proper estates, good quality council housing. Not this flimsy stuff they put up now. Solid brick, decent gardens… places people could be proud of.

… honestly, I’m just picturing rows and rows of runner beans, climbing everywhere. It’s a bit ambitious, I know, for a first year, but I’ve been watching Monty Don, and it all looks so  easy . Monty Don makes everything look easy, darling. He has a whole team of gardeners, probably. And remember, you’ve got a fairly small plot at the allotment, haven’t you? It’s not exactly a sprawling estate. It’s… respectable. About ten poles, I think. Enough for a really good go, I reckon. But I’m already overwhelmed thinking about the planning. You’ve done this before, haven't you? Your dad had an allotment for years. Any pearls of wisdom? Years and years. Dad was obsessed. Okay, first thing: soil. Have you had a chance to even  look  at the soil yet? Is it clay, sandy, loamy…? You need to know what you’re working with before you start dreaming of prize-winning marrows. I poked around a bit. It felt…compact. Not fluffy, definitely. So, probably clay-ish? I was thinking of getting some compost delivered, loads of it. Is that the right approach? Compost is  always  the right approach. But you’ll need more than just piling it on top. Clay needs loosening up, improving the drainage. Digging it in is essential - backbreaking, I know – but vital. And maybe some grit? That helps with aeration. Ugh, digging. Already dreading that. I was hoping for a low-dig approach, you know, like no-dig gardening. Less effort. No-dig is amazing once you’ve  built  the soil up. It’s not really viable for a first-year allotment plot, especially if it’s heavy clay. You'll just end up with compacted layers. Trust me. Dad tried a 'low-effort' year once. It didn't end well. Mostly weeds. Point taken. Okay, digging it is. What about what to  actually  grow? I’ve got a list somewhere… it includes tomatoes, obviously. And courgettes. And I really want to try growing some unusual varieties of lettuce. Tomatoes are good. Courgettes are… prolific. You’ll be giving them away to everyone you know. That’s not necessarily a bad thing, but plan accordingly. And unusual lettuce is lovely, but don’t forget the staples. Potatoes are a good bet for beginners, they’re pretty forgiving. And beetroot is surprisingly easy. Potatoes… hmm. I hadn’t really thought about them.

… honestly, I just think Liam’s a bit clueless, y’know? He keeps texting me askin’ if I’m alright ‘cause I haven’t been on his Insta story for, like, a day. A  day , Elsie! It’s proper weird. Oh, Liam. He does sound… intense. It’s just how people are now, isn’t it? Everything’s documented. Are you bothered? No, not bothered, just… draining. Like, I went for a walk down by the canal yesterday, proper needed some headspace, and I didn't even  think  to get my phone out. Beautiful sunset an’ all. He'd have had a meltdown if he knew I hadn’t ‘shared the experience’ with him. It’s performance, really. Everyone crafting their online persona. Though I must admit, I fall into that trap sometimes. Saw Amelia’s holiday photos – Santorini looked incredible. Makes you feel a bit… lacking, doesn't it? Lacking? Nah. I'd rather be breathin’ fresh air down by the Don than postin’ pictures of myself lookin’ tanned. Different strokes, I suppose. Speaking of doin’ stuff, are you still on for that gig at The Wool Market on Saturday? I managed to snag us tickets. They’re that new indie band, ‘Static Bloom’. Oh, amazing! Yes, definitely. I’d almost forgotten! It's been so busy with uni work. Honestly, I feel like I’m drowning in essays. What’s it like back home? Is your mum still badgering you about "proper" jobs? Don’t even  start  me on me mum. It’s constant. “University’s all well and good, love, but what’s the plan after? You need something to  fall back on .” She thinks I’m gonna end up a professional dog walker or somethin’. Honestly, she just doesn't get it. Classic Mum. Mine’s the same, though more subtly. She’s all about “career trajectory" and "networking opportunities”. It’s exhausting. It’s like, can't we just enjoy being… twenty-something and figuring things out? Exactly! And The Wool Market’s a good start to figuring things out, innit? It's not a bankin’ job, but it is fun. Plus, Old Man Hemmings always sneaks me a free sausage roll. You and your sausage rolls. Alright, Saturday then. Shall we meet at The Red Lion beforehand? Say… seven? I need to brief myself on Static Bloom, apparently they’re quite the talking point. Seven’s grand.

Right, right, gotta flank…Nah, got smoked. Again. Honestly, this Apex is a right carry on, innit? You say that every time, Liam. You just need to relax, stop rushing in like a div. You're too eager for the action. Honestly, I don’t get the appeal. All that shooting and looting… give me a good strategy game any day. Something with a bit of  thinking  involved. Like Civilization. Yeah, but that's slow burn, isn’t it? Apex is just… instant gratification. Plus, the movement's sick. You can just  fly  around. Makes a change from Luton, lets ya feel free. ‘Relax’? Easy for you to say, Chloe, you’re brilliant at this stuff. You always land with decent loot. I spend five minutes looking for a half-decent shield and then get downed by someone with a Kraber. It’s a joke. That's 'cause you land hot every time! And you panic-loot. I saw you yesterday, grabbing anything that glittered, didn’t even check the level. Honestly, it's painful to watch. Remember that time you tried to use a Level 1 Backpack against a fully kitted Wraith? Okay, okay, point taken. It was a bad day. Speaking of bad days, anyone see that new episode of  Wednesday ? Proper dark, that. Jenna Ortega is class. I did, yeah. It's a bit… much for me, though. I prefer stuff a bit less grim. I’ve been re-watching  Parks and Recreation . It's just so wholesome. Always a good vibe. You lot wouldn’t understand. Too much action for your tastes. Nah, I get the wholesome vibe. I've binged that a few times. But  Wednesday  is just…stylish. And the soundtrack slaps. I'm more of a true crime doc kinda guy myself. Gets me thinking, you know? True crime? Eesh, bit morbid that, isn't it? I saw this bloke at college the other day, wearing a t-shirt with a serial killer on it. Proper weirdo. Actually, talking about weirdos, remember Old Man Hemmings from sixth form? Always going on about pigeons. Oh god, Mr. Hemmings! He truly believed they were government drones. He’d spend his lunch break trying to photograph them. And then lecture anyone who got too close. That’s mental. Sounds like something out of a film. Speaking of films, anyone been to the cinema recently? I was thinking of seeing that new  Dune  film, but everyone says it's three hours long.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  what Patricia’s done now. Honestly, the woman. Going on about needing a ‘digital detox’ and then spends the entire weekend glued to that blooming TikTok! It’s beyond me. Honestly. Oh, Gran, you know Patricia. She’s always been a bit…hypocritical, hasn’t she? Though, a digital detox  is  a good idea, in theory. I feel permanently attached to my phone at work, honestly. It’s constant emails, production schedules… it’s relentless. Relentless! That’s the word alright. When I was working, it was a phone call, maybe a memo. A  memo , mind you! Not all this instant messaging. And Patricia, pretending she's above it all… she was showing me dances she’d learned! Dances, I tell you! I haven’t seen her move like that since… well, never! Oh, Gran! You’re terrible. But yeah, it’s addictive. I tried to limit myself last night, decided to watch a film instead. Have you seen anything good lately? I’m completely dried up for recommendations. Everything on Netflix feels so… samey. Oh, films. Hmm. I watched one of those, what do you call them… period dramas? With all the corsets and the handsome lords. It was alright. Kept me occupied. Though I kept getting muddled with all the names, they all sound the same to me, really. 'Bridgerton' or something? Your mother loves that one, she's always going on about it. 'Bridgerton’ is good, yeah, but it’s a bit fluffy, isn’t it? I need something with a bit more… grit. I saw 'Everything Everywhere All at Once' a few weeks ago. Absolutely blew my mind. It’s a bit chaotic, but brilliant. 'Everything Everywhere All at Once'? Sounds… exhausting just saying it. Is it one of those science fiction things? I can't stand all that flashing light and spaceships. Reminds me of that awful 'Star Wars'… all that beeping and whatnot. It's  kind  of science fiction, but it's more about a woman trying to connect with her family. It's really emotionally resonant, and the visuals are amazing. It’s nothing like 'Star Wars', honestly. You'd probably like Michelle Yeoh in it, she's fantastic. Michelle… who now? Oh, well. Maybe. I prefer a good Agatha Christie, myself. Something I can follow. All these modern films… you need a degree to understand them!

...Honestly, the sheer  audacity  of him thinking he could pull that off! Like, pretending to be a marine biologist after watching Blue Planet once. It was peak ‘Undateables’ material, I swear.      Oh, you’re brutal, Beth! But seriously, you’ve had some dodgy dates, haven’t you? Though, a marine biologist…that IS a stretch. Was it the one you met through that magazine subscription box? The ‘Artisan Eats and Eligible Bachelors’ one?      The very same. And don’t even get me started on the “artisan” part. The ‘eats’ were a slightly stale biscuit and a promotional leaflet for sheep cheese. Anyway, enough about my dating disasters. How was the interview? You were so stressed about it all last week.      It went…okay. Not amazing. The woman interviewing me, she was lovely, proper down to earth. But the job itself feels a bit... corporate. All talk of ‘synergy’ and ‘leveraging content’. It's editing, yeah, but for a financial services company. It's not exactly  literary , is it?      No, no it isn’t. And you’ve got such a good eye for detail, such a passion for language. You deserve something more… creative. Remember when you were talking about freelancing full-time?      I do. But the thought of the instability terrifies me, especially with rent in London being what it is. My Nan keeps sending me articles about clever investments, but I just glaze over. She thinks I need to be buying property, not DVDs of old films.      Old films are important. They tell you things.      Exactly! See, Anwen gets it. You need your comfort things, especially when work's a bit bleak. We should all have a massive DVD night soon. I’ve got the new Wes Anderson.      Ooh, yes! And maybe order some proper takeaway? Not sheep cheese this time…      Absolutely not. Pizza is mandatory. Actually, speaking of mandatory, we  need  to book that spa day we talked about. I’ve been running on fumes lately. This language research is fascinating, honestly, charting dialectal shifts in East London is genuinely brilliant, but it’s  exhausting . All that recording and transcribing…      I’m with you. I’ve been feeling completely frazzled. Constant deadlines, copy edits, plus trying to keep up with everything going on with Sarah and Liam. They’re moving again! This time to Bristol.      Bristol! That’s ages away. I’m going to miss them terribly. They’re the only ones who really understand my obsession with phonetics.

… honestly, I just don’t get why it has to make  that  noise. It sounds like a badger’s trapped inside, trying to get out. And it’s a new machine! Remember how much we debated getting a Bosch? Supposedly the quietest on the market. Lies, all lies. Aye, well, marketing, innit? Always selling a dream. Is it doing it on the spin cycle again? That’s usually when it goes into full badger impersonation. Worse. It was on the eco wash.  Eco ! Supposed to be whisper quiet. It sounded like it was about to launch itself into orbit. I nearly had a heart attack folding the towels, honestly. I’m starting to think we should just get a washboard and go back to basics. Now  that’s  a picture. You down at the launderette, scrubbing like your grandma. Though, to be fair, she always said modern washing machines weren't proper cleanin’. She’d boil everything. She wasn’t wrong, was she? Everything smelled aggressively floral, but it  was  clean. Speaking of clean… are you making that lentil soup again? The kitchen smells amazing. Spot on. Figured we could do with somethin’ hearty. Trying to use up all the vegetables before your mum and dad come down next week. Your dad’s a bit of a fussy eater, isn’t he? You have no idea. He’ll politely eat everything, then comment on how his mother made it ‘just a  wee  bit better’. It’s a running joke now. And he’ll ask about the washing machine, guaranteed. “Is it a good one, lass? Your mother always said…” Of course he will. It’s a Dad thing. Like asking if you’re wearing enough layers. Honestly, I was bracing myself for the ‘are you gettin’ enough iron in your diet?’ lecture last time. Oh, that’s a classic. He's concerned, bless him. It's just… exhausting. Anyway, lentils sound perfect. Did you manage to get through to my sister about the film night? Aye, she’s confirmed. She’s bringing that ridiculous horror film she’s obsessed with. The one with the… sentient scarecrows? Oh, no. No, no, no. I specifically said no horror. I haven't slept properly since I accidentally watched ‘The Ring’ when I was 14. She said it's “atmospheric” and “a metaphor for societal anxieties.” Honestly, she gets that from an English degree. It’s still a scarecrow coming to life, Liam!

…and honestly, the estate agent was practically giddy. "Demand is  high ," she chirped. High for what? Tiny boxes for extortionate prices? It's madness, absolutely madness. Not like Dublin at all, even back in the boom. Though, admittedly, that was a different kind of crazy. It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? I was looking at places near my sister in Guildford – properly needing a renovation, garden the size of a postage stamp – and they were asking for… well, I nearly choked on my tea. It’s the ‘southern pull’ again, isn’t it? Everyone wanting to be near London, driving up prices for the rest of us. Exactly. And it's not just London. Brighton, Oxford… even cities like Bristol have become totally unaffordable. I was reading an article about it only yesterday. Blaming a lack of housing stock, naturally. But it's more than that. It’s investment, isn’t it? Foreign investment, people buying up properties as assets, leaving them empty. Driving locals out. That’s it precisely. I mean, look at this little village, Hunsonby. So peaceful, beautiful countryside… but even  here  the prices are creeping up. People fleeing the south, thinking they’re getting a bargain, and driving up the local market. Still cheaper than Guildford, I suppose, but not by much anymore. It’s… frustrating. Being retired, you'd think I wouldn't be bothered, but I  do  worry about things for you two. Don’t worry about us, honestly. We're being sensible. We're looking at places further afield, maybe even back towards Birkenhead. It’s not glamorous, but at least it’s realistic. And Mum – you were telling me about that article on the VW emissions scandal again? Is it still rumbling on? Oh, it  always  rumbles on, dear. It’s utterly appalling, isn't it? The sheer scale of the deception. Millions of cars… deliberately programmed to cheat emissions tests. I was reading about the latest fines they’re facing. Billions! And they tried to wriggle out of it for years. I mean, as a maths teacher, the calculated nature of the fraud just… it gets to me. The algorithms, the deliberate manipulation of data… it’s a betrayal of trust. The thing that gets me is the arrogance. Thinking they could get away with it. Typical corporate behaviour, I suppose. They probably factored in the fines as a cost of doing business.

…No, I’m telling you, Arthur, it wasn’t a deliberate slight. Old Mrs. Higgins just… forgets things, bless ‘er. She meant well with the lemon drizzle, even if it  was  a bit dry. Honestly, getting flustered about a cake. Flustered? I weren’t flustered, Reginald. I were politely pointing out it tasted like sawdust! And she looked right offended, she did. Said her mum used to make it exactly the same way. As if that makes it palatable! It’s upsetting people for the sake of a soggy bottom, that’s what it is. Oh, don’t be so dramatic, Arthur. You know she’s sensitive. And Reginald’s right, it wasn’t meant to cause offence. Honestly, you’d think she’d personally invented the lemon drizzle. Exactly, Pat. It’s just… she expects a bit of deference, doesn't she? Being one of the ‘originals’ on the estate and all. Reminds me a bit of dealing with planning committees, actually. You have to tread carefully. Though at least with them, there was a bit of logic behind the fuss. Speaking of fuss, has anyone had a proper look at their pension statements yet? Mine’s landed, and it’s… underwhelming, to say the least. Underwhelming? Mine hasn’t even  arrived  yet! And I need that money, I do. Keeping on top of these bills… it’s a nightmare, that is. Especially with the price of everything shooting up. We need to move, Reginald, truly we do. This flat's getting smaller by the day. Move where, Arthur? The housing situation is a disaster. Everywhere’s building these poky little boxes, all crammed together. Remember when young Tim was looking for a place near Norwich? Couldn't find a thing he could afford. All these new developments… they're building up, not out, and they’re all the same ghastly beige. It’s ruining the countryside. It’s just… difficult, isn't it? This whole getting older thing. One minute you're pottering about, the next you're worrying about pensions and whether you can afford a bit of heating. I was looking at B&Bs in Cromer the other day, just for a week, mind. A change of scene. But they want a fortune! Bed and breakfasts? Pat, at our age? You’ll have your back going, lugging suitcases up narrow stairs. Plus, they're not built for people with a bit of a… wobble.

… honestly, Mr. Davies is taking the mick. Like, a fifteen-page essay on the evolutionary advantages of bipedalism? Who  needs  to know that? It's just… tedious. Tell me about it. Biology is relentless. At least History gives you a bit of gossip, you know? Kings having affairs and stuff. This is just bone structures and… and why we stopped being monkeys. Which, by the way, we  didn’t  come from monkeys. Everyone gets that wrong. Yeah, that’s the classic misunderstanding. Common ancestor, innit? Not directly from monkeys. It’s like… cousins, not grandparents. Right. Basic evolution. Although, the whole thing makes you think, doesn’t it? Like, what's  our  evolutionary advantage? Apart from being able to order overpriced cappuccinos in a Tesco café. Fair point. Probably just being good at arguing on the internet. Speaking of which, did you guys see that video of old Mrs. Higgins trying to use TikTok? It went viral. No way! Mrs. Higgins? The one who yells at pigeons? Brilliant. Send it in the group chat. Seriously though, the internet is wild. One minute you’re watching cat videos, the next you’re embroiled in some debate about… I don't know… gender roles. Oh god, don't even go there. I had a proper argument with my cousin over feminism yesterday. He was saying it’s gone too far. Oh, here we go. What did you say? I was like, “Too far? Women were legally considered property for centuries, mate! A little equality isn’t ‘too far’.” It just feels… basic human rights, you know? Totally. It’s just frustrating when people don’t get it. It's not about hating men, it's about fairness. My sister gets so much stick just for wanting to be an engineer. People assume she can’t do it because she’s a girl. It’s ridiculous. It’s the same with everything, isn't it? Like, if I’m interested in art, suddenly I'm 'not very masculine' or whatever. People just want to box you in. It's also weird how quickly things get racial too. You mention anything about social justice, and suddenly someone’s calling someone else ‘woke’ and shouting about ‘reverse racism’. Exactly! It's exhausting. It feels like people  want  to be offended. It’s like they’re looking for a reason to be awful. And then the whole religion thing gets thrown in… it just spirals.

…and honestly, the whole thing was remarkably straightforward. They said the keyhole surgery meant a much faster recovery, and they weren’t wrong. Still a bit tender, mind you, but nothing like what I expected. They had me up and walking the next day! Goodness me! Keyhole, is it? Sounds a bit futuristic, that. I still reckon a good, proper operation… well, at least you  know  they’ve had a good look then, don’t you? Though I suppose less mess is always good. Still, waking up after an op… it’s never pleasant. Pleasant? Doreen, dear, when have operations  ever  been pleasant? I remember when Arthur had his hip done… he swore the anaesthetist was a right comedian, kept accidentally calling him ‘Margaret’. He was furious! Oh, I remember that! Arthur went purple with rage! Typical Arthur, though. Couldn’t take a joke if his life depended on it. Speaking of needing things fixing, I’ve got to get the car MOT’d next week. And new tyres. The bloke at the garage says they’re bald as coots. Oh, the MOT. A necessary evil. You’d think after all these years, cars would just…maintain themselves. It's like everything these days needs constant attention. They’ve put me on these new tablets, too, after the operation. Supposed to prevent infections. They’re enormous! Honestly, feel like I'm swallowing horse pills. Infections are nasty things. Mrs. Higgins down the road, she got an infection after a little cut on her leg… ended up in hospital for weeks. They had to keep cutting away at it. Terrible. You just have to be so careful. Are you keeping the wound clean? Meticulously. And I’m slathering it with antiseptic. My mum's been on at me constantly, too. “Don’t overdo it, Penelope, but don’t underdo it!” Honestly, mothers. They never stop, do they? Even when you’re forty-something! Mine still thinks I need a cardigan when it’s seventy degrees! Still, she means well. Remember when you and Daniel went skiing in Austria? She nearly had a fit. Oh, don't remind me! "Too dangerous!" she said. As if accounts management isn’t dangerous enough. Although, skiing  is  a bit mad, isn't it? Hurtling down a mountain on planks of wood… Mad? It’s glorious! Used to go every year with the lads. Though my knees wouldn't stand a chance of it now.

…and so, the ships weren’t just carrying goods, Leo. They were carrying people. People who were  forced  to be there. Taken from their homes, families broken apart. Does that sound fair, sweetheart? No. But why did they take them? Was it a game? It wasn’t a game, Thomas. It was… a very, very bad thing. People in those days – a long, long time ago – believed it was okay to own other people. To treat them like things. They wanted people to work for them, to grow crops like sugar and cotton, and they didn't want to pay them. Like when I have to tidy my room and I don’t  want  to? It's…not quite the same, darling. Tidying your room is a bit annoying, definitely, but you choose to do it eventually, don’t you? And Mummy doesn’t  own  you. These people, they had no choice. They were kidnapped, put on those ships, and forced to work endlessly. They weren't allowed to choose. Endless? Like forever? Well, for a very long time, yes. And because it was so awful, many didn't survive the journey. Or the work. It was called slavery. It happened in America, mostly, but also in lots of other places, and Britain was… well, Britain was involved in it. Which is something we should be ashamed of. Ashamed? What’s ashamed? It means feeling very sad and sorry for something bad that happened. Like hurting someone’s feelings. We’re ashamed because people from Britain helped make slavery happen. It wasn’t right then, and it isn’t right now. My soldier fights bad guys. Was this like fighting bad guys? That’s a… a good way to think about it, actually. Later on, people  did  fight against slavery. There was a terrible war in America, called the Civil War. Lots of people fought to end it, to give those people freedom. It was a very bloody war, Thomas. Lots of people died. Like in the books with all the knights? Similar, but…real. This wasn't a story, it really happened. People were really hurting each other. And it wasn't just  one  war, you see. Throughout history, there have been wars over all sorts of terrible things. Sometimes over land, sometimes over money, sometimes just because people were cruel. Cruel? Like when Ben took my red car? Yes, a bit like that, but on a much, much bigger scale, Thomas.

…and honestly, the storylines are just getting  ridiculous . Honestly, ‘The Crown’ used to be so meticulously researched, now it's pure fabrication. They've taken so much liberty with things, it’s hardly history anymore. You’re telling me, Diane. It’s entertainment, love. Don't get your nurse’s cap in a twist over historical accuracy. They need to  sell  it, don't they? Drama sells. I kind of agree with Mum, though. It feels…disrespectful, almost. Especially with recent events. It’s hard not to compare, and when they're getting details so wrong… Disrespectful? Bit strong, isn’t it, Chloe? It's telly. Though, I did read an article saying the actress playing the Princess Royal isn’t quite capturing her…stoicism. She's a bit  too  smiley. Stoicism? What’s that, fancy talk for not grumbling? Princess Anne's always been a proper one, hasn’t she? No fuss. Mind you, back in my catering days, we did a function for her once. She barely touched her vol-au-vents. Proper picky, she was. Oh, Ken! You always have a story. Vol-au-vents! Fancy that. But seriously, the way they've portrayed Charles… it's just… unfair. Well, he’s hardly been a shrinking violet, has he? All those letters to the government... Still, the media are hardly kind to anyone in that family. It's the constant scrutiny. I was reading about how difficult it must be for Prince William and Kate now with everything happening. They're trying to modernize, but they're constantly being pulled back by tradition. Tradition's important, isn't it? Keeps things grounded. Though, a bit of updating never hurt anyone. Did you hear old Mrs. Higgins next door got a new dog? A little pug. Apparently, it's causing havoc. Oh, not another one! That's the third dog on the street. Honestly, the barking is driving me up the wall. I’m trying to get some peace and quiet so I can finish my book. This new Ruth Ware is a proper page-turner, you know. All twisty and clever. Books, eh? Always preferred a good crossword myself. Keeps the brain ticking. Though, my eyes aren’t what they used to be. Speaking of ticking, saw Barry down the pub yesterday. Said he’s off to Spain with Maureen next month. All-inclusive, apparently. Good for them.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Tupperware is just… astonishing. Honestly, Leo, you’ve got more containers than a science lab! Right, okay, plates go  here … and Elsie, darling, could you maybe pass me the mugs? Carefully now. Mummy, is Harry Potter better than George Stephenson? George Stephenson built  trains ! Trains are way cooler! They go  choo choo ! Well, that’s a big question, isn’t it? They’re… different sorts of brilliant. Harry Potter is brilliant because he’s magical and has adventures. George Stephenson was brilliant because he  made  things happen in a different way. He figured out how to make trains work, which totally changed how people travelled and how things were delivered. But Harry can fly on a broomstick! Trains are faster! They can carry loads and loads of people! Like, ALL of Year 3! That’s true, trains  can  carry a lot of people. Though I suspect Harry could probably apparate Year 3 somewhere even quicker, if he wanted to. Now, Leo, are you pretending to be a train again? I think I can hear a 'choo choo'… I AM a train! I’m the Rocket! George Stephenson built the Rocket! It was the first really fast one. Miss Davies showed us a picture. She did, did she? Good on Miss Davies. He was a remarkable man, really. Born in a tiny little cottage, practically no schooling, and yet he became  the  father of railways. It’s a lovely story about working hard and being clever. Did you know he started by mending shoes? Shoes? That’s boring. It might seem boring now, but it was how he earned money for his family. And while he was mending shoes, he was also thinking about machines, about how things worked. He was fascinated by engines, even the early steam engines used in mines. That's where he got his ideas from. It's like… building with Lego, but on a much, much bigger scale! Can we build a train track with the Lego? A  really  big one? We absolutely can. After the dishwasher is unloaded, maybe. That's the deal. Elsie, could you grab those glasses? Thank you, sweetheart. Now, back to George Stephenson. He didn't just build the Rocket, he also figured out how to build the  tracks  properly, so the trains wouldn't derail. That’s important, wouldn’t you agree? You don't want a train flying off the rails!

… honestly, I reckon Liam’s just salty ‘cos I beat him  again  at Words With Friends. He’s been going on about how ‘unfair’ my vocabulary is for like, two days. It’s just… I read a lot for uni, innit? Doesn't mean I’m cheating. Liam always gets competitive. Remember when we were kids and it was Monopoly? Absolute meltdown. Honestly, a tiny bit of vocab isn't cheating. Though, you  do  have a knack for finding those triple word score spots. He’s just embarrassed, that’s all. He tries so hard to sound clever. Speaking of hard work, this supper club thing is properly taking off, which is brilliant, but… I had a message from someone asking about, like, food hygiene certificates and insurance. All that legal stuff. Nightmare. Crikey. Sounds stressful, love. Over here, it’s just burnt milk and demanding customers. Old Mrs. Higgins wanted decaf, soy, extra foam,  and  a sprinkle of cinnamon at 7am this morning. Nearly lost it. Legal stuff is always a pain. You’ve got that mate, Sarah, who did law, haven’t you? Maybe she could give you a quick pointer, Caz? Saves you getting ripped off by a solicitor. Good shout, Alfie. Sarah’s a lifesaver. I’m making a quick gravy, by the way. Got a proper good recipe, Nana gave it to me. You lot want some with your roast? It’s got a splash of port in it, makes it lovely. Ooh, yes please! Nana’s gravy is legendary. Right, I’m thinking I need to look into public liability insurance. And maybe a food hygiene course – wouldn't hurt, even if it’s not legally required yet. It’s all a bit frightening when it comes down to it, running your own thing. Tell me about it. I’m thinking of chucking it in actually. This café is… it’s just draining me. The manager’s a proper piece of work. He’s constantly breathing down our necks about latte art and upselling muffins. Like, seriously? People just want a coffee! Really? That sounds grim, mate. You've been there ages, haven't you? What would you do instead? I dunno. Maybe try and get a gig in a proper coffee roastery. Something where I can actually  talk  about coffee, not just memorise a script about ‘aromatic notes’ and ‘balanced acidity’. It’s all fluff.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of detentions Mr. Harrison handed out this morning was ridiculous. Twelve! Over a spelling mistake on a history worksheet. Twelve! It just feels… punitive, doesn’t it? Like he's trying to make a point, rather than actually  teaching  them. Twelve is… a lot. Maybe he had a bad morning? My little sister's teacher does that sometimes. Though it's usually triggered by someone forgetting their PE kit, not historical inaccuracies. A bad morning? Every. Single. Morning it’s something. Anyway, enough about Harrison. How was your weekend, Anya? Did you manage to get out to that craft fair you were talking about? It was good, thank you. And yes, I did! It was… surprisingly busy. Lots of knitted things. Very… autumnal. I actually bought some yarn to try and finally finish that scarf I started last November. You know, the one I keep saying I’ll finish? Oh, we all have one of those! I started a cross-stitch of the Buckinghamshire countryside about three years ago. It’s currently about a quarter done. Life just… gets in the way, doesn't it? Especially with children. How’s Leo doing? Is he still obsessed with dinosaurs? Completely obsessed. It’s all roaring and ‘T-Rex is the king!’ currently. He’s started building elaborate forts in the living room, declaring them ‘Jurassic Parks’. It’s… chaotic, but adorable. He started school properly last month. It's been a big adjustment for him, and for me, honestly. Oh, the first proper school year. That  is  a big jump. My Thomas went through a phase of clinging to my leg for the first two weeks. Absolute heartbreak. It gets easier, though. They adjust, and you get used to the empty mornings – eventually! What about you, are you managing okay with the drop-offs and pickups? It’s… challenging. The traffic around here is dreadful. And coordinating with work is difficult. I'm trying to streamline things at the reprographics department – new filing system, automated ordering… It’s a lot, plus the usual IT glitches. It feels like I’m constantly firefighting. Tell me about it. This job... it's rewarding, sometimes, genuinely helping the kids when they need it, but the cover supervision workload is increasing all the time. Mrs. Davies keeps adding things to my plate. Did you try that new takeaway on the High Street last week?

...Honestly, Dad, I still think we should have just gone back to that Dunelm. They had  loads  of those weighted blankets Maisie was on about. Proper big ones, not just those little travel ones.      Dunelm is… chaotic, isn't it? And honestly, I’m not entirely convinced about the weighted blanket thing. Seems a bit much for a six-month-old. Though, to be fair, she  does  like being swaddled tight.      Aye, Dunelm’s a bit of a scrum, lass. Like a badger sett in there sometimes. But they’re cheap as chips, which is what matters, isn’t it? Though Mothercare hopefully has better quality stuff. And less screaming kids. Remember when your mum took us to that toy shop in Blackpool, the one with the animatronic dinosaurs? Now  that  was chaotic.      Oh God, Dad! I blocked that out! That dinosaur nearly gave me a heart attack. And you tried to win a giant Pikachu on one of those claw machines for, like, an hour.      Well, it  looked  winnable! Pure daylight robbery, those machines are. Anyway, you alright for water, love? Got a bottle there if you need it.      I'm good, thanks. Being pregnant makes me thirsty all the time though, ironically. It's weird, isn't it? Your body needs more fluid, but sometimes just the thought of drinking makes me feel a bit…off.      Seriously? I thought  I  was drinking loads but you’re carrying a whole human. That’s mental. College is tiring but that sounds a whole other level. How’s the survey going on the house, by the way? Anything new to worry about?      Surveyor said it’s all good, mostly. Just a bit of damp in the back bedroom, expected really for a house its age. Nothing structural. Just needs a good airing and maybe a bit of re-plastering. We'll get someone in to look at it properly next week.      That’s a relief. Honestly, I was picturing the foundations crumbling. Reminds me of my grandmother’s house back in Kosice. She refused to do anything about the damp for years. "It builds character," she’d say!      Grandmas are all the same. They think a bit of mold is good for the immune system. Speaking of characters... remember that dodgy bloke who used to hang around the bus stop when we were kids? The one with the bright orange jacket?      Old Arthur! Aye, the one who always smelled faintly of… well, I don’t even  want  to know what he smelled of.

…and honestly, the lag was  brutal . Like, I’d click to shoot, and it would register five seconds later. Absolute chaos. Did you see OldManJenkins raging in chat? It was glorious. OldManJenkins always rages, love. That’s half the fun of watching him. Still, five seconds? That’s… appalling. What game was this again? You’re always on something new. It's 'Aetherium Online', Mum. She’s been obsessed. It’s a massively multiplayer thing, really complex crafting system… honestly, I don't get it, but she’s brilliant at it. Brilliant! I’m a master crafter, thank you very much. I’ve practically single-handedly supplied the entire guild with enchanted armour. It’s all about efficiency, see? Optimising resource gathering routes. It's basically applied logistics, which is… science! Science, is it? That’s a new one. I thought it was just… tapping buttons really fast. Honestly, all this screen time. Are you even enjoying yourself, Chloe, or is it just… compulsion? You seemed a bit off yesterday. Off? No! Just… stressed about the history essay. Mr. Harrison is a nightmare. He expects us to write like we’re already PhD students. And Aetherium is relaxing. It’s a distraction. She  was  muttering something about the Norman Conquest and needing more Mithril ore. It was a weird combination. Hey! Don't mock my coping mechanisms, Leo! It's healthy to have hobbies. And Mithril  is  important. Alright, alright, no need to squabble. Though, Chloe, it’s Christmas next week. Maybe dial it back a bit? We’re hoping you’ll actually  talk  to us over the holidays, not just grunt responses whilst staring at a glowing screen. We were thinking about going to Cornwall. You and Leo haven’t been since you were little. Cornwall sounds good actually. Bit bracing, but good. Less…Minecraft-obsessed teenagers generally hang out there. Cornwall? Ugh. That’s ages away. And there’s probably no decent internet down there. How am I supposed to raid with the guild?! Seriously though…is Dad okay with this? He’s been working so late. He’s alright. Stressed, naturally. That new project at the hospital is demanding. He’s hoping to take a few days off  after  Christmas, possibly go visit his sister in York. He misses her terribly. He’s applied for some funding, apparently, for a new piece of equipment. Very technical stuff, something about brain scans

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of iron you need in Minecraft is ridiculous. It's like, everything needs iron! Tools, armour, buckets… you'd think they were made of gold the way you’re constantly mining for it. But gold  is  good! You can make golden apples! And they give you extra hearts! Yeah! I found a golden nugget yesterday! It was shiny! It was, wasn’t it? Though, practically speaking, iron's much more useful. Gold tools break  so  quickly. Speaking of useful things... remember when we were talking about fabrics earlier, Lily? You were asking about which is strongest? Yeah! Is silk stronger than… denim? That’s a good question. Not necessarily ‘stronger’ in terms of resisting a tear, but silk is incredibly strong for its weight. Think about spider silk – spiders build whole webs with it. Denim, because of the way it’s woven, is tougher, more resistant to abrasion. Like, if you were sliding on something rough, denim would hold up better. It’s all down to how the fibres are put together, you see. Like LEGO! Some LEGO bricks stick together really strong and some fall apart easy? Exactly! It's a bit like that. Different materials, different strengths. They use different metals too, for different jobs. Like, you wouldn't build a spaceship out of iron, would you? It needs something lighter and stronger, like titanium. Titanium! Is that in Minecraft? Not as far as I know, sadly. Though honestly, they should add it. It’d be a late-game material, super rare. We could invent a legend about it! What if titanium only appears when you defeat a really,  really  hard boss - a dragon made of obsidian and lava? Ooooh! And it needs a diamond pickaxe to mine it! But then it makes a sword that can break bedrock! That's brilliant, Thomas! A bedrock-breaking sword! Okay, that’s officially going into the family Minecraft lore. We'll have to build the boss later. Although, honestly, I’m more worried about getting you both to remember to take your vitamins. Ugh, vitamins. They taste yucky. The orange ones are the worst. I know, sweetheart, but they’re important. They help you grow big and strong, like… like iron armour! They protect you from getting poorly. Can I have a golden apple  instead  of vitamins? Absolutely not. Golden apples are a treat  because  you've been taking your vitamins!

…No, seriously, I just don’t get why he’s suddenly all ‘Mr. Sensitive’ about everything. Like, last week he was taking the mick outta Old Man Hemmings’ new haircut, and now he’s lecturing me about ‘respecting people’s choices’. Hypocrite, tha’ is. Ay, lads do change, don't they? Maybe summat's happened to him. Remember when ‘is grandad were poorly? He went a bit quiet then. Could be summat like that. Nah, it’s not that. He’s been spendin' way too much time online, I reckon. I saw ‘im scrolling through that… that forum again. The one all about guitars. It's a rabbit hole, that place is. He's obsessed wi' findin' a vintage Fender, spends hours just lookin’ at pictures. Says he needs one to ‘find his sound’. A Fender, eh? Dreamin’ big, our Kev. Still on about wantin' to start a band, is he? I thought that died a death after the incident wi’ the drums in yer mam’s shed. Don’t remind me. She still talks about it. And yeah, the band thing. It's always “this time it’ll be different!” But the ‘incident’… it wasn't just the shed, were it? It was… well, remember what he was tryin’ to name it? Ugh, don't even. "Little Thunder"? Crikey. Sounded dodgy as owt, even then. It was a bit creepy, lookin’ back. Dodgy doesn’t cover it, does it? It’s vile. Like, I know we were all daft kids, but even then, it felt… wrong. Especially after what happened wi' that bloke in Stainforth. That was awful, y’know? Makes ya think twice about stuff. It does. It really does. It's just… it’s scary how easily some people can… turn. Especially when they hide it behind a sense of humour or a hobby. It’s why I’m careful who I let near me niece. Exactly! And it's not just that. It's the way he’s been talkin’ about younger artists now, too. Not in a bad way, not overt, but… admiring, like. It just makes me uncomfortable. I’ve tried to subtly change the subject, but he keeps bringing it back to ‘appreciating talent’. It's creepy. You're right to be wary. Trust your gut. Look, maybe you should just have a proper chat with him. Not an accusation, just… a proper friend-to-friend talk.

… honestly, Mr. Davies just  doesn’t  get it. He thinks an EPQ should be another essay, just a longer one! Like, what’s the point of independent research if you’re just regurgitating information? I’m trying to build a working model of a Stirling engine, not write a ten-thousand-word dissertation on thermodynamics. Tell me about it. Mine’s on the history of grime music, which is cool, but he keeps asking for “more academic sources.” What academic sources are gonna cover Skepta, realistically? It’s a cultural movement, innit? You both sound stressed. At least you’ve  got  interesting EPQs. Mine’s… the impact of social media on teenage body image. Thrilling, right? It’s just endless scrolling through Instagram and feeling depressed. Oof, that does sound rough. Anything good happening to distract you, then? Like, are you still going to that photography exhibition in London next week? I am! Thankfully. Mum booked tickets ages ago. It’s the Wildlife Photographer of the Year. I need some visual beauty in my life after staring at filtered selfies all week. You guys fancy coming? London… expensive. And I’m supposed to be saving for Montenegro. Remember? We’re finally going this summer, yeah? Oh man, Montenegro! Honestly, I'm buzzing for that. Dad’s mate has a place near Kotor. Apparently the seafood is insane. I’m determined to learn how to cook some proper Balkan food when we’re there. No more beans on toast for me. Good for you. I’m still stuck on the ‘can’t cook anything beyond pasta’ level. Speaking of food, anyone tried that new vegan place on the High Street? ‘Green Bites’? Heard it’s alright. Bit pricey, though. I’m not massively veggie, but I’m trying to eat less meat, y’know? For the planet and all that. It's just…sometimes I really crave a proper roast dinner. It’s a tough one, isn't it? My nan’s always going on about how people had it hard when she was growing up. Proper poverty, she says. No choice  but  to eat what they could get. Makes you think. It does. It’s easy to get caught up in complaining about price increases when you’ve always had enough. My mum volunteers at the food bank, it’s shocking what people are going through. It is. My Uncle Raj used to talk about coming over from India with nothing.

… honestly, it’s just daylight robbery, innit? Seven hundred quid a month for a room that’s basically a glorified cupboard? Back home, for that, you’d get a  whole  flat, overlooking the harbour. Proper sea views. Not… this. Beige walls and a window onto a brick wall. Tell me about it, love. I’m convinced they just add a 'uni tax' on everything up here. My Nan keeps sayin’ I’m bein’ ripped off. She's probably right, the woman can sniff a bad deal a mile off. She’s always goin’ on about how much cheaper things were when  she  went to college, though. Everything’s relative, eh? My mum is the same. She keeps comparing prices to when  she  was doing her Masters. Says she lived on lentils and tap water, but managed to save a fortune. Though, to be fair, she was living at home. A slightly different situation, I think. My dad just sighs and tells me to focus on the degree. He wants me to get a proper job, doesn’t want me worrying about the cost of… well, everything. My mum just keeps sending me money. Which is nice, but feels a bit… patronising, y’know? Like I can’t handle it myself. She's constantly askin' if I'm eatin' properly. "Are you gettin' enough fruit and veg, lad?" Like I’m five! It’s the constant drain, though, isn’t it? Rent, bills, food… and then you want to actually  live  a little? Go out, have a laugh. It all adds up. My little sister's just started college near Bristol, and she's already moaning about the prices. It's universal pain, I reckon. Aye, exactly. I was tryin’ to explain to my cousin back home about how expensive a night out here is… He just laughed. Said I was livin’ in the North and gettin’ what I deserve. Cheeky bugger. He's spendin' all his money on trainers and football tickets. It’s just… managing it all, isn't it? I’m trying to pick up extra shifts at the pub, but it impacts my studies. My dad’s already worried about my grades. He keeps on about the future, getting a good job in engineering… . It's a lot of pressure. Speaking of pressure, did you hear about Amelia? From the History seminar? Apparently, her parents are making her retake her A-Levels because her predicted grades aren’t good enough.

…and honestly, the kids were  exhausted  by the time we got back. Little Leo was clinging to me, bless him, practically asleep standing up. It was all the excitement of the Christmas market, I think. Did you manage to get to one, Mam? Oh, yes, darling. Went to the one in Exeter with Gwyneth and her husband, David. Lovely, but… massively crowded. Felt like being packed onto the Central Line at rush hour! Though the mulled wine  was  rather good. They had a stall selling Welsh cakes, naturally. I had to. Reminded me of your Nan, really. She could churn those out all day long. Oh, Nan loved a good Welsh cake. She'd always sneak me extra when Dad wasn't looking. Speaking of Dad, how is he coping with everything? Is he still visiting Auntie Brenda every Tuesday? He is, yes. Though Brenda's a bit… worse, you know. The confusion is getting more frequent. He says she thinks  he’s  her son, sometimes. Breaks his heart, of course. He puts on a brave face, but I can see it getting to him. He insists on doing it himself though, won’t let anyone else take a turn. Stubborn man, your father. Just like you. Oh, don’t say that! I’m not nearly as stubborn as him. Honestly, though, it’s good he’s still going. I worry about him being lonely. It's just… a lot, isn't it? Dealing with ageing parents. It is, love, it really is. It’s a stage of life you don’t really prepare for. And it’s all happening so quickly. Seems like yesterday he was chasing you and your brother around the garden. Remember old Mr. Henderson next door? He used to complain about the football bouncing over his fence. Oh, God, yes! Mr. Henderson and his prize-winning roses. He threatened to call the police more than once. He and Gran used to have the most epic passive-aggressive fence disputes. It’s funny looking back. It is. Life’s funny, isn't it? Speaking of funny, did I tell you about this training session I ran in Birmingham last week? Absolute chaos. The IT system crashed mid-presentation, and then the fire alarm went off. Had to evacuate the whole building! Honestly, it felt like a sitcom. Oh, no! You're always getting yourself into scrapes with that consultancy work.

...Honestly, Dad, the signal was absolutely dreadful in that village hall. Trying to run a Zoom class with kids dropping out every five seconds? Nightmare fuel. I thought about getting a new phone, something with better reception, but they’re so expensive now, aren't they?      Expensive? You wait 'til you've been paying a mortgage for thirty years,  then  you'll know expensive! Phones are practically giving them away these days. Remember when a brick cost a fortune? And you needed a crane to lift it? Though, to be fair, they probably had better signal. Everything’s changed around Crayford, mind you. Used to know everyone. Now it's all new builds and…well, people who don't look you in the eye.      It’s happening everywhere, isn't it? Bedford’s the same. All these new estates. Though they did finally put in those speed cameras on the A6. Good, I say. People were driving like lunatics. Nearly lost my license a couple of times just cycling to work.      Speed cameras! Robbery, that is. Pure robbery. They just want your money. Reminds me of when Clive got nicked for doing 35 in a 30. Lost his license for a year. Couldn’t get to work. Ended up losing his job. Awful business. How’s work going, anyway? Still teaching those little blighters?      Still teaching. It’s… okay. It's exhausting, honestly. Year 9 are a handful. But it pays the bills. I'm thinking of doing a course, maybe something in TEFL, to try and get a job abroad. Brighton’s looking tempting, actually. Less frantic than London, still got a bit of life.      Brighton? Right, well, that's a bit of a move. Always loved Brighton, used to go down there on day trips when I was a lad. Good fish and chips. Just… watch out for the seagulls. Vicious things. Speaking of moves, your mum’s been on at me about her knee again. Says it’s getting worse. She's been really down lately.      Oh, no. Is she seeing a doctor? Tell her to push for a referral, you know? I feel awful I haven’t seen her for two years. It's just…everything with work and visas and then, you know…Tanzania. That trip felt like a lifetime ago.      Tanzania  was  amazing, wasn’t it? Still got the carved elephant you brought me. Though I think I'm putting on weight, need to start walking again.

… honestly, the sheer volume of people in John Lewis was  stressful . I just needed some decent tea towels, you’d think that wouldn’t require navigating a human obstacle course. And the Christmas displays are already up! It’s barely November. Honestly, the relentless commercialism. You sound like a proper Grinch, darling. It  is  a bit early, I’ll grant you. But John Lewis at the weekend is always… a commitment. Did you at least find the tea towels? The floral ones you wanted? Eventually. After battling a woman wielding a giant inflatable snowman. Floral ones secured, but at what cost to my inner peace? It’s just… it feels so manufactured, you know? All the ‘perfect Christmas’ messaging. It’s exhausting, especially when you consider some of the PR disasters companies have faced recently trying to  appear  authentic. Oh, don’t even get me started. I had a student practically write an essay on the backlash against that Lush campaign last week - the one about police brutality. Bold, yes, but executed… terribly. They got absolutely savaged online for seeming to capitalise on a serious issue. It's a minefield. You’ve got to be genuinely committed to something, not just tacking on a social conscience for marketing points. Exactly! And it’s the speed of the response now. One misstep and you’re cancelled. It used to be a slow burn, a letter to the editor, maybe a bit of bad press. Now it's a tidal wave of Twitter outrage. It makes me think twice about even  mentioning  brands in my lectures sometimes. It does, doesn’t it. Although, dissecting those failures is good teaching material. Speaking of lectures, mine was… surprisingly lively today. We were discussing post-war British music and someone brought up The Smiths. Always a rabbit hole. Oh, Morrissey. Always divisive. I actually saw them live, back when I was at UEA. It was… an experience. Mostly teenage angst and surprisingly aggressive floral shirts. Aggressive floral shirts! Perfect description. I've only ever listened to them through recordings, but their influence is massive. It's funny how much the mood of a nation can be captured in a guitar riff and some melancholic lyrics. It is, isn't it? It’s why I love teaching that module. Anyway, forget the horrors of retail and public relations for a moment. Have you thought about what we’re doing on Saturday?

… honestly, I’m still not convinced about the lilac. It just feels… a bit much for a bathroom, doesn’t it? Especially with the tiles already being quite pale grey. Lilac  is  bold, I’ll grant you that. But we need something, love. That shower curtain is practically screaming for a colour contrast. Beige on beige is just… depressing. It looks like a waiting room. Depressing is a strong word. Practical. Sensible. It doesn’t date. Though, I suppose anything is better than the last one. Remember that floral disaster? It looked like Nana’s sofa had exploded in the bathroom. Oh, don’t remind me. That was a low point. Honestly, I thought the cat was going to try and  live  inside the flowers. Though, to be fair, you picked that one. I was trying to be cheerful! After the… incident with the leaking tap. We needed something to lift the spirits. Anyway, lilac feels…frivolous. What about a deeper teal? Something a bit more calming? Teal’s good. Teal’s very good. But it might make the room look smaller. We need something that bounces light around. Look, while we’re debating bathroom aesthetics, have you made any progress on that beanbag? Progress is… a generous term. I’ve unravelled three rows already. This chunky merino is proving to be surprisingly uncooperative. I thought knitting a giant beanbag would be relaxing. It's anything  but . My hands feel like they’ve been doing push-ups all day. See, this is why I stick to spreadsheets. Predictable. Logical. No rogue wool trying to escape. Though, I appreciate the effort. It’ll be lovely for Elsie when it’s finished. She’ll practically live in it. That’s the plan. Though at this rate, she’ll be off to university before it’s complete. Honestly, I’m seriously considering just buying one. It feels like a defeat, I know. Not at all! Pragmatism! That’s what it is. And think of all the wool you’ll have left over for… other projects. More ambitious projects. Possibly ones that don’t involve unravelled rows and aching fingers. What are we having with this stir-fry, by the way? I'm starving. Just rice. Simple. I didn’t want to spend ages with my face over the hob. My brain is already fried from trying to visualise the colour scheme and simultaneously avoid dropping stitches.

…No, I’m tellin’ ya, Doreen, it weren’t right. Absolutely weren’t right. Young Timothy, bless ‘is ‘eart, tryin’ to fix that leaky tap for me. He’s a good boy, Timothy is, but ‘e gets ‘isself flustered, see? And then ‘e goes and chips the porcelain! A right mess, it was. Oh, Arthur, you and your taps! Honestly, you worry over the smallest things. It’s just a little chip. Nobody’s goin’ to notice. And Timothy was only trying to be ‘elpful. It's the thought that counts, Arthur. It  is  a rather nice basin, though. Antique, isn't it, Arthur? Your mother's, I believe? Antique it may be, George, but it were a perfectly good basin  before  young Timothy got ‘old of it! And ‘e didn’t even fix the leak, did 'e? Just made it worse, I reckon. Drippin’ like a nose, it is. Arthur! Don’t be so ‘ard on the boy. He’s barely eighteen. And honestly, you’d think the world was ending. You haven’t even  asked  him how he is, since he practically ran out the door after the, shall we say, incident. Well, I didn’t want to upset ‘im further, did I? I gave ‘im a right look, I suppose. He knows when ‘e’s done wrong. Still, a chip! On a lovely basin like that. Reminds me of when I used to… Reminds you of what, old boy? That story about your brother and the greenhouse? No, no, not that one. Though that were a disaster, weren't it? This reminds me of when I were a lad, down at Costessey. Old Man Hemmings had a proper workshop, and I used to go and watch him mend things. ‘E could fix anything, that man. Absolutely anything. Never chipped a thing in ‘is life. Things were different then, Arthur. People took more pride in their craftsmanship. Everything's disposable now. Throwaway society, that's what we are. Timothy probably hasn’t had the opportunity to learn proper skills. Doreen has a point. Vocational training isn’t what it used to be. It's all university, university, university. And not everyone  needs  a degree, is it? A good trade is worth its weight in gold. Though, confessedly, I wouldn't know the first thing about fixing a tap. That's the truth, George. Proper skills. That’s what’s missin’.

…and honestly, the price of sprouts this year is  criminal . Absolutely criminal. Five pound eighty for a kilo! You’d think they were covered in gold, wouldn’t you? Five eighty? Blimey, you’re right. I picked some up at Sainsbury’s on Tuesday, they were four seventy-five. Still, a bit steep, isn’t it? Though, frankly, I’m not a huge sprout fan myself. Oh, you’re missing out! Properly roasted with balsamic glaze…heaven. Though, yeah, prices are mental. Everything's gone up. I was looking at flights to Barcelona for a weekend in January - ridiculous. Trying to get a little sunshine, you know? Barcelona sounds lovely, love. Though January…bit chilly for sunbathing perhaps? I'm more thinking cosy nights in, personally. Christmas is looming, isn’t it? Have we even talked about what we’re doing this year? We haven’t, have we? I was thinking, maybe we could have it here? It would be nice, and we've got the space now, haven't we? Though, I'm dreading the cooking. Honestly, the sheer  volume  of food… Here would be good. Saves on the travelling, and I’m happy to help with the cooking, dear. Though, are we still doing the tradition of everyone bringing a dish? It's a bit…chaotic, sometimes. Remember Auntie Maureen's suspiciously green trifle last year? Oh god,  that  trifle! I think it actually glowed. But yeah, I like the ‘bring a dish’ thing, it spreads the load. I could do my chocolate orange cheesecake again, that always goes down well. Cheesecake sounds amazing! Right up my street. And I'm happy to tackle the roast potatoes, I used to make them for my family every year. Though, being honest, I'm still a bit nervous about Christmas. It's…different, not having Mum. It is, isn’t it? It really is. It won't be the same, love. But we'll make it special, won't we? Plenty of memories to share, and maybe we can start some new traditions too. Absolutely. We need to focus on what  is  happening, not what isn’t. We’ll have a lovely day, with all of us together. And we’ll raise a glass to your Mum, darling. Speaking of raising a glass… I’ve just brewed a fresh pot of tea. Anyone fancy one? Oh, yes please! Earl Grey if you’ve got it?

…and honestly, the driving here is something else, isn’t it? I thought Dorset roads were bad, but this is a whole different level of…enthusiasm. I nearly lost a wing mirror to a scooter yesterday. A  scooter , Arthur! Oh, you get used to it, love. They’ve got a different perspective on road markings here, shall we say. More…suggestions than rules. I’ve been coming here for fifteen years, you know. Since Margaret… well, since Margaret passed. Needed a change of scenery. Fifteen years! Goodness. You must know the place like the back of your hand. I’m only on my third week. It's lovely, truly, the weather is glorious, the people are incredibly welcoming. It’s just… different. Everything's so much more relaxed. Makes lesson planning a distant memory, thankfully! Relaxed is the word. That’s why I keep coming back. Back home… Bushey… everything’s so rushed, so  urgent . Here, you could be watching a tortoise cross the road for an hour and nobody would bat an eyelid. Have you been up to Bellapais Abbey yet? Not yet, no. It’s on the list. I’ve been trying to navigate the dolmuş system. That's been an adventure in itself! Trying to decipher which one goes where. And the music… oh, the music. It’s… vibrant, isn't it?
