Vibrant is putting it mildly! They love their Turkish folk music. Loudly. The dolmuş drivers are characters, too. Mine yesterday tried to convince me he was a distant relative of George Best. I didn’t argue. That’s brilliant! I had one trying to sell me a rug, mid-journey, naturally. I think he underestimated my haggling skills – honed by years of dealing with fifteen-year-olds demanding extra credit. You’re a teacher, aren't you? I remembered that. Secondary, wasn't it? What do you teach? English Literature. Though right now, I’m mostly teaching myself how to make Turkish coffee without it ending up like mud. It's no mean feat, I can assure you. Ah, a woman of culture! It takes practice. Old Man Hassan down the road makes the best. He’s been doing it for eighty years. Says the secret is to whisper sweet nothings to the pot. I'll have to try that. Though my pot might prefer a stern lecture on proper brewing techniques. Have you… have you found it easy to adjust, being here for so long on your own?

…and honestly, the student feedback was  brutal . Apparently, my lecture on post-structuralism was “too much, too soon” for a Tuesday afternoon. Honestly! You'd think they wanted me to just summarise SparkNotes. Oh, bless them. They always say that, don't they? It's the same every semester. They want the intellectual stimulation, but then they recoil when they actually  get  it. Are you going to adjust it for next year, or just double down? I'm tempted to double down. Honestly. Maybe force-feed them Foucault. But no, probably adjust. A gentler introduction, maybe. It’s just… frustrating. It feels like lowering the bar, you know? I’m lecturing  postgraduates ! They should have  some  baseline understanding. I get it. I had a similar thing with my media ethics class. Apparently, discussing the ethics of AI-generated content was “too dystopian.” Too soon, apparently, for them to consider the implications. It’s like they want everything neatly packaged and optimistic. Exactly! And it’s even more noticeable here, isn’t it? Living in a city like this… you’d think the students would be more engaged with these bigger, complex issues. Look at the air today, even with the recent improvements. It’s still…thick. Honestly, makes me cough just walking. It is grim, isn't it? Remember how blue the sky used to be in Norwich? Pristine. We take that for granted back home. It's a different world. Though, I suppose London wasn’t exactly known for its clean air either, just… different pollutants. Different, but just as insidious, I suppose. But here, it’s so  visible . You can see it. It hangs in the air. It makes you think about what we're all breathing in. Did you hear about old Mr. Chen down the street? Apparently, his asthma’s been playing up terribly. I did. Li Wei mentioned it. Poor man. It's scary. It's one of the reasons I'm glad we’re both tenured, frankly. The thought of having to constantly justify ourselves  and  navigate this…environment…is exhausting. Tell me about it. And speaking of exhausting, have you spoken to Helen recently? She sounded utterly frazzled on the phone last week. Apparently, her department is completely understaffed, and she's bearing the brunt of it. No, I haven’t. I meant to call her. She's always so reliable, taking on everything.

…and honestly, that picture of you, David, with the Hawaiian shirt and the oversized sunglasses? Absolute gold. I’m definitely framing that one for the downstairs loo. Oh, don’t you dare, Sarah! That was a particularly… regrettable fashion choice. Bournemouth, 1992. Thinking I was channeling Magnum P.I. Clearly, I wasn’t. You actually rocked it, Dad. In a wonderfully awful way. It’s a vibe. Honestly, I’m collecting embarrassing photos of everyone for my grandma’s birthday. It’s going to be a slideshow of shame. Good girl, Chloe. She’ll  love  that. She’s been saying for weeks she needs a good laugh. Right, so, I was thinking a simple roast chicken for lunch tomorrow? Nothing too fancy. I’ve got that lovely marinade from the farmer’s market. Sounds lovely, love. Is that marinade the one with the lemon and rosemary? That’s a good one. We haven’t had a proper roast in ages. Been too busy with… well, everything. That’s the one. It’ll be nice. A bit of normality. You alright, Chloe? You’ve been awfully quiet. Still stuck on that copy for the new campaign? Yeah, kind of. It’s just… they want ‘vibrant and energetic’ for a retirement village advert. Try writing that and not sounding patronising! It feels so off. Like I'm selling them assisted living with a side of forced fun. That  is  a tricky brief. You’re right, you don’t want to come across like you’re suggesting they’re all falling apart. Maybe focus on the community aspect? The freedom to pursue hobbies? Exactly. They want connection, not… being ‘looked after’. And honestly, some of those villages are  lovely . They've got bowling greens and everything. I tried suggesting that to Brenda – head of marketing – but she said it needs 'more punch'. Apparently, no one buys retirement based on bowling. Brenda sounds… demanding. She always struck me as a bit of a tyrant, even when she came to the hospital for her hip replacement. Honestly, thought she’d have a meltdown when I told her she couldn’t have Earl Grey instead of the hospital tea. Oh, Sarah! You and your tea standards. She probably thought you were rationing the good stuff! Speaking of Earl Grey, did you manage to catch that new detective series on BBC One? ‘Shadows over Whitstable’? I started it, but got called in to cover a shift.

… honestly, it’s just taking  ages  to get anywhere now. They’ve rerouted the 10 again, haven’t they? It used to go right past the Grafton, now it loops all the way around Milton Road. It's a right pain. Oh, is that what that delay was about yesterday? I was wondering. I just assumed it was typical Cambridge gridlock. Still, sounds annoying. You’re relying on it for getting to work, aren’t you? Aye, and back. Unless I cycle, which… honestly, after a full day wading through linguistic data? No thank you. It’s not like Sunderland, where everything’s five minutes away. I could practically walk to the beach from me mam’s. Cambridge isn’t exactly known for its practicality, is it? More known for… ancient traditions and expensive coffee. Speaking of which, did you manage to get that book you wanted from CUP? I walked past earlier, it was rammed. Tried! Absolute chaos. They had that student protest thing happening  inside  the shop. Some bloke with a megaphone going on about decolonising the curriculum. Honestly, it was a bit much at 10 in the morning. Couldn’t even browse the linguistics section without shouting over him. Really? Inside? That's a bit… bold. What was he saying, specifically? Something about the lack of diverse voices in academic publishing and how CUP is perpetuating colonial power structures. It was all a bit… intense. I just wanted a textbook on historical phonology, not a political debate. Sounds rather Cambridge, actually. They do love a good protest. It wasn't like that at Imperial. We had a union, obviously, but things were generally a bit more focused on practical engineering problems. Not, you know, dismantling the entire university. See, that's what I mean about universities being completely different. Durham was a bit like that, a bit 'worthy'. Loads of debating societies and people trying to save the world. Newcastle, where I did me undergrad, was just… a proper uni. People went out, had a laugh, actually  worked  on their degrees. Imperial was… clinical. Extremely focused. You were there to  do  engineering. Social life existed, of course, but it wasn't the be-all and end-all. Did you find Durham a big shift, coming from Sunderland? Massive. Everything was posh. Everyone had Barbour jackets and went shooting. It was a culture shock, to say the least. I stuck out like a sore thumb, even for a lass from the North East.

Honestly, this is just lovely. Proper chips, you know? Not those skinny fries they try to pass off these days. Reminds me of the chippers back in Dublin… though, you wouldn't get this kind of weather there, would you? Always damp.      You and your Dublin memories, Auntie Mary! Though, I get it. Good chips  are  a national treasure. And yes, this Cumbrian sunshine is…unexpected, to say the least. I’m really glad we managed to get out though. It's been ages since we’ve had a proper girls’ lunch.      Absolutely. Work's been manic. The new HR system is a nightmare – it's like they've deliberately made it as unintuitive as possible. But this is a welcome break. So, Mary, how are you really finding retirement? Honestly? Beyond the delightful chip evaluations, of course.      It’s…an adjustment. A big one. I miss the routine, you know? And the kids. Even the challenging ones. It’s funny, isn’t it? Spending forty years trying to get them  out  of the classroom, and then… silence. Though, Liam’s been a good boy, checking in. He sent a lovely email about his promotion last week.      That’s brilliant! He deserves it. He’s worked so hard. It’s amazing how quickly they grow up, isn’t it? It feels like yesterday I was being embarrassingly chaperoned by him when he was a teenager.      Tell me about it! Remember Sarah’s 16th birthday? The drama with… oh, never mind. . Anyway, Mary, you said on the phone you were a bit worried about David's visit? Is everything alright?      Oh, David. He’s… David. He’s lovely, truly. But he’s…precise. Very precise. And he's been asking me about my accent.      Your accent? What on earth does he want with your accent?      He says it’s “evolving.” Apparently, after all these years living in England, it’s becoming… diluted. He’s fascinated by the nuances of language, you see. He’s always been a bit academic, bless him. It’s just…it feels like he’s subtly pointing out how long I’ve been away from home.      He’s a linguist, isn’t he? That explains it. They  do  overthink things. It’s not meant to be critical, Mary, honestly. He’s probably just geeking out.      I know, I know. It’s silly of me to be bothered. Still… growing up in Dublin, your accent  is  you, isn't it?

… honestly, seeing the O2 from here, even looming like that, is a bit depressing. It just feels…massive. And not in a good way. It just blocks everything else out, you know? Like it’s shouting “LOOK AT ME!” over all the proper history. You’re not wrong. It's a bit of a concrete monstrosity, isn't it? Though, I’ll admit, I did enjoy seeing Beyoncé there a few years back. Just… ignore the surroundings, focus on the music. Easier said than done, admittedly. Still, preferable to battling the M25 to get to a gig. Remind me again why we don’t own a car? Because London  is  the car! Ridiculous expense, constant parking nightmares, and frankly, it’s not like we  need  one. We have the DLR, the tube, and lovely walks like this. Although, walking this far with the kids… that’s another matter. Speaking of which, are you still thinking Cornwall for the summer? I am. Assuming I can get the time off, of course. The boss is being particularly obtuse at the moment. Cornwall feels… manageable. Not too far, beaches for the little ones, and a pub within stumbling distance is always a plus. Though packing for them is a nightmare. Honestly, it’s like equipping an expedition. Tell me about it. And then there's Auntie Maggie and her insistence on sending over American recipe books. “Two cups of flour!” Two  cups ? What even  is  a cup? Is it a metric cup? An imperial cup? It’s a recipe for disaster, literally. I spent half an hour yesterday trying to convert a brownie recipe and nearly wept. Maggie and her transatlantic obsession. Bless her. You'd think after thirty years of living here, she'd embrace kilos and millilitres. But no. Everything has to be in 'cups' and 'tablespoons'. It feels deliberately antagonistic, doesn't it? Like a conspiracy to keep you in the kitchen forever. Exactly! Though, it's not just the measures. It’s the sheer… optimism in American baking. "Fold gently". Gently! As if a four-year-old hasn’t just grabbed a handful of chocolate chips and thrown them across the kitchen. It's a fantasy. Look, there’s the Cutty Sark. Now  that  is something to look at. Proper history. Built for speed, sailed the world… not built for attention seeking like… well, you know. Exactly. It feels…grounded.

…Honestly, though, the rain is  relentless  isn’t it? It’s been chucking it down since, like, Tuesday. Ruined my plans for a bike ride to the coast. I was so looking forward to it.      You’re telling  me . I had Mrs. Henderson refusing to get out of bed this morning. Said it felt like the world was ending with all the noise. Honestly, she’s dramatic, but it's grim out there. Makes getting to work… a bit of a slog.      Tell me about it. Little Maisie's sports day is next week and if it’s like this, it’ll be inside the hall. It's a  nightmare  trying to see anything when it's crammed in there. Last year I just ended up filming the back of someone’s head for the egg and spoon race!      Oh god, the sports day chaos. I remember those. Mum always insisted on getting right to the front, elbows out, blocking everyone's view! Speaking of chaos, have you seen how many cuddly toys Maisie’s amassed? It's a fluffy invasion.      Don’t even  start  me. It’s ridiculous. She wants to take them  all  to bed every night. And then demands I read each one a bedtime story! Honestly, I’m starting to think we need a cull. Though, she's been obsessing about going to Build-a-Bear again. She wants a unicorn that "poops rainbows".      Oh, children. They’re a handful, aren't they? My Sarah was obsessed with unicorns. Still is, actually, though she’s a bit old for rainbows now. Remember when we were little, Caz? You and I used to build forts out of anything we could find. Mum would go mad.      Oh, I do! The living room looked like a bomb had hit it. We used all your dad's good blankets! And you were always the architect, Caz, always directing. I was just the labourer. It feels weird though, being the mum now. It's like the roles reversed.      It is, isn't it? It's weird thinking I'm basically the baby of the family now. Though, you’ve always been much better at the mumming stuff than I’d ever be. I'm still trying to figure out how to work the new washing machine. It’s got, like, seventeen different settings!      Seventeen! Honestly! They overcomplicate everything. Mine’s basic, thank goodness.

…so, honestly, the biggest thing kicking around my head isn’t necessarily  what  I want to do next business-wise, it's… how much of my life I want to  be  doing business. You know? I’m starting to feel a bit… tethered. Like I’m always ‘on’. I get that. Completely. You’ve built something incredible with StellarTech, but it sounds like it’s starting to feel less like a passion project and more like a… responsibility? Exactly! A very  profitable  responsibility, thankfully, but still. That’s why I was thinking… maybe slowing down on the day-to-day, moving into more of an advisory role. David and Sarah were talking about expanding their ecotourism venture in Tasmania – maybe lending a hand there, strategically. Less pressure, more…impact, if that makes sense. That sounds lovely, actually. Something slower paced. And Tasmania is beautiful. Joining forces with David and Sarah…that would be good fun. You always work so well together. Though, are you sure you’re ready to relinquish  control ? You’re not one for letting go easily, are you? Point taken. It’s terrifying, honestly. But I’m forty-six now, not twenty-six. I need to think about… other things. Like, we’ve been talking about potentially extending our time here in Australia, maybe even looking at long-term residency. Australia  suits  us, doesn’t it? This house, the weather, the pace of life… It’s a world away from the grey skies of Dorset. And long-term residency… that feels bigger than just a house-sitting gig. Have you started looking into the requirements? Just preliminary stuff. Visas are a nightmare, obviously. But if I’m moving into a less hands-on role with StellarTech, it opens up possibilities for qualifying under a skills-based visa. And then there's…well, the family question. Ah.  That  family question. We’ve been dancing around it for a while now. I know, I know. It feels selfish, perhaps. My sister keeps dropping hints about wanting grandkids. Honestly, it's putting pressure on both of us. But I want to be… present. I don’t want to be some jet-setting entrepreneur who sees his children grow up via video call. Nobody wants that. And it's not selfish to want to be involved. We both agreed when we first got together that we wanted… a different kind of life to the one we’d both been living.

…and honestly, I still maintain, Mark sounds  nothing  like someone from Wigan. Absolutely nothing. You’d think he’d have more… grit, y’know? He sounds more…Scouse, almost.      Alright, alright, lay off Mark! He’s sensitive. And it’s all down to having a posh mum, honestly. She drilled the vowels outta him. Plus, he spent a year in Liverpool. Explains it. Anyway, we were talking about accents, weren't we? Yorkshire's proper weird, isn't it, Amy? Like you're constantly asking a question.      It's  not  weird! It's expressive! We just... enunciate. And it's not a question, it's just…how we say things! “You alright?” doesn’t  necessarily  mean are you alright. It’s just a greeting!      Oh, this is brilliant. You two at each other already. Remember when we all tried to do impressions after Sarah’s hen do? Absolute carnage. Speaking of Sarah, has anyone heard from her? She was going on about wanting to get back into Pokémon Go.      She messaged me earlier, said she’s battling a gym leader down by the canal. Apparently, there’s a massive Snorlax there. She’s proper obsessed again. Honestly, it’s like being fifteen again, wandering around town looking for digital monsters.      I proper don't get it. The walking, fine. Good for her. But staring at your phone all the time? And getting competitive about cartoon creatures? Still, it’s better than her when she started smoking again, that was a worry. Remember when she’d sneak off behind the college to have a fag?      Oh god, yeah. Mrs. Davies would have her hide if she’d caught her. That woman had eyes in the back of her head. She’d sniff out a cigarette a mile off. It’s just…bad manners, isn’t it? Doing that right in front of people.      Manners! You’re one to talk! You nearly took my head off trying to get to the last After Eight at Christmas.      Alright, alright, fair point. I was fuelled by Quality Street and spite. Plus, they're  way  better than Roses, and you were hogging them.      Speaking of fuelled, anyone fancy another round? My Fitbit’s telling me I’ve barely moved all day. I need to justify this pint somehow.      I’m good, but could you grab me a pack of biscuits when you’re up? The digestives, if they’ve got ‘em.

…and honestly, the students were baffled. I was trying to explain the nuances of post-structuralism and one of them asked if it was like, a really complicated building. Oh, bless them. You're dealing with a generation raised on TikTok, darling. Deep thought isn’t exactly a priority. TikTok, is it? Sounds a right kerfuffle. All these flashing lights and… what IS it even  of ? Back in my day, entertainment was a good game of bowls down the green, or a sing-song round the piano. Simple pleasures. Simple, and sociable, Albert. That’s what’s missing now, isn’t it? Everyone glued to their little screens. Though, I did see a lovely recipe on the telly the other day – a lemon drizzle cake. Remember those, Albert? Your mother used to make a cracking one. Aye, she did. Used a whole bottle of lemon juice, she did. Said it was the secret. Though I reckon a generous dollop of butter was more important. You never could skimp on the butter. Sounds delicious! We’re having a potluck at the department next week. I’m supposed to bring something. Should I attempt a lemon drizzle? I’m a reasonably good baker, but… You should! Though, honestly, half the ‘baking’ brought in looks like it came straight from a supermarket wrapper. People are busy, I suppose. Busy with what, I wonder? Seems to me, everyone's always in a hurry. No time for a proper chat anymore. Remember when you could spend an afternoon just…being? Without needing to be  doing  something. That’s true, Albert. Though, thinking about being busy, I’m starting to think about Christmas. We need to get organised. Are we doing it here again this year? I think we agreed, didn’t we, to rotate? It’s a lot for one house, even with all of us pitching in. Perhaps we could do it at my place? I’ve got a fairly decent dining table now, and… it’s just a bit more spacious. Though, I’d need help with the cooking. I’m good at the fancy bits – the soufflés and whatnot – but I'm hopeless at roast potatoes. Roast potatoes need goose fat, young lady. Goose fat. Don’t let anyone tell you different. Makes all the difference. And a good, strong parsnip. None of this watery rubbish you get in the shops now. Oh, you and your parsnips, Albert!

… honestly, I just feel like I’m drowning, yeah? Like, permanently. All these essays, and the lectures… it’s not  bad , exactly, just… pointless. What’s the point of knowing the mating rituals of the Lesser Spotted Newt when I feel like I can barely keep  myself  afloat, you know? The Lesser Spotted Newt, eh? Sounds riveting. Look, I get it. Honestly. First term always feels like that. Like everyone else got the instruction manual you missed. But you were so buzzing about archaeology, weren’t you? All those stories about Cornwall, digging up bits of history… I  was . But Cornwall feels a million miles away now. And all I’m digging up is a massive hole of debt. Mum and Dad are already… subtly hinting about getting a “proper job”. It’s just… I keep thinking maybe I made a mistake coming here. Maybe I should have just stayed at home, worked at the bakery, saved up… Don't talk daft, Liv. You’d be miserable! You need to get out, explore. Lancaster isn’t  Cornwall , granted, but it’s a good laugh. And the bakery? No offence to bakers, but you’re way too clever to be icing fairy cakes for the rest of your life. It’s not just that. Look at these shoes. Disgusting, aren't they? I walked across campus after it rained and… ugh. It feels symbolic, somehow. Me, traipsing through mud, making a mess of everything. They  are  grim. You’re a state, you are. Right, get ‘em off before you track it all over my rug. Seriously. But symbolic? You and your dramatic flair! You always were prone to seeing signs, weren't ya? Remember when you were convinced old Mr. Penhaligon's cat was a witch in disguise? Okay, fair. I was seven! And its eyes  were  really unsettling. But seriously, I think I’m just generally rubbish at this 'adulting' thing. It feels like everyone else has it figured out. No one has it figured out, Liv. Seriously. We’re all just pretending. Even me, pretending to focus on my dissertation when all I want to do is binge-watch dodgy reality TV. Actually, talking of names… you ever wonder where ‘Olwen’ came from? My nan always said it meant ‘white footprint’ or something mystical like that. Sounds a bit… grand, doesn't it? For a scally from Liverpool. It suits you, actually.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I get about ‘synergy’ and ‘thinking outside the box’ is enough to make me actively seek a job shelving books. It’s all just…fluff. How’s Pearson treating you? Still battling the marketing jargon beast? Oh, don't even  start  me. It’s worse. They've introduced ‘impactful storytelling’ as a core value. Impactful. Storytelling. Like, what did we do before? Just...tell stories? It’s exhausting. But the pay’s alright, and I’m actually getting to lead on a big social media campaign for their new qualifications, which is pretty exciting. What about you? Still wrangling project timelines and keeping everything afloat? Afloat is…a generous description. It's more like desperately bailing water out of a sinking ship with a teaspoon. This new client wants the world for a budget that wouldn't cover my lunch. Honestly, I spent most of yesterday just explaining basic feasibility to a man who clearly thinks project management is just ‘positive vibes and a good attitude’. Oh, bless. You always get the interesting ones. Remember Derek from uni? The one who thought he could become a millionaire selling personalised toilet roll? Oh god, Derek! How could I forget? He was so  confident . Still, at least he had a vision. This guy just wants things done, and doesn’t care  how . Speaking of uni… it feels like a lifetime ago, doesn’t it? I keep meaning to reach out to more people, but life just…happens. It really does. I’ve been trying to be better about it. I actually saw Chloe last month - you remember, the drama queen? – she's a solicitor now, unbelievably. Apparently, she thrives on conflict. Who knew? We had a proper gossip, it was brilliant. Have you spoken to Liam recently? He hasn’t replied to my messages. No, not for ages. I think he’s still travelling. Last I heard he was teaching English in Vietnam. Good for him, honestly. He always said he didn’t want a conventional life. It makes me think… are we stuck, do you think? In these… routines? Work, eat, sleep, repeat? That's a bit bleak, isn’t it? But yeah, sometimes. I’m starting to feel that itch to  do  something different. I've been looking at evening classes - pottery, actually. Seems ridiculously relaxing. Pottery! That's amazing. You always were the creative one.

…and honestly, lad, I just don’t trust ‘em all. All these pop-up shops appearing overnight, selling things you wouldn't touch with a barge pole. It's right dodgy, it is. I stick to the big names, mostly. Or eBay, if I’m feeling brave. eBay’s alright, isn't it? I got those Warhammer figures off there for a good price. A lot cheaper than Games Workshop's website, anyway. Aye, you can get a bargain on eBay, that’s true. But you’ve got to be careful. Read the description  properly . And check the seller’s feedback, mind. That's vital. I nearly got stung once, buying a supposed antique teapot. Turned out to be made in a factory last Tuesday, according to young Thomas next door who knows his pottery. Feedback's important. I always look at how many sales they've got too. Loads of sales usually means they're legit. Amazon’s pretty safe, though, innit? Amazon  is  generally safer, yes. But even they… they have issues. All those third-party sellers using their platform. It’s not always Amazon sending you the item, you see. Sometimes it’s someone else entirely, just  using  Amazon to get to you. That's where it gets a bit murky. They’ve got customer service, which is good, thankfully, but it can be a palaver getting things sorted if something goes wrong. Right. So it's like… Amazon are just the delivery guys sometimes? A bit like that, aye. They're the marketplace, see? They provide the platform, the payment system. But they don't necessarily  own  the stuff you're buying. It's a bit like a car boot sale, but online. You get good stuff, you get rubbish, you get the occasional con merchant. Makes sense. I was looking at getting a new graphics card for my computer. Amazon's got a few, but they're all really expensive. eBay’s got some cheaper ones, but…well, you’ve just put me off a bit! Don't be  completely  put off, love. Just be sensible. What card were you looking at? A GeForce RTX 3060. They’re around £300 on Amazon, but I saw one on eBay for £220. Sounds too good to be true, doesn't it? It probably is, lad. Seriously. If it’s significantly cheaper than everywhere else, there’s a reason.

… honestly, it’s the principle of the thing, isn’t it? They just  assume  because I’m a bit… well, you know, not working, that I’m suddenly incapable of understanding a simple bill. I had to explain to young Gareth at the post office,  again , that I know what a direct debit is. Oh, Dad, you and Gareth. He's probably just being polite, offering to go through it with you. He sees a lot of older folks struggling with those things. It doesn’t mean he thinks you're daft. Polite? Polite is offering me another biscuit, not patronisingly pointing out the date on a letter! It feels like they look at me and see someone who spends all day watching daytime television and forgetting what day it is. Which, incidentally, is demonstrably false. I know what day it is. Usually. Usually. Alright, alright. Look, I get it. It's frustrating. People make assumptions. Happens to me all the time at work, actually. Being a young woman in production, they assume I just… don't understand the mechanics of things. They'll explain something to me like I'm five. See! It’s the same thing! It’s about respect, isn't it? My father, now  he  wouldn't have stood for it. He'd have given 'em a proper telling-off. A right earful. Probably scared Gareth half to death, Dad. You'd need to dial it back a bit. Though, I understand where you're coming from. What was the bill for, anyway? Something dodgy? The water rates. They’ve put them up again! Honestly, it’s daylight robbery. And they sent two letters! One saying I owe £75, the other saying £82. I asked Gareth which one was correct, and he started explaining to me about estimated readings and… honestly, it was all jargon. I just wanted a simple answer! Two different letters, that's not good. Maybe there’s been a mistake. Have you checked the meter yourself? Checked the meter? Goodness me, no! That’s all down by the garden, and I haven’t been out there properly since… well, since last summer. Too much bother, all that bending and squinting. Right. Okay. Look, I'm off work on Tuesday. I could pop over after work and have a look for you? It's not much, but I could check the meter, maybe give them a ring and sort it out?

… honestly, the thought of actually  being  at the airport on Christmas Day fills me with dread. Like, picture it – everyone stressed, delayed flights… it’s a logistical nightmare. And for what? An extra hour with the family? Nah, I'm good with Boxing Day. You’re such a grinch, Leo! It's Christmas! A little stress is worth seeing Mum and Dad, isn't it? Besides, I'm already making plans based on getting down there on the 25th. I promised I’d bake the Yule log. It’s a tradition, remember? Oh, leave him alone, Chloe. He's always preferred a low-key Christmas. Although, last year’s attempt at a ‘low-key’ Christmas involved accidentally setting fire to the fairy lights… Hey! That was a faulty plug! And I put it out, didn't I? Anyway, flying on Christmas Day is just… chaotic. They give the pilots extra hazard pay just for doing it, apparently. A mate of mine flies for British Airways, he told me. Hazard pay? Bit dramatic, innit? Still, I get ya. Flying  any  day around Christmas is a headache. Reminds me of one year, tried to get back to Sydney, flight got cancelled, ended up sleeping on a bench in Singapore for twelve hours. Wasn't pretty. Oh, bless ya, Ben! That sounds awful! Right, Leo, we're talking logistics. If you drive Boxing Day, will you be alright with picking up the Brussel sprouts? Mum's insisted on  real  Brussel sprouts. Not the pre-shredded rubbish. Brussels sprouts… the bane of my existence. Fine, I’ll get the sprouts. But only if someone else is driving back. My car’s been playing up a bit. Keeps making this weird clunking noise. I can drive back! No problem. I actually enjoy a good long drive, weirdly. Gives me time to think. Though, speaking of drives, you wouldn’t  believe  what I saw on the A45 the other day… Oh god, here we go. What now, Jess? Did you nearly hit another pheasant? Worse! A deer. A massive stag. Right in the middle of the road. I slammed on the brakes, thankfully. Poor thing didn’t stand a chance if I’d hit it. It was… horrific. Roadkill deer. Lovely. Just what I needed to hear on a festive evening. Happens all the time down our way in the Blue Mountains. You get used to it, unfortunately.

… honestly, I still reckon it sounded a bit like Mr. Henderson from sixth form. You know, the history teacher? That nasal thing he did when he got excited about the Tudors? Oh god, Mr. Henderson. No way! I thought it was more… vaguely Welsh? Like someone trying to  do  a Welsh accent, but failing spectacularly. It was the vowel sounds, definitely. You’re both miles off. It was pure Brummie. Solid Birmingham. I spend far too much time on voice acting forums – you pick these things up. That flattened ‘a’ and the way they drop the ‘h’s. Distinctive. Brummie? You’re having a laugh, aren’t ya? I  am  Brummie! And I didn't sound like that! No offence, mate, but people’s own accents are the hardest to hear accurately. You get used to it, it kinda fades into the background. It was subtle, but it was there. Probably a younger lad, judging by the intonation. He definitely wasn't trying to be posh, that's for sure. It felt… grounded. A little rough around the edges. Which, thinking about it, fits with the Google Maps directions we’ve been getting. Half the time, they sound like they're reading off a shopping list. Speaking of directions, are we nearly there yet? This little Fiat is doing alright, but my back’s starting to protest. And honestly, it's a bit cramped in the back with all our bags. Almost, according to the app. Another fifteen minutes, assuming we don't hit any more tractor traffic. And honestly, it  is  a bit cosy back there. You should have taken your bigger car, Liam. I did offer! But you two said it was ‘overkill’ for a weekend trip to see your auntie Brenda. Apparently, a Mondeo is ‘showboating’. It was a fair point. Brenda lives in a village accessible by single-track roads, a Mondeo’s just asking for trouble. Plus, it’s good to be environmentally conscious, right? This little Fiat is surprisingly efficient. Efficient and… challenging to park. I nearly took out a lamppost back in Peterborough. You always exaggerate. It was a near miss, not a near take-out. And honestly, you’re a good driver. Much better than… well, than Dave. Remember when Dave tried to parallel park in London? Don't even. That was a trauma I've actively repressed. Three point turns in a space barely bigger than the car itself.

… honestly, it just felt  forced , you know? Like they were trying too hard to be edgy. The music video was just… a lot. Forced? Bruv, you’re talkin’ about Nova Skies? They're sick! Seriously, ‘Static Bloom’ slaps. You gotta appreciate the layered synths, the beat drop… it's proper grime-influenced but, like,  refined . I dunno, I get what you mean, Leo. It's a bit…much. It feels like they’re trying to be Radiohead but end up sounding like a really stressed-out computer. I prefer something a bit more straightforward, like IDLES. At least  they  commit to the chaos. Exactly! IDLES understand controlled chaos. Nova Skies is just…noise posing as art. Remember when we all went to that gig, the one in Reading, with The Static Current? Now  they  knew how to build a soundscape. Proper atmospheric. The Static Current were alright, yeah. A bit slow for me though. I need something with a bit more energy. Man like AJ from Nova Skies, he's a genius with production. You've gotta give him that. He samples everything! I read an interview where he said he uses field recordings from the Jubilee line. The Jubilee line? Seriously? That explains the constant feeling of impending doom. Look, I’m happy you two are enjoying processed noise, but I’m sticking with stuff I can actually  feel . Did anyone see ‘Dune: Part Two’ yet? The music in that was incredible. Hans Zimmer is a god. ‘Dune’ was amazing! The sound design overall was insane. It’s almost a physics lesson in itself, isn’t it? The way they represented the vibrations through the sand, the low frequency rumble… it’s about manipulating sound waves, fundamentally. Reminds me of what Mr. Harrison was talking about in physics – resonance frequencies. Physics?! What’s that got to do with anything? It’s a film! It’s supposed to look cool. Though, I gotta admit, the bit where the sand worms came through… my chair was vibrating. That was kinda…physical. No, Leo's got a point. Zimmer deliberately uses sound to create a physical sensation. It's all about those frequencies affecting your body. It's clever stuff. He’s basically weaponising bass. Exactly! And that’s what good music is, fundamentally. Controlled manipulation of wavelengths. Nova Skies just feels… haphazard. It’s like they threw a bunch of sounds at a wall and hoped something stuck.

…and honestly, Leo, you were absolutely flying on that Balanceability bike! Honestly, I was so proud. You didn’t wobble  once  after the first little push. Much better than some of the others in your class, I have to say.      It was easy. Miss Davies said I was a natural.      I want to try it now! Can I have a go, Mummy? Even though I haven’t properly learned yet?      Not right now, sweetheart. It’s Leo’s turn to tell us all about his amazing achievement. And after that, we’re making pizza, remember? That’s way more exciting than a bike at the moment, isn’t it?      Pizza  is  exciting. With pineapple?      We’ve had this discussion, Elsie. Pineapple does  not  belong on pizza. It's a culinary crime.      It’s good! Matthew at school had pineapple on his. He said it’s sweet  and  savoury.      Matthew is entitled to his opinion, even if it's… misguided. Anyway, back to Balanceability. Leo, did you feel scared at all? Even a little bit?      Nope. Just… wobbly at the start. But then it just… happened. Like magic.      That’s wonderful, darling. It's a brilliant feeling, isn’t it? When you finally succeed at something you've been working towards. It reminds me of when I finally passed my final teaching assessment. Remember how stressed I was?      Was it like learning to swim? I was scared of putting my face in the water!      It was a bit like that, actually. A lot of preparation, a lot of nerves, and then finally, a huge sense of relief. It's all about building up that confidence. Speaking of which, did you tell Miss Davies about your swimming assessment next week?      Yeah. She said I have to do a length.      A whole length! That’s brilliant! You’ll be absolutely fine. You're a strong swimmer. You've been going to lessons for ages.      My friend Lily said her mum and dad are renovating their house! They’re building a  swimming pool !      Oh, really? Whose house is that again? The Bakers, down on Mill Road?      No, the other Lily. The one who has a cat. Her dad said they're even adding a little manmade waterfall!      A waterfall! How extravagant. Though, lovely, of course. It just reminds me of something – you must  never  dive into shallow water, you two. Never ever. Even if it looks tempting, especially with a waterfall.

… honestly, I just feel beat. This conference at the Racecourse was  mental . Three days solid of catering requests, AV nightmares, and people complaining about the biscuits. Biscuits, Beth! You wouldn’t believe. Sounds charming. Though I suppose people always find something, don’t they? Production's been relatively calm, thankfully. Just… relentless. Endless spreadsheets. Reminds me why I need to actually  use  my legs sometimes. You still going to that boot camp thing? I  was . Did one session. Nearly died. Proper lactic acid city. It’s run by this ex-military bloke, all shouting and press-ups. I thought I was fitter than I am, y'know? I do a bit of walking with the dog, but that's about it. He made us carry logs. Logs, Beth! In Cambridge! It felt a bit… much. Logs? Oh, that's ambitious. I’ve been trying to get back into running. Signed up for a 5k next month. It’s mostly just a way to justify buying new trainers, if I’m honest. That’s sensible. Motivation through retail therapy. I approve. Though a 5k sounds… respectable. I’d probably need to be airlifted after a kilometre. Speaking of needing rescuing, how’s things with… Daniel? Still radio silence after the disastrous pub quiz? Don’t even. It’s been a week. A  week  of strategically ‘not being online’ when I know he's likely lurking. And my flatmate keeps saying I should just message him, but pride, you know? Aye, pride. A Yorkshire lass understands pride. Though, maybe just a little ‘hey, how are you’ won’t kill ya? He was a bit daft embarrassing you over general knowledge, mind. What was the question anyway? Apparently, it was about… the average wingspan of a Golden Eagle. I answered “A small car,” as a joke. A  joke , Maya! And he just… stared at me. Like I’d suggested we replace the monarchy with pigeons. Oh, Beth! That  is  bad. Though slightly brilliant. A small car! You're a legend. He sounds a bit… serious, doesn't he? Maybe that’s a good thing to learn now though, before things get more serious. That’s what Mum says. “He’s a good one, just a bit… intense.” Intense like a laser beam, maybe. It's just… I really liked him. And now I'm picturing him meticulously researching Golden Eagle wingspans, judging my entire life.

…and honestly, Arthur, you wouldn’t  believe  Old Man Hemmings. He tried to play that double-six like it was a personal insult, glaring at me the whole time! Thought he was going to have a proper huff when I blocked him.      He’s always like that, Auntie Brenda. Thinks Dominoes is life or death. Did you win, though?      Aye, Brenda’s a dab hand at ‘em, lad. Beats Arthur regular. Not as good as me, mind you… but regular. This pizza’s good, Brenda. Better than that place we went to last week - what was it called, ‘Bella Italia’? All show and no flavour.      Oh, don't even  mention  Bella Italia, George! Tiny portions and priced like they're serving gold. This is proper pizza, thanks to Deliveroo. You've finished yours already, Liam! You were saying something about needing new trainers for football?      Yeah, mine are falling apart. Proper wrecked. Need to get some decent ones for the trials next month. Think I need to ask Dad, but he’s been a bit… short lately.      Trials, eh? Good lad. Stick at it. Though I never understood this modern football. Too much diving, if you ask me. Back in my day, you got tackled, you stayed down and  stayed  down, then got back up and tackled harder!      George, you and your stories. Liam, don’t worry about asking your dad, I’ll have a word. Easter’s just around the corner, maybe a contribution towards those trainers would be a decent present. What about you, George? Anything you’d like for Easter? Don’t say another pair of socks.      Socks are always welcome, lass! Keeps the feet warm when you're mucking out the trailers. But… actually, there’s this new fella down at the auction mart… makes proper log furniture. I saw a coffee table last week, beautiful bit of oak. Real sturdy. That log's nearly slid out of the fireplace again, you know.      Honestly, George, you’d think with all your hauling experience you’d have secured that log properly! I swear, it's plotting against me. Liam, have you been listening to that new band your friend told you about? The ‘Static Void’ or something?      Yeah, they’re alright. Bit loud, but alright. They played at the youth club last Friday. Dad said I looked like I'd seen a ghost when I got home.      Loud?

… honestly, I just don’t  get  the hype around those gastropubs, y’know? People queue for ages for a tenner’s worth of posh chips and a pint of something vaguely artisanal. Give me a proper boozer any day. Like the Dun Cow back home. Now  that  was a pub. The Dun Cow? Right, the one near the stadium? That place was…robust. A bit sticky, if I recall correctly. Cambridge pubs are different. It’s all about the ambiance, isn't it? And the craft ales. It's a different beast entirely. Sticky is… a generous description. But it was  real . And the people were proper grafters. No one pretending to be a wine connoisseur. Plus, they did a cracking Sunday dinner. Speaking of which, I’m making roasted veg with this tea. You not allergic to Brussels sprouts, are ya? Brussels sprouts? Good lord, no. My mum practically force-fed them to me as a child as penance for…well, for being a kid. They’re alright. Though I still instinctively shudder. What about you? You weren’t exactly a veggie enthusiast growing up, if I remember. Strictly chicken nuggets and chips. Ay, that’s fair. Dad tried to get me to eat kale once.  Kale . In Sunderland. Nearly lost it. But I've… evolved. Postgrad life and all that. Suddenly feeling responsible for my internal organs. Though I did see someone on that celebrity cooking show – was it ‘Celebrity Kitchen Chaos’ or something equally ridiculous? – trying to make a beetroot Wellington. A  beetroot  Wellington! Oh, no. Don’t tell me it was Claudia Winkleman? She’d look fabulous doing it, even if it was a disaster. She always looks fabulous. Though, to be fair, half of those shows are just train wrecks for ratings. I mean, who actively  wants  to see Gordon Ramsay yell at Susan Boyle about a soufflé? It was… I think it was Joe Lycett. He was attempting it with this incredibly serious face. It was a thing of beauty. Honestly, though, the level of pretension on those shows. It's mental. Reminds me of some of the people we met at that art exhibition last week. All "oooh, the  nuance  of the brushstrokes." Mmm, lovely. Thanks. You’ve got a knack for making a proper brew, even down south. And you’re right about the art people. So performative. It's like they’re trying to convince themselves they understand something.

Right, okay, okay. No acting out  entire  scenes, Rhys! Just a description! Honestly, you were practically doing a full rendition of Hamlet trying to get us to guess ‘Shakespeare’. It wasn't fair! Well, now, Elana, don't be like that. A bit of dramatic flair is  essential  for Articulate, isn't it? Besides, you got it eventually! Though I suspect it was more relief than actual deduction. He was very committed to the "to be or not to be" bit. Nearly knocked over Auntie Megan’s tea. Oh, I didn’t see that, thankfully! Though, I  did  see your mum, Bronwen, nearly choke on a biscuit trying not to laugh at Rhys. That was a sight. Oh, she did! She’s terrible at keeping a straight face. Especially when Rhys gets going. It reminds me of when he tried to learn the ukulele… Don't  start  with the ukulele, Mam! That’s a closed chapter. A very embarrassing closed chapter. Speaking of closed chapters, can we just clarify the rule about sounds? Because I’m pretty sure you, Gareth, got away with humming the theme tune to ‘Jaws’ for ‘shark’ last round. It was evocative! It  represented  the shark! Artistic license. Hmm, I thought it was a rather blatant contravention of the rules. I’m with Elana on this. We agreed no humming, no singing… just sounds that a shark might  make . Honestly, you boys are like children. It’s a game, for goodness sake. Though, I did think Gareth was pushing it. A little ‘chomp chomp’ would have sufficed. But the  suspense ! The  mounting terror ! You have to build the atmosphere! Look, I’m explaining theatrical technique! It's… it’s pedagogical! Being a teacher and all. Pedagogical humming? That’s a new one. You know, growing up in Cape Town, we played a similar game, but with much stricter rules. You had to use only one word. One word to describe anything. It forced you to be incredibly precise. One word? That sounds… brutal. I thrive on ambiguity! It adds layers! It sounds wonderfully challenging, actually. Perhaps we could try that sometime. It would certainly rein in Rhys’s enthusiasm. Oh, that's a good idea, Elana! It might make it a bit fairer for those of us who aren’t drama queens. I am not a drama queen! I’m a… a communicator! A vibrant explainer of concepts!

Honestly, Rhys, you’re ruthless! Another point to the Welsh contingent. It’s becoming embarrassingly clear who the card sharks are in this family. Ruthless? Nah, just strategically gifted, Carys. Years of playing 'Rummy' with Nain kept me sharp. You wouldn't understand, being raised on… what IS it you played in South Africa? Something involving tiny little painted stones? Oh, here we go. Not stones, Rhys!  Draughts ! And it requires just as much strategic thinking, thank you very much. It’s a perfectly respectable game. Though admittedly, a bit less reliant on bluffing than… whatever this is you lot call a game. It  is  a good game, though. Been a while since I've played. Feels… normal. Good normal. That’s the point, isn’t it, Gareth? Just a bit of normal. Away from everything. This cottage is lovely, even if the WiFi is practically non-existent. Forced interaction is good for the soul. She’s right. And honestly, this forced interaction is revealing far too much about the competitive streak in all of you. I thought I was the teacher, supposed to be controlling things, but I’m being completely decimated! That's because you’re overthinking it, Carys. You’re approaching it like a lesson plan. Relax! Feel the cards! Embrace the chaos! ‘Embrace the chaos’? Is that a Welsh teaching methodology I’m unaware of? More of a Welsh  life  methodology, dear. Everything’s a bit chaotic, really. You learn to go with it. Remember that time your Uncle Bryn tried to build a shed with only a hammer and sheer willpower? Chaos. Glorious chaos. He insisted the shed was structurally sound. Until the first gust of wind. Structurally sound! It looked like a drunken giraffe had attempted carpentry. Speaking of which, anyone fancy a tea break? I’m starting to feel the need for a proper cuppa. Yes, please! And maybe while you’re up, could you grab the biscuits? I think I need some sugar to fuel my rapidly dwindling chances of winning. This is ridiculous. I’m losing to Gareth, who hasn’t said more than ten words all evening! He's a quiet soul, our Gareth. But he’s a cunning player, always has been. He used to beat his grandfather at chess when he was only eight. Chess, you say? That explains it. Systems thinking. Logical deduction. He’s probably calculated the probability of me drawing the Queen of Spades.

…and honestly, the reading list is  insane . Like, three novels a week, plus critical essays? Professor Davies is clearly trying to break us. It’s not even like enjoyable novels, either. It’s all…really dense Victorian stuff. Sounds rough, Chloe. Uni’s a big leap from A-Levels, innit? Remember when we all stressed about predicted grades? Feels like a lifetime ago. Still makes me grateful I went straight into care work after sixth form. Less reading, more…actual people. Yeah, it’s a different kind of pressure. I’m loving the accounting course, but the sheer  volume  of numbers is ridiculous. I swear I dream in spreadsheets now. Though, it’s good money, hopefully. Especially compared to retail, Holly. How’s that going alongside your studies? It’s…busy. Really busy. Especially this close to Christmas. Everyone's panic buying. I’m just counting down the days until I can actually sleep for more than five hours. Honestly, I'm starting to think I need to drop some shifts. It's impacting my coursework. You sound exactly like I felt doing my degree and working part-time at the pub. Found a balance eventually, but it’s a juggle. Speaking of juggling, how’s Auntie Brenda doing? Mum said she wasn't feeling brilliant last week. She’s a bit up and down, Tom. The arthritis is really playing up in the cold weather. She’s trying to be cheerful for Christmas, but she's getting frustrated she can't do as much baking as she used to. Keeps saying “My hands just won’t  do  it!” Oh no, poor Auntie Brenda. We should probably send her something nice. Maybe a really soft blanket? Or one of those heated throws? Good idea. And maybe a gift voucher for a massage? That might help with the pain. What are we all getting each other, anyway? Have we even talked about presents? I haven’t even  started  shopping. I've got a bit… disorganized. I was thinking of getting you all something small, but work's been mental. I did see a funny mug with a sloth on it…suited to everyone here, really. A sloth mug? Perfect. I’m pretty much sorted, actually. Got Mum a new gardening set, Dad some fancy whiskey, and trying to convince myself a voucher for Chloe is a thoughtful present.  Trying  to convince yourself? Sounds a bit last minute, even for you.

… honestly, I just don’t see the point of all this electric scooter business. It's a menace, it is. Youngsters whizzing about, no helmets, dodging pedestrians. Nearly took out old Mr. Henderson last week down Mill Road, apparently. Gran, you say that about  everything  new! Remember when you thought mobile phones were the devil’s work? That’s different! That was just… disruptive. This is  dangerous . And frankly, lazy. Why walk when you can scoot? When you can  enjoy  a nice walk? We used to walk everywhere when I was a girl. Miles we’d walk. Essex isn't flat like Cambridge, mind you, got some proper hills, but we did it! Built character. She's got a point, you know. It's nice to just… wander. I walked into town earlier, just to get a paper. Took me about forty minutes, but it was good to stretch my legs. Beats sitting around all day, that’s for sure. It’s just convenient, isn't it? I cycle to work most days, but sometimes, especially if it's raining, a scooter would be quicker. And safer than cycling in Cambridge traffic, truthfully. Drivers are awful. Awful! That's another thing. Everyone’s driving everywhere. Used to be, you’d see families cycling, taking picnics. Now it’s just cars, cars, cars. And the parking! Don’t even get me started on the parking. They've ruined this city with the cars. It used to be a lovely, quiet place. It has changed. I used to come here with Dad when I was a kid. We’d cycle along the Backs, have a picnic by the river… never saw this much traffic. He’d have a fit if he saw it now. He’d be saying “waste of good petrol!” even though he wasn’t a big driver himself, strangely. He always preferred the train, didn’t he? Remember him telling that story about getting stuck in a blizzard driving to Norfolk? He swore he'd never drive long distance again. Oh, that story! Stuck for hours, he was. Said he practically lived on biscuits and lukewarm tea. Poor man! Still, he always said a good walk clears the head. He used to say, “A tired dog is a good dog, and a tired man is a sensible man.” Corny, but true. Classic Dad. Speaking of sensible… are you still thinking of driving down to Brighton next weekend, Gran?

…and honestly, the way they’re framing it in the reports is  so  reductive. Like, “Oh, a slight dip in participle usage amongst younger speakers.” Slight! It’s a systemic shift, isn't it? A whole generation navigating language differently. It's fascinating, actually.      Absolutely. It's easy for people outside the field to just see it as ‘decline’, isn't it? They don’t grasp the nuance. It’s evolution, really. I was just reading a paper on dialect levelling in London – you wouldn't believe how quickly it’s happening.      London’s always been a bit of a melting pot for language, has it not? Though, in my day, the accents were much more…distinct. You could tell a Chelsea girl from a Bow boy without even trying. Now, it all sort of blends, doesn’t it?      Exactly! And that blending is  itself  a linguistic phenomenon. It's just, describing it to someone who thinks grammar is immutable… challenging. This alumni day is brilliant, though, isn't it? Good to connect with people who actually  get  it. I’m Eliza, by the way. Language Research Co-ordinator.      Hi Eliza, I’m Sophie. Research Administrator. And I agree, it’s nice to be away from the spreadsheets for a bit and actually  talk  about the work. Have you done much fieldwork outside of the UK?      A little. I spent a summer in the Basque Country a couple of years ago. Absolutely incredible. The language, Euskara, is so unique. Completely unrelated to anything else in Europe. It was a dream to study. Have you been to Spain?      Oh, yes, Spain. Lovely country. I lectured for a semester at the University of Salamanca years ago. Beautiful city. Always loved the cadence of the Spanish language – so melodic. Though, I confess, my Spanish is…rusty, shall we say. I spent more time attempting to explain cricket to my students. A baffling experience for everyone involved.      Cricket and explaining it to non-Brits… a truly Herculean task! I’ve been to Barcelona a few times, but no further afield in Spain. I’d love to go to the Basque Country though, it sounds amazing. It must be quite different culturally, too.      It is. Very proud people, and fiercely protective of their language and culture. It's a tiny region, but packs a punch. It made me think about language preservation in a different light, you know?

… honestly, seeing Auntie Maureen share  everything  on Facebook is a bit much. Like, do we  really  need a photo of every single meal? It's just…a lot. Oh, bless her. She only joined last year, didn’t she? She’s making up for lost time. Remember when she didn't even know how to turn a computer on? It's a far cry from the ice bucket challenge days - she was  terrified  of getting wet, but did it for charity anyway. Good old Maureen. That's true! She was a mess after that. Shivering for days! Though, speaking of charities, did you two donate to that children's hospital one, the one Sarah was fundraising for? I completely forgot, and now the deadline's passed. I did, yeah. Put a tenner in. Small contribution, but it adds up. How’s Sarah doing, anyway? Haven't spoken to her in ages. Last I heard, she was thinking about adoption. She is good. She and Mark finally started the process. It's a long haul, obviously, but they’re really excited. She says the paperwork is…a nightmare, though. All those forms! Sounds familiar, doesn’t it? Remember all the university application forms, Liam? Don’t even  go  there. The UCAS form single-handedly aged me ten years. Though, looking back, maybe I should've just gone straight into work like you, Chloe. You were always the sensible one. Sensible and stuck doing admin for a dentist! Don't romanticise it, Liam. Though it pays the bills. And it’s not  all  bad. Mrs. Higgins tells me everything, you wouldn’t believe the stories. It’s like a real-life soap opera. Speaking of bills, Mum's been going on about needing help with her garden. Says her back's been playing up again. Honestly, she won't take it easy. She still tries to dig everything herself. She's always been stubborn. Remember when she insisted on building that shed herself? Nearly broke her arm. We need to get her doing something less… energetic. Maybe gentle exercise classes? Good idea. And we need to talk to her about eating better. She's practically living on biscuits and tea. Honestly, it's a miracle she’s still going strong. It's worrying, you know? Seeing her slow down. It is. Makes you think about our own parents, doesn’t it? And what’s going to happen as they get older.

…and honestly, the instructions for this machine are  criminal . Absolutely criminal. It's supposed to be automatic, isn't it? Automatic! I’ve spent the best part of an hour trying to get it to froth milk properly. It just…splutters. More like a grumpy cat than a coffee machine.      Sounds frustrating, Mary. Are you sure you’ve used the right setting? Maybe the milk’s too cold? I remember Dad complaining about something similar with his last one.      Cold? It’s practically shivering! I’ve tried every setting going. And your father’s machines are…well, a different breed of complicated altogether. He likes things that require a PhD to operate. This one  should  be simple. Honestly, a simple cup of decent coffee is too much to ask for.      You’re both making a mountain out of a molehill. It’s a coffee machine, Mary. A luxury, frankly. I remember when a cup of instant was a treat.      Oh, don’t start with the ‘when I was a lad’ stories, Arthur. Things are allowed to improve, you know. Besides, it's not about the coffee  being  a luxury. It’s about something being advertised as easy and then being utterly perplexing. It’s the principle of the thing!      Speaking of principles… did either of you get a chance to look at those quotes for storage? I’m a bit worried about how much it's all going to cost. Getting rid of things is harder than I thought.      I had a quick look. It’s daylight robbery, that’s what it is. £80 a month? For a glorified shed? They’re taking advantage of people downsizing.      And we’ve a  lot  of downsizing to do, haven’t we? Years and years of accumulated…stuff. It's a grim thought. I was hoping to keep the piano, but there’s just no room in the flat.      That’s a shame, Mary. You used to play beautifully.      Used to being the operative word. Haven’t touched it properly in years. It feels wrong, though, letting it go. It’s…symbolic, almost. Like letting go of a part of myself.      Sentimental claptrap, if you ask me. It’s a piano. A large, cumbersome piece of furniture. Practicality must prevail. Although… speaking of things going wrong… have you been following the Labour leadership shambles?      A little. It's all rather messy, isn’t it?

… honestly, Mum, I’m starting to think December is just a relentless march of obligations. It's not  joyful  anymore, it's just... a to-do list with tinsel. Oh, don’t be dramatic, love. It’s Christmas! A bit of organised chaos is part of the fun. Though I grant you, it  does  get more complicated the older we get. Remember when it was just about the anticipation of Santa and ripping open presents? Vaguely. Nowadays it’s coordinating three different family Christmas dinners, making sure Uncle Barry doesn’t start a political argument, and trying to buy thoughtful gifts for people who already have everything. And the school Christmas fair! Don't even get me started. Barry  always  starts a political argument. It’s tradition now, isn’t it? Though your Auntie Margaret usually shuts him down pretty quickly. Are you going to manage all three dinners this year? Totnes, Cardiff, and… where is your partner’s family again? York. Which is… a trek. I was thinking maybe we suggest a neutral venue next year? A pub somewhere in the Midlands? Less pressure on anyone’s house. A pub? That’s…different. Though, not a bad idea actually. It certainly bypasses the cleaning frenzy. What does David think? He’s diplomatic. He says whatever I think is best. Which usually means he’s bracing himself for a weekend of travel. He's a good egg, really. Speaking of which, how are your plans looking? Are you sticking with us in Totnes this year? I am, yes. Though I’m already dreading the drive. That A38 is a nightmare this time of year. I’m hoping to get down a couple of days before to help you with the preparations. I was thinking of doing a big batch of mince pies, if you’d like. Mum, that would be amazing! You make the best mince pies. Seriously. I attempted it last year and they were… well, let’s just say they resembled something more akin to pastry frisbees. Oh, darling. Some things are best left to the experts. So, work-wise, how's the TEFL going? Still enjoying it? It's…fine. It pays the bills. But honestly, I'm starting to think I need a change. It's just, what else would I  do ? I only did Sixth Form, remember? A degree feels so far away now. Don’t write yourself off, love.

… honestly, I’m telling you, I nearly choked on me own tongue last night. Liam was  right  out of it. Absolute log sawin’. Liam? Snorin’? Never! He always claims he doesn't. Him and Dad, both the same. Denial merchants when it comes to noisy nights. Oh, he does. Last time I stayed at his, I swear the windows were rattling. I had to shove a pillow over my head. It was like living next to a pneumatic drill. You’re lucky it was just a pillow. My flatmate, bless 'er, sounds like a walrus giving birth. I’ve considered ear defenders. Proper, industrial strength ones. Walrus giving birth? That's a visual. You alright for sleep, though, Amy? You look a bit knackered. Just uni deadlines, mostly. And the walrus. It’s a combo. But hey, at least it’s Friday. What are we all up to this weekend? I’m supposed to be helping Mum with a clear-out. Dreadful. She’s decided she needs to “re-organise” the attic. Which means finding things she hasn’t seen in twenty years and insisting I admire them. Oh, the attic saga. That's a classic. You'll find loads of old photos and probably a box of Dad’s handkerchiefs. He’s still got about a million of them, hasn’t he? He does! And he uses them. Proper folded-in-the-pocket sort of handkerchief wearer. It's so…old fashioned. It is, isn’t it? Like something out of a film. Speaking of old fashioned, did you see Waterfields is doing those Eccles cakes again? The proper ones, with the currants? Ooh, get in! I love Waterfields. Their sausage rolls are decent too, but the Eccles cakes are the main event. I'll have to pop in on Saturday. Waterfields is the best. Beats Greggs any day. Although, I'm craving a Richmond sausage roll right now, to be fair. That’s a proper guilty pleasure. Richmond sausages are alright. A bit… processed, aren't they? Still, they do the job. Remember when Sarah tried to make her own sausages? That was a disaster. Oh god, yes! They were all different sizes and shapes, and half of them didn’t stay together when she fried them! She had sausage pieces bouncing all over the kitchen. And the seasoning was completely off! Some were practically salt-free, others were like eating pure chilli powder.

… honestly, the sheer  volume  of glitter. Everywhere. I’m still finding it in my hair. Little flecks just… clinging on for dear life. Sounds like Maisie had a good time then, eh? She loves a bit o’ sparkle, that one. Though glitter… that’s a parent’s nightmare, that is. Gets  everywhere . Reminds me of when young David used to insist on decorating the entire kitchen for Christmas with tinsel. Brenda nearly had a fit. It was a craft afternoon. A ‘magical unicorn’ theme. I thought it sounded sweet, but it descended into chaos pretty quickly. Ten four-year-olds armed with glue and glitter is a recipe for disaster, honestly. Still, Maisie was beaming. She made me a sparkly horn, which is… endearing, even if it sheds. They do live for those things, don’t they? It's that pure joy. Beats any fancy holiday, that. Speaking of which, did you manage to get anything sorted for your mum’s birthday next month? I know she was hinting about that little pottery place in Rye. Oh, crikey, I almost forgot! Rye… yes, she mentioned that. I’ve been so swamped with the Henderson account at work, it's flown by. They’re being particularly difficult. Endless revisions on the marketing materials. It's like talking to a brick wall sometimes. I was thinking maybe a voucher, just to be safe? Give her the freedom to choose? A voucher’s always sensible. Though, to be fair, your mum likes experiencing things more than… stuff. That pottery class would be lovely. They do a weekend workshop as well, you could even go with her! Quality time and all that. Hmm, that’s a good shout, actually. I could definitely do with a weekend away from spreadsheets. Though, the Henderson thing is stressing me out. Mr. Henderson himself keeps emailing me directly, bypassing David – my manager – and it feels… off. He keeps questioning every decision. Bypassing David, you say? That  is  odd. Sounds like he's trying to micromanage, and not very subtly. You’ve been doing a good job, you always do. Don’t let him fluster you. Agricultural businesses are full of folks like that, y’know. Always thinkin’ they know best, despite never having actually  done  the work. It's just… it's making me doubt myself, which is ridiculous. I’ve got a degree, I’ve been doing this for two years, I know what I’m doing!

…and honestly, the kids were lovely, absolutely lovely. But marking 150 essays on the subjunctive  every  week? It just…drained me. It felt like all I was doing was correcting grammar, not actually  teaching  them to communicate. Ugh, the subjunctive. A linguistic black hole. I feel your pain. Though, to be fair, my Year 9s are currently wrestling with conditional sentences. It’s not much better. At least you were teaching something… beautiful, in a way. I’m stuck doing data analysis for behaviour reports now. Glorified spreadsheet jockeying. Spreadsheet jockeying! That’s brilliant. Sounds… fulfilling. Is it a big step down from the classroom? Massively. I miss the interaction. I miss the little breakthroughs when someone finally  gets  something. You know? This is just… numbers. And meetings about numbers. I took it because it was ‘development opportunity’ and, frankly, financially it’s a bit better. But I’m already thinking I made a mistake. How are you finding things at the language school then? Still enjoying the adult learners? Much more so, actually. They  want  to be there. They're learning French for pleasure, for travel, for their brains. Not because they’re being forced to. I’ve got a retired solicitor who’s determined to read Proust in the original, which is… ambitious, to say the least. And a lovely couple planning a cycling holiday through Burgundy. It's genuinely rewarding. That sounds idyllic! Honestly, I’m seriously considering retraining. I even looked into TEFL, but I worry I’m too… settled here. And then there’s the whole baby situation. Ah, yes! How are things progressing on that front? Any news? You and Mark were talking about trying for a while now, weren’t you? We are! Just found out last week. Seven weeks, apparently. Still a bit surreal, to be honest. Trying not to get  too  excited, you know? One step at a time. Though, I've already downloaded about twenty pregnancy apps. Don't judge! Oh, darling, absolutely no judgement! That's wonderful news! Congratulations! Honestly, that's brilliant. It's terrifying and amazing all rolled into one, isn't it? We’re trying too, actually. No luck yet, but we're staying optimistic. It's just… timing feels tricky with the job and everything. It  is  tricky. And I’m already convinced my career is over! No one wants to hire a pregnant woman, or a mother returning to work.

…No, I’m tellin’ ya, Doreen, it wasn’t the blackbird. Blackbirds are a bit more…refined, aren’t they? This was a proper right mess. Bits of twig everywhere, lookin’ like a bomb’d hit the rose bush. Must’ve been a magpie. Always the magpies, causin’ trouble. Bold as brass, they are. Bold as brass is right, Arthur. Saw one tryin’ to nick a biscuit right off my plate last week. Little beggar. Though, mind you, they're clever birds. Built a nest in old Mrs. Higgins’ gutter last year, right above her front door! Oh, the cheek of it! She was furious, wasn’t she? Remember her wavin’ her umbrella at it? Honestly, some birds have no respect. Did you manage to clear up the mess, Arthur? I brought a slice of Victoria sponge, hoping we could enjoy it  without  avian interference. Cleared most of it. Still findin’ little bits of moss in the lavender. It's a thankless task, this gardening, when you get these feathered hooligans involved. Bit of a shock, though, seeing it so close to the bird feeder. You’d think they’d be already well-supplied. Maybe they were buildin’ a spare? You know, a holiday home. They do get ambitious, those magpies. Though I’ve been worried about the feeder, actually. Haven’t seen much activity lately. It could be the heat. They slow down a bit when it gets scorching. Though, I did read something about diabetes affecting birds… something about them getting too sluggish to visit. Sounds daft, doesn’t it? Diabetes in birds? Now you’re pullin’ my leg, Doreen. Next you’ll be tellin’ me they need little insulin injections! Though, I suppose, old age gets to everyone, feathered or not. It’s all slowin’ down, isn't it? I feel it in me knees. Aye, it is. Old age creeps up on you like a fog. Remember when we used to be able to go for a proper ramble in the woods? Now it’s a careful stroll ‘round the garden with a cup of tea. I tell ya, lookin' after that garden is good for us. Keeps us movin'. Honestly, you two. Don’t talk about being old! It's depressing. Here, have some cake. It might cheer you up. I was thinkin’ of gettin’ the puppets out later. Little Timmy Mitchell left them here last week.

…and honestly, the meze just  keeps  coming! I thought I’d ordered a small plate, but it’s a feast. Are you enjoying yours, Arthur? Oh, it’s lovely, Sarah. Absolutely lovely. Proper food, isn’t it? Not like some of the, shall we say, ‘adapted’ Cypriot cuisine you get back home. This tastes… genuine. I’ve gone for the Kleftiko, you see. Been meaning to try proper Kleftiko for years. Good choice. I went for the grilled halloumi and chicken skewers. It's perfect for a hot day like this. Speaking of hot, did you notice that couple over there? The man's trying to discreetly fan himself with the menu! Oh, bless him. They look a bit out of their depth, don’t they? First time in Cyprus, I reckon. Everyone’s a bit flushed at first. This heat gets to you. Reminds me of that time Brenda, my sister, came to Spain with us. Thought she could cope… ended up needing a lie-down for half the week! Brenda and heat don't mix! How  is  Brenda, actually? I haven’t spoken to her since… well, since Dad passed. She’s… managing. The arthritis is getting worse, though. Being stubborn, naturally, refusing to properly take the medication. Says it ‘makes her feel foggy’. It's like talking to a brick wall sometimes. She won't even consider getting one of those new hearing aids, says they're for 'old people'. And she's only a few years younger than me! Oh, Arthur. It’s awful watching them decline, isn’t it? Mum was exactly the same with her hearing. Stubborn as a mule. I kept saying, “Mum, it's not admitting defeat, it’s improving your quality of life!” But she just wouldn’t have it. It made conversations so difficult in the end. Exactly! You feel so helpless. It’s funny, she used to be so…full of life. Remember how she used to go on about that man she met at the tennis club? That Geoffrey? Oh, Geoffrey. The retired dentist with the terrible toupee. She was convinced he was ‘the one’ for a good six months. That ended with a lot of tears and a rather pointed remark about his dental hygiene. Oh, good grief. She had a knack for romantic disasters, didn’t she? Anyway, this heat makes me philosophical. Makes you think about destiny, don’t you think?

… honestly, the flat hunt is  brutal . You wouldn’t believe the state of some places. And for the price! I saw one yesterday, barely bigger than a postage stamp, and they wanted £1200 a month! In Tooting! Oh, you poor thing. London’s just… ridiculous now. Remember when we could get a decent flat for, what, six hundred? Seems like a lifetime ago. It's a complete rip-off. Aye, it is. Everything's gone up. Even the price of a pint! Though, to be fair, I was complaining about that even  before  inflation really kicked in. Just an old man grumbling, I suppose. How's work, though? Still buried in spreadsheets, are you, love? Pretty much, Dad. It’s the usual. Project co-ordination is basically just glorified herding cats. Everyone has an opinion and no one can agree on timelines. But the new campaign is interesting, it's for a sustainable fashion brand, which is...nice, to actually feel like I’m working for something I believe in. That  is  good, dear. It's important to enjoy what you do, or at least find something worthwhile in it. Now, have you thought about maybe looking a little further out? Like, Croydon or even further south? Might get more for your money. I have, Mum, I really have. But the commute would be awful. I’m already spending two hours a day just getting to and from the office. I need to find something reasonably central. It's tempting to just move back in here forever, honestly. Don't you start! Your mother would have a field day redecorating your room. Though, speaking of redecorating… we finally got a quote for the kitchen. It’s… substantial. Substantial is putting it mildly, David! It’s a small fortune! But honestly, it needs doing. That lino is older than your daughter! And the units are falling apart. Ooh, can I see the plans? I might have some ideas. I've been Pinterest-ing kitchens obsessively to distract myself from the flat hunt. I’ve discovered a surprising fondness for shaker kitchens. Shaker kitchens? Sounds… sturdy. We’re thinking something similar. Practical, you know? We’re not getting any younger. Although, your Auntie Brenda was telling me she’s taken up competitive ballroom dancing. At seventy-two! Brenda! Always one to surprise. She’s got more energy than all of us put together.

… honestly, I still can’t believe she fell for it. A bloke pretending to be a soldier stationed overseas? Come  on ! It’s like something straight outta Jeremy Kyle, innit? Seriously! And she sent him money! Loads of it, apparently. Me mam was tellin’ me all about it, she works with ‘er auntie. A proper catfish situation, like. It’s just…sad, really. She’s a lovely woman, our Brenda. Too trusting, like. It’s awful. I saw something on TikTok about it, some compilation of catfish stories. It’s just people preyin’ on vulnerability, isn’t it? And the lengths they go to! Fake photos, fabricated stories… It's proper manipulative. Aye, that's what gets me. The  effort  they put into lyin’. Could be using that energy for somethin’ useful, like learnin’ a trade or somethin’. Instead, they’re spendin’ it craftin’ a whole fake identity. Is it boredom, d’you think? Or are they genuinely malicious? I reckon it's a bit of both. Some are probably just lonely and desperate for attention. But then you get the ones who genuinely enjoy hurtin’ people. They’re the proper weirdos, aren’t they? Like that fella on Jeremy Kyle who turned out to be… well, you remember that one, didn't ya? With the lie detector? Oh God, yes! The one who claimed he wasn't the father, then the machine went  boop  and he completely lost it. Classic Jeremy Kyle. It’s car crash television, but you can’t look away. It's awful, but you’re right. Like, you  know  it’s gonna be bad, but you need to see just  how  bad. Brenda’s story reminds me a bit of those Jeremy Kyle ones, actually. She was convinced she was building a relationship and planning to move to Germany to be with him. Germany! She’s never even been to Blackpool. Oh, bless her. Poor cow. And apparently, 'he' was sendin’ her all these poems and talkin' about marriage and everything! She was walkin’ around lookin' like she’d won the lottery. Then her niece did a reverse image search on one of his photos… and it turned out to be some model from Italy. No way! That's mental. Reverse image search is a saviour, though, isn’t it? I always do that if someone looks a bit too good to be true on a dating app.

… honestly, the WiFi's been a right state all morning. Trying to upload this essay for Professor Davies is driving me mental. It keeps timing out halfway through. You wouldn’t believe the amount of data it is, all those diagrams I had to create. Oh, technology. Always a drama, isn't it? Reminds me of trying to get a decent telephone line to my studio in the early nineties. Absolute nightmare. Are you sure it’s not just the router? Have you tried switching it off and on again? The universal solution to everything, darling. Yeah, course I have, Gran! Several times. It’s not that. I think it’s the university servers, overloaded with everyone submitting at the last minute. Speaking of overloaded, Paris was  packed  last weekend. Absolutely rammed. Paris! Oh, I haven’t been back in… goodness, must be twenty years. Though, truthfully, I always preferred Italy.
