Honestly, you’d think we were running a specialist dietary hospital, not a primary school. And the lunchboxes… oh, the lunchboxes! Half of them are miniature versions of a health hazard. Crisps, chocolate biscuits, sugary drinks. It defeats the whole point of the free school meals, doesn't it? It’s a nightmare. I’m doing the rotas and trying to make sure we have enough staff to supervise all the… considerations. Though, I must say, the new system  is  getting more food to families who need it. That’s good. But the admin! It’s burying us. It is, isn't it? Though I remember a time when ‘admin’ was rationing coupons and knowing what was available, not what wasn’t allowed! My mother-in-law, poor woman, had quite a story. Escaped Siberia during the war, travelled all the way to Africa… can you imagine? They ate whatever they could get their hands on. Roots, berries, things that would make your stomach turn now. No talk of gluten-free then, believe you me. Goodness me, that  is  a journey. My Nan used to talk about wartime rations, but Siberia… that’s something else. She just made do. Everything was boiled to within an inch of its life, apparently. Said it didn’t matter what it was, as long as it filled you up. She’d make a sausage casserole to feed the whole village, even though sausages were a real treat. Sausage casserole! Now  that  sounds good. Speaking of sausages, have you been to the Farm Shop lately? They do a lovely Cumberland, proper pork, none of that watery stuff. Much better than the Village Shop, even though it’s terribly convenient. Actually, I prefer the Village Shop for everyday things. It’s just… easier. And Mrs. Higgins always has a gossip. I did try the Farm Shop Cumberland once. It was good, admittedly. Though my husband, Arthur, is a bit of a sausage connoisseur. He makes his own, you know. Does he now? Arthur's a clever man.

… honestly, I just feel like everyone’s got their lives  sorted , y’know? Like Chloe’s landed that amazing job in Manchester, and you, Freya, are practically running the whole production line at yours. And me? I'm still chasing RSVPs for a vegan cheese convention. It's not exactly glamorous, is it? Oi, don’t sell yourself short, Maisie. Vegan cheese is a booming market! And honestly, production control is… stressful. People expect things  now , and if a single widget is delayed, it's my head on the chopping block. It’s nothing glamorous, believe me. More spreadsheets than social life. You both sound exhausting! I mean, admin is… admin. Lots of filing, lots of emails, lots of people needing things yesterday. But it's not like I'm building rockets, is it? It’s just… consistent. And comparatively low pressure. Though Brenda in accounts is currently convinced I’ve stolen her stapler. That’s my excitement for the week. Brenda and her stapler, classic. Seriously though, I'm starting to wonder if I picked the wrong degree. Events management seemed so… fun. All fancy parties and networking. Turns out it's mostly logistics and dealing with dietary requirements. And Yorkshire hospitality doesn’t quite translate when you're telling someone their request for a gluten-free, sugar-free, dairy-free, nut-free canapé is a bit much. See, that  is  stressful! I had a similar crisis last month. We were launching a new product and someone demanded we source ethically-sourced, fair-trade glitter. Glitter! Like, what even  is  ethical glitter? It’s tiny plastic particles! Oh, God, the demands people make! I had someone ask me to re-format a presentation in Comic Sans. Comic Sans! I politely explained that wasn’t really “on brand” for a law firm. They weren’t pleased. Oh, bless you. You handled that brilliantly. Look, I’m just craving some… normalcy, I think. Remember when we used to just hang out, not worrying about career paths or Brenda’s stapler? Vaguely. It feels like a lifetime ago, doesn't it? Uni feels a million miles away. We were all just figuring things out then, without the pressure of actually  having  to have it figured out. We should definitely do something. Proper catch-up, not just a quick cuppa whilst simultaneously replying to emails. I'm surprisingly free next weekend. No urgent stapler-related crises anticipated.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it! They’re proposing a luxury flats development. Luxury flats, David! In Plumstead! Who are they building them  for ? Not the people who live here, that’s for sure. Mmm. It’s the usual story, isn’t it? Borough council chasing revenue. They probably looked at the land value, saw potential for a quick buck, and the library just…didn't factor. It's infuriating. I saw old Mrs. Higgins practically in tears down there yesterday. She uses the computers three times a week. Exactly! It’s not just about the books, David. It's a community hub. The kids go after school, the pensioners have their reading groups… it's  vital . We absolutely have to fight this. I was thinking, a petition is a good start, but we need a proper one, online  and  paper. I've got a template drafted, actually. I just need to refine it. Good, good. You’re brilliant at that sort of thing. I’m useless with the tech side of it, you know that. My shift at the office yesterday was a nightmare, though. New system implementation. Absolutely chaotic. Spent the whole day fielding complaints. Felt like I was putting out fires, honestly. Oh, bless you. Sounds ghastly. Being an administrator with a new system is… well, it’s a special kind of hell, isn't it? It's amazing how resistant people are to even the smallest changes. They think everything was perfect the way it was, even if it clearly wasn't. You’ve hit the nail on the head. And then they blame  us ! Anyway, back to the library. What kind of numbers do you think we need on a petition to get them to even listen? I’m aiming for five hundred, at least. But it's not just the number, it’s the accompanying message. We need to emphasize the impact on vulnerable groups. And we need to focus on the lack of consultation. They didn’t even  ask  us! It's all decided behind closed doors. Absolutely. They announce these things as fait accompli. Reminds me of that mnemonic I was trying to teach the kids – ROY G. BIV for the colours of the rainbow. They just couldn’t get their heads around it. Keeps popping into my head, actually. Political decisions feel similar – all colours blending together to create something…murky. That's a brilliant analogy!

…and honestly, Doreen, they keep comin' back. Every month, like clockwork. Jehovah’s Witnesses. Knockin' on the door. I try to be polite, you know. “No thank you, already got me beliefs, thank’ee.” But they don't half persist, do they? It’s like they think wearin' you down is a legitimate tactic.      Bless 'em. They’re determined, I'll give 'em that. Old Mrs. Griggs down the lane, she actually got into a full-blown debate with ‘em about the Book of Revelation. Took a good hour, apparently. She’s a tough one, is Doris.      Oh, Doris! She’ll argue with a post. Though, to be fair, they  are  rather insistent. I had one try to explain to me that birthdays are pagan. Pagan! My grandson’s eighth birthday is next week. What am I supposed to tell him, eh?      Exactly! It’s all a bit much. Reminds me of young Timothy… remember Timothy, Bernard? Always had an answer for everything. Never listened, just talked. Married that girl from Attleborough, didn't he? Didn’t last six months.      Attleborough, aye. Poor lad. Always thought he was a bit too clever for his own good. Still, can't hold that against him. Marriage is a tricky business, innit? Especially these days. All this divorce…      It is. My Margaret’s sister, Brenda, is on her third husband. Honestly, it’s a revolving door. Though, she says this one’s ‘the one’. They always say that, don’t they? This one likes his food, I’ll say that much. He's a big fella.      Speaking of food, this quiche is lovely, Carol. Did you make it yourself?      I did, Arthur. Little bit of cheddar, some leeks from the garden… simple but tasty. Would you like more?      Don’t mind if I do. You always were a good cook. Though, remember that roast you did one Christmas? A bit… well, a bit dry, wasn’t it?      Oh, Arthur, always bringin' up the past! It was alright! A bit of cranberry sauce sorted it. You’re always so critical. Did you vote, by the way? In the local elections?      I did. Though honestly, I don't hold much faith in 'em. They all say the same things, don’t they? Promise the world and deliver… well, not much really. And the taxes… they just keep going up.      They do, don’t they? It's outrageous.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of logs we’ve gone through this winter is startling. I thought we’d have enough from last year's felling, but clearly not. Are you sure Mr. Henderson is giving us seasoned wood, Mum? It feels… damp still. Oh, don't start, Eleanor. Henderson’s been supplying wood to this village for forty years. He knows seasoned wood when he sees it. You’re probably just used to that fancy gas ‘fire’ you had in London. A proper log burner needs a bit of effort, you know? She’s right, you know. Takes a bit of getting used to, the real thing. Reminds me of the school dormitories, trying to coax a good flame from damp wood. Always a challenge. Though, we didn't have the luxury of a proper burner, just a grate! It  is  chilly in here, though. Even with the burner going. Maybe a draught? I’ll have a look around the windows later. Speaking of chilly, that trip to Tokyo… completely wiped me out. The jet lag was brutal. Oh, Tokyo! Was it everything you hoped for? I always wanted to go. Did you manage to get to that cat café you were talking about? It was…intense. Brilliant, but intense. And yes, the cat café. Utter chaos, but adorable chaos. Hundreds of cats. More cats than I’ve seen in my life. It makes me think of next door’s Mrs. Higgins and her fourteen! Fourteen! Good heavens. She’ll be overrun. Though, at least it keeps the mice away. We had a terrible time with mice at the school, before they brought in that terrier. Wonderful dog, Buster. Completely changed the atmosphere. Dogs are far more practical than cats. Now, now, Margaret. Don't start that again. Both have their merits. Though, I confess, I've always been a dog man. Reminds me of old Winston, my Labrador. Wonderful companion. Anyway, back to more pressing matters…the budget. It’s looking a little tight this month. That new restaurant, “The Willow Branch”, looks lovely, but…£30 for a starter? I think not. You're right. A bit steep. We could stick to our usual pub. They do a perfectly good steak and ale pie. Speaking of budgets, have you seen what they're doing with the school academies? Outsourcing everything to India. My cousin, she’s a teacher, says it's a disaster.

…No, I’m tellin’ ya, the council’s gone mad. Mad, I say! They’re talkin’ about changin’ the bin collections  again . Honestly, what’s a body to do? I spent half an hour sortin’ plastic from cardboard just last week, only for them to stick a sticker on it sayin’ it’s ‘contaminated’. Contaminated with  what ?! A bit of tape? It’s ridiculous. Aye, Norman, you always were one for a moan about the bins. Reminds me o' yer father, always complainin’ about the milkman leavin’ the bottles crooked. But they do make it difficult, don’t they? All the colour-codin’ and rules. I mostly just get Maureen to sort it, bless her. She’s got a system. It  is  a faff, isn’t it? And the taxes! Don't even  start  me on the council tax. I’m payin’ more now than when I was actually workin’! They say it’s for services, but I haven't seen much improvement around here lately. Still potholes bigger than my Morris Minor would’ve been. Exactly! And they’re always goin’ on about buildin’ more houses. More houses! Where are people gonna work, eh? And what about the infrastructure? Another few estates crammed in and the roads’ll be jammed solid. I saw a program on the telly about them tryin' to build houses up in Scotland, proper remote places. Couldn't get anyone to  go  there, let alone build the houses! Aye, I saw that. Awfully bleak. Lovely scenery, mind you. Reminded me o’ when we used to go campin’ up in the Highlands. Used to rely on a map and compass, you know. None of this Sat Nav business. Remember gettin’ lost near Loch Ness once? Maureen nearly left me! Oh, Sat Navs… a blessing and a curse. My grandson tried to take me to Norwich city centre last month. Thing took me through all the back lanes! Ended up near the sewage works! I said, "Honestly, Stephen, a map would've been quicker!" He just mumbled something about algorithms. Algorithms! They’re the ruin of everything, they are. All this modern technology. I was talkin’ to old Arthur down the pub, he was sayin’ his pension's barely coverin’ the electric bill. They keep fiddlin' with it, don’t they? Always some new tax or contribution. Remember when we had a decent state pension guaranteed? Those days are gone.

…and honestly, the fella in the shop, he was lookin’ at me like  I  broke the thing deliberately! Said it was water damage. Water damage! I haven’t even spilled a drop near it, not a single one. It's a grand machine, it was, for runnin’ the accounts. Was it expensive, Da? Like,  really  expensive? A bit pricey, yeah. Not a fortune, thankfully. But enough to make a man want to throttle a warranty claim form. It's still under warranty, surely. Honestly, Liam, you’d think they’d be a little more helpful. It’s only a couple of months old. What exactly did they say, the techie? He mumbled somethin’ about ‘evidence of liquid ingress.’ Ingress! Sounds like a disease, doesn’t it? And then he started goin’ on about voidin’ the warranty. I told him I’d be takin’ it up with head office. More sauce! More sauce! Hold on a sec, sweetie. Here you go. You do that. Don’t let them push you around. And you have all the receipts, right? Of course, I do. I’m not a complete eejit, woman! Everything's filed away. Though findin’ it is another story… Right, anyway. What’s the plan for tomorrow, then? Young Padraig was talkin’ about a rugby match. Yeah! I’m supposed to meet Jack and Tom at Musgrave Park for the under-14s game. Can you drop me off around half eleven? Half eleven, aye. Might be able to. Depends on how this computer saga unfolds, I suppose. I might have to be on the phone all mornin’ fightin’ for my rights. What about you, Sarah? Anything planned? Not really. Just the usual toddler wrangling. Daniel seems to have developed a new obsession with… well, everything. Did you try that new fajita sauce I picked up? It’s a bit spicy, even for me. I had a taste of it. Nice kick to it, alright. It needs a good dollop of sour cream though, to cool things down, wouldn't you say? Ears! Sticky out! Yes, darling, your ears  do  stick out a little. They're very cute ears. Liam, you remember to book Daniel’s swimming lesson for next week? I keep forgettin’. Swimming, right. I’ll do it tonight, promise. After I've finished attemptin’ to reason with customer service robots. Are we all good for the Rest? I mean, do you want me to pick you up after rugby, Finn?

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of glitter that ended up in the living room after the fairy garden building was…concerning. It's still turning up, honestly. Right, Leo? You’ve got a bit on your nose. It's fairy dust! Makes me strong for handstands! I did a handstand! Well,  almost . Mummy had to hold my legs. It’s really hard. You did brilliantly, darling. Absolutely brilliant. You were holding it for a really good few seconds. Leo, you’re getting so good too, aren’t you? Though perhaps a little less focus on the glitter application  during  the handstand practice next time? But sparkly handstands are  better ! They are…visually more interesting, I’ll give you that. Right, pizza is almost ready. Pepperoni okay for everyone? Can we have pineapple too? Like Hawaii? Oh, controversial! Pineapple on pizza. A divide in the nation, as they say. No, sweetheart, this time we’re sticking to pepperoni. We can have Hawaiian another time. Though personally, I think it’s a crime against Italian cuisine. But Hawaii is where the Loch Ness Monster lives, right? The Loch Ness Monster lives in  Scotland , love. Hawaii is…well, it’s famous for volcanoes and beaches and really good pineapples, actually. But I read a book! It said the Loch Ness Monster went on holiday to Hawaii! And wore sunglasses! Oh, a very well-travelled monster, then. You read a very imaginative book. Maybe Nessie needed a break from the cold Scottish water. Though, you know, it's a very big lake and a very shy monster. No confirmed sightings, unfortunately. Maybe she’s hiding! Playing hide-and-seek! That's a good thought. A very clever Nessie. Okay, pizza's here! Let’s see…eight slices. If Leo has two and you, Amelia, have three…how many slices are left? Uh… one, two, three…five! Five slices left! Exactly! Well done, Amelia! You are a mathematical whiz. Leo, your turn. What's three plus two? Five! Like Amelia! Fantastic! So, five slices left for Mummy. Not bad. You two are excellent at sharing, even when discussing the whereabouts of mythical creatures. Mummy, when is Poppy’s party? I need to pick my dress! It's next Saturday, darling. We'll have a good look through your party dresses tomorrow after school, okay? Do you want glitter on your party dress? Perhaps  controlled  glitter application this time?

… honestly, I still can’t believe how cheap the wine is here. Like, proper good wine for less than a fiver a bottle. Back in Bolton, you’d be lucky to get something drinkable for that. Aye, it’s a proper bargain, isn’t it? And the food! This  fuži  with truffles… I could eat this every day. Better than anything I've had at the hospital canteen, that's for sure. Though speaking of hospitals...did you see that documentary about the Ebola outbreak? Gave me the shivers. Ebola? Blimey. Sounds…rough. I was more worried about seagulls nicking my chips on the beach earlier. They’re proper aggressive here. Aggressive seagulls are a universal constant, it seems. Though the Croatian ones are arguably more sophisticated chip thieves than the London variety. Seriously though, the swimming pool at the villa is fantastic. Best holiday pool we’ve had in years. And a lot calmer than the beach, eh, Liam? Yeah, loads better. I’m trying to get some good photos for school. Mr. Harrison wants us to do a project on composition. It's a pain, though. He keeps going on about the 'rule of thirds’ and stuff. Oh, photography! That's good, Liam. You’ve always had a good eye. I was thinking of taking a photography module next term at Uni. It’s a bit of a change from food technology, which is…interesting. We're doing stuff with encapsulation now. Basically, making tiny flavour bombs. It's weird, clever, and a bit unsettling all at once. Encapsulation? Sounds a bit futuristic, doesn’t it? Like something out of a science fiction film. Reminds me of all that talk about Steve Jobs and innovation. He always predicted things. Absolutely. He had an uncanny ability to see where things were going. Though I’ve seen a LOT of ‘innovations’ lately that are just… repackaged old ideas. Like this buzz about vertical farming. It's good, but it’s hardly new. I was dealing with a company trying to secure funding for something similar ten years ago. Still, it's no bad thing, is it? Trying to grow food more efficiently. Especially with all the…well, with everything going on. It's just a nightmare getting through airport security now. Remember that time your friend Sarah got stopped because of that lavender oil, Mum? Oh, don't even get me started on immigration officers!

…Honestly, the cheek of ‘em, sending another letter! PPI, they call it. Payment Protection Insurance. From twenty years ago! As if I even  remember  taking out insurance with whatever company it was. They reckon I’m owed something, but they want a fee to ‘process’ the claim. A fee! It’s a right con, it is.      Oh, don't I know it, Arthur. They get you every time. Happened to Doreen next door. Signed up for something expecting a payout, ended up paying them! It’s daylight robbery. You just bin it, love. Honestly. Don’t give ‘em the satisfaction.      It’s the modern way, isn’t it? Predatory practices. They prey on people who don't necessarily understand the small print. Though frankly, even  I  struggle with the small print these days. I was reading an article in the ‘Spectator’ – rather long-winded, naturally – about algorithmic lending and how it exacerbates these situations.      Algorithm lending? Good grief, David, you  are  fancy. Sounds terrifying. It’s bad enough dealing with a person on the phone, let alone a…a computer deciding if you owe money. Speaking of which, Arthur, are you still getting on alright with that new computer? I know you were a bit dubious.      ‘Dubious’ is putting it lightly! It’s a blinking menace. Keeps asking me for passwords. Passwords I can’t remember  having ! Fiona – that’s Speaker_4, for those not in the know – showed me how to look things up, but it’s all…pictures and moving things. Gimme a good book any day. Still prefer the telly, even if it is all reality shows nowadays.      You’ll get used to it, Arthur. It’s good to keep your mind active. Though I agree, reality TV is dreadful. We were watching that 'Love Island' thing briefly…absolutely dreadful. Mind you, we’re having Gladys and Bernard round on Saturday, and Gladys  loves  it. We're having a little party. Just sandwiches and a bit of bubbly.      That sounds lovely. A bit of socialising is good for the soul. I can bring the cheese and biscuits if you'd like? I picked up a rather nice mature cheddar.      That would be brilliant, David, thank you. Arthur, did you ever get around to ordering those sunflower seeds you were talking about? They’re supposed to be good for the bees.      Seeds? Oh, yes. Ordered ‘em online. Should be here any day now.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of cases today was just… exhausting. Three shoplifting incidents, two arguments escalating into minor assault – honestly, you’d think people would have better things to do with their time. Did you have a busy one, Moira? Och, aye, busy enough. Mostly traffic offences, a bit of benefit fraud. Nothing as…  dynamic  as what you deal with, teaching all those youngsters. Though, honestly, the excuses people come up with! One chap claimed he didn’t realise there was a speed limit on the M40. The M40! You’re kidding! That’s… spectacular levels of denial. It's similar with the students sometimes. "The dog ate my homework" feels almost sophisticated compared to some of the justifications I get for late essays. It’s the human condition, isn’t it? Always a story. Aye, a story. And most of 'em, like, built on a foundation of… well, let's just say optimism with the truth. Still, it pays the bills. Though these petrol prices are crippling, aren't they? Getting to and from Birmingham is costing a fortune. Reminds me of the seventies, queues at the petrol stations and all. It is ridiculous, isn’t it? I’m trying to cycle more, but Solihull isn’t exactly cycle-friendly. They  talk  about improving infrastructure, but it’s slow going. I’m seriously considering looking into getting a small electric car, but they're still so expensive. Thinking about a trip to France next year, and the cost of getting the car on the ferry… it all adds up. France? Lovely! I haven’t been abroad in… oh, goodness, must be ten years now. Used to go to Spain with my husband, every year. He loved the heat. Miss that, to be honest. This weather we're getting now… it’s all over the place. Flooding one minute, drought the next. It worries me, it really does. What kind of world are we leaving for the grandchildren? Exactly! It's terrifying. I try to bring it up in class, with the younger ones, the importance of environmental responsibility, but it’s hard to get through. They’re overwhelmed by everything, you know? It feels so enormous. My niece, Lily, she’s just started university, studying Marine Biology. She’s fiercely dedicated, but even  she  seems discouraged sometimes. That’s good she’s studying something like that, at least. Science needs bright minds.

…and honestly, that's what it feels like, doesn’t it? Just…peaceful. Not needing anything extra. Though, a little more sleep wouldn't go amiss! Mummy, if we had  loads  of money, could we buy a bouncy castle that’s as big as the garden? And a robot dinosaur! A really, really big one that breathes  fire ! Oh, you two. A bouncy castle the size of the garden… that  would  be something. And a fire-breathing dinosaur. Right. Where would we even  put  a fire-breathing dinosaur? In the garden! With the bouncy castle! Logical. But you know, having loads of money wouldn’t automatically make us happy, would it? Why not? Money buys you everything! Ben at school got a new Lego spaceship because his dad has money. That’s true, money  can  buy things. But it doesn't buy happiness, sweetheart. It buys…well, things. Like Lego spaceships, and maybe even a bouncy castle. But happiness comes from different places. From spending time together, like we are now. From reading a good book. From helping someone else. Like when we gave Mrs. Higgins flowers? She looked really smiley. Exactly! That made  you  feel good, didn't it? That’s happiness. It's a feeling. But…the dinosaur! The dinosaur is a lovely thought, honestly. But imagine having all the money in the world and feeling lonely. Or having all the toys but no one to play with. That wouldn’t be very fun, would it? No. That sounds…sad. It would be. You know, there's a little rhyme I learned when I was little. Do you want to hear it? Ooh, yes! A rhyme about dinosaurs? Not  about  dinosaurs, but it’s good. “Money can’t buy you laughter, it can’t buy you cheer, it can’t buy you a sunny day to chase away a tear.” “Money can’t buy you laughter…” That’s a good one! Can it buy you chocolate? Yes, it can buy you chocolate. But eating too much chocolate doesn’t make you  happy  for very long, does it? It might for a little bit, but then you feel a bit…yucky. True! I felt yucky after I ate all my biscuits last week. See? So, happiness isn’t about  having  lots of things, or lots of money. It’s about…feeling grateful for what we  do  have. Like a warm house, and each other.

… honestly, it just feels a bit pointless, doesn’t it? Like, Mrs. Davies keeps going on about ‘future-proofing’ our choices, but how can you  possibly  know what jobs will even  be  around in ten years? It's not like my grandad, knowing he’d stay a mechanic all his life. Tell me about it. My dad’s massively into investment now, keeps talking about ‘disruptive technologies’. Which basically means he watches videos about Elon Musk and thinks he’s got the next big idea. He was on about quantum computing the other day. I just nodded and pretended to understand. Quantum… what now? Sounds terrifyingly complicated. Though, I suppose that’s the point, isn't it? Something new all the time. It's just… overwhelming. I was thinking maybe something with engineering. You know, actually  making  stuff. But even then, it’s all AI assisted design now, isn’t it? Will there be any actual  designers  left? Probably. But they’ll be coding the AI, I guess. My cousin, Liam, he’s doing a foundation year in computer science. He's completely obsessed with patents. Apparently, someone invented a self-folding laundry basket and made a fortune. A  laundry basket , Sam! No way! Seriously? That’s… ridiculous. And brilliant. I mean, who thinks of that? Though, thinking about it, patenting stuff sounds like a headache. All the legal bits, making sure no one steals your idea. He says it’s surprisingly complex. Loads of loopholes, international law, all that. But the rewards can be huge. He's actually got an idea for a better bike lock – one that uses facial recognition. Slightly terrifying, maybe, but apparently, bike theft is a massive problem. That’s…actually quite good. Safer. Still, feels a bit Big Brother-ish. Speaking of big… have you been reading about China lately? It feels like they’re just… everywhere. Economically, technologically. Yeah, my geography teacher's been banging on about it. The Belt and Road initiative, all that. Apparently, they’re investing massively in infrastructure all over Africa and Asia. They're aiming to control everything. It’s kinda scary. Scary and… impressive. They're building things at a scale we haven’t seen since, well, probably the Romans. And they’re not messing about with ethical considerations like we are. They just  do  things. Exactly! Dad reckons that’s why they’re winning. No red tape. Easier to get things off the ground.

… honestly, I just think Darren’s getting a bit too confident. He was practically showing off on that red run this morning, carving these huge turns, and then nearly took out little Timmy Perkins! Honestly, the man. Oh, Darren. He  is  a bit of a show-off, isn't he? But bless him, he’s enjoying himself. Timmy’s fine, apparently just a bit winded. Did you see old Mr. Henderson practically doing the splits trying to avoid him? That was almost better than Darren’s actual skiing. Oh, I did! Poor man. He's nearly eighty, that fella. I felt terrible laughing, truly. But it was… unexpectedly funny. Anyway, I’m worried about Mum and Dad trying the blue run tomorrow. Dad hasn't skied in  years . They’ll be alright. Ben said he'd stick with them, and he’s a very sensible skier. You know, he’s really taken to it. I didn’t expect that. He always said he preferred snowboarding. He did, didn’t he? Funny how things change. It’s nice seeing him enjoy something with Mum and Dad. It’s… it’s nice seeing them all together, to be honest. We don’t get enough of that back home. Everyone’s so busy. Tell me about it. Work, kids, life… it just sweeps you along. That’s why I insisted on this trip. A full week, just us, away from everything. Although, ‘away from everything’ doesn’t mean ‘away from Auntie Brenda’s constant updates on the cat’s digestion, does it? Oh, don’t even  mention  Fluffy. I got three photos of his… output… this morning. Three! I’ve muted her WhatsApp group for the week. She’ll forgive me. Probably. Good. You deserve peace. Listen, about Friday… Are you still happy to swap rooms with me and Michael? He’s already complaining about the noise coming from the bar downstairs, and I think a bit of peace and quiet will do him good. No problem at all. It’s easier for me, honestly. I need to do a bit of work on Saturday morning – some proofreading for that American client. Lower floor means better wifi, apparently. That hotel’s wifi is patchy at best. Good thinking. Actually, speaking of work… How’s things going with that new marketing gig? The one for the estate agents? It’s… challenging. They want everything yesterday, and they have very specific ideas about  everything , none of which are very good, frankly.

…and honestly, Arthur, I just don’t see why you keep getting through strings so quickly. Are you  really  hitting them that hard anymore? It’s not like you’re competing at Wimbledon, is it? Now, now, Margaret, don't be like that. It's not about hitting hard, it's about the… the tension, I think. And the frame flexing. It’s a combination. Remember Old Man Hemmings at the club? He said the newer rackets are just… less forgiving. Hemmings said a lot of things. Mostly about the price of biscuits in the clubhouse. Anyway, we’re talking solutions. The cable ties are a temporary fix, and frankly, quite unsightly. I’m still leaning towards the reinforced grommet system. Perhaps with a small, rubber washer in there too, to absorb some of the shock. Grommets, yes. Good. But sourcing them… that’s the problem. Finding them in the right size, consistently. And the cost. We’re trying to keep this accessible, remember? The whole point is not to rip people off. A fiver for a repair, maximum. A fiver is ambitious. Especially if we’re talking about replacing several grommets  and  restringing. Maybe six, then? And we need to factor in the cost of the string itself. I was looking online, a decent roll of badminton string is… well, it’s not cheap these days. Right. And then there’s the question of positioning. Where exactly do we reinforce? Just the main string holes? Or are we thinking… a wider support structure? It almost feels like building a mini… fleet of supports. A  fleet , Arthur? Really? That’s a rather dramatic way to describe a few grommets. Though, I suppose you’re picturing a squadron of tiny reinforcements defending against breakage. It just… came to me! Anyway, and speaking of reinforcements… . Sorry, just need to… adjust the guard. Now, this is where it gets tricky. I'm attempting a little tidy up. It's been getting a bit long, you see. Arthur! Careful! That’s awfully close to my ear! Oh dear, you’ve… you’ve nipped it! Just a tiny bit, thankfully. Oh, blast! I am  so  sorry, Margaret! It’s the light, you see. And trying to concentrate on grommets and fleets at the same time is a bit much, even for me. It stings! And… oh, look. You’ve also taken a stripe off my hair.

…No, no, I’m tellin’ ya, it weren’t right, see? All that blue. Far too much blue. Reminded me o’ bein’ seasick, truth be told. Though I 'aven’t  been  seasick, mind you. Just the  feel  of it. Like lookin’ at a storm brewin’ over Breydon Water. Depressin', that's what it was. Oh, Arthur, you always say that about modern art! Anything that isn’t a nice landscape with sheep gets a bad rap from you. You liked that Turner exhibition, didn’t you? Plenty of blue in  that ! Turner were different, Elsie. He knew 'is colour. He painted the  light , he did. This…this was just a load o’ splodges. And the young lady, our Sarah, she's tellin' me it's expressin' the artist's inner turmoil. Inner turmoil? Sounds like ‘e needed a good cup o’ tea and a lie-down, if you ask me. Dad, it's often about communicating feelings that are difficult to put into words. It's not necessarily about representing something  real . It's about evoking a response in the viewer. The artist, Anya Petrova, apparently went through a really difficult period when she was creating that series. Evokin’ a response? It evoked a desire for a biscuit, that’s what it evoked! A nice digestive. Now that's somethin' worthwhile. It’s interesting, isn't it, how subjective art is? I actually quite liked the intensity of the blue, the way it dominated the canvas. It felt…claustrophobic, almost. Which, if Sarah’s right about the artist’s experiences, makes sense. I thought it was quite striking, actually. A bit much for the lounge, mind you, but striking. And Sarah’s a clever girl, she studies this sort of thing. She'd know. Anya’s work is rooted in Abstract Expressionism, so it’s intentionally non-representational. It aims to create an emotional resonance directly, bypassing the need for recognisable imagery. Think Rothko, but a bit more…visceral. Rothko? Sounds like a plumber. Visceral? What does  that  even mean? It means it affects you on a gut level, Dad. It's a strong, intuitive reaction. It's not about thinking about it, it’s about  feeling  it. Well, my gut told me it needed a frame with a good strong border, maybe somethin' oak. And a nice bit o’ floral paper behind it to cheer it up. Arthur! You'd ruin it!

… honestly, I just don’t  get  her. Like, posting that selfie with the filter that makes you look like a cartoon cat? Seriously? It’s Gemma, not Garfield. Oh, bless her. Teenage regression, I reckon. She’s probably dealing with something. Though, yeah, aesthetically… questionable. You still on about the hen do stuff? It’s not just the hen do! It’s  everything . She’s constantly fishing for compliments, and then gets offended if you don’t gush enough. I spent an hour helping her pick an outfit for Dave’s work party and then she just said ‘It’s okay, I guess.’  Okay ?! Harsh. People are weird, Liv. You’re a project coordinator, you deal with weird all day. Remember Mr. Henderson and his obsession with staplers? That’s different! Staplers are objectively fascinating. This is…performative suffering. Anyway, enough about the drama of Gemma. Work was a nightmare today. Old man Peterson decided  now  is the time to restructure the entire filing system. The  entire  thing. Oh, you poor thing. Sounds… thrilling. I had a patient today who tried to convince me she was a teapot. A full-on, spout-and-handle teapot. No way! Did you… did you offer her a biscuit? I was tempted! Protocol says de-escalation, not catering to delusions. It’s exhausting, honestly. You deal with the filing, I deal with the teapots. It’s a good balance. Although, sometimes I think Peterson’s filing system  is  a delusion. It honestly is. And the language people use in emails! “Per my last email…” Who talks like that? It’s so…aggressive-passive. It’s like they’re trying to subtly assert dominance through grammar. Stop. You’re going down a linguistic rabbit hole. Remember last week when you spent twenty minutes ranting about the misuse of ‘literally’? It's important! It  means  actually! Not figuratively! It's the downfall of civilisation, I tell you. Right, I need to do the dishes. I’ve been putting it off all week. Procrastination station central, is our kitchen. Honestly, it's a hazard. I tripped over that box of your craft supplies again this morning. Sorry! I really need to sort that out. I swear, I’ll do it tomorrow. After I’ve organised Peterson’s filing system in my head. And analysed the etymological roots of ‘literally.’ You’re hopeless. Look, I’m knackered. Long shift.

… honestly, the sheer volume of emails I sifted through today was ridiculous. Mr. Henderson decided  everyone  needs to be cc’d on  everything . It's like he thinks transparency equals drowning in admin. And then Sheila wanted me to book her a ‘wellness retreat’ in Bali. Bali! Like she’s stressed dealing with stationery orders. Sounds like a typical Tuesday for you, then. Still, Bali sounds nice. You deserve a bit of Bali after wrestling Henderson’s email habits. Though, knowing you, you'd spend the whole time networking and trying to sort  their  IT out. Don’t even. And it's not just the work, it's… all of it. The school run, remembering Amelia has recorder practice, making sure your mum's got her shopping… I feel like a logistical operation. Sometimes I just want to light a cigarette and stare into space. Now, now. We talked about the cigarettes. Remember what Dr. Davies said? Your lungs aren’t getting any younger, love. And honestly, you're much nicer to be around  without  the constant craving looks. Want another glass of wine instead? Helps with the ‘logistical operation’ feeling. Fine. Wine it is. But it's a temporary fix, isn’t it? It doesn’t actually  solve  anything. It's a vice, pure and simple. Like Henderson’s need to CC everyone. It’s… illogical. Illogical? That’s a strong word. Maybe it's not illogical, it's just… lacking common sense. There’s a difference, you know. My old boss, Bernard, was brilliant with code – a genuine genius. But ask him to parallel park? Utter chaos. Highly intelligent, zero common sense. That's true, I suppose. Intelligence isn't the same as being… well, sensible. It feels like a lot of people mistake the two. Especially with all this talk about ‘disruption’ and ‘innovation’ – sometimes you just need to use a bit of good old-fashioned common sense. Exactly! It’s the same when we were in Spain last year, wasn’t it? That woman lecturing us about ‘cultural sensitivity’ while simultaneously complaining about how ‘backward’ their lunchtimes were. Oh,  her . Honestly! “They shouldn’t rest for two hours in the middle of the day, it impacts productivity!” It's their culture! And a perfectly lovely one, I thought. It just feels like some people think their way is the  only  way, and any deviation is a failing. It's almost… anti-feminist in a weird way.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of mud! I swear, Leo, you looked like you’d been wrestling a pig. A very happy pig, admittedly. I  was  near the pigs! A little one licked my hand! It was slobbery. Mine didn’t lick me! I petted a sheep, though. A fluffy one. It smelled… farmy. ‘Farmy’ is a good description, actually. It wasn’t quite the idyllic countryside scene I’d envisioned, more…robust. Still, you two seemed to really enjoy it. Did you tell your teachers about the pigs and sheep at school today? I told Mrs. Davies! She said pigs are very intelligent animals. She asked if I’d learned anything about their food. I told Miss Evans. She said sheep need shearing, or they get too hot. But Thomas kept talking about tractors and wouldn’t let anyone else speak. Thomas, darling, were you perhaps… dominating the conversation again? We talked about using our listening ears, remember? He always does that! He talks and talks and talks. And he makes silly faces when Miss Evans is trying to read. Right. Okay. We'll have a little chat later about remembering to share the floor, shall we? It's important to let other people have a turn. It’s not just polite, it’s… it’s a skill, actually. Thinking about how others feel and letting them contribute. It’s something I teach  all  the time at school. Funny how hard it is to put into practice sometimes, isn’t it? Is it like teaching grown-ups? Sometimes, Leo, it absolutely is. Now, back to the farm. You both had a good lunch, didn’t you? Those sausage rolls were disappearing at a rate of knots. I had two! And a juice box. And a biscuit! That's a lot of fuel for farm-exploring. I was quite pleased you both ate something substantial. I’d packed loads, bracing myself for the ‘I'm not hungry’ chorus. I was hungry! Running around with the pigs makes you hungry. Can we go again next weekend? Next weekend’s already booked with Grandma and Grandpa. But we can definitely think about another farm trip soon. Actually, I was thinking we could have a movie night on Saturday. I’ve got that new Wallace and Gromit DVD. Oh! The one with the sheep? The very same! Although, knowing you two, you’ll probably spend the entire film re-enacting the sheep escaping.

… honestly, it’s just so satisfying, isn’t it? The click-clack of the needles. Proper mindful, like. I’m trying to do a Fair Isle pattern, though, and it’s…ambitious. Especially after just finishing that plain garter stitch scarf for me mam. Felt a bit basic after all the research I’ve been doing for work, if I’m honest. Ambitious is putting it mildly. I saw a picture of a Fair Isle jumper on Instagram the other day – looked like it required a PhD in colourwork. You’re a braver woman than I am. I still can’t get my head around cabling. It just…baffles me. Aye, well, I’ve been watching a lot of tutorials. And honestly, the YouTube knitting community is  intense . Like, seriously dedicated. Anyway, speaking of intense… did you see that article about Benedict Cumberbatch? He’s painting now, apparently. Proper landscapes. No way! That’s…unexpected. I always figured he’d be more of a pottery sort of chap, you know? All that concentration. Landscapes though… interesting. Is it any good? Apparently so! The article said he’s been taking lessons for ages, and apparently, it’s actually quite good. Not just “celebrity dabbling” good. Though, let’s be real, anything he does gets a bit of a lift because  it's him . It's that whole fame thing. It reminded me a bit of that Hockney exhibition we went to in London, actually. All the light and colour. Oh, that was brilliant. I still think about that bigger picture with all the trees. Completely immersive. I’ve been meaning to look into getting back into sketching, but my PhD leaves approximately zero time for hobbies that don’t involve staring at spreadsheets. Tell me about it. This research project is eating my life. Although, knitting  is  technically research, isn't it? Market research, at least. I'm supposed to be understanding consumer trends in craft hobbies! It’s a good excuse, if I'm being honest. A very good excuse. So, no Olympics obsession this year then? Usually, you’re glued to the telly. I'll watch bits, aye. But it feels a bit…weird, doesn’t it? Without the usual crowds. And to be honest, I've been more preoccupied trying to figure out what we're doing for Easter. Mam’s expecting us, obviously. Predictably. She already started hinting about chocolate eggs in a text message a week ago.

…and honestly, Arthur, the Natural History Museum is just  packed  on a Sunday. Packed! You could barely see the dinosaur skeleton for all the little ‘uns clambering about. Though, mind you, they were dead excited. Little faces lit up, you know? But for a peaceful look? Forget about it. Right, well, that’s what you get going to the popular ones, isn’t it, Doreen? Should’ve suggested the Science Museum. Less… prehistoric mayhem. Though, I maintain, they should stagger the entry times. It's just not designed for that many people. Staggered entry times. You’d think so, wouldn’t you? But no. Just a free-for-all. I was thinking, maybe next time, something a bit different? Have you ever been to the Postal Museum? I read a little about it, and it sounds… quirky. The Postal Museum? Is that near King’s Cross? I seem to recall something about the Mail Rail being down there. Never been, though. Sounds a bit… niche, even for me. I was hoping for something a bit grander, maybe even an IMAX. They've got that new one near Waterloo, haven’t they? Showing that space thing? Oh, space… I don’t know, Arthur. I get a bit travel sick with those 3D things. Remember that film we saw, the one with the penguins? Nearly lost my tea! And Waterloo… getting there is a nightmare. Honestly, the Northern Line on a Sunday afternoon is like being crammed into a sardine tin. You and your Northern Line complaints! It's not  that  bad. A bit crowded, admittedly. But it’s efficient. And that IMAX screen is enormous, Doreen. It’s not like your little cinema back in Liverpool. Oh, don’t start on my little cinema! The Plaza has charm, thank you very much. And it doesn’t involve fighting for a seat and breathing in someone else's perfume. I’m telling you, public transport in London is enough to put anyone off a day out. We stood waiting for a bus for ages after the museum, Arthur! Ages! Well, we  could  get a taxi. But you know what those cost these days. Highway robbery, I tell you. Remember when a pound could get you a decent cup of tea and a biscuit? Oh, you and your reminiscing! Times were simpler, weren’t they? Though even then, getting around Liverpool wasn’t always a breeze.

… honestly, the sheer volume of baubles my mother sends over is becoming a hazard. Last year, little Mei nearly took an eye out reaching for a particularly sparkly snowman. It’s lovely, don’t get me wrong, but it’s…excessive. Excessive is a polite word for it, Alistair. Your mum’s always been a bit of a maximalist, hasn’t she? Mine just sends a card. A very lengthy card, detailing everyone’s ailments and marital status, but a card nonetheless. Much easier to manage. So, Christmas dinner, then. We’re sticking with yours this year, right? You’ve got the bigger oven. Yes, definitely mine. And honestly, after last year’s…incident… at David’s, I’m happy to take on the logistical challenge. Remember the turkey? Oh,  that  turkey. Burnt on the outside, practically raw in the middle. And the smoke alarm going off every five minutes. He claimed it added ‘atmosphere’. Atmosphere of panic, more like. Honestly, David's cooking has always been… adventurous. Adventurous is one word for it. Disastrous is another. Right, so we’re aiming for the 24th, 7pm? Gives people a chance to get here after work. I was thinking roast goose this year, bit different from the usual. Goose sounds brilliant! Much more flavour. Though you'll need to be careful, they render a  lot  of fat. You’ll be swimming in it. We need to get a list sorted. I can handle the stuffing. My grandma’s recipe, it’s legendary. Perfect! You and your grandma’s legendary stuffing are a welcome addition. I'll do the goose, obviously, and the potatoes. What about starters? I was thinking maybe soup? Something simple. Soup’s good. Or we could do some smoked salmon blinis? Bit more festive. Speaking of festive, have you seen any decent Christmas films over here? The selection on the streaming services is… limited, to say the least. Limited is an understatement! I tried to find  Love Actually  the other day and it wasn’t anywhere. I ended up rewatching  Die Hard . Technically a Christmas film, right? That’s debatable, Alistair! Very debatable. But I'll allow it. I've been trying to get the students into  It’s a Wonderful Life , but they just don't get it. Too sentimental for this generation, I think. They all want explosions and superheroes. It’s a shame, isn’t it? Some of those older films are genuinely brilliant.

… honestly, the replies to that tweet were  wild . Someone genuinely thought I was arguing for pigeons to have voting rights. Voting rights! Like, I was making a joke about the council ignoring actual issues, and suddenly I’m a pigeon rights activist. The internet, innit? Oh, bless ‘em. People will latch onto anything. You know, I get similar with the bakery. Someone left a one-star review because we ‘didn’t have enough vegan options on a Sunday’. A  Sunday ! Like, we’re a small shop, we bake fresh daily, it’s not a supermarket. It’s just… exhausting. Tell me about it. I had a woman yesterday chewing me out because her latte wasn’t ‘Instagrammable’ enough. Instagrammable! I was like, “It’s coffee, love, it’s for  drinking !” I swear, some people live their lives through their phones. Right? It’s mental. And then they use that power to just…be horrible. It’s too easy to hide behind a screen. I saw this restaurant in Margate got absolutely  smashed  on TripAdvisor. Apparently, the wallpaper was “dated.” Dated! It’s a seaside town, half the shops are deliberately retro. Margate's lovely, though, isn’t it? I went down there last summer. That Turner Contemporary is wicked, and the old town’s got a really good vibe. Though, yeah, the food scene’s a bit hit and miss. I reckon there's space for a proper, small-batch bakery down there, actually. You thinking about it, then? Another venture, Chloe? You’re already running Flour Power, you’ll be exhausted. Just… brainstorming. I'm a bit disillusioned with the current shop, to be honest. The landlord's decided he wants to 're-imagine the space' which translates to 'triple the rent'. And honestly, the layout is awful. It's all cramped and the counter's in the wrong place. I’ve been sketching out ideas for something completely different – more of a café-bakery hybrid, with a focus on design. Everything needs to  flow . That sounds ambitious. Margate seems to be gentrifying rapidly though. Could be a good move timing-wise. Have you looked at property prices? They’re probably going through the roof. Oh, I have. Eye-watering. But there are a couple of places on the high street that are surprisingly affordable. It’d need a lot of work, though. I’m picturing exposed brick, lots of plants, a really warm, inviting atmosphere.

…and honestly, the slugs have been  awful  this year. Devouring everything. I thought I’d protected the lettuce well enough, but no. They’re quite relentless, aren’t they?      Are slugs slimy? Like… really,  really  slimy?      Yeah, super slimy. They leave trails everywhere. Gross. It’s why I don’t go near the garden after it rains.      Don’t be dramatic, Leo. A little slug slime never hurt anyone. Though, I did step in some once and nearly lost a shoe. It was quite the ordeal. Speaking of ordeals… anyone thinking about those exams next week?      Oh dear, yes. Leo, how are you feeling about the History one? It’s a big one.      It’s alright. I think I’ve got the dates sorted. It’s the ‘causes’ bit I’m struggling with, you know? All the interconnectedness. It’s a nightmare.      It always is. Remember to break it down. Think about economic factors, social factors… make little mind maps. That’s what I tell my students.      Can I have more raspberries? Please? They’re yummy.      Of course, darling. But eat some broccoli first. Need to build up your strength for all that thinking!      Broccoli is green and… pokey. Raspberries are red and sweet!      One little floret, then a raspberry. A bargain, I think. Now, I was telling Sarah about the garden. I’m thinking of getting some more bird feeders. I found a broken eggshell this morning, which means something’s nesting nearby.      Cool! What kind of bird?      I couldn’t tell, sadly. Just a small, speckled shell. It could be a robin, maybe a blackbird.      Remember when we tried to keep gerbils, darling? That was a disaster. They escaped  constantly . Little Houdinis, the pair of them.      Oh, don't remind me! They chewed through everything. The sofa, the carpets… even the phone charger! And the smell…      Gerbils are alright. A bit boring though. I’d rather have a dog.      I want a puppy! A fluffy one!      We’ve talked about this, sweetie. A puppy is a  lot  of work. Now, Leo, are you finished? It’s nearly bedtime.      Almost. Just finishing my peas. Are we going biking tomorrow?      Weather permitting. It’s looking a bit grey at the moment. We might have to find something else to do. Perhaps a walk down by the river?      Or… we could get ice cream! Chocolate ice cream, specifically. It’s been a long week.

… honestly, I just don’t  have  the energy for a full supermarket shop this weekend. It’s not just the shopping itself, it’s the sheer mental load of remembering everything. Did I get low-fat yogurt? Do we need more dishwasher tablets? It’s exhausting. Tell me about it, love. I do a shop for Mum every week, and it’s the same. Though she usually just needs biscuits and a paper. It's getting her  to  the shop that's the problem now. Her legs aren't what they were. Oh, don't I know it. Though I can still manage a little potter around the corner shop for a paper and a chocolate biscuit. Not the fancy ones, mind you. Just a digestive. Can’t beat a digestive. Mum, you deserve fancy biscuits! Anyway, I was thinking… could you maybe pop to Sainsbury’s on Tuesday, Jan? Just for the essentials, I’ll make a list. I could pick up your Mum’s biscuits then too? That would be brilliant, Sarah, honestly. Saves me a whole trip. Thank you. She'd appreciate that a lot. Bit of a treat for her. No problem at all. It’s the least I can do. Speaking of treats… I’m seriously considering booking us all a table at The Olive Branch next week. I fancy a proper night out, and their sea bass is divine. Oh, The Olive Branch! Lovely place. Though a bit…fussy for me these days. All that olive oil. Still, it would be nice to get out. Have they still got that young man with the lovely haircut? The one who always remembered my name. They do, Mum! He's still there. And you  always  get compliments on your hair, you know. Though you’re looking a bit grown out now, aren't you? Maybe a trim is due? Definitely a trim. And while we’re on the subject of looking good… my eyebrows are driving me mad. They’ve gone completely rogue. I need to find someone who doesn’t just wax them into oblivion. It's a skill, eyebrow shaping, honestly. Old Mrs. Higgins down the road used to do mine, ages ago. She was a proper artist with tweezers. Though she smoked like a chimney while she was doing them! It smelled awful. Oh, Mabel Higgins. Always had a fag dangling from her lip.

…and honestly, the pureed sweet potato just isn’t cutting it anymore, is it? She just  hates  it. Spits it straight back out. It’s like, “Mum, I’m evolving, I need texture!” Honestly, you'd think she'd be grateful for anything after months of milk, wouldn’t you? Oh, she’s a little madam already, isn’t she? Just like her Auntie Carol. Remember Carol refusing everything green as a child? It was a battle every dinner time. Don't remind me. That woman and her aversion to vegetables… It’s a family trait seemingly! No, seriously though, I’m thinking maybe we move straight to finger foods? Little steamed broccoli florets, soft cooked carrot sticks? What do you think, being the professional? It’s not a bad idea, actually. At eight months, she’s definitely showing all the signs. Good head control, sitting up well... just make sure everything’s  really  soft. And watch her like a hawk, obviously. You don’t want a choking scare. The guidance now is much more about letting them explore texture than sticking rigidly to purees. Good, good. That’s what I thought. I felt a bit guilty skipping the next stage, but the sweet potato saga is just… exhausting. Anyway, enough about baby food drama. What’s happening this week? Are you still on for dinner with Liam and Chloe on Wednesday? Yes! Definitely. I think Chloe’s been feeling a bit down lately, needs a good gossip. Liam’s been working ridiculous hours, so it’ll be good for him to switch off too. I told her we could do a quick pasta bake, nothing fancy. Sounds lovely. I wish I could join, but I promised Mum I’d pop round on Wednesday evening. She’s been a bit lonely since Dad started going to his bridge club three times a week. Says the house feels ‘empty and echoing’, whatever that means. Ah, bless her. She's not one for quiet, is she? I’m glad you’re going. It’s important she feels connected. Are you going to brave the tea and biscuits with her? Probably. And a lecture about how I haven’t visited enough, and how this baby needs ‘proper feeding’ - despite the fact I’m following all the health advice! It’s a routine now. Still, it's Mum. You do it. You’re a good daughter.

… honestly, it’s just so  flat  here, isn’t it? I mean, beautiful, obviously, but after the Chilterns… it feels like all the personality’s been ironed out. You don’t get that sense of scale. Ironed out. That’s a good way to put it. You city folk and your hills. It’s a different kind of beauty, darling. Subtler. It’s about the vastness, the sky pressing down. London always felt… contained, even when you were in a park. Contained is definitely a word for it. But I miss  seeing  things. A proper incline, a little bit of drama in the landscape. Here, you look for a hill and you get a gentle rise. It’s practically a suggestion of a hill. You’re being dramatic. Look over there, towards Brancaster. That little bump? That’s technically a hill. And it’s a landmark for miles. People navigate by it. A 'landmark' that a determined cyclist could probably conquer without changing gear. Honestly. It's not like the South Downs, is it? You could lose yourself for days wandering those. No, it’s not. And that’s the point. Norfolk isn’t about getting “lost” in the landscape. It’s about… being  within  it. Being part of this huge, open space. It's about the textures, the light on the fields. And the villages. Have you noticed how each village feels completely self-contained? I have, yes. They're very… individual. Quite charming, actually. But that’s almost because they  have  to be. There’s nothing to connect them structurally, is there? No overarching geographical feature. In the Cotswolds, everything revolves around the hills, the valleys. Here, it's just… a collection of pretty places dotted about. You see, I think that’s its strength. They evolved organically. Look at Burnham Market – it was a port originally, you know? Completely reliant on the creek. Then the creek silted up, and it shifted. It  had  to adapt. It wasn't pre-ordained by a dominating landform. It’s that adaptation, that resilience, that makes them special. That's a really interesting way to look at it. I hadn’t considered that. It's just… Norwich is so flat, and then everything around it feels equally so. It creates this… homogenous feeling. Norwich is on the River Wensum, remember? There  are  subtle gradients, little pockets. You just need to look. And honestly, I think after years of living in London, where everything feels relentlessly  built , this feels wonderfully uncluttered.

… honestly, I just think it was  trying  too hard, y’know? Like, all the twists and turns, it felt…contrived. Not natural, like. ‘The Lighthouse’ was proper unsettling, though. Now  that  was a film. Right, ‘The Lighthouse’ was brilliant. Willem Dafoe, genuinely terrifying. But I did enjoy ‘Knives Out’. It was just a fun, clever whodunnit. Sometimes you don't need deep existential meaning, do you? Just a bit of escapism. Aye, I get that. It’s just… everything’s a franchise now, isn’t it? Or a reboot. There’s nae originality left. And that one was supposed to be, like, a groundbreaking psychological thriller. It just felt like they’d read a list of tropes and just… slapped ‘em all in. True. It’s a bit depressing. Speaking of depressing, how's Liam taking the new job? He sounded a bit…flat on the phone yesterday. Oh, aye, Liam. He’s… not thrilled, to put it mildly. Apparently, it’s just endless spreadsheets and meetings about meetings. He thought it would be more hands-on, more… building things. He’s stuck in some massive corporate office in Reading now. Far cry from being on site, innit? Reading! That  is  bleak. He was so passionate about the engineering side of things when we were at uni. Seems a shame he’s ended up just… shuffling papers. Is he looking at other options? He says he is, but he feels a bit stuck. He’s got a mortgage now, y’know? And he’s only been there six months. Doesn’t wanna look like he can’t commit or owt. He’s proper stressed about it, poor lad. I tried to tell him to be careful taking it, all that talk of "career progression" and "fantastic opportunities"… sounded like a load of cobblers. Classic. They always do. Promise the world and deliver… grey. It’s the same in my field, honestly. Loads of talk about innovation, but mostly it's just risk aversion. Anyway, enough about work doom and gloom. Almost there, aren’t we? Aye, just around the corner. God, have you seen the state of the roads around here? It’s a disgrace. And with all these cyclists now… Oh, here we go… No, seriously! I’m not hating on cyclists, I’m just saying they need to learn some road awareness. Nearly got doored on the way to work yesterday, one just swerved right out, no signal, nothing!

…and honestly, the sheer scale of it is what gets me. I mean, fields and fields of daffodils. It’s almost… unsettling, isn’t it? Feels less ‘natural beauty’ and more ‘agribusiness’. You’re projecting your economics lectures onto the daffodils again, aren't you, El? It  is  a bit much, I’ll grant you. It’s not like stumbling across a little patch in a wood. This is…intentional. Intentional  and  profitable. I was reading an article last night, actually, about the bulb industry here in Norfolk. Vast amounts of money tied up in these things. They're practically a cash crop now, more so than wheat in some areas. It makes you think, doesn't it? All this ‘English countryside’ is often very carefully cultivated for maximum return. Precisely. It's the illusion of pastoral idyll. Makes good marketing for tourism, too. Though, I will say, they  are  beautiful. Look at that buttery yellow. Reminds me of… hmm…Chelsea Flower Show, actually. We went a few years back, didn't we? Before Leo was born? Oh god, yes. The absolute chaos of it all! And the prices… outrageous. I remember eyeing up a tiny lavender bush that cost more than a week’s groceries. Honestly, I'd rather pick wildflowers. Which, admittedly, are a bit thin on the ground  because  of all the daffodil farming. You and your principles. It's a fair point. Speaking of picking things up, I'm trying to brush up on my Italian again. Found a rather good online course. Oh, really? Still aiming for fluency? That's ambitious. What prompted it this time? Last time it was the promise of authentic gelato... Well, the gelato is  always  a factor. But actually, Professor Rossi, the one I collaborate with on the linguistic mapping project, is organising a conference in Bologna next year. It'd be brilliant to be able to actually converse with him properly, rather than relying on overly formal English. And it’s fascinating, the subtle variations in dialects in Emilia-Romagna… That sounds amazing. It’s so different from the Anglo-Saxon roots of English. All those lovely Romance language sounds. Though, I’m still battling with subjunctive moods. They just feel… unnecessary. That's your Norwich pragmatism showing. You want everything to be direct and functional. Italian isn’t about function, it’s about  feeling . Much like supporting Norwich City, I suppose.

…Aye, well, that’s what I mean about parking ‘round there, isn’t it? Absolute nightmare. Like trying to land a spaceship on a postage stamp. Honestly, after six o’clock, forget it. You’re circling the block ‘til kingdom come. You’re not wrong. Luckily, the office has that underground car park, so I’m usually alright. But visiting’s a different story. Though, worse parking I’ve seen… was that time we went to see the Angel of the North. Honestly, the sheer volume of cars! Oh, don’t even get me started on the Angel! It’s brilliant, mind, proper iconic. But the car park was jam-packed, and everyone was just…winging it, pulling onto the grass, blocking each other. Typical Bank Holiday. You’d think they’d anticipate it, wouldn’t ya? You’d hope so. Still, worth it for the photo, I suppose. Anyway, back to the flat viewing. Saturday at two? Does that work with your…corpus stuff? Aye, Saturday’s grand. I’ve got a deadline on Tuesday, so I’m trying to get as much done now as possible. Corpus work’s alright, keeps me busy. Just loads and loads of tagging and cleaning data, you know? Proper geeky stuff. Though, it pays the bills, which is the main thing. Are you bringing your measuring tape this time? Last place we saw, the kitchen was  tiny . Absolutely. Learned my lesson there. I thought it looked okay in the photos, but the estate agent was very…optimistic with their wide-angle lens. I’m also going to check the water pressure. Remember that flat near Clapham Junction? Took five minutes to fill the kettle! Ugh, horrendous. I remember. Honestly, it’s the little things, innit? Speaking of little things, did you see the tennis at Wimbledon? Djokovic looked untouchable. He was… relentless. Though Alcaraz is definitely one to watch. He's got that…fire. Reminds me a bit of when Newcastle were playing really well a few seasons back. That energy. Ooh, don't mention football. I’m still recovering from the season. It was a rollercoaster, wasn’t it? Proper gut-wrenching at times. Hoping Eddie Howe can build on it, though. We’ve got a good team, just need to be a bit more consistent. Actually, talking of cars… you thinking of upgrading anytime soon? Yours is getting on a bit, isn't it?

… honestly, the whole thing just feels so… manufactured. This whole Depp versus Heard saga. It’s been  weeks  on the television. Weeks! And for what? A very public, very messy break-up. It’s not like anything genuinely new came out, is it? Just a lot of performative distress. Well, it  is  a bit of a spectacle, innit? Me and Margaret – that's my sister – we were saying just yesterday. You can’t help but watch, even though it’s awful. All that money… and for that. Makes you wonder, don’t it? Spectacle is right. Back in  my  day, if someone had a disagreement, they sorted it between themselves, or maybe with a bit of gossip down the pub. Didn't need the whole world weighin’ in. Though, mind you, Old Man Hemmings and his wife… now  that  was a spectacle. Had a right shouting match one Christmas, right outside the church! Oh dear. Well, I suppose drama is always appealing. It’s just this feels… different. More calculated. Anyway, changing the subject entirely, have you seen the geese are back in force down by the river? Oh, yes! Honestly, they're a menace. I had to cycle round them last week, nearly came a cropper. They just stand there, lookin’ at you like  you’re  the one in the wrong. They’re building nests already, too. Plenty of goslings coming, I reckon. They are. It’s amazing, isn’t it? The whole migration thing. The instinct to fly thousands of miles, back to the same spot year after year. It’s… breathtaking. I read an article about it recently, about how they navigate using the Earth’s magnetic field. Extraordinary. Magnetic field, you say? Always thought they just followed the sun and remembered the way. My father used to tell me stories about the geese flying over Peterborough in V-formation, said it was a sign of a good harvest. All a bit silly, probably, but he believed it. He weren't wrong with the harvest part, though! We always had good crops when the geese were around. Old wives' tale, maybe, but they’re clever birds, geese. We have a little family of Canada geese down near the park where I walk the dogs. They recognise me now, they do! They’ll come right up, expecting a bit of bread. That's lovely. I’ve been trying to attract more birds to the garden.

… honestly, the courgette ribbons were a disaster. They just went completely soggy. I saw this chef do it on Saturday Kitchen and thought, ‘Oh, that looks easy!’ It absolutely wasn’t. Oh, you and your Saturday Kitchen ambitions! I feel your pain. I tried to make macarons once. It ended with a kitchen looking like a bomb had hit it and a bin full of almond flour. Macarons! Good grief, you’re braver than me. At least courgettes are relatively cheap to replace. Anyway, enough about my culinary failings. How  was  the interview? You were so nervous last week. Ugh. Don’t even. It was… fine. Which is the worst, isn’t it? Not disastrous, just… bland. The headteacher was very keen on ‘synergy’ and ‘whole school approaches’ – buzzwords galore. I felt like I was in a corporate training seminar, not talking about Year 3 literacy. Oh, the dreaded synergy! They love that in education, don't they? It means absolutely nothing practical. Did they ask you anything about actual teaching? A little, but mostly about how I’d ‘contribute to the school’s drive for excellence’. And they kept circling back to my experience with data analysis. I’m a primary school teacher, not an accountant! Honestly, I think they were hoping I'd be a spreadsheet wizard. Sounds exhausting. Did you get a feel for whether they’d be supportive of, well, you know… everything? That's the tricky bit. I subtly brought up the nursery provision and the need for flexible working, and she kind of… brushed it off. Said they were ‘committed to work-life balance’ but didn’t actually  say  anything about being accommodating. It’s the same old song and dance, isn't it? It is. It’s infuriating. You’d think they’d understand that good teachers need to be able to, you know,  have  lives. Especially considering… everything. Speaking of which, how are you feeling? Honestly? Tired. Really tired. And a bit stressed about the job, obviously. It's just… a really long process. Plus, little Leo has decided sleep is optional. He was up every two hours last night. Oh, bless him. That’s rough. Remember when I was a trainee and thought I could function on four hours of sleep? Those were the days! It’s utterly different when  you’re  the one exhausted and responsible for a tiny human. Tell me about it!

… honestly, it just feels a bit…stuck, doesn’t it? Like, I  should  be feeling excited about having a proper job, a flat, all that ‘adult’ stuff, but it just feels…overwhelming. Especially seeing everyone else on LinkedIn, you know? “Thrilled to announce I’ve joined X company as a Y!” Ugh. Makes me wanna delete the app. Oh, LinkedIn. The highlight reel of everyone's lives. Don't let it get to you, Liv. It's all curated. I’m pretty sure half of them are quietly panicking internally, just like us. Maybe. But it’s hard not to compare, isn’t it? Especially after all that effort at uni. I did a Masters, for goodness sake! I was supposed to be…launching a career, changing the world, or something. Instead, I’m mostly just making sure the widget factory doesn’t run out of bolts. Production Controller is a serious job, though. It’s important. And you're  good  at it. Remember when old Mr. Henderson was completely losing it with the delivery schedule last month? You sorted it all out. Yeah, but it doesn’t  feel  like it’s leading anywhere. I mean, what’s next? Senior Production Controller? Then what? Head of Bolts? It's not exactly inspiring, is it? What about you? How are things going with the council? Still battling with planning permission for garden fences? You have  no  idea. Mrs. Higgins is convinced her new shed is ‘architecturally insensitive’ to the street. Architecturally insensitive! It's a shed, Liv! A beige, utilitarian shed. But honestly, admin is…steady. It pays the bills. It's just...I thought I’d be using my degree more. I did all that research on sustainable urban development and now I'm mostly filing reports on bin collections. See? Exactly! We’re both slightly…underwhelmed. Do you ever just think about…packing it all in and becoming a florist? Or a shepherdess? Something completely different? A shepherdess in Cambridgeshire? Where would the sheep even  go ? Though, honestly, the thought has crossed my mind. My nan always said I had green fingers. Maybe a little flower stall at the market? Low risk, potentially lovely. That actually sounds…amazing. Better than spreadsheets, anyway. But realistically? I don’t even know where to  start  with something like that. I know. It's easy to get stuck in the 'sensible' lane. Remember Sarah from school?

… honestly, I just don’t get why he even bothered messaging me back. After ignoring me for a  week ? The cheek of it. Like I was just sat there, twiddling my thumbs, waiting for Prince Charming to deign to acknowledge my existence. Oh, Liam? He’s always been a bit like that, hasn't he? Hot and cold. Drives you mad, proper. You're better off without him, anyway. Honestly, you deserve someone who doesn’t treat you like a backup plan. You two. Still dissecting Liam, are you? It’s been… what, six months since you two finished? It’s like a Yorkshire soap opera, honestly. Six months and still annoying me, alright? It's not  dissecting , it's just… baffling! He messaged asking if I was going to Sarah’s party next week. Sarah, who  he  knows I’ve been looking forward to seeing for ages! It’s a test, I swear. A pathetic attempt to see if I still care. Probably just wants to show off to his mates that he can still get a reaction outta you. Classic Liam. Remember that time he pretended to be interested in photography just ‘cos he knew I liked it? He didn’t even know what aperture was! Oh, God, yes! The one picture he took looked like a blurry mess of grass. He tried to tell me it was "artistic". See, this is why I stick to books. Men are… complicated. Especially Yorkshire men, it seems. Mine’s fairly straightforward. Prefers football and silence. Can’t complain, really. Easy for you to say, you’ve got Daniel. He’s about as predictable as a sunrise. It's lovely, though, isn't it? Just…nice. I’m just a bit fed up, that’s all. And then Chloe's been going on  all  week about how amazing Ben is. Ben? Oh, right. The one with the motorbike? He's alright… a bit full of himself, though, isn’t he? That’s putting it mildly. He spent twenty minutes telling me about his 'investment portfolio' last Friday. Investment portfolio! He’s 22! It’s like he’s trying to be some city boy when he’s still lived in Doncaster his whole life. There’s a certain… bravado that comes with a motorbike, I think. Suddenly you’re James Dean. It's a bit embarrassing, honestly. Although, I did have a very brief flirtation with a man on a scooter once… Oh, here we go.

…and honestly, the carbonara was  almost  as good as Nonna Emilia’s. Almost. Though, nothing truly beats her secret ingredient, does it? I still reckon it's a whisper of nutmeg. Mmmph, it was good. Better than school dinners, anyway. Did you see Ben scoring that goal in the hockey match, Dad? It was  amazing ! He just…whipped it past the goalie. Whipped it past the goalie, eh? Sounds dramatic. I missed the match, unfortunately. Had that conference call with the team in Germany run late. They’re still struggling with the new logistics software. Honestly, it's like talking to a brick wall sometimes. Ben deserves all the praise. He’s been practicing loads. Old Mr. Henderson said he's got real potential, a natural talent. Shame about losing overall though, wasn't it? It is a shame, but a good loss isn’t always a bad thing, is it? Builds character. Anyway, about the weekend… I was thinking, if the weather holds, we could finally go to Drayton Manor. You two have been asking for ages. YES! Drayton Manor! Can we go on Shockwave first? And then Maelstrom? I’ve grown loads since last time, I’m definitely tall enough for everything now. Shockwave's alright. I prefer G-Force, it’s way faster. We should try and get on Apocalypse too, that one looks insane. Drayton Manor sounds good. It'll be nice to get out. I was looking at flights actually, thinking about maybe a quick trip to Barcelona in the autumn. There’s a marketing conference there, but I could easily tack on a couple of days for us all. Barcelona? Oh, that sounds lovely! We haven't had a proper family holiday in… well, a while. Although, remembering last time we went to Spain… didn’t young Master Two nearly lose his passport in that tapas bar? It wasn’t  nearly  lost! I just… put it somewhere safe. And then forgot where ‘safe’ was. You were distracted by the churros! You ate like five of them! That was a memorable trip. Perhaps this time we stick to a list – passports, wallets, phones. Standard issue. I’ll have a look at some flights tonight. Anything you'd specifically want to do in Barcelona? Oh, the Sagrada Familia is a must. And a walk down Las Ramblas, even if it is a bit touristy. I’d like to find some decent paella, too.

… honestly, it’s just  exhausting  being the designated family diplomat. Aunt Carol genuinely thinks Uncle Barry’s passive-aggressive comments about my ‘career choices’ are just ‘him being supportive’. Supportive! Like needing a translator for family gatherings is a life goal. Oh, Carol. She’s…a character. Though, to be fair, Barry  is  massively passive-aggressive. Remember that Christmas where he ‘accidentally’ bought Mum the cat-themed jumper knowing she's allergic? Don't  remind  me. Mum was sneezing for a week. It’s always something. And then they get offended when I point it out! “Oh, you’re so sensitive, darling.” Sensitive? I’m a translator! I spend my life deciphering nuanced meanings, it's practically a professional hazard applying that skill to family dynamics. Maybe they just don’t  get  what you do. They probably think “translator” means you sit around waiting for someone to ask you to say “hello” in French. Exactly! I tried explaining the legal translation I did last year - a massive contract for a renewable energy company – and Carol’s eyes glazed over halfway through the sentence. She asked if it involved translating recipe books. Recipe books, Lucy! Oh, bless her. She’s living in a different world. Though, you know, it's good you can laugh about it. It must be draining constantly feeling like you have to manage everyone’s feelings. Especially when they're being… well, Barry. It is. And the guilt! Because I know they mean well, in their own warped way. It’s just… it’s  always  me. Mom always says I’m the ‘sensible one’. Which translates to ‘the one who has to clean up everyone else’s messes’. What about you? Any family dramas brewing back home? Not so much drama, thankfully. Mostly just… stagnation. My brother, Tom, is still ‘finding himself’.
