Currently, that involves living in Dad’s shed and ‘experimenting’ with homemade kombucha. Oh dear. That sounds… aromatic. Is Dad coping? Dad’s putting on a brave face. He keeps saying Tom’s a ‘free spirit’. I think he secretly just wants him to get a job. Mum’s giving him passive-aggressive lectures about responsibility, which, ironically, is just making things worse. It's basically a carbon copy of the Barry and Carol show, but with more fermented tea. See! It’s a universal phenomenon. Family. At least  this  is peaceful. It’s amazing how quiet it is amongst these trees.

…and honestly, the chicken Kievs weren’t the same. Not a patch on what you’d get back home, you know? All sauce and no… substance. It just  exploded . Nearly took out young Leo there. It was kinda funny, Dad. A big, garlic-y explosion. Don’t talk with your mouth full, darling. And yes, it  was  a bit messy. Honestly, Leo, you've inherited your father's enthusiasm for… chaotic eating. Chaotic is a strong word, Mary! I’d call it appreciative. Anyway, that rugby match yesterday… absolute nailbiter, wasn’t it? I was nearly chewing the furniture in the last ten minutes. It was brilliant! That try by Farrell? Unbelievable. Though Liam at school was saying England would have won if… Ah, now, don’t be starting that. We won’t be having that talk, not at the dinner table. We’re guests in Ireland, show a bit of respect. Now, now, Sean. Let him have his opinion. It’s just a game. Although, honestly, the shouting nearly gave me a headache. I’ve been battling one all day. I think little Sophie kept climbing on my head while I was trying to nap. Terrible toddler, that one. A little wallie, completely fearless. But brilliant. Still, that rugby… you remember old Paddy O’Connell? He’d have been in raptures. We should try and get down to Granny’s next week. She's been asking about Leo. Can we take the hedgehog stuff with us? I want to show Granny the pictures I took in the garden. The hedgehogs? Ah yes, your little wildlife photographer phase. You and that phone. Did you get them uploaded to Flickr yet? I keep telling you, Dropbox is a safer bet for backups, you know. Flickr’s got better filters, Dad. And I uploaded some to Instagram too. Mrs. Peterson said she saw them and thought they were really good. That’s lovely, darling. Speaking of uploading things, I’ve been meaning to get some photos of Sophie sent to your mother, Sean. She's been on at me. It's just… finding the time when the little one’s not trying to dismantle the router. Tell me about it. Actually, I need to look at the router. The internet's been a bit flaky all day. It's driving me mad. Did you eat all the biscuits, Leo? Don't deny it. I saw the crumbs.

… honestly, the postage on that Shelley one was ridiculous. Twenty-two quid for postage! It’s china, not a grand piano. I nearly backed out, I did. But look at the floral detail, David. It’s just  exquisite . Twenty-two quid? They’re robbing you, love. Absolutely robbing you. eBay sellers, the lot of them. They always inflate the postage. Still, if it’s a Shelley, and it's in good nick… it’s probably worth it in the end. Where are you going to display it? The dresser’s getting a bit crowded, isn’t it? It is, isn’t it? I was thinking maybe swap out the Royal Albert ‘Old Country Roses’ set for a few weeks. They’re lovely, but… a bit  everyone  has them, you know? Shelley feels a bit more special, a bit more… me. Besides, I promised Mrs. Higgins I’d bring some nicer things round when she comes for tea next week. She deserves a proper cuppa. Good woman, Mrs. Higgins. Always has a kind word. Speaking of which, did you manage to get hold of that buckwheat bread from the market? I fancy a slice with some cheese tonight. I’ve been craving it all day. Oh, yes! Managed the last loaf, actually. Old Man Hemmings said it nearly didn't rise properly this morning, something about the humidity. Lucky me. It's in the bread bin. Want me to get it out while I finish chopping the veg? That would be brilliant, thanks. So, have you finalised anything about your leaving do at work? They’re being a bit slow, aren’t they? I thought they’d jump at the chance to throw a party for their star transcriber. Don’t even start me on work. It’s all a bit…muted. Apparently, budgets are tight. They’re suggesting a buffet in the staff room. A  buffet ! After fifteen years! I was hoping for at least a pub meal. I’ve hinted heavily about The Red Lion, but Sharon from accounts keeps saying it’s ‘unrealistic’. Unrealistic? She spends half her day online shopping! Tell her the Red Lion is perfectly realistic, and you’ve earned a decent send-off. Honestly, some people. Have you spoken to Mark about it? He’s usually pretty good at rallying the troops. I mentioned it to him briefly. He said he’d ‘have a word’.

…Aye, but tha knows how it is, doesn’t tha? Uni’s bleedin’ expensive. Even wi’ a student loan, it feels like I’m perpetually skint. I’m workin’ shifts at the pub, but it barely covers rent an’ books. Tell me about it. Though, bein’ self-employed, it’s a different kind o’ skint. Feast or famine, y’know? Right now, it's leanin' towards famine. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if all the paperwork and stress is worth it. How’s that dissertation comin’ on, anyway? Still focused on Victorian literature? More or less. It's the footnotes that are killin’ me. It's just… endless. But listen, Dad mentioned somethin’ the other day, a right odd thing. He was talkin’ to Mr. Harrison, an’ Mr. Harrison, well, he’s got a lot o’…  connections , apparently. Harrison? That one? Always lookin’ a bit shifty, him. What’s he been up to now? Apparently, he’s involved in somethin’ to do with movin’ money about. Proper dodgy, apparently. He was talkin' about “layering” and “structuring” and stuff. Sounded like somethin' outta a film. Dad was worried he was gettin' mixed up in money launderin’. Money laundering, eh? Old Harrison. Never surprised me. He always had an… entrepreneurial spirit. Though usually it involved selling slightly suspect car parts. "Structuring" and "layering” are code, alright. Breaking large sums into smaller deposits to avoid reporting thresholds, moving it through multiple accounts. It’s risky business. Very risky. The fines alone… you’re talkin’ serious money, potentially jail time. Seriously? That’s frightening. Dad should be keepin’ well clear of him. He’s got too much to lose. I’ve just opened a new business account, actually. So many compliance checks. They want to know  everything . Source of funds, expected turnover… it’s a nightmare, but you’ve  got  to do it. Banks are gettin' really strict. He said Mr. Harrison’s offered him a bit of work on the side, “consultancy” he called it. Just inputting data, he said. But Dad reckons it’s somethin’ to do with trackin’ these transactions. I told him straight, don’t even think about it. He’s a retired teacher, not a criminal! Good on yer Dad. Don’t need that hassle. Speaking of hassle, how’s little Lily doin’? She started school this term, right? She’s loving it, actually. Settled in really well. But the school uniform… extortionate.

…and honestly, the traffic getting here was  awful . Just gridlocked on the A38. You wouldn’t believe it for a Tuesday morning. Did any of you get caught in that? Not me, thankfully. Left early, knowing how it is. Though I did hear a report on the radio about an accident near the motorway junction. Probably that. Still, good to be here, nice and warm. Smell that coffee, Sarah? Lovely. It  is  good coffee, Mum. Though I think my class this morning were more energetic than the caffeine could handle! Year twos are… a handful, let’s just say. Little Leo tried to ‘help’ me staple the art projects together. Ended up stapling his jumper. Oh, bless him! Kids are brilliant, though, aren't they? A bit chaotic, but brilliant. Work was pretty quiet at the shop yesterday. Which is a blessing, honestly. Means I actually got through some of the paperwork. It’s always piling up. Paperwork is the bane of my existence, whatever you do. Though I haven't had much of that lately, being between projects. It’s a bit unsettling, actually. Still, gives me time to focus on the sign language course. Ah, yes, the sign language! How’s that going then? Remember old Mrs. Higgins down the road? She was partially deaf, always wished she'd learned it. Would have made such a difference to her life, I reckon. It’s going well, actually. Really challenging, but rewarding. It’s the facial expressions that get me. You have to make sure you’re conveying the right emotion  with  the signs, otherwise it doesn’t mean anything. I’m hoping it’ll be useful when the little one arrives. Wouldn’t it be wonderful to communicate with her even before she can talk? That’s a lovely idea, Mum. It’s brilliant you’re thinking ahead like that. It's definitely a skill that would be valuable throughout life, not just with the baby. It is! And maybe we could all learn a few basic signs? Imagine being able to ask for another biscuit without actually having to  say  it. You’re a cheeky one, aren’t you, Chloe? Though, thinking of biscuits… Sarah, are those chocolate digestive you’ve got? My favourite. Of course, Dad. Wouldn't dream of offering anything less. Now, about the baby shower… I was thinking the community hall in Lichfield? It’s got plenty of space, and we can decorate it nicely.

… honestly, the sheer volume of data is what’s stressing me out. We’ve got transcriptions from, like, six different dialects already, and that’s just the initial phase of the corpus building. It’s not just  transcribing  it, it’s tagging for all the nuances - the glottal stops, the T-glottalisation… it's a nightmare trying to standardise it all. Especially when you’re dealing with speakers who code-switch, you know? Oh god, yeah. That sounds… immense. I mean, I’m just mostly chasing authors for edits and checking proofs, which is stressful in its own way, but not… linguistically stressful. Do you find people get self-conscious when they're being recorded? Like, do they change how they speak? Definitely. I’ve seen it a lot in manuscript submissions – people trying to sound ‘more’ something, usually closer to Received Pronunciation. It's bizarre. Though I think with proper ethical procedure, you can mitigate that. We had a training session at the press on informed consent, specifically about the impact of observation on natural language. It’s interesting you say that. In Sweden, there's a lot of discussion about how formal interviews change language use. We did a whole module on it during my Masters. People become… performative, almost. Trying to give the ‘right’ answer, which bleeds into how they  phrase  the answer. Is this corpus for a particular project, or just general language research? It’s broadly for dialectal variation in Eastern England, focusing on how things are shifting with increased mobility and, y'know, the internet. Aylesbury is… well, it's getting increasingly less distinctive. Loads of people commuting to London, bringing influences back with them. That's why I'm so keen on getting a good grounding in the more rural pockets surrounding it. It’s proper fieldwork stuff though, going out to villages, recording spontaneous conversations. Sounds brilliant, actually. Really important work. It's just… a lot. Are you working alone on the analysis or do you have a team? It’s a small team, thankfully. A couple of undergrads helping with the initial transcriptions, but the detailed phonological analysis is mostly on me. Hence the stress. And the caffeine. Lots and lots of caffeine. We're increasingly seeing the impact of online communities on vernacular speech, aren’t we? I was reading a piece the other day about how TikTok slang is infiltrating younger generations' speech patterns, even in areas where you wouldn’t expect it.

...Honestly, the visa stuff is stressing me out more than the actual driving, y'know? Like, getting to Mongolia is one thing, but actually  getting permission  to be there, with all the bureaucratic nonsense… It’s a right headache. Did you get your application form sorted, Liam?      Aye, mostly. Sent off for the initial invite code thingy last week. Still waiting for that to come through. Apparently, it can take up to ten days. Ten days! We’re leaving in… what, seven weeks? It feels a bit tight, doesn’t it?      Tight? It’s mental! I was banking on having the visa in hand by now. I’ve got all the other bits – the letter from the charity, proof of funds… Mum actually helped me with that, bless her. Said I wouldn't have "a bean to my name" otherwise. She’s proper worried, you know. Keeps asking if I've packed enough socks.      Mothers, eh? Mine just keeps going on about the dangers. ‘Mongolia, Liam! It’s  Mongolia ! What about bears?’ Like, seriously? We're driving a car, not hiking through the wilderness looking for Yogi.      Exactly! Though, I did read something about wild dogs. Never even considered wild dogs. Right, gotta add ‘dog repellent’ to the list. Speaking of lists, have you managed to sort the donations yet? I’ve only had a few quid through my JustGiving page.      It's slow going. I put an ad on Gumtree, offering to do gardening for donations to the rally. Had one bloke offer me a fiver to weed his petunias. Fiver! I told him I'd rather push the car to Mongolia. Seriously considering hitting up the local pubs with a collection bucket.      Good shout with the pubs! We should definitely do that. Maybe next weekend? I was thinking we should get some proper flyers printed, too. Something a bit more professional than a scribbled bit of card.      Agreed. Flyers are a must. But who's doing the photos? I look like a right chump in every picture ever taken of me. Especially the ones for official documents.      Oh, God, passport photos. Don't even. I had a disaster trying to do mine at that booth in Tesco. It kept telling me my head was too big.  Too big!  Honestly. I ended up going to that proper photography place on Market Street. Cost a fortune, but at least I don't look like a criminal.

… honestly, I still can’t believe you ended up in A&E over an arm. It sounds completely like something  you  would do, though, doesn't it? Right dramatic entrance, the whole shebang. Oi! It wasn’t dramatic! It  hurt , alright? Proper bad. I thought I’d broken it, falling off that dodgy step outside Sugarhouse. And you weren't exactly a pillar of support, were you? Just filming me! You did look a bit…flailing, Liv. No offence. Though, fair enough, filming  is  Maya’s default response to everything. It’s documenting history! Plus, you were muttering about needing a ‘dramatic backstory’ for your uni application if it  was  broken. Don't deny it. Okay, maybe I said that. But seriously, the wait was ages. And the doctor was proper dismissive. Just said it was a sprain, told me to take paracetamol. A sprain that made me see stars, mind you. I'm still aching now. You poor thing. Well, at least it wasn’t broken. That's something. Are you managing okay with lectures today? You look a bit rough. Rough is an understatement. I feel like I’ve been run over by a bus, then forced to do a history essay. I nearly fell asleep in Dr. Peterson’s lecture – the one on the Tudors! Can you imagine? Falling asleep during Henry VIII. The shame. Ugh, lectures. Don’t even. I’ve got two back-to-back this afternoon on post-structuralism. Post-structuralism! It's just…words. Abstract words. I’m seriously thinking of just pretending to cough dramatically and fleeing. You wouldn't. You always end up feeling worse about skipping. Remember last week with the seminar on Romantic poetry? You spent the entire evening playing catch-up. That was  different . That seminar was actively trying to bore me to death. This one…well, I should at least  try . Speaking of actively trying to deal with things, how’s it going with… you know… Finn? Don’t even  start  me on Finn. He’s being…distant. Like, replying to texts with one-word answers distant. I asked him if he wanted to go to the quiz night tomorrow and he just said “Maybe.”  Maybe ?! Oh, that's…not good. He’s usually pretty enthusiastic about quiz night. Seriously. What’s up with boys, honestly? They’re all emotionally stunted, aren’t they? I had a really nice chat with Tom last night, though.

…and honestly, lad, your Auntie Brenda nearly took young Timmy’s head off with that feather boa. Honestly! She was whirling it around like a blooming helicopter. Did you  see  his face? Pure terror. Yeah, I did. He was hiding behind Grandad all night, wasn't he? Grandad looked a bit pleased, actually. Like he was enjoying being a human shield. He was! He always does. Loves a bit of drama, your Grandad. But it was a good do, wasn’t it? Mum and Dad’s fortieth was a proper success. Though I’m still finding glitter everywhere. It’s like a plague, glitter is. Gets  into  everything. It was good. A bit…loud though, wasn’t it? Especially when Uncle George started on the karaoke. “Bohemian Rhapsody”? Really? Oh, George. Bless him. He thinks he’s Freddie Mercury reincarnated. He’s got the enthusiasm, I’ll give him that. Just… not the voice. Your Grandma was trying to subtly signal for someone to switch it off, but no one noticed until halfway through the guitar solo. I saw! She was waving her napkin around like a flag. Did you think Cousin Sarah looked a bit…down? She didn't seem to be chatting much. Now you mention it, yes. She did seem a bit quiet. I thought maybe she was just tired. She’s been working really long hours lately, down at the vet’s. It's harvest season for the farmers, so it's always busy. I tried to ask her if she was alright, but she just said she was fine. Probably just stressed, love. She always bottles things up, that one. Mmm. Maybe. It just seemed…weird, you know? Considering she and Mark were only arguing last week, according to Mum. Something about him going on a lads’ holiday without telling her. Oh,  that . Yes, well. Mark's always been a bit…impulsive. Your mother's got a nose for these things, she does. I wouldn't worry too much, though. They’ll sort it out. They always do. They've been together since they were teenagers, haven't they? It's just one of those little wobbles. I suppose so. It just…felt a bit awkward. Especially with his brother being there too. They're always competing, aren't they? Always. It’s a right Yorkshire trait, that. Constant one-upmanship. You’ll be the same, you mark my words!

…and honestly, Dad, I don’t get why you needed  three  water bottles. One for you, one for me, and then that massive one? It’s just… excessive. Are you planning on dehydrating spectacularly? Now, now, lass. Gotta be prepared. You never know when a thirst’ll strike. And that big one’s for emergencies. Strategic hydration, I call it. Plus, yours leaks a bit, doesn't it? Remember that time it soaked your history notes? That was  one  time! And it wasn’t leaking, it was… condensation. Besides, I’ve got a pen now, a proper one, not that cheapy one you gave me. It actually  writes . It was five quid from Holland & Barrett, can you believe it? Five quid for a pen! Holland & Barrett for a pen? What were you doing in there, anyway? Getting some spirulina for your brainpower? You know, that shop's a goldmine. Reminds me, I need some magnesium for… well, you know. The IBS. Oh,  please  don’t talk about your stomach right now. I'm trying to enjoy the scenery, and the fact we’re actually going on holiday. It feels like ages since we’ve done this. Are we stopping for lunch in, like, Devon or something? I’m already thinking about pasties. Devon sounds good, yeah. Pasties it is. Thinking about it, remember when we moved everything into storage? That was a right palaver. Boxes everywhere, Amazon delivering stuff to the wrong address… and the washing machine nearly didn’t fit through the doorway! That was chaos! And all because you insisted on keeping  that  armchair. The one that looks like it belongs in a manor house. Honestly, Dad, it clashes with everything. It's a classic! Solid wood, good craftsmanship. They don’t make ‘em like that anymore. Speaking of classics, and money… the price of petrol is outrageous, isn't it? It’s like they're taxing us just for breathing. Tell me about it. Everything's expensive. I’ve been saving up for that new digital art tablet. It's… a significant amount of money. You work hard at school, you deserve it. Plus, you’re better at that stuff than I'll ever be. I can barely work the satnav. Honestly, travelling further south always feels different. You start hitting these counties – Cheshire, Staffordshire, Worcestershire – and it changes. Yeah, it feels…older? Do you think people are more insular down here?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of it is just… draining. Three hours of Mrs. Higgins rambling about her cat’s digestion. Three! I barely had time to flag the particularly juicy bits for you, David. You know, the bit where she thinks the postman is deliberately leaving bills under her doormat to stress her out. Gold dust, that is. Right, the Higgins files. A veritable treasure trove of local eccentricity. Though, honestly, three hours  is  a bit much, isn't it, Marion? You’re a trooper, though. I appreciate you sifting through it all. It makes my job so much easier. Just highlight the key bits and I can structure the community newsletter. Eccentricity? Or simply loneliness manifesting in peculiar ways? Mrs. Higgins was a perfectly bright girl at school, you know. Head girl, actually. Always very kind. It's a shame to see people…unravel. Now, now, Moira. Don’t go diagnosing folks. Everyone’s got their own way of coping, hasn't they? I spend half my day talking to planks of wood, and I don't think  that’s  unraveling, exactly. Just…focused. It’s not about diagnosing, Moira, it’s about local interest! People  read  about the Higgins’ saga. It gives them something to talk about at the shops. Plus, it fills a page. David’s under pressure to get content. Exactly. We need to keep the community engaged. It's not just about reporting news, it's about  being  the community. And truthfully, the Higgins stories do get a lot of shares on the village Facebook page. Facebook. Honestly. That’s where all sense of proper communication went to die. Everything’s reduced to snippets and sensationalism. When I was headmistress, we encouraged proper letter-writing. Nuance, considered thought… Letters take time, Moira. Time people don’t have. I’m lucky if I get a text message these days. It’s all about quick and easy. And frankly, a good story is a good story, whether it’s in a handwritten note or splashed across the internet. Even if it  is  about a cat’s digestion. He's got a point. And before you launch into a treatise on declining standards, Moira, have you seen the numbers for the gardening club raffle? They're down again. David was saying he needs to feature it more prominently. It’s a good cause, Marion. And Old Man Hemmings puts a lot of work into those dahlias.

…and honestly, the glitter is  still  turning up. I found some in the dog’s water bowl this morning! Honestly, Leo, you were a crafting machine yesterday. It was fun! Making the card for Grandma was the best bit. Did you put enough sparkles on hers, Mummy? Enough sparkles? Darling, it’s practically a disco ball. She’ll need sunglasses to read it! And Alfie, you were surprisingly focused on the painting. Usually you’re more interested in the paint  on  you than  with  the paint. It was a monster truck! A really,  really  fast monster truck! Painted it bright orange. I saw! A very impressive monster truck. Right, so, Mother’s Day. We’ve got the cards, breakfast is planned - pancakes with blueberries, Nana’s favourite, remember? - and I was thinking we could maybe go for a little walk afterwards, perhaps down to Grantchester Meadows? Can we go to Forest School instead? Please? We haven’t been for ages! We could build a fairy house for Grandma! Hmm, that’s a good idea, sweetheart. But Forest School is a bit muddy this time of year, isn’t it? And Nana isn’t terribly keen on mud. Remember last time? “Oh, Penelope, look at your shoes!” She said. She  did  say that! And she made me wash my hands for ages! Exactly. Plus, we promised her a gentle outing. Maybe just the meadows will be nice. We can look for daffodils. And then afterwards, we can  think  about building a fairy house for her in the garden. How does that sound? Okay…but can we collect sticks for it  during  the walk? Just in case we forget? We can definitely collect sticks. As long as we don't try to smuggle half the forest home with us. You two are like magpies. Speaking of… did you hear what happened at school today? Old Mr. Henderson tried to explain an idiom. What’s an idiom? It’s a funny way of saying something, where the words don't  literally  mean what they say. Like, if I say “it’s raining cats and dogs”, it doesn’t  actually  mean cats and dogs are falling from the sky, does it? Really? But…cats and dogs?! No, darling. It just means it’s raining heavily. Mr. Henderson tried explaining “break a leg” to a little boy who was terrified of performing in the school play.

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, isn’t it? Just knowing she  knew  something wasn’t right for months, but put it down to just ‘getting old’. Mum’s always been fiercely independent, you see. Wouldn't dream of making a fuss. Oh, absolutely. It’s the classic thing with our generation, isn't it? Mum’s the same. ‘Oh, it’s just a twinge,’ or ‘I’m just tired’. Then suddenly, it’s stage three and you’re reeling. How’s your sister coping? Sarah, is it? Sarah’s…holding it together, I think. She's taking on a ridiculous amount. Not just the practical stuff, the appointments and everything – which is exhausting enough – but the emotional weight of it all. She feels responsible, you know? Like she should have forced Mum to go to the doctor sooner. That's awful. That’s something you  always  feel, isn’t it? Even when logically you know it wasn’t your fault. I went through it a bit with Dad, after…well, after everything. Spent ages convinced I should have noticed something earlier. Even though the doctor said it was incredibly aggressive, quick-moving…the guilt lingers. It does. And it's not helped by Auntie Brenda, is it? Sticking her nose in, ‘Saying she always suspected something, she could  see  it in Mum’s face’… Honestly, the woman thrives on drama. Brenda’s been like that forever. Always needing to be the one with the insight, the one who knew all along. Ignore her. It’s easier said than done, I know, but she’s just…Brenda. How’s little Leo taking it? He’s close to your Mum, isn't he? He’s confused, mostly. He keeps asking when Nana’s going to be ‘better’. He saw her after the chemo started, and she was so tired. He didn’t recognise the ‘better’ Nana he knows. I tried to explain it, but…how do you explain cancer to a six-year-old? I ended up saying she was having a very long sleep to get strong again. Terrible, I know. Not terrible, love. You do what you have to do. Little ones have such a limited understanding. Thomas asked similar things when Grandad was…failing. We just said he was very, very tired and needed to rest his body. They pick up on the sadness though, don’t they? Even if they don’t understand the specifics.

… honestly, the way Dr. Aris presented that Chomsky hierarchy this morning was just… baffling. Like, he just  threw  the diagrams up and expected us all to magically understand the recursion. I spent the entire lecture just sketching little trees trying to make sense of it. Oh, Aris. He's brilliant, genuinely, but massively assumes prior knowledge. It’s like he forgets not everyone spent their childhood voluntarily dismantling sentences. Is that what you're teaching next week with the Year 10s – syntax? Yeah, a really simplified version of it. Honestly, I’m dreading it. They barely grasp the concept of a noun, let alone a phrase structure rule! Though, thinking about it, maybe I should actually  show  them a tree diagram, even a simple one. You're right, he just… leaves it hanging. Did you manage to confirm if Professor Kim will supervise your dissertation? I did! Emailed her yesterday, got a reply this morning. She’s up for it, which is a massive relief. Turns out she’s done quite a bit of research into language acquisition in South Korea, which, as you know, is exactly what I’m looking at. Apparently, the gendered language is really fascinating, especially how it impacts perceptions. Oh, really? I vaguely remember reading something about that. Something about different verb endings depending on who's speaking and who they’re addressing? It sounds… complex. Is it purely politeness, or is there more to it? It's everything. Politeness, showing respect, signalling social hierarchy… it's deeply ingrained. She told me there's a subtle pressure, even now, for women to use more deferential language. It’s tied into Confucian ideals, apparently. And the festivals! She was talking about Chuseok - a huge harvest festival. Sounds amazing. I really want to go, properly, not just a quick tourist trip. That sounds incredible. We should definitely put South Korea on the ‘places to visit’ list. After China, maybe. Though, remembering the food situation there… I’m still slightly traumatized by the duck feet. Oh god, don’t remind me! I tried to be adventurous, I really did, but…no. You know what I fancy for dinner? Something proper. I was thinking a veggie shepherd's pie? I picked up some really good sweet potatoes from the supermarket yesterday. Shepherd's pie sounds amazing, actually. You’re a culinary whiz, you know that? I’d offer to help, but last time I attempted to make mashed potato, it resembled wallpaper paste.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of glitter on that Secret Santa gift was offensive. Like, aggressively sparkly. Auntie Brenda, I love you, but a glitter-bombing kit is just asking for trouble. Especially in this house. Aye, glitter’s the devil’s dandruff, isn’t it? Still finding the stuff from Christmas ‘21. You’d think it’d biodegrade eventually. Speaking of trouble, anyone check the flooding updates? Saw a photo of the cycle path totally submerged. Oh god, really? I walked that yesterday! Didn’t realise it was  that  bad. I thought it was just a bit boggy. I’m starting to think Lancaster was a bad shout for uni, honestly. The rain alone… Dramatic, much? It's just a bit damp. It's Northern England, what do you expect? Remember that camping trip to the Lake District last summer, though?  That  was a proper soaking. I still have nightmares about trying to peg a tent into a mudslide. Oh, don't even. That was traumatic. Though, funnily enough, it felt less stressful than trying to understand Dr. Aris’s quantum physics lecture this morning. Honestly, it’s like he’s speaking another language. I’ve got module assessments due next week and I'm completely lost. Physics, eh? Always been a mystery to me. Give me Chaucer over chirality any day. I'm trying to decipher Jack Whitehall's logic on  The Big Fat Quiz . He’s utterly bonkers, but brilliant. Did you see him do the impressions? He's amazing! And have you lot seen that clip of him trying to explain airport scanners? I nearly choked on my tea. Oh, yes! “It’s looking for things you wouldn’t  want  it to find.” Classic. Speaking of finding things… did anyone steal my sports kit top? The bright orange one? It was on my bed this morning. No, but I did see someone wearing something suspiciously orange on the way back from Sugarhouse last night. Vaguely… silhouette-shaped. Remember when we all tried to do the  Rocky Horror Picture Show  dance after a few too many flavoured vodkas? Don't remind me. My legs were aching for a week. And the bruising! I think I genuinely collided with someone during the ‘Time Warp’. Though, it was worth it to finally appreciate Cloud Atlas. That film’s a masterpiece. Cloud Atlas is… a lot. I prefer something simpler, like  The Vampire Diaries .

…Aye, so like I said to Brenda, it just doesn’t  make  sense, does it? All this fuss about 'optimising' the tagging. Optimising for  what , eh? They want everything categorised down to the minute detail, but the point of a corpus is to see what happens naturally, isn’t it? Not force it into a neat little box. You sound exasperated, Liv. Still battling with the academics then? They always want things their way, don’t they? It’s the curse of being a details person, you give them an inch… An inch? They want the whole bleedin’ yard! Honestly, it’s this professor, Dr. Armitage. He's convinced identifying every instance of ‘like’ as a discourse marker is vital to understanding youth slang. Like,  really ? There's a million ‘likes’ in there, most of ‘em just filler. Folks in Sunderland have been saying “like” since I was a bairn, and nobody needed a fancy PhD to figure that one out. Right, so less ‘linguistic breakthrough’ and more ‘counting how many times people say ‘like’?’ Sounds… thrilling. You’d think with a postgraduate degree in engineering, I’d be immune to pointless categorization, but honestly, project management is basically the same thing. Just different jargon. Exactly! It's the principle. I’m meant to be a Corpus Administrator, not a linguistic detective. I’m cataloguing language as it  is , not deciding what it  should  be. And it's taking up all my time! I haven't even started on the digitisation of the Durham Miners’ Gala interviews. That stuff is  gold , real working-class voices, and I’m stuck here wrangling with ‘like’. The Gala interviews sound amazing, though. You were telling me about that archive. Properly important stuff, capturing a dying culture. That feels a lot more… worthwhile. It is! Me grandad marched in that Gala every year until he couldn’t walk anymore. Proper proud man. This tagging…it feels so… sterile, y’know? Like stripping the life out of it. I get it. It’s the distance, isn’t it? You're a bit removed from the actual  people  speaking. I have that sometimes with projects. Designing a bridge is brilliant, but you lose sight of the fact it’s people who will actually  use  it. Actually, reminds me of this site visit I did last week. This old bloke, a farmer, kept trying to explain how the proposed changes to the access road would affect his sheep.

…No, no, I’m tellin’ ya, this knee. It’s not gettin’  better , it’s gettin’ worse. Worse than last week, I swear. Remember last week, Doris? I could at least hobble to the shed for the paper. Now? Forget it. Absolute forget it. Oh, Arthur, you  say  that every week. It’s the damp, that’s what it is. Norfolk damp gets into your bones, it does. And this weather… look at it out there. Drizzly, grey. Depressing, the lot of it. Makes my arthritis sing, I tell ya. Gran, Dad, honestly, you both find something to complain about with the weather, whatever it’s doing! It was lovely yesterday. And Dad, have you actually  done  your exercises the physio gave you? Exercises?! At my age? Don't be daft, love. Those 'exercises' nearly put me in a hospital last time. Bendin’ and stretchin’…sounds like somethin’ a contortionist does, not a retired… well, not a retired anything, really. He’s got a point, actually. They sometimes do tailor things a little enthusiastically for older folks. But seriously, Arthur, a bit of movement helps. Maybe just a few gentle stretches? He’s got a good point there, Arthur. Gentle’s the word. Don’t go tryin’ to be an Olympic athlete now. It wouldn't suit ya! Though, having said that, I did see a programme about a ninety-year-old who ran a marathon… Ninety! Ninety! They’re made different, them lot. I’m tellin’ ya, it’s the cold. And speakin’ of cold, this electric blanket? It’s gone on the blink. Hardly warms up at all. Cost a fortune, it did. Oh no, not again! You had trouble with it last winter, didn’t you? Maybe it’s time to just get a new one, Dad. They’re not  that  expensive, and it’s getting colder every night. Yeah, a new one would be a good shout. We could have a look online for you. There's some with timers and different heat settings... much safer than fiddling with an old one. Online… hmm. All this newfangled technology. I can barely work the telly remote, let alone order things from the internet. Used to be simple. A trip to the shops, a chat with old Mr. Henderson… now it’s all clickin’ and scrollin’. Don't you start on the technology, Arthur. At least it keeps us connected.

… honestly, the seating plan is giving me actual nightmares. Aunt Carol  insisted  she needs to be near the buffet, and Uncle Barry thinks he deserves a front-row seat to watch everyone eat. It's like herding cats! Oh god, family weddings, aren’t they just… a performance? Mine was similar. Mum spent weeks agonising over whether Great Aunt Mildred would be offended by being placed too far from the loo. Seriously. You’re lucky you had a Mum to do that! I’d be lost. I’m still trying to figure out if I can actually  cook  a roast dinner for everyone at Christmas, let alone plan a wedding. Speaking of which, are you still loving Ben, Chloe? He seemed… quiet last time I saw him. He’s alright. A bit beige, if I’m honest. But Chloe’s head over heels, and that's what matters. Though, beige is probably stable, right? After that disaster with Liam… Hey! Liam wasn’t  all  bad. He was… enthusiastic. And he did try to learn German for me, which was sweet, even if his pronunciation was horrific. "Ich bin ein Berliner… but a very confused one!" he’d say. Oh, Chloe! You always find the silver lining. Look, enthusiasm is good, but stability is golden, especially when you’re talking about marriage and potentially… little ones. Have you guys talked about kids? Briefly. Ben wants them, eventually. I’m… apprehensive. I mean, I love my job. I’m finally getting somewhere with the grant applications at the council. And the thought of sacrificing sleep and my free time… it’s a bit terrifying. It is huge. Massive. My flatmate, Sarah, had a baby six months ago. She barely remembers what a hot shower feels like. She’s amazing, obviously, but it’s a complete life overhaul. And expensive! Don't even get me started. Everything's so ridiculously expensive. Even just baby clothes. I'm starting to think I'll just have a cat. Several cats. You say that now, but you’ll change your mind. You're such a softie, Amy. Anyway, enough about potential offspring. We need to talk about something more pressing – dinner! I’m starving. I was thinking that new Italian place on Bridge Street? It's got really good reviews. Oh, yes! I’ve heard about that one. Is it pricey? My budget’s a bit tight this month with the wedding stuff eating all my money.

…No, I’m tellin’ ya, this ‘internet of things’ is just a fancy way o’ bein’ spied on, isn’t it? My Maureen - bless ‘er soul – she got one o’ them voice-activated things, you know, the ‘Alexa’. Said it’d make life easier. Easier for  who  I ask ya? It were listenin’ to every bleedin’ word! Oh, Arthur, you and your suspicions. It’s just technology, dear. You get used to it. I had one for a while, helped me with the shopping list mostly. Though, I did tell it to play Vera Lynn once and it put on some rap music! Honestly. Sounds about right, Brenda. They’re not perfect, these things. Though, as a teacher, I've seen how useful it can be for the kids. Research, learning resources… it opens up a world. It's about teaching them  how  to use it safely, you see. That's the key. Safely? Hmph. My grandson, Jamie, he’s glued to that screen. Says he’s ‘gaming’. All shootin’ and killin’, as far as I can tell. Never used to be like that. Used to be out buildin’ dens and climbin’ trees. Proper boys’ stuff. Oh, they still do that, Arthur, some of them. I used to have a garden full of little ones. Always gettin' muddy, buildin' castles. Lovely it was. Though, screen time is a worry. My granddaughter, Chloe, she's always on TikTok. I don't even know what TikTok  is  properly, just that it involves dancin' and lookin' at phones! It's a short-form video platform, Brenda. Basically, very short clips. It’s addictive, though. The algorithm is incredibly clever at keeping people engaged. It’s all a bit… engineered, isn’t it? Reminds me a bit of how they target advertising, and speaking of… I just had a rather nasty bill come through for some online learning software I needed for work. Seems they've quietly increased the subscription. Bills, bills, bills. That’s all it is these days. Never enough. Maureen and I, we had a bit put by, you know. After her mum passed. Thought we were comfortable. Then… well, you know. Health, and then everything just seemed to… disappear. It's dreadful, Arthur, truly. And it's getting harder and harder, isn't it? Even for those who worked all their lives. I never did much, childminding mostly, cash-in-hand, but I always tried to be sensible.

…and honestly, the sheer variety of accents  within  Birmingham is fascinating. I had a student yesterday, born and bred in Handsworth, and it was a good five minutes before I fully grasped what she was saying! Not because her English wasn’t perfect, you understand, just…the intonation, the dropped ‘h’s, it’s beautifully distinct. It's a world away from what I’m used to, coming from Hitchin. Oh, you get that everywhere, don’t you? Essex was the same. You could travel ten miles and sound like you’d landed in another country. I remember my old man, he worked down by the docks in Tilbury. Said he could tell which town a chap came from just by listening to him shout orders. Clever, he was. Though, not much book learnin’, mind. Just a lot of… experience. Absolutely. It's a testament to how localised language can be. That’s what I try to get across to my students – language isn’t a rigid set of rules, it's  living . It's constantly evolving. I had them doing a little exercise on dialectal variations last week, and they were horrified to learn how much ‘standard English’ is actually…a construct. Horrified? Why’s that? Seems sensible enough to me. Makes things easier for everyone, doesn’t it? When I was runnin' the firm, clear communication was paramount. Couldn’t have lads on site misinterpreting instructions thanks to some fancy local slang. They felt it was…elitist, I think is the word. Like we were implying their own ways of speaking were ‘wrong’. It led to a really interesting discussion about power dynamics and social perception. They’re a bright bunch, though. Most of them are first or second generation, so they're already navigating multiple languages and cultures. Ah, see, that's different. I can see their point there. When you're dealin' with folks from all over, a common tongue is a godsend. I did a bit of travel with the company, you know? Germany, France…even a quick trip to Japan once. Try explainin' a complicated contract in broken Japanese! Let me tell you, sign language becomes your best friend. I can imagine! I’ve always fancied Japan. It's on my list. Though, I haven’t done much travelling recently, with work and everything. What about you, any holidays planned? No, no big trips this year.

… honestly, it was just  peak  Valentine’s Day cringe. Like, everywhere you looked, couples glued together, sharing spaghetti like it's a scene from a film. It was a bit much, innit? Tell me about it. I was trying to get a coffee, and nearly walked straight into a bloke attempting a grand romantic gesture with a single red rose. Nearly took my eye out. Where  were  you anyway? Avoiding the carnage? Pretty much! I went to see my nan. She doesn’t do Valentine’s, thinks it’s all a commercial ploy. Spent the evening playing Scrabble and eating biscuits. Much preferred it, honestly. Way less pressure. Did you… have plans? Sort of. Liam wanted to take me to the cinema. But then his mate needed a lift, so it ended up being him disappearing for two hours while I sat there looking at the popcorn machine. Honestly, it was drier than the Sahara. Oh, no way! That’s rubbish! He couldn’t even just, you know, hang out  with  you? That's proper disrespectful. What did you even  want  to see? There was that new horror film, “The Hollows”. Everyone’s saying it’s terrifying. But I didn’t want to go alone. It’s always awkward when you’re the single one surrounded by couples on a date night. Yeah, I get that. It feels like you're intruding on something. Speaking of awkward, I nearly bumped into Jasmine and Ben at the supermarket earlier. They were doing the big shop  together . Like, who needs to strategise grocery shopping on Valentine’s Day? Oh, Jasmine and Ben. They take everything to the extreme. Remember when they tried to recreate that pottery scene from “Ghost”? It ended up with Ben covered head-to-toe in clay and Jasmine threatening to divorce him five minutes into a relationship. Don’t even remind me! That was iconic. Anyway, what are you doing this weekend, apart from possibly ghosting Liam? I’m thinking maybe a bit of shopping – need a new jacket. And definitely some food. I’m craving a proper curry. Ooh, a curry sounds good. Have you tried that new place, “Spice Route”, near the station? Apparently, they do authentic Filipino dishes as well as the Indian stuff. My mum says it’s amazing. No, haven't heard of it! Filipino eh? Nice. I’m always up for trying new food.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the Levelling Up agenda just feels like a re-branding exercise. It’s throwing a bit of money at places that have been systematically underfunded for decades and calling it ‘levelling up’. It doesn’t address the core issues, you know? The structural inequalities. Exactly! It's performative. Like a plaster on a gaping wound. And honestly, the rhetoric around it feels…coded. Like, ‘we need to appeal to these voters’ without actually saying  what  voters or  why  they need appealing to. It’s frustrating. Speaking of frustrating, these Dan Dan noodles are amazing, are they not? A bit fiery, but amazing. Did you get the chilli oil on yours? Oh, definitely chilli oil. I live for the spice. And yes, completely agree. It’s infuriating because they’re not even trying to hide it anymore. It’s all about electoral calculations. It ties into everything, doesn't it? Like, the way they talk about immigration… it’s all designed to stoke division. It is. I was writing an article this week, a follow-up on the Windrush scandal actually, and the parallels are just…horrifying. The same language, the same ‘othering’… it’s exhausting to keep reporting on it, to be honest. You feel like you’re screaming into the void sometimes. I can imagine. It must be. It’s different for me at work, obviously. More… subtle, office politics. But it's still there. The old boy's network is  very  present in architectural firms, let me tell you. Plenty of unconscious bias when it comes to project assignments. It's always the men getting the big, flashy stuff. Oh,  please . Don’t even get me started on corporate structures. It's the same in media. You have to constantly prove yourself, double the effort, just to be considered on par. And then there's the pay gap… It’s all connected, isn’t it? This whole system is designed to keep certain people down. It absolutely is. It's capitalism, isn't it? In its purest, ugliest form. And then look at housing! Honestly, I’m starting to seriously contemplate just… moving back in with my parents. Even with my salary, saving for a deposit in London feels impossible. Tell me about it! I’m renting a tiny room in Kensal Rise, and it’s costing me a fortune. My parents keep saying I should move back to Mum and Dad’s too, but then where’s the independence?

…and honestly, the thought of leaving her for even half a day at nursery is just… awful. I keep picturing her little face, all confused.      Mum, you’re worrying too much. She'll be  fine . Honestly, Mrs. Davies at Blossom & Bloom seemed lovely. Properly qualified too, not just anyone off the street. And she said little Leo, who started last month, settled in really quickly.      Leo’s mum’s a stay-at-home mum, isn’t she? That’s different. She can pop in, check things are alright. I’ve got deadlines looming, the Henderson project… it feels selfish going back to work full-time when she’s only just turned nine months old.      Selfish? Mum, you  need  to go back! You'll go stir-crazy just being with Elara all day, as lovely as that is. And Dad’s been amazing, truly, but you both deserve to have your own things going on. Plus, the Henderson project is a big deal for you, remember? You were so excited about it before maternity leave.      I know, I know. It’s just… everything’s changing so fast. One minute she's a tiny newborn, the next she's gurgling and grabbing and soon, she'll be running off with strangers at nursery! And then there’s the weaning. It’s a battlefield! She refuses everything except sweet potato. Everything.      Classic Elara. Stubborn, just like her grandma. Have you tried blending it with a bit of apple? That’s what my friend Chloe did with her little boy, Alfie. He wouldn't touch anything green until she hid it in apple puree.      I’ve tried everything! Apple, pear, even a tiny bit of banana. She just spits it all out. Honestly, I feel like I’m force-feeding a tiny dictator. It's exhausting.      Okay, okay, deep breaths. Don’t stress. She won’t starve herself. Maybe just go back to milk for a bit and try again in a week? And honestly, don’t listen to all those people on Facebook groups telling you what to do. Everyone’s a bloody expert.      You’re right. It’s just… relentless, isn’t it? Actually, talking of relentless, have you seen what’s on TV lately? Just endless reality shows. Absolutely dreadful. I miss proper drama.      Oh, totally! I’ve been re-watching  Line of Duty . Still brilliant. You should join me! We could have a girls’ night when you’re back in the routine.

…and honestly, the sheer audacity of it! They’re claiming I used data roaming when I  specifically  checked before leaving for Cornwall that I had a sufficient allowance. It’s this EE bill, isn't it? Always something with them. It's infuriating. Aye, they’re a right pain, EE. I had a similar kerfuffle last year, ended up speaking to about six different people before they finally admitted their system had messed up. Did you keep a screenshot of your allowance check? I  think  so. I’m rummaging through my emails now… yes! Here we go. Dated the 12th, clearly showing 5GB roaming data. I’ll send it over to you, David, you’re better at navigating these things than I am. Honestly, phone companies just assume you’re clueless. It's a tactic. They rely on people just giving up and paying it. It's predatory, really. They know most people just don't have the time or energy to fight it. I dealt with something similar with a dodgy energy supplier last month. Endless hold music and aggressively polite deflection tactics. Exactly! It’s the principle. And it’s not a small amount, it’s nearly seventy quid! Think of what we could do with seventy quid… a nice bottle of wine, maybe. Now you’re talking. Look, send me that screenshot, I’ll draft an email for you. I’ve had practice writing strongly worded letters, unfortunately. Speaking of things that are stressful, how did the statement go today, Sarah? About the incident with… well, you know. Oh, God. It was awful. Just…reliving it all again. The officer was very understanding, thankfully. He kept reassuring me it wasn't my fault, but still. It’s all a bit of a blur, to be honest. They asked about everything, minute details. What colour the car was, what time exactly… It felt like they were looking for inconsistencies. That's what they do, isn't it? It's standard procedure, but must be terrifying. I can’t imagine. It is. They're trying to build a watertight case, and that means covering all the angles. Did they give you any indication of how long the investigation might take? He said it’s ‘ongoing’ which, of course, means ‘don’t hold your breath’. He said they’re interviewing other witnesses. Hopefully, that'll help. I just want it all to be over.

…and honestly, the CGI in the new  House of the Dragon  is just breathtaking. It’s a completely different level to what they were doing with  Game of Thrones  initially. Though, you know, dragons aside, it’s still all political machinations and backstabbing. Very Roman, really. Roman? You think so? I always saw  Game of Thrones  as more… Medieval fantasy. The Romans were pretty organised, weren’t they? Proper infrastructure. Roads, aqueducts… not just throwing tantrums and setting fire to things. Though, I suppose they had their fair share of that too. Remember that documentary we watched, about Caligula? Bonkers. Well, the power struggles  are  the key. The constant vying for power, the conspiracies… it’s all straight out of Suetonius. And the sheer ruthlessness! You look at the Targaryens, or the Julio-Claudian dynasty… same energy. Speaking of which, have you ever actually delved into proper Roman history? Beyond the gladiator films? Not really, no. I mean,  Spartacus  was alright. Bit… stylized. All that slow motion. And everyone dying young. Honestly, it’s depressing. Makes you appreciate getting to, you know, thirty without a legionary’s sword finding you. True enough. Though thirty isn’t exactly over the hill, is it? Remember Liam Gallagher getting all precious about turning thirty? Now he’s… well, considerably past that. He’s aged, that’s for sure. Still sounds alright though. Got a proper voice, does Liam. Speaking of alright… you made a cracking cuppa, by the way. What tea is this? Not that builder's stuff, I hope? Good taste as always. It’s a Darjeeling, actually. Auntie Margaret sent it over. She’s still obsessed with tea. Says it’s the only civilized thing left in the world. I've been trying to get her to branch out with herbs though. I got a proper mortar and pestle the other day – feels very…ancient, you know? I’m thinking of making my own chai blends. A mortar and pestle? Fancy! I'm more of a ‘chuck it all in a bowl and hope for the best’ kind of cook. I’ve been messing about with spices for this Moroccan tagine. Got some proper preserved lemons, too. Makes all the difference. You know, when I'm travelling for work, I always try and bring back spices. Oh, you still do gardening jobs all over, then? Yeah, bit and pieces. Last month it was a big estate near Cambridge.

… honestly, Miss Davies is  obsessed  with semicolons. Like, it’s all she talks about. “Consider the judicious use of the semicolon, girls!” It’s exhausting! And the test was just… brutal. All about Victorian poetry. Honestly, who even  reads  Victorian poetry anymore? Tell me about it! I completely blanked on the Tennyson question. I knew it was something about… like, honour and fallen soldiers, but I couldn’t remember the actual poem. Honestly, I think she sets the tests to be deliberately difficult. It’s like she  wants  us to fail. Exactly! And then she looks all disappointed when everyone does badly. It's so performative. Did you finish the analysis of ‘My Last Duchess’? I couldn’t get my head around Browning’s… well, everything. Ugh, yeah, but it took me ages. I had to go online and read like, three different SparkNotes just to get a grasp of what he was on about. It just felt so… cynical, didn’t it? And really long-winded. Much prefer Shakespeare, honestly. Anything but Victorian poetry. So much better. Speaking of better, art is the absolute  best . Old Mr. Henderson actually lets us experiment. We’re doing clay sculptures next week, apparently. I'm thinking of trying a gargoyle. Ooh, a gargoyle! That sounds amazing! I’m still trying to get over messing up my perspective drawing last week. It looked like the buildings were all melting. Henderson just sort of chuckled and said, “Interesting interpretation!” He's so lovely, isn't he? Completely different from Miss Davies. Right, French. Don’t even get me  started  on French. Monsieur Dubois just drones on and on about irregular verbs. Don’t remind me! I swear, my brain just shuts down every time he starts talking about the subjunctive. And he always picks on Chloe! She tries so hard, but she always gets flustered and can’t remember the genders. It’s awful to watch. It is. She's really sweet, though. Did you see her trying to convince Mr. Palmer to let the wind band play at the summer fete? I did! Bless her. He seemed a bit hesitant. Said something about needing to check if the scheduling worked. It would be good for the band, though. We haven't had a proper gig in ages. Are you still enjoying flute? Yeah, it’s alright. A bit stressful with the solos, but it’s fun.

…and honestly, Liam, the price of a loaf of bread these days! It's scandalous. Used to be you could get a decent white sliced for under a pound, now it's pushing two. Two pounds, mind! What’s the world coming to, eh?      Aye, it’s daft, Miss. But Ms. Davies said in economics it’s ‘inflation’ and stuff. Something about supply and demand. Sounds made up to me.      Inflation’s very real, love. I used to try and explain it to kids too, back when I was teaching. It’s easy when you’ve seen prices creep up over the years. Remember when a packet of crisps was ten pence?      Oh, don't  start  me on crisps, Carol! Walker’s used to be the one, didn’t they? Still alright, but they’ve shrunk the bags, haven't they? Sneaky little things. And the flavours…all these fancy ones. Give me Cheese & Onion any day. Simple.      Cheese & Onion  is  the best. Though Salt & Vinegar's alright if you're feeling brave. Speaking of brave…did you see the match on Saturday? Newcastle absolutely hammered Sheffield United.      I did! Heard it on the radio while I was marking papers. Honestly, the commentary was dreadful. All bias towards Newcastle, of course. Although, I must admit, I was chuffed for you, Liam. Your face lit up when you were telling me about it yesterday.      He lives and breathes football, doesn’t he? Though I think he’s more interested in transfers than actual games these days. All this talk of millions… it’s obscene.      It's strategy, Auntie Carol! Gotta get the best players. Think about Bellingham. He's changing the game. Though, speaking of changing the game, have you seen that new app everyone’s on? “Vibes”? It’s like TikTok but…different.      Oh, no. Another one? Honestly, these youngsters and their phones. When I was your age, Liam, we were outside building dens! Not glued to screens.      It's not  just  screens, Miss. You can connect with people, share stuff… it’s… social.      Social used to mean a cup of tea and a chat, love. Like this. . Though I will admit, I do use Facebook to keep up with distant relatives. Found out my cousin’s grandson is a chef in Australia.      Australia! Lovely. I always wanted to go. Never had the money, though. Never prioritised it, I suppose.

…and honestly, the traffic getting  out  of Cambridge was worse than getting in. It felt like everyone decided to simultaneously take a driving lesson. Honestly, it’s a wonder anyone passes their test these days. You say that, love, but you passed first time, didn’t you? Remember boasting about it for weeks? That was a lifetime ago, Dad! And purely down to Miss Higgins at school drilling ‘mirror, signal, manoeuvre’ into our heads until we dreamt about it. It's just…people aren't paying attention. Phones, mostly. It’s terrifying. It’s all this rushing about, isn’t it? Nobody takes a moment. When your father and I were courting, we’d walk everywhere. Proper walks, not these power-walks everyone does now trying to burn off…well…everything. Mum’s got a point. There's a real issue with obesity, isn’t there? It’s not just about personal responsibility, though. It’s availability of healthy food, marketing, societal pressures…it's complex. Complex? It’s people eating too much, simple as that! When I was a lad, we didn’t have this nonsense. Fish and chips on a Friday, and that was it. Everything in moderation. Now it’s supersize this and mega-portion that. But Dad, that's a simplification. There's a huge genetic component now that's being understood. Some people are predisposed to gaining weight more easily. And it’s not just about  what  you eat, it’s  how  your body processes it. It's linked to all sorts of things. My sister, bless her, always struggled with her weight. And her children did too. Doctor said it was something to do with their metabolism. It's not laziness, you know. It's just…different. She always said it felt like she was fighting her own body. Exactly. And that predisposition can be exacerbated by environmental factors. It’s nature  and  nurture. Speaking of things being pre-determined…I was reading an article about how religious belief can be partially genetic. Genetic? Don’t be daft. That’s just a way for people to explain things they don't understand. Faith is a choice, plain and simple. My Nan, she was a rock of faith. Taught me everything I know. Never heard her saying it was in her genes. It's not saying it  determines  belief, Dad. It’s suggesting certain personality traits – openness to experience, a need for meaning – might have a heritable component, and those traits might correlate with religious belief.

…and honestly, the student feedback was  brutal . Apparently, navigating the Moodle quiz settings is akin to “untangling a plate of spaghetti with chopsticks,” which, honestly, felt a little harsh, but… not entirely inaccurate. Ouch. That’s a vivid image, though. Moodle. The bane of every lecturer’s existence. What specifically did they struggle with this time? Was it the randomised questions again? No, surprisingly not. Though that  always  causes issues. It was the feedback conditions. You know, the whole ‘show correct answers after submission’ versus ‘delayed feedback’ business. They kept getting scores of zero because they weren’t realising they couldn’t see what they got wrong  immediately . Several thought the quiz was broken. Oh, the classic. You’d think after all these years, they’d just…expect it. I still get emails about that one, even with the explicitly worded instructions. Did you put a clear disclaimer on the quiz page? Something like, “Feedback will be released on [date]” in bold? I did! I thought I did, anyway. I even put a little banner at the top. Maybe it was too subtle? I feel like I’m constantly walking this tightrope between making it accessible and preventing cheating. If I give too much away upfront, then everyone’s just googling the answers. It’s a nightmare. Have you considered using conditional releasing of activities? So they  have  to attempt the quiz before they can access the feedback explaining the settings? It’s a bit fiddly to set up, admittedly, but it forces them to engage with the process. Conditional releasing… hmm. That’s actually a really good idea. I hadn’t thought of that. It adds an extra layer, doesn’t it? Just enough to make them pay attention. I usually just rely on the ‘completion tracking’ for the introductory module, but that clearly isn’t enough. Completion tracking is… optimistic, let's say. They all click 'completed' without actually  doing  anything. I’ve seen it. It's astonishing. I'm spending far too much time chasing up students who haven't even looked at the materials. Tell me about it. I had one student email me yesterday asking a question that was answered verbatim in the first video of the course.  The first video!  I’m starting to suspect they believe lectures magically appear as fully formed knowledge in their brains. That’s a lovely thought, isn’t it?

… honestly, I still feel like I’m operating on New York time. Woke up at five this morning, convinced I was late for a seminar. Utterly pointless getting up that early, just stared at the ceiling for an hour. You and me both, love. Though five is practically sleeping in for you, generally. Still, jetlag is brutal. Especially when you've been running on adrenaline fuelled baby-wrangling for ten days with the folks. Don’t remind me about the baby-wrangling! Mum and Dad are  wonderful , truly, but…constant offers of pureed carrots. It’s a power play, I swear. And the unsolicited advice! “She needs more layers!” “Is she getting enough tummy time?” Honestly, I needed a holiday  from  the holiday. They mean well. They’re grandparents. It’s in their coding. Although, your mum  does  have a very specific vision of optimal baby development. Remember when she tried to get us to start potty training Leo at eighteen months? Oh god, don’t even. We agreed to a firm ‘no’ on that one. Right, anyway. Back to the present. Are we still on for the Marlowe Society performance on Friday? I booked the tickets ages ago, but with the travel… I didn’t want to assume. Absolutely. I wouldn’t miss it. It’s been ages since we've had an evening just the two of us, doing something…civilised. Baby-free civilisation, at that. What are they doing,  Doctor Faustus ? Yes! Apparently, it’s a rather unconventional take. The director’s a former student of mine, actually – a really bright spark, but a bit…avant-garde. Said he’s leaning heavily into the psychological torment aspect. Prepare for a dark evening. Sounds perfect. We could both do with a bit of psychological torment, after the last week. Seriously though, how are you holding up? Beyond the jetlag, of course. You seemed…a bit overwhelmed when we landed. It's just…seeing Mum and Dad with the baby. It’s lovely, of course. But it makes you realise, you know? How much has changed. And how quickly. And the guilt of not being there more. It's ridiculous; they know we’re busy with work. That’s completely normal, isn’t it? It's the grandparent dynamic. They’re meant to make you feel momentarily inadequate, then swoop in and save the day with biscuits and unconditional love.

…and honestly, Karim, I’m still pulling my hair out over old Derek. He's convinced he can just  walk  into America. No visa, just a charming smile and a story about needing to “find himself.” Honestly! He's been watching too many films. You deal with this sort of thing professionally, doesn’t he understand the sheer bureaucracy involved? Derek sounds…optimistic. You’d think people would learn. I get requests  all the time  from folks who think a heartfelt letter explaining their need for a holiday is enough. The US system, especially post-9/11, is…robust. It requires paperwork, evidence, the right categories…and often, a bit of luck. What’s he hoping to do  in  America, anyway? Something about visiting a nephew he hasn't seen since the lad was a baby. Lives in California. Derek keeps banging on about ‘family ties’, but he hasn’t bothered to  establish  any legally. He thinks a Facebook message counts as proof of relationship! It's hilarious, if it wasn't so stressful for his sister. She’s worried he’ll get detained. Detained is a real possibility, yeah. Especially if he attempts entry without applying correctly. It’s a shame, though. Family should be able to see each other. It reminds me of trying to get my sister over from Kurdistan. Endless forms. And the expense! It's not just the visa fee; it’s proving funds, demonstrating intent to return… it’s a whole rigmarole. It makes you wonder why people bother with international relations sometimes. It all seems designed to keep people  apart . It’s the oil, isn’t it? At the root of so much of it. All this border control, security…it’s about controlling resources, controlling movement. Look at Libya. Chaos, instability, all tied up in who gets access to the stuff. And then you’ve got the rise of Wahabi influence throughout the region adding another layer of complexity. Honestly, trying to explain it all to my students feels futile sometimes. You're not wrong about the oil. And Libya… a disaster, orchestrated from outside, really. I have family who were working there before everything fell apart. They lost everything. It’s not simply a political issue, you know? It's people's lives ripped apart. The Wahabi influence… that’s a different beast. It’s about control in a different way – control of thought, control of behaviour.

… honestly, I still think a TV in the dining room is just  asking  for trouble. It's just…distracting. We've managed perfectly well for years without one. Though, admittedly, having something to watch while clearing up would have been nice after that lamb. It was delicious, though, wasn’t it? Perfectly pink. It  was  good, Mum. You’ve really mastered the roast lamb now. And I see your point about the TV, actually. It feels a bit…American, doesn't it? All these massive screens everywhere. Though, a little football during dinner wouldn’t go amiss sometimes, I’ll admit. Oh, you two. Always debating. I think a small one wouldn’t hurt. Just for background noise, maybe the news. Better than you two bickering over who does the washing up! And the lamb  was  lovely, dear. Though, a little more mint sauce wouldn’t have gone amiss. Reminds me of a roast we had on the cruise last year… now  that  was a spread. Lobster, too. A cruise… you’ve completely spoiled us with stories of that cruise, Mum. Honestly, Clive and I are saving, but it feels like a lifetime away. Especially with the landlord hinting at another rent increase. Honestly, the cheek of him! Tell me about it. He keeps saying the market dictates things. Like we're all just puppets dancing to the tune of property prices! It's infuriating. We’re looking at moving eventually, but it’s just… daunting. Everything is so small and overpriced. Landlords! Don't get me started. They breed like rabbits. When I was Headmistress, dealing with parents was child’s play compared to handling a bad landlord. Though, you’re lucky you’ve got a garden, at least? It’s good for Barnaby. He’s thriving, isn't he? Getting so big. He needs a good run, which is why I try and get us all out for a walk every day. Though, honestly,  I  need a good run – or maybe just a proper workout. I keep meaning to rejoin that Pilates class. It did wonders for my back. You should, love. You’ve been saying that for months. I’ve been trying to get back into running, but my knees are playing up. Old age catches up with us all, eh? Speaking of which, Mum, did you bring that Scottish tablet you made? I've been craving it all week.

…Aye, but honestly, me mam’s shepherd’s pie is just… different class. It's not like anything else, y'know? She puts a secret ingredient in, refuses to tell anyone. Drives us all daft. Yer mam and her secrets! She’s always been like that. Remember when she wouldn't tell us what she put in her Christmas pudding for  years ? Turned out to be brandy butter. Brandy butter! Sounds lovely, though. I miss proper home cooking. Living with housemates is alright, but it’s mostly pasta and things you can microwave. Not a lot of shepherd's pie going around. Tell me about it. Sustaining yourself on a TA’s wage and a student diet is… a challenge. I’ve become a pro at batch cooking. Chilli mostly. Keeps for days. Chilli’s good. But it's not the same as something proper, comforting. Like, I haven’t had a decent meal cooked  for  me in… well, a long time. Since I finished uni, I suppose. You should come round for tea more often, Liam. I’m trying to learn more than just beans on toast now I’m at sixth form college. Though, admittedly, most of it still ends up slightly burnt. I feel bad, always just turnin’ up unannounced. Just… a bit stuck at the moment, y’know? Still searchin’ for a job. Seems like nobody wants someone with a history degree. Don't beat yourself up about it, lad. It’s tough out there. It's not just you. Plenty of graduates struggling. Did you try applying for that assistant role at the library? Aye, did. Got a polite ‘thanks but no thanks’ email. They said they needed someone with “experience in a public-facing role.” What’s a history degree then, a qualification in staring at books? That’s awful! They should appreciate the skills you have. Research, analysis… those are valuable in any job. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if sixth form is even worth it. Like, what’s the point of getting good grades if you’re just going to end up stuck like… well, like Liam. No offence, love. None taken. It’s the truth, innit? Sarah, how’s uni going for you anyway? Still lovin' it down in Leeds? It's alright. The course is good, but it’s expensive. I'm always skint. And I miss everyone here, obviously. Especially you lot and me mam’s cooking!

…and honestly, the buttercream was a disaster last time. It just  wouldn’t  pipe properly. It was like trying to wrestle with slightly melted plasticine. Plasticine! Was it pink? Pink plasticine is the worst! It was pale yellow, actually, which, looking back, wasn't helping. Too close to the colour of…well, you know. Anyway, this time we're going for chocolate. Less visual ambiguity. And I've watched about ten YouTube videos on the perfect buttercream consistency. Is it for the little ones at school? Are they gonna get to  eat  it? They are! It’s part of the food technology lesson, remember? We’re making shortbread biscuits, and then decorating them. It's Year 3, so they're just learning about where food comes from, basic measuring…and the joy of sugar, obviously. I helped you measure the flour last time! I got flour  everywhere . You did, my love. You did. A very thorough flouring of the kitchen. Good work. This time, maybe you can supervise the sprinkles? A much less messy job. Can I put the chocolate on? Even though you already said it’s in the buttercream? You’re a clever one. You’re thinking ahead! We can definitely have extra chocolate on top, little man. Maybe some chocolate chips? Ooh! And rainbow sprinkles! And the little silver balls! Steady on! We don't want a sugar rush of epic proportions. Although… it  is  almost your half-birthday. Didn’t we say we’d do something special? Half-birthday? What’s a half-birthday? It's when you're halfway through the year since your birthday! So, like, a mini-birthday. We can have a tiny cake, and maybe watch a film. Can we play Tomodachi Life too? My Mii is married to a pink dinosaur! A pink dinosaur? Oh, that’s brilliant! Yes, we can definitely play Tomodachi Life. Look, I was thinking, while I'm running errands tomorrow, I need to pop into Morrisons. Do you two want to come? Morrisons has good biscuits! They do! But actually, I'm hoping to find that book Mrs. Peterson recommended. ‘The Lost Words’. She says it’s beautiful, all about forgotten nature words like ‘bracken’ and ‘newt’. Apparently, it's designed to get children reconnected with nature. Newts are slimy! I saw one in Grandad's pond. They can be a bit slimy, yes. But fascinating!

… honestly, it’s just baffling. Old Mrs. Henderson posted  another  one of those ‘share if you love Jesus’ things. It’s like, Brenda, seriously? You’ve shared it three times this week! And it’s always got that awful blurry photo of a sunset. Right, the blurry sunset brigade. It’s a phenomenon, isn’t it? I swear my aunt Margaret is single-handedly keeping Facebook afloat with inspirational quotes over landscape pictures. It’s more than just the quotes, it’s the… the  everything . People believing absolutely anything they read. I saw a post claiming the government was putting microchips in the COVID vaccines to control our… what was it? Our toast settings? Toast settings? That's a new one. They've moved on from 5G controlling minds to toast? Progress, I suppose. Though honestly, I switched my newsfeed to ‘Favourites Only’ months ago. It's blissfully ignorant. I’ve considered it. But then I feel… detached. Like I'm actively ignoring what’s happening, even the ridiculous stuff. It’s the echo chamber effect, isn't it? Everyone grouping with people who already agree with them. It’s terrifying. It is. Though, speaking of things people believe despite evidence to the contrary… have you seen Dave's new car? Oh, don’t get me started on Dave’s ‘investment’. The bright orange monstrosity? It looks like a traffic cone on wheels. Exactly! And he’s convinced it’s “a future classic”. He was going on about its ‘limited edition’ status and how it’ll be worth a fortune in twenty years. A bright orange Kia Picanto, a  future classic . He's always had terrible taste in cars. Remember that lime green Rover he had in uni? It was… a statement. A very loud, regrettable statement. And the fact he researched it all online, obviously. “According to a forum,” he kept saying. As if that makes it reliable information. It never does, does it? The internet’s amazing, truly. But it's also a breeding ground for misinformation and questionable car choices. I mean, I looked up that model myself – depreciation is  horrendous . He’s throwing money away. It's the same mindset though, isn’t it? The same willingness to believe what reinforces their existing beliefs. “Oh, this online forum says it’s valuable, therefore it  is  valuable.” It's like Facebook, but with wheels. Precisely! You apply the same critical thinking – or lack thereof – to both.

...Honestly, the amount of people asking for things we just  don’t  have is unbelievable. Like, seriously, “Do you sell garden gnomes?” At a phone shop! Where do people even  think … Anyway, how was your day? Still wading through essays, I presume?      Yeah, pretty much. History’s a killer this week. It’s all about the Suffragettes. It’s… well, it’s a lot. This film is much more relaxing, though. Remember when we used to watch this  constantly  when we were little?      Oh, god, yeah. ‘Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs’. Basic childhood. Though, I don’t think I ever really  thought  about it, you know? Like, beyond "giant food is cool".      I was thinking about that! It's kinda… a commentary on consumerism, isn’t it? Like, Flint Lockwood just kept wanting to  make  more, bigger, better food, and it just spiralled out of control. And everyone just… accepted it.      Woah, deep thoughts for a Saturday afternoon watching a kids’ film. You’ve been spending too much time with those history essays. Speaking of accepting things, can you pass me the remote? I can’t reach it from here. And seriously, why do remotes have like, a million buttons and none of them do what you want them to?      It's under that cushion. And I know, right? It's designed to confuse us. About the film though… It feels like it’s about how we take things for granted. All that food, just…falling from the sky. No thought for where it comes from, or the consequences.      Hmm. Maybe you're right. I was just thinking about lunch, actually. I haven’t eaten since that questionable sausage roll at work. It was…an experience. Pretty sure it was mostly bread.      You need to eat something proper. Work sounds stressful. Still dealing with terrible customers?      Always. It’s just… draining. And then everyone assumes because you're ‘just’ in retail you don’t have a brain. Old Mr. Henderson actually asked me if I was going to university  eventually . Like, failing retail is a stepping stone to higher education.      That’s awful! People are so rude. It’s linked, I think, to that whole… dismissing women’s careers thing we were reading about for the Suffragettes. People thinking certain jobs are ‘suitable’ for certain genders.      Totally. It's frustrating. It’s like, mind your own business, yeah? It’s just… the world feels a bit… messy right now, doesn't it?

...Honestly, the sheer arrogance of it all, John. They promised a new dawn, didn’t they? A break from the Thatcher years. New Labour, all sunshine and roses. And what did we get? A slick PR machine with a penchant for war.      Aye, you’re not wrong there, Professor. Tony Blair, eh? Polished shoes and a smile that could sell sand to the Arabs.
