Though, to be fair, things  were  a bit grim before him, weren't they? Me dad was a docker, lost his job with all the closures. New Labour at least  talked  about helping folks like him.      Talked being the operative word, John. Talked and… well, redefined what ‘helping’ meant. Stakeholder society, remember that nonsense? Everyone having a stake, but the biggest stakes still ending up in the pockets of the already wealthy. It’s a classic bit of linguistic manipulation, really, framing inequality as inclusivity. I lecture on it, of course. Post-structuralism and the power of discourse.      Post-what-now? Sounds fancy. I just know what I see. I drive people around all day, Professor. Doctors, lawyers, builders… and plenty who’ve been shafted by the system. Heard a lot of stories, I have. More than you'd get from reading books, probably.      There’s a value to lived experience, absolutely. That's why I enjoy these chats, actually. It grounds the theory. Still, the cleverness of the rhetoric… it’s fascinating. They managed to convince a generation they were progressive while fundamentally upholding the status quo. And the Iraq War... that was a turning point, wasn't it? Completely eroded any trust.      A disaster. Pure and simple. Me nephew went over there. Came back a different lad. Still can’t sleep right, he can’t. All for what? Oil? Some dodgy intelligence? The whole thing stinks, it does. Though, speaking of disasters, did you see Everton on Saturday? Absolute shambles.      Ah, yes. Football. A welcome distraction from the failings of humanity, perhaps. Though even there, the money is ruining it. The Premier League… it's a global entertainment product, hardly a sport rooted in community anymore. Honestly, it's a tragedy. I remember going to Goodison Park with my grandfather. It was… different.      Different alright. Used to be proper passion, you knew? Not this manufactured hype. Now it’s all about the sponsors and the billionaires. Still, I’ve got to have hope, haven’t I?

…Honestly, the sheer  volume  of data in those BNC recordings is just…daunting. I’ve been trying to isolate instances of non-standard ‘be’ usage in the East Anglian samples and it's like finding a needle in a haystack made of needles. Proper linguist’s problem, I suppose.      Tell me about it. Editing copy is bad enough, wading through marketing guff all day. You're dealing with  actual  language formation, though, aren’t you? That’s…proper academic. Mine’s just making sure ‘affect’ and ‘effect’ are the right way ‘round for the fiftieth time today.      It sounds exhausting, whatever you’re both doing. I just spent the morning battling LinkedIn. I swear, everyone's a ‘thought leader’ these days. It’s incredibly…performative.      Oh,  don’t  even get me started on LinkedIn. I barely touch it. I had one connection request from someone claiming to be a ‘synergy architect’. A  synergy architect ! What does that even  mean ? Makes me want to delete my profile and live as a hermit.      Proper cringe. I use it, sadly, ‘cause the job market. But it feels so…artificial. Everyone’s highlighting their ‘key competencies’ like they’re Pokémon cards. Speaking of escapes… did you see those Maldives pictures I put on Instagram?      Oh my god, yes! Seriously, turquoise water as far as the eye can see. Pure envy. You looked so blissed out. Though, knowing you, you were probably stressing about the optimal filter for maximum aesthetic impact.      Hey! Filters are an art form! And yes, it  was  blissful. Except for the flying. Always the flying. I was a wreck, honestly. Gripped the armrests so hard my knuckles went white.      You still scared of flying, then? I thought you’d managed to… conquer it?      Conquer is a  strong  word. Tolerated, maybe. It’s the not being in control, innit? And the turbulence. I read some article about how turbulence is just normal air currents, but it doesn’t  feel  normal when you’re bouncing around like a ping pong ball. You alright with flying, then, Liv?      I manage. I just…distract myself. Podcasts, books, excessive amounts of biscuits. I'm thinking of trying meditation next time. Though, the thought of a long haul flight…reminds me, my aunt just moved to Spain. Marbella, of all places.      Oh, Marbella! It’s…a lot. I visited a friend there once. Very shiny.      Exactly! Not really her vibe, but apparently, she’s decided she’s ‘finding herself’.

… honestly, Mum, I still don’t get why you’re so fixated on the placement. Like, it’s  my  arm. A little bit of rebellion isn't gonna kill anyone, is it? And it's not like it's a massive dragon, it's just that little geometric design. Rebellion? Oh, please, Leo. You're a post-grad student, not a punk rocker. It’s just… well, you know I’m a bit old-fashioned. And visible tattoos on a future educator… it just feels… a bit much. Imagine meeting parents, darling. Mum, seriously? It's 2024. Loads of teachers have tattoos. And I’m aiming for secondary, not a prep school. They’ve seen things. Besides, it’ll mostly be covered by a sleeve anyway. Look, can we drop it? I’ve already booked the appointment. I'm more worried about this risotto being an utter disaster. Did you get enough parmesan? Plenty of parmesan. And yes, alright, drop it. But don't come crying to me if you regret it. Speaking of disasters, how’s the flat renovation going? Any closer to having a functioning kitchen? Slowly. So, so slowly. The electrician is a myth, I swear. He promised to come Tuesday, then Wednesday, now he's saying next week. It's a nightmare. Honestly, living on takeaways is getting expensive.    Hello, hello! Am I interrupting a domestic dispute over ink? And is that the smell of impending risotto doom I detect? No dispute, just Mum being Mum. And yes, potential risotto catastrophe is a distinct possibility. This is Clara, by the way. Clara, this is my mum, Helen. Lovely to meet you, Clara. So glad you could make it. Help yourself to a glass of wine while we wrestle with Italian cuisine. Don’t mind if I do. Right, burn-prevention duty aside, how are we all doing? Leo, heard any word about the internship applications? Actually, yeah. Got an email today. First round interview for the Tate Modern one. Next Thursday. Oh, Leo, that’s  fantastic ! The Tate! That's brilliant news. It is, yeah. Bit nervous, though. It’s pretty competitive. You’ll be amazing. You know your stuff. Speaking of competitive… Christmas. My sister already sent me a spreadsheet detailing gift preferences. A  spreadsheet , Helen. Oh, Brenda. She’s always been… organised. Are you doing Christmas at yours this year? I think so. But the office is  hellish  right now.

… honestly, the butternut squash risotto was a disaster. Utterly. I think I added too much stock too quickly, it just… dissolved. Like baby food. Oh dear. Risotto is  temperamental . Sounds like you needed a Nonna on hand, whispering Italian secrets. Don't worry, mine’s looking marginally safer. Though I did almost set off the smoke alarm trying to caramelise the onions. That sounds about right for you, actually. Always on the edge of culinary chaos. Honestly, I was aiming for something vaguely healthy after all those Christmas biscuits. I felt positively sluggish all week. You wouldn’t believe how many mince pies my Aunt Mildred insisted I take. She genuinely thinks I’m wasting away. Aunt Mildred. The woman who once tried to feed me a whole cream tea because I looked ‘pale’. She's a force of nature. Speaking of sluggish, I attempted a HIIT class yesterday. Attempted being the operative word. Oh no. Don’t tell me. Your knees? My everything. My knees, my hips, my dignity. The instructor was this incredibly fit… creature. Bounding around like a gazelle. And I was just… wheezing. I swear she said “feel the burn” at least ten times. I felt more like “feel the impending doom”. Honestly, I'm sticking to yoga. Gentle stretching and mindful breathing. That’s more my speed. See, I told you! You’re a yoga person through and through. I've been doing the Pilates classes at the community centre, and they're actually brilliant. Little bit more challenging than yoga, but low impact, so my back is grateful. Although, Mrs. Henderson wears  the  most incredible outfits. Bright lycra, headbands… it's a whole look. Oh, the activewear aficionados. They exist everywhere. It’s a tribe. I saw a woman in leggings with a full-length sequined cardigan at the supermarket this morning. Walking the dog. That's Birmingham for you. Only in Birmingham. Have you started planning that trip to Italy yet? You were talking about going to Puglia. I have! Finally booked the flights. April. Can you believe it? I'm so excited. I’m thinking of doing a bit of a food tour – truffle hunting, pasta making, the whole shebang. I’ve been brushing up on my Italian, which is… rusty, to say the least. That sounds absolutely amazing! You'll have to send me pictures. And bring back some olive oil. Proper, authentic olive oil.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking is just… draining. I feel like all I  do  is read essays about the socio-economic impact of the Opium Wars. It's fascinating, truly, but relentless. How was your afternoon with the first years? Still battling the existential dread of referencing? You know it. Apparently, Wikipedia isn’t considered a ‘scholarly source’. The shock! Honestly, you’d think they’d never used the internet before. It’s like teaching them to breathe, sometimes. Though, little Mei-Lin asked a really insightful question about the power dynamics in 19th century trade. A bright spark, that one. Much brighter than… well, never mind. Oh? Do tell. Was it another ‘my uncle said’ contribution to the discussion? You know, the ones where historical fact goes to die a horrible death? Worse. He tried to argue that colonialism was  beneficial  because it brought… roads. Roads, Amelia! Like that justifies everything. I nearly lost it. I had to take a deep breath and steer it back to the devastation caused, the exploitation… the whole point of the lecture! It’s exhausting. It really is. You need to develop a thicker skin, darling. Or a particularly withering stare. Mine seems to work reasonably well. Though, occasionally, they just look confused, which is almost worse. I’m working on the stare. It needs… refinement. It's more ‘mildly disappointed’ than ‘fear-inducing academic authority’ at the moment. Anyway, enough shop talk. How are  you  holding up? You seemed a bit distracted at lunch. Just thinking about Sarah, actually. I haven’t heard from her in ages. Her mum wasn’t well last I heard, and… well, you know how she is. Keeps herself to herself when things get tough. I tried to text her this morning, just a ‘thinking of you’ message, but nothing back. That’s… typical Sarah. She's a fortress, isn’t she? Always has been. Remember that awful breakup she had with James at university? She completely disappeared for a month. Only resurfaced when she’d practically mastered origami just to avoid human contact. Oh god, yes! The origami! She turned our flat into a paper crane sanctuary. That was… a time. It’s just, I worry about her. She’s always been so fiercely independent, it's hard to know when she genuinely needs help. She knows you’re there, Amelia. She always has. And she'll reach out when she's ready.

… honestly, the CGI in the new  Dune  was just breathtaking. But it felt… cold. Like spectacle over substance, you know? Paul Atreides just didn’t  feel  real enough, despite Timothée Chalamet being… well, Timothée Chalamet. Cold’s a good word, actually. That’s exactly it. Villeneuve is all style, isn’t he? Brilliant visuals, makes everything  look  amazing, but you’re not emotionally invested. I mean, I read the book when I was a kid. I  felt  the desert, the fear, the weight of the prophecy. Film just didn’t deliver that. Speaking of delivering… have you seen what’s happened with that Russell Brand thing? Ugh, don’t even get me started. It's horrifying. Absolutely horrifying. The allegations… it’s just… I feel incredibly uncomfortable even talking about it, knowing how much influence he had. It’s a bit of a kick in the teeth, isn’t it? He positioned himself as this anti-establishment figure, and then… this. It makes you question everything. Makes you wonder what else is lurking under the surface, doesn’t it? It’s a bit like those QAnon types, always looking for the ‘truth’ behind the truth. I was talking to Dave at work about it yesterday. He’s proper down the rabbit hole with that stuff. Keeps telling me the government are putting chemicals in the chemtrails. Oh, Dave. Bless him. Honestly, the things people believe. It’s frightening. It must be incredibly isolating, living in that mindset. Though I suppose it provides a sense of control. My brother, he’s always been a bit of a conspiracy theorist. Nothing as extreme as chemtrails, thankfully, but always questioning everything. It's probably the effect of growing up with Dad, always doubting authority. Sounds familiar. My old man was a trade union man, always fighting the system. Probably rubbed off on me a bit. Though I’m more likely to fight it with a good business plan these days! How’s the teaching going, by the way? Still wrangling teenagers with their grammar? Oh, you know. The grammar battles are eternal. Though actually, I’ve got a really promising group of Year 10s this year. They actually  want  to learn, which is a shock to the system. We're doing Shakespeare at the moment, and they're surprisingly into it. Though one of them keeps trying to convince me  Hamlet  is actually a time traveller.

...Honestly, Dad, I still think it's weird they filmed  Jamaica Inn  up on Bodmin Moor. It just…feels wrong. Like a glamorous hotel shouldn’t be clinging to a bleak, windswept hill. Doesn’t fit, does it?      Aye, it does look a bit out of place, doesn’t it? Daphne du Maurier, she really captured that wildness though. A properly gloomy moor, that. Reminds me a bit of when we went to the Lake District. Though there weren’t any smugglers, thankfully. Look at the gorse, though! Proper yellow, isn’t it? Brightens things up, even on a grey day like this.      It  is  a good colour. Though it looks a bit…aggressive, doesn't it? Like everything’s shouting at you. It’s nothing like the Emerald City in  Wizard of Oz . Everything was so… curated. Perfect.      Curated? That’s a fancy word for an eleven o’clock film, love. You’ve been reading too much for school. Speaking of reading, have you started that Sherlock Holmes anthology Mrs. Davies set you?      Halfway through ‘The Speckled Band’. It's good! But the language is… dense. It’s not like modern stuff. It's almost like Lewis Carroll, all winding sentences and hidden meanings.      Aye, Victorian writers were a different breed. Proper wordsmiths, though. They didn’t have texts or anything back then. Imagine trying to solve a case sending telegrams! Can you picture Holmes dictating a message to Watson, tapping it out in Morse code?      Morse code! Gran showed me that once. It's clever, but I couldn't get the hang of it. It’s so… tactile, isn’t it? Like braille. It's amazing people can  read  with their fingers.      It is. Human ingenuity, that. It makes you think, doesn't it? All these ways of communicating throughout history. From smoke signals to instant messaging. You know, your Great-Grandad used to work with the Post Office. He was a telegraph operator. Said the clicking of the telegraph was like a second heartbeat.      Wow. That's cool. Are we nearly there yet? My legs are getting proper numb.      Not for another couple of hours, sadly. We've still got Devon to get through. Have you checked the directions again on your phone? Signal's been patchy.      Yeah, it's good. Says we need to take the A30 after Exeter. Apparently, there's a really scenic route through Dartmoor, but it’s slow.

…Aye, well, that’s what I mean, like. Grandad, you were saying earlier about petrol stations bein’ different when you were a lad. Did they actually  have  self-service back then? 'Cos it feels like that's a relatively new thing, doesn't it? And the prices... honestly, I nearly fainted last week fillin' up the Fiesta. Self-service? Lad, in my day, you didn't get  any  service unless you wanted it! You pulled up, a lad in overalls came out, wiped your windscreen – even if it didn't need it, mind you, that was part of the show – filled ‘er up, checked the oil and water, and you paid him inside. A full service! Sixpence, maybe a shilling, depending on how much you needed. And the petrol… cheaper than a pint of milk nowadays, I reckon. Though, mind you, a pint of milk wasn't much to speak of even  then . It’s almost unbelievable, isn’t it? Everything’s automated now. My work’s actually involved optimising petrol station layouts for EV charging. It's completely changing the business model. They’re having to rethink everything from convenience stores to… well, not needing forecourt attendants anymore! See! Told you. It’s mad. It's like, what  did  folk do with all that time the attendants used to spend just… standin' there? Did they chat? Chat? Oh aye, they chatted. All the local gossip. Every bloke in Timperley knew everything about everyone else by the time they’d paid for their petrol. Used to be a cinema right next to the station too, The Regal. Tuppence entry on a Tuesday. Now they want fourteen quid a ticket, it’s daylight robbery! Right? My mum was saying the same thing. Took my little cousin to see the new Marvel film, and it was basically a mortgage payment. It feels like everything's just… going up. Even rent. I'm lucky I can live with my parents still while I save. Aye, rent's a killer. I’m back in Sunderland for now, thankfully, so it’s a  bit  easier, but even there it's climb’in. Reminds me, Mam always says Mrs. Henderson down the street used to teach her geography. Remember how strict she was, Grandad? Apparently, she made everyone learn all the county towns. Old Mrs. Henderson! A fearsome woman. She used to tell us stories about the war, you know.

… honestly, Mum, I’m still adjusting to the time difference. Woke up at four this morning convinced I’d slept in for work. Total jet lag brain. Did you manage to get hold of Auntie Carol about the wedding guest list? Oh, love, you poor thing. Four o’clock! No wonder you look a bit… faded. And yes, Carol called. She’s being  very  particular about who gets a plus one. Apparently, cousin Brenda is demanding her pottery instructor comes, and Carol’s put her foot down. Honestly, the drama. She says Brenda's already asked for a specific type of weaver fish to be served at the buffet. A  weaver fish ! Can you imagine? Brenda and her… eccentric tastes. A weaver fish? Seriously? She's trying to one-up everyone, isn't she? It's just a wedding, Mum, not a Michelin-star tasting menu. Though, speaking of, how's the catering going? You said you were looking at a few options? It is going, slowly. They’re all wanting deposits now, straight away. It's a nightmare. And they all want to know about dietary requirements – gluten-free, vegan, nut allergies… the list goes on. It’s exhausting. Which reminds me, about moving things out of the spare room… have you started making a proper list of what needs to go to the charity shop? I found a box of your old school books, ironically including your A-Level English Literature notes, and I’m trying to decide if anyone would actually want them. Oh gosh, those notes! Probably not. I was a rather chaotic student, if I remember. I’m happy to have a sort through tomorrow, if you like. I’ve got a free afternoon. The list… yeah, I’ve been meaning to. My head's a bit all over the place still. It's funny, isn't it? I haven’t lived at home properly since uni, yet it feels like yesterday I was raiding the fridge for biscuits at midnight. It  is  funny. You were a little scamp, always sneaking about. And your memory's good! I remember thinking I’d hidden those biscuits well. Everything seems to blur into one long… thing, doesn't it? I was talking to Margaret the other day - you remember Margaret from the library? - and we were trying to recall when we first met, and neither of us could quite place it.

… honestly, I just don’t get the point of all these fancy ferns. They’re  so  needy. Like, look at Brenda over there . She’s practically screaming for misting again. Whereas my snake plant, Stanley, he just…exists. Blissful, green existence. No drama. You’re projecting, love. Brenda just needs a little TLC. Like the NHS, really. Needs constant attention to function properly. Which, speaking of…did you see that report about the waiting lists? It’s…grim. Aye, grim is an understatement. It's ridiculous. My nan was saying she waited three months for a routine appointment. Three months! Back home, in Sunderland, it wasn’t  that  bad. Maybe a bit of a wait, but not…this. They’re always fiddling with things, aren’t they? Always "restructuring.” It just feels like they’re dismantling something that, while flawed,  worked  for most people. It’s the funding, isn’t it? The consistent underfunding. And these A-Level reforms… honestly, making everything so hyper-specialised so early. It’s going to create a cohort of students who are brilliant at one specific thing but completely lacking in broader understanding. Remember when everyone had to do General Studies? Oh, aye! I used to love General Studies. All those weird and wonderful topics. Nowadays, they're practically forcing them to pick their entire career path at 16. It’s mental. Like, what if they change their mind? I nearly ended up doing marine biology, can you imagine? All because of a really enthusiastic teacher in Year 9. Thankfully, stats won out, but still. Imagine you wrangling jellyfish instead of data. A very different trajectory. Speaking of different… what  is  going on with your hair? It’s… shorter. Again. I just fancied a change, alright? It was getting to here . It's easier, less fussy. Plus, it feels more…me. Like a proper Geordie lass, you know? Not trying to be something posh. You always were a proper Geordie lass, regardless of hair length. Though, I will admit, the long hair suited you. It was very…Rapunzel-esque. Which brings me to another point - did you fill the car up today? Ugh, don’t even. It cost me nearly seventy quid! Seventy quid for a full tank! It’s daylight robbery. This whole petrol crisis thing is a complete shambles. They keep saying it’s stabilising, but it doesn’t  feel  like it. They need to get a grip.

… honestly, I just don’t get why anyone  starts  smoking now. Like, we  know  the damage it does. Grandad’s cough is a right reminder, init? He’s barely able to walk up the stairs now. It's a bit different though, isn’t it, when it's a social thing? Everyone at uni seemed to take it up during Freshers'. It's just…convenient, I guess. A reason to step away from the library and chat. Conveniently kill yourself slowly? Nah, I’m good. I tried it once, felt dreadful. Plus, Yorkshire air is fresh enough as it is. Don’t need to pollute it further. Although, I'll admit, the smell  can  be…comforting sometimes. Odd, I know. Comforting? You’re joking, aye? It smells like an ashtray and regret. Seriously though, uni is stressful. Loads of people smoke to cope. It's easier than actually dealing with the pressure, I reckon. That’s why it’s so prevalent. I get the stress, definitely. Coursework's piling up already, and student finance is a joke. Seriously, £9,250 a year! For what? Lectures delivered via Zoom half the time? It's robbery. I'm working at the pub every weekend just to keep my head above water. Tell me about it. I’m interning at this law firm, unpaid, three days a week. They’re basically exploiting us, saying it’s “valuable experience.” Valuable experience doesn’t pay the rent, does it? I’m having to borrow from my mum. It's embarrassing. Unpaid internships are disgusting. Capitalism at its finest. I’m lucky, I’ve got a part-time job tutoring A-Level History. It's actually alright, and it's relevant to my degree. Though, explaining the Black Death to teenagers who’ve never experienced a real crisis is…challenging. They just don’t  get  the sheer scale of it. The Black Death, aye. Now  that  was a pandemic. Imagine, losing a third of the population. Makes worrying about a sniffle seem a bit silly, doesn’t it? Though, I do wonder if it inadvertently kickstarted some kind of feminist movement. All those men gone, women having to step up and run things… That's a good point, actually. It's funny how history always throws up connections you don’t expect. Makes you think about how things like Brexit, or even just…increased tuition fees…will affect things down the line.

…and honestly, the guilt was awful. Like, genuinely awful. I kept thinking, ‘She’ll  expect  me to be there for her hen do,’ and honestly, the thought just filled me with dread. Not because I didn’t want her to be happy, you understand. Just… not with  me  as a key participant. Ugh, I totally get that. It’s that pressure, isn’t it? The social obligation. It feels so much worse when it’s someone you’ve known for ages. It’s not like you can just block them on Facebook and be done with it. Exactly! And Sarah’s one of those people who doesn’t…read subtext. Not at all. She's very literal. So just implying I was busy wouldn't cut it. She’d pick up the phone and interrogate me about  what  I was busy doing. Oh god, the interrogation. I know that type. I had a friend at Uni, bless her, but she just needed… a lot. Like, constant reassurance, constant checking in. Eventually, I just started needing… space. It wasn’t anything she  did , exactly. Just… exhausting. It's not about them doing anything wrong! That’s what makes it so difficult to navigate. It's about  you  changing, wanting different things, different energy. With Sarah, we just... grew apart. We used to bond over really silly things – terrible reality TV, complaining about boys – and that just stopped being… relevant. So, how  did  you handle the hen do then? Did you just bite the bullet? No! No biting. I did the slow fade. It took months, honestly. Started with taking longer to reply to texts, genuinely apologising for being slammed at work – which sometimes was true, let's be honest. Then politely declining coffee, citing deadlines. Then, when the hen do invite came, I sent a lovely, heartfelt card, wishing her all the best, listing a prior commitment… a course I’d booked. A slightly exaggerated course. Slightly exaggerated? You’re a translator, you could probably invent an entire international conference! Tempting, but I kept it to a weekend pottery workshop. Seemed plausible. And the key was, I didn't offer alternatives. Didn’t say, ‘Oh, I can’t make the hen do, but let’s have lunch the week after!’ That just keeps the door open. That’s smart. I've always struggled with that. I end up feeling bad and offering alternatives I don't actually  want  to do.

… honestly, the library's a bit of a joke. They said they had all these resources for postgrad research, but half the journals are either missing or online access is perpetually down. It’s proper frustrating, innit? Especially with the dissertation looming. Oh, universities. Always promising the world, never quite delivering, are they? It was much the same when  I  was at the Academy, though admittedly, then it was more a matter of a lack of funding for materials, rather than faulty Wi-Fi. Though, I suppose a broken loom is much the same as a broken website in terms of impeding progress. A loom? You were studying textiles then? I always thought you just…  were  an artist, you know? Like it always existed. Goodness, no. My father insisted on a ‘proper’ education. He wasn’t keen on the idea of a daughter being a ‘bohemian’. Sculpture was the compromise. But textiles, yes, briefly. It demanded a precision I lacked, I think. Too controlling. I prefer the freedom of paint. Though, I often think about my grandmother, in Vienna. She was a  master  embroiderer. Such detail…absolutely breathtaking. We didn’t speak much, owing to the…well, the distance, both geographical and emotional, after the war. Right. Aunt Helga, was it? Mum mentioned she wasn’t…happy about leaving Vienna. “Unhappy” is a considerable understatement, darling. She felt utterly uprooted. Lost everything. She never truly forgave my father for taking her away, despite knowing it was to save her. It cast a long shadow. It's funny, isn’t it? How things from so long ago still ripple through generations. Speaking of families, how’s your cousin Leo doing? Last I heard he was thinking of moving up north. He did! To Manchester. He’s loving it. Says the music scene’s incredible, and rent’s… well, still expensive, but less mental than London. He’s doing graphic design now, you know. Turns out he’s brilliant at it. Mum sends me photos of his work constantly. It’s actually really good. That's wonderful to hear. He always had a creative spark. I remember him as a small boy, constantly drawing little monsters. You always were the sensible one, though. Head down, working hard. This dissertation - what's it on again? You’ve mentioned Baudrillard a few times. It’s about hyperreality and the influence of social media on political discourse.

...Honestly, the thought of a full meal before the gym just  fills  me with dread. It’s bad enough thinking about actually  going  to the gym, let alone feeling sluggish afterwards. A banana, maybe. A small banana.      You and your bananas, Auntie Pam. You've been saying that since I was little. Honestly, you need fuel, though. You’ll just end up feeling worse. I had a proper breakfast this morning – porridge with fruit and nuts. Felt brilliant for my spin class.      Brilliant for  your  spin class, darling. I’m not aiming for ‘brilliant’. I'm aiming for ‘not collapsing after ten minutes on a treadmill’. And frankly, this driving is strenuous enough. It's a mental gym, isn’t it? Negotiating Polish roads… it’s a workout in itself.      Right, because parallel parking this beast in Tarnow was  so  relaxing. You were practically vibrating with zen, I recall.      Don’t remind me. Honestly, I think half my life is spent waiting for someone to move their car. It's the time, isn't it? Everything takes so much… time. Getting anywhere. Doing anything. Back home, everything’s so… regimented.      Regimented? Cambridge is hardly the picture of regimentation, Pam.      Oh, don't be obtuse. Socially, it is! Expectations. Appointments. It’s a different pace. Here, things feel… looser. Which is nice, occasionally, even if it involves a lot of waiting. Speaking of the gym, I’m still not convinced it’s necessary.      We talked about this! You said you wanted to feel stronger after your back pain. And you do enjoy a good swim, don't you?      I enjoy  thinking  about a good swim. The actual getting there, getting changed, encountering… people… It’s all rather fraught. And the changing rooms! Honestly. It's always the same.      What's always the same?      The…  atmosphere . Young men flexing, staring. It’s just… uncomfortable. It always feels a bit performative, doesn’t it? Like you have to be 'seen' to be working out. It feels very… male-focused.      That’s a good point, actually. They are often geared towards that. Though, loads of gyms are trying to be more inclusive now. More female-only classes, things like that. It's slowly changing, I think. But yeah, it’s a really valid observation. It’s like they assume women want to be… subtly assessed.      Exactly! And the unspoken judgements. It’s just exhausting. It’s not about being ‘strong’, it’s about navigating the social landscape  while  trying to be strong.

…and honestly, the handle on that one’s just  perfect . Not too chunky, not too delicate. Proper hand-thrown, you know? Not like those mass-produced things you get in supermarkets. It just  feels  right in your hand. Aye, it does. A good mug’s a treasure, lass. Reminds me of old Mrs. Hinchliffe. She had a collection, she did. Every one with a story. Though mostly the stories were about how much milk she put in hers. She’d drown it, she would. A proper swimming pool for a biscuit. Oh, bless her. She was a character. Speaking of milk, are we running low? I think I used the last in me coffee. I’ll have a look, dear. Seems like only yesterday I was getting a delivery. This weather… it’s been funny, hasn’t it? Sun one minute, threatening rain the next. Not proper weather for gardening, is it? Though you’re out there regardless. Well, someone’s got to tackle the weeds! They’re gaining ground, honestly. The courgettes are doing surprisingly well though, despite everything. And the tomatoes are starting to blush. Hopefully, we’ll have enough for chutney this year. Chutney’s lovely. Though I always worry about spiders getting in the jars. Little blighters. I found one in the bathroom this morning, big as me thumb it was! Nearly gave me heart failure. Oh, don’t! I hate spiders. You know I do. Though, I have to admit, they do their bit for the garden. Keeps the greenfly at bay, doesn’t it? It’s a balance. Like everything. A balance, aye. Though I’d happily tip the scales in favour of spider-lessness. Remember when young Timmy fell off that step ladder trying to clean the guttering? Oh, goodness, yes. Scared the life out of us both. He was so adamant he could do it himself. “I’m a man now, Aunty Carol!” he said. A man with a badly sprained wrist! He was always a stubborn lad. Still is, I reckon. Heard he's helping organise that Bradford Festival this year. The one with the music and the stalls. He is! He’s throwing himself into it. Says it’s good for the community. I’m glad he's got something to occupy him. He’s a good lad, Timmy. He is. Just like his mother. I’ve been meaning to ask… did you ever get round to putting up those shelves in the hallway?

…and honestly, Mum, I don’t  care  if Auntie Carol says Cornwall is ‘proper British’. It’s always raining there! Can’t we just… go somewhere with sun? Like, Spain or Greece? Now, Lily, we’ve been over this. Cornwall is lovely, and your Aunt Carol did offer us her cottage for a very good price. It would mean we could all go, including your Grandad, without breaking the bank. Aye, breaking the bank’s not on the cards, is it? Though a bit o’ sunshine  would  be nice. My bones ache enough as it is without getting a soaking in a drizzle. I’m not expecting the Bahamas, mind, just… a bit less grey. But Grandad, you said last week you were looking forward to walking the coastal path! Isn't that, like, famously windy in Cornwall? You'll lose your hat! I have a few hats, lass. And a head for a bit o’ wind. It’s the damp that gets to me. Still, Carol’s cottage  is  a good offer. Access for the old legs is important, you know. Exactly! And think of the cream teas, Lily. Proper Cornish cream teas. They’re a tradition. Ugh, cream teas. They’re just…scones and jam. I’d rather have churros. Or gyros. You and your exotic tastes. We haven’t even talked about who we could invite. Carol was suggesting her friend Margaret and her grandson, Thomas. Thomas? The one who collects beetles? No way. He tried to make me hold a stag beetle last summer. It was horrifying. Now, now, Lily, be polite. He’s just a lad with a hobby. A bit unusual, maybe, but harmless. Harmless?! It had pincers! And it felt… crunchy. I’d rather spend the week with Mrs. Higgins from school. At least she only talks about cats. Mrs. Higgins… that’s a thought! Maybe not. Look, we want everyone to enjoy the holiday. Perhaps we could compromise? Cornwall for a week, then maybe a few days in a warmer place? Although, practically speaking, that's tricky with Grandad and the cottage… Hold on, hold on. A few days in Spain… that's not a bad idea. There’s a little town not far from Malaga – Nerja, it’s called – I played there once, years ago. Decent fish and chips, surprisingly. Bit of sun, a nice beach… Really? Fish and chips in Spain?

…and honestly, the whole thing with Joey Donner being  so  oblivious just made me laugh every time. Like, he genuinely thought Kat would fall for him just because he was ‘popular’ and had a modelling career. It's ridiculous! Totally! He was a bit of a prat, wasn’t he? But Heath Ledger…oh my god, Heath Ledger was  amazing . I’ve decided I now have a thing for guys who write poetry. Even really bad poetry. Oh, don’t go starting that now, you’ll be writing sonnets to Mr. Henderson in History! Speaking of which… History is  killing  me. That test on the Tudors is going to be the death of me. I just can’t remember all the Henrys and their wives. It’s just…names and beheadings. Tell me about it. I’m proper stressing. I keep getting Elizabeth I mixed up with Mary Queen of Scots. It’s a disaster. Miss Davies will have my head. Have you started revising yet, or are you leaving it to the last minute like me? Last minute, naturally. It’s my special talent. Procrastination. My mum keeps saying I need to be more organised, but honestly, it feels so much better to leave it all until the pressure’s on. Gives it…flavour, you know? Flavour? That's… an interesting way to put it. My nan keeps telling me I need to start thinking about GCSE options. It’s so far off, though! It feels weird having to decide things now that are going to affect the rest of our lives. I know, right? It’s terrifying. Everyone’s talking about A-Levels and universities. I haven’t even properly thought about what I  like  doing, let alone what career I might want. Though… remember when we were little and all we wanted to be was vets? Oh god, yes! And we’d try to ‘operate’ on your nan’s cats with plasters and Sellotape. She wasn't impressed. She  definitely  wasn’t. Good times. Anyway, speaking of planning things… have you spoken to your mum about the London trip yet? I was thinking we could go during half term? I have! She said maybe if we both get good results on these awful Tudor tests. Typical, isn't it? Always a bribe. But yeah, she's up for it. I was thinking we could go see that musical,  Wicked ?

…and honestly, the amount of misinformation on there is just… exhausting. I had a student genuinely ask me if 5G caused the pandemic, because of something they’d seen on Facebook! Facebook, eh? Still can’t get me ‘ead around it. All that lookin’ at pictures o’ folks you haven't seen in fifty year. Seems a right waste o’ time to me. Though, Doris showed me a picture o’ little Elsie the other day – your cousin, isn’t she? - lookin’ like a right little angel. That was nice. Elsie’s lovely, isn’t she? She’s putting pictures up of her garden. All those flowers…makes a change from all the political arguing, doesn’t it? Though, I do keep an eye on what Margaret’s up to. Makes you wonder sometimes, the things people post. It's designed to be addictive, isn't it? The algorithms prioritize engagement, and outrage gets engagement. It’s a really clever, and somewhat sinister, system. Algorithms…Cor! Sounds complicated. Back in my day, you just spoke to people. Face to face. None o’ this…internet malarkey. Mind you, I never  worked , so I didn’t need to keep up with things, did I? Just pottered about. Though, I did ‘ave a bit o’ a… a thing, about things bein’ just so. All lined up. Oh? Like what, Grandad? Oh, everything. Cans in the cupboard, all the labels facin’ forwards. Shoes in a neat row. If something were…out of place, it’d bother me all day. Couldn’t rest 'til it were right. Mother said I were a fussy boy. That sounds a little bit like obsessive-compulsive tendencies, actually. OCD. It’s a recognised anxiety disorder. It’s about intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviours to alleviate distress. OCD? Fancy that. Never thought there was a  name  for it. Just thought I were… particular. It weren’t so bad, though. Just a little twitch. Now, young Stephen next door, 'e had a proper bad one. Always washin’ his ‘ands. Got ‘em raw as anything. Poor Stephen. Remember when all the children had chickenpox? That was a nightmare. Every single one of them, peeling and itching. I was covered in calamine lotion most weeks! They used to say you needed to get it young to get it over with. It’s still around, though vaccination helps. It's amazing how quickly things change medically.

…and honestly, the German just baffled me. I mean, I  tried  to learn a bit before we went, Duolingo and all that, but it just wouldn’t stick. It’s not like French, is it? A little bit familiar. This was just… guttural. Guttural’s a good word for it, Karen. I’ve always said German sounds like someone clearing their throat for five minutes straight. Dad, you say that about every language that isn’t English! Remember when you tried to order a coffee in Italy and just pointed at a picture? Now, that's a slight exaggeration, Amelia. I managed a "caffè, please," thank you very much. Though the barista did look at me like I’d sprouted a second head. Anyway, Germany was lovely. Bit clinical, maybe, but very efficient. Efficient. That's putting it mildly. They run like clockwork, don't they? Reminds me a bit of your Auntie Maggie, actually. Everything meticulously planned. Oh, goodness yes! Maggie and her spreadsheets. Speaking of meticulous planning, whose turn is it to do the roast next week? I did it last month, and honestly, I’m knackered as it is with the shifts at the hospital. I could do it, Karen. I’m free. Though, I'm warning you, it won’t be as fancy as yours. I’m more of a ‘chuck it all in and hope for the best’ kind of cook. No harm in that, Chloe. Good honest cooking. Though, we all benefit from Karen’s culinary skills, that’s for sure. Remember that Christmas dinner she did, the one where everything was perfectly timed? I remember because I was tasked with carving the turkey and nearly took a finger off! That bird was massive. And Dad kept commenting on how “brown” everything was. Honestly, it felt like being graded on my plate presentation. I just appreciate a good, well-cooked roast! It’s a tradition, isn’t it? Reminds me of me own dad, actually. He had a real thing for cars. Used to spend hours polishing his old Austin Cambridge. Ah, the Cambridge. Solid motor. Remember those? Everything was built to last back then, unlike these plastic boxes they build now. I had a Ford Anglia, lovely little thing. Though, it did leak like a sieve when it rained. Leaky cars and meticulous planning… sounds about right for our family, doesn't it? I remember Mum trying to pack for a holiday.

… honestly, the sound on the recording just doesn’t do it justice. They’re  so  much tighter live. The energy is…well, it’s a different beast altogether, innit? Like, you can  feel  the bass vibrating through your chest. Yeah, I get you. Albums are polished, obviously, but they lose something. It’s always the raw energy, isn’t it? Especially with a band like Static Bloom. Proper mosh pit material. Did you see Ben at the gig? Ben? Nah, he messaged saying he was stuck at work. Something about a double shift at the pub. Poor bloke. He's forever stuck behind the bar. You go with anyone else? Just Liam and Chloe. She was loving it, though she mostly just stood back and filmed everything on her phone, typical. Liam was right in the thick of it, nearly lost a shoe. He's a proper adrenaline junkie, that one. Speaking of which, how’s the drumming coming along? Still bashing the skins in your parents’ garage? Still is, yeah. Though Dad’s been giving me  looks . Says it’s “structurally unsound” now. He secretly loves it, though. I’ve been trying to work on some more complex fills, actually. Trying to get past just the basic rock stuff, you know? Been listening to a lot of Gavin Harrison – Porcupine Tree, obviously – trying to dissect his playing. It's… humbling. Gavin Harrison’s a god. Proper technical wizardry. I tried to learn a bit of drumming years ago, but realised I had absolutely zero coordination. I’m much better at wielding a knife than drumsticks, apparently. How’s the degree going, by the way? Still firmly planted in the world of theoretical physics? Still slogging through it, yeah. It’s… challenging. Honestly, I’m starting to doubt whether I actually want to  do  this as a career. It feels so… abstract. Like, I’m learning about things that won’t matter in five years. That’s rough. It’s good you're thinking about it now though, better than getting halfway through a PhD and realising you hate it. Remember Mark? He did that with history. Now he's selling insurance. Exactly! It’s terrifying. I was thinking about maybe applying for some internships over the summer. Something… practical. Thought about maybe trying to get into a recording studio, see if I can get some experience with the sound engineering side of things.

…Honestly, lad, I just think Old Man Hemmings is getting a bit too keen on the loyalty scheme. Three coffees, get a biscuit? It’s hardly revolutionary, is it? And the way he was shouting it through the drive-through window…you could hear him in Durham!      Mmm, biscuit sounds good though. Were there loads of people in the drive-through? I saw a fancy car, a red one.      Loads! It was chaotic. And yes, a red sports car. Probably some southerner lost. They never know their way around up here. And shouting about biscuits… honestly. It’s not Newcastle, is it? People don’t  shout  here.      Maybe he’s trying to be like those American coffee places on TikTok. All bright colours and shouting.      TikTok? Don't start on that TikTok, young man. It'll rot your brain. Anyway, listen. About the summer holiday… I was thinking, instead of just another week at grandma’s, maybe we could do something… different. Remember when we went to Durham Cathedral last year? You seemed to enjoy that.      Yeah, it was cool. The cloisters were spooky. And that shop had amazing Lego.      Exactly. We could spend a few days there. Maybe a bit of walking, a bit of history, and I promise we’ll find a Lego shop. But we’d need to book something quickly. And… beds. We’d need sleeping bags, wouldn’t we? Or a proper bed, depending on where we end up. I need to make a list. I’ve got that shopping list for the house, but this needs to be separate.      Sleeping bags are good. More adventurous. You think we’d need a tent?      Oh, no, no tent. I’m not wrestling with tent poles at my age. Let’s stick to a B&B or something similar. Speaking of lists, did you remember to text your dad about the domino drive on Friday?      Oh! No! Completely forgot. Sorry. He'll be proper annoyed. He’s been practicing his blocking all week.      He has! He's taking it awfully seriously. I swear, he thinks he's running a business. He’s constantly talking about ‘market penetration’ and ‘customer loyalty’ when all he’s doing is shuffling dominoes with old Mr. Bailey and Mrs. Peterson. Honestly, he’d be a terrible entrepreneur.      He just likes winning. And showing off. Did you see the football last night?      Don’t even mention it.

…and honestly, the audio quality on that recording is  terrible . I spent ages getting Mrs. Kim to repeat the minimal pairs, and all you get is this muffled ‘ship’ versus ‘sheep’ that sounds exactly the same! It’s frustrating because their pronunciation  is  improving, they just need clear examples for them to mimic. Sounds about right. Teaching’s never dull, is it? Still, at least you’re doing something you enjoy. Beats staring at spreadsheets all day, trust me. How’s Sussex treating you, by the way? Settled in alright? This flat’s nice, a lot bigger than I imagined. Yeah, it's growing on me. Still feels a bit…empty, you know? Lots of unpacking still to do. It's a proper adult flat, which is terrifying. Speaking of adulting, Liam and Sarah… they're actually having a baby. No way! Seriously? Liam, the one who used to live on noodles and Red Bull during finals? That's mental. Congratulations to them, though. When did that happen? I haven’t seen them since… well, graduation, I guess. Found out last week. Sarah posted a scan picture. They're over the moon. It makes you think, doesn’t it? About, you know… the future. They’re talking about getting married next year too. Wow, they're really going for it. Marriage… bit of a commitment, isn’t it? Have you thought much about that sort of thing? Not seriously. It's tempting to scroll through Rightmove looking at houses with gardens, though. Especially when I’m filling in all these forms for council tax and utilities. Honestly, the bureaucracy here is a nightmare. Back in Bedford, things were simpler. It's just... everything's so expensive. The cost of living down here is ridiculous. Tell me about it. I'm lucky with my job, the salary is decent, but even  I  wince at the supermarket bills sometimes. We were talking about joint bank accounts at work the other day, for couples sharing expenses. Sounds… sensible, but a bit scary. Very scary. Too sensible. Speaking of sensible, remember old Mr. Davies from university? Apparently he's living in South Korea now, teaching English. Said it's amazing. No! Really? That’s brilliant. He always had that adventurous streak. I always figured he'd end up doing something left-field. I nearly went abroad myself, considered a year teaching in Spain after uni but panicked about the language barrier.

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, isn’t it? Not being able to  do  anything. Just… watching. It feels so fundamentally wrong. It absolutely is. It's that helplessness, that inability to fix things, even though logically you  know  you can’t. With Mum, it was the same. You spend your life thinking you’ll protect your parents, and then… then they're needing  you  to just… be there while things fall apart. Exactly! And she was so stoic, your Mum. Always. Remember how she dealt with Dad’s heart scare? Barely batted an eyelid. But this… this cancer just seemed to… strip everything away. It’s just not fair. No, it’s not. And it’s easy to fall into the trap of ‘what ifs’, isn’t it? Should we have pushed for a second opinion sooner? Should we have noticed something earlier? Though, realistically, with pancreatic cancer… it’s so sneaky. Don’t do that to yourself, Sarah. You did everything you could. We all did. And David… well, he was brave. So incredibly brave. I keep replaying that last conversation, trying to remember everything he said. It’s hazy, though. All emotions and very little… concrete. It will be. Trauma does that. My brain did a similar thing with Mum. It protects you, I think. Blocks out some of the sharpest edges. How are the kids coping? Leo’s taking it particularly hard, isn’t he? He is. He’s mostly withdrawn. Just… quiet. Apparently, he told Mrs. Davies at school he feels like his ‘safe place’ has been taken away. Breaks your heart, doesn’t it? Ellie’s being… practical. Organising photos, talking about memories. She's always been the strong one. I think she's trying to hold it together for Leo, and for me. That’s Ellie. A little mini-me, always capable. But don’t let her  be  everything for you, Anna. You need to lean on people. On me. That’s what friends are for. You haven’t been yourself since… well, since the diagnosis really. You’re hiding it, but I can see it. I know, I know. It's just… work is piling up, the house is a mess, and then there's the kids... I feel like I'm failing at everything. I even messed up a proofing job last week! A  proofing  job, Sarah! It’s humiliating. Oh, Anna.

…and honestly, the amount of homework they’re setting now is just ridiculous. It's not quality time, it’s just…volume. Are you getting buried, Leo? Nah, not  buried , Mum. It's alright. History is a bit heavy though. We’re doing the Reformation, and Mr. Davies just…talks  at  you for an hour. No breaks. Sounds familiar. University lectures were often the same. Endless monologue. Though, to be fair, the Reformation  is  a lot. My history teacher makes us do debates. It’s way better. Last week we had to argue for or against Henry VIII. I was Henry, obviously. Got to wear a crown! See,  that  sounds engaging, doesn't it, Leo? Maybe you should suggest debates to Mr. Davies. Though knowing him… unlikely. Anyway, how's tennis going, both of you? Leo, you had a match yesterday, didn’t you? Yeah. Lost. Again. This kid, Finn, is just… he's on another level. He's got coaching, proper coaching. I just get a bit of advice from Dad between sets. It’s not the same. Now, now. Don't be too hard on yourself. Finn’s parents are really pushing him, I know. He's aiming for county level. You’re playing for fun, aren’t you? I  want  to be good, Dad. It’s just frustrating. I feel like I’m hitting a wall. We could look into some coaching sessions for you, darling. There’s that new coach at Lichfield Tennis Club, Sarah Miller, she comes highly recommended. It wouldn’t break the bank, and it might just give you that little bit of focus you need. I’d like some lessons. My serve’s rubbish. Although, I’m more into football, really. Got a game on Saturday. That's excellent, Ben. Though, honestly, I’m starting to worry about the future a bit. All this… uncertainty. Did anyone see that article about the proposed changes to apprenticeships? It's all a bit murky. Oh, don't get me started on the referendum fallout. It feels like everything is constantly shifting. And these apprenticeship changes are concerning. Honestly, I'm worried about what opportunities will be available for you two when you're older. University isn’t the only path, you know. I’ve been thinking, maybe even looking at some small business opportunities…something I can invest in alongside the marketing, give us a bit more security.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of shellfish they were pulling up was just… unsettling. It felt greedy, even then, knowing it couldn’t possibly be sustainable. You remember the Morecambe Bay cockle disaster, right? 2004? Vaguely. Wasn’t that… really bad? I think I remember something on the news about people illegally harvesting and then, like, a sudden tidal surge? Yeah, that was it. Twenty-three Chinese cockle pickers drowned. It was awful. And it all stemmed from this insatiable demand. Makes you think twice about that portion of cockles with your fish and chips, doesn’t it? Definitely. Although, to be fair, a good portion of fish and chips  is  non-negotiable when we’re heading to the coast. Lancaster isn’t exactly known for its exotic cuisine, is it? No, it is not. Though I’m hoping your Aunt Carol will whip up something lovely. She’s a phenomenal cook, even if her tastes  are  a bit… traditional. I'm mostly excited for a break, honestly. This dissertation is slowly breaking me. Tell me about it! How's the data coming along? Still wading through endless transcriptions? Endless is an understatement. I’m at the stage where I’m starting to dream in phonemes. Honestly, sometimes I think I’d rather  be  a phoneme than analyse them. It’s the semantic analysis that’s really killing me, though. Trying to find nuanced meaning in hours of conversational data... it's brutal. Are you feeling alright about your bits for the project? Yeah, I’m okay. The logistical side is pretty firmly under control, thankfully. Getting access to participants hasn't been too problematic, which is a relief. It’s just… feeling a bit lost about what I want to  do  with all this afterwards. This job's great, don’t get me wrong, but is it a career? Is it  enough ? That's a good question. I’ve been asking myself the exact same thing. I love the research, the linguistics itself, but the constant short-term contracts… it's exhausting. I’m thinking maybe a Masters after this? Something a bit more focused, perhaps forensic linguistics. Forensic linguistics! That actually sounds amazing. A bit  CSI , but with words. Exactly! Though realistically, it'd probably involve a lot more interviewing than glamorous crime scene investigation. My mum keeps suggesting I come home and teach. She thinks my brother's influence is rubbing off on me with this "research lark".

…Nah, I’m tellin’ ya, ‘Spectre’ were  way  better live. Proper energy, y’know? Like, you could feel the bass thumpin’ in yer chest the whole time. Did you see ‘em at the Leadmill last month? Aye, I did. It were good, I’ll grant ya that. But a bit… chaotic, weren’t it? Liam kept knockin’ over his amp and Sarah nearly got trampled when the mosh pit started. I preferred ‘em when they played at The Red Lion, more intimate, less… organised chaos. Organised chaos is  their  brand, lad! That’s what makes ‘em good! It’s not supposed to be pristine, it’s supposed to be a right good ruck. Anyway, speaking of chaotic, how’s your little brother, Alfie? Still obsessed with buildin’ those Lego spaceships? You know it. He spent all weekend buildin’ a Millennium Falcon. Mum says the living room’s a minefield. He’s proper dedicated, though. Says he wants to be an aerospace engineer. Bit ambitious for a ten-year-old, innit? Nah, good on him! Better than spendin’ his time glued to TikTok like half the kids his age. I’m still tryin’ to get my head around TikTok, honestly. It's all just… dances, isn't it? Mostly. Though I saw Old Man Hemmings doin’ a duet on there the other day. Scared the life out of me. It's a weird place. What about your pottery? Still muckin’ about with clay? Oh aye. I’ve started a new course at the community centre, wheel throwin’ this time. It’s considerably harder than hand buildin’, let me tell ya. Nearly lost a whole pot this morning – it just collapsed in on itself. Looked like a sad, muddy blob. Sounds about right. You always were a bit of a perfectionist. Remember when you spent a week re-paintin’ that birdhouse for Grandad? Don’t remind me! He barely noticed! He just put it up next to the shed and a pigeon promptly… well, you know. Still, I enjoy it. It’s just… therapeutic, y’know? Better than stressin’ about uni applications. Tell me about it. I still haven't properly started my personal statement. Just starin’ at a blank page. I'm thinkin’ of just writin’ about how much I love chippy tea. Is that too cliché?  Definitely  too cliché! Though, to be fair, a good chippy tea  is  a valid life goal. Seriously though, think about what you actually want to do.

Right, okay, so  clearly  my plans for containing the black disease in South America were flawed. Rhys, you just waltzed right through with three cubes already! Honestly, it's like you  want  to see the world end.      Now, now, Sarah. It’s just a game. A very stressful game, admittedly. But a game nonetheless. I had a good hand, see? And a little bit of luck. Plus, you were distracted trying to build your research station in Atlanta.      Distracted? She was practically building a second home in Atlanta! You'd think she  wanted  to get infested. Honestly, Sarah, you're a teacher, you should be strategizing, not choosing locations based on… what  was  it, again? Good coffee shops?      Don't be ridiculous, Ben. It was geographically central! And there’s a higher concentration of research grants in the southeast, logically. I was thinking long-term containment strategy! Anyway, it didn’t work.      You’re putting too much pressure on yourself, Sarah. It's meant to be fun. Remember last year when Dad nearly flipped the table because the eradication counter was dropping?      Ah, now  that  was a night. I was convinced young Ieuan was deliberately sabotaging us by hoarding event cards. He was only eight at the time! Little rascal. Though, in my defence, I  did  have two outbreaks happening simultaneously. Singapore prepared me for logistical nightmares, but not this!      Right, let’s not rehash past Pandemic trauma. We need a plan. Sarah, maybe you should focus on Asia this turn? It’s relatively clear at the moment. And Rhys, put down the blue cubes for five minutes and  think  before you move!      Oi! I’m thinking! I’m thinking about global domination… I mean, disease eradication. Similar skill sets, really. Honestly, action is better than overplanning. You scientists always want to analyse everything to death.      “Scientists”? I teach history, Rhys.  History . And it teaches you that hasty decisions generally lead to disaster. Like, say, ignoring the rampant spread of a rapidly mutating virus.      She's got you there, mate. Though, in fairness, I'm more of a containment-through-delicious-food kind of guy. If everyone was well-fed, they’d be too happy to get sick. Problem solved!      That’s…an interesting theory, Ben.      There’s something to be said for morale, I’ll grant you that. During the SARS outbreak in Singapore, the hawker centres stayed open, and that really helped.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the CBeebies panto this year was just  brilliant . Did you two manage to catch much of it? The costumes were incredible! I loved the dragon! It breathed  sparkles  Mummy! And Justin Fletcher was a princess! Yeah, and Mr. Tumble was the… the evil wizard! He kept trying to steal the magic berries. He did, didn’t he? He’s so good at being silly. It got me thinking though, about Leo’s birthday. It’s creeping up, isn’t it? Middle of July. What are you thinking, darling? A proper party this year, or something a bit more low-key? A party! With a bouncy castle! And cake! A really,  really  big cake! With superheroes! Can we have a superhero party? And pin the cape on Spider-Man? A superhero party sounds good. We can definitely do superheroes. A bouncy castle… hmm. Space might be a bit tight in the garden, even with moving the garden furniture. We could look at hiring a hall again, like we did for Maisie’s fifth. Ooh, the hall had more space for dancing! It did. And we could have face painting. Remember how much you liked that, Maisie? Although, you insisted on being painted entirely blue… Blue’s a good colour! Like the Bluey characters! They're awesome! Do you think Bluey would come to  my  party? Oh, I doubt Bluey is available for children’s parties, sweetie. But we can get some Bluey decorations, how about that? And we can watch episodes. Speaking of CBeebies, have you seen that new story they’re doing about the little penguin who lost his way? It’s really sweet. The one with the sparkly ice? I watched it! He found his mummy at the end! You did! You have a good memory. It reminds me of that saying, doesn't it? "Lost and found." My Nan used to say that all the time. Though she'd usually be referring to her glasses! Nan always says "Bob's your uncle!" What does that  mean ? Oh, that's a tricky one. It's… an old saying. It means if you do things in the right order, everything will be alright. It's a bit… British, really. You wouldn’t hear it much anywhere else. It’s very Dartford, actually! Bob's my uncle? Is Bob coming to the party? No, darling. It’s just a saying.

… honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork is what’s putting me off more than the actual move itself. It’s not like popping next door, is it? It’s Germany! They want  everything  documented. Birth certificates translated, qualifications verified… it’s a nightmare. Sounds…thorough. More thorough than dealing with the council here, at any rate. Though, I’m still wondering why Germany, of all places? You grew up around here, didn’t you? Doesn’t feel… intuitive. Intuitive? Not particularly. But it’s the job, isn’t it? Massive opportunity with this engineering firm. Basically, my field, but ten years ahead in terms of the projects they’re dealing with. Plus, the cost of living in that area, near Munich, is surprisingly reasonable. Certainly cheaper than trying to buy a place in Hitchin, Sarah. Oh, absolutely. Trying to get on the property ladder around here is… well, a joke, isn’t it? I’m renting indefinitely, I think. It’s just impossible. But Germany… that's a big leap. Will you miss the pubs? The questionable British weather? The pubs, definitely. And surprisingly, yes, sometimes even the rain. There’s something…comforting about a proper drizzle. But I'm told Bavarian beer more than makes up for it. And I can always fly back. It's not the moon. True. Though it feels like it sometimes, with Brexit and everything. It wouldn't be quite the same popping over for a pint, would it? Still, Munich sounds lovely. Have you started looking at schools for little Leo yet? I know you want him to be bilingual. That’s the next rabbit hole, isn’t it? The schools. It’s a completely different system. And naturally, needing to prove his immunisations and all the rest. Apparently, they’re very keen on that. He’s actually quite excited, though. Keeps asking if German kids have the same games we do. That's sweet. It'll be a challenge for him, adjusting to a new language and culture. But kids are remarkably resilient. Have you started trying to learn any German yourself, beyond ‘bier’ and ‘thank you’? Duolingo is my nemesis. It keeps telling me my pronunciation is appalling. I can order a beer and ask where the toilet is, which I’m told is a good start. I’m hoping immersion will do the rest. Thankfully, everyone speaks English anyway. Don't rely on that!

…and honestly, the way she described her grandmother’s kitchen, it just  smelled  of apple crumble. It transported me straight back to Nan’s. She always had something baking. Though hers was more Victoria sponge, if we’re being accurate. Did your nan bake much, Brenda?      Oh, constantly! My Nan Elsie was a force of nature in the kitchen. Not fancy, mind you. Real proper home cooking. Lots of suet puddings and spotted dick. Not much apple crumble, actually. She was more a jam roly-poly woman. Though she did make a mean treacle tart, I remember. And she’d always insist on serving it with proper clotted cream, even though it cost a fortune. Said it ‘wasn’t the same’ without.      Sounds lovely. My grandma, bless her, burnt everything. Seriously. Everything. But she made up for it in enthusiasm. She’d always be trying new recipes from magazines. It was a disaster zone every time, but we all pretended to enjoy it. She did teach me a bit of French though, which is odd, considering.      French? That  is  odd. Where did that come from?      No idea! She used to live near a language school in Southend, I think, and she'd pick up phrases from the students walking past. She could say “Bonjour, comment ça va?” with alarming confidence, and then immediately follow it up with a request for a cup of tea. It was hilarious. It's probably why I’m terrible at languages now, honestly. Just a weird association with burnt dinners and misplaced greetings.      Oh, that’s brilliant! It's funny the things you remember. It's like, growing up in Peterborough, everyone sounded…well, Peterborough. Very flat vowels. But then I’d go to Cambridge for a school trip and realise how  strong  regional accents can be. It’s only when you’re exposed to something different you notice your own.      Exactly! Being from Boston – Lincolnshire Boston, not the American one, obviously – I always felt a bit…isolated dialect-wise. We’re kind of in this linguistic no-man’s land. Not quite Yorkshire, not quite Norfolk, just…Boston. It’s served me well enough in sales, I suppose. Keeps people guessing where I’m  really  from. Though sometimes I get "Are you alright love?" which always makes me smile.      I get that. Essex is weird. We’re so close to London, but there’s still very much a distinct accent, especially the older generation.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of knitted Dalmatians was just  bizarre . Gran really does have a theme this year, doesn’t she? She’s committed, I’ll give her that. Dalmatians. Of all things. Did she at least get a good deal on the yarn? Because she was moaning about prices last time I saw her. Oh, she’s a bargain hunter, your Gran. Always has been. Found a whole box of it at a car boot sale, apparently. Five quid! She was chuffed to bits. Though, frankly, five quid’s a bit steep for something that’s just going to sit on a shelf gathering dust. Speaking of gathering dust…that reminds me of the time I tried to take that antique barometer to Blackpool. Thought it’d be a nice thing to have with us, check the pressure. Ended up leaving it on the outbound train. Dad! Seriously? The barometer? You and your gadgets. Well, it  was  a lovely barometer! Victorian. Your grandfather’s. I was distracted, alright? Little Timmy – remember Timmy? From next door – was pretending to be a pirate and needed rescuing from a particularly aggressive sandcastle. Priorities, you see. A pirate and an aggressive sandcastle. Sounds about right for Blackpool. Honestly, though, leaving a Victorian barometer on a train… Blackpool’s changed a bit, you know. Used to be proper family fun. Now it’s just arcades and overpriced fish and chips. We went last year, didn't we, Arthur? That we did, love. And it  was  overpriced fish and chips. Still, a good walk along the prom, even if it was blowin’ a gale. We saw a bloke tryin’ to fly a kite with no line. Brilliant. You two are hopeless. So, back to the actual trip. How was the Lake District? You two were saying it was really peaceful. Lovely, truly lovely. Away from all the hustle and bustle. We did a bit of walking – not too strenuous, mind, my knees aren’t what they used to be. And the scenery… breathtaking. You really should go, Lizzie. You’d love it. Yeah, the photos looked amazing. Did you manage to get to any of the little villages? Hawkshead, maybe? I’ve heard good things about the Beatrix Potter museum there. We didn't go  in  the museum, no. Too many children. But we walked around Hawkshead. Quaint little place. Had a smashing pub lunch, though.

… honestly, the sheer  volume  of plastic packaging on that thing was ridiculous. A single satsuma, individually wrapped. It’s just… unnecessary. Tell me about it. I boycotted individually wrapped biscuits after the Christmas debacle last year. Ended up with a mountain of cellophane. Luckily, I've found a farm shop that does refills for almost everything now. It's a bit of a drive, but worth it. Speaking of unnecessary, did you see the article about that influencer who chartered a private jet to go to… Burnley? Burnley! For a photoshoot. The carbon footprint alone… Oh, don't even get me started on influencers. It's all performative wokeness and then blatant excess. It's a wonder anyone takes them seriously. Though, I will admit, I occasionally fall down a rabbit hole of engineering channels on YouTube, and some of those guys are genuinely clever. See, you’re enabling them! Though, I understand the engineering thing. It's fascinating, isn't it? You explaining modular construction to my mum last Christmas felt like translating ancient Sumerian. She’s a tough audience. She just wanted to know if it meant the house would fall down if one bit was wobbly. Practical woman, your mum. Speaking of practical, I need to sort the car out. The bloody exhaust is playing up again. It’s an absolute pain. I thought I fixed it last month, but… You and your cars. You’d think, being an engineer, you’d build your own from scratch. A fully sustainable, self-repairing vehicle. Oh, if only! The time, the space… and frankly, the money. That’s the killer, isn’t it? Everything costs a fortune these days. Even a decent exhaust. Don’t remind me. School trips are eye-watering. Little Leo wants to go on the residential to the climbing centre, and it's… significant. I’m trying to justify it as ‘character building’ to myself. Character building that requires a second mortgage. Honestly, I’m starting to think parenting is just a series of expensive guilt trips. You're not wrong. Though, seeing them enjoy something…that makes it worth it, doesn’t it? Anyway, what are you two up to later? Fancy heading into town? Maybe catch that new exhibit at the art gallery? Ooh, that sounds nice. Though I promised Leo we’d build a den in the garden. It's a rainy day kind of activity.

… honestly, I still think relying solely on the satnav is asking for trouble. Remember Auntie Brenda in Cornwall? Ended up down a farmer's track barely wide enough for the car! Google Maps at least  shows  you what the road looks like beforehand, you know? Yeah, but Google Maps drained my phone battery last time we went to Cambridge. Right down to nothing. And I’m rubbish at reading maps, always have been. Reg, you were a navigator in the forces, weren’t you? What’s your take? Aye, well, maps were different back in me day. Big, paper things, folded up 'til they were nearly smaller than a postage stamp. And navigate by the stars, that’s what we did sometimes. Satnavs are grand, mind you, for getting you generally there. But they haven’t got the common sense God gave a goose. Brenda’s story rings a bell, though. Happens all the time. They follow the digital line regardless. They’re alright if you know where you’re  going . But if you’re just… exploring, like we were trying to do last month, they just take you around in circles. Kept telling us to do U-turns in village high streets! Gave me a right headache. Exactly! It's the lack of context. And speaking of headaches, how’s the decorating going, Mum? You mentioned needing to choose paint colours last week? Oh, don’t even get me started. Your Auntie Carol is having  opinions . Every single one of them, powerfully voiced. “That magnolia is too bland, Reg!” “That blue washes me out!” Honestly, she’s turning the whole thing into a military operation. I swear she has a colour palette approval board. Sounds… stressful. You need a beer, Reg. Another pint? I’ll get it. Appreciated, lad. Very much so. This is a good pint, this. Proper stuff. And it’s good to see you all. Knowing I'm heading out to Saudi is…well, it’s a bit daunting, if I'm honest. Saudi? Still doing that then? Thought that might have fallen through. No, everything’s confirmed. Six months training in the UK, then straight over there. Advisor role. Helping train up their security forces. It’s a good job, good pay, but blimey, it’s a long way from a Liverpool pub. It must be. Are you worried about… well, everything? The culture, the heat… everything?

… honestly, I’m just feeling a bit… sluggish. It’s not a cold, not really. Just this low-level fatigue that’s been hanging around for weeks. Probably just the travel, I suppose. Stockholm’s lovely, absolutely lovely, but the jet lag is a beast. You always say that, David. Every trip. You  enjoy  the ‘beast’ as you call it, the excuse to be grumpy for a week. Honestly, you need to hydrate more. You were practically rationing water on the flight. That’s a bit harsh, Eleanor. I had water! Just… not as much as you seem to think necessary. And it’s not just the travel, I've been thinking. Remember old Mr. Henderson, back in Wellington? He swore by daily cold showers. Said it shocked the system into life. Oh, Mr. Henderson. The eccentric botanist who insisted on wearing tweed, even in summer? He was a character. And yes, he absolutely  lived  by those cold showers. Though, I recall him also ingesting copious amounts of elderberry syrup. Said it boosted the immune system. Elderberry syrup sounds much more appealing than a freezing cold shower. Though, David, you’re always trying out these… alternative remedies. Last time it was activated charcoal. Hey! Activated charcoal worked wonders. Cleared me right up. Though, admittedly, my teeth were a little grey for a day or two. This feels different though. More…internal. I’ve been trying to eat better, but all these amazing Swedish pastries are making that difficult. Speaking of amazing, look at the rhododendrons. They’re incredible here. The soil conditions must be perfect. Sarah, the head gardener at Kew, was telling me how difficult they are to get thriving outside of very specific environments. It's all about the acidity, apparently. They  are  stunning. Though, I’m more a peony girl myself. Such elegant, delicate blooms. But back to you, David. Are you sleeping alright? You’ve been burning the candle at both ends with this new venture, haven’t you? Sleep’s been… patchy. That’s an understatement. The deal with OmniTech is finally moving forward, which is fantastic, but it requires a lot of late nights. I keep telling myself it's temporary. But maybe you're right. Maybe it’s wear and tear. Perhaps a digital detox would help? Put the phone down, step away from the laptop for a few days. We could go hiking in Tyresta National Park on Friday.

… honestly, Dad, it’s just… when you start  trying  to sound like you’re from London, it’s a bit much. You weren’t raised in Bethnal Green, you were born five miles from here! It's like you've been watching too much  Only Fools and Horses . Right, well, excuse me for attempting a bit of culture, dear. It’s not like I’ve got much else  to  do, is it? Besides, I think I manage a decent enough cockney impression. Better than yours, anyway. You sound like you’ve swallowed a dictionary, always so precise. Oh, leave her alone, George. She’s just saying you’re a bit… performative. It's harmless. Though, you did used to say "loo" instead of "toilet" when we first met, which was a bit of a giveaway you weren't a true Londoner. Yeah, Dad. Remember when you tried to order a pint in a pub in Shoreditch and they just stared at you? You asked for a 'half of mild and a biscuit'. That was one time! And the barman was a rude boy. Honestly. Anyway, it’s all down to how things  sound . I’ve been thinking, actually, about these new voice recognition things on the phones. They’d never understand a word I say, not properly. They’re all trained on posh voices, aren't they? They’re getting better, actually. I use mine all the time for messages. Although, it did transcribe 'need to get milk' as ‘need to get Malkovich’ once. Weird. But it’s learning. Speaking of needing things… has anyone heard anything from Mark lately? Still completely off the rails, is he? Sarah’s proper stressed. He texted me yesterday. Apparently, he’s volunteering at a bicycle repair shop. Which is… progress, I suppose. But he mentioned needing money. Again. That man. Honestly. The last time I lent him money, he spent it on a new Minecraft server. A  Minecraft server , Mum! When he can barely afford food. He always was a bit of a dreamer, that boy. Like his mother. Though she always had a good head for figures. Remember that awful mattress we had at your Grandma’s? The one that sagged in the middle? She haggled that shopkeeper down to half price. Oh god, yes! That mattress was torture. My back ached for a week after staying there. It's no wonder Mark ended up wanting to escape into a digital world, spending all his time in Minecraft, poor love.

… honestly, the meringue just wouldn’t peak. I whipped it for ages, proper elbow grease, but it just stayed… floppy. It's the humidity, I reckon. Suffolk air, even in October, is deceptively damp. Ruined the whole Baked Alaska. Floppy meringue? Sounds disastrous, Mum. Was it, like, completely liquid? Not  liquid , darling, just… unwilling to cooperate. It’s supposed to stand up proud, you know? Like a little snowdrift. This just slumped. It’ll be a trifle for pudding, I suppose. Still delicious, just… not showstopping. You know how I was planning to impress Mrs. Henderson with it? She’s on the recruiting panel. Oh, right, for the new admin assistant. Is she strict? Leo said she asked him what his favourite spreadsheet formula was. Spreadsheet formula! Can you  imagine ? She's… thorough. And quite old-fashioned. That's why a slightly flamboyant Baked Alaska felt necessary. A bit of 'look at me, I'm a dynamic Programme Director who also bakes!' I also spent ages grating the cheese for the lasagne, and even  that  felt like a battle against gravity. It kept clumping. Maybe you need a different grater? The one with the bigger holes? Perhaps.
