Or different cheese. Honestly, the trials of domesticity! Speaking of trials, have you finalized your costume for Ethan’s Halloween party? It’s next week, isn't it? Yeah, pretty much. I’m going as… well, I haven't told anyone yet. It’s a surprise. Ooh, mysterious. Is it scarier than last year’s vampire? Because last year’s vampire was rather convincing. Reminded me of your Great Uncle Arthur, actually. All pale and brooding. Very funny, Mum. No, it’s… different. Anyway, Leo reckons he’s going as a zombie astronaut. Apparently, it requires a lot of silver duct tape. Sounds… creative. This reminds me of when  I  was your age, Halloween was… simpler. We just went trick-or-treating in the village and hoped no one gave us apples. Remember the scare about poisoned apples? Vaguely. Dad told me about it. It was awful. Suddenly, all this fun thing became… tainted. It makes you think, doesn't it? About how quickly things can change. It's also why I get so worked up about safety regulations on the programme. You have to protect people. Yeah. Speaking of protecting people… a friend at school was saying something about someone getting in trouble for… well, it was a bit weird.

…and honestly, the bagels weren’t  nearly  as good as everyone makes out. All hype, I tell ya. Proper Yorkshire scones are a different kettle of fish entirely. Though this toast is lovely, thank you, Alys. Really good bread. Glad you like it. It’s from the bakery down the road. They do a cracking sourdough too, if you fancy trying some later. You were saying about New York? Bit disappointed then? Disappointed isn’t quite the word. Overwhelmed, maybe? It's just… so  much . Everything’s bigger, louder, flashier. It felt a bit… performative, if you know what I mean. Give me the quiet of the Dales any day. Though the museums were excellent, mind. The Met was absolutely staggering. I can imagine. I’ve always wanted to go, but the thought of the crowds… puts me off a bit. You seem to cope alright with crowds, teaching and all. Aye, but there’s a different sort of crowd. Those are students, mostly. I know why they’re there. New York felt like everyone was  trying  to be seen. Anyway, enough about my grumbles. Speaking of things a bit out there… are you still considering those flying lessons? Don’t remind me! I looked into it last week. It's terrifyingly expensive. And the closest airfield is ages away. But… it’s still tempting, isn't it? Just the idea of being up there, seeing everything from a different perspective. It's a bit like when we were in Japan, remembering how different everything looked from the train. Japan. Now  that  was an adventure. Remember that tiny little ramen shop in Kyoto? And getting horribly lost in Osaka station? We were right daft kids, weren’t we? Always ending up on the wrong platform. Always. Though we always found our way eventually. How is Rhys doing, by the way? Still messaging you on… what is it, Instagram? That thing confounds me. Oh, he’s fine. Messing about with computers as usual. And yes, Instagram. It's a plague, really. Everyone presenting a perfect version of their lives. Though it's handy for seeing what the grandkids are up to. Rhys keeps telling me to ‘story’ things; I have no idea what he’s on about. I still prefer a good letter, you know? Proper handwriting, a stamp… much more personal. I agree. Though I admit, I’m guilty of doom-scrolling through Facebook sometimes.

Right, that  should  hurt. Honestly, I’m amazed anyone even knows how to spell ‘qi’ let alone have it lurking in their tile bag. Though, to be fair, I was nearly half an hour late to Professor Davies’ lecture on post-structuralism today… probably wasn't fully concentrating on spelling anything. Half an hour? Liam, that’s… a Liam thing, isn’t it? You’re consistently operating on ‘Liam Standard Time’. Is it the buses again? Or did you get lost in a philosophical debate with yourself? It was… an incident involving a particularly stubborn sheep. Honestly! On the way to the bus stop. Blocked the whole road. Farmer was having a right time of it getting it moving. Apparently, it was a prize-winning ram. Sheep, eh? Sounds about right for Wales. Good luck explaining  that  to Professor Davies. Still, at least you have an excuse. I was ten minutes late for my shift last week because my alarm didn’t go off. Chef was not impressed. Said I "lack discipline.” Like I  chose  to let the sunrise dictate my schedule. You know, it’s weird the origins of some words. ‘Discipline’ – comes from ‘disciplina’ meaning training, like… teaching a pupil. So, you were momentarily untrainable, Ben? Sounds fair enough. That's actually a really clever point, Tom. I always wonder about etymology. Like "scrabble" itself. Sounds so…onomatopoeic, but it doesn’t actually  sound  like anything. Apparently, it’s from a Swedish word, ‘skrabba’, meaning ‘to scratch’. Makes sense, I suppose, considering what we're doing. Though I'm currently scratching my head trying to figure out how to get rid of these vowels. Vowels are the bane of my existence. Especially Es and As. I'm banking on some high-scoring consonants later. Although, honestly, I’m more focused on blocking you lot than actually building words. It’s cutthroat, this game. Remember those ridiculous spelling tests we had in A Levels? Mr. Henderson’s obsession with the correct placement of commas? I'm still recovering. It's all very relevant to Scrabble, actually. Knowing the obscure rules. Oh god, Henderson. He once deducted marks because I wrote ‘colour’ with a ‘u’. He insisted it was “Americanised”. I was seventeen! I didn’t need a lecture on linguistic purity. Speaking of purity, have you all seen the Chelsea Flower Show coverage? It’s stunning this year. I flicked through it on the TV in the kitchen.

…and honestly, Doreen, I still reckon they overcharge for the sprouts at Morrisons. It's daylight robbery, I tell you. Daylight robbery. Used to get ‘em for pennies down at the farm shop, didn’t we? Before Old Man Hemmings sold up. You and them sprouts, Arthur. Always the sprouts. They’re not  that  bad, are they? And the farm shop’s gone, love. Has been for fifteen years. You dwell on things. Dwelling? I’m just pointing out the principle of the thing! Fifteen years… feels like yesterday, though. Remember that massive marrow Hemmings grew in ’08? Won a prize, it did. As big as a bloomin’ armchair. I remember you trying to lift it and nearly throwing your back out. You were moaning for a week. That’s what I remember. Honestly, you’ve got a selective memory. All the good bits, and the bits where you make a fool of yourself. Well, someone's gotta provide the entertainment, haven’t they? Keeps life interesting. Though, these days… entertainment's a bit thin on the ground, isn't it? Not much to  do  now we’re… well, you know. Proper retired. Don’t start with that, Arthur. We're not useless. We watch the telly, we potter in the garden , and we have a good natter. That’s something, isn’t it? Better than being stuck in work, I say. Remember Mrs. Higgins from next door? Still slaving away at the council, bless her. Looks ten years older than she is. Poor soul. Still, she always had a good pension, didn’t she? We weren’t exactly flush, were we? Never really saved much, did we. Took things as they came. Which, looking back… maybe wasn’t the cleverest plan. We managed. We always managed. And we had some good times. Remember that trip to Bournemouth? The donkey rides and… oh, and the knitted egg cosies! You insisted on buying me three of them. You looked lovely in a knitted egg cosy, Doreen. You always did appreciate a good bargain. And they kept the eggs warm! Practical  and  stylish. Practical, maybe. Stylish… debatable. Though, you’re right, we did have some good times. It’s just… sometimes I worry about… well, about the future. With everything going up and up. And the youngsters not having a look-in. Our Brian’s struggling, you know. Aye, Brian’s a good lad.

… honestly, I still think a bit of Worcestershire sauce livens up a Bolognese. Just a  dash . People get so precious about it, you know? “Authentic Italian”, pah! My mother always put it in, and she was a cracking cook. Dad, you say that about everything. Remember when you tried to convince me pineapple belonged on pizza? That was a valid experiment! Don’t knock it ‘til you’ve tried it properly. Anyway, this is lovely, Sarah. Really lovely. You’ve outdone yourself with the potatoes. Is that rosemary in them? It is, Arthur. And a tiny bit of garlic rubbed into the skins before roasting. Makes all the difference. It’s the simple things, isn’t it? Though I  am  trying to watch the carbs a bit. Went for a decent walk this morning along the coastal path. Good for you, love. Though walking doesn't burn off nearly enough to justify a second helping of these potatoes, just saying. I’ve been trying that fitness app, you know, the one Chloe recommended? “MoveMore” or something. Absolute nonsense. Tells me I need to do high-intensity interval training at my age. As if! Oh, Dad. You and technology. It's not going to understand your…unique fitness regime of armchair observing and biscuit consumption. Hey! I do a bit of gardening. And I walk to the shops. It’s… purposeful strolling. And it’s not about the biscuits, it's about having something  with  a nice cup of tea! Speaking of shops, have you seen anything in the  Gazette  about the station? Still not open, is it? That’s the latest. Another month’s delay. Apparently, there were issues with the signalling system. Honestly, you’d think they’d have sorted that before announcing a grand opening date three times already. It’s a disaster, really. It was meant to be a game-changer for the village and surrounding areas. Less reliance on cars, better access for people coming to visit… they promised so much. Promised, promised. Politicians. Always promising. It’s the same story, no matter where you are. Remember when they promised to reopen the line in Southend? That was back in the eighties. Never happened. Always something. Well, hopefully this time it’ll actually materialise. It would be brilliant for getting to Exeter without having to drive. And easier for Mum to visit. Absolutely. It’s a real shame for the local businesses too, they were banking on the extra footfall.

… honestly, the portions were ridiculous. I mean, I’m a student, not a competitive eater! Fifteen quid for a burger and a handful of chips? Robbery, pure robbery. Though, the atmosphere  was  good, I’ll give them that. All fairy lights and exposed brick. Very Cardiff. Fifteen quid? Blimey. You’re getting ripped off even by Cardiff standards. Down in St. Austell, you get a proper pasty and a drink for under a fiver. Different world, innit? Speaking of different worlds, did you catch that new Marvel film? The one everyone’s buzzing about? Nah, not yet. Been buried in seminars, to be honest. Shakespeare’s been taking over my life, the old Bard. Actually saw a production of  Hamlet  on the telly last night. David Tennant was brilliant, completely brilliant. Properly unsettling. Oh yeah? Tennant's good. Always a bit intense, though. I'm more a  John Wick  kinda guy, you know? Action, explosions… less soliloquies. Been trying to get a few games in too, been on  Apex Legends  lately. You still playing  FIFA ? Occasionally. But it's… stressful. Especially watching Forest this season. They’re playing alright, but consistently dropping points. It's infuriating! You follow anyone? Massive Arsenal fan, through and through. Been a good season so far, touch wood. Though, honestly, the Premier League is getting a bit predictable. It's always the same few teams at the top. Saying that, saw a clip of that guy, Curtis Jones, Liverpool, doing a ridiculous nutmeg. Proper skill. Yeah, the skill levels are insane these days. Speaking of insane… remember Ben’s stag do last year? Absolute chaos. He nearly ended up marrying a… well, let’s just say a very enthusiastic performer. Oh god, don’t remind me! Prague was a mistake. A glorious, hilarious mistake. I still have flashbacks. He’s got some stories he  doesn't  tell the missus, I reckon. Although, I'm starting to think about my own...should probably start planning something. My brother's getting married next year. Right, that's a proper undertaking. Where are you thinking of? Something equally… adventurous as Prague? Maybe not  quite  Prague. Thinking more along the lines of Bristol, or maybe even just a really good weekend in London. Budget’s a concern, you know? Uni life. What are you reading for your course at the moment, by the way? Beyond the Bard, I mean. Just finished a really dense book on post-colonial literature.

...Honestly, the sheer volume of emails I had waiting for me this morning was  criminal . It's like everyone decided to save all their queries for my two days off. And Mr. Henderson, bless him, keeps 'cc-ing' everyone on updates that literally only concern me. It's passive-aggressive project management at its finest.      Oh, Henderson. He sounds… delightful. Sounds like the kind of person who delegates  up . How was the actual break though? Did you manage to properly switch off? You looked a bit frazzled last time we spoke.      It was okay. Mum and Dad were… Mum-and-Dad-ing. Which is lovely, truly, but a lot. Constant questions about when I’m settling down, if I’m seeing anyone nice, the usual. And Dad tried to explain cryptocurrency to me  again . Honestly, I think he just wants to feel useful.      Oh god, the 'settling down' question. My nan's been hammering me with that since Christmas. I swear, she thinks turning 26 is some sort of expiry date on having a fulfilling single life. Speaking of, how  are  things with… you know… Liam?      Don’t even. It’s been officially six months, and I still get a little pang when I see a navy jumper. He’s moved on, apparently. Instagram is telling me he’s happily hiking in the Lake District with… someone. Very outdoorsy. Very not me.      Ouch. Instagram is the worst. Trust me, I unfollowed half my uni course after seeing all the curated "perfect life" nonsense. Honestly, he always struck me as a bit vanilla anyway. You deserve someone a bit more… chaotic, like you.      Chaotic is a good word for me, isn't it? But you’re right. He was… safe. And I think I needed someone a bit less… predictable. Anyway, enough about my disastrous love life. How’s work treating  you ? Last I heard, you were knee-deep in the new textbook campaign?      Knee-deep doesn't even begin to cover it. It’s been… intense. Pearson are pushing this new digital platform  so  hard. Trying to convince lecturers it's the future of education while simultaneously dealing with tech glitches and feedback saying it's totally unintuitive. Plus, marketing budgets are tighter than ever. It feels like we're expected to do the work of three people.      Sounds stressful. You always did thrive under pressure though. Remember that advertising project we did at uni?

… honestly, Mam used to kill anything green she touched. Absolutely  murder  it. You'd give her a cactus expecting it to thrive, and within a week it'd be looking all sad and droopy. It's a wonder I turned out remotely capable with plants, y'know? Well, genetics aren’t everything, are they? Maybe you inherited the stubborn streak instead. That’s definitely a Sunderland trait. Stubborn, aye, that’s me alright. Mam's was more… optimistic ineptitude. She  believed  she could nurture something, but it clearly wasn’t meant to be. Remember that poor fern she got for her birthday? The one Auntie Brenda gave her? Oh god,  that  fern. It looked like it had been through a warzone within days. Brenda was proper miffed. She babied  her  ferns. They were like her children. They were! She’d named them all. Honestly. But me, I think I learned from watching what  not  to do. Plus, being at uni, surrounded by all those botanical gardens… you pick things up. I started small, spider plants, then succulents. Now look at the chaos in the spare room. Chaos is a bit strong. It’s a… thriving jungle. A very controlled, carefully curated jungle. You’ve got labels on everything, humidity levels monitored… it’s a full-time job. It kinda is! It’s relaxing though, isn't it? Especially after a day of wrestling with research data. Speaking of which, how’s the PhD going? Still dissecting the mating rituals of microscopic worms? Sadly, yes. Still observing worms. Though ‘dissecting’ makes it sound far more dramatic than it is. It’s mostly watching them wriggle and hoping something interesting happens. I’m starting to feel a bit like a worm voyeur, to be honest. You need a hobby! More plants, maybe? I could give you a cutting of my Monstera. It’s getting  massive . Tempting…very tempting. Though I’m fairly sure I’d just end up neglecting it and feeling guilty. I can barely manage to consistently cook something beyond pasta. Which, by the way, you’re amazing at. Seriously, that Shepherd's Pie you made last week… that was heavenly. Mam would have been jealous. Oh, stop it. It’s just mince and mashed potato. Although, I did use a proper lamb stock this time, that made a difference. It’s all about the little things, aye? Like getting enough water to your ferns.

… honestly, appalling. Absolutely appalling. They gave him a straight red for  that  tackle? It was a robust challenge, a bit full-blooded maybe, but a red? The game’s gone soft, Gwyn. Utterly soft. Now, now, David. You say that every week. Same tune, different referee. Though, I’ll grant you, some of these decisions are…questionable. Did you see young Bellingham’s boy the other day? Apparently, already being scouted. Nine years old! It's ridiculous, the pressure they put on them. Exactly! It’s a circus. A complete circus. My grandson, he’s ten, brilliant at maths, wants to be an astrophysicist. Now  that’s  a worthwhile pursuit, not chasing a leather ball around a field for millions. It sets a terrible example. Though, I suppose it pays the bills. Speaking of distractions, how was your weekend? Anything more stimulating than televised football horrors? Quite peaceful, actually. Got a good few hours in the garden. The dahlias are finally coming out. Though the slugs are having a field day, the devils. I’m thinking of getting one of those copper tape barriers. Old Mrs. Evans down the road swears by them. Copper tape, eh? Clever. I’ve been battling aphids on the roses. Tried the soapy water trick, doesn't seem to do much good. I’m considering a more…drastic solution. Perhaps relocating the entire rose bed. It's a monumentally tedious task, though. Speaking of tedious, I've got a mountain of essays to mark. Third years are truly testing my patience this year. The standard is...variable to say the least. Tell me about it. I’m wading through dissertations on post-structuralism. Half of them are just regurgitating Foucault without any original thought. It’s disheartening. I keep thinking, they have so much potential. Though, a lot of them seem to have their minds set on…well, not academia, let’s just say. Quite. I had a student last week asking for advice on joining the police force. Said he liked the ‘action’. I tried to gently point out the reality of paperwork and dealing with…difficult members of the public. It’s not all car chases and shootouts, you know. Same here. Got a lad wanting to go straight into the Paras after graduation. Brave, I suppose. But completely unprepared for what it entails. These days, it feels like there's a real disconnect between their expectations and the reality of those professions.

… honestly, the meeting could have been an email. A  long  email. Three hours of people talking  at  each other, not  to  each other. It’s draining, you know? Absolutely draining. Is draining like when the bath water goes down the plug? Sort of, petal. A bit like that, but for your brain instead of water. It makes you feel…empty. Sounds about right for a corporate strategy session. They’re designed to make you question your life choices, aren’t they? How was the actual content, Mum? Anything useful come out of it? Useful? Not particularly. More vague aspirations and buzzwords than concrete plans. They want us to “synergize” more. Honestly. Synergize. It makes me want to scream. And then Mrs. Henderson spent twenty minutes detailing her weekend pottery class. Did she make a unicorn? I want a unicorn! I don’t  think  she made a unicorn, darling. Probably a bowl. A very…artistic bowl. Anyway, enough about work. We need to finalize plans for Lily’s christening. Have you spoken to Auntie Carol about the guest list, Sarah? Yeah, I messaged her this morning. She’s already started compiling it, apparently. Predictably, it’s ballooning. She’s invited half the WI and anyone who's ever delivered a parcel to her door. Carol and her social life. Right. I suppose we can’t completely veto anyone. It’s her sister, after all. But we need to contain it. Maybe suggest a limit? Fifty people max? I’ll try, but you know how she gets. She’ll say it’s a ‘special occasion’ and everyone deserves to be there. I’ve also looked at venues, and ‘The Old Mill’ seems the most suitable. It’s got a nice garden for the kids to run around in. Can we have a bouncy castle?  Please ? A pink one! She’s already thinking about the entertainment. A bouncy castle might be…a bit much for a christening. Although, it  would  keep her occupied. I was thinking more along the lines of a magician. Or face painting. Something a little less…energetic. And less likely to cause a trip to A&E. A magician sounds lovely. We also need to think about catering. I was thinking a buffet would be easiest. And a cake, of course. It’s not a celebration without cake! Chocolate cake! With sprinkles! And a fairy on top! Possibly, darling, possibly. We'll see.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork is just… draining. They keep changing the forms, you know? Every time I think I’ve mastered one system, they bring another one in. It’s designed to make life difficult, I swear. Sounds familiar. Corporate loves a good reshuffle, doesn’t it? I had a similar thing with the new till system last month. Took a week to get my head around it, and then they ‘simplified’ it and it was  worse . How are you coping, honestly? You seemed a bit stressed on Wednesday. Coping? Well, I’m fuelled by caffeine and sheer willpower, mostly. It’s just… it’s not the  work  itself, it's the bureaucracy. I miss actually  doing  things, rather than documenting that I’m going to do things, documenting that I did them, and documenting why I did them that way. Mummy talks like a grown-up! Well, someone has to, doesn’t she? And you’ll be talking like a grown-up soon enough, little one. Are you excited about Saturday? We’re going to see Grandma and Grandpa, remember? And get ice cream? And definitely ice cream. They promised a double scoop, didn’t they? Speaking of Saturday, I need to get stock sorted at the shop beforehand. It's been manic all week; everyone's getting ready for the summer holidays. Thinking of a mini-break myself afterwards, maybe somewhere in the Cotswolds. Just a couple of nights. Oh, that sounds lovely. You deserve it. You work so incredibly hard. We were talking about something bigger, remember? New York? New York is still the dream, yeah. But saving is… slow. And with everything going up, it feels even further away. I did a rough calculation last night and suddenly that cute little apartment we saw online looked significantly less cute when I added up the exchange rate and potential tourist trap prices! It  is  expensive. Remember when we went to Rome, back when… well, before everything changed? That felt manageable. This feels… ambitious. Rome! Did you see the Colosseum? It was  huge ! I want to go to New York and see a really tall building! You do. You absolutely do. We’ll get you to see a really tall building, love. Perhaps next year. Maybe if we really knuckle down and save. It would be amazing to take you at Christmas, see the Rockefeller Center tree… That would be magical.

…and then, right, the whole thing’s just…a mess of data. Honestly, I spent three days just cleaning it. Three  days . It was all exported from different machines, different software versions, you name it. Fields labelled differently, dates in completely bizarre formats. It's a wonder anything actually  works  with this stuff. Sounds delightful. Postgraduate research, eh? Glamorous, isn't it? Me, I’m just grateful my fieldwork is…well, observing people. Relatively clean data, mostly. Just transcriptions and coded notes. No wrestling with legacy systems. You are  lucky . Seriously. This is for the fluvial geomorphology module, remember? Trying to model sediment transport in the River Lune. The Lune! It's practically on my doorstep back in Lancaster, and yet I’m spending more time wrangling spreadsheets than actually  thinking  about the river. The Lune is, uh, brown, isn’t it? I’ve driven past, vaguely. So, what’s the actual issue? Is it just the formatting, or is some of the data… suspect? A bit of both. The formatting was the initial nightmare. But then, digging deeper, I found a load of outliers that just don’t make any sense. Flow rates higher than theoretically possible given the rainfall data for those dates. And some depth readings that...well, they're negative. Negative depth! As if the riverbed is  above  the water level. Right. Someone's been having a laugh, or the sensors were malfunctioning. Have you checked the metadata for those specific readings? Like, what time were they taken? Was there anything logged about conditions? I’ve tried. That’s where it gets even more frustrating. The metadata is…sparse, to put it mildly. It’s mostly just date and time, and a vague “sensor ID.” No notes about calibration, no maintenance logs, absolutely nothing. It’s like they just chucked the sensors in and hoped for the best. Classic. That always happens, doesn’t it? People collecting data without thinking about the data  after  the collection. It’s infuriating. So, what are you going to do? Just…discard the dodgy bits? I’m trying to be more methodical than that. I’ve cross-referenced it with long-term data from the Environment Agency, see if those dates correlate with any known issues – flooding, maintenance work, that sort of thing. Found a couple of potential explanations for some of the outliers, but others… I’m genuinely stumped. I’m worried I’ll have to contact Dr. Davies, which I really want to avoid.

… honestly, it was  bizarre . I was giving a presentation, right? Standard Monday morning stuff at Prospect. But everyone in the room… they were all squirrels. Proper bushy tails and little beady eyes, just staring up at me. And I was trying to explain ROI on philanthropic giving to a room full of  squirrels . Oh, Mark, you and your dreams. You’ve got the most ridiculous ones. Remember the time you were a competitive cheese sculptor? Don’t remind me! That was mortifying, even in the dream. This was different though. It felt… stressful. Like I was genuinely failing to connect with the audience. And they kept burying acorns in the projector. Can we have a doggy? Please? Like, a really fluffy one? Yeah! A golden retriever! They’re good at catching things, like acorns! We’ve talked about this, darlings. It’s a lovely thought, but it’s a big responsibility. And with both of us working… She’s right, you two. A dog needs walks, and training, and everything. Though… a labrador  would  be nice. A bit of company. Especially when I’m dealing with squirrel clients in my subconscious. See? Even  you're  having dog-related thoughts now. It's contagious. It’s just… the thought of picking up poo every morning doesn’t fill me with joy, I’ll be honest. Fair enough. Although, winning the lottery would completely change that equation, wouldn’t it? We could employ a dedicated poo-picker-upper! Oh, stop it. You and your lottery fantasies. Did you buy a ticket this week? Of course! You know I do. Every week. It’s a small investment in a potential life of luxury. Imagine, no more spreadsheets, no more convincing people to donate to worthy causes. Just… lounging around, ensuring the dog’s poo is dealt with appropriately. And a massive garden! With a trampoline! And a swimming pool! Filled with jelly! Let’s not get  too  carried away. The jelly pool is a bit ambitious, even for lottery winners. But a bigger garden… that’s not a bad idea. I am starting to feel a bit cramped. This kitchen is great, but we're bursting at the seams. Exactly! We could get a proper dining table, too. Not just this… …organised chaos. It’s called ‘family life’, Mark. And honestly, I wouldn't trade the chaos for all the lottery money in the world.

… honestly, it was chaos. Absolute chaos. I waited nearly five hours just to be  seen  by a nurse. Five hours, Liam! And for what? They just told me to ice it and take paracetamol. Five hours? Blimey, that's rough, isn't it? What happened, properly? You just said you ‘banged your head’ on the phone, which doesn’t exactly paint a full picture. Is it… serious? Serious? Nah, not  serious  serious. Just… daft, really. I was trying to get that bookshelf sorted in the spare room, yeah? The one I’ve been meaning to do for months? And I stood on the wobbly chair – I  knew  I shouldn't have – and lost my balance. Head went straight into the corner of the wardrobe. Ouch. A wardrobe corner doesn’t sound forgiving. You and dodgy furniture, honestly. Remember that time with the collapsing coffee table at your mum’s? Don’t remind me! That was mortifying. But this was different. I got a proper goose egg, like straight out of a cartoon. And felt a bit dizzy afterwards, hence the A&E trek. Old habits die hard, I panicked. Mam always said to get checked out if you hit your head. Well, your Mam's not wrong, to be fair. Concussion's not something to mess with. But five hours… they’re just constantly understaffed, aren't they? It’s a symptom of everything being underfunded. Did they actually  look  at the lump, or did they just wave you away? They poked it. Literally. The nurse poked it and asked if I could remember my name and the date. Tick boxes, innit? I told her I’m a fully functioning corpus administrator, I think I know my name! And then she said, “Ice and paracetamol.” I felt a bit silly complaining, with other people clearly in worse states. There was a lad with a broken arm, and an older woman who’d fallen… It’s still frustrating though, isn't it? Especially when it’s a long wait for seemingly minimal attention. You should've pushed for a scan, maybe? I mean, with a head injury… I thought about it, but I felt a bit awkward. Like I was wasting their time. Plus, I was starting to feel a bit silly, and I just wanted to get out. I'm pretty sure it's just a really impressive bruise. It’s throbbing a bit now, actually.

…and honestly, Harold, the sheer audacity of it! Claiming they  didn’t  know the plans for the pipeline were…well, let’s just say environmentally questionable. It’s right there in black and white in the impact assessment reports! Honestly, the world’s gone mad. Mad it certainly has, Arthur. Mad as a box of frogs, as my old mum used to say. Though, I’ve found switching off the news helps immensely. Too much doom and gloom. Speaking of gloom, how’s the, uh, ‘retirement project’ coming along? Still tinkering with those miniature railways? Tinkering is a polite way of putting it. More like wrestling with a stubborn beast, to be frank. The points keep sticking, the signals are unreliable… it’s all rather… frustrating. But it keeps the brain active, I suppose. Though, I've been mulling over something else, actually. Something a bit more… ambitious. Oh? Do tell. You thinking of expanding the empire to include fully-sized trains now? You always did have a passion for them, even as a boy down on Brighton beach. No, not trains. Though, tempting. No, I was reading an article about online tutoring, specifically for GCSE history. And it struck me – I’ve got decades of experience, a good understanding of the curriculum, and a quiet room. I could offer help to students struggling with the subject. It's not a fortune, I know, but it's something. Online tutoring eh? Not a bad shout, Arthur, not bad at all. Plenty of kids struggle with history. They need someone who can  make  it interesting, not just drone on about dates and kings. You always were good at bringing history to life, even back in the classroom at Blatchington Mill. Always loved your stories about the smuggling tunnels under Brighton. Well, a little dramatic flair never hurt anyone. But I'm worried about the technical side. Websites and Zoom calls… It’s all rather alien to me. You’ve always been the one with your finger on the pulse when it comes to that sort of thing, being a business owner and all. Don't you worry about that. I've got a nephew, young Liam, who's a whizz with computers. He built my website when I first started up the carpentry business. I’m sure he'd give you a hand setting things up. A few quid and a promise of a good biscuit selection, and he’ll have you tutoring the world in no time.

… honestly, I’m still thinking about that shepherd’s pie I had last week. It was  divine . We should try and recreate it. Though, recreating anything that good is probably a fool’s errand. What are you leaning towards tonight? Everything on this menu looks…pub-y, doesn't it? Predictable, if you know what I mean. Predictably comforting, I’d say. After a day dealing with spreadsheets and departmental memos, ‘predictable’ is actually rather appealing. I was eyeing the fish and chips, actually. Can’t go wrong. Though, you're right, it’s not exactly pushing culinary boundaries. It’s a far cry from that little bistro we found in Richmond, remember? Oh,  that  bistro! The one where they served the duck confit with cherry jam? Good times. It’s just…this place is nice, don’t get me wrong. But look at the décor. All dark wood, and slightly sticky tables. It screams ‘historical significance’ but feels just a bit…tired. It  is  the Guardhouse, love. What did you expect, minimalist chic? It has a history, this place. Used to be part of the Royal Arsenal, apparently. All this Woolwich regeneration is making it feel a bit out of place, though. Remember when this whole area was just…well, a bit rough around the edges? Vaguely. I wasn't spending much time down this side of the river back then. More focused on surviving essays at uni. Speaking of which, how’s your nephew coping with his applications? Still aiming for Edinburgh? He is. Absolutely fixed on it. Says he wants the ‘authentic student experience’. Which, knowing him, probably involves a lot of late nights and questionable life choices. He’s a bright lad, though. Just…impulsive. Reminds me a bit of myself, actually, back when I was at York. You? Impulsive? You, the paragon of organisation? I find that hard to believe. Are you cold? You’ve got your coat on inside. It’s a bit drafty, I think. And this coat… it’s just… practical. Doesn’t exactly scream ‘fashion icon’, does it? Your scarf is lovely, though. Very autumnal. Thanks. Found it in a little shop in Rye. They had a whole collection of vintage woollens. This place has got some odd music choices, doesn’t it? Is that…Kenny G? I think it is. Awful. Someone's got questionable taste. It's probably adding to the 'charm' though, isn't it?

…Aye, so the lightin’ was absolutely mental, right? Like somethin’ outta a film. I’d been plannin’ this shot for ages, see, standin’ right on the edge o’ the cliffs at Neist Point. Nearly blew away, honestly. Proper wild. Neist Point, eh? Ambitious. You and your photography, Alistair. Always chasin’ the dramatic. I can practically  feel  the wind just hearin’ ye. Was it worth nearly bein’ swept into the Atlantic for? Worth it? Man, it was… transformative. I got the shot, though. Black and white, obviously. The basalt columns, the waves crashin’… it just  worked . It's on my Instagram, if you want to see. Though Instagram doesnae really do it justice, to be fair. Loses the… the  scale  of the place. I'll take a look later. I'm just back from a wee trip myself - nothing quite as dramatic as cliff edges, mind you. Just a conference in Barcelona. Work, unfortunately. Though the tapas were exceptional. Barcelona? Fancy. Always wanted to go there. Is it as sunny as they say? We’ve had nothin’ but dreich weather here for weeks. Proper grey and damp. Makes photowalks a right pain. Need a filter just to make things look vaguely cheerful. Sunny is an understatement. Blazing, more like. Though even  that  gets tiring after a bit. I’m used to the… subtlety of the Scottish light, I think. All those shades of grey. You actually appreciate a bit of sun when it finally shows its face. Plus, the architecture is amazing – Gaudi, obviously. Perfect for photography, actually, if you were there with your gear. Gaudi, aye? I've seen photos. Pretty bonkers, right? All curvy and colourful. My stuff tends to be a bit… starker. More landscape, less… flourishes. Though I did try a bit of street photography in Glasgow once. That was… an experience. I can imagine. Glasgow’s a different beast entirely. Did ye get any good shots? A few. Mostly folk lookin’ thoroughly unimpressed at havin’ their picture taken. Gotta be quick, ye know? It’s no’ like coaxing a sheep to pose for ye. Mind you, I’m thinkin’ o’ goin’ back up to Skye next month. Hopin’ for some autumn colours. Was thinkin’ about tryin’ some long exposures with the waterfalls. That  would  be good. Skye in autumn… now  that’s  a photograph waitin’ to happen. Be careful though, the weather can turn on a dime up there.

… honestly, the sheer volume of options is overwhelming. Muslin squares in every shade imaginable, organic cotton this, bamboo that… it’s all a bit much, isn’t it? I just want something soft and clean for the little one. Mum, you’re getting worked up over baby blankets. It’ll be fine. Honestly, Leo’s mum just used whatever was on offer at Tesco and he turned out alright! Though, I suppose things are different now, aren’t they? Everyone’s an expert. Different how? It’s not about being an ‘expert’, it’s about… well, wanting to give him the best start. And frankly, I’m finding the nursery planning incredibly stressful. It feels like a full-time job on top of everything else. Have you even started looking at cots yet? It’s a minefield of safety regulations. I had a quick look online. They’re expensive, aren’t they? And heavy! I was thinking, maybe just the Moses basket to start with? He’ll be in with us for the first few months anyway, won't he? Saves a bit of cash, and less to assemble. I'm teaching Monday to Wednesday this week, then inset day on Thursday, which is good - planning time. What about you? Anything exciting planned? That sounds sensible, the Moses basket. Yes, he’ll be in with us initially, though your father’s already offering to ‘babysit’ in  his  armchair. The thought terrifies me. And no, not exciting. Just… work. Trying to finish that report before the end of the week. It's dreadful, completely dull. Though I did manage to catch up on ‘Happy Valley’ last night. Honestly, Sarah Lancashire is phenomenal, isn’t she? Oh, I’ve heard good things! Everyone’s talking about it. I’ve been too exhausted to watch anything proper lately. Just endless re-runs of ‘Great British Bake Off’ while marking. It's brain mush. Speaking of exhausting, little Finley was  particularly  energetic today. Apparently, he built a tower out of shoes. A very wobbly tower, according to Mrs. Davies. That sounds like Finley. He's a whirlwind, that boy. Bless him. It’s good you’re enjoying teaching though. You always were a natural with children. Do they still have that ridiculous dinosaur obsession? Oh, massive. It's all Tyrannosaurus Rex this week. I'm pretty sure I can recite the entire dinosaur family tree now.

… honestly, it were reet hectic last week. Mr. Henderson decided,  last minute , he wanted a falconry display at the corporate do. A  falconry display ! In a marquee! Can you imagine the paperwork? And convincing health and safety it weren't gonna be a disaster? Falconry, eh? Sounds posh. What kinda company were they, anyway? A financial investment firm. Loads o’ suits. They wanted somethin’ “unique”. Unique translates to “loads more work for me” usually. Honestly, I nearly lost it when they rang on Friday wanting to add a bouncy castle. A bouncy castle! With investors! Oh, bless you, Anya. You always get stuck with the… eccentric requests. I had a similar thing last month. A client wanted a ‘vintage telephone booth’ for photos. Like, a  functioning  one. Took me a week to even locate one. See? It’s always somethin’. And then they act like it’s just, like,  nothing  to organise. “Oh, just get a falconer, Anya, it’ll be grand.” Grand for  who  exactly?! Sounds stressful, yeah. My day’s a bit different. Bricklaying’s pretty straightforward, thankfully. Just…cold. It’s proper Baltic out there at the moment, even with all the layers. Got new gloves though, made a difference. Good. You need to look after yourself, Liam. That cold weather’s brutal. Are you still seeing Chloe? Yeah, things are… alright. Bit up and down, to be honest. She’s been a bit distant. I think she’s annoyed I haven’t got the cash for that weekend away she wanted. Oh, love. That’s rough. Women, eh? Always wantin’ a romantic getaway. Though, t’be fair, I wouldn't mind one meself. This job's drainin’. It's not just women, Anya. Everyone wants something! Liam, don't beat yourself up about it. A weekend away is a luxury, especially with everything being so expensive. Have you just talked to her about it? Tried. She kinda just shuts down. Says I don't understand her need for… I dunno, escapism or somethin’. Sounds a bit fancy for me, that. Escapism? Sounds like she needs a good cuppa and a natter, not a pricey hotel. Honestly, sometimes people just want to vent. Speaking o’ ventin’, I saw Jess the other day wearin’ this outfit… bright orange jumpsuit! Honestly, it were a crime against fashion. Oh my god, Jess? She has  interesting  taste. Remember that floral dress she wore to your birthday last year?

…No, no, I’m tellin’ ya, Doreen, it  has  to be a proper brew. None o’ this fancy fruit infusions, see? Makes a right mess o’ the colour, and don’t taste o’ nowt. Just…watery. Like dishwater, almost. Oh, Arthur, you’re such a stick-in-the-mud! A little chamomile never hurt anyone. Calming, it is. Especially after all the fuss with young Thomas and his scooter yesterday. Needed something to settle my nerves, I can tell you. Now, now, you two. A good cuppa is a serious business, I agree with Arthur there. But Doreen's right, variety is the spice of life, as they say. Though, personally, I lean towards an Earl Grey. Touch of bergamot, elevates the experience, don’t you think? Honestly, you’re all making a mountain out of a molehill. It’s tea! As long as it’s hot and there’s a biscuit to dunk, I’m happy. Though I do favour a builder's brew myself, strong enough to stand a spoon in. Reminds me of the staff room at school. Never a moment’s peace, always a pot on the go. Builder's brew, eh, Margaret? Now you’re talkin’. That’s got some backbone, that has. I used to get me mum to make it strong for me, when I was a lad. She’d say, “Arthur, you’ll strip the paint off the walls with that!” But I liked it like that. Used to warm ya right through on a cold Norfolk morning. Not like these flimsy teabags they sell nowadays. Oh, your mum sounds lovely, Arthur. Mine was always one for a delicate Darjeeling. Said it was 'civilised'. Always had a little silver strainer, she did. Never understood it, myself. Too much faff. Give me a Yorkshire Tea any day. Yorkshire Tea  is  a solid choice, Doreen. Reliable. Though I find it can be a little…ordinary. It lacks that certain…je ne sais quoi. It’s the little things, you know? The water temperature, the steeping time, the type of milk… These are crucial elements! Steeping time? Oh, honestly, Peter, you're such a perfectionist! I’ve never timed my tea. Just brew it until it looks dark enough, add milk and sugar, and get on with things. There’s only so much time in the day. Milk first or milk last, that’s the real debate, innit?

… honestly, the portions were ridiculous. I mean, enormous. You’d think they wanted you to  fail  at finishing it, just for the spectacle. And it all tasted…fine. Just…a lot. Sounds about right for The King’s Head. They’re all about quantity over quality, aren't they? Remember when Dad tried to do the ‘King’s Challenge’? Oh god,  that  was a sight. The man was beetroot red and sweating like he’d run a marathon. And Mum was mortified, absolutely mortified. Said he was going to give himself a heart attack for pub bragging rights. He’s always been a bit of a showman, your Dad. Though I’m fairly certain he just wanted to avoid paying for the meal. Speaking of which, is anyone else utterly baffled by the price of a pint these days? Six quid! It's daylight robbery. It is! And it’s not just London, is it? Even here, in relatively rural Norfolk, it’s creeping up and up. I was talking to one of my students – his dad runs The Red Lion – and he said the energy bills are crippling them. It’s everything, isn’t it? It’s not just the pub. Still, it’s hard to imagine a Friday night  not  involving a pub visit. It's ingrained, isn’t it? Though I did see something online about protests planned for next weekend… apparently targeting pub chains over their pricing. Protests? Really? About pints? Bit extreme, isn’t it? People are struggling, sure, but to protest about…a pint? People protest about everything these days, Rhys. It’s the modern way. Though, I confess, I’m more concerned about the new CRB checks they’re making us lecturers get. Apparently, they’re being much more thorough. It feels a bit intrusive, frankly. Oh, yes, I had my forms through. It’s the online searching that bothers me. They're trawling through everything. I mean, my student days were…spirited. Probably a few questionable Facebook photos lurking around somewhere. Don't worry, you were a good student, even if you occasionally cut a lecture to go to an art exhibition. Remember that Hockney exhibition in London? We practically lived at the Tate Modern that week. Honestly, it was worth skipping a few sociology lectures. Ah, London. Always a distraction. I've got a conference there next month, staying near Southbank. Hopefully, the hotel won’t be too…quirky.

… honestly, the paella was just…sad. Like, they clearly hadn’t used proper bomba rice. It was all mushy. And barely any seafood! You wouldn’t  believe . Anyway, how was your week in Cornwall? Did you actually manage to surf, or was it all bracing walks and cream teas? Mushy paella? That  is  tragic. You deserve better, honestly. And yes! I actually surfed! Well, “surfed” is a strong word. More like spectacularly fell off a board repeatedly for about an hour. But I stood up once! Once! It was glorious. And yes, bracing walks  and  multiple cream teas were definitely involved. Mum sent me home with a box of shortbread, naturally. Oh my god, a single stand-up is a win! Progress! And your mum and the shortbread… predictable, but lovely. I’m just, I’m so glad to be back. Work was… intense while I was gone. They decided mid-holiday to completely change the scope of the Henderson project. Ugh, not again! They do that  all  the time, don’t they? Seriously, are they deliberately trying to give you an aneurysm? What’s changed this time? Is it still vaguely related to marketing or have they decided you’re now in charge of astrophysics? Pretty much astrophysics, honestly. It’s now partially a user experience audit  and  they want me to spearhead a competitor analysis. Which, fine, I can do, but it’s completely outside my remit. And Ben from accounts keeps emailing me asking for budget justifications… he’s so passive aggressive, it’s exhausting. Ben is the  worst . Seriously, the man thrives on making people uncomfortable. Look, you need to just email your manager and say, “This is beyond my scope, I need support.” Don’t let them walk all over you. You’re brilliant at your job, you just need them to actually let you  do  it. How’s the house hunt going, by the way? Anything promising? I sent an email, actually. Vague, I admit. Something about needing clarity. Ben will probably still email me questioning the cost of staples. And the house hunt… bleak. Everything is either a shoebox or requires a mortgage the size of a small country. We saw that one in Totterdown, the one with the garden? Sarah and Liam said it was ‘quirky’. It was falling apart! Totterdown is… enthusiastic about its “quirkiness”. It usually translates to ‘structurally unsound’. We need to widen the search area.

…and honestly, the oncologist seemed…guarded. Not  negative , exactly, but not overly optimistic either. Saying it’s responding to the treatment is one thing, but the phrasing was all “stable” and “managing expectations.” You know how Sarah is, she'll latch onto any sliver of hope, and then crumble if it doesn’t pan out. Yeah, she’s a fighter, but she  needs  realistic information. Did they say anything about the next stage? The clinical trial, if she’s still eligible? They’re still assessing her for it. Apparently, there were a couple of… markers that weren't quite right in the initial tests. They’re running more. It's all so frustratingly slow. I just wish there was more  doing  and less  waiting . I offered to go with her to the next appointment, you know, just for moral support, but she said Ben was taking her. Good, Ben’s solid. He’s a good egg. It just…it feels so unfair, doesn’t it? She’s always been so vibrant, so full of energy. Remember that hiking trip we all did in the Lake District? She practically dragged us up Scafell Pike. She did. And complained the entire way, about her blisters and the weather, and then demanded a celebratory pub lunch at the bottom. God, those were the days. Right, enough doom and gloom. Let’s talk about something…more concrete. Have you had any luck with Rightmove? I spent an hour last night scrolling and just ended up overwhelmed. A bit. There’s one, Old Man Hemmings’ place, that’s just come on the market. Three bed, decent garden, needs some work, obviously, but structurally sound according to the estate agent. And it's within walking distance of the pub. Crucial, naturally. Hemmings’ place? Oh, that’s the one with the slightly wonky gable end, isn’t it? I always thought it looked a bit… precarious. That's a minor thing! A bit of pointing will sort it. Honestly, it's prime location. And it's  realistic . Everything else is either a complete wreck needing a full renovation, or astronomically overpriced. We’re not looking for a grand design project, are we? Just a comfy, manageable house. No, you’re right. Comfy and manageable. But is the garden south-facing? I need sun for my tomatoes. It's non-negotiable. Of course you do. Let me check… …looks like it gets the afternoon sun, so yes, tomato-friendly.

...Honestly, it's the posters, innit? Every single year. They stick 'em up  everywhere . On the doors, on the lifts, plastered all over the noticeboards. And they're always… aggressively bright. Like someone's vomited a rainbow onto a piece of card. It gives me a headache just lookin' at 'em.      Oh, you and the posters. It  is  a bit much, yeah. Especially when they’re advertising ‘Free Pizza & Mindfulness’. Like those two things naturally go together. It's the sheer volume, though, really. You can barely see the fire escape signs for all the flyers.      Exactly! Health and safety, see? That's  my  job to make sure everyone knows where to go in an emergency. How can they if it's buried under a mountain of discounted cinema tickets and notices about a ukulele society? Honestly, a ukulele society.      Alright, alright, lay off the ukulele society. Someone's gotta bring a bit of culture to Salford Quays. But yeah, I get your point. Mine's probably the constant noise complaints. It’s always the same flats, always after midnight. “Someone’s playing music too loud,” or “Someone’s having a party.”      Oh, don’t even get me started on the parties. Last week, someone was playing banging techno until 3 am. I had to go round, and they just looked at me like  I  was the bad guy for interrupting their fun. "It's a student union night, mate!" they said. Like that's an excuse for disturbing the whole building.      See! They treat it like it’s still freshers’ week, every week! And it’s not even just the music. It’s the shouting in the corridors, the doors slamming… I swear, some of them used to live in padded cells, the way they carry on. It’s exhausting mediating all that. Especially when they start trying to blame it on each other.      Aye, the blaming. That's a favourite. It's never their fault, is it? It's always "it were 'im" or "she started it." Makes you feel like you're back in primary school, breaking up playground scraps. I’d rather deal with a proper break-in, to be honest. At least then you know who you’re dealing with.      Don't say that! You'll jinx us. But I do see what you mean. It's the  petty  stuff that drains you. And the parents.

… honestly, seeing Brenda and Derek in Barcelona was  such  a shock. They were on one of those package tours, bless ‘em. All matching bucket hats and fanny packs. Derek insisted on speaking Spanish – terrible Spanish – to every shopkeeper. It was mortifying, but also… kinda sweet? Bucket hats, eh? Sounds about right for Derek. He always did like a bit of comfort. Package tours aren’t so bad though, are they? Gets you around. Though I can’t stand being herded like sheep. Give me wandering, getting lost, any day. Wandering’s lovely when you’ve got the time, Geoff. I haven’t had a proper holiday, just  wandering , in… well, decades. A weekend in Herne Bay doesn’t really count. Though I did find a lovely little shop there last month, reduced Christmas decorations already! Got a head start on the shopping, you see. Herne Bay? Really? I always thought it was a bit… faded glory, wasn’t it? Is it still full of retired folk and amusement arcades? Oh, it's changed a bit. Still got the arcades, naturally. And plenty of pensioners! But there’s a few nice cafes popping up. It's good for a quick shop if you don’t fancy the Brighton crowds. Speaking of which, have you even  started  Christmas shopping, Layla? Not really. I keep meaning to, but uni’s been hectic. This linguistics module is fascinating, though. Trying to learn Dutch now, because of the Antwerp trip next month. It's  hard . They put vowels in the weirdest places. Dutch? Fancy that. I tried a bit of German once, thought it’d be useful travelling. Gave up after about five minutes. Too many rules. I always preferred a bit of rhyming slang, myself. Keeps things interesting. You and your rhyming slang, Geoff! Still going on about ‘apples and pears’ and ‘trouble and strife’? It’s a lost art, I tell you! The youngsters don't understand. It's about being clever, isn't it? Using your wit. Speaking of youngsters, how's your cohort at university, Layla? Anyone interesting? It's a good group, actually. A few international students – a lot from China, surprisingly. It's good to have different perspectives. Though everyone's stressed about exams already. It feels like it's all deadlines and essays. Sounds familiar. Remember when Mark turned fifteen? The stress he was under with his GCSEs. He swore he’d never look at a textbook again.

...Honestly, Mum, I just don’t get why everyone’s making such a fuss about it. It’s just… letting people marry who they love, innit? Like, what’s the big deal? Old Mr. Henderson at school was going on about ‘the sanctity of marriage’ and it was just  so  cringe.      Cringe is a good word for it, love. Though, honestly, you’d think people would have moved on by now. It's not about ruining marriage, is it? It’s about  adding  to it. Giving more people the chance to have that happiness.      Exactly! I tried to tell him that, but he just went on about biblical this and traditional that. It's Ireland, though, right? I thought they'd already sorted all this stuff out. Isn't it a much more…liberal place than people give it credit for?      They’ve been fighting for it for years, darling. It’s a big deal  because  it took so long. Before, it was illegal. Can you imagine? Someone telling you you can’t marry the person you love, just because of who they are? It’s monstrous. And remember Auntie Moira’s friend, Siobhan? She and her wife had to go all the way to Canada to get married. Years ago.      Wow, really? That’s…grim. Still, it seems weird thinking about marriage anyway. Loads of people get divorced. Look at Uncle David and… well, you know.      Oh, don't you start on your Uncle David. That’s a whole other can of worms. And yes, people  do  get divorced. But that doesn't mean marriage isn't important to those who  want  it. It's about having the choice, isn’t it? Plus, honestly, your Uncle David’s problems weren’t about  marriage  being bad, they were about  him  being… well, let’s just say he wasn't the most considerate bloke.      No kidding! Remember that time he tried to serenade you with a recorder at your birthday party? That was legendary. You went absolutely  ballistic .      Don't remind me! The shame! Honestly, your Uncle David and your grandmother…they’re cut from the same cloth. Always have to have an opinion, and always have to share it, loudly. Speaking of birthdays, yours is next month, isn’t it? Are you thinking anything special?      I dunno. Maybe a laser quest thing with the lads? Or maybe just a massive pizza and a gaming marathon.

…No, no, you wouldn’t get away with that now, Patricia. Not with ‘em cameras everywhere. Though, mind you, young Timothy down the road, he  did  try and swap the sugar for salt in Mrs. Higgins’ tea. Nasty bit o’ work that was. Oh, Arthur, you and your stories! Timothy was always a little terror. But a hamster in a microwave? Honestly, David, you’re making things up. Just to wind us up, aren’t you? Not making it up at all, Patricia. It was a neighbour’s grandson, years ago. A particularly…creative child. Apparently, he was convinced Horace, the hamster, was poorly and needed ‘warming up’. Thankfully, the mother walked in before anything actually  happened . It was a right kerfuffle. Warming up? Good Lord. Poor little beast. Makes you wonder what goes on in these youngsters’ ‘eads. Reminds me o’ when I was a lad, we tried to make a rocket out of a jam jar and gunpowder… nearly blew me shed to smithereens, it did. Father weren’t best pleased. You and explosions, Arthur! It’s a wonder you made it to seventy-eight. Though, honestly, David, a hamster… it’s just so bizarre. Anyway, this quiche is lovely, wasn't expecting such a treat. Did you make it yourself? I did, actually. Found a recipe online. Trying to be a bit more adventurous in the kitchen. Less review reports, more rhubarb crumble, that’s my motto these days. Speaking of adventurous, Arthur, you were telling me about those lathe tools you were cleaning out? Found anything interesting? Oh, aye, the tools. Dustier than a mummy’s tomb, they were. Found me old skew chisel. Beautifully balanced bit o’ kit, that. Used to turn some lovely things with that, I did. Bowls, candlesticks… even a small rocking ‘orse for young Emily once. Emily loved that rocking horse, she did. Remember how she used to drag it everywhere? Leaving little dents in the furniture. Aye, a right little whirlwind she was. The skew chisel… it's a delicate thing, needs a proper hand. Nowadays, they all want these fancy computer-controlled ones. No soul in it, I reckon. You don't  feel  the wood when you’re letting a computer do all the work. There’s definitely something to be said for the traditional skills, Arthur. Though the precision of the modern ones is undeniable. It’s just a different approach.

…and honestly, the sheer arrogance of it! Charging five pence for a plastic bag. Five pence! Like it’s going to solve anything. It just feels like another little nibble at our pockets, doesn't it? It’s the principle, isn’t it? They claim it’s environmental, but I bet the cost of  administering  the charge outweighs any good it does. My mum was going on about it, refusing to pay, causing a right scene at Tesco. Classic. Oh, your mother. Always a firebrand. Though, I do agree with the sentiment. It’s performative activism, really. A tiny gesture to make people  feel  like something is being done. Reminds me a bit of all this fuss over American politics. Endless bluster, very little substance. Absolutely. I was reading an article about the debt ceiling… it’s just baffling. It feels like they’re deliberately courting disaster. And the way they talk about it… like it’s some kind of game. It’s horrifying, isn't it? Makes you appreciate relative stability, even with all our own little grievances. Speaking of grievances, have you seen house prices lately? Absolutely insane. We’re never going to be able to downsize to the coast at this rate. Don’t even  start  me on house prices. I was looking at places for… well, for potential future scenarios. Just researching. And even a tiny little bungalow in Dorset is beyond ridiculous. It’s criminal, really. Generations priced out. It's a disgrace, truly. When I retired, my pension combined with the house allowed for a comfortable life. Now, young people need two incomes  and  help from their parents just to get on the ladder. It’s a different world. It is. Though, you always managed brilliantly, Agnes. You built that school up from almost nothing. A proper legacy. Well, someone had to. Children deserve the best start, regardless of their background. Though, I sometimes wonder if I spent too much time ensuring everything was perfect and not enough time… enjoying life. Although, I did have Tibbles. Tibbles! Oh, I remember Tibbles. Your magnificent Maine Coon. I saw that story in the news today, about the cat that wandered into a brewery and started ‘working’ as a mouser. It reminded me of Tibbles, stalking through the garden like a tiny lion. A brewery? That's brilliant! They were giving him beer tokens as payment, apparently. Though, knowing cats, he'd probably trade them for a nap in a warm box.

…and honestly, Leo, I just think a bit of quiet time with a book wouldn’t go amiss. You’ve been glued to that Ninjago game for nearly three hours straight! Your eyes are going square. But Mummy! Zane’s got a new ice power and I  need  to unlock it! Kai needs upgrading, too. It’s really important! Yeah, and I’m building a super-secret base in Minecraft. It’s got a redstone elevator and everything. You wouldn’t understand. I probably wouldn’t. Although, I used to be quite good at Tetris, if that counts. Look, it’s not that I don’t want you to enjoy your games. They’re fantastic, creatively. But everything in moderation, alright? Remember when we visited Grandma last week and she was telling us about the new library in Norwich? They have a whole section just for Ninjago books, actually. Books about Ninjago? Really? Yes, really. They tell the backstory, show you how they train… things the game doesn’t always cover. It’s a different way to experience the story. Think about it. Minecraft has stories too. You just… build them. It's a different kind of story. I get that, Arthur, I really do. It’s amazing what you can create. But reading uses different bits of your brain, eh? It makes you imagine things yourself, build  your own  pictures. It’s good exercise for your imagination. But the game  is  imaginative! I’m pretending to  be  Kai! And I’m strategising, and… and building my skills! I know, darling, you are. And that's brilliant. But wouldn’t it be brilliant to then try and write your  own  Ninjago adventure? Or maybe design your own ninja? A book lets you do that. Can I still finish my elevator? It’s almost working. It keeps… sticking. Of course, you can finish your elevator. But how about a deal? Thirty more minutes on Minecraft, then twenty pages of reading, and  then  back to the game. Sound fair? Twenty pages feels like  loads . It’s not, love. It's just a chapter or two. We can even read one together. Maybe one about Cole? You love Cole, don't you? He's the earth ninja. Solid as a rock. Can  I  have thirty minutes of Lego, then read a Minecraft wiki page? That’s kind of reading, right? It tells you how to make really cool stuff.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of people at the Colosseum was just  ridiculous . It felt less like experiencing history and more like being herded cattle. Still, Rome was lovely, though. Truly lovely. Did you two manage to get anything useful done while I was gallivanting around Italy? Useful? Mum, you were gone for ten days! I practically lived at the shop. It was half term, remember? Absolute chaos. Little Timmy Hargrave tried to swap price tags again. Honestly, some kids… Sounds about right. I had a mountain of essays to get through, actually. Dissertation research is… absorbing, to put it mildly. I finally finished the initial literature review though, so that’s a win. It felt like it would never end. How was the food in Rome? You always go on about the food. Oh, the food! Don’t even get me started. Carbonara that genuinely tasted of  carbon , not just cream and bacon. And the pizza… forget everything you think you know about pizza. It’s just another level. I brought back a little something for you both, actually. In the shopping bag by the door. Not food, sadly. Just… little trinkets. Ooh, lovely! I always appreciate a trinket. Though, honestly, a full-sized Margherita would have been welcome too. Did you at least bring back some limoncello? No limoncello, I’m afraid. I thought of you, but I knew it wouldn’t survive the journey in my suitcase. Speaking of surviving, how are you both doing, really? Work must be draining, Liv, and you, Chloe, look a bit pale. Still working those late nights on the thesis? Yeah, pretty much. It's just… a lot. Trying to balance everything - part-time job to pay the rent, and then this. It's fine, though. I mean, it  will  be fine. Just need to get through this initial stage. It’s the same at the shop. The new assistant is… enthusiastic, let’s say. But requires a  lot  of supervision. And Mrs. Peterson keeps asking for things that we definitely don’t stock. Like swan-shaped biscuits. Swan-shaped biscuits! Oh dear. Sounds stressful. Right. Enough of that. We're supposed to be relaxing. I thought we could have a potter around Lichfield this afternoon? There’s that new antique shop opened on Bird Street, and I know Chloe you've been wanting to look at some vintage jewellery. That sounds really nice, actually.

… honestly, Mr. Harrison is taking the mickey. Giving us three essays  and  a practical for next week? It’s ridiculous. Especially after that history test on Tuesday. I barely slept. Tell me about it. He's proper wound up lately, isn’t he? Think it’s because old Mrs. Davies retired? She always covered for him when he was late marking. Ooh, true! She was a lifesaver. Though honestly, Harrison’s marking is always… questionable. Like, how  I  got a C on that poetry analysis is beyond me. It was a masterpiece! A masterpiece, eh? You and your dramatic flair, Chloe. Anyway, this sandwich is… functional. Just bread and cheese. Mum clearly wasn't feeling inspired this morning. Yours look alright, Raj. It's a chicken salad from Greggs. Can't go wrong, can ya? Though it’s kinda depressing that this is a highlight of the week. We’re sixth form! Shouldn’t we be, I don’t know, debating the merits of Sartre over gourmet sandwiches? Speaking of depressing, did you see what happened on the news last night? That thing in…where was it? Sudan? Absolutely awful. My uncle was telling me about his time in the army, and it just… it makes you think. He wouldn't talk about specifics, just said things are never black and white. My grandad was in the army. He never talked about it either. Just said it "hardened" him. Bit scary, that. It's mad to think people are dealing with that right now, while we're arguing about sandwich fillings. Yeah, it’s a bit… jarring. Still, gotta focus on surviving Harrison, right? Fancy a game of Magic while we finish up? I've been testing out this new deck. Ooh, yes! I need to beat you both. You’ve been gloating all week since beating me last time. Although, honestly, I think Ben in our class is secretly cheating. He  always  pulls the winning card. It's suspicious. Ben? Nah. He's just lucky. Besides, he’s too busy trying to impress Prefect Johnson. Seriously, that guy thinks he's God's gift to Slough Grammar. Johnson is a joke. All power, no substance. He spends more time polishing his badge than actually  doing  anything. Remember when he tried to stop Liam from wearing a band t-shirt? Called it “inappropriate attire”. Oh my god, yes! The irony!

…and honestly, Miss Davies just  stared  at me. Like I’d grown a second head when I said I didn’t understand chain rule. It's just… numbers, innit? Why does it have to be so complicated? Oh, God, Miss Davies. She's the worst for that. The judging stare. It's like, we're all meant to be mini-Einsteins or something. Did you ask her to go through it again? Yeah, but she just sort of… re-explained it the  same  way. Slower. Which doesn't help if you didn’t get it the first time, does it? Honestly, Mr. Henderson is miles better. He actually tries to make it make sense. He used, like, a rollercoaster as an example once. Mr. Henderson  is  good. He's the only reason I haven't completely failed physics. Though, let's be real, I'm still probably going to scrape a C. Have you heard anything about what Mrs. Thompson’s doing about the reading lessons? She said she was going to 'shake things up', but all she’s done so far is make us read poetry. Ugh, poetry. Don’t even. I’d rather be doing integration. Seriously. It's always stuff no one actually cares about, like Wordsworth rambling about daffodils. I mean, what’s the point? Exactly! It’s all just…flowery language. And then she asks us what it  means . Like, it's a daffodil, Mrs. Thompson. It’s yellow. Done. Speaking of pointless, have you seen Poppy Millington trying to act all mature since getting a boyfriend? Oh, don't even  start  on Poppy. She's convinced she’s in a rom-com. She keeps sighing and looking dramatically out the window. Honestly, she's trying way too hard. Remember when she tripped over her own feet in the canteen last week? Totally ruined the ‘mysterious, lovelorn’ vibe. Oh my god, yes! And then blamed it on the uneven flooring! It was hilarious. It reminds me of that film, '17 Again'. Remember that? Matthew Perry turning back into a teenager? Oh yeah! I love that film. Imagine Mr. Lewis, our form tutor, as the teenage version of himself. The chaos! He’d probably just spend all day eating crisps and winding everyone up. Oh,  definitely . And trying to play pranks on Mrs. Davies. That would be brilliant. So, you reckon he’d be trying to sneak into a sixth form party then?

… honestly, I still can’t believe you’re actually going through with it, Chloe. Laser eye surgery? Sounds proper terrifying, innit? Terrifyingly  liberating , Leo. Honestly, I'm so done with contacts. Plus, think of the holiday photos! No squinting, no reflections… pure, unadulterated vision. It’s happening next month. Good on ya, love. It’s a big step, but if it’ll make you feel better, then go for it. How’s work been, by the way? Still slinging sourdough like nobody’s business? You know it, Maisie. Absolute chaos this week. Wedding cake orders are insane. I swear, everyone’s getting married this summer. Keeps me busy, though. Keeps the bills paid. Liam – that’s the Aussie – he’s been helping out a lot. He's a lifesaver. Just doing my bit, eh? Gotta earn my keep. Though, you British lot and your cake… it’s a serious business. Back home, a cake’s just… a cake. Bit of icing, maybe some sprinkles. You lot turn it into architectural masterpieces. He’s not wrong, actually. Chloe’s cakes are works of art. Proper Instagrammable. Speaking of art, have we finalised Transylvania then? Because I need to book flights. Oh! Transylvania! Yes! I was looking at flights this morning. I found some decent ones, landing in Cluj-Napoca. It’s the best access point, yeah? That sounds right. I’ve been doing a bit of reading about it. Honestly, it’s less Dracula and more… medieval towns and beautiful countryside. I’m hoping for proper castles. Don’t want to go all that way and just see touristed bits. Crikey, castles! Sounds brilliant. Although, I still reckon Dracula’s real. Just… hides really well. We got any idea what we’re doing once we get there? Just winging it? I was thinking a bit of both. Cluj-Napoca for a day, then rent a car and just… explore. Bran Castle, obviously. And maybe some of those salt mines I read about? Sound a bit mad, but apparently, they’re incredible. The salt mines sound amazing! And Liam was telling me about some hiking trails in the Carpathian mountains. Said the views are insane. He’s been travelling a lot, he’s got loads of insider knowledge. Ooh, hiking. I'm in. Although, knowing me, I’ll be complaining after five minutes. Fancy a trip to the pub this weekend? Need a proper catch-up, just the four of us.

…and honestly, the playlist needs a serious overhaul. Too much of  that  repetitive dance stuff, not enough stuff we all actually  like . Remember how good it was at Auntie Carol’s, with the mix of everything? Can we have ‘Shiny’ on there? From  Moana ? ‘Shiny’? Oh, Ursula’s song! That’s a good shout, darling. Absolutely. We can definitely have ‘Shiny’ on. Leo, any requests? Can we have the one with the really loud drums? The one where the man yells? Oh, Lord. That'll be… Rage Against the Machine? Possibly not for a children’s party, love. Though, actually, maybe  one  track… no, bad idea. We'll stick to ‘Shiny’ and things a bit less…enthusiastic. So, playlist – sorted-ish. Right, photos. I was thinking we could try and recreate some of the  Alice in Wonderland  photos Grandad took of me when I was your age. Remember those, Leo? I had the blue dress… The one with the big bow? You looked like a princess! I did rather! We could do some with you two as the Mad Hatter and the Queen of Hearts. Though I suspect getting you to wear a crown may be a battle. I  want  to be the Queen of Hearts! I can shout “Off with their heads!” Woah there! Perhaps just a strongly worded “Please be quiet” instead, hmm? No actual 'off with their heads' talk. We don't want to give Grandma a heart attack. I'm thinking we do these photos  before  the party, while everyone is still relatively clean. Which brings me to…the obstacle course. Yessss! The muddy one! Yes, the wonderfully muddy obstacle course. But  after  the photos. Absolutely. And then a good wash down. Now, I ordered pizza, but I was also thinking of doing some of those little sausage rolls everyone loves. Should we go for sausage rolls? Yes! And crisps! And dip! Crisps and dip it is. Right, I need to quickly check the helium tank for the balloons. And remember, no swearing! Even accidentally. I caught Leo saying ‘blooming’ last week, and it’s a slippery slope, honestly. But Dad said… Dad says a  lot  of things, darling. But at a children’s party, we keep the language… polite. Speaking of Dad… he promised to help me set up the aerial hoop in the garden. He’s convinced he can still get up there. Is it the shiny one?

…and honestly, the pressure these kids are under now is just…immense. It wasn't like this when  I  did my O-Levels. Though, admittedly, I probably wasn’t paying enough attention back then either. So, Chloe, how did  you  feel waiting for those GCSE results? You seemed pretty calm, actually. I was bricking it, honestly. Everyone was talking about needing 7s and 8s for everything, even just to get onto A-Levels. It's ridiculous. I just wanted to get decent grades, you know? Not become a genius. Yeah, same! I kept checking UCAS like every five minutes. It was driving Mum mad. Brickin’ it, eh? That’s a good way to put it. Back in my day, passin’ was good enough. Didn’t need all these fancy numbers. Though, mind you, I weren’t exactly aiming for Oxford University, were I? Spent most of my time down the river, fishin’. Good times. Simple times. Oh, don't romanticize it too much, Arthur. You were “helping your mother” – which meant avoiding work! And we didn’t have the expectations these girls have now. It’s a different world. Still, good grades are important, though. Did you both get what you needed for what you want to do? I got a 7 in English Lit, which I’m really happy with, and mostly 6s and a couple of 8s. Enough for what I want to do, thankfully. I got mostly 6s and 7s too, a bit disappointed about Maths, but I can retake it if I need to. I’m thinking about doing Art and Design. Excellent! That sounds fantastic. Anything creative is good. Now, speaking of pressure, has anyone asked about driving lessons yet? Your mother’s been dropping hints all week, Chloe. Don't even! Gran keeps showing me articles about young drivers and accidents. It's terrifying. She keeps saying, “Think of your Auntie Brenda….” Auntie Brenda were a right terror behind the wheel, I’ll give ‘er that. Nearly ran old Mr. Henderson into a hedge once. Though she blamed  him  for standin’ in the road. Oh, Arthur! You always have a story. Honestly, she was just a bit… enthusiastic. Chloe, your grandmother just worries. And it  is  a good idea to learn, you know? Independence. Freedom. I think I want to learn too, eventually. But maybe after A-Levels. I don’t want to think about parallel parking right now.

…and honestly, the raspberries are looking remarkably good this year. Despite this dreadful weather. Honestly, one minute sunshine, the next a downpour. It’s enough to give you a headache, isn’t it? You wouldn’t believe the slugs though, absolutely  ravaging  the hostas. Yeah, it’s been a weird summer. I was reading something about microclimates earlier - apparently Northamptonshire's got a lot of them. Explains why your garden’s doing so well while Mrs. Higgins down the road is complaining about everything dying. Microclimates, eh? Sounds a bit fancy for gardening, doesn’t it? I just chuck some slug pellets down and hope for the best. Speaking of fancy, are you still obsessed with that… Xiangqi, is it called? Chinese chess? You know I am, Kevin! It’s a lovely distraction. And it  is  fascinating. Though, young Daniel, you’re far too quick. You’ve got me on the back foot again. It’s just pattern recognition, honestly. Reminds me of analysing sentence structure, actually. Spotting weaknesses, anticipating moves…similar skillset, really. Bit different to teaching absolute beginners though. They struggle with the present perfect, let alone strategic thinking. Oh, I can imagine! I remember trying to explain tenses to little Timmy last week. Bless him, he just wanted to build with the Lego. Now, are you two still thinking about going to South Korea, Daniel? You mentioned it a while ago. Planning stages. Trying to work out tuition fees, mostly. It's a bit of a shock, even with scholarships. Seems like they’ve hiked them up again. Tuition fees…back in my day, you got a grant. Simple as that. Now it’s a mortgage just to learn a few things. My Sarah was saying something about it for young Jamie. Dreadful. Still, better a degree than nothing, I suppose. Absolutely.
