Sea, sand, and a good book. Can’t beat it. Bournemouth’s alright. A bit… predictable though, isn't it? We did Blackpool once, back in the 70s.

…and honestly, the way he was building with those Duplo blocks this afternoon, you’d swear he was an architect already. A very messy architect, mind you, blocks  everywhere . But still, impressive for a little fella. They are amazing at that age, aren’t they? Leo spent all of last week trying to build a tower as tall as himself. It kept collapsing, naturally, and he’d just get more determined. It was quite a sight. How was your walk with Cillian, David? Did he manage to stay upright for the whole thing? Relatively! There was…an incident involving a puddle. A  large  puddle. And a complete lack of awareness of its existence until he was knee-deep in it. Himself and I were soaked, naturally. He thought it was hilarious. Puddles are the best! I jumped in one on the way back from school last week. Mum wasn’t too pleased, though. She said I’d catch my death. Mothers always say that, don’t they? It's a biological imperative. David, you should have seen the state of Leo after he ‘helped’ me wash the car. He didn’t  help  so much as attempt to dismantle the hose pipe. Sounds about right. Boys will be boys, eh? Though, Cillian’s more into the soft toys lately. He’s had that little lion, Rory, practically glued to his hand all week. It's a bit odd, wouldn’t you say? He usually goes for things he can bang together. Soft toys are alright, I guess. I used to have a dinosaur, Rex, but I grew out of him. Now I’m more into… well, video games mostly. I was playing this new RPG all afternoon, ‘Eldoria Online’. It’s amazing! You build this character and… Now, now, let’s not overwhelm David with talk of online games. He’s just trying to get through a walk with a puddle enthusiast. What's it  about , this game, then? No need for all the technical details. It’s about saving the kingdom from this dark lord. You level up and get better weapons and stuff. It’s got a really good story. And you can play with your mates online. Sounds…involved. A bit different from building block towers, anyway. Cillian's fixated on Rory, though. He's giving him tea – imaginary tea, thankfully – and reading him stories. I caught him trying to put Rory to bed  in his own cot .

…and honestly, the sheer volume of glitter on that angel was astonishing. Little Chloe practically  glowed  with smug satisfaction. You’d think she’d invented glitter herself! Glitter, eh? Gets everywhere, that stuff. Like a stubborn rash. Reminds me o' me Doris, always coverin' everything in doilies. Everythin'. Couldn't  see  the table for the doilies. Oh, Arthur, you and Doris! You two were a pair. Though, I must say, a bit of festive cheer never hurt anyone. Speaking of which, are we still on for doing the Christmas dinner at your place this year, Arthur? I'm happy to bring the pudding, of course. Well, I ain't gettin' any younger, am I? The kitchen's a bit…cramped. Especially with all o' you lot. But alright, alright. We can manage. Just no glitter, mind. And someone's gotta help me with the spuds. I can peel potatoes, Mr. Arthur! I'm really good at it now, Mum says so. Good girl, Rosie. You and… what's her name? Your friend? The one with the horses? That's Maisie, Mr. Arthur. She’s waiting in the car. She couldn't come in, she's a bit… shy. Maisie's a lovely girl. Very passionate about her riding. She was telling me all about her new mare. It's a beautiful thing, apparently. Oh, horses. I used to love riding when I was a girl. My dad wouldn’t let me have one, said it was too expensive. Ruined my childhood, it did! Don’t tell anyone I said that. Expensive, eh? Everything's expensive these days. Even gettin' the car serviced. Took it down to Stan's last week, and he nearly had a heart attack when he saw the bill. Said the timing belt needed doin'. Timing belt! As if it had a schedule to keep! Stan’s a bit of a rogue, isn't he? Always finding something "urgent" that needs fixing. You've got to get a second opinion with him. Mum, can I tell you about Liam? He… he asked me to the cinema on Friday. Oh, Rosie, that's lovely! Liam, is it? He seems a nice boy. What film are you seeing? It’s… it's a scary one. He likes scary films. I’m a little bit scared, actually. Ooh, exciting! Is it the new one with the… the spooky clown? Yeah!

… honestly, Mrs. Higgins nearly had a fit when I suggested she try a pressure bandage for her swollen ankle. “Oh, a  nurse  thinks she knows best, does she?” Honestly, the woman’s stubborn. Could’ve saved her a trip to A&E, I reckon. You and Mrs. Higgins, always a battle of wills. She just doesn't like being told what to do, even if it’s for her own good. Reminds me of your mother, actually. Speaking of stubborn… I’m still trying to get Dad to understand the concept of targeted ads. He thinks Facebook is actively  listening  to him. He was telling me yesterday he mentioned wanting new gardening gloves and BAM, an advert. It's algorithms, Dad! Algorithms! Bless him. He’s a generation that doesn't quite get it, does he? Makes you feel ancient sometimes, doesn’t it? Though, I must admit, I’m no tech wizard either. You’re the one who explained to me how to video call Mum last Christmas. I'm fairly competent, I think. Although, this new smart fridge... that's just showing off. It tells me when I'm running low on milk. Like I can't  see  when the milk's gone. Right, who wants stew and dumplings? It’s nearly ready. Ooh, stew and dumplings! Yes, please. That’s proper comfort food. Perfect for a chilly evening. It's a world away from the salad I had at lunch. Trying to be ‘healthy’ for five minutes. Didn't last. Healthy’s overrated. Especially when you’re on a twelve-hour shift chasing doctors and dispensing meds. I ran on biscuits and coffee today, and frankly, I was thriving. Speaking of thriving, how did that meeting with the new client go today, love? Actually, it went really well. Landed the account. They're a small chain of care homes, needing marketing assistance. Good fit for us. Means a bit more pressure, but the finances are solid. Brilliant! That’s fantastic news. You deserve a treat. Though, knowing you, the treat will be a new spreadsheet. Harsh! Perhaps. Though, you’re right. I’m a bit of a workaholic. Now, about your birthday, Lucy. We've still not sorted a present. Any ideas? Honestly? I don't want anything extravagant. Maybe just a voucher for that spa in Tunbridge Wells. A massage would be heavenly after the week I've had.

…No, I’m tellin’ ya, Doreen, this ‘ere heating, it’s a right disgrace. Used to be you could rely on a good frost to get things movin’, now it’s just…damp. Damp and chilly. Makes yer bones ache somethin’ awful. Oh, Arthur, you say that every year. You were sayin’ it last November, remember? And the year before. It IS chilly, mind you, but we’ve got layers. And Bertie keeps us warm enough, don’t you, boy?  [She pats a small terrier sitting at her feet]  Frankly, the whole infrastructure is falling apart. The electricity grid is barely holding together. Remember that outage last February? No power for a whole day. Honestly, felt like going back to the Stone Age. I was on a Zoom call with a client in Frankfurt, utterly disastrous. Stone Age, Nigel? You and your Zoom calls! Though you’re right, it was a bit of a palaver. I ended up using my mobile as a hotspot. Younger generations wouldn't cope, would they? All glued to their screens, reliant on everything working perfectly. Remember  Big Brother ? They’d have a meltdown.  Big Brother ? That were telly, weren’t it? All a load o’ rubbish, if you ask me. Givin’ folks ideas above their station. Now, there were this woman at the shops…old Mrs. Higgins, she were tellin’ me about her niece. Apparently, she's run off with a married man. A  married  man, can you believe it? Oh, Arthur, don’t start on the affairs! It’s all just… sadness, really. People searching for somethin’ they ain’t gettin’ at home. Though, a mistress… honestly, the scandal. Still, Mrs. Higgins always had a keen eye for gossip. It’s a symptom of societal decline, I tell you. Lack of commitment. Lack of… moral fibre. Speaking of commitment, are you two still planning on going to the village fete next Saturday? Millie’s doing a stall, selling her jams. We are, Nigel. Though last year was a bit of a washout, wasn't it? Still, good to get out and see people. Doreen, are you bringing your scones again? Everyone raves about them. Possibly. If I feel up to it. I was thinkin’ of nipping into Harrow Town Centre tomorrow for a bit of shoppin’. Need some new dog treats for Bertie, and maybe a little something for myself. Though, honestly, they don’t make things like they used to.

…and honestly, tha' was just  awful . Like, genuinely dreadful. All that build-up for nowt. Honestly, I think they just threw a load of CGI at it and hoped for the best. You're still on about ‘Galactic Frontier’? I thought it looked…okay, from the trailer. A bit overdone, maybe. Okay?! Okay?! Chloe, it were  rubbish . Remember how excited I was? I’d been telling everyone about it for weeks. Proper build-up. And then… nothing. Flat characters, predictable plot. It felt like they'd nicked bits from Star Wars and Avatar and mashed 'em together. Harsh, but fair enough. You’re a tough critic. I’m more easy-going when it comes to that stuff. Especially after a long week. Though, admit it, the special effects  did  look impressive. Aye, visually it were alright. But a good film's more than just pretty pictures, innit? It needs a heart. This 'ad none. Reminded me of that one we saw at uni, that awful space opera thing… what was it called? ‘Nebula Knights’? Oh god, don’t remind me. That was objectively terrible. Remember Ben falling asleep halfway through and snoring so loudly Professor Davies had to ask him to leave? Aye! Poor Ben. He said he’d stayed up all night finishing an essay. Anyway, speaking of terrible things… how was your Mum’s birthday do? You said it was a bit… chaotic? Chaotic is putting it mildly. Aunt Susan decided to ‘spice things up’ with a karaoke machine. You know how tone-deaf she is. And then Uncle Barry got into a debate with Dad about Brexit  again . It was a masterclass in awkwardness. Oh dear God. Sounds like a classic family gathering, then. My nan’s turning eighty next month, and I’m already bracing myself for a similar level of… drama. She's already hinting she wants a full brass band. A  brass band , Chloe! In my back garden! A brass band? That’s…ambitious. Maybe you can subtly suggest a smaller ensemble? Or a DJ? My cousin used a silent disco at his wedding, that went down surprisingly well. A silent disco for an eighty-year-old? I don't think so! She’d have a heart attack trying to figure out the headphones. No, I think I’m just going to have to accept my fate and pretend to enjoy the oompah. So, you free next weekend for a proper catch-up?

…and honestly, lad, I just think it’s all a bit of a mess, isn’t it? Another referendum. After the last one? It feels like they’re just going round in circles. Though, I suppose folk feel strongly about it, don't they? Aye, well, a few of the lads at school are proper into it, like. Mostly for independence, they are. They reckon it’s about taking control back, being their own country. Taking control back… Aye, that’s the tune they always play, isn't it? It sounds good, doesn’t it? But control of  what , exactly? And at what cost? You’ve got to think about the practicalities, Ethan. Beyond the flags and the slogans. I remember the last time around, 2014, the worry about what’d happen with the currency… all that. They were talkin’ about that at school. About keepin’ the pound, or startin’ a new one. But apparently, it’s complicated with the banks and stuff. Complicated is an understatement! It's a right tangle, it is. Look, I'm a maths examiner, remember? I deal in things being neat and tidy, in solutions. This… this is far from neat and tidy. And think about borders, lad. What happens to the border with England? Seamless? Checked? It’s not just about waving a Saltire. They said it’d be like… the Schengen Area, like in Europe. Open borders. Europe! There you go. Already bringing Europe into it! See, that's the thing. It's all interconnected. It's not a simple ‘yes’ or ‘no’. I remember me dad, bless him, he was a staunch Labour man, and he was completely torn about it. He loved Scotland, went up to the Highlands every year for his holidays. But he was worried about the economic impact. He said, "Elsie," - he always called me Elsie - "it's all well and good wanting independence, but can they  afford  it?" So, you think it’s a bad idea then? I’m not saying it's a  bad  idea, Ethan. I’m saying it’s hugely complex and needs a proper, hard look. It's not something to rush into based on emotion. And the SNP have been… well, let’s just say their record's not spotless, is it? They've had issues with things like the ferries and the NHS. You’ve got to look at the whole picture.

…and honestly, she’s blaming  him  for bein’ a liar? Look at ‘er face! She’s a right one, isn't she? Oh, come on, Elle. You say that every time someone looks vaguely shifty on this show. It’s Jeremy Kyle, what do you expect? Everyone's a bit of a… character. It's just… exhausting, isn’t it? All the shouting. I don’t know how they find people this dramatic. It's like they audition for sadness. Nah, it's the lies, innit? That's what gets me. They're all at it. And then the lie detector… pure theatre. You know it's rigged somehow. Rigged or not, it's addictive. I swear, I shouldn't be watchin' this but I am. It's like a train wreck, you just can’t look away. It's not just the lies, it's  how  they tell ‘em. Listen to that woman. She’s droppin’ her ‘h’s like it’s goin’ outta fashion. “E’s a liar,” she just said. “E!” It's… it's almost performative, isn’t it? Like they think soundin’ rougher makes ‘em believable. Oh, you and your accent obsession, Elle! You’re always pickin’ apart how people talk. You're the queen of elision, yourself, mind. Remember that time you tried to order a “cuppa” in France and the waiter had no idea what you meant? That’s different! That was cultural misunderstanding! This is deliberate. They're changin' how they speak. It's all a bit… Susan Boyle, trying to sound more 'proper' when they think they should. I think you're overthinkin’ it a bit. People just speak differently depending on where they are, or who they’re talkin’ to. I find myself speakin’ more carefully when I’m with me gran. It's not about 'performin', it's about politeness. She’s got a point, Elle. It’s like, when I'm back in Wakefield, I automatically slip back into full Yorkshire. All the ‘tha’s and ‘thee’s and whatnot. Then when I’m here in Chester, I tone it down a bit. Don't want to sound like a right alien, do ya? Yeah, exactly. An’ listen, that fella’s got a right Scouse twang, doesn’t he? Proper strong. You can tell straight away he’s from around ‘ere, like you, Liv. You can’t mistake it!

Honestly, that was a  terrible  tackle. Absolutely reckless. They’ll be lucky if he doesn't get a red card. Though, to be fair, the ref's been letting a lot go today. Yeah, pretty rough. Bit much, even for the Premier League. Still, makes a change from watching endless adverts for…what  is  that, anyway? Some kind of protein shake for pigeons? Don’t be daft! It's for… athletes? Apparently boosts recovery. Though I’d rather boost my recovery with a nice cup of tea and a bit more yarn, to be honest. This scarf needs finishing before the Olympics start. Olympics! Right. Are you still convinced you can knit Team GB a full set of bobble hats in time? Last time I checked, you’d barely finished one stripe. I'm making good progress! It’s a  big  scarf, alright? And bobble hats are… ambitious. Maybe wrist warmers. Or little flags. Something manageable. Though, speaking of the Olympics, have you seen the gymnastics line-up? Proper inspiring, that. It is. Incredible athleticism. Makes my PhD work feel… a little less important, suddenly. All those hours spent staring at spreadsheets, while they’re flipping and twisting and defying gravity. Och, your work is important! Don't be putting yourself down. Besides, spreadsheets are a kind of puzzle, aren't they? Just a slightly less… acrobatic one. Remember when your mam used to knit you those awful, itchy jumpers for Christmas? You looked like a walking spreadsheet back then, all squares and geometric patterns. Please don’t remind me. The beige one with the reindeer? That was a low point. I swore I’d never wear anything knitted again until I met you. And even then, it was a slow conversion. See? Knitting wins eventually. It's a silent, patient art. Kind of like research, in a way. You put in the hours, and eventually, a beautiful thing emerges. Although, sometimes it just unravels completely. Good analogy. Speaking of emerging things… have you given any more thought to baby names? We’re getting closer to needing those, aren't we? Oh, don't start me! I keep falling down rabbit holes on naming websites. I want something… strong. But not  too  strong. Definitely not a footballer’s name. No Rooneys or Beckhams, thank you very much. Fair enough. I was thinking maybe something a bit classic? Arthur? Edward? They feel solid, you know?

…Honestly, the bit where Barry B. Benson sues the humans is  genius . It’s such a clever premise, isn’t it? Though, explaining the concept of lawsuits to you two is probably a bit much for a Tuesday evening.      Bees are funny! They make honey. Can we have honey on our toast tomorrow?      But they sting! My friend Leo got stung and he cried  really  loud.      They only sting if they feel threatened, sweetie. And usually, they’re too busy making honey. Which, actually, brings me to thinking… Royal jelly. Do you know what royal jelly is? It's what they feed baby queen bees.      Is that why kings and queens eat posh fruits? Like, really posh?      That’s a good question! Well, historically, I suppose. They did have access to the best fruits, because they… owned everything. Or, rather, the country owned it, but  they  got to enjoy the best bits. Strawberries for Queen Victoria, pineapples for…well, lots of them, apparently. They were showing off.      So, like King Arthur? Did he eat posh strawberries?      King Arthur’s a bit… complicated. Some people think he was real, some people think he was a story. Either way, he probably had access to good food. It was a sign of power. All those feasts! But now… paying £30 a head to walk around Buckingham Palace? Honestly!      But it's pretty! Mummy, we went! Remember the sparkly bits?      I do, darling. It  is  pretty. But it feels a bit… odd, doesn't it? That we’re paying to see where people live just because their ancestors happened to be in the right place at the right time. Makes you think about being a republic, doesn't it? No kings or queens, just…a president or something.      I want to be a king! Then I can have all the strawberries!      You could be a politician, maybe. That’s a different way to have influence. Though, probably more paperwork. It's not all posh strawberries and sparkly bits, believe me!      Can politicians have honey?      I imagine they can. Though, I’d hope they’re also taking their vitamins. You two need to finish your spinach, you know. Important for growing strong.      Spinach tastes like grass!      It does not! It tastes… green. Look, we're changing the subject. Remember we’re going to see the diving at the Olympic Stadium next week?      Ooh, yes! All the splashes!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of things your father has accumulated! It’s like he was preparing for the apocalypse, not just downsizing for a smaller place. Did you see the five different types of sandpaper? Sandpaper, lad! What does one man  need  with five different grits? Aye, he's always been a bit of a hoarder, hasn’t he? Though I think it’s less apocalypse prepping and more ‘you never know when it might come in handy’. He’s like that with everything. Remember the box of bottle caps he saved for years? Bottle caps?! Seriously? What for? He told me once he was going to build a mosaic. A mosaic of… well, I don’t actually remember  what  he was going to make a mosaic of. Something significant, I'm sure. He always has a grand plan, doesn’t he? A mosaic! Oh, that’s rich. He couldn’t build a bird table without needing assistance, let alone a mosaic. Honestly, I’m surprised the tip didn’t charge us by the weight. And the smell! Goodness gracious, some of that stuff should have been dealt with decades ago. Speaking of things needing dealing with, how are you feeling about the move, Margaret? Still nervous? You've lived in that house for… well, forever. Nervous doesn't even begin to cover it, love. It's not the  moving  that bothers me, it’s leaving all the memories behind. That house… it’s seen everything. Your father and I, the children growing up, Christmas dinners, everything. And finding a flat that doesn’t feel… sterile. All these new builds look the same. No character. We’re trying to find something with a bit of a garden for you, Mum. You’ll miss your roses. Miss them terribly. Though, truthfully, my back isn't what it used to be. Kneeling to deadhead… a genuine ordeal now. Perhaps a small patio garden would be sensible. Though, I saw a rather lovely window box display in Thirsk the other week. Really bright geraniums… it gave me an idea. Thirsk? That’s ages away, isn’t it? Did you go to the races? He didn't go to the races, love. He went to visit old Mrs. Ainsworth. She's not been well. She used to teach me history, you know. A fearsome woman, but a brilliant teacher. She still remembers every date.

… honestly, the Walker's parking is a joke, innit? I spent twenty minutes circling yesterday just to get a space for that meeting with Mrs. Davies. Twenty minutes! And she was late anyway. You and parking, Liam. It's a lifelong battle. You know you could get the train, right? It's literally right there. Aye, I know, I know. But then I'm relying on the train being on time, and well, you know… Northern Rail. It’s a gamble, love. Speaking of Mrs. Davies, how’s the teaching going? Any little terrors in your class this week? It's...fine. Honestly, draining. Year 7 are a whirlwind. Little bundles of energy, mostly directed at disrupting everything. But I had a breakthrough with young Leo today. He finally grasped the concept of relative clauses. Small wins, eh? How was your day? Apart from the parking saga. Not bad, not bad. Prep for the new intake next term. It’s always a bit hectic. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if I should just bite the bullet and apply for that Masters. Oh, the Applied Linguistics one at Manchester? You absolutely should! You’ve been talking about it for ages. And you’d be brilliant. Have you started on the application, at least? They want that personal statement, right? Yeah, that's the killer. The personal statement. I keep staring at a blank page. And then there’s the interview… I’m bricking it already. It’s a proper commitment, mind. More studying, less… well, less having a life. And it’s not cheap, is it? We’ll figure it out, Liam. If you get in, we’ll figure it out. We always do. Maybe a little less impulsive shopping for vinyl? Hey! My records are an  investment ! Anyway, are you still on for your sister’s wedding next month? I still haven’t figured out what to wear. Yes! It’s going to be massive. And honestly, she's stressing me out. Guest lists, colour schemes… it’s a full-time job just being a bridesmaid. You'll look nice in your navy suit, won't you? Just… iron it. Ironing. Another battle I’m consistently losing. Right. Okay, navy suit. Sorted. Listen, we need to start thinking about Christmas properly. Have you started on lists? I'm already dreading the queues in Liverpool One. I’ve got a few ideas. Your mum keeps dropping hints about a fancy cheese board.

… honestly, it’s just  exhausting  scrolling through Instagram. Everyone’s life looks perfect. Like, literally perfect. Zara’s posting pics from some fancy rooftop bar - apparently, she’s ‘just popped out for a quick drink’ with some bloke I’ve never seen before. Quick drink?! In  that  outfit? Give me strength. Oh, Zara. She’s always been extra. Don’t believe everything you see online, yeah? It’s all curated. My cousin, she’s a photographer, and she spends hours making even a simple brunch look like a Michelin star meal. I  know  it’s curated, obviously. It’s just… depressing. Makes uni feel even more… grey, doesn't it? Like everyone else is living their best life and I’m here, surviving on caffeine and instant noodles. Relatable. Although, instant noodles are a  vibe , don’t knock ‘em. What are you working on for your dissertation anyway? Still history? Sadly, yes. Still history. It's on the social impact of Victorian music halls. So, basically, hours of reading about blokes in top hats and women in frilly dresses. Thrilling, I know. You still doing psychology? Yeah, still psychology. Though I’m seriously considering switching. It’s… a lot. All the case studies. It’s draining. Plus, Liam keeps going on about how I'd be amazing as a criminal profiler, and that sounds slightly terrifying. Liam, huh? Still going strong then? He's alright, a bit… intense, though. Remember that time he tried to explain the intricacies of football to me for an hour? I just kept nodding and pretending to understand the offside rule. Oh god, yes! He genuinely thought he was converting me. He’s obsessed. He’s convinced Arsenal are going to win the league this year, bless him. But yeah, we’re good. He got me into  Avatar: The Last Airbender  though, which is a win. Have you seen it? No! I’ve heard good things. Is it actually good or is it just another one of those things people hype up? I need something new to watch. I’ve rewatched all the Disney classics about a million times.  Little Mermaid  still hits different, though, doesn’t it? It is genuinely good! It's a cartoon, but it's complex. Proper good storytelling. And yes,  The Little Mermaid  is a classic for a reason. Ursula's amazing. Speaking of good storytelling, have you started watching  Wednesday ?

...and then, like, seriously, the Shiny Charmander was  right there . Just glinting in the tall grass. I nearly screamed, Mum! But then a Zigzagoon jumped out and scared it off. Proper gutted, I was.      Oh, darling, that's awful! You have such bad luck with Shiny Pokémon. It’s just a game, though, isn’t it? Don't let it ruin your evening. Though I do understand the frustration. It’s like when I  almost  managed to get a good deal on those new slippers online last week…      Poke-mon! 'Mon!      Yeah, 'Mon, little dude. It  is  Pokémon. You wanna see Charmander on the Switch?      Now, Leo, let Oisin eat his dinner first. He'll be sticking his fingers in the screen. And honestly, you’ve been on that thing all afternoon. We need to organise getting ramen tomorrow. I was thinking that place near the English Market?      Ooh, yeah! With the proper crispy noodles? Sound good. But can I level up my Squirtle before then? I’m trying to get him ready for the gym battle.      Always with the Pokémon. Alright, half an hour. Then it’s screen-off time. Speaking of levels, you've gotten so much better at the guitar since Uncle Mark gave it to you. Are you still practicing?      Yeah, kinda. I'm learning that riff from… what's that band called… Arctic Monkeys? It’s hard. My fingers hurt.      More! Mores!      Oh, sweetie, you're a messy one, aren’t you? Right, back to you two. Leo, have you seen those really skinny jeans everyone’s wearing at school? I saw some in town, they looked…restrictive.      Mum! Don’t start! Everyone’s wearing them. Even Ben. He says they’re comfortable. I want a pair!      Comfortable? They look like they're painted on! You’ll be complaining you can’t breathe. Honestly. You’re still growing. You need clothes you can  move  in. Maybe when you're older.      But… but everyone! It’s embarrassing if I don’t have them.      Embarrassing? Nonsense. Being yourself is never embarrassing. Remember what we talked about? Besides, Oisin here is far more embarrassing. He tried to wear one of your socks on his head earlier.      Seriously? He did? He’s so weird.      He's a toddler, Leo! They  are  weird. He’s finally started saying more than just “Dada” and “Mama”, though. He tried to say ‘ice cream’ today.

… honestly, it’s just  full  of dust bunnies, isn’t it? And bits of… well, I don’t even  know  what some of this is. I thought we’d cleared this cupboard out ages ago. Ages ago, darling? That’s optimistic. We said we would, didn't we? Six months? A year? It’s a bit of a repository for ‘things we might need someday’, isn’t it? Though I can’t imagine  what  we’d need a single, chipped plastic spoon for. Exactly! And oh… look at this. Oh, heavens. This takes me right back. Oh, the gardening set! Goodness me. Remember that? Plastic watering can, little rake… and the bright pink wellington boots. You always insisted on wearing the pink ones, even though I wanted them. Well, they  were  a much nicer shade of pink! And yours were that horrifying lime green. Honestly, Mum and Dad had no taste. We spent hours in the garden with that, didn't we? Pretending to grow prize-winning marrows. Hours! And meticulously arranging pebbles around the plant pots. We’d meticulously weed, though usually just transferring the weeds to a different part of the garden. It was the  intention  that mattered. Do you remember making mud pies and selling them to Mrs. Higgins over the fence? Oh, that poor woman! She was far too polite to say they tasted awful. She’d give us a penny each, and we thought we were millionaires. That gardening set… it feels like a proper bit of Margate childhood. It is. Before everything… changed. Before we moved up here. Speaking of childhood… dig this out. Bako! Oh my goodness, Bako! I haven’t seen a Bako set in decades. Is it… complete? Not even close. Look, half the coloured panels are missing. And all the little windows. But it’s still… evocative. We built  castles  with this. And spaceships. And enormous, wonky houses. We did! And you always had the blueprint in your head – a perfect, symmetrical design. I was all about just sticking things together and seeing what happened. Which inevitably led to collapse. A slightly more chaotic approach, yes. You were always more… free-spirited. This is why it took us forever to tidy  anything  as children, isn’t it? One of us wanted order, the other wanted… artistic license. Exactly! It’s probably why I dread this sort of thing now. All these memories attached to bits of plastic.

… honestly, I’m still finding bites, even with the plug-in. It's ridiculous. I thought September meant a ceasefire with the mosquitoes, but clearly, they didn't get the memo. Little blighters. Did you get bitten at all last night? A couple, yeah. One right on my ankle. It’s infuriating. I swear, they can hear you breathe when you’re trying to sleep. We really need to look at getting some netting for the bedroom, don’t we? Before this gets completely out of hand. Though, imagining trying to wrangle that around the cot… feels like a whole other operation. Tell me about it. It’s already enough getting him settled. Speaking of settled, he was  fantastic  in the park earlier. Actually slept for a good forty minutes in the buggy. A whole forty minutes! It felt like a small miracle. Progress, right? Massive progress. I was bracing myself for the usual ten-minute nap and immediate screaming. You’re a wonder, honestly, getting him out and about like that. I was still mentally recovering from marking those essays. Honestly, the standard this year…it’s dropping. Oh, don’t even  start  me on marking. I’ve got a pile looming over me like the Tower of Pisa. I need to dedicate a whole weekend to it, I think. But then… that new band, ‘Static Bloom’, are playing at The Waterfront on Friday. I was looking at tickets. Static Bloom? Aren’t they that post-punk revival thing? I saw a snippet of them on TikTok. Seemed quite loud. Loud is good! It’s been ages since we’ve had a proper gig. Remember that amazing show at the UEA a couple of years ago? Before…well, before everything. Vaguely. Mostly I remember the horrendous traffic getting  to  the UEA. It took us nearly an hour from here. Honestly, Norwich traffic is getting worse and worse. It's baffling. London traffic prepared me for a certain level of chaos, but Norwich is just… inefficient. Inefficient is the perfect word. It's not even  volume  of traffic, it’s just…badly planned junctions. And everyone seems to forget how to indicate. Though, to be fair, I was probably half asleep after a long day of lecturing about Victorian poetry. It doesn’t exactly set the pulse racing. No, I suppose not. Still, you're brilliant at it. You truly bring Tennyson to life.

...Honestly, the putting green was  brutal  today. Felt like trying to roll a marble uphill in treacle. Spent a good hour just… chipping away at it, you know? Nearly chucked a club, didn’t I.      Sounds stressful, babe. More stressful than endlessly scrolling LinkedIn, that’s for sure. Still nothing decent. Apparently, ‘demonstrable enthusiasm’ isn’t enough when you’ve got a first and a 2:1.      Demonstrable enthusiasm? What even  is  that? Sounds like something a recruitment bot made up. You’re well clever, don’t you worry. They’re missing out. Did you at least manage to write a proper cover letter for that marketing assistant one? You were stuck on the opening line yesterday.      I did! Finally. Took me about three drafts. I ended up going with “Following your advertisement…” – riveting, I know. Mum reckons I should hand-write them still. Says it shows commitment. Honestly, who even  does  that anymore? It'd take ages, and the post is so slow these days anyway.      Your mum’s a traditionalist, innit? Speaking of slow, did that package I ordered for Halloween arrive? The fake spiderwebs? I’m planning a proper spooky setup this year.      Not yet. It's probably stuck somewhere in a depot. Honestly, I'm not even bothered about Halloween this year. Just feel… blah. I did watch a bit of telly earlier, trying to distract myself. Caught the end of that ghost hunting show.      Ghosts? You and your ghost stories! You know I’m a man of science. It’s all drafts and bad wiring. Though, Grandad  did  swear our old house in Barbados was haunted. Said he heard footsteps upstairs when no one was there. He was a storyteller though, that man.      He was. Remember those tales he used to tell? Always involving rum and some sort of mischievous spirit. It's just... everything feels a bit stuck, doesn’t it? You’re off gallivanting around golf courses, making a proper living, and I'm here, living off savings and applying for jobs that want five years’ experience for an entry-level position.      Hey, don’t talk like that. You smashed uni. It’s just a rubbish job market right now. And I’m not ‘gallivanting’, I’m working my backside off! Remember those six years I spent grinding on the mini-tour? Sleepless nights in dodgy Travelodges, eating pot noodles… not exactly glamorous.      Okay, okay.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the cloud migration at work is a complete shambles. They promised seamless, they delivered… well, let's just say a lot of frantic phone calls and emergency patching. It’s like they didn’t even  test  the thing properly. Sounds boring. Tell me about it. A seamless transition. Ha! That’s a laugh. Trying to get Leo to transition to solids is a seamless transition compared to that. Honestly, I’m exhausted. He decided ‘no’ was his favourite word this morning…for  everything . Baa baa black sheep, have you any wool? Yes sir, yes sir, three bags full! Ah, the joys. Himself has a talent, that one. Though perhaps we should encourage a slightly wider repertoire, eh? Can we watch a film after dinner? A proper one, not one of Mam’s… you know…  feelings  films. Oh, I resent that! They’re called dramas, darling, and they’re perfectly valid! But yes, we can talk about a film. Maybe something with superheroes? Though you’ll have to promise not to spend the whole time dissecting the CGI. Superheroes are always a safe bet. Though, I’m still lobbying for a good old western. They don’t make ‘em like they used to. A western? Liam, are you serious? You know the last time you watched a western, you fell asleep halfway through and snored so loudly the dog started barking. That was a particularly good western! Very atmospheric. Look, all I’m saying is, a man needs a bit of Clint Eastwood in his life. Can we at least choose the snacks? I want those cheesy puffs, not carrot sticks. Carrot sticks are for rabbits. We’ve discussed this, Finn. A small bag of cheesy puffs  after  you’ve eaten something vaguely nutritious. No arguments. He’s got a point about the carrot sticks, love. Even  I  could do with something a bit more…substantial. How’s the lasagne? It smells lovely. It's fine. It would be lovelier if I’d had a bit of help with getting Leo to stop attempting to redecorate the kitchen with yogurt. Honestly, it's like living with a tiny, sticky whirlwind. You're a saint, you are. A saint, I tell ya. I don’t know how you do it. Managing a toddler and keeping this house somewhat functional… it’s a superpower in itself. Is being a superhero harder than being a mam?

… honestly, I still can’t believe he slept in just his pants last night. And not even  nice  pants, like, old boxy ones. I know! I checked on him about midnight and just… there he was. Peaceful as anything, but completely exposed to the Suffolk chill. I thought, ‘Right, definitely need to make sure he doesn’t roll out of bed.’ He said he was being a ‘superhero without a cape!’ Yeah! Superheroes don’t wear pyjamas! They just have… pants powers! Vroom! Pants powers, eh? I suppose that’s as good a reason as any. Though I suspect it was more to do with the heat and general laziness. You’d think with a proper duvet he wouldn’t need to air things out  quite  so much. He did say he was warm. Still, it’s a bit of a talking point, isn't it? The whole family will be mentioning ‘Pants-Man’ for weeks. Speaking of warm… I was thinking about the back of the house again. Oh, here we go. The grand extension plans. Don’t tell me you’ve been sketching again while the kids were building Lego castles? Maybe. Just a few ideas. I was looking at that space behind the kitchen, where the shed is. We could knock the shed down, extend out, and have a proper utility room, and maybe even a little downstairs loo. Imagine! No more traipsing through the house when someone needs to go. A downstairs loo… that actually doesn’t sound terrible. Especially with the kids. But knocking down the shed? That’s where I keep all my… stuff. The camping gear, the vaguely useful bits of wood, the ambitions I’ll probably never get around to… Is that where the sparkly rocks are, Daddy? It is, darling. Some of them, anyway. They might have to find a new home if Mum gets her way. It wouldn’t be a massive extension. Just enough to make life a bit easier. And think of the space! We could finally have somewhere to dry clothes properly instead of draping them over every chair in the house. Could we have a slide in the new room? A really long one! That goes  whoosh ! A slide, you say? Now  there’s  an idea. Though I suspect your mother wants something slightly more… practical. We’d need planning permission, wouldn’t we? And the cost… We could get some quotes, see what it’s looking like.

…and honestly, the magnolia was a mistake. A complete and utter mistake. It just…sucked all the life out of the hallway. My wife, bless her, she wanted ‘neutral’. Neutral is just beige pretending to be sophisticated, I tell you. Ah, the eternal struggle with the colour palette. My Eira’s the same. Thinks everything needs to be ‘calming’. Calming is code for drab, in my experience. We’ve got this rather…vibrant wallpaper in the downstairs loo now, a sort of turquoise and gold swirling thing. Nearly gave the postman a heart attack. Turquoise and gold! That  is  bold, Gareth. Very bold. More interesting than magnolia, certainly. Though I suspect my wife would faint. She’s currently obsessed with Farrow & Ball. As if paint justifies the price tag. It's all marketing, you know. Pure marketing. Reminds me of trying to secure funding for the particle physics project. Oh, that. Still fighting that battle, David? I heard whispers the EPSRC weren’t overly impressed with the preliminary data. Whispers are polite. They practically laughed it off! Said it wasn’t ‘transformative’ enough. Transformative! We’re talking about simulating conditions a fraction of a second after the Big Bang! What’s more transformative than  that ? Honestly, these funding bodies… they want instant results. They want something they can stick on a press release. The Hadron Collider didn’t spring into being overnight, you know. It took decades. I know, I know. It's the same in history. Trying to get funding for the Welsh coalfield oral history project is… challenging. Everyone wants something about the Tudors, or the Romans. No one cares about the grit and the grime of the industrial revolution, apparently. Though, ironically, that’s  where  the real stories are. Precisely! It's all about narrative, isn’t it? A good story sells. Speaking of good stories and things that sell… have you ever considered a research trip to Italy? Italy? What prompted that? I was reading an article – actually, last night, over a rather disastrous attempt at soufflé – about the structural integrity of Roman aqueducts. Remarkable engineering. And the water companies here… Honestly, Gareth. They’re letting the infrastructure crumble, and then blaming us for using too much water during a heatwave. The hypocrisy! Don’t get me started on the water companies. It's a disgrace. They’re privatised, you see, down here. Always a bad sign.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Lego is astonishing. It’s like it  multiplies  when you’re not looking. Right, Lily? You’ve been remarkably quiet, building something impressive over there? It’s Hogwarts! I’m making the Astronomy Tower. It needs… lots of grey bricks. I’m building the Turtle Van! With all the weapons! It needs grappling hooks and… and pizza launchers! Can we  get  Lego pizza launchers, Mum? I think actual Lego pizza launchers might be pushing it, Finn. Although, you never know. They do sell everything these days, don’t they? We’ll have to see. Are you separating the pieces at all? That’s what I was trying to get you both to do. This mountain of bricks is… well, a bit overwhelming. I  am  separating them! All the grey ones are for the tower, and I’ve got a pile of brown for the walls. Good girl! See, Finn? Lily’s showing you how it’s done. Maybe we can put on some music? Something… not too distracting. Perhaps no  Simpsons  theme tune? Last time, it ended in a wrestling match over a yellow brick. But Bart is awesome! And he does cool pranks. I want to be Bart when I grow up. I think perhaps we aim for something a little less… prank-focused. How about we think about Saturday? We talked about going to the cinema, didn’t we? What film were you both leaning towards? The one with the dragons! The new one! No! The Ninja Turtles one! It’s got Shredder! He’s the bad guy and he’s really scary. Right, so we have dragons versus turtles. A classic dilemma. We could maybe flip a coin? Or… how about we look at the trailers again tonight and  then  decide? That fair? Fine. But turtles are cooler. We’ll see. Honestly, a quiet afternoon in a darkened cinema sounds like heaven after the week I’ve had. Mrs. Peterson's class decided to have a full-scale debate about whether Voldemort was misunderstood. He  was  misunderstood! He just wanted someone to love him! Lily, darling, where do you get these opinions? Still, it was a fascinating discussion, even if it took up the entire humanities lesson. Speaking of lessons… Granny’s house is a bit of a lesson in chaos at the moment, isn’t it? All the renovations. Granny said she’s getting a new kitchen!

… honestly, the paella was just…sad. Like, they clearly hadn’t used proper bomba rice. It was all mushy and flavourless. You  know  how much I love a good paella. Oh, darling. That  is  a tragedy. Spain, and a bad paella? The injustice! How was the rest of the trip though? You were gone for a full week, felt like ages. Did you at least get some sunshine? Sunshine, yes. Plenty of that. Barcelona was gorgeous, honestly. The architecture, the vibe… just a bit let down by the rice situation. And the crowds! Honestly, it felt like Piccadilly Circus sometimes. Not the relaxing beach holiday I’d envisioned. How was work? You said you had a particularly rough patch before you went? Brutal. Honestly. Old Mr. Henderson completely unravelled. Became convinced his medication was being swapped out, started refusing everything. Took three of us to just  talk  him down. It was exhausting. Hence the need for a week of doing absolutely nothing in Cornwall. Which, by the way, was blissfully crowd-free. And the cream teas…oh, the cream teas. Oh, Cornwall sounds  perfect . Cream teas are essential. Mr. Henderson sounds…challenging. You deserve a medal. Still, you’re practically a professional de-escalator, aren't you? Sadly, yes. It’s…rewarding, but draining. Anyway! Enough about my work dramas. What about  your  dramas? Any news on the dating front? Did you bump into… you know…  him  while you were away? Don’t even  start . No, thankfully. I actively avoided all the places I knew he might frequent. Just in case. It’s been six months, and I still get a twitch in my eye if I hear his name. Honestly, the audacity of him, just disappearing like that… Ugh, honestly, Liam. He was always a bit of a…flake. Though, I always thought you saw something in him that wasn’t there. Remember Sarah saying he reminded her of a golden retriever? All enthusiasm, no follow-through? That’s… surprisingly accurate, actually. A very handsome, emotionally unavailable golden retriever. Anyway, no Liam sightings. Focused on failing paellas and avoiding tourist traps. Speaking of friends, did you hear back from Chloe about the gig next week? She messaged this morning! She’s in! So, we’re on for that awful indie band at The Fleece? Prepare for questionable fashion choices and even more questionable music. Oh god. I’d almost forgotten. Fine.

…and honestly, lad, the state of some of those papers this year. You wouldn’t  believe  the number of students who thought pi was 3.1416, and then rounded it to… 3.1! Three point one! After all this time, still. It’s disheartening, it really is.      Right. Sounds… stressful. Is that why you were muttering about ‘irrational numbers’ at breakfast?      Aye, well, stressful  and  frustrating. They're irrational for a reason, aren't they? They go on forever! It's a key concept!      Oh, numbers. Always were a bother to me. Give me a good gossip any day. Though young Thomas, your dad, he was always good with figures. Used to balance the books for old Mrs. Higgins down the road, even after he retired from the docks.      Aye, he was. Clever lad. Though didn’t have the patience for explaining it to anyone. Said it was like trying to teach a pig to sing - wasted effort.      Grandad! That’s a bit harsh.      It's just a saying, lad! No offense meant to anyone. Speaking of wasted effort, are we still on for the bingo tonight, Margaret? My lucky dabber’s calling to me.      We are, Arthur. Though I’m warning you, Doris next door has been practicing. She’s got a new pair of glasses and claims to see the numbers before they even come up.      Doris and her glasses! She thinks she’s psychic. She told me last week I’d meet a tall, dark stranger. All I met was the postman, and he’s got a bit of a limp, poor lad.      Maybe the postman  is  your tall, dark stranger, Grandma! You just need to look closer.      Don’t be daft. He’s delivering bills, not romance. Now, have you made arrangements for getting us back to Hull later, Eileen? My legs are starting to ache.      Of course, love. I’ve asked young David – the lad with the taxi, remember? He’s picking us up at six. It’s a bit of a drive, but better than relying on the buses, especially this time of day.      Good, good. Buses are full of youngsters these days, glued to their… whatchamacallits? Phones, that's it. No respect for their elders.      They’re just… communicating, Grandad. It’s how we all talk now.      He's right, Arthur. It's different, but it's not necessarily disrespectful. Although, sometimes I wish they’d look up and appreciate the world around them.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt a bit…off. Not dreadful, you know, but not  Peter Pan  at all. Joe Wright’s ‘Pan’… it just didn’t capture the magic. It felt too… gritty. Too trying to be a proper ‘origin story’ when the beauty of Peter Pan is in the  mystery  of him. But it had pirates! And Captain Hook had a cool hat! He did, didn’t he? Hook  did  have a good hat. Though, honestly, Robbie wasn’t quite the Hook I pictured. Too… handsome? Hook’s supposed to be menacing! And he lost his hand to a crocodile! A  big  crocodile! Was it real? Well, in the story it was, darling. A big, tick-tocking crocodile who really fancied Captain Hook’s hand. Though, I suspect in the film it was probably computer generated. It's just a story, remember? Is Great Ormond Street Hospital in the Peter Pan story? Mummy, you said something about that? That’s right, sweetheart. J.M. Barrie, the man who  wrote  Peter Pan, he actually gave all the copyright of the play and the stories to Great Ormond Street Hospital. So every time someone puts on a production of Peter Pan, or sells a Peter Pan book, the hospital gets money. Isn’t that lovely? So… the hospital gets pirate treasure? Sort of! It's not  actual  pirate treasure, but money that helps the hospital look after poorly children. It’s a really important hospital. They do amazing things. Better than Neverland? Neverland sounds a bit scary. There’s Captain Hook and Lost Boys and… and… It  can  be scary for those who aren’t careful. But it’s also a place of adventure, and freedom. That's why Peter doesn't want to grow up, isn’t it? He wants to keep that adventure going forever. But growing up is good! You get to have ice cream whenever you want! True! Growing up has its perks. Ice cream on demand is definitely one of them. But sometimes... sometimes it’s nice to hold onto a little bit of that Neverland feeling, you know? That feeling of possibility, of believing in magic. Do you think Tinkerbell is real? Oh, I  hope  Tinkerbell is real. She’s tiny and sparkly and a little bit mischievous. But believing in Tinkerbell is a bit like believing in kindness, and friendship, and the power of imagination.

… honestly, it feels like we were just unpacking boxes in that little cottage near Chudleigh. Remember how damp it was, love? Always a bit of a chill, even in August. Oh, Dad, don't remind me! Mum was forever battling mildew in the bathroom. It was lovely, though, wasn't it? Really quaint. And much closer to Exeter than this side of Dartmoor. It was a nice change from Taunton, at least. Though your Aunt Carol never let us forget we'd  left  Taunton. “Devon’s alright, but it’s not Somerset,” she’d say. Every. Single. Time. Carol’s always been…particular. Still, Taunton was a good run, wasn’t it? We had some happy years in that house on Hamilton Road. You two were just little terrors, tearing around the garden. I remember replacing the fence three times! We were energetic. And you always built the best dens, Dad! Remember the one with the old blankets and chairs? Oh, goodness yes. And you’d sneak biscuits in there, wouldn’t you two? That’s why you were always so full of beans. Speaking of which, are you both alright for the journey? It’s a good two and a half hours to Bristol, and then the airport… I’m fine, dear. Just thinking about all this driving. Makes me appreciate my retirement, I can tell you. Though I do miss having a project, a purpose. Never thought I’d say that, after all those years in management. You’ve got plenty of purpose now, Dad! Keeping Mum entertained is a full-time job. Touché. And you’re right, she keeps me on my toes. Though my sleep’s been proper disrupted these last few weeks, what with all the fuss about the move and getting everything sorted. Up at five, even when I haven’t got anything to do. You and me both. The stress of everything plays havoc, doesn’t it? I’m hoping once we get settled in properly at the new place, things will calm down a bit. It's a lovely house though, isn’t it? So much light. It is beautiful, Mum. And having that garden is amazing. Perfect for Alfie to run around when he’s older. We need to think about Christmas now, don’t we? Are we doing it here this year? Or are you two coming down to Devon? I think coming down to Devon makes the most sense.

…Honestly, it's just the  thought  of all that bending and lifting again tomorrow. My back’s been a right state since we cleared that bramble patch. Though, I did read an article – silly really, in one of those magazine things – about Swedish massage being good for muscle recovery. Never had one, mind. Sounds a bit…frivolous for a woman my age, don’t you think?      Frivolous? Now there’s a word. Don’t you believe that, love. Frivolous is spending a fortune on fancy hats. A bit of massage, that’s sensible. My Doreen – she had terrible trouble with her hips towards the end. A lovely young woman at the hospice used to give her hand massages. Didn’t cure everything, nothin’ does, but it lifted her spirits, it did. Proper comfort it was.      Oh, a hospice, yes. Dreadful places, aren’t they? Though I imagine they do good work. My sister, she volunteered at one for years. She always said it wasn’t about  curing  people, but making their last bit peaceful. It's just… confronting, isn’t it? All that talk of endings.      It is. It’s about dignity, mostly. And kindness. Doreen always said the staff were angels. She used to be a nursery nurse, you know, before she had the kids. Loved working with little ‘uns. Always said they were honest. Couldn’t understand a thing they said half the time, but honest.      Nursery education's changed so much since… well, since I had my children. They wouldn’t have  dreamt  of asking a woman to run a nursery back in Somerset in the seventies. Good Lord, no! It was all ‘teacher’ and everything was very proper and…male dominated. Things have improved, haven't they? Though still not equal, I suspect. You see it even now, people using terms like ‘chairman’ when ‘chairperson’ is perfectly acceptable. It’s subtle, but it’s there.      Aye, subtle it is. I worked for the Nationwide, you see. Nationwide Building Society. Saw a bit of that over the years. Felt a bit silly pointing it out sometimes, saying 'shouldn't that be 'manager' rather than 'man-ager'?' but you’ve got to try, haven’t you? Doreen used to say I was a right busybody. She weren't wrong.      A good busybody is a valuable thing. It's the quiet ones you have to watch. Now, this ME event next year… Have you heard anything more about what they’re hoping to achieve with it?

… honestly, Mum, I just feel a bit silly even  thinking  about all-inclusive. It feels… wasteful, doesn’t it? Like we’re just going to sit and eat and drink and not  do  anything. Wasteful? Darling, you work your socks off teaching those lovely youngsters. You deserve a bit of ‘wasteful’ now and then. Especially after the year it’s been. And let’s be realistic, you’ll want a holiday where you can truly switch off. Remember Italy? All that navigating, the language barrier… you were stressed within twenty-four hours! That's true, Italy was… ambitious. Beautiful, obviously, but utterly exhausting. I was spending more time stressing about train times than actually enjoying the gelato. But still, all-inclusive feels… contrived. I liked the freedom of finding little tavernas, stumbling across hidden gems. And you did, you found some  wonderful  places. But that takes energy, doesn’t it? And you said yourself you’re feeling run down. Crete is different. We're not going to one of those massive, formulaic resorts. I spent ages looking at smaller ones, family-run places. This one, ‘Villa Eleni’, has excellent reviews. It’s on the quieter side of the island, near Chania, but still has easy access to towns. They do cooking classes, there’s a small beach nearby… and the food is supposed to be incredible. All local produce. Cooking classes  do  sound good. I’ve been meaning to improve my Mediterranean cooking. And Chania… I remember reading about it, lovely Venetian harbor. What about exploring the Samaria Gorge? I saw some photos, it’s breathtaking. That’s a possibility, yes. But it’s a full day trek, quite strenuous. We don’t have to do it if you’re not up to it. The point is, we have options. With all-inclusive, it takes the pressure off. No worrying about where to eat, how much things cost. You can just… relax. And I'm not suggesting we stay  at  the hotel the whole time, goodness me! We can rent a car for a few days, explore at our own pace. A car would be good. I feel so helpless when I can’t just… get up and go. Remember that tiny village in the Algarve, the one we found by accident? That was magical. I do indeed. But even getting to that magical village involved a lot of confusing road signs and a near-miss with a donkey!

… honestly, I still can’t believe how much that gig ticket was after fees. Sixty quid for one night, it’s daylight robbery! Did you see what happened with the Ed Sheeran tickets though? Absolute chaos. Sixty quid? Aye, that’s a bit steep, innit? But youngsters these days, you gotta have your entertainment. Sheeran…Lord have mercy. I saw the news. People camping for days, bots snapping them up… it’s a whole industry built on disappointment, that is. Reminds me of trying to get West Indies cricket tickets back home. A right scramble, that was. A scramble is putting it mildly! My mate Liam was trying for ages. He said the resale sites were asking for  double  the price. It’s just… greed, isn’t it? Anyway, enough about infuriating ticket sales. How was work today? Did Old Man Hemmings finally crack under the pressure of the quarterly reports? Hemmings is a piece of work, truly. No, didn’t crack  today . Just… flapped. More frantic pacing, more loudly dictating emails he barely understands. The reports are looking good though, thankfully. Sales are up this quarter, mostly down to the new marketing campaign. I suggested it, naturally. He takes all the credit, of course. Standard Hemmings. Sounds about right. He's a proper wind-up merchant. Still, good on you for the idea. You've got a good head for that sort of thing. Better than me, that’s for sure. All my brainpower goes into trying to decipher post-structuralism. Post-structuralism! What  is  that even? Sounds complicated! Listen, talkin’ about brains… your Auntie Carol rang earlier. She's worried about your Grandad. Says he’s been a bit off his food, complainin’ about his knees. Oh, bugger. How off his food? Like, just not fancying his dinner, or… worse? He's been moaning about his knees for years, they're properly knackered. I promised I'd ring him tomorrow. She said he managed a bit of stew, but barely touched his pudding, which is  always  a bad sign. She's thinking of takin’ him to the doctor's on Friday. She wants you to give him a bell just to cheer him up, y’know? He always brightens up when he hears your voice. Says you remind him of your Dad when he was your age – full of energy and questions. Right, I’ll definitely give him a ring tomorrow.

…No, no, that’s what I mean, Doreen. This globe, see? It's not  accurate  anymore. Not really. Not since… well, not since everything’s changed. Used to spend hours with me Dad, spinning it, pointin’ at places. He’d say, “One day, Arthur, one day…” Never did get to most of ‘em, did he? Not after the leg went. Oh, Arthur, don't start on that again. Your Dad had a good life, he did. And you were always a good son, takin’ him to the seaside and such. This globe's a lovely ornament though, isn't it? Reminds me of when the kids were little. They used to trace their fingers 'round the countries, askin' where Father Christmas lived. It  is  a bit dated, isn’t it? All those empires still marked out. Makes you think about how much the world alters. Funny, isn’t it? I was telling my class about the British Empire last week, and they were… well, they were questioning everything. Rightly so, I suppose. Questionin’ everything! That’s the youth of today for ya. No respect! Though, I suppose we were a bit rebellious back in our day too. Remember Scarborough, Doreen? Proper holiday camp, that was. Used to go every year. Scarborough! Oh, the penny arcades! And those awful little hats they sold. Arthur looked quite the dandy in one, I recall. Though, truthfully, everything looked better in those days. Simple, y'know? We did a school project on Yorkshire a few years back. Had the kids research different towns, the food, the history. It's a beautiful county, truly. Though a bit… brisk, even in summer. Brisk? You wouldn't believe the wind up there! Blastin’ off the North Sea. We tried stayin’ in a youth hostel once. Awful! Damp, cold…youngsters snorin’ like anything. Never again. Give me a B&B any day. Youth hostels! Honestly, Arthur. You’d complain about a five-star hotel, you would. Remember that little B&B in Cornwall? The one with the hideous floral wallpaper? You loved it! Said it was “characterful.” I actually did a placement year in Yorkshire, teaching. A small village near Harrogate. Lovely people, very down to earth. Though getting around without a car was a nightmare. Not like Birmingham, with our surprisingly efficient – for a British city – underground system. Underground? Never been a fan, myself. Feels like bein’ buried alive. Give me a nice, open garden any day.

… honestly, I just don’t get why they’ve increased the baggage allowance fees  again . It’s daylight robbery, it is. Like we don’t already pay enough for the flights themselves, y’know? Mmm, yeah, it’s a pain. Ryanair are the worst for that, aren’t they? They lure you in with these ridiculously cheap base fares and then just nickel and dime you to death with everything else. Did you manage to get anything decent for the Barcelona trip? I’m still scrolling through endless options. Aye, I think so. Got us flights with EasyJet in the end. Bit more expensive than Ryanair, like five quid each more roughly, but worth it just to avoid the stress, honestly. And they  include  a cabin bag that isn't microscopic. I booked 'em just after six, luckily, before the price jumped up again. They're proper sneaky like that. Good thinking. Six is the sweet spot, isn’t it? I always hear that. I’ve been looking at flights leaving on the Friday evening, thinking we could maximise the weekend. But everything’s showing up at nearly two hundred quid return! It feels…a lot. Two hundred?! Ooh, aye, that’s rough. I got ours for around a hundred and forty, leaving Saturday morning. Maybe try shifting the days slightly? Honestly, I've found Tuesdays and Wednesdays are always cheapest. Though leaving on a Tuesday does kill the vibe a bit, doesn’t it? It does! I really want to be there for the tapas crawl Sarah’s planned on Friday. She’s been going on about it for weeks. She reckons she knows this tiny little place… authentic, apparently. Not touristy. Oh, she always finds the hidden gems, doesn’t she? Right, lemme have a quick look on Skyscanner for you. Sometimes if you put in ‘anywhere’ for the destination, you get a bit of inspiration… or at least a laugh at the prices. Though don't actually fly anywhere random, obviously. No, definitely not. Just… desperate times, desperate measures! It’s just, I've been saving up for a new lens for my camera and Barcelona felt like the perfect excuse. Now I’m wondering if I should just stay put and continue saving. Don’t do that! You need a holiday. You’ve been working non-stop since uni finished. And you deserve that lens, love. Think of all the amazing photos you could take!

…and honestly, the price of a tin of peaches now! Seven-five pence more than last month. Seven-five! You wouldn’t believe it. Used to be you could get a decent tin for under sixty. Under sixty, I tell you. Gran, you  always  say that. It feels like you’ve been complaining about supermarket prices since, well, since I was born! But you’re right, it’s all creeping up. I noticed petrol again this morning. Nearly £1.50 a litre. Don’t even  start  me on petrol, love. I’m driving into town for court tomorrow, and that's a good twenty quid just to get there and back. Not to mention the parking… the council are robbers, honestly. They’ve put the price up again. Robbers is right, Daphne. Absolute robbers. It’s the same with these banks, isn't it? Always charging you something, even when you're just  keeping  your money with them. I was looking at switching, you know. This new one, ‘Starling Bank’ or something… all online. Starling are actually quite good, Dad. A lot of my colleagues use them. Their customer service is surprisingly responsive, which is rare these days. Though, you do need to be comfortable doing everything on your phone. That’s the rub, isn’t it? I’m not entirely averse. I manage to send you pictures of Winston, don’t I? Though I still need a hand with it sometimes. Speaking of Winston, he’s been off his food a bit. Vet said it’s probably just the change in the weather. Says it upsets their tummies. Animals are sensitive things. My Tabby, Percy, gets all mopey when it’s grey outside. Right little drama queen he is. Though, he’s worth it. Still, vets aren't cheap, are they? Another expense. Everything feels like an expense these days. Seriously. It’s exhausting. Are you still getting by alright on your pension, Gran? You mentioned a few months ago you were worried about the heating bills. Oh, it’s…manageable. I’ve turned the thermostat down a notch or two, and I’m wearing a cardigan indoors more often. Luckily I paid off the mortgage years ago. That was the best thing I ever did, that. Even with the rates as they were then. Smart thinking, if I may say so myself. You were always sensible with money, Agnes. Unlike some!

… honestly, I just think penguins are criminally underrated. Like, everyone goes on about lions and tigers, but have you  seen  a penguin waddle? It’s pure joy distilled into bird form. And they’re proper resilient, aren’t they? Living in the Antarctic, proper hard graft. Aye, they’re canny little things, penguins. Though I still reckon a good Northumbrian sheepdog is where it’s at. Intelligent, loyal… and they can actually  do  something. Besides look well cute, like. Oh, now, don’t be dissing the penguins! They’re grand. But give me a good Irish Wolfhound any day. Massive, gentle giants, they are. My auntie Maggie has one, and it's basically a furry horse. It needs its own seat on the bus, I swear to God. I’m with Saoirse, honestly. Big dogs are the best. My family always had Welsh Sheepdogs. Brilliant for working, brilliant for snuggling. Though, speaking of animals, has anyone thought about holiday destinations based on what animals you might see? Ooh, now you’re talkin’. That’s a good one, Beth. I’d go somewhere with loads of puffins. They’re like the clowns of the sea, aren’t they? Little faces, colourful beaks… just proper cheerful. Where’s the best place to see ‘em? Scotland? Iceland, actually. Loads of puffins, and the landscapes are just… otherworldly. I was thinking about going there next summer, if I can save up. Although, the food’s supposed to be a bit… challenging. Fermented shark, anyone? No chance! I’ll stick to a good chip butty, thank you very much. Proper northern comfort food. You can’t beat a bit of grease to set you right. What about you, Saoirse? Any particularly Irish holiday food you’re missin'? Oh, everything, honestly. My nan’s soda bread… and a good full Irish breakfast. Black pudding, white pudding, sausages, bacon, eggs… the works. None of this ‘small portion’ nonsense. You need fuel for a day of exploring. And maybe a bit of tayto crisps afterwards. Tayto? Oh, I love those! We don't get those in Wales very often. I'm more of a bara brith kinda girl meself. And laverbread, if you're feeling adventurous. It's seaweed, but actually lovely with cockles and bacon. Seaweed? Seriously? I’m a simple lass, give me a good Sunday roast any day. Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes, gravy… the holy trinity.

… honestly, seeing Gran like  that  last weekend just… rattled me a bit, y’know? It wasn’t even a sudden thing, she’s been slowing down for ages, but just  watching  her try to remember my name… It makes you think, doesn't it? About what comes after all this. All the uni, the… everything. Yeah, I get that. My Nana’s the same. Keeps asking me what I’m ‘studying to be’ like it’s a completely new concept every time. It’s heartbreaking, init? But it's natural, though. They’ve lived full lives. Still… kinda freaky to think we’ll end up like that one day. Freaky is an understatement! I was trying to distract myself afterwards, went to that exhibition at the Peter Scott Gallery. The one with the textile art? Proper weird stuff, actually. But good weird. All these layers and textures… it felt like looking at someone’s memories, all jumbled up. Oh, aye, I saw somethin’ about that. You know I'm terrible with art. Anything that isn't a vaguely recognisable landscape just goes straight over my head. Is it all, like, patchwork and stuff? Not just patchwork! There was this one piece, massive, all these different fabrics stitched together, bits of lace and old clothes and… I dunno, stuff. But it wasn't  about  the clothes themselves, it was about what they represented. Like, childhood, loss, things like that. It made me think a bit about Gran, actually. All the things she's held onto, the stories woven into her life, kinda like those fabrics. Woah, deep. You and your arty interpretations. Honestly, you should be studying something creative, not letting your brain get all philosophical over fabric scraps. Speaking of studying… how’s that essay comin’ along? The one on post-structuralism? Don’t even  mention  it. It’s a right mess. I think I’m just getting bogged down in the jargon. It’s all ‘discourse’ and ‘deconstruction’ and I’m just sitting here thinkin’ “What even  is  reality?!” Professor Davies is lovely, but she expects us to absorb this stuff passively, and I need to actually  fight  with an idea to understand it. Tell me about it! I’m still wrestling with Foucault. Honestly, it's like he actively  tries  to be incomprehensible. I've been trying to bribe Liam - you know, the guy from our seminar? – to explain it to me properly but he just wants to talk about his new gaming setup.

… honestly, I just don’t get why she keeps doing it. Every single time we go out, she has to order the most complicated thing on the menu, then spends the whole meal dissecting it and complaining about one tiny ingredient. It’s exhausting! Sounds like Chloe, alright. She's a bit of a…performance artist when it comes to food, isn’t she? Remember that time at the Italian and she sent her carbonara back three times because the guanciale wasn’t ‘crisp enough’? Oh god,  don’t  remind me! The poor waiter looked like he was about to cry. It's not the sending back, it’s the  drama . Like, just enjoy your pasta, Chloe! Anyway, what are you making? Smells amazing in here. Just a simple veggie curry. Needed something comforting after the shift I’ve had. Old Mr. Henderson was…well, he was Mr. Henderson. Repeatedly asking for his slippers, convinced the nurses were trying to steal his Werther's Originals. You know the drill. Oh, bless him. That sounds draining. You deal with so much. Honestly, sometimes I feel a bit silly complaining about Chloe’s food choices when you're literally holding people’s hands through panic attacks. Hey, your complaints are valid! It's frustrating when a friend consistently makes things difficult. And everyone’s problems are valid, regardless. It’s all relative. Besides, sometimes I  need  to hear about Chloe being fussy to remind myself things could be worse! What’s going on with you and Ben anyway? You’ve been a bit quiet about him lately. It’s…complicated. We had a bit of a row last week. Nothing huge, but it's just…he's been really busy with work and suddenly seems less interested in, well,  everything  we usually do. Like film nights or just properly chatting. That doesn’t sound good. Has he said anything about why he’s pulling back? No, not really. Just says he’s stressed. Which is fair, I guess, work  is  intense right now. But he used to be better at compartmentalising. He used to tell me if something was bothering him. Now it’s just…vague answers and early nights ‘because he’s tired’. Maybe try and have a proper sit-down with him? No distractions, just you two. Tell him how you’re feeling. It’s easy to let things fester when you don’t communicate.

Right, so I’ve had another look at this consent form, Carol. Honestly, it reads like it’s been written for a medical trial, not a seminar on doing business in Japan. “Potential risks and discomforts”? What discomfort are people going to experience learning about keigo?      Now, now, Brenda, you’re being a bit dramatic. It’s standard practice to cover all bases, isn't it? Especially with GDPR and ethical considerations. Students need to know how their input – if we have any group activities, say – will be used.      I agree with Brenda, actually. It feels… excessive. And a bit off-putting. We're trying to  encourage  participation, not scare them off with legal jargon. I mean, 'potential psychological distress'? Really? We're talking about business etiquette, not exposing them to trauma.      Exactly, Sarah! I grew up in Shipley, lass, and even  my  grandma knows this is a bit much. It’s a university seminar, not a covert operation. We need to simplify it. Just something stating we might use anonymised examples of student contributions for teaching purposes, that’s all. No need for talk of ‘unforeseen consequences’.      But the university's legal department were quite insistent on this wording, Brenda. I had a long email exchange with David in compliance. He said they’ve had a couple of incidents recently with students claiming distress over feedback… apparently, some quite strongly worded tutor comments.      Good grief. Still, there's a difference between constructive criticism and dissecting someone’s cultural faux pas in front of the whole group, isn’t there? We’re aiming to be supportive, not publicly shaming anyone for getting a business card exchange wrong.      Aye, that’s what I’m saying. Right, form aside for a moment – let’s get back to the seminar structure. I was thinking we start with a broad overview of Hofstede’s dimensions, then move into specific country examples. Japan and Germany, definitely. Maybe France too?      France is good. We should probably dedicate a section to non-verbal communication. It's often underestimated. Things like eye contact, personal space… they vary enormously. I’ve seen deals fall apart because of a misinterpreted gesture. I remember one trip to Spain… let’s just say the volume control was set a bit too high for my liking.      Definitely non-verbal. And we need to stress the importance of research. Students need to understand it's not just a case of memorising a few dos and don’ts.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking is just…criminal. I swear, half of them haven't even  read  the core texts. It’s just summaries of summaries from Wikipedia. It’s exhausting. Tell me about it. Mine are obsessed with citing random YouTube videos as academic sources. YouTube! I had one student seriously argue that a gaming streamer was a leading expert on post-structuralism. Oh,  no . That’s…peak undergraduate. Seriously though, I feel like I spend more time untangling misinformation than actually engaging with thoughtful analysis. It makes you question the whole point sometimes, doesn’t it? It does. It feels like herding cats. Though, I suppose we knew it wouldn't be all intellectual stimulation and groundbreaking research, eh? Still, it’s frustrating when you genuinely want to foster critical thinking and you’re met with…that. Did you manage to get through to Professor Chen about the syllabus changes? I did, eventually. It took three emails and a rather pointed question during the faculty meeting about departmental consistency. He's…resistant to change, shall we say. Stubborn as a mule. He kept going on about ‘traditional methodologies’ which, frankly, are letting students down. Sounds about right. He’s a lovely man, but definitely set in his ways. Speaking of changes, have you given any more thought to the house hunt? We’re officially running out of time on the lease. I have. And honestly, it’s even more depressing than the marking. Everything remotely decent is either astronomically expensive or tiny. And the agents! They’re all completely useless. I viewed one place yesterday that was advertised as having ‘character’. It was basically a crumbling shack with damp. ‘Character’ is code for ‘needs a complete gut renovation and probably exorcism’. I saw a similar one last week. They called peeling wallpaper “vintage aesthetic”. Exactly! And the location… everything with space is miles outside the city centre. Walking distance to university is becoming a mythical concept. I’m starting to think we might have to compromise on size. I’m not sure how much we  can  compromise. Remember the flat we looked at near the market? It was a shoebox! I practically needed to do yoga just to turn around in the kitchen. Yes, that was…cozy. But honestly, I'm starting to miss Norwich. Remember when we had that little cottage with the garden? Everything felt so much simpler.

… honestly, it’s just frustrating. I made a huge lasagne last night, thinking everyone would be ravenous, and there’s still nearly half left. It feels criminal to throw it away, but I can’t see us eating it all before it goes off. Gran would have  never  tolerated that level of waste. She’d have repurposed everything. Gran was a magician with leftovers, wasn’t she? Remember those shepherd’s pie creations using up every scrap of roast? Though, to be fair, she also probably had a different standard of ‘off’ than we do now. I reckon she'd happily have eaten something  I’d  bin immediately. Probably! She lived through a different time, didn’t she? She’d be horrified by how much we just…discard. It makes me think about that documentary we watched on arranged marriages and dowries. It’s a world away from our experience, but that sense of  value  – valuing resources, family connections, everything – it felt really strong. Yeah, that was a stark contrast. Though I still think the whole dowry thing is… problematic, to say the least. But you're right, there was a different attitude to waste. Everything had a purpose. Speaking of purpose, how’s work going? Still battling the curriculum changes? It’s relentless. Trying to convince 14-year-olds that careers advice is important when they're glued to ‘Bridgerton’ is a struggle. And honestly, trying to advise them about future prospects feels a bit hollow when so many industries feel… closed.
