Like engineering is booming, and you're doing great, but so much is reliant on knowing someone, or getting the 'right' internship. It is frustrating. Work experience is key, absolutely. But access isn’t equal. And you’re right about ‘closed’ industries. Aerospace is still feeling the pinch, for example. It’s almost entirely reliant on government contracts at this point. Private industries are scared to touch it. It's a shame, really. There's so much potential. Exactly! It feels like we’re funneling everyone into tech or finance. It's… limiting. Did you see that article about urban farming initiatives? They're turning rooftops into vegetable gardens in cities. I did! Pretty cool, isn’t it? A step in the right direction, at least. Trying to make food production more sustainable and local. It’s a bit fiddly, though, isn’t it? Imagine trying to get a school garden going.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of revisions they’ve asked for on the grant proposal is just… exhausting. It’s not  bad  feedback, per se, just… relentless nit-picking. Like, does the font  really  affect the science, you know? Oh, absolutely. The font is clearly a make-or-break element of epidemiological research. Seriously though, funding bodies are the worst. They make you jump through hoops just to prove you deserve a pittance. What are they obsessing about this time? Methodology? Sample size? Both, a bit. Mostly the ‘impact’ section. Apparently, outlining the potential benefits to public health isn’t enough. They want specifics. Quantifiable, measurable impact. As if I have a crystal ball. I’m trying to predict behavioural change, not the stock market! It feels less about the actual research and more about ticking boxes. Tell me about it. We’re having the same battle with justifying the new assessment tools. Head just wants everything tied to a percentage point increase in attainment. Like children are algorithms you can just tweak. I keep trying to explain the nuance, the qualitative benefits, the improved wellbeing… it goes in one ear and out the other. It’s infuriating, isn’t it? It’s like they’ve completely lost sight of the  people  involved. Both our fields are fundamentally about improving lives, yet we spend so much time justifying that to… people in offices. Exactly! And it bleeds into everything, doesn’t it? Even just thinking about things with Mum and Dad… they were on at me again about getting a ‘proper’ garden. Like, I’m not utilising the space to its full potential. As if my little herb garden isn’t enough! Oh, bless them. They're from a generation where everything had to be…  productive . A garden wasn’t for enjoyment, it was for growing your own veg to survive the winter. It’s lovely they care, but it can be a bit much. It is. Though, honestly, I’m starting to feel guilty about not visiting more. Work's been manic, and by the time I finish, I just want to collapse. Are you managing alright with seeing your Nan? Yeah, I try to get down every other weekend. It's a bit of a trek, but she’s… sharper than me some days. Always has a story to tell. Though she's been hinting she wants me to meet someone.

…and honestly, Doreen, it weren’t just the sea air, though that did ‘elp. It was gettin’  out . Just… away from these four walls. Used to be, I'd pop down to the pub most days, see a familiar face, ‘ave a quick half. Now… well, you know. Can't afford it, for a start, and truth be told, even if I  could , I don’t fancy the company much these days. Everyone’s got their worries, and it just… adds to it, don't it? It does, Arthur, it really does. It's a weight, ain't it? That constant… heavy feeling. You’re right about gettin' out, though. Even a walk around the block helps me sometimes. Though, truth be told, I mostly just potter in the garden. Keeps me busy, I suppose. Have you been thinkin’ about what we talked about last week? The volunteering? Just jumping in here, actually. I think volunteering  is  a good idea, Arthur. You’ve always been good with your hands. Remember that model railway you built for young Thomas, Doreen? He was absolutely mesmerised. Something practical might be just what you need. A focus. Model railway was years ago, David! And Thomas is a grown man with kids of his own now. Time flies, don’t it? Volunteering… I don't know. Seems a bit… pointless, if I’m honest. What good am I to anyone? I’m just an old bloke, skint and feelin' sorry for himself. Don't talk like that, Arthur. You’re not pointless. You’ve got a lifetime of experience. And honestly, thinking about being ‘skint’ all the time… it’s just makin’ things worse for yourself. It’s understandable, with everything that’s happened with the house prices and pensions, but dwelling on it won’t change things. Remember when we talked about down-sizing? Don't start on the house again, Doreen. It's a bad memory. We lost a fortune on that place, remember? Tried to do the right thing, move closer to the sea, but it all went wrong. And now look at me, rattling around in this little flat, wishin’ I 'ad a garden like yours. It's easy to get caught up in regrets, isn’t it? But you have to look forward, Arthur. Focusing on what  could  have been isn't helpful. Maybe the volunteering could be a way to meet people, make a difference.

… honestly, I just don’t  get  the whole gel polish thing. It looks amazing when you leave the salon, yeah, but the removal is a nightmare! I chipped one after, like, three days last week. Three! And then the soaking, the filing… my nails felt completely wrecked. Oh, you’re telling me! I had a right palaver last month. It felt like I was chiselling the stuff off. I ended up at the chemist’s buying cuticle oil and a hand mask just to recover. Though, I  do  love how long it lasts. You know Sarah from work? She gets acrylics, and they're on for weeks! Sarah’s are always immaculate. But acrylics seem so… permanent? I’ve always been a bit wary. I can’t imagine the damage that does long-term. I’m trying to be a bit kinder to my nails at the moment. Been using this cuticle oil – it’s from Boots, really basic – and it’s actually making a difference. Boots do some good stuff, yeah. I usually pick up my nail varnish remover from there. Though I’ve been branching out into shopping online a bit lately. Found this amazing little site selling all sorts of beauty bits, really cheap. You’d love it. Oh really? Do send me the link. I’m always up for a bargain. I’ve been wanting to try one of those face rollers, the jade ones. Seen them all over Instagram, obviously. Seems a bit…faddy, doesn’t it? But everyone says they reduce puffiness. They do! My cousin, Chloe, she swears by hers. Says it’s made a huge difference to her sinuses too. The site I was talking about, it’s called ‘GlowUpGetIt’. Ridiculous name, I know, but they had a jade roller for a tenner! Tenner! Boots is like twenty-five for a basic one. Tenner? Right, link, please. Immediately. I'm a sucker for a good beauty deal and I need something to distract me from the grey weather. Honestly, Torquay’s looking particularly drab today. Stoke must be even worse… It’s not  too  bad, thankfully. Bit drizzly, but not full-on grim. And that's the joy of online shopping, isn't it? Gets you through the gloom. Speaking of which, have you seen what’s happened with Emma? Emma? No, what's going on? Last I heard she was supposed to be going on that weekend break to Brighton.

… honestly, the Walker's parking is a joke, innit? I was only nipping in to see the Linda McCartney exhibition, right? Lovely stuff, genuinely, but spent half an hour circling like a vulture just to find a space. Then nearly got a ticket 'cause the machine wouldn’t read my card. Tell me about it! I had a similar thing last week trying to get into the Tate. It's daylight robbery, the prices they charge for parking too. Especially when you’re already shelling out for the museum entry. You enjoying the Linda McCartney though? I keep meaning to go. Yeah, it was brilliant. Really affecting, y’know? A lot of the stuff I'd seen in books, obviously, but seeing it blown up… it hits different. Makes you think. Anyway, enough about my cultural adventures. How's work been? Still battling the bureaucracy? Don't even get me started. Had a case this week with a family, proper heartbreaking. Mum's just trying to hold everything together, but the council keeps sending her around in circles for support. Honestly, some days I feel like I'm fighting  against  the system more than  for  the people I'm supposed to be helping. It’s draining. That sounds rough, mate. Seriously. It's good you’re doing it, though. Someone's gotta. Speaking of draining, I've got this Masters interview next week. Feeling proper stressed about it. No way! Really? That's brilliant, Liam! Which uni? What's it in? Uni of York. Applied for Applied Linguistics. It feels like a proper reach, though. They were asking about my research interests on the phone, and I just… mumbled something about phonology. Sounded like a right prat. You'll be grand. You’re a teacher, phonology is your bread and butter! They'll see how passionate you are about the language. You always put so much effort into your lessons. Though, admittedly, sometimes I just glaze over when you start talking about vowel sounds. Fair enough! It's a bit niche, I’ll grant you. It's just… it’s expensive, y’know? The course fees are hefty, and then trying to live on a student loan again… Ugh. Gotta start saving, I suppose. Maybe cut back on the coffee? Don't you dare! This is essential fuel for surviving. Maybe less shopping? Sarah and I were down Bold Street yesterday, she went mental for vintage clothes.

…and honestly, the whole thing with Mark’s daughter, Chloe, just feels…exhausting. It’s not  her  fault, obviously. She’s twelve, going through it, dealing with divorced parents. But it’s like walking on eggshells constantly. Any suggestion, even a harmless one about homework, is met with this glacial silence. Oh, darling, I can imagine. Step-parenting is…a beast. It really is. It's not something anyone prepares you for, is it? When you fall in love with someone, you don’t sign up for negotiating adolescent angst as part of the package. Exactly! And I feel terrible saying that, truly. I want to be a good influence, a supportive figure. But I’m not her mum, and she doesn't  want  another mum. It's just…I’m starting to feel like a spare part in my own home, sometimes. Mark’s understandably protective, which is good, but it means I tend to defer to him on everything Chloe-related. You’re being too hard on yourself, Sarah. You  are  a good influence. Just by being you, by being a stable presence in their lives. And deferring to him…well, that’s sensible. It’s new territory for everyone. Though, honestly, sometimes I think Mark could be a little more mindful of  your  feelings in all this. He’s lucky to have you, you know. Especially after…well, you know. After the disaster that was David? Yes, I suppose I am rather good at picking projects. Though sometimes I wonder if ‘projects’ is the right word for people! It’s just…remember when I was completely heartbroken, and you were the one who dragged me out, made me re-join the world? I feel like  I  should be doing that for you now. You've been so wonderfully selfless with little Leo, putting your whole life on hold… Oh, stop it. Leo is my world, absolutely. But it's not the same. You’re building a life  with  someone, navigating all this family complexity. I'm…well, I'm sort of in a holding pattern. Ben's no help, frankly. He’s lovely, but hopelessly adrift. Still 'finding himself' three years after graduating. That's awful, Kate. Truly. You deserve so much more. You’re so intelligent, so capable. You could be doing anything. It must be incredibly frustrating. It is. And it’s not just the financial thing, though that’s a huge pressure, obviously.

… honestly, I just don’t  get  the appeal of those renovation shows. Like, ‘Homes Under the Hammer’ – it’s just…stressful to watch. All that damp proofing and structural integrity talk. Makes my own flat feel a bit precarious, y’know? You’re a research manager, you deal with precariousness all day! Shouldn’t a bit of crumbling plaster phase you? I find it oddly satisfying. Seeing something potentially awful transformed. Plus, Martin Roberts is a national treasure. Martin Roberts is…enthusiastic. That’s being kind. And work precariousness is different. That’s data and deadlines, not potential woodworm. Anyway, I've been scrolling Pinterest again. Dangerously. It's a rabbit hole, I tell ya. Pinterest? Still? Thought you’d given that up after the ‘Scandinavian minimalist kitchen’ phase nearly bankrupted you. Alright, alright! That was one expensive mood board. But now it’s just…birthday ideas for Gran. She’s convinced she doesn’t want anything, but we  have  to get her something. Last year’s gardening gloves were a disaster. She said they “felt like sandpaper”. Oh dear. Gran’s a tough crowd. What are you thinking this year? I can brainstorm. Though, knowing your Pinterest, it’ll be something involving hand-thrown pottery and ethically sourced alpaca wool. Don't you dare! Though…there  is  a really lovely hand-knitted blanket…no. No Pinterest influence. I was thinking maybe a framed photo? Of all of us? She always says family is the most important thing. Cheesy, I know. Not cheesy at all. Actually, that’s a brilliant idea. Much better than alpaca wool. Though, knowing you, you’ll spend three hours choosing the perfect frame. Possibly. It has to be just right. Speaking of family…have you heard anything from Liam? Haven’t seen him post anything on social media in ages. He’s alright. Actually, he messaged me earlier. He’s completely immersed in his new coding project. Living off instant noodles and the sheer power of caffeine, apparently. Classic Liam. He said he'd try and make your birthday bash, but it depends if he manages to debug this algorithm by then. Typical. Always the drama. He promised his presence at my 26th, then his laptop died. Said it was a sign from the universe. A sign from the universe . He's a good lad, though. A bit…eccentric. You’ve got a good group of friends, you know.

…No, that one's  definitely  too fussy. All that glass, honestly. It'll be a dust trap, and you know how I feel about dust. Remember the debacle with the chandelier in the dining room? Never again. Right, the 'chandelier incident'. A lesson learned, definitely. Though I still maintain it  would  have looked lovely. You just didn’t give it a chance. This one’s simpler though, isn’t it? The brushed chrome? Simpler, yes. But… a bit  boring ? I was hoping for something with a little… personality. Something a bit more 'wow'. We’re putting in a new ceiling, we should at least have a light fitting to match. Have you checked the industrial ones again? The metal cages? I did, briefly. They were mostly over a hundred quid, and frankly, they looked like something off a battleship. I thought we were trying to move  towards  cosy, not industrial revolution. Plus, remember the ceiling height in the hallway is lower. A big, hanging thing would just make it feel cramped. Hmm, fair point. Okay, okay. Let’s go back to the search and filter by ‘flush mount’. And maybe ‘art deco’? I saw a couple on Pinterest that were quite nice…Oh! Hang on, look at this one. Sort of a frosted glass with the chrome rim. Not  too  fussy. That’s… actually quite nice. It’s subtle. How much is it? Fifty-nine ninety-nine, plus postage. Looks like it's coming from Sheffield. Seems decent. While you're looking at that, have you had any luck with Rightmove? Anything remotely resemble our 'dream cottage' popping up? A few. Mostly needing a  lot  of work. And predictably, outside our price range. There was one in North Yorkshire, near Richmond… looked promising in the photos, but then I read the details. Damp proof course needed, complete rewire, new heating system… it was basically a shell. Richmond’s lovely though, isn’t it? We had a good weekend there a few years back. But you’re right, we're not DIY enthusiasts. We want somewhere we can move into and  live , not spend the next five years renovating. Precisely. It’s the gardens I’m craving, more than anything. A decent sized garden. This flat’s been lovely for a while, but… you can't really  get  your hands dirty, can you? Just a tiny balcony. No, you can’t. And the neighbours complaining if you even  look  at a potted plant slightly askew.

… honestly, I just don’t know what Mrs. Henderson  does  all day. I popped in to check her medication – she keeps forgetting, the dear – and honestly, the state of the place! It’s not  dirty , exactly, just…cluttered. Like a magpie’s nest. And she was watching daytime TV, obviously. Oh, bless her. She’s always been a bit…eccentric, hasn’t she? Remember when she tried to pay for her shopping with bottle caps? No way! Really? Honestly! Poor checkout girl looked mortified. I had to step in and sort it out. It’s getting harder, though, isn’t it? Seeing the decline. It reminds me a bit of Mum, towards the end. Though Mum was never keen on bottle caps. More of a sherry lady, she was. Oh, don't remind me of your Mum and sherry! She always tried to sneak a little bit to me when your Dad wasn't looking. Cheeky as anything. Still, it’s tough, seeing people you know…fade. Especially when you’re trying to keep everything going at work. I'm knackered as it is. Tell me about it. Old Mr. Davies at the residential home nearly gave me a heart attack this morning. Tried to wander off again. He keeps saying he’s going to “catch the 32 to Dover”. There isn’t a 32 to Dover anymore! Oh, that’s awful. They do get fixated, don’t they? It’s the confusion, I suppose. I've been thinking, actually… I'm seriously considering going for that Team Leader role at the hospital. Oh, the one they advertised? That’s brilliant, Sarah! You’d be perfect for it. More money, too, wouldn't it? Hopefully. Bit more responsibility, obviously. But I’m tired of just…being on the floor, you know? Always dealing with the immediate stuff. I want to be able to actually  make  a difference, influence things a bit. Plus, Gary said it'd help us with the deposit on a conservatory. A conservatory? That’s lovely! You’ve been talking about that for ages. Though I can’t imagine Gary doing much of the building work himself! That’s putting it mildly. He’s more of a ‘supervisory’ role kind of builder. Honestly, he’s better at admiring the finished product. Speaking of houses, have you started properly looking, Chloe? You said you were thinking about moving? Yeah, a bit.

… honestly, the sheer volume of conflicting advice is baffling. Apparently, blue light  is  awful, but then another study says a small dose right before bed can actually help regulate your melatonin. It’s just…noise. What did you think of the bit about temperature though? Lowering it to like, sixteen degrees? That sounds…uncomfortable. Sixteen degrees? Good Lord, no. I’d be shivering all night. I think the idea has some merit, though. I read something similar about needing to feel slightly cool to fall asleep. We already have the bedroom quite chilly, but sixteen…that’s ambitious. It’s all a bit ‘one size fits all’ isn’t it? What works for a research lab in Sweden isn’t necessarily going to work for me in Cambs. Exactly! It’s the same with all this ‘optimal sleep schedule’ nonsense. As if life allows for that. Speaking of needing a break from everything, have you been thinking about that camping trip we discussed? I was looking at sites in the New Forest. Oh, yes! That sounds lovely. Though, knowing us, we’ll probably end up completely lost attempting to navigate there. Remember that time in Rome? We spent a good two hours walking in circles trying to find the Colosseum. Don’t remind me. I swore I had a good mental map, and then suddenly we were back at that little gelateria for the third time. It’s my spatial awareness, or lack thereof. It’s tragic. At least with camping, everything’s pretty much…outdoors. Less opportunity to get spectacularly lost. Though I  did  once get turned around on a walking track near Wellington. Thick bush, no signal. Thankfully, I just backtracked, but it was a bit unnerving. Wellington…you always manage to bring it back to New Zealand, don’t you? But you’re right, a forest is different to a city. With a city, everything looks the same after a while. All those identical buildings. Speaking of getting places, I was talking to Sarah about her brother, the pilot. Oh, the one who flies those little Cessnas? Is he still doing that? Yes, he is. And apparently, he had a near miss last week. Not a crash, thankfully, but a rather hairy situation approaching Stansted. He misjudged the wind shear coming off the runway – apparently pretty strong gusts. Wind shear is nasty stuff. Really tests a pilot’s skill.

… honestly, I still can’t believe Old Man Tibbles managed to escape  again . He’s a proper Houdini, that ‘amster. I swear, he’s planning something. Honestly, a hamster escaping is hardly a criminal mastermind situation, is it, Chloe? Probably just smelled the biscuits. Though, I do agree, they’re surprisingly resourceful little things. My nan had one when I was little, it used to stuff its cheeks so full it looked like a tiny, furry football. Biscuits? Nah, Tibbles is after freedom, pet. He’s seen the world outside his cage, felt the wind in his whiskers… probably. Though, knowing Leeds weather, it was probably just a drizzle in his whiskers. Aye, freedom! Or maybe just looking for a better quality sunflower seed. My cousin’s ‘amster was obsessed. Spent a whole afternoon trying to tunnel through the sofa. Ruined it, she said. A better quality sunflower seed is a valid point, I'll give ya that. But this is the third time this month! I’m startin’ to think he’s got a little accomplice. Maybe Luna’s put him up to it. She looks at him all shifty-like. Luna? The cat? Chloe, are you suggesting your cat is  helping  a hamster escape? That’s… a bit much, even for you. I’m just saying! She’s been awfully quiet lately. Too quiet. And she keeps nudging his cage. It’s suspicious. She’s a cat, lass. Nudging cages is what they  do . It’s instinct. Though, I will admit, Luna’s a bit of a character. Reminds me of my auntie Maureen – always up to no good but lookin’ all innocent. Speaking of characters… anyone else think it’s a bit weird how many gingers there are around here? Like, statistically, it shouldn’t be this many. Gingers? What prompted  that  observation, Bethany? Dunno, just noticed it today. Walked to the shops and saw three, then saw another two on the bus. It’s a ginger conspiracy, I’m telling ya! They’re plottin’ somethin’. Oh, you and your conspiracies! It's just chance, love. Though, I  do  think gingers are rarer. It’s a recessive gene, isn’t it? Me dad always said he was blessed with the fiery hair. He’s not wrong, it’s recessive. My history teacher went on about it for a whole lesson. Said Scotland’s got the highest percentage of natural redheads in the world.

Right, well, that’s another continent tentatively held. Though frankly, Nigel, you’re looking dangerously strong in North America. Seriously, is that… eight armies in Alaska? You absolute menace. Alaska’s the key, lad, the  key . You gotta control the choke point. Didn't anyone teach you Risk strategy? Though, to be fair, you were probably too busy grading essays or whatever it is you young’uns do these days. Honestly, Nigel, you always go for the aggressive early game. It’s exhausting just watching. And the way you pronounce ‘Kamchatka’… honestly, it’s appalling. It’s  Kam-chat-ka , not ‘Kam-chatch-ker’! Oi, leave my Kamchatka alone! It’s a perfectly good pronunciation! Sounds more… robust, innit? Besides, nobody cares when you’re about to wipe the floor with ‘em. Anyway, Sarah, did you manage to find that chocolate I hid earlier? I need sustenance for this epic battle. Seriously though, is anyone else finding this update version of Risk a bit… clunky? The troop movement feels slower, and I’m sure the dice rolls are weighted against me. It’s infuriating. Remember the old cardboard version? Simpler times. I rather like it. It’s nice to have the automatic calculations. It saves my brain a bit, honestly. Though I do miss the smell of the cardboard, you're right. It smelled like Christmas and arguments all rolled into one. Speaking of Christmas, have you lot started thinking about presents yet? Christmas already? Good grief. I’m still processing Halloween. Though, thinking about presents… Aaron mentioned something about wanting a new gaming headset. He’s convinced his current one’s affecting his K/D ratio. The things kids worry about. Aaron's getting a bit old for that now, isn't he? Nearly a teenager. Remember when they were tiny? Those pregnancy tests… honestly, terrifying things. And then the constant worry. I wouldn't trade it for the world, mind, but it changes you. It does. It's… a different kind of responsibility. Friends of mine are having real debates about whether to have another. One’s considering… well, other options. It’s a difficult conversation. The ethics of it all. They were talking about sterilization even. Wow. That’s… intense. My generation feels so different. Fewer people are having kids, or they’re waiting until much later. I mean, I’m 27 and the idea of little humans running around feels… alien.

… honestly, I just feel a bit lost, yeah? Like, everyone else seems to have this  plan . Chloe’s already interning at some fancy marketing firm, and Ben's applying for grad schemes left, right and centre. I’m here, still vaguely considering marine biology, which, let’s be real, isn’t exactly known for its booming job market. Oh, love, stop comparing yourself. Chloe’s dad practically  owns  a marketing firm, and Ben’s been prepping for this since year ten. It’s not a fair fight. And marine biology’s brilliant! You were always obsessed with Jacques Cousteau as a kid. Remember dressing up as a diver for fancy dress? Alright, alright, you got me. The flippers were a bit ambitious, admittedly. But it feels… impractical, doesn’t it? Staying here another three years just to potentially end up working at the National Marine Aquarium? No offence to the aquarium, but…it’s not exactly Hollywood, is it? Hollywood? What's brought  that  on? You been watching too much telly again? No! Well, a little. I was scrolling through Insta and saw this article about Florence Pugh. Apparently, she dropped out of drama school after a year and is smashing it. Makes you think, doesn’t it? Maybe formal education isn’t always the be-all and end-all. Florence Pugh is a special case, petal. She's a ridiculously talented actress. And everything you see on Insta is polished up, remember. It's not the whole truth. Look, you've got a good brain, you smashed your A-Levels. Don’t throw away a degree because someone famous took a different path. Unless you fancy busking outside the Sugarhouse for a living? Very funny. No, definitely not busking. It's just… I'm starting to wonder if I even  want  a ‘career’ career. Like, the sort of thing where you get stuck in an office for forty years. I get it. I’m terrified of that. Honestly, sometimes I look at my mum, bless her, and I just think… no. No spreadsheets and pointless meetings. Though, to be fair, she’s started a dog grooming business, so she’s not  totally  chained to the desk anymore. See, that's amazing! That's… inspiring, actually. Maybe I should just open a little seashell shop in Falmouth. 'Shells by Sophie'! Oh, god, that is peak Falmouth. You’d be a millionaire.

… honestly, Mr. Davies is taking the mickey. A fifteen-page report on the socio-economic impact of the closure of the old bus depot? Who even  cares  about that? It’s Slough, not…I dunno, Wall Street. Tell me about it. It’s just busywork. He's trying to make us sound all sophisticated, like we’re little social scientists. But it IS a bit grim, though, isn’t it? My nan used to get the bus from there. Said it was the only way she could get to her doctor's appointments affordably. Yeah, I guess. Mum was saying something about it affecting loads of people in the estate. More walking, longer journeys… it’s all a bit rubbish, really. Makes you think, doesn’t it? Like, everyone’s just trying to get by. Absolutely. It's a proper postcode lottery, innit? Like, we're lucky. We both get to come to a decent sixth form. Loads of lads I know from Wembley just… didn’t. Went straight into some dead-end job or, well, worse. It's not  fair . I mean, Lewis is seriously smart but he’s working at his uncle’s garage now. He said he couldn’t afford the travel to college and his mum needs the money. It’s proper depressing. It is. And it’s not like anyone’s doing anything about it, is it? Just more talk from politicians. Did you see that thing on the news about the new tax cuts? Giving money to people who already have loads. Ugh, don't even get me started. It's ridiculous. Like, focus on helping people who genuinely  need  it, you know? Instead of lining the pockets of the already rich. It's just… consumerism gone mad. Everyone chasing stuff they don't need, while other people can’t even afford to eat properly. Totally. It's like they want us all to be constantly buying things to feel good. Even  I  fall for it sometimes, wanting the latest trainers or a new game. It’s brainwashing, almost. It is! Speaking of games, did you see the new  Cosmic Crusader  comic? The artwork is insane. Proper retro-futuristic. No way! I haven’t! Is it as good as the first one? Old Man Hemlock's story arc was brilliant. Proper philosophical, that. It’s even better. They’ve got this new villain, Xylar, who's basically a reflection of humanity’s greed.

…and honestly, the whole recording process was a nightmare. Trying to get a decent vocal take when Mrs. Higgins next door decides 3pm on a Tuesday is the  perfect  time to practice her tuba? Utterly ridiculous. It sounded like a distressed elephant was living alongside my mixing desk. Oh, bless her. Old Mrs. Higgins, is it? I remember you mentioning her. Always seems to be…enthusiastic about  something . Was it for the village fete practice, or just general tuba-ing? Just general tuba-ing, apparently! No rhyme nor reason. And she doesn’t even sound  good , darling. It’s…robust. Let’s leave it at robust. Anyway, it threw off the timing completely. I’ve lost a perfectly good hour trying to edit around it. Oof, that’s frustrating. Editing is such a faff. I tried to do a little video editing, ages ago, for that…well, never mind. It just ended up looking awful. Still, at least you  have  something to edit! I've been mostly…existing. Nonsense, you’re not ‘just existing’. You’re…resting. Recuperating. Planning your next epic adventure. How’s the physio going, anyway? Still battling those knees? It’s okay. It’s…slow. Honestly, I feel like a ninety-year-old sometimes. Every time I bend down to pick something up, it’s a full-body operation. The physio keeps saying it’s strengthening, but I think my joints are just actively rebelling against me. Oh, I know that feeling! My hips are playing up something awful. Honestly, I feel like I’ve been assembled from spare parts, and none of them quite fit anymore. It’s a right nuisance. I’ve been trying to be more diligent with the exercises, but it’s hard when everything aches. It is. It really is. I saw this ad for one of those meal replacement shakes…you know, promising weight loss and everything? I was tempted. But then I thought, what’s the point? It'll just be bland sadness in a bottle. Don't even go there, love. Those things are dreadful. I tried a juice cleanse once, back in the nineties. Complete and utter misery. And it didn’t even work! Plus, you need  proper  food. Comfort food! I was making a treacle tart yesterday, remember? Did I offer you a slice? You did, and it was glorious. Absolutely glorious. So much better than pretending to be fulfilled by a beige liquid.

… honestly, I just don’t get why they keep changing the layout of the conference centre. It was  fine  before! Perfectly functional. Now they’ve put all the breakout rooms miles away from the main hall. Old Mrs. Higgins nearly had a heart attack trying to find room three for her ceramics workshop last week. Oh, tell me about it. Reorganisations for the sake of reorganisations. It’s the same at work. They decided to ‘streamline’ production last month, which actually just meant adding three extra steps and confusing everyone. How was your week otherwise? Apart from the architectural sabotage? Chaotic, as usual. Trying to wrestle vendors into agreeing on sensible pricing. You wouldn’t believe how much some of these linen companies try to charge for tablecloths! It’s daylight robbery, I tell you. Proper Yorkshire grit needed to negotiate with ‘em. And then, Derek from AV keeps ‘forgetting’ to book equipment. Honestly, I think he does it on purpose to make his life more interesting. Derek sounds… a character. Sounds like you're earning your wage then. Production’s been a nightmare as well, actually. We had a supplier issue with a vital component for the new batch. Nearly ground everything to a halt. Spent two days on conference calls, going back and forth. They kept saying “logistical challenges,” which, let's be real, just meant they messed up. "Logistical challenges." That’s corporate speak for "we’ve dropped the ball." Honestly. It's just… draining. I keep thinking I should’ve just taken that job at the garden centre. Less stress, more plants. Though I doubt Mrs. Higgins would’ve appreciated a greenhouse instead of a breakout room. Don’t even think about it. You’re brilliant at what you do, even if Derek tries to ruin your life one powerpoint presentation at a time. And a garden centre? You’d be bored within a week. You need the chaos. Plus, think of the free canapés. You’ve got a point about the canapés. Alright, alright. I’ll stick with the organised mayhem. Speaking of sticking with things… are you still seeing that lad, Leo? The musician? Oh, uh, yeah. We are. It’s… good. He’s writing a new song, actually. It’s all moody and atmospheric. Very Leo. He’s playing a gig next week at that little pub near Mill Road, ‘The Blue Moon’. Fancy coming?

… honestly, I just don’t  get  the hype around superhero films anymore. It's all just… explosions and no substance. Like, yeah, the CGI is impressive, but give me something with actual character development, you know? Oh, come on, Liv! That’s a bit harsh. Some of them are genuinely good!  Guardians of the Galaxy  is hilarious, and even the recent  Spider-Man  ones have got some emotional weight to ‘em. It’s a bit of escapism, isn’t it? We’re all stressed with uni. Aye, I’m with Aoife there. It's a bit of a laugh, isn't it? I mean, I wouldn't be queuing up for a serious drama after a long day of lectures, would ye? Something to switch the brain off. Though I did think the last Batman was alright, a bit dark even for me, mind. Dark is good, though! I loved the Nolan Batman trilogy. That’s proper filmmaking, thinking about the psychology of the characters. This whole Marvel/DC thing… it's just… repetitive. It's like they're churning them out for the money. Oh my god, you’re all so old! Superhero films are amazing! Have you  seen  the new  Deadpool ? It’s so funny and self-aware. It's not like the others. It knows it's ridiculous. See? This is what I mean! It's  because  it knows it's ridiculous that it feels… empty. Like it’s poking fun at itself instead of trying to tell a story. I’d rather watch something like  Aftersun . Have any of you seen  Aftersun ?  Aftersun ? Vaguely. Isn’t that the one all the artsy people were going on about? Was proper slow-burn, wasn't it? I wouldn’t put that on for a casual Friday night, would I? You’d need a whole mood for that. I tried to watch it, actually, but I fell asleep about twenty minutes in. No offence, Liv, but it was a bit… depressing. I needed something a bit more uplifting. Depressing? It's  realistic ! It's about grief, and memory, and… Hold on now, girls. Don’t be at each other’s throats over films. It's just a matter of taste, isn’t it? I think ye’re both right, in yer own way. Some times ye want something thought-provoking, other times ye just want a wee bit of mindless fun.

… honestly, the queue for the Louvre was  insane . Like, winding all the way down the street insane. We spent a good hour just shuffling forward a few feet. Oh, Paris. Always so popular. Did you at least get to see the Mona Lisa? It's a right scrum to get near, apparently. We did, eventually. It’s… smaller than you think. And there’s a bulletproof glass barrier and about fifty phones being held aloft. It’s less ‘appreciating art’ and more ‘witnessing a tiny painting through a forest of iPhones’. Exactly! It felt like a pilgrimage to a tiny, slightly underwhelming celebrity. Honestly, the pastries were the highlight. And the wandering. We got properly lost in Montmartre. Montmartre is lovely. I went years ago with your father. We had a terrible row about a beret, if you can believe it. He thought it was terribly cliché. Dad and clichés, a timeless battle. Anyway, the wandering was nice until… well, until I managed to trip over absolutely nothing. Oh no! Not again. Is your ankle alright? You were limping a bit when we got back. It’s… fine. I think. I twisted it pretty badly. It's swollen. I’m blaming the cobblestones and my complete lack of spatial awareness. I was showing Chloe that little antique shop, talking about a ridiculously overpriced porcelain doll, and BAM. Down I went. Honestly, you are a magnet for mishaps, love. Remember that time you broke your toe on the garden gnome? Mum! Don’t remind me! It was a particularly aggressive gnome. And this is worse. I’ve been icing it, but it’s still proper tender. I might need to get it checked, actually. Work’s going to be a nightmare if I can’t walk properly. The new project launch is next week. You’ll be okay. I can look at it properly later, give you a proper assessment. Being a nurse has  some  perks, even for friends. Just promise you won’t try and hobble around on it and make it worse. You're a lifesaver, seriously. Chloe was trying to convince me to just tape it up and carry on. Chloe! Honestly, sometimes that girl is all thrills and no sense. Speaking of which, how  is  she? You haven't mentioned much about her lately. Oh, she's good. She’s really stressed about her dissertation though. It’s on… wait for it… the semiotics of TikTok dances.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of referencing errors I saw in those essays last week was  depressing . It’s like they haven’t even  looked  at the style guide. Honestly, you’d think after three years of an undergraduate degree… Tell me about it! I was explaining to Sarah on shift yesterday – she’s doing History, first year – how to properly cite a webpage. She just looked at me blankly. It’s a skill, innit? Not something that just…happens. Though, being a retail supervisor, I feel like I spend half my time explaining basic human interaction, so maybe I’m biased. A very valid point. You’re dealing with the general public; I'm dealing with, theoretically, future academics. Though sometimes the line blurs. How was your weekend, by the way? Did you finally get to Chichester? I did! It was lovely. Proper quaint, you know? Found a little tearoom, had a scone… stereotypical, I know, but brilliant. It’s just…different to Croydon. Everything’s so  fast  there. Did you do anything exciting? Not especially. Just a lot of marking, sadly. Tried to get some writing done on my novel, but it’s slow going. It’s a bit of a mess, grammar-wise, actually. Trying to use a lot of passives for a particular voice, and it's…tricky. Plus, ironically, spotting my  own  referencing mistakes is a nightmare. A novel! That’s amazing, Liam. What’s it about? Is it, like, a gritty Bedfordshire drama? No! It’s… sci-fi. Very far removed from Bedford, trust me. It pays to have hobbies unrelated to linguistics, otherwise, you become completely obsessed with parsing every sentence you hear. Speaking of which, I've been meaning to ask, did you ever get to see your sister? She was talking about a theatre trip. Oh, yeah! We went and saw ‘Wicked’ on Friday. Proper good. Bit cheesy, but good. She’s been going through a bit of a…time. You know, post-divorce. She finds musicals therapeutic. It's a bit of a long story. I remember her mentioning things were rocky. Horrible situation. Is she alright, though? She’s getting there. It’s just…the legal stuff is exhausting. And she's trying not to be bitter about  him  proposing to someone else already. Honestly, the audacity! It feels so soon. That’s just… awful. No manners. On a lighter note – pay day is tomorrow, right?

…No, seriously Mum, you  have  to get the rice-to-water ratio right. It’s not just chucking it in and hoping for the best. See? One cup of rice, and then…about one and a half cups of water. Maybe a little more, depends on the rice. This is basmati, it needs a bit extra. Right, right. One and a half. Sounds…precise. I used to just wing it, honestly. It usually ended up okay-ish. Though your Dad always complained it was sticky. "Okay-ish"?! That’s why we're having takeaway most weeks! Look, the key is not stirring it after it boils. None. Just put the lid on and let it do its thing for fifteen minutes. You'll forget, I know you will, but  don’t . Always the teacher, aren’t you? Alright, alright, no stirring. Fifteen minutes of blissful silence while you explain the intricacies of carbohydrate preparation. Speaking of which, are we definitely doing curry tonight? I saw that voucher for 'Spice Paradise'… fifty percent off mains. Spice Paradise? Ew, no way. Last time we went there, I swear the lamb tasted…off. Like,  really  off. And it was swimming in oil. No. We’re nailing this curry. It’ll be healthier, and better. Plus, I found those jalapenos in the cupboard. We can add a proper kick. Jalapenos? You know I can't handle spicy. A tiny bit of chilli powder is my limit. Honestly, that lamb probably wasn’t off, it was just… intensely flavoured. You're a bit dramatic sometimes, Liam. Intense flavoured? It smelled like something had died in the fridge and then been resurrected as a curry. Look, I'm checking the chicken now. Fingers crossed it’s still good. Remember that time we bought that chicken and it…well, it wasn’t good. The smell… Don’t remind me. Honestly, I'm always worried about things going off. It's difficult, you know? With everything…being tight. I don’t want to waste food. It's awful. It's like... I read this article the other day about the amount of salt and fat they put in pre-made meals. It’s scary. Yeah, that's why cooking from scratch is better. You control what goes in. And less salt, definitely. Remember Uncle David? Not the best example, is he? All that processed stuff… Liam, don’t. It’s not fair.

…Aye, but honestly, the telly’s just rubbish these days, innit? Nothing on. Used to be able to flick through and find summat, even if it were just a bit o’ rubbish. Now it’s all…repeats, or that American stuff. Proper headache inducing. Mmm, it is a bit bleak, Liam. Though I’m kinda hooked on that baking show, the one with the posh judges. It’s pure escapism, you know? Gets me mind off coursework. How’s the job hunt goin’, by the way? Still nowt? Nowt. Absolutely nowt. Sent out another load o’ applications this week. All entry level stuff, mind, ‘cause a degree in History doesn’t exactly scream ‘employable’ does it? Just gettin’ auto-replies sayin’ “we’ve had a high volume of applicants.” High volume! Likely every other lad fresh outta uni’s sending the same application. It’s rough, yeah. My mam keeps tellin’ me I should just get any job, even workin' in a shop, but I don’t know… feels a bit defeatist, doesn’t it? I’m thinkin’ about a gap year before uni, but even  that  costs money. Your mam’s just worried, Lena. She wants the best for you. And Liam, don’t beat yourself up about the degree. History's brilliant! It just…doesn’t always translate directly into a job. Have you thought about tailoring your CV more? Focusin' on transferable skills? Like research, analysis…that sort o’ thing? I’ve tried, Chloe. Honestly, I have. They all want experience, though, don’t they? And how am I supposed to  get  experience if nobody'll give me a chance? It’s a right catch-22. Gran keeps offerin’ me money, bless her, but I can’t keep takin’ it. Feels…wrong. Gran’s a sweetheart, though. She worries about you. Remember when she tried to set you up with Mrs. Higgins' granddaughter? Don’t even. That was…awkward. She was lovely, but she talked non-stop about her guinea pigs. Guinea pigs! Oh god, I remember! She’d bring pictures. She just wants to see you settled, Liam. Honestly. Speaking of settled, Lena, how are things with Mark? Still goin’ strong? Yeah, it’s good. He’s been helpin’ me with my personal statement for uni. He’s really good at writin’. Though he keeps tryin’ to convince me to apply for the same course as him, which… I don’t know.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I had waiting for me this mornin’ was just  criminal . People expectin’ instant responses when they know full well I was at a wedding reception 'til midnight! It’s ridiculous, it is. Like, do they think I just  live  at my inbox? Sounds stressful, love. Though, to be fair, weddings  are  usually pretty draining. Worth it, though, right? Who did you go with? Aye, it was good. Proper good actually. Went with Jamie. He's alright, Jamie. Good dancer, which is always a plus. But work… work’s a nightmare currently. This conference in November… trying to get all the speakers sorted, the venue’s being difficult, and the budget… well, the budget’s tighter than a Scotsman’s purse strings. November already? Blimey. Doesn't time fly. You always seem to be organising  something . It must be exhausting. I used to get tired just thinking about having a proper job. It has its moments, that's for sure. But it's good money, and I enjoy the creative side of it. Plannin’ things out, seein’ it all come together… That’s the bit I like. Though I’m beginnin’ to think I need to start takin’ up runnin’ or somethin’. I’m feelin’ proper sluggish. Runnin’? You? I remember you complainin’ about PE at school. Said Mrs. Higgins made you wear that awful navy blue kit. Oh, don’t remind me! That kit was the bane of my existence. But that was years ago! I need to do somethin’ for meself, you know? Get a bit fitter. Just walkin’ the dog isn’t cuttin’ it anymore. You wouldn't believe the amount of steps I do at these events, though. Honestly, by the end of a three-day conference, my Fitbit thinks I’ve climbed Everest. See, there you go! Plenty of exercise already. Though I suppose it's a different kind than headin’ out for a jog. I did try walkin' a few years back, ended up with blisters the size of 50p pieces. Gave up pretty quick. Aye, you’re not much of an outdoorsy type, are ya? Not like us Yorkshire folk. We’re bred to withstand a bit of wind and rain. I much prefer a nice cup of tea and a good book, thank you very much. Though, speakin’ of gettin’ out… Do you fancy comin’ to that little tea room in Grantchester with me next week?

Right, that was…substantial. Honestly, your father makes a shepherd’s pie like it’s a national crisis if it’s not at least an inch thick.      It  was  good though, Mum. Proper good. Can I go and play Fortnite now?      In a minute, Leo. Just help your brother clear these plates. And honestly, the state of your room. It looks like a bomb’s hit it. I swear, socks reproduce in there.      It’s not  that  bad, is it? I just…had a lot going on yesterday. Building a Lego Millennium Falcon takes commitment, you know.      Commitment is one word for it. Chaos is another. You two are a pair. You know, when I was your age, my mother just… accepted the mess. Said it was ‘creative energy’.      Your mother had a very different approach to parenting, darling. And 'creative energy' doesn’t explain the biscuit crumbs under the bed. Leo, honestly…      Okay, okay, plates. But can we talk about the tennis afterwards? Alcaraz is insane. Did you see that shot against Djokovic?      I did, actually. Very impressive. Though I still maintain Wimbledon should have stricter rules about grunting. It’s frankly rude.      Rudeness on a tennis court? Is that really a pressing matter?      It is when it’s distracting! It's like listening to someone trying to give birth every single shot! Speaking of distracting…Leo, who  is  this girl you keep looking at on Instagram? The one with the pink hair?      Oh, um…her name’s Chloe. She’s in my year.      Right. And is Chloe aware you’ve been analysing her every post for the last three weeks? Because it’s slightly…creepy.      I'm not  analysing ! I’m just…seeing what she’s up to.      Sounds like analysing to me. You were showing me screenshots of her stories yesterday.      Teenage courtship. It's a whole new world. It used to just be passing notes in class.      It’s more complicated now, that’s for sure. Remember when all you had to worry about was someone drawing a picture of you with a moustache on it?      Oh, don't remind me. There was a particularly vicious one in university involving a handlebar. And then  someone , who shall remain nameless – – decided to grow an actual one shortly after, purely out of spite.      That was a dark time. You looked like a Victorian villain. Speaking of villains…Did you guys learn anything interesting at school today?

…and honestly, the state of that sideboard when they delivered it! Scratched to bits. I had a right go at the delivery lads, I did. Said it looked like it had been dragged ‘round the tip. Speaking of which, did you manage to get rid of that old rug, Mum? Oh, aye. Took it down to the tip on Tuesday. Queue was horrendous, as always. Seems everyone decides Tuesdays are the day for a clear-out. Nearly didn’t bother, actually. Just thought, “Nah, not today.” Seriously? Tuesdays? That's a thing? I thought it was always weekends. No, Mum’s right. Tuesdays and Wednesdays are apparently the peak days. Something to do with the bin collections, I reckon. People realise what they  really  have to get rid of after bin day. Anyway, back to the sideboard… I'm thinking of getting them to replace the whole thing. It's just… the colour's perfect, isn’t it? It is lovely, that grey. Suits the room down to the ground. But scratched… that's not on. Did you tell Sharon about it? About the sideboard? She was asking how the furniture shopping went. Speaking of Sharon, did she mention how Dave’s doing? She said he wasn’t looking good last week. Aye, she did. She's really worried. Said he’s been forgetting things. Little things, at first, like where he put his keys, but now… she’s starting to worry it’s something more. She’s been talking about dementia, can you believe it? It's awful. It's terrible, that. My neighbour, old Mr. Henderson, went through that. Dreadful to watch. The person just… fades away. It's scary, isn't it? You hear about it, but when it’s someone you know... And she’s already got so much on her, with the kids. Exactly. She's a strong woman, Sharon. But this will test her. I told her to make sure she looks after  herself  too. It's easy to get swallowed up by it all. Did you hear, by the way, that Lisa’s friend, the one with the twins, has finally had a little boy? Oh, really? That's brilliant! After two girls, she was desperate for a boy. Good for them. Though I'll never understand folks who wash each other’s clothes. I overheard young Emily saying her friend, Chloe, washes her work uniform for her.

… honestly, Mum, it’s just  so  messed up. They called a meeting this morning, completely out of the blue, and announced redundancies across the department. Three of us gone, apparently. Oh, love, no! That’s dreadful. Which department? Was it…was it you, then? Don’t tell me it was you. Not  yet . They haven’t said who specifically, but the criteria they gave were pretty clear. Last in, first out, basically. Which, you know… that’s me. I only started six months ago. I’m trying not to panic, but it’s hard. I put so much into that project with Harrison Foods, I thought I was making a good impression. Oh sweetheart. That’s rotten luck. Absolutely rotten. They can’t just do that! You’ve got a degree, you’re a hard worker… Honestly, some companies! Right, don’t dwell on it now. We’ll figure something out. Have you spoken to anyone at work about it, like your manager? Yeah, briefly. She was…vague. Said she’d fight my corner, but she seemed pretty resigned to it all. Honestly, the whole office atmosphere is awful. Everyone’s walking on eggshells. Anyway, enough about work. Distraction tactics! What are you up to this weekend? Anything exciting? Not terribly exciting, no. Mrs. Peterson at school’s poorly, so I’m covering her exam invigilation on Saturday morning. Then…probably a bit of gardening, finally tackled that rose bush. Trying to be productive, you know? Though, I did promise your Grandad I’d pop over for tea. He’s been a bit quiet lately. Oh, that’s nice. He does love a good chat. You’ll have to tell me what he says. He’s been on about finally getting back to his wood carving, hasn't he? Still eating those biscuits with his tea, I bet? He pretends he doesn't… Oh, absolutely. A digestive biscuit is a vital component of Grandad’s afternoon. Honestly, I try to get him to eat more fruit, but he says it's 'too fiddly'. Men of his generation, honestly. You should be getting yourself down the gym, darling, instead of worrying about work and Grandad’s biscuit habits! That's what  I  do when things get stressful. Easy for you to say! You’re a gym bunny. I keep meaning to get back into it, but honestly, with everything going on, it’s the last thing on my mind.

…and then Old Man Hemlock just  vanished ! Like, poof! Right in the middle of telling a story about a badger. It was proper weird, Mum. Even for ‘Stick with Mick’. Honestly, that programme is a bit odd, isn’t it? All those weird characters. Right, dinner’s almost ready. Pasta with pesto, everyone? Leo, darling, stop trying to dismantle the salt shaker. Gah! Saaalt! No, Leo. No salt. It’s not a toy. Thomas, put your phone down for two minutes and tell me what you’ve been thinking about for the summer. We need a plan, a  rough  plan, to avoid you spending the entire six weeks glued to that thing. Ugh, a plan. I was kinda hoping to just…chill. Maybe see Finn, play some FIFA. Finn’s lovely, but you can’t see Finn  every  day. We need variety! We're in Cork now, remember? It's not Bristol. We need to explore. I was thinking maybe some swimming? The pool’s not too expensive. Swimming’s alright. But it gets boring after a bit. And it’s freezing, even with the indoor one. Well, what  would  you like to do? Anything? Your cousin, Emily, said they’re doing a Japanese language taster course at the community centre. Japanese? Seriously? What would I even  do  with Japanese? It’s just an idea! It might be fun. Learn a few phrases. And it’s something different. Honestly, Thomas, sometimes you’re as bad as your Dad at brainstorming. Just throw something out there. Anything. Well, I’ve been trying to get better at guitar. Maybe I could practice more. But then Mr. Henderson next door will complain again. He says it sounds like a “dying cat”. Oh, Mr. Henderson. He complains about everything. He complained about Leo learning to walk! Look, could you maybe practice in the shed? It’s not ideal, but it’s better than upsetting the neighbours. Leo, have you managed to get salt on  everything  yet? Mmm! Yummy! No, not yummy! It’s bad for you. Right, Thomas, what about helping me with some jobs around the house? A bit of gardening? Painting the fence? Painting the fence?! Mum, come on! That's a summer holiday punishment, not a summer activity! It’s character building! And honestly, it needs doing. It’s looking dreadful. Look, I’m just trying to get us organised. I feel terrible sometimes, being stuck here with Leo all day, not doing anything…it’s hard.

…No, seriously, the bit where the bloke just  casually  pulls out a medieval flail? It’s just…unexpected. Like, the film’s been a fairly grounded thriller up to that point, and then BAM! Flail. It's mental. Aye, it’s a bit much, innit? Though, to be fair, the writing’s been a bit dodgy all the way through. Feels like three different scripts mashed together. Still, better than going to the dentist, eh? Worlds better. I had a check-up last week. Dr. Patel’s a nice enough fella, but the sound of that drill… genuinely sends shivers down my spine. Reminds me of that time I tried to fix a shelf and nearly drilled through a pipe. Nearly flooded the whole flat. You and DIY! You're a disaster waiting to happen. Remember that Citibike you tried to assemble last summer? Took you a whole afternoon and half a bottle of wine. Don’t remind me! It was a symbolic representation of my life falling apart, really. Anyway, this film… what do you reckon we should do after? I was thinking that new Italian place, ‘Bella Notte’? Heard their pasta’s proper good. Sounds decent. Though, are we talkin’ proper Italian, or proper  Scouse  Italian? You know, where everything’s covered in garlic salt and chips are mandatory with everything? Please, no. I need a break from the chips. Speaking of breaks, I really need to get back to rewriting that short story. The deadline’s looming and I'm still stuck on the ending. Keeps feeling… flat. Still plugging away at that one, eh? What’s it about again? The bloke who collects vintage tea sets? No, that was the  other  one. This is the sci-fi thing. About the… well, it doesn't matter. It's rubbish. I'm considering chucking it and starting on that idea I had about the music scene in Leicester. Oh, the gig thing? That sounds more up your street. You were always bangin’ on about the music venues there. Proper indie scene, yeah? It was, yeah. Though, it’s changed a lot since I left for uni. Plus, trying to write authentically about that accent is… tricky. I keep ending up sounding like someone doing a bad impression. “Ey up, chuck! Fancy a brew?”  Stop it!  That’s… offensively inaccurate. It’s more subtle than that. It’s the vowel sounds, see?

… honestly, the traffic getting here was  awful . They’ve started roadworks on the A38 again, haven’t they? It’s always something. Anyway! Right, where were we? Oh yes, your new class. How are you finding them? Really, truly? Don’t just say ‘fine’. Mum, they’re… a handful. Properly. A lot of them are behind where they should be, especially with reading. And the behaviour! Little Leo tried to eat a crayon yesterday. A  purple  crayon. Oh, bless him. They do things like that, don’t they? You’ll have stories for years. It’s a tough age, Year Two. Requires the patience of a saint. Remember when your cousin, Emily, did her teaching practice in Year One? She nearly threw in the towel after the first week. I’m starting to see why! It's just… draining. But it's also rewarding when you see a little breakthrough. Little Maya finally grasped digraphs today. That was lovely. It's just the constant needing, you know? And the parents… some of them. Oh, the parents. Don’t even get me started. I remember when  your  parents were dealing with you and your… artistic phases. Mum! I was expressing myself! Anyway, enough about my woes. How was your weekend? Did you manage to get that Easter cake recipe perfected? Nearly! Nearly. I think I’ve finally cracked the icing. Last year it was a bit… runny, wasn’t it? Looked like a melted snowman. This year it’s firm, but still light. I’ve made three already, one for us, one for Auntie Brenda, and one for… well, for the Christening. Oh, right! The Christening. Still can’t believe little George is getting baptised already. It feels like yesterday Sarah was pregnant. Are you still organising the buffet and things? Yes, pretty much. I’ve ordered the sandwiches, and I’m doing a cold meats platter. Your father’s insisted on doing the vol-au-vents. He thinks he’s a chef, the man. Honestly, they’ll probably be slightly burnt around the edges. Classic Dad. I can offer to do a cake, other than your Easter ones, of course. Maybe a simple Victoria sponge? That would be lovely, actually. You always make a beautiful Victoria sponge. And it would take something off my plate. So, you’re definitely free on the 18th then? Everything alright with work? Yeah, I managed to swap a duty day with Mrs. Davies.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking I had last week was  criminal . Sixteen year olds, you know? They think a complex sentence is one with more than two clauses. It's exhausting trying to instill some nuance. Oh, tell me about it. Though mine are a bit younger, Year 8, grappling with the present perfect is like pulling teeth. Still, sixteen is… a phase. My niece, Chloe, she was exactly the same at that age. Now she’s doing English Lit at Warwick. Shocked me, honestly. She used to refuse to read anything that wasn't TikTok captions. Warwick! That’s brilliant. See, there’s hope. It’s just…it feels like the basics are disappearing, doesn’t it? Standards are slipping. It's a constant uphill battle. How are things at your school? Still facing the funding cuts I know you were worried about? Sadly, yes. They’ve ‘restructured’ – that’s what they call it – and we’ve lost two teaching assistants. It’s impacting the kids with SEN terribly. We're supposed to differentiate for everyone with fewer resources. It's just…madness. On a brighter note, Reginald is thriving. Reginald? Oh, the cat! How’s the fluffy tyrant? Last I heard, he was attempting to dismantle the Christmas tree. Dismantle is putting it mildly. He  conquered  the Christmas tree. Anyway, he's become obsessed with the laser pointer. It's hilarious watching him. He’ll chase it for hours. Though, my neighbour complained he was trying to scale the fence after it. Apparently, he thought it was leading him to Narnia. Oh, Reginald! He’s a character, alright. My Daisy is being a nightmare, actually. She’s decided the sofa cushions are hers, and claws anyone who disagrees. I tried that Feliway diffuser, supposedly calming, but she just glared at it with utter disdain. Feliway…hmmm. I’ve heard mixed reviews. Have you tried those Lickimats? Spread some pate on them – keeps them occupied for ages. It's a lifesaver when I’m trying to grade papers. Speaking of which…have you seen that new range of anti-ageing serums that Boots are doing? The one with the retinol? Oh, the No7 line? I’ve been eyeing it up! I’m definitely starting to notice…lines. It's all the stress, I think. Plus, I’m convinced smiling too much creates wrinkles. It’s a dilemma. Exactly!

… honestly, the charoset was  way  too heavy on the apples this year, wasn’t it? Reminded me of that crumble Nan makes, all soft and… well, crumble-y. It needs more walnuts, definitely. A bit more kick. Oi, don’t diss the crumble! My Nan’s crumble is legendary. But yeah, alright, maybe a touch too apple-forward. I was going for a softer texture, trying to please everyone. It’s hard when you've got a whole spectrum of charoset preferences, innit? It’s always the charoset. It’s the battleground of every Seder. My mother used to put dates in hers – dates and a ludicrous amount of wine. Said it represented the mortar the Israelites used. Though I suspect it mostly represented her wanting a sneaky extra glass. Mortar  and  a sneaky glass. Sounds about right for a good British mum. Speaking of sneaky… anyone fancy another bit of brisket? It’s genuinely amazing, ANON. You’ve outdone yourself. Don't mind if I do. Seriously good stuff. So, you lot actually  went  to Italy then? You were talking about it last Seder, remember? We did! Florence, Rome, a bit of Tuscany. It was…intense. Beautiful, obviously, but so busy. And the pasta… I mean, good, but nothing beats a proper bagel, does it? A bold statement, darling. A  bold  statement. Florence is wonderful, though. I went years ago, researching a piece on the Medici family. The Uffizi Gallery… breathtaking. Did you manage to see  David ? Yeah, saw David. Bit… imposing, if I’m honest. I’m more of a film kinda guy. Been proper obsessed with this Italian neo-realist stuff recently –  Bicycle Thieves , that sort of thing. Really gritty. Neo-realism? Sounds depressing. I need something a bit lighter. Was re-watching  Paddington  last week, actually. Always cheers me up. Paddington is a national treasure! Speaking of treasures… I tried recreating that chocolate babka recipe I found online, the one from that New York bakery. Total disaster. It just… didn't rise. It was like cement. Babka is notoriously tricky. You need the right kind of flour, the right temperature… it’s a whole science. Though, frankly, demi-glace is a much greater culinary challenge. You and your culinary challenges, ANON. I’m happy with a well-engineered bridge, thank you very much. Less likely to collapse mid-construction. So, any plans for the summer, apart from rescuing babkas?

…and honestly, the pacing was  awful . Three chapters dedicated to describing the wallpaper! Wallpaper, honestly! I nearly threw the Kindle across the room.      Oh, don’t tell me it was ‘The Crimson Thread’ again? You know I adore Beatrice Plumtree. Her descriptions  are  detailed, but that’s part of the charm. It builds the atmosphere.      I think it depends on what you’re after, doesn’t it? If you want a fast-paced thriller, Plumtree isn't your woman. I tried her once, found myself completely bogged down. I much prefer Gillian Flynn. Now  there’s  someone who knows how to keep you hooked.      Gillian Flynn is brilliant, agreed. But even I, a confessed drama queen, was struggling. I'm finding I’m generally leaning towards eBooks more and more, though. Just…easier. Less clutter. But then, sometimes, I miss the  feel  of a book. You know? The weight of it.      I’m old fashioned, I admit it. Give me a proper book any day. The smell, the turning of the pages… it's a whole experience. Though, I did get a Kindle for Christmas and I use it on holiday. Saves lugging five novels in my handbag. Although, talking of holidays, have you booked anything for the summer, Sarah?      We’re thinking Cornwall. The kids are at that age where a beach and a bit of walking are enough to keep them happy. Hopefully. Last year's attempt to drag them around the Roman ruins in Italy was… stressful.      Cornwall sounds lovely! I’ve been meaning to go for ages. My sister's just bought a little cottage near Padstow. I’m hoping to go down and visit soon. Speaking of stressful, I've been trying to teach my nephew to crochet. It’s…a challenge.      Oh dear. He’s a bit young for that, isn’t he? I’ve been working on a blanket for the new baby, actually. It’s a complicated stitch, though. Taking ages. I’ve been watching ‘The Great British Sewing Bee’ for inspiration. Honestly, those people are incredible.      I saw an episode! They were making fitted sheets, weren't they? Seemed impossible. I can just about manage a hem. I much prefer watching ‘Call the Midwife’ myself. It's just so comforting. And the costumes are glorious.      I binge-watched ‘Silo’ recently. That was gripping. Properly dystopian. Though, it did leave me feeling a bit bleak afterwards.

...Honestly, it's just baffling, innit? They used to  own  this game. Nokia. Remember those brick phones? Unbreakable. You could probably build a small house with one. And now… well, now they make slightly better-looking feature phones. It's a bit sad, really.      It is. Though, to be fair, the landscape changed massively. It wasn’t just about building a durable phone, was it? It was about apps, connectivity, the whole ecosystem. Something Nokia were… slow to grasp, let’s say. This one's lovely, though. The colour is perfect.      Aye, it is a nice bit of kit. Though, all this… …feels a bit extravagant buying new phones while we're  in  Finland. Like we're actively mocking the ghosts of Nokia past.      Don't be daft. We needed new ones! Mine was practically held together with prayer and sticky tape. And yours was… well, yours was refusing to recognise anything after 2014. Honestly, you were complaining about it every five minutes. Plus, this was a good deal. Duty-free and all that.      Alright, alright, you're right. Praticality won. Though, setting these things up... Honestly, it's like learning a new language. I still get flustered with transferring contacts. It's not like the old days. Remember just writing them in a little book?      Oh, you and your notebooks! I’ve already started backing mine up to the cloud. Much easier. Do you want me to walk you through it? Setting up the Google account, transferring your contacts… I can do it all.      Would you mind? Seriously. I feel like a dinosaur sometimes. I manage to lecture on Victorian poetry, but a smartphone throws me for a loop. It’s the whole security thing that worries me, too. All the permissions and data tracking. It’s a bit unsettling.      It  can  be, but you can control a lot of it. We can go through the privacy settings together. And I've got a good VPN we use. It helps. Right, first things first, let's get your Google account sorted. Do you remember your password? It’s probably the one you use for your university email, right?      I  think  so. Though I have about twelve different passwords swirling around in me 'ead. I swear, I need a password manager. You got one of them, do you?      I do. LastPass. It’s brilliant. It generates strong passwords and remembers them all for you.

…and honestly, Mum, I still think Red Pandas are cooler than Malamooches. Don't get me wrong, Winston’s a brilliant dog, a proper softie, but Red Pandas  climb  trees and eat bamboo and they look like little, fluffy foxes! Right, well Winston’s brilliant at licking faces and needing constant attention, which is a different kind of skill. And speaking of brilliant, Leo, stop trying to climb the bookshelves! You’ll bring the whole thing down. But I wanna see the dinosaurs! There aren't dinosaurs on the bookshelf, love. Just books. Now, back to the pandas. They  are  cute, I’ll give you that. But remember Mrs. Higgins’ cat, Clementine? She looked a bit like a miniature tiger. Clementine was ancient! And she hissed at everyone. A bit different to a fluffy, tree-dwelling acrobat. Anyway, we were meant to talk about Finn’s present. His birthday’s next week, isn't it? It is! Thursday. Seven years old. Time flies. We agreed on a board game, didn’t we? Something he can play with you? He’s been moaning about wanting a new one. Yeah, but I'm stuck on which one. He’s got, like, Monopoly Junior and that animal one… what’s it called? Snuggle Safari? The one with the little plush animals? That's the one. I was thinking maybe Ticket to Ride: First Journey? It’s a bit more strategic. That sounds good. He loves trains. And it's not  too  complicated. Right, present sorted. What about the party? Have you asked about gymnastics hall availability? I emailed them. Haven't heard back yet. It’s a nightmare, Mum. Everyone wants it on Saturday, and I need to know soon so I can send out the invites. I thought we could do a theme… maybe Japanese? I saw this amazing film the other day,  My Neighbour Totoro … Totoro! Oh, that's lovely. A bit different. I can try and look up some decorations. Though, if the hall falls through, we might have to have it here. Honestly, this house will be chaos with ten seven-year-olds running around. Leo's already enough chaos as it is. Chaos good! Building! We  could  have it in the garden, if the weather’s nice. Dad could help set up. He's surprisingly good at fairy lights. Your father? Good at fairy lights? That’s a new one.

…Honestly, tha' was just daft, weren’t it? Trying to get a Christmas tree delivered to a student halls room. Ended up havin’ to lug it five floors meself, lookin’ like a right eediat.      Five floors? Blimey. You Northerners and your real trees, eh? We just had a little plastic one growing up. Mum said no mess, no fuss. Plus, space in a flat in London is… premium.      Oh, plastic trees are perfectly acceptable these days, dear. Though, there’s something about the smell of a real one, isn’t there? Transports you right back. My father  always  had a real tree. A magnificent thing it was, filled the whole drawing room. And the ritual of decorating it…      Ritual is the word, Margaret. A proper production. My mother insisted on silver tinsel.  Only  silver. Said gold was…vulgar. Can you imagine?      Silver tinsel! Sounds posh, that. We just had whatever was cheapest at Woolworths. Used to sneak extra baubles on when me mam wasn’t lookin’. She’d always count ‘em afterward, makin’ sure none’d gone missin’. Proper strict, she was. Barrow-in-Furness Christmases were…practical.      My Lola - that's grandmother in Tagalog – she'd make these incredible Filipino Christmas ham,  lechon . It’s roasted pig. It would take days to prepare! The whole house smelled amazing. Completely different to turkey and sprouts. Though I have to admit, I’ve grown to like sprouts.      Oh, the food is so important. It’s how we connect to our memories, isn’t it? We always had plum pudding, of course, drenched in brandy butter. And my grandfather, he’d always tell the same story every year about almost setting the kitchen on fire trying to make it.      Brandy butter! Waste of good brandy, if you ask me. I liked a bit of a stronger tipple myself, in my younger days. Christmas Eve in the pub with the lads, that was a tradition. Though, I suspect times have changed.      Changed a lot, yeah. Now it’s more like, who can get the most ridiculous Christmas jumper. An’ everyone’s got to ha’ a photo for Instagram. It's all a bit… much, innit?      It’s the pressure, I think. Social media makes everything feel like it needs to be perfect. We didn’t have that growing up. Just family, food, and a questionable selection of Christmas cracker jokes. Speaking of different, have you guys ever been to the Philippines for Christmas?

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of transcription work coming through this week is ridiculous. It’s all true crime podcasts now, isn't it? Everyone's obsessed. Though, I did have one lovely little academic piece on Victorian gardening the other day. A nice change. Victorian gardening, that  does  sound peaceful. Better than listening to people detail, well, you know…the darker side of humanity all day. How are you managing? Still chained to the headphones? Pretty much. Though I’ve started taking more breaks. Dr. Lewis helped. He said I was getting a really tense neck. Speaking of Dr. Lewis, have you seen the new series? The one with the Oxford professor? Oh, darling,  yes . Utterly gripping! Though I do wish they wouldn't make him quite so…brooding. It’s a bit cliché, isn’t it? The tortured genius detective. Still, the plots are excellent. Much better than that awful thing we watched last week, the one with the Icelandic detective. Remember? Oh,  god  yes. That was…slow. Painfully slow. And the scenery, while beautiful, didn't really compensate for the lack of actual detective work. Exactly! It felt like they were deliberately trying to be arty rather than telling a compelling story. I'm a sucker for a good twist, though. Lewis delivered on that front. Did you see how… …it was the gardener all along? Yes! Genius! Though I suspected the housekeeper. She had that  look . You know the one. All tight-lipped and judgmental. You two and your detective series! I’m more worried about feeding everyone. I was thinking shepherd’s pie on Saturday? It’s easy, and everyone seems to like it. Unless you've both gone off shepherd’s pie? Shepherd's pie sounds  wonderful , actually. Perfect comfort food for a chilly evening. I can bring the peas. Lovely. And I'll contribute a decent bottle of red. Though I'm starting to worry about Margaret. She hasn't been returning my calls. Oh dear. That’s not like her. Is everything alright? Did she mention anything when we last saw her? No, nothing specific. Just a bit…distant. And she’s usually glued to her Kindle. Says she's lost interest in reading. That's really worrying. She lives for her books. That  is  strange. Maybe she’s just got a bit down. You know how she gets with the weather. Has she been out much?

…and honestly, Doreen, I’m telling you, young Timothy next door, he’s got no respect. Absolutely none. Leaving his scooter right across the path again. Nearly tripped over the blooming thing this mornin’, I did. Oh, Arthur, you and that scooter! It’s a child, Arthur. A little boy. He’s not  trying  to trip you. Though I do agree, it's a bit thoughtless of his mother to let him. Actually, I was speaking to Mrs. Henderson yesterday. Timothy's mum’s been a bit under the weather, apparently. Bad back. She's relying on him to entertain himself in the garden while she rests. A bad back, you say? Well, that changes things a bit, don’t it? Still, shouldn’t leave hazards lying about. Used to be, children knew their place. Didn't run wild like they do now. Back in my day… Here we go. Arthur, ‘back in your day’ horses and carts were the hazards, not scooters. And you were probably running wild yourself, upsetting Old Man Hemmings with your cricket ball! Now, now, Doreen. A bit of harmless fun, that was. Hemmings just didn’t appreciate a good game. No, the point is, things were different. People had more… consideration. Perhaps it's less about consideration and more about a shift in societal norms. Things  are  different, Arthur. We’ve moved on. It’s the same with this business of young people and their phones, isn't it? It drives you mad to see them glued to the screens. Drives me bonkers! Utterly bonkers. Never see ‘em looking at the sky, do you? Or talking to proper folk. All thumbs and faces. And this newfangled social media… utterly bewildering. I tried to look up ‘knitting patterns’ on that Facebook thing, Doreen, and got bombarded with pictures of cats.  Cats!  Oh, Arthur, you are hopeless! Facebook isn't the place for knitting patterns. You need Ravelry, dear. It's a website specifically for knitters. I showed Susan – remember Susan from the Women's Institute? – and she was thrilled. Actually, social media can be quite useful for keeping in touch with family. My daughter, Emily, lives in Australia now. Without it, I'd barely see pictures of the grandchildren. Australia! Goodness me. A long way to go for a bit of sunshine. Still, a phone call is a phone call, isn’t it? Don’t need all these fancy pictures.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of biscuits required for a proper Cambridge do is  astronomical . Like, we’re not talking a packet of digestives, are we? We need variety. Hobnobs, Rich Tea, Jammie Dodgers…the works. Aye, you're right there, love. People go  mad  for a good biscuit selection. Don't skimp on the chocolate ones either. Though, honestly, after last year’s Christmas party, I needed a lie-down. Too much sherry, too much festive cheer…and too many mini sausages. I’m happy to do a run to Waitrose? I've got a car, and I can get a decent discount with my staff card. We should probably make a list though, just to keep it organised. No point in ending up with ten packets of shortbread. Aye, a list is a good shout. And someone needs to sort the music. Not more bloody Christmas songs, please. I’m still having flashbacks. I was stuck next to Brenda from accounts for a solid hour while she belted out ‘All I Want For Christmas Is You’. Traumatic. Right, music’s my domain.
