I'll curate a playlist that’s festive but not…suffocatingly so. A bit of upbeat indie, maybe some classic soul. Something everyone can enjoy. But back to the biscuits, that sounds…intense. Are we really expecting this many people? Well, we’ve invited everyone from the ELT department, plus a few key people from Marketing. It’s Horace’s last day, isn't it? We have to make it a good send-off. And he  loves  biscuits. It’s a known fact. Speaking of Horace, did anyone see what happened earlier? I swear, that poor wee fly was buzzing round his head for ages, and then landed right in his tea! Oh my god, I saw! He didn't even notice. Just calmly carrying on reading his report. Honestly, I’d have been flapping about like a startled pigeon. I can't stand insects. But Horace…he’s a saint. I actually scooped the fly out with a sugar spoon and put it outside the window. Felt a bit daft, but couldn’t just let it drown. That was incredibly kind of you! See, that's the academic spirit shining through. Saving the tiny creatures. Although, I’m pretty sure a hot cup of Earl Grey isn't a fly’s ideal habitat. You’re probably right.

…and honestly, Mr. Davies just  stared  at me. Like, a proper, unblinking stare. It was SO awkward. I was trying to explain about the history essay, how I’d totally misinterpreted the question about the Suffragettes, and he just… stared. No way! Davies does that, doesn’t he? It's his go-to. It’s supposed to be intimidating, I think, but it mostly just makes him look like a surprised owl. Did he at least let you resubmit it? Eventually. After a solid minute of silence. He said, and I quote, “Miss Albright, your understanding appears… tangential.” Tangential! What even  is  tangential? It sounds like a medical condition. Oh, he’s so dramatic. It just means you went off on a bit of a tangent, like, you went off-topic. Don't worry about it. Everyone messes up history essays. Remember when I wrote about Queen Victoria being a punk rocker? Oh my god,  please  don’t remind me! Mrs. Henderson nearly choked on her tea. But that was funny. This just felt… humiliating. And it’s not even the worst thing! French is killing me. Madame Dubois is convinced I’m deliberately trying to be obtuse. Dubois is the worst. She treats us like five-year-olds. “Ah, Chloe, you ‘ave not remembered ze gender of ze table!” Honestly! Does it even  have  a gender? Exactly! And the verbs! They just…shift around! I keep getting the past participles wrong. It’s like she enjoys watching me struggle. I think she subtly  smiles  when I mess up. She definitely does. I’ve seen it. She’s a master of the passive-aggressive smile. Are you doing the listening comprehension tomorrow? The one about the family going to the boulangerie? Ugh, yes. I’m terrified. My French listening skills are abysmal. I can read it okay, but when they  speak  it…it's just a blur of sounds. Do you think it’ll be anything like the practice one? Probably not. She always throws in a curveball. Last time it was an interview with a professional mime artist. A MIME artist, Chloe! Who needs to know about a mime artist’s grocery shopping habits? You’re right. It's just academic torture. At least English is alright. Though Mr. Peterson is obsessed with analyzing metaphors. Everything is a metaphor for something else apparently. Oh, Peterson. He's obsessed  beyond  reason.

… honestly, the deadline for the grant applications is just  insane . They expect a fully fleshed-out proposal, budget breakdown, impact assessment… all for a relatively small amount of funding. It’s basically a full-time job on top of my actual full-time job. Sounds rough, El. You’re always taking on too much. Remember what happened last Christmas? You nearly had a meltdown trying to organise everything. Aye, that was a sight. Though, to be fair, your Auntie Brenda  is  a handful. Still, El, you need to learn to delegate. Nobody expects you to be Superwoman. I  know  Mum, I know. It’s just… I feel responsible. It's the community outreach programme, you know? If we don't get the funding, we'll have to cut back on the workshops for the kids. That’s fair. But you can’t burn yourself out. Is there anyone else at work who could help shoulder some of the load? Sarah offered, but she’s swamped with the new marketing campaign. Honestly, everyone's stretched thin. It feels like the council keeps promising resources and then… nothing. It’s just paperwork and hoping for the best. Which, by the way, is a shockingly accurate description of my degree, now that I think about it. All that research, for… this. It’s good work, lass. Don’t undervalise yourself. It's important, what you do. I was talking to Doreen down at the shop today, and she was saying her grandson really benefited from the after-school club you helped organise last year. He’s a completely different lad now, more confident, reading properly. Oh, really? That’s lovely to hear. It’s moments like that that make it worthwhile, I suppose. Although, a pay rise would also be pretty worthwhile… Always gets back to the money, doesn't it? Speaking of which, this lasagne is amazing. Mum, you've outdone yourself. It's my nan's recipe. Secret ingredient is a splash of Worcestershire sauce. Don't tell anyone. She'd have my hide. How was your day, Liam? Still wrestling with Mr. Henderson’s insistence on avocado green office chairs? You have  no  idea. He’s convinced it’s ‘on brand’. I’ve tried explaining to him that we’re a plumbing supplies company, not a Californian health food café, but he won't listen. He keeps sending me links to ‘mood boards’.

… honestly, the whole thing with Leo’s detention has just been a complete headache. Three hours! For forgetting his PE kit  again . It’s not like he’s five, you know? He's fourteen. He knows the rules. Three hours, blimey. Sounds harsh, doesn’t it? Our Darren was always forgetting somethin’. Usually his homework, but never PE kit. Though he did once turn up to school wearin’ two different shoes. Oh, bless him. Leo’s just… distracted. He’s been spending all his time at Chloe’s. Apparently, she’s finally let him help her with her coding project. Something about a game. Honestly, all this screen time… It’s the way things are now, innit? When I was at school, we were outside buildin’ dens and gettin’ muddy. Now it’s all virtual worlds. Though, good for him takin’ an interest in somethin’ like coding. Might lead to somethin’. I suppose. It’s just… I worry. He's been so withdrawn since his Dad’s diagnosis. So, any focus, even if it  is  on a computer screen, feels… positive. How’s everything goin’ with… you know? Is he still holdin’ up alright? They said the operation went well, didn’t it? The operation was, technically, a success. They got everything they needed to, but the recovery is… slow. He gets incredibly tired. And the waiting for the biopsy results is awful. It feels like everything is on hold. I’m trying to keep things normal for Leo, that’s why I’m so hung up on the detention. One less thing to worry about. It’s hard, isn’t it? Seein’ someone you love go through all that. My mum had breast cancer, years ago now, thankfully she’s clear. But the worry… it eats you up. You just try and cope day by day. You’re doin’ the right thing, keepin’ things steady for your son. Thank you, that means a lot. It just feels like everything's a struggle at the moment. Work is mental, too. That new account with StellarTech? Demanding. I had a nightmare trying to get a decent rate from the building society for a loan to cover some of the medical expenses. Honestly, they were useless. Kept rattling on about credit scores and affordability assessments. They didn't even seem to  understand  the situation. Oh, the banks are all the same. Never any help when you actually need it.

… honestly, I just don’t get how some folks can be so  chill  about awful tips. Like, last night this bloke, proper flash car outside, ordered a double Bombay Sapphire and tonic, then left a pound change. A  pound ! After nearly ten quid for the drink! Oh, you’re kidding! That’s… infuriating, isn’t it? I mean, I get working for minimum wage is rough, but deliberately being a cheapskate? Just rude. Aye, rude doesn’t even cover it. It’s a slap in the face, innit? Especially when I’m grafting, studying for this bloody Masters at the same time. It’s not like I’m just standin’ there polishing glasses all night, you know? Essays to write, readings to do… all fuelled by lukewarm coffee and the hope of decent tips. Tell me about it with the balancing act! Uni's stressful enough without, like, needing to actively worry about money all the time. Though, at least  my  job - temporary Christmas staff at Boots - doesn’t involve dealing with… that level of cheek. Mostly just wrapping presents and trying to navigate the perfume counter. Sounds… marginally less soul-destroying. Though I bet you get earache from Christmas tunes on repeat. It's awful, isn't it? They start playing 'em in November now. Ugh, don’t even  mention  Mariah Carey. Seriously, I think I’m developing a twitch. But it’s… easy, you know? Standing, wrapping, ‘Happy Christmas!’ – it’s brain-off work. And it’s just ‘til January, then back to properly stressing about A-Levels. What are you doing your Masters in, by the way? You’ve never really said. Marine Biology. Bit of a jump from a Psychology undergrad, I know, but I always loved being near the sea when I were a kid. Growing up in Hull, you’re always aware of it, even if the water’s a bit… grim sometimes. It’s just… I needed a change. Psychology was becoming too much about people's problems, and I felt like I needed to go and study  something  beautiful. That’s… really cool actually! Hull’s a bit far from proper oceans, though, isn’t it? Well, you’ve got the North Sea, and there's loads of research going on with estuaries and coastal environments. Plus, loads of fieldwork opportunities. It's demanding, though. The course is intense, and the bar work pays the bills, but it's draining.

… honestly, I just need to  get  away. Even a weekend in Blackpool feels too close to civilisation after the semester we’ve just had. Did anyone actually manage a decent break this year? Blackpool? Oh, lad, you're ambitious! I went to Scarborough. Not exactly the Maldives, mind, but it was breezy and the fish and chips were alright. Though, honestly, half the time was spent trying to keep my niece from launching herself off the pier. She’s a whirlwind, that one. Scarborough’s lovely. Though a bit…exposed. I went back home to County Clare. Proper quiet, you know? Just the sound of the Atlantic crashing and the occasional sheep bleating. Bliss. And my sister makes the best soda bread in the world, so there was  that  to look forward to. Sounds idyllic, Mary. I did the usual – a week in Italy. Tuscany. Trying to convince myself I was living  Under the Tuscan Sun . Turns out, owning a dilapidated farmhouse and learning Italian is significantly harder than it looks in the film. Still, the wine was excellent. Tuscany! That’s a bit posh for us lot, isn’t it? I was eyeing up the Lake District, maybe. Bit of walking, bit of reading… escape the endless student essays for a few days. I’ve got a pile of books practically reaching the ceiling. Urgent reading, all of it. Walking? In the Lake District? In  this  weather? You’re braver than me, Mark. I require sunshine and a guaranteed ice cream cone within a five-mile radius. I tried to get my husband to go hiking once. Once. He nearly divorced me. Oh, the men folk! My brother, God rest his soul, once tried to convince me a ‘camping holiday’ was romantic. Romantic? Sleeping on the ground with midges biting your nose? I think not! He learned quickly. Midges are a real problem. Italy was mercifully midge-free, though the mosquitoes took a particular liking to my ankles. I’m starting to think I’m just naturally attractive to biting insects. Anyone got any good repellant recommendations? I swear by citronella. Though, you end up smelling like a giant lemon. Still, better than being eaten alive. Actually, that reminds me of a joke. Why don’t skeletons ever go on holiday? Oh, here we go… Oh, let him tell it, love. He’s been saving that one all morning. Because they have no  body  to go with!

Honestly, this is painful to watch. Absolutely painful. They’re just… passing it sideways! What’s the point? Come on, now, it’s only the first half. They’re easing into it. Building the play. You're sounding like my Gran, always wanting a through ball first minute. Easing into it?! It’s Newcastle, Liam! They should be  flying  at them. It’s the derby! You’d think they’d have a bit more… urgency. It’s not like Sunderland anymore, is it? At least  they  had passion, even when they were getting battered. Oh, here we go. The Sunderland lament. Look, I know you’re still bitter about the League One years. But Newcastle have come a long way. And honestly, they’ve got a pretty solid midfield. They’re just being… strategic. Strategic is a fancy word for scared, I reckon. They're scared of losing possession. Honestly, I'd rather see them try something and fail than just… this. It's like watching paint dry. Fancy a cheeky Nando’s later? This is giving me stress-eating vibes. Nando’s? Now  that’s  a strategic move. Always happy to be fuelled by peri-peri. Though, maybe we should wait and see if this gets any more exciting? I’m feeling a mild chicken piri-piri myself, but extra hot is always the move if they pull it together. "Pull it together." The optimism is admirable. Honestly, I’m already planning what I want. A double chicken wrap with halloumi fries. Don’t judge. And garlic mayo, naturally. It’s a necessity, not a choice. No judgement here. You and your garlic mayo. It’s a… commitment. I usually go for the butterfly chicken with coleslaw, slightly less messy. Remember that time you got it all down your white shirt at that conference in London? Don’t remind me! I looked like I’d been attacked by a chicken. It was mortifying. And it was  important ! I was presenting my research on… well, never mind. It’s not as important as halloumi fries. Speaking of, do you think they’ve improved their peri-tamer sauce? I swear it used to be genuinely inedible. I haven’t tried it in ages. Probably still weapon-grade. But they’ve been doing those limited edition sauces, haven't they? I saw something about a mango and lime one… might be worth a gamble.

…and honestly, the whole thing was a disaster. The client wanted a complete overhaul of the system  mid-project . Like, after we'd already signed off on the initial spec! Can you believe it? Total chaos. Chaos, you say? Oh, I've seen chaos. War time, that was chaos. Though, I suppose changes mid-stream are frustrating, aren't they dear? It’s like trying to re-knit a jumper when you’re halfway through. Sounds about right, love. Clients…they always want something different. I've got one at the moment wants a discount  after  he’s already agreed the price. Says his wife saw a similar thing cheaper online. Honestly! Exactly! It's the principle of it. We spent weeks scoping this out, getting it just right. Now I'm pulling all-nighters trying to rewrite code. It’s exhausting. Though, nothing like wartime, I imagine, Gran. Oh, exhausting it was. But a different sort. Rationing, air raids…you wouldn’t believe the things we did. We used to grow vegetables in the bomb craters, you know! Made the best soups. Not like this shop-bought muck. Mam, you’ve told us about the bomb craters. Several times. Honestly, you'd think you enjoyed it. Enjoyed it? No! But you had to get on with it. No moaning. Now, what was that film you were talking about, Michael? Last week, was it? Something with spaceships? Oh,  Dune . Yeah, it was pretty good. Visually stunning, but a bit…dense. A lot to take in. Bit slow for Mum, I reckon. Slow? I like a good sci-fi! Though I haven’t seen that one yet. I was watching that new detective show with Robson Green. Good stuff. Reminds me a bit of  Inspector Morse , and I always loved  Inspector Morse . Robson Green’s good. I used to watch  Soldier Soldier  when I was a lad. Remember that, Mum? Oh,  Soldier Soldier ! That was a bit of alright, that was. All those young lads running around. Though your Grandpa would have had a fit! He was a stickler for respectability. Speaking of running, have you been out on your bike lately, Michael? You promised you’d show me that new route down by the canal. I know, I know. It's been hectic with work. I'm hoping to get a day free next weekend. It’s a lovely ride, Gran, really flat, perfect for a gentle cycle.

…and honestly, Leo, leaving half your pancake is just… wasteful. We talked about this. People are genuinely struggling, you know? There are kids who wouldn’t  have  a pancake, let alone leave half of one. It was too hot. Mine was yummy! I ate all mine, Mummy. Except the teeny bit of lemon. Lemon’s sour. That’s brilliant, Daisy! See, Leo? Daisy understood. It’s good to finish what’s on your plate. It’s really important. Did you tell Mrs. Davies about the assembly tomorrow? Yeah. I told her I’m the one doing the… the rhyming couplet about planets. Good lad. And remember to project your voice, alright? You were a little quiet in practice. You’ve got a lovely one. Something about Saturn's rings, wasn’t it? I helped him practice! I said it  really  loud! “Saturn’s rings are shiny and bright, circling the planet with all their might!” Oh, you did! Well done, Darling. You’re a fantastic coach. Right, pancakes demolished – mostly. Now, we’re still on for the Science Museum on Saturday, aren't we? I booked the tickets online. Can we go to the space bit  first ? Please? We can  try  to go to the space bit first. No promises, it gets very busy. Speaking of busy, I had a right day at school today. Little Thomas didn't brush his teeth properly this morning. His breath smelled... distinctive. I had to have a little chat. I always brush my teeth! Mummy helps. You do, Sweetheart, you always do. It’s just some children… well, things aren't always easy at home, are they? You see it, even just in little things like that. It reminds me of my Gran. She grew up during the war, you know. Everything was rationed. She used to tell me stories about how they’d save every little scrap. It makes you think, doesn't it? What’s rationed? It means you only get a little bit of something. Like… if you only had one biscuit a week. Imagine! One biscuit? That’s awful! I like biscuits! I know, darling. Thankfully, we don’t have to worry about that. Right, Saturday, then Science Museum. Sunday… what shall we do? I saw there’s something on at the Festival Hall, a children’s concert? It’s a bit pricey, though. Can we go to the beach?

… honestly, the spring roll was a bit soggy, wasn’t it? Not like Mei’s used to make. Remember Mei’s? Proper crispy, you could practically stand a chopstick up in it. Yeah, it's not the same since her daughter took over. She doesn’t have the same… finesse, shall we say? Still, decent enough for a Tuesday. Better than cooking, eh? Especially after the day I’ve had. Definitely better than cooking. And after  your  day, Liam, you deserve a treat. How did that meeting with old Mr. Henderson go? Still trying to get him to understand the value of a properly worded bid? Don’t even  start  me on Henderson. He thinks ‘synergy’ is a spice. Honestly, I spent half an hour explaining the difference between ‘value proposition’ and ‘just a good price.’ It’s exhausting. Sounds… stimulating. Though, honestly, I spent my day wrestling with nitrogen levels and a farmer who insists his barley is 'just fine.' It’s always ‘just fine’ until it yields about a fifth of what it should. Oh god, farmers. My Gran used to live near a farm, the smells… unforgettable. Speaking of unforgettable, did you guys hear about old Mrs. Higgins? Down the road? No! What happened? I used to see her tending her roses all the time. Sadly, she passed away last week. The funeral’s on Friday. Apparently, it’s going to be a big one. She knew  everyone  in Peterborough. Oh, that's awful. She always had a wave for me when I was walking the dog. A proper lovely woman. I’ll have to send flowers, won’t I? Definitely. It’s the least we can do. Funerals are… odd, though, aren't they? A weird mix of sadness and remembering funny stories. I was thinking about Uncle George’s, remember when little Timmy mistook the vicar for Bob the Builder? Oh my god, yes! Timmy shouting “Can we fix it?!” during the eulogy! Poor Reverend Davies looked utterly bewildered. That was epic. Although, Gran wasn't impressed. She said it was disrespectful. She was very... traditional. Which reminds me, she'd  hate  this Chinese. Said it wasn’t “proper food”. Your Gran was a woman of strong opinions. She’d probably complain about the cricket being on in the background too. Actually, speaking of cricket, England are doing pretty well, aren't they? Ben Stokes is on fire.

…and honestly, Auntie Maureen’s stories about Mr. Henderson next door are getting  wilder . Last week it was him trying to train squirrels to deliver his post. Squirrels! Henderson… now there was a character. Not like people nowadays. Always tinkering, that one. Though squirrels… that  is  a bit much, even for him. Reminds me of Old Man Peabody down the road in Wolverhampton. Tried to build a flying machine out of bicycle parts and bedsheets. Nearly took out Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses. Oh, the lengths people go to! It’s quite endearing, in a slightly terrifying way. Speaking of terrifying, have you seen the news about that driverless car trial in Bristol? Apparently, it got confused by a roundabout. Don’t even get me started. Honestly, I’m very happy driving myself, thank you very much. Though, I did have a rather harrowing flight back from Barcelona last month. Turbulence was dreadful. I was convinced we were going down. Barcelona, eh? Lovely place. Though I’ve never been one for flying. Gives me the jitters. Used to be you could rely on a train, didn’t you? Proper comfort. And you could  see  the country. Nowadays, it's all “get you there as fast as possible,” never mind enjoying the journey. Remember when we used to go to Bournemouth by train, Emily? Vaguely, Dad. I was quite small. I remember Mum packing mountains of Rice Krispy cakes. You always had a sweet tooth, didn't you? A small indulgence! And rather good with a cup of tea. Though I tell you, those supermarket prices are getting ridiculous. Went to get some Rice Krispy cakes myself last week – daylight robbery! Absolutely! And the self-scan checkouts? I swear they actively  look  for things to flag up. I bought a banana yesterday and it insisted it was a courgette. A courgette! They're designed to catch people, aren't they? Although, I find them useful when it’s busy. Remember when supermarkets didn’t even  have  checkouts? Just a little counter and Mrs. Patterson with her adding machine. Ah, Mrs. Patterson! A proper community spirit, then. Everyone knew everyone. It’s all so impersonal now. Building all these new estates, too. They're all the same. Identical houses. And the insurance on those… astronomical! I was talking to young Mr. Davies – he’s just bought one over near Callington - and he said the premiums are through the roof.

…and honestly, the glitter just  everywhere . Honestly, Leo, you looked like a disco ball exploded near you. Did you at least manage to get most of it off before bedtime? I did! Mostly. A little bit stayed in my hair though. It was  dragon  glitter, though! Dragons need glitter! Mine too! My dragon was pink! And it had wings! Did yours have wings, Leo? Yes! Big ones! And scales. Lots and lots of green scales. Were yours shiny, Maisie? Super shiny! Mummy helped me with the sparkly bits. It's for Chinese New Year, isn't it? Is the dragon important? It absolutely is, sweetheart. Dragons are really important in Chinese culture. They symbolise power, strength, and good luck for the New Year. That’s why we were drawing them – to bring good luck for the year of the Dragon. Although, judging by the glitter explosion, we’ve probably brought enough  sparkle  luck too. Can we watch the fireworks on TV later? Like at New Year? Perhaps. It depends what time. But we'll definitely have our Chinese food tonight. Do you remember what we’re having? Noodles! And spring rolls! And... dumplings! I like the dumplings best. I like the noodles. Can I have chicken noodles? Of course, you can. Mummy’s ordering it all. Speaking of ordering things, how was school today? Anything interesting happen, you two? We learnt about planets! Saturn has rings! Really big rings! Mrs. Peterson showed us a picture. I built a spaceship! Out of Lego! It can go to Mars! And Jupiter! Wow, a spaceship! That sounds amazing, Leo. You’re going to be an astronaut, aren’t you? You know, thinking about planets, it's funny. I was reading about ancient Chinese astronomy, and they had really sophisticated understandings of the sky, even without telescopes. Was it like looking at stars? I liked looking at the stars when we were camping. Exactly like that. Although, they named the constellations and planets differently. It's all quite fascinating. Right, anyone practicing their instruments this week? Maisie, how’s the piano coming along? I learned a new song! It's… …it’s really hard! I keep forgetting which fingers go where. Practice makes perfect, love. And Leo, are you still enjoying your drum lessons? Yes! I can do a proper roll now! Mr. Henderson said I was getting really good at the beat. He said I could join the band… eventually.

… honestly, the AirBnB photos were  way  better than the actual place. Like, they’d clearly used a wide-angle lens and… strategic lighting, yeah? It smelled faintly of mothballs, which is…a vibe I wasn't going for in Rome, y'know? Oh, bless you! That's rough, Leo. Rome and mothballs don’t really go hand-in-hand, do they? Mine’s decent enough, thankfully. Just a bit…small. But it’s got a balcony, so I'm not complaining. I’m just hoping it doesn’t rain again. This humidity is killing my hair. You two are stressing! It's Rome! Rain or shine, it's amazing. Honestly, I'm just glad we all made it. Remember when Aunt Carol tried to convince us she couldn't come because of her ‘bad back’? Straight up lied, she just didn’t want to leave Winston, the cat. That Carol, eh? Always a character. She’s convinced Winston understands Italian already. Told me he was practicing his ‘Buongiorno!’ this morning. Classic Carol. She treats that cat like royalty. So, are we still on for dinner tonight? I was thinking that Trastevere place, the one Mia recommended? Apparently, the cacio e pepe is to  die  for. Sounds perfect. Trastevere is lovely, especially at night. I’ve been trying to pick up a bit of Italian, but it’s slow going. I can order a coffee and ask where the bathroom is, which is… progress, I guess. You’re doing better than most tourists, honestly. Half of them just yell English louder, thinking it’ll magically make the Italians understand. I've lost count of the times I’ve had to translate for people at the cafe. It's exhausting. Yeah, the accents are a bit all over the place too. I was chatting to a bloke earlier and I swear he was trying to do an Italian accent  while  speaking English. It was… confusing. I just stuck to pointing at things. Works a treat. You’ve got a point. I overheard an American trying to order a pizza with a full-blown opera voice earlier. It was... impressive, but probably didn’t help his cause. Still, I’m loving this city. It's so different from London. Everything feels…older, you know? More lived-in. Definitely. And the light! It's incredible. Makes everything look gorgeous, even slightly dodgy AirBnBs. I’m trying to take loads of photos for the bakery, inspiration for some new designs.

…and honestly, Chloe's hen do ideas are  wild . Like, a silent disco in a vineyard? It sounds… stressful. Not fun stressful, just  organisational  stressful.      Oh, Chloe. Predictable, isn't she? Always gotta be extra. Though, a vineyard… that actually sounds quite nice, if you can wrangle the logistics.      It  is  a lot, though. Remember Sarah's? The escape room followed by karaoke? We were all absolutely shattered by 9pm.      That was a good one! A bit much, maybe, but we all bonded over how terrible we were at escape rooms. And honestly, Sarah lived for the karaoke. But yeah, a vineyard…holds a different level of…expectation.      Exactly! And she wants  everyone  to make their own flower crowns. Which, okay, I’m fairly crafty, having grown up half in Germany where  Basteln  is basically a national sport, but seriously? Not everyone can just whip up a floral masterpiece! I’m picturing a lot of glue gun burns and wilting petals.      Oh god, the glue guns. I’ve got scars from those things. Remember when we tried to make those Christmas decorations last year? Disaster.      A complete disaster! My glitter ended up  everywhere . Literally found some in my hair a week later.      Right, so, the flower crowns are a potential minefield. Maybe we could suggest a workshop? Like, book someone to come to the vineyard and actually  teach  people? That way Chloe gets her theme, and everyone doesn’t end up looking like they’ve been attacked by a bouquet.      That’s…actually brilliant, Ali! I hadn’t thought of that. I'll subtly suggest it to her. She's very…strongly opinionated. Speaking of crafts and things, I was thinking about making a cake for the hen do. Nothing elaborate, just something…nice.      Ooh, yes! You make amazing cakes, Imogen. Remember that lemon drizzle you brought to my birthday? It vanished in approximately five minutes.      It was nothing special. Though I did experiment with a new lavender icing this week. I'm thinking a vanilla sponge with lavender icing, decorated with…well, maybe tiny edible flowers? Not everyone will  have  to make their own!      Edible flowers! That's so you, Imogen. So elegant.      Sounds perfect! It’s a nice touch, and it fits the floral theme without relying on everyone being an expert florist. Are you up for doing cupcakes as well? Just in case?      I could do cupcakes, yeah.

… honestly, the buffet breakfast at that Travelodge was a  disgrace . Like, lukewarm scrambled egg and sausages that looked like they’d seen better decades. You wouldn’t feed that to a dog, would ya? Dramatic much? It’s a Travelodge, Liam. What did you expect, a full English cooked by Gordon Ramsay? You know you were only staying there ‘cause it was five minutes from the exhibition. I expect  edible , Ben. That’s all. I felt proper rough all day after it. Proper dodgy stomach. I reckon that’s why I was feeling so peaky when I got back. Honestly, I thought I was coming down with something properly nasty. Peaky? You haven’t said “peaky” since we were kids! And you weren’t looking great, I’ll grant you that. You were all pasty. Did you take any of the Lemsip I left you? Yeah, eventually. Tried powering through, like. Thought it was just the travel, you know? Two hours on the train, then all that walking around the gallery… plus the dodgy sausage. It was a triple whammy. You shoulda seen the state of the hotel room too, though. Dust bunnies the size of… well, small rabbits. Alright, alright, calm down. Sounds like your artistic sensibilities were offended by the lack of cleanliness. Seriously though, are you still feeling off? You’re looking a bit pale even now. This chilli should perk you up, though. Vit C and everything. Cheers, mate. I think I'm alright now. Just a bit… fragile. It’s daft, innit? I’ve travelled all over, seen some proper rough places, but a sausage in Bedford nearly takes me down. Bedford is a breeding ground for gastronomic disappointment, that's a known fact. Speaking of travelling, you actually thinking about going to Barcelona next month? You were saying something about that art residency? Yeah, well, the application's gone in. Long shot, mind. It's six months, though. Six months! I’d have to sublet my flat. It's a big decision. That’s amazing, Liam! You  have  to try and make it work. Imagine, six months in Barcelona! You could actually finish a decent portfolio, not just churning out stuff for that print shop. Easy for you to say. You're happy teaching grammar to Japanese students. I need to  make  stuff, not explain the difference between ‘there’, ‘their’ and ‘they’re’. No offense.

… honestly, I just think it’s a bit daft, putting ages on birthday cards now. Especially when, well, you know… we’re both getting to  that  age. It feels… pointed. Like a little reminder! Oh, you’re such a drama queen, Doreen. It’s just polite. People want to acknowledge it. Though, I do agree with you about the specificity. “Happy 67th!” Who needs to know? “Happy Birthday” is perfectly sufficient. Brenda sent one last week, 68! As if I needed reminding I’m heading towards seventy. Exactly! And it's not like we're pretending to be younger. It just feels… unnecessary. Anyway, less existential angst, more practical matters. We need to make a list for the shops tomorrow. Milk, obviously. Bread. And I was thinking… those little calendar fobs? The ones you get for keyrings? Oh, the ones with the year on? Good idea. Useful. I always lose track of what year it is, you know. Feels like 2018 was only yesterday. What else? Need any biscuits? Yes, definitely biscuits. Digestives, I think. And do you remember Mrs. Henderson, from primary school? God, she was strict. But brilliant at art. We made the most wonderful collages. Always used that lovely, bumpy wallpaper stuff. Oh, Mrs. Henderson! She smelled permanently of lavender and chalk dust. She  was  good at art. And remember how she’d make us all sing those awful, patriotic songs? "Land of Hope and Glory" at the top of our lungs. It was dreadful, but she was so enthusiastic. They don’t do that anymore, do they? All health and safety these days. No, no patriotic fervour. It’s all about ‘emotional wellbeing’ now, isn’t it? God, they've changed schools. Talking of changes, remember when hockey was  huge  at school? You were brilliant at it. I was terrible, always tripping over my own feet… and the hockey boots! Dreadful things. Hard as rock. I did enjoy hockey. Though, even then, I was secretly dreaming of being a historian. Funny, isn't it? I ended up teaching history. You always fancied something more… technological. Well, I was fascinated by sound recording. That’s what I wanted to study at university. Actually recording sounds, manipulating them… it felt so  new  then. Compared to what kids can do now with their phones! I remember the equipment we had – enormous reel-to-reel machines. It’s all digital now, of course.

…Honestly, Doreen, the sheer  speed  they drive down that lane! I nearly had a shunt backing out yesterday. You’d think living in the countryside would mean a bit more… consideration. Back in Southend, even with the traffic, people understood a bit of give and take.      It’s Devon, Brian. They seem to operate on a different timescale, and definitely a different road etiquette! I had a similar experience on the A30. Someone overtook me on a blind bend. Nearly gave me a heart attack.      Oh, you get used to it, love. It's the farm vehicles too, isn’t it? Huge tractors, muck spreaders…they own the roads, basically. Especially during lambing season. Though, to be fair, Old Man Hemmings warned us about that lane. He said it's a favourite shortcut for the lads from the next village.      Hemmings, is it? Seems a decent sort. Offered to help me with the guttering when he saw me struggling. Honestly, my DIY skills are…lacking. Always were. Should've taken more notice of my father, but he was always on about me getting a proper education. Said fiddling with pipes was beneath me.      Beneath a future management guru, eh? Though I suspect you were more comfortable  managing  people to fix the pipes, weren’t you?      Guilty as charged. Still, the garden's coming along. Though I’m completely lost with the soil. It's so different to what I was used to. All clay and… stuff.      It  is  heavy clay around here. You'll need to get some compost worked in, and plenty of it. Have you spoken to Mrs. Pengelly at the garden centre in Holsworthy? She’s a font of all knowledge. Helped me resurrect my roses last year.      Holsworthy’s lovely. I went for groceries yesterday. They've got a surprisingly good butcher. I picked up a joint of beef for Sunday roast.      Good, good. We need to get settled with a good butcher. I attempted a Shepherd’s Pie last week. It was… edible. Though I suspect even the dog looked at it with suspicion. Sarah sent me a recipe, of course. She's convinced I'm reverting to bachelor ways.      Sarah's a treasure. Remember that Christmas she tried to teach you to make mince pies? Nearly set the kitchen on fire!      Oh, don’t remind me! The smoke alarm went off for a solid hour.

… honestly, it’s just taking the mick, innit? Four pound eighty for delivery? Four pound eighty! For a cable? A  cable ! Aye, well, that's Amazon for ya. They know we’re all hooked. What cable is it anyway? HDMI, like. Needed a new one for the telly. Old one's given up the ghost. Started flickering like a disco. Honestly, I was hoping to get it sorted today and binge that new true crime thing everyone’s bangin’ on about. Oh, the Yorkshire Ripper one? I've seen bits. Proper grim. You really think you should be spendin' money on that though? Especially with delivery… Look, it's not like I'm buyin' a new telly! It's a tenner cable, alright? And I'm stuck in here all day, what else am I gonna do? Stare at the wallpaper? It's depressing enough as it is. You  could  be lookin’ for jobs. Remember that thing about volunteering at the library? They said they needed help with the computers. The library? Seriously? I’ve got a degree, lass. A proper degree in history. I’m not shelving books and showin’ old ladies how to send emails. It’s experience, isn't it? Gets you  out  the house. And it's not just that. They said it involves some digital archiving, which is... like, using computers. Relevant. Relevant to what? Fillin’ out more application forms that go straight into the digital abyss? I’ve sent out a hundred applications, Jess. A  hundred . Not a single reply. It’s a joke, a proper joke. Don't be so down, Liam. It takes time. Maybe your CV needs tweaking? I could have a look if you want. I'm pretty good with that sort of thing. Helped Sarah with hers for her apprenticeship. I doubt it'll make much difference. It's not the CV, it's…everything. It's the fact I’ve got nothin’ on there. Nothin’. Everyone wants experience, but how am I supposed to  get  experience when no one will give me a chance? Fair enough. Still, you shouldn't just give up. Did you see old Mr. Henderson down the shop yesterday? He was saying they need someone at the garage, just for odd jobs. Odd jobs? Changing tyres and gettin’ grease under me nails? I spent three years at uni, Jess. It's better than nothing, isn’t it?

…Honestly, the central heating’s a bit temperamental, isn’t it? I was fiddling with it this morning, trying to get the hot water to actually  be  hot. It’s that timer thing, I reckon. Old boy at the hardware shop in Hatherleigh said they’re notoriously fiddly. More trouble than they’re worth, really.      You’d think with a new build, it would all just  work , Dad. It’s frustrating. Are you managing to get lunch sorted? I brought a bit of that pasty from Launceston, if you’re stuck.      Oh, no, no, I managed a cheese sandwich. Though I did nearly set off the smoke alarm trying to toast it. Everything’s so…sensitive. It's a far cry from the old house in Southend, I tell you. Things just  lasted  back then. That cooker I had… forty years, easy. Forty years!      You say that about everything, Brian. You romanticise the past. Remember that Ford Cortina that broke down every other week?      That was different, Margaret! Character! It had character. This modern stuff… disposable. Like those washing machines. Lasted five years, five years! My mother’s Hoover, now  that  was a machine. Still going strong, apparently, with young Tim.      Speaking of Tim, did Mum mention how Auntie Brenda is? She was sounding a bit poorly last time I spoke to her.      She’s…being Brenda. Complaining, mostly. Bit of a cough, apparently. Ninety-two, you know. She’ll outlive us all, I reckon. Stubborn as a mule.      She certainly has a resilience. Right, about this walk you’re planning, ANON? Have you settled on a route? We were discussing it earlier, and I was thinking maybe Hartland Quay? Beautiful views.      Hartland Quay sounds lovely. A bit ambitious, though, isn’t it? With the hills. I'm not as sprightly as I used to be, you know. Perhaps somewhere a little flatter… Bude Canal?      Bude Canal's good. It’s easier underfoot, and we could stop for a cream tea afterwards. I’ve been meaning to try that little cafe in Bude.      Ooh, yes! That sounds perfect. And we can check out that furniture shop near Clovelly. I've been eyeing up a new bookcase for ages. This place needs some proper organisation.      Furniture, eh? You two are always trying to spend my money. I was thinking of getting a new armchair. Something proper, leather. Not this…fabric stuff.      Dad, you need something comfortable!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of revisions on that grant proposal is doing my head in. It’s like, write a clear, concise argument, get it peer reviewed,  then  someone from finance decides they want the budget broken down to the nearest pence, allocated by hour spent on each task. It’s… draining. Oh, tell me about it. Assessment leads are having the exact same battle with the local authority. They want ‘impact metrics’ for every single early years intervention programme. Impact metrics! For three-year-olds learning to share! What are we supposed to measure, the reduction in playground squabbles? Precisely! It's the performative aspect of it all, isn’t it? It's not about genuinely understanding if something is  working , it's about ticking boxes and justifying funding. Makes you question why you even bother. Exactly. Though, I suppose, someone has to hold the purse strings. Still, it's exhausting. How’s your study progressing, despite the grant drama? Anything interesting bubbling up with the long-Covid fatigue patients? Actually, yeah. It's fascinating, and frustrating in equal measure. We're seeing a really strong correlation between pre-existing levels of anxiety and the  persistence  of fatigue, even accounting for the severity of the initial infection. Which, logically, makes sense, right? But proving causality is the killer. Is the anxiety causing the fatigue, is fatigue causing anxiety, or is it a complex interplay? That’s classic, isn’t it? Everything’s interconnected. It’s why I sometimes envy the hard sciences. You drop something, it falls. Simple. Education… and health psychology… it’s all just people, and people are messy. Messy is putting it mildly. I had a participant yesterday, lovely woman, genuinely trying to get her life back on track, but she’s convinced her brain is permanently ‘broken’ because of the Covid. The cognitive distortions are… significant. And combating that, trying to get her to focus on small wins, feels like pushing a boulder uphill. It must be. You're basically a professional hope-dealer then, aren't you? Providing a bit of scientific scaffolding to help people rebuild. I suppose so. It's rewarding when it works, genuinely. It’s just…heavy sometimes. What about you? How’s little Leo taking to year one? Is he enjoying all the phonics and learning to read? He’s… adjusting. Mostly. He’s a very sensitive soul, Leo.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of food young Leo puts away is astonishing. He's a growing lad, I know, but it’s like a black hole, isn't it, Dave? One minute there’s a plate piled high with pasta, the next…gone. He gets that from your side, love. Your brother Mark was always the same. Remember the Christmas turkey incident of ‘89? Oh,  please  tell the turkey story. I've only heard snippets. It’s become family legend. Oh, don’t encourage him! It’s embarrassing. Mark, bless him, practically disassembled the entire bird himself. Didn’t offer anyone else a slice until he’d demolished half of it. Mum was fuming. Sounds like a proper feast, that. Reminds me of old man Hemmings down the pub. Could polish off a Sunday roast faster than you could say ‘Yorkshire pudding’. Big fella, Hemmings. Built like a brick outhouse. It’s amazing how different appetites are, though. I struggle to finish a normal portion sometimes. Makes you wonder what’s going on inside, doesn’t it? Metabolism, mostly. And good old genes. Speaking of which, has anyone noticed how many left-handers we’ve got in the family? Leo’s a southpaw, isn’t he, Sarah? He is, yes. And your niece, Emily. I always found it fascinating. My grandmother, my Nan, she was left-handed and they used to  make  her write with her right hand at school. Can you imagine? Cruel, absolutely cruel. That’s awful! It’s all about brain development, isn’t it? Different sides being dominant. I did a little research for a copywriting project once – fascinating stuff. Apparently, left-handers are overrepresented in creative fields. Creative? Hmm. I’m a decorator, and I reckon a steady right hand is more useful when you’re trying to paint a straight line. No offence. None taken, George! You’re a perfectionist, that's why. It's not about  better  hands, just different. Like, I've always wondered why so many nurses are left-handed. Maybe it's the dexterity when cannulating or something? It’s probably a complete coincidence. Actually, there’s some thought that it might be related to spatial awareness, which is important for a lot of medical procedures. It’s just a theory, of course. See? Sarah’s onto something. You’ve always had a good head for that sort of thing, even without the nursing degree.

…Aye, so like I said to Mam, the parmo wasn’t  quite  right. Too much béchamel, not enough seasoning, y’know? It’s a science, making a proper parmo. A proper one. Parmo, is it? Never heard of it in my day. We had steak and kidney pudding, proper hearty fare. None of this…béchamel business. Sounds French. Everything’s French these days, isn’t it? Ruining a good British plate. It's a North-East thing, Grandad. Think chicken parmigiana, but… well, better. And covered in cheese. Loads of cheese. It's a regional delicacy. I tried explaining it to a colleague from Australia the other week – he just looked baffled. Baffled is right! He was asking if it was like a schnitzel. A  schnitzel ! Honestly. Anyway, it got me thinking about food on our travels, didn't it? That paella we had in Valencia, though...  that  was a science. Valencia? Fancy that. Never been further south than Blackpool, myself. Too hot. Always preferred a bracing wind off the Irish Sea. Though I did have a spell down in Bournemouth with the Post Office, years ago. Awful stuff, the food down there. All avocado and ‘healthy’ options. Give me a good sausage and mash any day. Bournemouth is… different. You’d probably hate it, Grandad. But Valencia was incredible. The seafood, the oranges, the whole atmosphere. I'm trying to convince Chloe here to go to Morocco next year. I've been doing some consulting work for a solar farm company out there. Morocco sounds brilliant! I’d love to go. Imagine the tagines, the spices… though I’d probably miss a good chip shop for a week. You’d need to be careful with the water, wouldn't you? Mam would have a fit. Water! That’s the thing. Used to take my own tea bags when I went on business trips. Couldn't trust the water anywhere. Horrible stuff, some of it. And the biscuits! Foreign biscuits are always dry as dust. Digestives are the only biscuits a man needs. I think they have digestives in Morocco, Grandad. Though maybe not the same quality. Speaking of travel, you never really travelled much, did you, with work? Just the occasional training course? Just the occasional course, aye. Mostly in London. Dreadful place, London. Too loud, too many people. And the traffic! I saw a man try to parallel park for a good ten minutes once.

…and honestly, the student feedback from last semester on the Baudrillard section was… lukewarm, to say the least. They just didn’t  get  simulation and hyperreality. I think I need to rethink how I approach it. Maybe less theory, more practical examples? Mmm, lukewarm is generous, isn't it? I remember you looking utterly defeated after the module review. Honestly, Baudrillard at undergraduate level is always a risk. They’re used to things being… tangible. Simulation feels deliberately obtuse to them. Practical examples are definitely the way forward. What were you thinking? Reality TV? Isn’t that the prime example these days? It feels almost  too  obvious, doesn’t it? But actually, yes. I was thinking of using episodes of  Love Island . It’s infuriatingly popular, and it’s basically constructed reality at its finest. We could deconstruct the editing, the manufactured drama, the curated personalities… Perfect! And it’s something they’ll recognise, which is half the battle. You'll have their attention, at least. Though, brace yourself for debates about whether contestant X is ‘actually’ playing a role or is ‘just being themselves’. That’ll eat up an entire seminar. Oh, I can already see it. “But maybe she  is  genuinely that shallow!” Right. Speaking of attention spans, how are you feeling about your introduction to postcolonial literature? Are you sticking with the Achebe/Conrad pairing? I am, but I’m adding a visual element. I found some amazing documentary footage from the time – newsreels, colonial propaganda… It really highlights the power dynamics at play. And it’s short-form, which is crucial. They switch off if you lecture for more than twenty minutes. You know how it is. Tell me about it. I’ve started incorporating more group work, just to keep them actively engaged. It's exhausting marking all the bits and pieces, but it's better than staring into a sea of glazed-over faces. Right, focus. Achebe. Good stuff. We need to coordinate our reading lists a bit more closely this semester, I think. It feels like we're operating in silos. Agreed. Especially with the core modules. We should do a proper sit-down next week with the syllabus and map things out. This stir-fry needs tasting… Honestly, this chilli oil I got from the market is incredible. It's got fermented black beans in it. Have you been back since we went together?

…and honestly, the instructions for this machine are  criminal . Absolutely criminal. It's supposed to be automatic, isn't it? Automatic! I’ve spent the best part of an hour trying to get it to froth milk properly. It just…splutters. More like a grumpy cat than a coffee machine.      Sounds frustrating, Mary. Are you sure you’ve got the right setting? Maybe the milk’s too cold? I remember Dad complaining about something similar with his last one.      Cold? It’s practically shivering! I’ve tried everything. Warm milk, cold milk, different quantities. It’s a conspiracy, I tell you. A conspiracy to deny a retired woman her morning cappuccino.      You and your cappuccinos. You were perfectly happy with a strong brew for fifty years. This is all this fancy village life doing to you.      Oh, don’t  you  start, Peter. It’s not ‘fancy’ to want a decent cup of coffee. It’s called enjoying one’s retirement. Speaking of enjoying things… have you got a proper breakdown of those storage costs yet? For the furniture?      I’m working on it. They’re… unpleasant. More unpleasant than this coffee machine, even. It's a right rip-off, frankly. They’re charging by the cubic foot, and it all adds up when you’ve accumulated a lifetime of… things.      How much are we looking at, roughly? Just so I can budget. I’m hoping to get a decent chunk of freelance work in next month, but everything feels a bit uncertain at the moment, politically.      Uncertain is an understatement. Honestly, the state of things. Starmer… he's just… bland. Utterly bland. He feels like a focus-grouped personality, not a leader.      He’s got to tread carefully, Mary. After Corbyn, they’re terrified of appearing… radical. It's all about centrism now, isn't it? Capturing the swing voters.      Centrist is just another word for lacking conviction, Peter. Where's the fire? Where's the… the idealism? We used to  believe  in something. Remember the days when Labour actually stood for something other than… not being the Conservatives?      It's tough, isn’t it? It feels like everyone's lost a bit of faith in the whole system. You see it online, with the constant outrage and misinformation. It's exhausting. Although, I do think some of the younger MPs are trying to inject a bit of energy.      Energy, yes.

…No, seriously, ‘Barnaby’ as a pseudonym? It’s a vicar, innit? Like, straight outta a Miss Marple novel. You’re trying to blend in with the criminal underworld, not join the parish council, Jess. Oh, relax, Leo. It just  sounded  good when I was filling out the online form for that dodgy club night. Besides, it’s better than ‘Penelope’, which was my other option. Imagine trying to look intimidating as Penelope. Penelope's lovely! Sounds posh. Fit for a canal boat, that does. Speaking of, has anyone actually  been  on the Regent’s Canal lately? I'm thinking of doing a little promotion for the café – ‘Canal-side Coffee & Cakes!’ – and need to scope out the vibe. Mate, the Regent's Canal is alright. Bit… gently paced for my liking. Reminds me of the Murray River back home, but without the crocodiles. Thankfully. Though, you do get some interesting characters living on those boats. I saw a bloke building a full-sized replica of Stonehenge out of driftwood last week. Stonehenge? Seriously? Only in London. Though, to be fair, it’s probably more structurally sound than a lot of the buildings around here. You know, talking about rivers, does anyone actually know why the Thames is called the Thames? Always bugged me. Is it Celtic or Roman or… what? Ooh, good question! I vaguely remember something about it being a pre-Celtic name, Tamesis, the Romans just Latinized it. Something to do with a wide, flowing river. It's all a bit blurry from uni. That sounds right. Though my nan always said it was named after a goddess. Probably completely made up, mind you. She had a thing for goddesses. More importantly, back to food – anyone fancy Italian tonight? I’m craving a proper carbonara. Italian sounds good! Although, genuine Italian carbonara? You and your rules, Rach. No cream, right? Just egg yolks, guanciale, pecorino romano…the works. Oh, the rules! Rach is militant about Italian food. She once sent back a pasta dish because the basil wasn't  exactly  the right shade of green. It’s a matter of principle! Speaking of principles… did anyone bring the chilli flakes? These chips are begging for some heat. They’re a bit bland, even with the mayo. I thought you had them, Leo? You're always adding chilli to everything. No, I swore  you  had them last time we were at my flat!

… honestly, I just swiped right on, like, everyone last night. I’m desperate for a distraction, y’know? Uni's proper draining me, and Doncaster feels a million miles away. Oh, you and me both, love. Chester’s alright, but it’s not…home. Though, at least it's not Wakefield, is it? No offence, girls. None taken, Liv. Wakefield's grand. It's just…different. And you’re one to talk, coming from Chester, all posh and canals! She's just jealous 'cos we get proper pies. And Yorkshire pudding. Canals don’t compare. Alright, alright, settle down. Pie wars aren't necessary. I'm just trying to revise here. Though, I will admit, Tinder is a black hole of time. I downloaded it on a whim and now I’m convinced all the lads in Derby are either gym bros or obsessed with fishing. Gym bros are the  worst . Always with the mirror selfies. I got matched with one who only talked about his protein intake. It’s baffling. I'm lookin’ for someone to have a laugh with, not hear about creatine. Tell me about it. I had one ask me what my 'stats' were. Like, I’m a person, not a Pokémon! Honestly, it’s less about finding 'the one' and more about validating my existence at this point. Validating your existence, that’s a good way to put it. Honestly, I just want someone to watch awful reality TV with and share a pizza. Is that too much to ask? Definitely not too much. I’d settle for someone who doesn't leave dirty dishes in the sink. Honestly, our housemate, Ben, is driving me up the wall. He thinks the dishwasher is just…decorative. Oh, housemate dramas! I’m avoiding that this year, thank goodness. I managed to bag a room in the quiet halls. Apparently, everyone in my block is a pre-med student. It’s terrifyingly studious. Quiet halls? You're braver than me. I purposefully chose the lively ones. Better to be surrounded by chaos than silence, I reckon. Though, it does mean I have to listen to Sophie's questionable music choices at all hours. Sophie? The one who did a whole interpretive dance to ABBA at the freshers’ party? Aye, that’s her! She’s…a character. A character is putting it mildly. But she’s harmless. Unlike Ben and his Mount Everest of dirty plates.

…No, I’m tellin’ ya, it’s all a smokescreen, Derek. All of it. They bleatin’ on about levelling up, but what’s  actually  levelled up is the cost o’ livin’! It's a right pickle, isn’t it? Used to be, a proper state pension, you could get by. Now… well, now you’re lookin’ at choosin’ ‘tween heatin’ and eatin’, aren’t ya? Don't I know it, Arthur. Don't I know it. Been sayin’ it for years, mind. These politicians, they don’t live in the real world. They’ve got their nice houses, their pensions… they wouldn’t know a hardship if it bit 'em on the backside. Remember when Maggie Thatcher… Oh, don’t  start  on Maggie Thatcher, Derek! Honestly. Always with the Thatcher, you are. It’s been forty years! It's just dredging up old arguments. And Arthur, you always jump on the political bandwagon. We're supposed to be havin' a nice afternoon with a cuppa. Now, now, Mavis, a bit o’ discussin’ politics never hurt anyone. And Derek’s right, in a way. Thatcher started a lot o’ this, didn’t she? Sellin’ off everything, bit by bit. The utilities, the council houses… and look where we are now. Private companies holdin’ us to ransom. Exactly! Used to be, the council looked after folks. Provided decent houses, affordable rents. Now, it's all about profit, innit? And the benefits… don’t even get me started on the benefits. So much paperwork, so many hoops to jump through. And for what? A pittance. It  is  complicated, though, isn't it? I helped old Mrs. Higgins fill out her PIP form last week. Took me nearly a full afternoon. Honestly, it's designed to confuse people. And she’s got arthritis something awful, poor soul. They expect you to explain things you shouldn’t even  have  to explain. It’s a system designed to wear people down, Mavis. Deliberately. They want you to give up. You know, I were lookin’ at the telly last night – that program about the cost of food. Shockin’ it was. A loaf of bread, nearly three quid! Three quid! In my day, you'd get a loaf and change from a shilling. Shillin’s! You’re showin’ your age, Arthur! But you’re right. Everything’s gone through the roof. I saw a fella on the news, sayin’ he was havin’ to choose between fuel for his car to get to work, or feedin’ his children.

… honestly, the sheer volume of emails I had to sift through today. It was ridiculous. Absolutely ridiculous. I swear, half of them were just people replying to replies, all saying ‘thanks’ and ‘received’. Utterly pointless. Mmm. Sounds like a Tuesday. More gravy? Don't change the subject, David. It's infuriating. I mean, I have actual work to do, you know? Not just acknowledge the digital ether. And speaking of work, how was your day chasing donations? Did old Mrs. Higgins finally crack and promise something substantial? Not quite substantial, no. Managed another fifty quid off her. Said she’s worried about the roof needing repair, fair enough. But every little helps, eh? It’s a slog, I tell you. People are tightening their belts. Even the usually generous ones are being… cautious. Cautious is putting it mildly, I suspect. It’s everything, isn’t it? The price of petrol, gas bills… even just a loaf of bread. Honestly, I saw the price of cheddar in Sainsbury's today and nearly had a heart attack. Tell me about it. I stopped looking at the meat aisle a while ago. It’s cheaper to just have more potatoes, isn’t it? Though, you’ve done a lovely job with this roast, love. Honestly, the best. Oh, stop it. You always say that. Just trying to make a decent meal, that’s all. Though, you’re right about the potatoes. They're reasonably priced. Did you speak to Emily today? She said she’d ring about the school play. Aye, spoke to her. Said she’s got the part of a tree. A tree, can you believe it? All that drama club, all that singing, and she’s a bloody tree! Well, it’s a start, isn’t it? At least she’s involved. And she seemed really pleased. Honestly, she was practically vibrating with excitement about her ‘branch extension’ – whatever that is. Branch extension! Honestly! Still, she’s happy. That's the main thing. Did you catch  Garden Rescue  this afternoon? Charlie Dimmock was on, looking amazing as always. Honestly, David, you’re obsessed with Charlie Dimmock. It's bordering on unhealthy. And no, I didn't. I was trying to get on top of those emails. I did catch a bit of that antiques thing you like, though. The one with the grumpy bloke. David Dickinson? He’s not grumpy, he’s… characterful!

… honestly, it’s just  grey . Relentlessly grey. I thought Poland would be…brighter. You’d think being closer to the Mediterranean would give it  some  sort of boost, but no. Just perpetually overcast. Is it like this all the time in Tarnow, Anon? Oh, it’s a bit worse now, actually. We had a properly sunny spell last month. It felt almost…wrong, after so long. It's definitely a lot greyer than Bury. You get used to it. Though, to be fair, Bury's grey is a different kind of grey. More industrial. This is… a melancholic grey. Melancholic. That's a good word for it. I’m feeling rather melancholic myself, actually. This whole trip… it's brought everything back, you know? Aunt Margaret…it wasn’t unexpected, she was so frail, but still. Going back to Cambridge for the funeral… it felt so… alien. Alien? You  grew up  in Cambridge! I did. But I haven't  lived  there in decades. All my friends have moved on, bought houses elsewhere. Everything felt… smaller. And everyone talking about 'home' as if it’s still inherently Cambridge. I said I felt more at home here, actually, with you, and the look I got! Like I'd grown a second head. People are funny about ‘home’, aren’t they? Especially Brits. It's a ridiculously loaded concept. I feel that too, even though I’ve moved around a lot. Bury will always be  a  home, but it doesn’t necessarily feel like  the  home anymore. Teaching in Spain for a year…that felt like a proper shift, a proper start. What was your favourite job, do you remember? Before everything… stopped? Oh, that’s a difficult one. The museum work was stimulating, I suppose. All those manuscripts…but terribly underpaid. And the politics! Endless internal squabbles. The TEFL is…fine. It keeps my brain active, gives me a bit of income. It’s just…isolated. Not like a proper career. You seem to really thrive on the teaching, though. I do. Especially with the older students. They’ve usually  chosen  to be learning, which makes a massive difference. Honestly, watching someone click with a new concept is the best feeling. I saw a post on Instagram earlier from old Mrs. Higgins – remember her, from the village? – she’s on a cruise! Looking ridiculously tanned. Oh, bless her. Always did love a bit of glamour.

… honestly, the brief was  wild . Like, "Write copy for a beige washing machine that appeals to millennials who are deeply invested in sourdough baking." Seriously? Who even  is  that person? Oh, God. That's… specific. Sounds like a marketing meeting brainstorm gone completely off the rails. You're kidding, right? Beige washing machines and artisan bread? Swear on a stack of sourdough starters. It’s for a new campaign. They reckon millennials want "reliability and authenticity" in their appliances. Apparently, beige screams both. I pitched back suggesting we focus on the machine being quiet enough not to disturb proving dough. They weren't thrilled. Classic. They always want  the thing , but don’t actually understand  the people . It's probably some bloke in a suit who last baked anything in 1982. How are you even supposed to approach that? I ended up focusing on the energy efficiency, pretending it’s a sustainability angle. Easier sell, you know? Anyway, enough about the existential dread of advertising. How’s the survey programming going? Still drowning in data? Relatively. It’s… monotonous. I’m mostly cleaning data, which feels profoundly pointless. It’s to do with public perceptions of AI, which  sounds  interesting, but mostly involves correcting ‘N/A’ to ‘Not Applicable’ about a million times. Plus, everyone lies on surveys. Especially about their shopping habits. Oh, tell me about it. I swear, everyone says they buy organic, locally sourced everything, but then their Tesco Clubcard tells a different story. Speaking of shopping, I tried that new Turkish supermarket near Elephant and Castle. Honestly, game changer. The one everyone’s been raving about on Instagram? I’ve been meaning to go. Is it actually worth the trek? I need to stock up – I’m attempting a proper shepherd’s pie this weekend. Postgrad life means eating significantly less well. Worth it. The produce is amazing. And the spices! Forget Waitrose, honestly. I got enough filo pastry to build a small fort. It's… cheap too, surprisingly. Which is a miracle in London. You'll need to get there early though, it gets  packed . Filo pastry fort sounds ambitious. I’ll aim for just a pie. Are you seeing Chloe and Liam next week? They were asking about you. Apparently, Liam’s finally finished his dissertation. Oh, brilliant! Yes, we’re having dinner on Wednesday. I swear that dissertation has been looming over their relationship for like, five years.

…and honestly, the cat was  right  on my face. Not like scratching, just… pressing her whole head against it. It’s a wonder I didn’t suffocate! Six thirty, honestly. Six. Thirty. Was it a good dream though, Mummy? A sparkly unicorn dream? It was… a dream about marking fifty sets of year six literacy tests. Not particularly sparkly, darling. Though, given enough coffee, I could  pretend . Right, you two. Breakfast time. Leo, are you even awake? ‘Mmmph. Nearly. Need fuel for circus practice.’ Circus practice? Not before porridge, young man. And a proper breakfast. No negotiating. We’ve got a full day, remember? Neon Moon is tonight. Ooh, sparkly dresses! Can I wear my butterfly clips? Butterfly clips are  always  allowed for Neon Moon. But first, food. I was thinking we could try and make those little pancake faces again? With blueberry eyes and banana smiles? YES! But can I make a really scary pancake face? With raspberry jam blood? We’ll see about the blood, Leo. Let's get the blueberries sorted first. Right, so, breakfast, then we need to pack your bags for after Neon Moon – staying at Grandma and Grandpa’s, remember? I packed my unicorn already! He needs a holiday too! That’s very thoughtful of you, Lily. He does deserve a little break. Speaking of breaks… I really need more coffee. Honestly, I’m still operating on about 30% power. Mummy, what does ‘G’day’ mean? Auntie Carol said it when she called last night. Oh, that’s Australian, sweetheart. It means ‘good day’. Auntie Carol’s friend, Sharyn, is from Australia. They say it all the time. It's like saying 'hello' and 'good morning' all in one. Do Australians have unicorns? I’m pretty sure they do, Lily. Probably rainbow-coloured ones. It’s a very magical country, from what I hear. Huge spiders, though. We don't talk about the spiders. Spiders?! Ewww! I’m better at juggling than facing spiders. I almost got three balls in the air yesterday! Almost is good, Leo! Practice makes perfect. We can practice in the garden later, maybe. As long as it’s not too muddy. We definitely don’t want muddy juggling balls. Can we get sausages with our pancakes? Please, Mummy,  please ? Alright, alright, sausages it is. But just one each. We need to leave room for dinner later. Neon Moon usually has fantastic food trucks... although knowing our luck, it will be raining.

… honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it all. Claiming it’s ‘levelling up’ when it’s clearly just shuffling money from one pot to another, and mostly benefiting their donors. It makes my blood boil. Now, now, Eleanor. You know better than to get yourself worked up over Westminster. It's a theatre, pure and simple. They  need  to create narratives, even if they're flimsy. It’s how they stay in power. Though, I’ll grant you, this one’s particularly… transparent. Grandad’s right, Mum. It’s all posturing. Though, it  does  affect people, doesn’t it? Like, the funding cuts to universities. I’m lucky, finished my Masters, but loads of people I know are really worried about next year. Exactly, Rhys! It’s not just abstract outrage. It's real people's lives. And it feels… deliberate. This whole dismantling of public services, slowly, slowly. It’s just… infuriating. Remember when your father was applying for teacher training? The grants available then? Not a hope now. Ah, yes. ’88, wasn’t it? He had a decent LEA grant, supplemented by mine, naturally. He always was a good lad, Gareth. Proper calling to teaching, he had. Pity he didn’t stick with it longer, though the pressure was immense. He did. He was brilliant with those children. It just wasn’t sustainable, was it? The workload, the lack of support…and the politics, even then. Remember Mrs. Henderson, the headmistress? Constantly bending over backwards to appease the local council. That sounds awful. It’s a bit like my research grant application, actually. Had to write it to fit  exactly  what they wanted to fund, not what would actually be most useful. Felt a bit… disingenuous. That's the world we live in now, Rhys. Form over substance. It's not a new phenomenon, mind you. My grandfather, your great-great-grandfather, worked in the mines in Nantyglo. He used to tell tales of the mine owners promising improvements, safety measures… and then conveniently ‘forgetting’ when it came to actually spending the money. Just different scale, same principle. Speaking of your grandfather, Huw, did you ever find out more about his brother, the one who emigrated to Australia? I was looking through some old family letters the other day and found a postcard from him, dated 1923. Barely a scribble, just saying he was doing alright, working on a sheep station.

…and honestly, the bit with the runaway badger was  inspired . Helen Moss just has this knack for making even the most ridiculous situations feel…plausible, doesn’t she? Even for eight and six year olds. The badger stole Mr. Henderson’s slippers! And then wore them to the village fete! It was  so  funny! It was! It really was. Though, it did lead to quite a discussion at school about whether badgers  would  actually wear slippers. Apparently, their claws make it very difficult. Maybe if they had special badger slippers? With holes for the claws? Ooh, that’s a brilliant idea, Lily! You’re a natural storyteller, you are. Honestly. We were trying to come up with ideas for our own story earlier, remember? The one about the…what was it? The talking teapot? And the pirate guinea pig! Don't forget Captain Nibbles! Right, Captain Nibbles! Of course. And we got a bit stuck, didn’t we? I think we needed a bit of a…plot twist. Something as good as a slipper-stealing badger. Captain Nibbles finds a treasure map  inside  the teapot! Oh, Lily, that’s excellent! Inside the teapot! That’s… genuinely good. Where does the map lead? To a mountain of carrots! A mountain of carrots? For Captain Nibbles? Well, guinea pigs  like  carrots! It's pirate treasure  for him ! It is! It absolutely is! It’s perfect. See? This is why I love doing this with you two. You think of the most fantastic things. We're going to have the best story ever. Can we draw pictures of it later? Captain Nibbles with an eye patch! Definitely. We can draw pictures and everything. Perhaps we could even… well, I was thinking of taking you both to the Linton Book Festival next month. They usually have workshops and author signings. I saw Helen Moss is doing a reading! Helen Moss?! The badger lady?! The very same! Wouldn’t that be amazing? We could even ask her how she came up with the badger idea! Ooh, yes! And maybe she'll sign my copy of 'The Lark's Secret'! I love that one. I’m pretty sure she would. It’s a really lovely festival. Lots of different authors, and usually some craft things too. Do you think you’d both enjoy it? Will there be pirates? I don’t know about actual pirates, but with our story about Captain Nibbles, maybe we can  pretend  there are!

… honestly, I just don’t get the appeal of actively  choosing  to eat something that's been grown in a lab. It feels… unnatural, doesn’t it? Like, okay, it avoids the animal cruelty aspect, which is good, obviously. But it still feels a bit dystopian. Dystopian? Oh, come on, Chloe! It’s progress. It’s solving a problem. Think about the environmental impact of traditional farming. Methane emissions, land use… shmeat, as you so eloquently put it, could massively reduce that. And it  is  meat, at a cellular level. It just hasn't had to… live a life. She’s got a point, though, Liv. The ‘unnatural’ thing is a strong feeling. It's kind of like those vitamin tablets, isn't it? You know you  should  take them, they’re good for you, but it feels…less satisfying than getting nutrients from food. Like you’re missing out on something. Exactly, Finn! It’s that missing-out feeling! And it’s not just the environmental side, is it? It feels like we’re just shifting the ethical problem, not solving it. Who’s to say the cells aren’t grown in a way that’s still exploitative, just to a different organism? It’s a different type of oppression, potentially. Exploitative to…cells? Chloe, you’re going deep down a philosophical rabbit hole now. They’re not sentient. It's not the same as a living, breathing animal. Look, I know you’re passionate about animal welfare, I am too. I just think this is a practical solution. Remember that documentary we watched about factory farming? That was horrific. This is  better  than that. Actually, thinking about horrific, it always gets me thinking about hunting. It's still ending a life, obviously, but there’s something…more honest about it, I think. A direct connection to where your food comes from. It’s brutal, but it’s not hidden away in an abattoir. Oh, Finn, don’t even start with the romanticised hunting thing! That’s just… justifying cruelty with 'honesty'. An animal suffering in a field is no different than one suffering in a slaughterhouse. Both are awful. And the idea of needing to kill something for food just feels so…primitive now. We have options! Plus, the whole ‘hunter-gatherer’ argument is a bit dodgy. Our ancestors weren’t exclusively hunting. They were foraging, gathering plants… a pretty vegetarian-leaning diet for a lot of the time, actually.

… honestly, Mum, I just don’t understand why you keep  everything . Honestly, Derek’s old rugby boots? They’re falling apart! What possible sentimental value could they have now? Now, now, Brenda. Don't start on your mother. They were good boots in their day, and your Auntie Carol specifically asked if we could keep them, said they reminded her of him scoring that try against Blackheath. It’s true, she did. I remember her going on about it at Christmas. Though, I think she mostly remembers him looking rather dashing in his kit. Speaking of which, did anyone see that new series on Netflix,  The Crown ? It's brilliant! The costumes are just…wow. Oh, I started it, but honestly, all that posh talk is a bit much for me. Sounds like they’re swallowing marbles half the time. Give me a good crime drama any day. And honestly, Carol’s memory is…selective. Derek was terrible at rugby. He wasn’t  terrible . He was… enthusiastic. And Brenda, you’re sounding very harsh. It’s just a pair of boots! Besides, we’ve got bigger worries. The washing machine’s making that awful rattling noise again. Think it’s going to pack up properly this time? Oh, no! Not again! Is it the thingy with the… drum? I always forget what it's called. Dad, you fixed it last time, didn't you? I did my best. It's probably the bearings. It'll last another few weeks, I reckon, until I’ve got time to actually do something about it. Reminds me of your Uncle George, always putting things off. Remember when he said he’d fix the shed roof for a year? It collapsed in the middle of summer, full of garden gnomes! Oh, George! He was a disaster. Though, I do think he did it deliberately, just to get out of gardening. Speaking of disasters, has anyone thought about New Year’s Eve yet? Are we doing anything here, or are we all going our separate ways? I was thinking of maybe going to a friend’s party in London. It's a bit of a trek, but apparently it’s going to be a proper knees-up. Though, I’m not sure the internet connection on the train will be any good. I need to upload some copy before Monday. London, eh? Sounds expensive. We could have a quiet one here.

… honestly, I still don’t understand  why  you needed a butterfly fork. It wasn’t even for fish! You were having spaghetti. But Mum, it felt… more sophisticated. Like I was having a proper grown-up dinner. All my mates use normal forks. Yeah, it’s just… a bit much, isn’t it? I’m happy with a regular fork. Less fiddly. Sophisticated? Darling, you were wearing dinosaur pyjamas ten minutes ago. Sophistication isn’t really the word I’d use. Though, I admire the ambition. Your grandfather would have loved that, actually. He collected odd cutlery. Grandad collected  everything . Remember that time he tried to build a robot out of old toasters? And it nearly set the shed on fire! Dad was  fuming . He was a character, your grandfather. He always said life was too short for boring cutlery. Speaking of which, did you both remember to observe the two minutes silence this morning? Oh, yeah. At school. It was really quiet. Everyone just… stopped. It was weird, actually. Normally, it’s chaos in the canteen, but it was properly silent. Ms. Davies gave us this whole speech beforehand. Good. It’s important to remember. It’s getting further away in time, isn’t it? For you two, it’s history, almost. Not something you lived through. It makes me think of… well, everything that’s going on now, with Russia. It’s frightening. Is it like, going to be a war? I don’t know, love. I truly don’t. Hopefully not. But it’s a very dangerous situation, and sadly, history has a habit of repeating itself. That’s why remembering is so vital. Do you think they’ll… like… use the big bombs? I hope not, darling. No one wants that. It's a terrible thought. We can only hope the leaders find a way to resolve things peacefully. It's something your father and I talk about a lot. Speaking of things happening… my birthday's soon, isn't it? Is that all this is about? A thinly veiled attempt to steer the conversation towards presents? No! Well… maybe a little.
