I was just thinking. I'm turning fourteen, which is a proper big birthday. He wants a new gaming chair. A really expensive one. A  really  expensive one, you say? We’ll see. We’ll see. What about you, darling? Anything you're hoping for?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Year 6 SATS papers is  criminal . I’ve marked, I think, seventy this evening already. Seventy! It's just endless. Though, admittedly, having this chat is a lovely distraction. So, Cornwall… are we definitely leaning that way this summer? Cornwall! Can we go to the beach  every  day? And build a really, really big sandcastle? Bigger than last time? And can we go crabbing? I really liked crabbing last time. Did you get any crabs, Lily? I got three! One was massive! It nearly pinched my finger! Three is a good haul. And yes to beaches, and hopefully lots of crabbing. Though, perhaps not  too  close to the claws, Leo. We need all our fingers intact. Cornwall feels… do-able. It's a longer drive, obviously, than Adventure Island, but it feels like we’d all get more out of it. Adventure Island was good though. The rollercoasters were really fast! They were very fast, weren't they? A bit too fast for Mummy, perhaps. Speaking of things that make Mummy feel a bit wobbly, I was thinking about food. I’ve been feeling a bit… off lately, and I booked a food intolerance test. Turns out, I’m mildly intolerant to gluten. Gluten? What’s gluten? Is it in biscuits? It's in biscuits, and bread, and pasta... lots of tasty things! It means I might have to be a bit more careful about what I eat, that’s all. Doesn’t mean no biscuits forever, just… less! It might mean we need to be a little more mindful when we’re in Cornwall, checking menus. Will you get poorly if you eat gluten? Just a bit tummy-achy, mostly. It won’t be a disaster. Anyway, back to happy holiday thoughts! I was reading an article about the V&A exhibition, the one on Alice in Wonderland. They've got some amazing costumes and original illustrations. Alice in Wonderland! We have the book! Read it to me again, Mummy? We will, sweetheart, we will. But maybe after I’ve marked another twenty SATS papers. Actually, maybe Cornwall’s sounding even better now. Escape the papers, escape the gluten… enjoy some fresh sea air. Can we get ice cream in Cornwall? Proper ice cream? Not the stuff from the shops? Proper ice cream, definitely. We'll find a farm shop and get clotted cream ice cream.

… honestly, Mr. Davies is taking the absolute mickey. Like, a fifteen-mark essay on the socio-economic impact of the Industrial Revolution  and  a source analysis due next Wednesday? It’s mental. Tell me about it! Davies is proper harsh. I think he just likes seeing people stress. My mum practically had to rewrite half my history homework last week, it was that bad. Though, to be fair, I  did  spend most of Saturday at Jamie’s birthday. Jamie’s party was decent. Bit crowded though, wasn’t it? Nearly got knocked over by Ben trying to show off his… well, whatever  that  was. And then Chloe spilled juice all down my new trainers. Classic Chloe. She’s a walking disaster zone. But yeah, it did get proper rammed. Still, worth it for the pizza, right? Did you see Liam trying to chat up Sarah? It was painful. Oh god,  painful  is an understatement. He just kept going on about his bike. “It’s got disc brakes, you know. Really responsive.” Like, she cares! Speaking of bikes, I need to get mine checked. The gears are all messed up. Might take it to Cycle Republic on Saturday. Good shout. Mine’s alright, just need to pump up the tyres. Dad promised he’d do it. He’s been on about getting a new mountain bike himself, says it’s for ‘exercise’ but we all know he wants to go bombing down Northala Fields. He’s a big kid, your dad. Anyway, back to school. Have you heard about Oldman wanting to make a big deal out of people being late? Apparently, he’s on a power trip now he’s a prefect. Seriously? Oldman? He's always late himself! It's ridiculous. He was moaning at Finn for being two minutes late this morning, but he strolled into English ten minutes behind schedule yesterday. Double standards, massive ones. Exactly! He's the worst. I'm convinced he just wants the authority. And they're starting to crack down on phones too. I nearly got detention just for  having  mine out in the common room. It was in my hand, not even on! They're going overboard. Miss Patel keeps going on about ‘respecting the learning environment’. Like we’re all just rabid animals trying to disrupt her lesson. I swear, she thinks we've all got ADHD. She needs to chill.

…Aye, but like I said, the A19 roundabout at the Boldon interchange is just  mental . They’ve been 'improving' it for, what feels like, a decade now? And it’s still chaos. I swear, getting to mam's on a Sunday is a test of endurance. You wouldn't believe the near misses. Sounds… stimulating. Hertfordshire roads are rarely  that  dramatic, thankfully. Mostly just endless queues on the M1 if there's an accident. It's less about skill and more about resignation, honestly. You just accept it’s going to take three hours to get anywhere. Resignation? Nae man, it’s pure aggression! Everyone's just honking and barging. It’s like the Hunger Games, but with Vauxhalls and Fords. Seriously, you need to be a proper defensive driver up here. Did I tell you about old Mrs. Henderson cutting me up last week? Nearly ended up in a field of sheep. Sheep! Right. Okay, that  is  a bit more exciting than my commute. Though, speaking of potentially disastrous encounters, did you catch the cricket yesterday? England were looking proper shaky there for a bit. Root played a blinder though, didn’t he? I caught a bit. Was more focussed on getting the washing in, to be honest. Cricket's alright, but it drags a bit, doesn’t it? Give me a good rugby match any day. More likely to have a bit of… incident. But aye, Root saved their bacon, dinnae he? He always does. He does. He's the glue. I’m trying to get back into cycling, actually. Thought it would be a good way to, you know, escape the M1 misery. Got a new road bike, pretty swish carbon frame. Oh, a bike! Brilliant. You’d need a proper mountain bike round here though, not one of them fancy things. Potholes the size of craters, they are. And the drivers… they don't seem to  see  cyclists. I’ve nearly been doored about five times just going to the shops. That’s… reassuring. I was picturing idyllic country lanes. I suppose I’ll need to stick to the cycle paths then. There are a few decent ones around Harpenden, thankfully. Have you ever done much cycling yourself? When I was a kid, aye. Round the Hetton Lyons park mostly. But I were always more of a football lass. And now…well, getting to work involves a 20-minute bus journey.

… honestly, I still think Golden Wok is consistently better. Their Kung Pao chicken has  actual  peanuts, not those little dusty things you get everywhere else. Mate, you're obsessed with peanuts. It's a chicken dish, not a peanut dish! Happy Dragon’s salt and chilli ribs are legendary. Legendary, I tell you. Plus, they actually deliver to this postcode now, which is a win. Hold on, both of you. Legendary is a strong word, Liam. They were a bit greasy last time I ordered from them. And Sarah’s right about the peanuts – it’s a textural thing. I need the crunch! Besides, Golden Wok does a really good vegetarian spring roll. Not the soggy kind. Exactly! See? Hannah gets it. It’s the principle of the thing. You order Kung Pao chicken, you expect peanuts. It’s like ordering a bacon sandwich and getting ham. Outrageous. Right, dramatic. Look, I’m starving. Let’s just  pick  a place. I've been staring at Just Eat for ten minutes while you two debate legume content. Happy Dragon or Golden Wok? Final vote. Hmm… okay, quick question. Does Golden Wok still do that special fried rice with the char siu pork? I’ve been craving it all week. Yes! They absolutely do. And it's proper char siu, not that weird, pink stuff some places try to pass off. Honestly, I’ve had some experiences with Chinese takeaways… one place tried to convince me their sweet and sour sauce was homemade! Homemade! It tasted suspiciously like it came straight from a catering-sized bottle. Oh, Sarah. You’re such a food snob. But alright, alright. Char siu pork  is  a good point. Look, I’m willing to compromise. Let’s go Golden Wok, but we’re getting a side of Happy Dragon’s chips, just because they’re massive and always perfectly seasoned. Deal! That sounds perfect. Massive chips are always a good idea. Although, they  did  forget the prawn crackers last time I ordered from Happy Dragon… a cardinal sin, frankly. Oh god, don't even  mention  missing prawn crackers. It ruins the whole experience. It's like, what even  is  a Chinese takeaway without prawn crackers? It's just...sad. Alright, alright, enough about tragically missing prawn crackers. I’m ordering. Sarah, what are you having? The Kung Pao, obviously. Predictable, but accurate. And a portion of the special fried rice.

… honestly, the waiting lists are just getting ridiculous, aren’t they? Old Mrs. Higgins down the street, needs a hip replacement, been on the list for eighteen months. Eighteen! And she’s practically housebound as it is. Tell me about it. It’s the same story everywhere. I’m seeing it day in, day out at the clinic. People are suffering massively while they wait. We’re doing our best, patching them up, managing symptoms, but it’s just… a sticking plaster on a gaping wound, innit? The system’s creaking, proper creaking. Creaking is an understatement. It’s about to fall apart, I reckon. I was talking to a colleague, Dr. Aaltonen – Finnish, brilliant woman – and she was explaining how their system works. Preventative care, massive investment in primary care… completely different philosophy. Finland, eh? Always hear good things. Though, swapping the grey skies of Liverpool for Finnish ones… I don’t know. Still, anything’s got to be better than this. I mean, they’re brilliant doctors and nurses, genuinely. It’s not  people  failing, it's the  system . Exactly! And the funding. Always the funding. It’s ironic, isn’t it? We’ve got people like my sister, practically working themselves into the ground as a consultant, and then you hear stories about management consultants brought in for a fortune, telling everyone how to save money. Money that directly impacts patient care. Don’t even get me started on the bean counters. It's infuriating. They wouldn't last a shift on the ward, let me tell you. Speaking of the street, have you heard anything more about what’s going on with the Millers next door? They’ve been getting builders in non-stop for weeks. Just rumours, really. Something about needing a new boiler, but I heard old man Peterson say they’re knocking walls down. Apparently, they’re trying to create an annexe for his mother. He’s always moaning about something, mind you, so take it with a pinch of salt. An annexe… that’s ambitious. This street's getting packed, isn't it? Everyone squeezing into these Victorian terraces. My eldest, Liam, he’s desperate to get his own place, but good luck with that. The prices are mental. Even renting’s a nightmare. It's the same everywhere, sadly. Trying to find somewhere decent in the city centre is impossible without winning the lottery.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork involved with even  suggesting  extensions to deadlines for students is becoming ridiculous. It's like the university thinks we’re all just filing machines now, not, you know, actually  teaching . Though, I suppose it's all part of the ‘audit culture’, innit? Everything has to be accounted for, quantified… Audit culture? Sounds fancy. Back in my day, if a lad was having a rough time, you just  talked  to him. Didn’t need a form in triplicate. Though, I suppose things were different then. Not so many youngsters fretting about… everything. Different is an understatement, Arthur. You grew up in a Liverpool that barely exists anymore. It was… tougher, wasn’t it? Real grit. Tough? Oh, you’ve no idea, lad. No idea. Me dad, never worked a day in his life. Said it lowered a man’s dignity. Lived off his mother’s pension, and a bit of…well, let’s just say resourceful dealings down the docks. The police  knew  him, let me tell ya. Always a wink and a nod. They weren’t bothered as long as there weren’t any real problems. A wink and a nod… things have changed. You see what happened down on Edge Lane last week? The raid? Heavily armed police, kicking doors in. Apparently, a suspected cannabis farm. Heard about that. All that fuss. Used to be you'd smell it wafting down the street and nobody batted an eyelid. These young fellas, though, getting involved in things they don’t understand. And the police, all heavy-handed. They used to be  our  lads, you know? Now it’s all about targets and procedures. It's complicated, Arthur. There's a lot of new faces around here now too, isn't there? A lot of folks coming from… elsewhere. It’s put a strain on everything, hasn't it? The resources, the schools… ‘Elsewhere’. That’s what they call it now. In my day, we just said ‘immigrants’. And we welcomed 'em. Polish lads after the war, Irish builders, Italians with their ice cream vans… brought a bit of life to the place. These ones… well, they keep themselves to themselves. Don’t integrate, not like they used to. Though, to be fair, nobody tries to  make  them integrate. It’s not always that simple. Language barriers, cultural differences… it takes time. My wife, Erika, she's German, you know.

…Aye, well, it’s just… frustrating, innit? Like, we spend all this time building these corpora, meticulously tagging everything, and then the requests come in and it’s always “Can you just quickly pull all instances of ‘like’ used as a discourse marker?” As if it's a five-minute job!      It  is  a bit reductive, isn’t it? Especially when you know the nuances we’ve captured. It’s not just ‘like’ - it's  how  it’s used, the speaker’s intention, the co-text. People treat corpora like giant search engines sometimes.      Exactly. I had someone last week wanting a list of all uses of ‘innit’ across the entire spoken corpus, and then asked if we could categorise them by age group. As if that’s a simple correlation to draw! It's the social factors, the context… it's everything.      You guys are describing my daily life. It’s the same in ELT research. Everyone wants the easy answers. “Which grammar point causes the most errors for Chinese learners?” Okay, well, that depends on  which  Chinese learners,  what  task they’re attempting,  their  previous language learning experience…it's complex! They want a silver bullet, and linguistics just doesn’t  do  silver bullets.      I hear you, completely. Publishing’s similar, actually. Editors wanting to know what 'vibes' with Gen Z, like it’s some formula you can just… plug in. “What’s the new slang? What’s trending?” But language is always shifting, always evolving. What’s cool today is cringe tomorrow. It’s impossible to keep up!      It's just...people seem to think 'language' is static. They want to box it up neatly. I was explaining to me mam about the corpus the other day, and she just said, "So, you just look up words?". I nearly choked on me tea! She thought it was like a really big dictionary.      That’s lovely, in a way, though. It shows how much work we do is invisible. People appreciate the result – better textbooks, more accurate language learning tools – but they don’t necessarily understand the process behind it.      It's the qualitative side that gets lost, isn’t it? It’s easy to quantify ‘frequency,’ but much harder to quantify ‘meaning.’ We’re battling against this desire for everything to be numbers.      And the misinterpretation of numbers! People take stats out of context all the time. Suddenly, a 0.5% increase in the use of a certain preposition is ‘proof’ of some fundamental shift in the language.

...Honestly, the sheer  volume  of rubbish on streaming services these days. It's relentless. Remember when telly was… curated? You had a schedule, a controller with  taste . Now it's just algorithms chucking anything at the wall, hoping something sticks. I tried to watch that new historical drama everyone was on about, ‘The Serpent’s Kiss’ or something, and it was just… baffling. Historically inaccurate, terribly acted, and the plot drifted off into total fantasy about halfway through.      Oh, I know what you mean. It’s the paradox of choice, innit? Literally thousands of things to watch, and 99% of it is… filler. I’ve been sticking to documentaries, mostly. Safer bet. Though even  they  tend to sensationalise everything these days. I was watching one about the Amazon rainforest the other night, and it felt more like a thriller than a nature programme.      Exactly! It’s the 'dramatisation' of everything. Nobody trusts genuine observation anymore. It’s all hyperbole. Speaking of observation, I was thinking about your fieldwork in Morocco. How did you find navigating the cultural differences, especially from Hull? Quite a leap, I imagine.      You are  not  wrong. It was… an adjustment. Hull prepares you for a certain kind of bluntness, you know? Straight talking. But Morocco is all nuance and indirect communication. Took me ages to learn when someone was saying ‘yes’ when they actually meant ‘no,’ or vice versa. Nearly caused a diplomatic incident trying to buy a rug, I think.      Crikey. I can see that. It's funny, isn't it? We think of language as just words, but it’s so much more than that. It’s about all the unspoken rules, the shared understandings. That’s what I’m wrestling with in my thesis, actually. The pragmatic influence of culture on linguistic choices.      Sounds… intense. How’s the thesis coming along, by the way? Still battling with the verb conjugations of Old Cornish?      Don’t even  mention  Old Cornish. It’s a linguistic nightmare. No, I’ve moved onto the sociolinguistic aspects now, thankfully. I’ve been trying to get some people from the Cornish language revitalisation movement to participate in interviews. It's proving tricky. They’re understandably protective.      I can imagine. It's a sensitive topic. They're trying to resurrect something precious. I've found that with my own research on dialect variations in Yorkshire - people are very attached to their way of speaking.

…and honestly, lad, the state of some of those papers this year. You wouldn’t  believe  the number of students who thought pi was 3.1416, and then rounded it to… 3.1! Three point one! After all this time, still. It’s disheartening, it really is.      Right. Sounds… stressful. Is that why you were muttering about ‘irrational numbers’ at breakfast?      Aye, well, stressful  and  frustrating. They're irrational for a reason, aren't they? They go on forever! It's a key concept!      Oh, numbers. Always were a bother to me. Give me a good gossip any day. Though young Thomas, your dad, he was always good with figures. Used to balance the books for old Mrs. Higgins down the road, even after he retired from the docks.      Aye, he was. Clever lad. Though didn’t have the patience for explaining it to anyone. Said it was like trying to teach a pig to sing - wasted effort.      Grandad! That’s a bit harsh.      It's just a saying, lad! No offense meant to anyone. Speaking of wasted effort, are we still on for the bingo tonight, Margaret? My lucky dabber’s calling to me.      We are, Arthur. Though I’m warning you, Doris next door has been practicing. She’s got a new pair of glasses and claims to see the numbers before they even come up.      Doris and her glasses! She thinks she’s psychic. She told me last week I’d meet a tall, dark stranger. All I met was the postman, and he’s got a bit of a limp, poor lad.      Maybe the postman  is  your tall, dark stranger, Grandma! You just need to look closer.      Don’t be daft. He’s delivering bills, not romance. Now, have you made arrangements for getting us back to Hull later, Eileen? My legs are starting to ache.      Of course, love. I’ve asked young David – the lad with the taxi, remember? He’s picking us up at six. It’s a bit of a drive, but better than relying on the buses, especially this time of day.      Good, good. Buses are full of youngsters these days, glued to their… whatchamacallits? Phones, that's it. No respect for their elders.      They’re just… communicating, Grandad. It’s how we all talk now.      He's right, Arthur. It's different, but it's not necessarily disrespectful. Although, sometimes I wish they’d look up and appreciate the world around them.

…and honestly, seeing those photos from the Lakes really makes me ache for a proper Sunday roast. It's just  not  the same here, is it? Everything feels…different. Not bad, just…different. Different is putting it mildly. Trying to explain gravy to someone who’s only ever had soy sauce is…an experience. Though, to be fair, Lin tried to make a Yorkshire pudding last month. It was…enthusiastic. Oh, bless her. I remember when she first came to Norwich. The sheer confusion over what a crumpet was. It took a full twenty minutes of explanation and a demonstration. And then she tried to dunk it in her tea, didn’t she? She genuinely thought that was the  point . She did! It was hilarious. Honestly, sometimes I feel like we’re cultural ambassadors. Constantly explaining the intricacies of British life. Though, looking at these photos of Sarah and Mark’s wedding… that just reminds me how much I miss everyone. Me too. Sarah looked incredible. I still can’t believe she managed to pull off a vintage dress  and  wellies. Typical Sarah. Did you see Ben in the background trying to sneak sausages off the buffet? Of course! Some things never change. He practically lives on sausages. Gosh, I haven’t seen him properly in…nearly a year now? It feels like a lifetime. It does. And thinking about it, it’s been even longer since we’ve been back. Two Christmas’s missed now. It feels a bit…guilty, doesn’t it? We’re loving it here, truly, but… I know. The university is brilliant, the students are fantastic, and living in Chengdu is…well, it’s an adventure. But birthdays and weddings... those things feel harder when you’re 6,000 miles away. I keep promising Mum I’ll make it for her birthday next year, but honestly, the flights get more expensive. We'll make it work. We always do. Maybe we need to start planning further in advance, saving specifically for trips home. Although, honestly, I’m already thinking about our summer break. Remember that little coastal path walk we talked about in Cornwall? Oh, yes! The one with the pub afterwards? That sounds absolutely heavenly right now. Actually, have you seen that article about the new hiking trail near Guilin? They say the landscapes are spectacular. Maybe we could do a little internal travel instead of going all the way back this summer?

… honestly, I still feel wrecked. Like, properly wrecked. Did you see Chloe trying to order chips at 3am? She was convinced they were called ‘potato smiles’. Potato  smiles , Liv! No way! Chloe and her… unique vocabulary after a few VKs. Honestly though, she wasn't the worst. Remember Ben trying to explain quantum physics to the bouncer? He got nowhere. Absolutely nowhere. Oh god, Ben. He’s a menace. Though, to be fair, the bouncer looked  very  unimpressed. It's just…my head is pounding. I need about a week of sleeping and just water. And maybe some of your Nan’s adobo. That stuff is magic. Tell me about it. I’m surviving on caffeine and regret. And yeah, Nan’s adobo is a life saver. I’ll ask her to make a massive batch this weekend when I go home. You can have some, yeah? Although, Mum will probably make me take half back to uni – she’s obsessed with saving leftovers. You’re an angel. Honestly. My mum just judges my life choices, especially anything involving a night out. “Are you  sure  this is a good use of your student loan, darling?” she said yesterday. As if going out occasionally is some moral failing. Ugh, mums. Mine’s got a similar vibe. Always asking about my ‘future prospects’ when all I want to do is figure out which filter looks best on my Insta story. She keeps going on about my cousin, Paolo, who's apparently 'doing so well' as an accountant. Paolo the accountant? The one who wears socks with sandals? No thanks. Honestly, I’d rather spend my life failing art history than becoming an accountant. Speaking of failing… how’s that gym membership going? You were adamant you were going to become a fitness influencer. Don’t remind me. I went twice.  Twice . It’s just… cold, and loud and everyone is judging. Plus, I realised I'd rather spend my time scrolling TikTok than actually lifting weights. It’s a sacrifice I’m willing to make for the sake of my mental health. Fair enough. Though, you did look good in that sports bra. Very… athletic. Oh, shut up! You’re just saying that. Anyway, did you see Josh last night? He was chatting up that girl from the law society. The one with the really long hair. Oh, yeah. Chloe said she’s super posh.

Honestly, this is lovely. Peas and chips. Reminds me of being a girl, though my mother would’ve insisted on Brussels sprouts alongside. Dreadful things. So, are we settled on picking up Gran from the station next Tuesday?      Yeah, all good from my end. I’ve put it in the diary, and I can do the whole round trip. Shouldn’t be too much bother. Though knowing Gran, she’ll want to stop at every garden centre between here and Penrith.      You are not wrong there, love. Last time she visited, we spent a good hour admiring petunias. Still, better than dealing with a grumpy passenger, eh? At least she’s cheerful.      Cheerful and…opinionated. Especially about the football. She still thinks Best was the greatest. Says these modern players wouldn’t last five minutes in  his  day.      She’s got a point, though, doesn't she? It's all a bit…manufactured now, isn’t it? All tactics and no flair. I watched a bit of the Euros yesterday, and honestly, it felt more like watching chess than football.      Chess with incredibly fit, highly paid players. True, true. Though I’ve been getting back into FIFA myself, you know, on the PlayStation. Keeps the brain ticking over.       You ? Playing FIFA? Honestly, Arthur, I thought you’d have more dignified hobbies in retirement. Like…stamp collecting.      Don’t knock it ‘til you try it, Mary. It’s surprisingly addictive. And competitive. I’m building a team from scratch, focusing on youth players. It's all about spotting the potential, you see? Like developing a good planning strategy, only with footballers.      That sounds…intense. Are you, like, yelling at the TV?      Occasionally. When the referee makes a ridiculous decision. Which is disappointingly often. It's not  yelling , exactly. More…emphatic commentary.      Bless you. It’s good you’re finding something to occupy yourself. It's important. Though, speaking of questionable decisions… I was thinking about young Liam and that incident with Mrs. Henderson’s garden gnome.      Oh, here we go.      Liam? What’s he done now?      Well, apparently, it wasn't a simple “accident” with a football, as he claimed. Old Mr. Davies saw the whole thing. Said Liam was deliberately trying to kick it over the fence and graze the gnome.      Oh, honestly. He’s eight years old! It was a bit of mischievous fun.      Mischief is one thing, deliberately aiming for something is another.

… honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it. Trying to claim a software update bricked the touchpad. It’s a ten-year-old laptop, Sarah! It's practically a museum piece. They wanted me to remotely access it and…and  fix  it. Oh, David, you and your tech support woes. You’re far too polite. Just tell them it’s beyond economical repair. Speaking of things breaking, how’s the shelf you were putting up? Did you manage to get it level? Level? That’s a laugh. Anything level in this country’s a miracle these days. I tried puttin’ a picture up in me flat last week…ended up lookin’ like the Leaning Tower of Pisa. Oh, don't I know it! My Geoff's hopeless with DIY. Bless him, he tries, but it always ends up… wonky. Although, to be fair, he  did  manage to change a lightbulb yesterday without electrocuting himself, so that's progress. It’s… mostly level. I think. It’s close enough for books, anyway. So, anyone fancy venturing out for a walk around Brighton before you all go? The forecast is actually looking decent. Not like last week’s monsoon. Oh, I'd love to! A stroll along the pier sounds perfect. Though, it's getting chilly, isn't it? I saw Old Man Hemmings across the hall bundled up in a coat this morning. He reckons his arthritis can predict the weather. Hemmings? Him and his weather predictions. Used to work with his brother, years ago. Proper character, that one. Always moaning about the council. Now it’s the bin strikes, isn’t it? Makes a right mess of everything. It  is  a mess. Honestly, the smell! And they're saying it could last weeks. Still, better than the water situation, I reckon. Did you see what Southern Water are up to now? Another hosepipe ban? Apparently. They're blaming leaks, naturally. It's either that or they're filling private swimming pools for millionaires. Honestly, I’m starting to think bottled water is the future. Though, even  that  feels wasteful. What's the difference between Highland Spring and Evian anyway? It all tastes like… water. It's the minerals! Apparently. I tried to get Dad to switch to reusable filters, but he's convinced tap water gives him indigestion. Stubborn as a mule, that man. Your Dad’s alright, though. Reminds me of me old man.

… honestly, I still can’t believe how badly United played. Honestly! They were absolutely dreadful. Did you see the score? Yeah, saw it pop up on my phone just before I came in. 3-1 to City, right? Absolutely gutted for you, Auntie Carol. You were so optimistic this season. Optimistic is a strong word, darling.  Hopeful . There's a difference. And it's just…deflating. It’s a bit like everything at the moment, isn’t it? Grey skies, grey football. You know, it’s really hit me this week… this proper SAD thing. I’m just feeling…low. I get it. Poland in November isn’t exactly brimming with sunshine. It's a shock to the system after even a mild British autumn. Are you managing okay? Are you getting out at all? Trying. I walked to the market earlier, but it was drizzling. And honestly, seeing everyone bustling about, doing Christmas shopping… it just made me miss Cambridge more acutely. It sounds silly, doesn't it? Missing the  hustle  of Cambridge. Not silly at all. It’s the little things. Speaking of things making you miss home, I had a message from Liam earlier. He’s said he's started a winter league five-a-side. Honestly, the cheek! Like I'd be tempted to swap Polish pierogi for soggy pitches and over-enthusiastic dads. Oh, Liam! Always the sportsman. How’s your teaching going, anyway? Any particularly challenging students? It’s busy. I’ve got this one student, Marek, who’s brilliant, honestly. Really quick, picks up everything. But he’s terrified of the speaking exam. Completely freezes. I feel so responsible, you know? Like I need to magically imbue him with confidence. It’s exhausting. Oh, I understand that completely. It's that feeling of wanting to protect them, wanting them to succeed. It’s why good teachers are worth their weight in gold. It's odd, isn't it? I used to just…float through life. Now, even thinking about Marek's exam makes me stressed. Although, oddly, I sometimes miss practical work. Practical work? Like…? Oh, ages ago. Before everything, you know? My brother had a smallholding for a while, and I used to help out. Mucking out stables, picking fruit… surprisingly satisfying. And much more  real  than, well, this. Wow, I didn’t know that! You? On a farm? That  doesn’t  fit the Cambridge image!

… honestly, it’s just relentless at the moment. This wedding fair next month? Absolute chaos. Like herding cats, I swear. She wants  everything  bespoke, and thinks ‘bespoke’ means ‘cheap’. It’s Doncaster levels of demanding, honestly. You wouldn’t believe the colour swatches… fifty shades of beige, practically. Fifty shades, eh? Sounds intense. Beats graftin’ on a building site, I suppose. Though at least bricks don’t argue about the  tone  of grey. What’s she like, this bride? She’s apparently a bit of a social media influencer, isn't she, Chloe? All about the aesthetic. Which, naturally, means  you  have to make her unrealistic Pinterest dreams a reality. You hit the nail on the head, Liv. All about the ‘gram. And the mother of the bride is worse. Wants everything to look like something out of a magazine. I spent an hour yesterday just explaining the difference between 'ivory' and 'cream'. An  hour ! It's a colour, love, not a philosophical debate. Blimey. Sounds stressful. I’m glad I just lay bricks. Simple. You build it, it stays put. Though even that’s getting complicated with all the new regulations. They’re always changing things. Anyway, how’s the dating life, Chloe? Still swiping? Swiping is an understatement, Ben. It’s more like endlessly scrolling through a catalogue of disappointment. Met someone last week, seemed alright on the app, turns out he spends his weekends re-enacting Viking battles. Full chainmail and everything. No way! Seriously? Dead serious. He tried to explain the strategic importance of a seax. I politely excused myself to ‘check on the soup’ which was, conveniently, not even started. Honestly, I’m starting to think I’m destined to be a crazy cat lady. Although, even the cats would probably judge my taste in men. Viking battles? That's… dedicated. I went on a date a couple o’ weeks ago, she kept talking about her ex. For two hours. Just… relentlessly. Said he was a 'free spirit'. Sounded like a right pain in the backside to me. They’re all ‘free spirits’ until they’re free to date someone else. I've been trying online dating too, actually. It’s… a process. Mostly people sending unsolicited pictures.  Eye roll . I did meet someone decent last month, a biochemist, but he was ridiculously obsessed with lab coats. Like, actually wore one on our first date. Oh my god!

…and honestly, the sheer scale of it all, you know? Trying to explain landscape to them, proper  landscape  – not just ‘big mountain, pretty’. They’d seen pictures, of course, but nothing prepares you for the reality of the karst formations in Guilin. It's like something out of Avatar. Guilin, yeah. Right, that’s the one with all the… pointy hills? Sounds incredible. Did they get much chance to get  out  out there? Beyond the cities? A little. We did a river cruise, which was good. I tried to point out the wildlife, the birds particularly, but they were more interested in filming everything for WeChat. Every blooming pagoda, every slightly odd rock formation. It’s a different relationship with…with appreciating things. It’s about  having seen  it, rather than  being  with it, if that makes sense? Totally. It's the documentation, isn't it? Proof of experience. Like when we were in Paris, and everyone was snapping pics of the Eiffel Tower, barely looking  at  the Eiffel Tower. Speaking of which, you wouldn’t believe what happened here in Gordon Square earlier. This little lad – must’ve been eight – actually  caught  a pigeon. No! Really? How? I don’t know  how , but he had it! A flailing, feathery mess. His mum nearly had a heart attack. It was all very dramatic. Reminded me of those stories you hear about bears wandering into villages in China. Apparently, it’s becoming more common, habitats shrinking and all that. It is. They've got a real problem with that. I was talking to a colleague - Li Wei, you remember, the one doing the linguistics stuff? - he reckons the panda reserves are the only proper success story with wildlife conservation. But beyond that, it's a fight. He was telling me about travelling through Tibet…a lifetime ago, effectively. It was completely different then, much less…polished for tourism. Tibet. Now there’s a place. Although getting there sounds like a logistical nightmare. Completely different to a weekend down in Devon, even. Speaking of which, are you still planning on driving down to see your mum next month? Hoping to. Though the thought of navigating those country lanes again fills me with dread. It's not the driving  per se , it's the tractors and the tourists. And everyone thinking it’s perfectly alright to stop in the middle of a blind bend!

…Aye, well that's what I’m sayin’, isn’t it? It’s not just  a  bit annoying, it’s fundamentally messed up the whole tagging system. Like, I spent all last week cleaning up the metadata for the Chaucer stuff, right? Proper detailed, every manuscript variation noted, and then  this  happens. Right, the ‘incident’ with the automatic keyword assignment. Sounds… chaotic. Honestly, I don't understand half of what you  do , Ella. “Metadata for Chaucer”? You're basically an archaeological digger of text, aren’t you? Basically! It's important though, like. If the data's rubbish, the research is rubbish. And now it’s all labelled with 'Medieval Food' because someone thought 'manners' and 'meat' were interchangeable concepts. Manners! Can you imagine a PhD student basing a thesis on that? Ouch. Okay, that  is  bad. So, is it salvageable? Is it a full rebuild, or can you script something to… un-foodify everything? I'm tryin' to script somethin', aye. But the algorithm’s really sticky. It’s like it’s  determined  to see every reference to a celebratory feast as proof of medieval culinary habits. I've got it down to about 60% fixed now, but there's still a load of false positives. It’ll take another day, easy. That’s rough. Listen, are you still on for Mum and Dad’s on Saturday? I told them I’d bring a plus one, and I was hoping… well, you know. Oh. Right. Saturday. Yeah, I… I'd like that, actually. It’s just... I was kinda hoping to get a proper chunk of this tagging mess sorted beforehand. I feel awful goin' round there knowing I'm gonna be thinkin' about 'Medieval Food' and dodgy algorithms the whole time. You won’t. I promise. I’ll divert you. We can… strategically discuss my work. Which is, admittedly, slightly less entertaining than discerning medieval dining practices, but… Slightly? You spend your life designing pipes, Ben. It's not exactly  Beowulf . Hey! Those pipes are vital infrastructure! People need water! Besides, I’ve recently been looking into some pretty complex fluid dynamics models. Fascinating stuff, honestly. Oh, I'm on the edge of my seat. Listen, tell you what, I’ll try and get as much done as I can before Saturday. Maybe if I can at least get it down to a manageable level, I won’t be a complete stress-head.

… honestly, I just think she’s using it as an excuse, y’know? Like, 'Oh, poor me, I’ve got a migraine,’ every time she doesn’t fancy going out. It was the same last month with her aunt's birthday. Said she couldn’t make it 'cause of a headache. Bit convenient, isn't it? Sounds a bit rough, yeah. My nan pulls that one all the time. Says her arthritis is acting up when really she just wants a quiet night in with the telly. Can’t blame ‘em, though, can ya? Sometimes a person just needs a bit of peace. I think you’re being a  little  harsh, Anya. Migraines are genuinely awful. I get them sometimes – debilitating. It's not just a headache, it’s… everything hurts. Light, sound, smells… you just wanna curl up in a dark room. I know, I know, and I  do  feel bad saying it. It's just, it’s a pattern with Chloe. And she's been moody as owld hell lately, ever since… well, ever since she and Liam split. So, I'm wondering if it's all linked. Liam, right? The builder? Seemed a decent bloke. Didn't he build that fancy decking for your uncle last year? Yeah, that's him. Apparently, he… well, he met someone else. At a footie match, apparently. Honestly, a footie match! Couldn’t he have cheated somewhere more original? Oh, Anya, that's awful! No wonder she’s feeling rubbish. That’s a proper kick in the teeth. Even if the migraines  were  a bit of an excuse before, they’re probably real now, fuelled by heartbreak. You think so? I feel awful for her, I really do. I just get frustrated, 'cause she won’t  talk  about it properly. Just shuts down and says she’s got a migraine. And she's cancelled on our cinema trip next week, naturally. Least she's not workin' through it, then. I had a breakup a couple of years back and tried to just… carry on as normal. That were a disaster. Ended up droppin’ a load of bricks on me foot. Didn’t even feel it ‘til later. Oh, Ben! You always manage to injure yourself in the most dramatic ways. But you're right, forcing yourself isn’t the answer. Anya, maybe you could just… go round with a takeaway and sit with her?

… honestly, it’s just  exhausting  dealing with Mark. He’s convinced this new software is going to magically solve all our scheduling problems, but he hasn’t even bothered to ask anyone  how  we currently schedule things! It's like he thinks we’ve all been operating in the dark ages. Mark, huh? Still being…Mark? Sounds about right. Is it the same Mark who tried to implement that colour-coded filing system last year that nobody understood? The very same! Honestly, it's the lack of consultation. I spent an hour this morning trying to explain to him  why  the existing spreadsheet works well, and he just kept talking over me about 'synergies' and 'streamlining'. It's buzzword bingo with that man. Ugh. Workplace buzzword bingo is the worst. Makes you want to scream, doesn't it? Though, to be fair, streamlining  can  be good. Just not when it’s imposed from above without a clue. How’s the rest of the team reacting? Mostly eye-rolling. Sarah’s brilliant at passive-aggressive comments. She just said, “Oh, that’s… innovative,” with the biggest raised eyebrow you’ve ever seen. But everyone’s secretly dreading the inevitable training session. They know it’ll be two days of him ‘explaining the vision’ rather than actually teaching us the program. Classic. So, work's a mess. Anything good happening outside of the battlefield? How was drinks with Chloe and Liam last night? Oh god, don't even  ask . It was… awkward. Really awkward. Liam and Chloe have officially imploded. No! Seriously? I had a feeling things weren't great. They’ve been a bit off for a few weeks, haven’t they? What happened? Apparently, Chloe found messages on his phone. Nothing… explicitly scandalous, but enough to suggest he's been talking to his ex. He claimed it was just “friendly catching up,” but she wasn’t buying it. She was  devastated . Honestly, she was trying to be strong, but her mascara was definitely running. Oh, poor Chloe. That’s awful. Liam always struck me as a bit… flighty. Not intentionally malicious, but easily distracted. So, full-blown breakup then? Seems like it. She said she needs space and time to process. I just kept trying to be supportive and offering chocolate. Chocolate seems to be the only sensible response to heartbreak, right? Absolutely. It's a medically proven cure, practically. You did the right thing.

…and that’s why the Green Man is often depicted with leaves growing  from  his face, you see. It’s not creepy, it’s…renewal. It's the forest reclaiming things, bringing life back. Does that make sense, Leo? Kind of. So, he's…good? Well, he’s not  good  or  evil , exactly. He's more…a force. Like the weather. The weather isn’t good or evil, is it? It just  is . The Green Man represents the wild, untamed parts of nature. Sometimes that’s beautiful and helpful, sometimes it’s…powerful and a bit scary. Is he like Maleficent? She was scary, but then she was nice at the end. That’s a good comparison, Elsie! Maleficent  started  as seeming pretty evil, didn't she? And that’s a lot of what these old stories are about – things aren't always black and white. They’re shades of grey. Think about dragons… they often hoard gold, which seems greedy, but they also protect things. They're powerful. My friend, Finn, says dragons are just big lizards. Finn sounds very practical. They  might  have started as stories about big lizards, perhaps. But stories change, don't they? They get…embellished. They tell us something about what people  fear  and what they  hope  for. What about goblins? Are goblins evil? Goblins are tricksters, Elsie. Nasty little tricksters. They’ll play pranks, steal things, lead you astray. They're often motivated by greed or just plain mischief. So, leaning towards evil, I suppose, but not necessarily world-destroying evil. More…annoying evil. Like when you hide my Lego? That was  not  goblin-like behaviour, young man. That was me trying to encourage you to tidy up! A totally reasonable request. But goblins steal shiny things, right? Like Mum’s earrings? Not  my  earrings! Though that's a good image. Goblins definitely like shiny things. The stories say they live underground, in caves and mines, and they’re always searching for treasure. Now, is anyone else hungry? I was thinking we could make those fairy cakes I promised. Yes! With sprinkles! And pink icing! Can we make them look like little dragons? Dragons, excellent idea! Although, maybe not goblin-sized dragons. They might try to steal all the sprinkles. Right, let’s get the ingredients out. Elsie, could you get the flour? Leo, you're on sugar duty. And while we're baking, we can talk more about good  versus  evil… perhaps about giants?

…and honestly, the whole thing sounded a bit chaotic. Apparently, they filmed scenes  in  the local supermarket. Can you imagine? Little ‘uns running around, holding up checkout queues! Oh, Comberton High. Never a dull moment. Did they get permission for everything? Sounds like a logistical nightmare. Was ANON excited about being in a ‘real’ supermarket? It was SO COOL! I was a shopper! I had to pick up pretend beans and… and a banana! I was a security guard! I told everyone to ‘Move along now!’ It was brilliant. They both were buzzing about it all day yesterday. Though little ANON here has managed to hurt her leg somehow. Said she tripped over thin air. Oh, darling. Let me see. Doesn’t seem too bad, just a bit of a graze. Put some antiseptic on it earlier. You were probably just over-excited, running around pretending to be a shopper. It  does  sting a little. Speaking of cooling things down, it’s been surprisingly mild these past few nights, hasn’t it? I’ve actually had the window open a crack. It has. I was worried we’d have another freezing October. Though I still put the heating on for half an hour before bed. Old habits, I suppose. It's a bit drafty in the bedroom. My feet are cold! Right, well, maybe some thicker socks are in order for you, young man. Listen, I was thinking about getting back to the gym. Haven’t been in ages. Oh, good! You said that last week, and the week before… I know, I know! Life gets in the way. But I’m serious this time. I feel… sluggish. Need to do something. Thinking of sticking to the running machines mostly. Less chance of embarrassing myself trying to lift weights. That's sensible. Remember last time and the slightly dramatic protest involving your lower back? Don’t remind me. I felt 90. Although, oddly, I had a massive craving for doughnuts afterwards. It's a weird link in my brain – physical exertion equals sugary goodness. Doughnuts are yummy! Especially pink ones! With sprinkles! Honestly, you two. You’ve got a sweet tooth the size of Cambridgeshire. No doughnuts today, though. Maybe as a reward  after  your dad actually goes to the gym a few times. Harsh, but fair. I might need a reward myself, come to think of it. Maybe a small one, after the first session.

…and honestly, Arthur, the physio’s given me a whole new set of exercises. It's all about core strength, apparently. Core strength! At my age! Feels like I’m training for the Olympics, not just trying to bend down to tie my shoelaces. Though, bending down  is  becoming a proper ordeal, I won't lie. Core strength, eh? They tell me the same thing. Though mine’s more about keeping upright after a particularly enthusiastic round of gardening. Bad back, you know. Comes with the territory of digging up prize-winning dahlias. Speaking of which, did you see that report about the Green Party gaining traction in the local elections? A little. I was more focused on trying to understand what my grandson was explaining about TikTok. Honestly, it's another language. But the Greens, yes. Good for them, I suppose. Though I still worry about the practicalities. All very well wanting to ban petrol cars, but what about chaps like me who rely on them to get to the boot sales? Boot sales! Now you're talking. Found a lovely little set of brass candlesticks last weekend. Only a fiver! Seriously, the bargains you can pick up… keeps a man occupied, it does. And as for the Greens, well, I’ve always thought they had a point about local issues. Brighton’s getting choked with tourists, isn't it? Used to be a proper seaside town. Now it's just…shops selling overpriced pebbles. Overpriced pebbles! Exactly! And the parking. Don’t even get me started on the parking. It's a nightmare. But you’re right about the tourists, it’s changed. Remember when the pier was full of amusement arcades and families? Now it’s all cocktail bars. Still, it provides jobs, I suppose. Though most of them seem to be seasonal and poorly paid. My ex-pupil, young Liam, he’s working three jobs just to make ends meet. Bar work, delivering takeaways… it’s a disgrace. That  is  rough. I remember when leaving school meant you had a decent chance of finding a proper trade. Now it feels like young people are just bouncing between zero-hour contracts. My nephew, Daniel, he’s a graphic designer, talented lad. But finding a full-time role? Nearly impossible. He's thinking of going freelance. Scary, that. Freelancing's a gamble. It suits some, but it's no life being constantly worried about where the next commission's coming from.

… honestly, I just don’t  get  the appeal of those tiny houseplants everyone’s obsessed with. Like, a two-inch succulent? What’s the point? It’s just…sad. Give me a proper fern, something with a bit of  presence , y'know? Like the ones my Nana used to have, trailing all over the kitchen window. You and your grand scale, lass. It’s about the aesthetic, isn’t it? The miniature world. Plus, they're low maintenance. PhD life leaves little room for daily fern misting, sadly. Speaking of aesthetics though, did you see that monstrosity Sarah wore to the conference dinner? That…sequined jumpsuit? Oh,  God , don’t even. It looked like a disco ball had an unfortunate accident. Honestly, some people have no self-awareness. It clashed with everything – even the wallpaper. I went for a classic, navy shift, sensible shoes. Practicality rules. Although, I did splurge on a new handbag… it was on sale, though, you understand. Strictly within budget. Sensible is good. Though a bit of sparkle never hurt anyone. Budgeting is important, though. Especially with the way things are going. I’ve been trying to figure out this ISA stuff. It’s baffling. Feels like every financial product is designed to confuse you. Tell me about it. I’ve been looking at stocks and shares, trying to be all responsible. My dad keeps telling me I need to start thinking about pensions, and I’m just… twenty-six. It feels like a lifetime away, but he’s right. It’s just… overwhelming. It's like, how do you even  begin  to predict the market? Especially with everything going on politically. Exactly! It’s terrifying. And then you get someone like… well, you know who. Still rattling on about rigged elections, even after everything. Honestly, the sheer audacity. I saw a clip online… it was just… exhausting. Don’t even  mention  him. I actively avoid any news that features his face. It’s detrimental to my mental health. It's just constant noise. It feels like the world’s gone mad. Remember when we were worried about Brexit? That feels… quaint now. Quaint is a good word. Remember travelling through Cornwall, just before the referendum? All the pasty shops had signs up, "Vote Leave - Protect the Cornish Pasty!" It was surreal. Actually, talking of pasties, there's a new place opened near my college. Supposedly authentic. Ooh, a proper Cornish pasty is a serious undertaking.

…and honestly, the student just blinked at me. Blinked! After I’d spent fifteen minutes explaining the semiotics of a Constable landscape. You’d think  something  would have registered. It’s just… exhausting sometimes, isn’t it? Trying to make them see what you see. Absolutely. The glazed-over look is a universal lecturer experience, I think. Though, mine tend to manifest when I start talking about the socio-political context of post-war British sculpture. Doesn’t exactly lend itself to TikTok, does it? Here, let me top up your wine. This Norfolk stuff is surprisingly good. It is lovely, actually. Thank you. It’s just… I feel like I’m battling against a tide of instant gratification. Everything needs to be  now , visually stimulating, short-form. Art demands a bit of… contemplation. Contemplation being a lost art, it seems. Speaking of visually stimulating, did you see that documentary about killer whales the other night? Absolutely breathtaking. The way they hunt, their social structures... it’s more complex than half my committee meetings. Oh, I missed that! Sounds fascinating. We were glued to that awful reality show mum was watching. Honestly, the amount of manufactured drama… it’s unsettling. I read something about how exposure to that level of vicarious aggression actually alters brain development. Proper worrying stuff. It is. And it's  everywhere . Even kids’ TV isn’t immune. Remember how wholesome  Blue Peter  used to be? Now it's all challenges and competitive elements. I’m pretty sure I still have my silver badge somewhere, though. Mum insisted I display it prominently. Oh, absolutely! The holy grail of childhood achievement. I remember being devastated when my application for the gold badge was rejected. Apparently, my diorama of a badger sett wasn’t up to scratch. Still think it was a perfectly good badger sett! Harsh judges, those  Blue Peter  folks. It's funny the things you remember. Speaking of things you remember… remember that squat we got kicked out of in Camden, back in uni? Oh…  that  squat. Don’t remind me! Honestly, the smell… and the questionable plumbing. That place was a health hazard. A character builder, definitely. Although, Old Man Hemmings, the landlord, was terrifying. I swear he was armed with a cricket bat at all times. He looked like he'd seen action in the Falklands. He  had  that look about him, didn’t he?

…No, no, that’s what I mean about these hostels, see? They just don’t  manage  ‘em properly. Used to be Old Man Hemmings ran the one down Norwich Road, lovely fella. Kept it spotless. Proper forms for everything, y’know? Now it’s all… chaos. Bookings all over the place, teenagers runnin’ wild. It’s a shame, real shame. Oh, Arthur, you worry too much. It’s just youngsters having a bit of fun. Though I do agree, standards seem to have slipped everywhere. Remember Mrs. Gable's boarding house near the station? Always a pot of tea brewing, biscuits on offer… proper hospitality. I’ve got these photos from when we stayed there in ‘78, want to see? Little blurry, mind you, cameras weren’t what they are now. Blurry photos, the hallmark of a good holiday! Though, thinking about standards slipping… I’ve got a colleague, poor bloke, his mum’s in hospital. Apparently, the ward is chronically understaffed. Says she's waiting ages for basic things. It's not just hostels, is it? It's everything. Hospitals, eh? Poor soul. Old Maggie next door, she’s been in and out with her hip. Says the same. “Not enough nurses, Arthur, not enough nurses!” She was a whirlwind, Maggie, ran the sweet shop on Dereham Road for forty years. Worked her fingers to the bone, she did. And her husband, George, the butcher… Oh, George! Lovely man, always gave the children an extra sausage. Though I do remember the smell… abattoirs aren't exactly fragrant. Still, they provided for their family, didn’t they? My mum and dad, they had the greengrocer's in Harrow. Up at dawn to get the fresh produce from Smithfield Market. Hard work, relentless work. It’s that generation, isn’t it? Grafted for everything. My grandad was an engineer, worked on the railways. Always tinkering with things, building models. Got me fascinated with how things  work . That’s why I went into teaching, I suppose. Wanted to pass that on. Though sometimes, trying to explain basic science to teenagers… it’s like talking to a brick wall. Science... Pah! All this modern science. Too complicated for me. Give me a good steam engine any day. Proper engineering. Now, my cousin, Fred, he worked at the aircraft factory during the war. Top secret stuff, he couldn’t tell us much. But he did say it involved a lot of precision.

… honestly, the difference is just  massive . I mean, you said yourself you were in recruitment before this, didn’t you, Ben? It’s a whole other universe, isn’t it? Trying to get undergraduates to grasp referencing is… a different kettle of fish to convincing someone they  need  a job. You’ve hit the nail on the head, actually, Eleanor. Massively different. It was all about persuasion, reading people, crafting a narrative. The academic literacy stuff… it’s about deconstructing narratives, almost. Less ‘sell’ and more ‘unpick’. And frankly, a lot more… frustrating. Frustrating is putting it mildly! I’m marking these essays for the introductory module, the one everyone  has  to take, regardless of their subject, and it's… well, some of them genuinely don’t seem to understand the fundamental point of an argument. They just string together a load of vaguely related facts. Right? It’s the ‘information dump’ phenomenon. They think if they just include enough evidence, it somehow constitutes an argument. I’m seeing it in my seminars too, with the history students. They’ll quote three historians who all disagree, and then just… leave it there. No synthesis, no analysis. Exactly! It's like they think the research  is  the essay. They haven’t grasped the ‘so what?’ element. Did you find this at all in recruitment? Did you have to explain  why  a skill was important, beyond just listing it on a CV? All the time. You'd be talking to someone, and they'd say, ‘Yes, I’ve used Excel.’ And you have to probe. ‘Okay, great. What  for ? How did you utilise its functions to, say, solve a problem or streamline a process?’ It's the same principle. They can  name  the tool, but not  apply  it effectively. And I think that’s what’s missing with a lot of this academic writing. They can recognise a source, maybe even summarise it, but can’t interrogate it. It’s terrible, isn’t it? And you know, it’s not necessarily a lack of intelligence. Some of them are perfectly bright. It’s just… a gap. A huge gap in their educational scaffolding, I suspect. I remember teaching A-levels back in Dorset and even then, we were drilling the importance of constructing a coherent argument. Dorset, huh? Lovely part of the world. My grandmother lived near Lyme Regis. But yeah, I think you’re right about the scaffolding.

… honestly, I just spent the last hour trying to decipher this article on post-structuralism. It's like they  want  to be incomprehensible, innit? Makes you wonder if they actually understand it themselves. Tell me about it. I'm more used to selling phone cases, not grappling with… whatever that is. Though, explaining the difference between tempered glass and plastic to someone feels pretty philosophical sometimes. Right? Like, “This one  protects  your phone, this one just looks nice.” Deep stuff. I’m Sarah, by the way. I'm doing a Masters in English Lit, hence the shared pain of confusing academic texts. Hi everyone! I’m Priya. I’m a bit lost actually… I’m new to Salford Uni. This is the library, yeah? It's massive! Aye, it is a bit of a labyrinth. I'm Chloe, and this is Liam. We're both…suffering through postgrad life, apparently. Don't worry, you get used to getting lost. And the existential dread. Liam here is my source of moral support… and occasional terrible jokes. Don’t encourage him, Priya. Oh! Welcome, Priya! What are you studying? I’m doing a Masters in Data Science. Trying to find the quietest corner for some coding. It's… a lot different from my undergrad. I did History over in Leeds. Data Science, that's proper clever. I struggle with Excel, let alone anything with actual code. I’m doing a Masters in Sociology. Which mostly involves having strong opinions and arguing about them. Originally from Bradford, me. Bradford, nice! I'm from a bit closer, Rochdale. Bit grim, but home, you know? And yeah, Sociology sounds…intense. I'm just plugging away at retail, saving up for, well,  something . Hopefully something involving not folding clothes for the rest of my life. I feel that. Bolton's not much better than Rochdale, to be honest. Though, we do have a decent market. It’s the little things. So, Priya, Leeds is a good shout. Did you enjoy it? I loved it! Really vibrant city. Moving here felt a bit…quiet. But Salford Uni seemed to have a really good Data Science program, so I thought I’d give it a go. It's just… everyone seems to already know each other. It's like that at the start. Everyone’s formed their little study groups and inside jokes. You’ll find your people. We were just moaning about assignments, don’t let that put you off!

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt a bit…glorified, y’know? Like that film  1917 ? Stunning visually, absolutely, but it felt like it skipped over the sheer  monotony  of being in the trenches. All the waiting, the boredom, the rats…Grandad never talked about the fighting, not really. It was always about the awful food and how much he missed proper tea. Right? It's always the heroic bits they focus on. My uncle did a tour in Afghanistan, and he said the biggest struggle wasn't the threat of IEDs, it was just… keeping sane during the downtime. He got really into cross-stitch, of all things. Cross-stitch! No way! Grandad was a proper gardener. Tried to grow roses even when he was stationed in Egypt, can you imagine? Said the sand kept getting in the soil. He’d send photos back to my Great-Gran, all dusty and faded. Makes you think, doesn’t it? All these fancy war films, and it’s little details like that which stick with you. Totally. Speaking of little details, I was flicking through a magazine at the dentist –  Wired , actually – and they had a whole spread on retro computing. It got me thinking about the Commodore 64 my dad had. Do you remember those? Oh, aye! Course I do. Our neighbour had one. I used to spend hours round there playing  Manic Miner . Proper pixelated torture, that game. It wouldn't be half as difficult now, everything’s so…easy. Exactly! I was reading about how complicated it was to actually  load  a game. Taping it from a cassette, waiting ages, hoping it didn’t corrupt halfway through…the suspense! Now you just download it instantly. No romance in that. No romance at all. It's all 'instant gratification' this generation. Still, I’ve got a bit of a weakness for old tech. I collect vintage cameras, actually. Mostly Polaroids. That's cool! I'm more of a 'new tech' person myself. I'm currently wrestling with a new video editing software for work. Production are wantin' to do more online promotional stuff, and frankly, the learning curve is steep. I feel like I'm back at uni, coding all night. Oh, bless you. Sounds stressful. Being a Production Controller, you're always under pressure, aren't you? Conference work isn't exactly relaxing either, but at least it’s usually people being pleasantly excited about things, rather than looming deadlines and technical glitches.

… honestly, the audacity of him thinking I’d be interested after  that  line. "Do you come here often?" Seriously? It's 2024, Liam! Get some new material. Sounds about right. Guys are predictable. More predictable than, say, the outcome of a Tory leadership contest, and that’s saying something. Oh god, don’t even  start  on the politics. I spent half of Sunday arguing with my uncle. He actually said immigration is ‘ruining Winchester’. I nearly choked on my roast dinner. Ugh, the closed-mindedness is exhausting. Growing up near Watford, it was always so… diverse. You just don’t  think  about that stuff, y’know? It’s just… people. Totally. Up in Wirral, it was a bit more… homogenous. Though even there, you got your pockets of brilliantly different stuff happening. Makes you realise how sheltered some people are. Still, family, eh? You can’t pick ‘em. No, you can’t. Anyway, whose brilliant idea was it to suggest playing basketball after three pints? My legs feel like jelly. Mine! And don’t pretend you weren’t enjoying yourself, you were surprisingly competitive. Remember when you tried to block Ben and almost took his head off? Classic Chloe. Though, in fairness, Ben was winding her up. Speaking of winding people up, my cousin’s coming down from London next weekend. Prepare for a full-on culture clash. He thinks everything north of the M25 is “the sticks.” Oh,  lovely . Another Londoner with an inflated ego. Is he one of those ones who judges your postcode? Almost certainly. He’s a ‘digital strategist’ or something equally vague. Basically, he looks at TikTok all day and calls it work. He keeps going on about how ‘dynamic’ London is. Dynamic and overpriced, you mean. I spent a week there last year shadowing some architects, and honestly, it was a nightmare. Tiny flats, aggressive people… I was glad to get back to Hampshire. Tell me about it. I had a placement in Canary Wharf – a concrete jungle. I need green spaces, fresh air. It's why I'm so keen on incorporating more sustainable designs, more greenery into everything. Building things that  benefit  the community, not just line someone's pockets. You're a good egg, Liv. Properly passionate. What about your five-year plan, anyway? Still aiming for that eco-village project? It’s still the dream. It’s slow going, finding the right land and investors.

…and honestly, the window cleaner just  looked  at me like I was asking him to dismantle the Large Hadron Collider when I asked if he could do the ones on the landing too. Absolute state, the look on his face. Oh, Dad would  love  that story. He’d say it's typical Sussex, all a bit…reserved about extra work. Are you sure you explained it clearly? You know how people can mishear. Scones, for example. Half the country says “scone” to rhyme with “gone”, and the other half says it to rhyme with “cone”! It’s a national crisis. That's true, that is. My nan always said scone rhymes with 'gone'. Proper scone. And cream  before  jam, naturally. None of this Devon nonsense. Oh, cream first, absolutely! Though I must admit, after a bit of a scare with my cholesterol last year, I’m trying to limit the clotted cream. It’s delicious, but…well, you know. Dr. Patel said I need to be mindful. Mindful of joy, you mean? Honestly, Mum, a little clotted cream won’t hurt. Speaking of things that might hurt, have we sorted the money for Dad’s train ticket back? I think I owe you a tenner, didn’t I? You do, yes. And I think I’ve got enough loose change for it. It’s just…seeing him worrying about the cost, even a little, feels awful. He pretends he’s alright on his benefits, but… Don’t you fret about me. I’ve seen worse. Lived through rationing, you know. A tenner doesn’t break the bank. Though, a new bike would be nice…seeing as you've got that lovely cycle path near here. Remember when I used to race bikes as a lad? Down in London, we were a right bunch of tearaways. Oh, you? Racing bikes? I can’t picture it! You always seemed more the…dominoes and a pint man. Though, it explains the stories about gambling on greyhounds. Water under the bridge, love. A bit of fun. Never got carried away. Though, young Timmy next door…he was a proper betting man. Lost a fortune, he did. That’s why he ended up on the dole. Right, well, let’s avoid discussing potential financial pitfalls. How about the kitchen? Anything you particularly like, or is it all a bit…modern for your tastes? I was thinking of getting some new spice racks.

… honestly, it’s just  exhausting  trying to explain to people why a comma splice isn't just a stylistic choice, it's… a structural issue! Like, the whole point of the corpus is to show how language  actually  works, not how people  think  it should work. They’ll be like, “Oh, but it sounds fine!” Right, well, ‘sounds fine’ doesn’t mean it's grammatically correct, does it? Sounds about right. People and grammar. A classic mismatch. Though, you're dealing with a really specific corner of it, aren't you? I mean, most people wouldn’t even  know  what a corpus is, let alone a comma splice in one. My work’s more… concrete. Literally. Steel, concrete, the occasional disgruntled badger digging up foundations. Disgruntled badgers? Seriously? Oh, yeah. Little blighters. Had one try to build a sett right under the access road for a new housing development last month. Delayed everything by a week. Anyway, it's less arguing about punctuation and more arguing about load-bearing walls. Which, surprisingly, doesn’t leave much room for nuance. How’s Cambridge treating you? Still ridiculously expensive? Ridiculously is an understatement. I was looking at flats the other day - tiny, poky things - and they’re asking for more than my mam and dad paid for their  house  in Sunderland back in the day. It’s mental. Makes me wonder if I’ll ever actually own anything. Speaking of which, did you see that article about the government potentially scrapping Help to Buy? Ugh, don't even get me started. Another scheme that benefits the already-wealthy while doing jack all for people trying to get on the ladder. It's just… frustrating. My sister’s trying to buy in Tunbridge Wells, and it's basically impossible. She’s a teacher, a  teacher , and even with a deposit, she's being outbid by cash buyers every time. It's awful, isn't it? It’s like they actively want to make it impossible for our generation to own a home. Honestly, sometimes I think about just buying a caravan and living off-grid. Less stressful, cheaper… and probably better for the environment. You and a lot of people, I suspect. Though you’d need to find a spot that doesn't get hit by torrential rain every five minutes. Did you see the weather forecast? It’s supposed to be biblical this weekend.

… honestly, the shift was  chaos . Old Mrs. Henderson decided she wasn’t taking her meds again. Saying they were “poison brewed by the government,” you know the drill. Honestly, you’d think after ninety-two years she’d have exhausted all her conspiracy theories, but no. Oh, bless her. They do get stuck in their ways, don't they? Sounds stressful though, dealing with that. It's a world away from writing ad copy for scented candles, believe me! Though  sometimes  I feel like I'm convincing people of a conspiracy – ‘This candle will change your life!’ Tell me about it! I had Mr. Davies this morning convinced his slippers were plotting against him. Plotting! Said they were trying to trip him. I spent a good ten minutes reassuring a man his footwear wasn't sentient. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if  I’m  the one losing it. That's… something. I was just telling Mum about the dog this morning. Barnaby ate half a packet of biscuits and then pretended nothing happened. Just sat there, looking angelic, covered in crumbs. Barnaby sounds delightful. A proper little scamp. You haven’t told us what’s happened with your gran’s appointment yet, have you, love? The rheumatologist? Oh, right. It went… okay. Apparently, it’s just age, mostly. A bit of wear and tear. She’s not thrilled, naturally. Wants a ‘proper diagnosis’. She’s always been a bit of a hypochondriac, bless her, but she gets anxious. I had to promise to take her for a proper Sunday roast afterwards to cheer her up. That’s good, at least there wasn’t anything serious. My sister’s been nagging me to book a doctor’s appointment. Says I look peaky. I keep saying I’m fine, just tired from the shifts. It’s all the lifting, I reckon. You should go, honestly, Shaz. You work so hard. Mum's always saying the same about me – “You're burning the candle at both ends!” – but it’s just… it’s difficult getting time off. They're always short-staffed. It's the same everywhere, isn't it? Even at the hospital, we're crippled. Young Emily, the student nurse, was practically in tears yesterday. She said she felt completely useless, running around trying to find equipment. It’s disheartening for them. And the pay… don’t even get me started. It’s awful.
